# AWAKEN — Implementation Spec (v1)

This is the source of truth for builders. The player-facing design and its reasoning live in `docs/plan.html`.
When this spec and the plan disagree, this spec wins. When something is unspecified, pick the simplest
behaviour that serves the five pillars and write it down here in the same commit.

Pillars (every feature must serve two): **Main character energy · Pulled, not pushed · Every door is different ·
Learn by touching · Awareness is power.**

Hard rules:
- Nothing runs on real-world time. Timers count **play-days** (in-game days that pass while at least one player is online).
- Never more than **3** active Directives. Never a quest list. Undiscovered things are never listed.
- A reward is granted at most once per claim id. Loot moves, it is never copied.
- **Patent rule:** something done to one hostile NPC never changes a *different* hostile NPC's stats.
  Consequences go into world state (gate rank, blight, timers, loot, spawn budgets). The Rival is authored and advances on
  the player's rank milestones only. Nightmares are chosen from authored templates by the player's own death counts.
- No language model, no network calls. Everything local and deterministic (seeded).
- Performance: p50 ≥ 110 fps in a full gate fight on an M4; server tick p95 ≤ 25 ms; ≤ 60 active combat entities;
  ≤ 3 ms/tick of main-thread work for any background job.

Rules for builders:
- Touch only your module's package, your module's resources (namespaced file names), and your merge folder
  `src/main/merge/<module>/`. Shared JSON (lang, sounds.json, tags) is **merged at build time** from those folders.
- Each module has `XxxModule.init(IEventBus modBus)` (called from `Awaken`) and optionally `XxxClient.init(IEventBus)`.
  Register your own DeferredRegisters, payloads (own `RegisterPayloadHandlersEvent` listener), attachments, commands
  (as `/awaken <module> ...` subcommands via `AwakenCommands.register(...)`), and GameTests.
- Cross-module calls go through the small public API classes listed in §12. Never reach into another module's internals.
- Verify every Minecraft/NeoForge API against `/Volumes/MEDIA/Awaken/.ref` and `docs/api/*.md`. 26.3 differs from 1.21.1.
- **Blocks that stop motion** (`core.MotionTags`; Euan 2026-10-30, "get the rain inside Awaken houses fixed"). 26.3
  builds the heightmaps that rain, snow, lightning, spawning and Lens read from `#minecraft:blocks_motion`, and
  suffocation, fluid push, teleport targets and lava's fire from the tags it feeds, so a mod block is air to all of
  them until a tag adds it (rain fell inside Carillon's clay-tile houses). The rule is vanilla's own and gives
  vanilla's list back exactly: a block stops motion when any of its states is solid (`BlockState.isSolid`: a collision
  box most of a block or a whole block high, or `forceSolidOn`), except webs (they slow, never stop), layer blocks (snow
  layers, our drifts: thin layers would float the rain), standing and wall signs, and the bamboo sapling. Such a block
  goes in `#minecraft:blocks_motion_no_leaves` from its module's
  `src/main/merge/<module>/data/minecraft/tags/block/blocks_motion_no_leaves.json`; leaves go in `#minecraft:leaves`.
  322 blocks joined on 2026-10-30. GameTest `core_blocks_motion` walks every `awaken:` block and names each one the rule
  says should stop motion and no tag holds (exceptions in `BlocksMotionTests.EXCEPT`, each with its reason; none
  today), checks the rule against vanilla's own tag, and builds a city-brick house under clay tiles whose heightmaps
  must sit on its roof. Old saves keep their saved heightmaps, so a chunk that loads without the
  `awaken:motion_heights` mark at `MotionTags.HEIGHTS` (1) re-primes its two motion heightmaps once (only when a
  section's palette holds one of our tagged blocks), before it reaches the client, and is marked; bump `HEIGHTS`
  whenever blocks join the tags. Every reader of those heightmaps (citizens' footing, room scans, village growth,
  spawns, Far Sight, Delve's sense) now sees Awaken roofs and walls the way it sees vanilla's.
- **Creative tabs** (`core.api.Tabs`; Euan 2026-11-11: "everything in Awaken is in a single tab for creative, so let's
  put it in multiple tabs and all, like, correctly organized"). The creative menu has ten Awaken tabs after vanilla's,
  owned by core: Awaken Weapons, Armour, Tools and Gear, Stations and Machines, Materials, Building Blocks, Gate World
  Blocks, Nature and Food, Relics and Keepsakes, Creatures (titles `itemGroup.awaken.<id>` in core's lang). Each tab is a
  run of shelves in browsing order (`Tabs.Shelf`). A module never registers a tab or listens for
  `BuildCreativeModeTabContentsEvent`: from its init it fills its shelves (`Tabs.fill(shelf, items...)`, or a filler
  given the menu's parameters for registry-made stacks), sets together and tiers in order, and the module that owns a
  tab's icon item sets it (`Tabs.icon`). The shelves:
  - Weapons: the forged weapons (a style at a time, E to S, the Lords' own after), the Hunter blades and foci, the
    Blueprints.
  - Armour: the forged sets (helmet to boots, then the set's pattern), the Hunter armour, the Frames and their modules.
  - Tools and Gear: picks (the Waking Pick, the Delver's old head and the forged picks form by form, the Delver's pick),
    the Hunter mattocks, climbing (rope fittings, pitons, runner rope), gear (binoculars, the band, lamps, the lode map,
    the Burin, the Mallet, the handbell, the bridle and whistle, the Dream Journal, the Scanner).
  - Stations and Machines: the Hearth (Anchor, Ember, mat, Forge, trophy mount, monolith, the role pads), workshops and
    stands (War Anvil, Inscribing Table, Fitting Stand, pattern stand), bell hooks (the frame and both beams), the
    beasts' works, the Precursor machines, courses and the movement blocks.
  - Materials: essence (shard, Lord Heart, dream residue, core shard), a power core of every power the menu shows, a
    page of every inscription, Precursor parts, the deep's metals, what gate creatures and Lords leave (and the Hearth's
    trophy), what the wild's beasts leave, and Unsorted.
  - Building Blocks: Precursor blocks, monuments (the Olden stone, the finds' props), the home kit (every bloom of the
    window box), the Descent's strata, the Veil's and the Stillpoint's blocks, the dream's blocks.
  - Gate World Blocks: a gate's own pieces (frames, shrine, seal, cache, set pieces, the rig), then every world's blocks,
    each with the slabs, stairs and drifts cut from it beside it.
  - Nature and Food: the Awakened Lands, the ground (cover, wild plants, soft slabs), caves (deepglass and the lode
    hearts, then the caves' rock and growths), herbs and meals.
  - Relics and Keepsakes: relics (the wayfarers' and the finds'), the bells (the hundred in number order, the heart
    clapper, the Sovereign's relic, a village's bell), keepsakes (the licence, letters, keys, the Delver's logs, a
    village's keepsake and token), the townsfolk's things.
  - Creatures: the gates' creatures and bosses in bestiary order (and Vael), the wild's beasts.
  Every Awaken item sits in exactly one tab. JEI lists exactly what the tabs hold (§14), so an item no shelf places would
  be lost there: it lands on Materials' Unsorted shelf instead and the check names it. A stack a shelf gives twice is
  kept once (vanilla throws and the whole tab goes empty), and a filler that throws loses only its own shelf (logged).
  An item shown in several kinds says what tells them apart (`Tabs.variants`), so JEI keeps each kind. The check
  (`Tabs.audit`): `/awaken core tabs` (admin; to chat and to the log as `[core] creative tabs`) and GameTest
  `core_creative_tabs` fail on an item in no tab or in two, a stack placed twice, an item in several kinds undeclared or
  not told apart, and a filler that throws. `BlockSet` takes its shelf. `CoreModule.TAB_KEY` (the old single tab,
  `awaken:awaken`) stays, deprecated, so older branches still compile; no tab has that key, so what they add lands on
  Unsorted and the check names it.

## 2. Numbers (from `tools/sim/pacing_sim.py`, tuned 2026-10-23)

```
xpToNext(L)      = 90 * L^1.45 + 60
RANKS            = E, D, C, B, A, S, SOVEREIGN          (index 0..6)
RANK_LEVEL       = D 10, C 25, B 45, A 70, S 100, SOVEREIGN 135   (level needed to take the Reassessment)
RANK_MID         = E 5, D 17, C 35, B 57, A 85, S 118, SOVEREIGN 150  (gate content level)
SHARE            = E .28, D .16, C .065, B .22, A .60, S .55, SOVEREIGN .50   (v2, see §13; v1 was .81/.39/.25/.23/.18/.12/.12)
floorReward(r,f) = GATE_PAY[r] * SHARE[r] * xpToNext(RANK_MID[r]) * 1.4^(f-1)   (§50.3; the open world's camps, stars and rifts use it without GATE_PAY)
GATE_PAY         = E 2, D 3, C 4, B 2, A 1.25, S 1.25, SOVEREIGN 1.25
   60% arrives as kill XP during the floor (split across the floor's spawned mobs)
   40% is the floor bonus, carried as "Satchel XP" and banked only on extraction or boss kill
gate below your rank pays x0.3; above your rank x1.5 per rank above; a Lord's first clear +50% of the whole gate's floors
home activity XP ~ 1.2% of a level per active minute (capped per minute; see §4.3)
Daily Regimen    = 0.25 * xpToNext(L) + 1 stat point   (gone since §27.13)
death            = lose Satchel (items + Satchel XP), keep gear & kill XP, gain Insight, Fracture 8 min (Hunter mode)
story length     = config multiplier on all XP: 2.0 (≈50 h), 1.0 (≈100 h, default), 0.67 (≈150 h)
```

Gate shape: floors = min(6, 3 + rank/2 + coin). Breaks in = max(1, 4 - rank/2 + (0|1)) play-days.
Modifier budget by gate rank E..S: 1,2,3,4,5,6; max count 1,1,2,2,3,3; Sovereign = S.
Twist: 1/8 chance, guaranteed on the 12th gate without one (per player).
Director gate rank roll: 70% player rank, 20% one below, 10% one above. Keep 1–4 open gates within 300–1500 blocks of each
online player. Themes come from a bag per player (§50.2), no layout from the last 2.

Second reward rhythm: the Director tracks minutes since the player's last *new thing* (new power, title, Truth true,
latent, depth record, trophy, scanned machine). After 20 min it biases: next elite drop → Power Core (+50%),
next Directive → one that completes quickly. Power Core pity: guaranteed from a Gate Lord if none in the last 3 bosses.

Mob scaling by content level `lv` (RANK_MID of the gate/stratum):
```
health = base * (1 + 0.075*lv)       damage = base * (1 + 0.04*lv)       armor += lv/12
```
Player scaling (stats, §3) and gate gear tiers keep an on-level player at roughly 3–6 hits per normal mob.

## 3. Stats

Six stats, start at **5** each at awakening. **+3 points per level**, +1 per completed Regimen, some Truths give points.
Respec: Precursor "Recalibrator" machine (above), costs essence.

| Stat | Effect (per point unless noted) | Implementation |
|---|---|---|
| STR | +2.5% melee damage; Kinetic power scaling | ATTACK_DAMAGE multiply_base modifier `awaken:stat_str` |
| AGI | +0.4% move speed (cap +40%), +1% attack speed (cap +60%); Flow +0.05 s | MOVEMENT_SPEED / ATTACK_SPEED modifiers |
| VIT | +0.6 max health; +0.5% damage resistance (cap 35%) | MAX_HEALTH add_value; resistance in damage event |
| INT | energy pool 100 + 5/pt; Energy/Tech power damage +1.5% | read by powers |
| PER | crit chance 0.4% (cap 35%, crits ×1.6); secret glow radius 4 + PER/4 blocks; omen detail tiers at 20/40/60 | damage event + clients |
| SPI | cord length 32 + 6/pt (cap 1024); Veil time 30 s + 3 s/pt; lucidity gain +1%; Echo cap 3 + SPI/6 | read by veil/lucidium/hearth |

Energy regen: 4/s + 0.08 × INT per second, paused for 1 s after spending.

## 4. Progression

### 4.1 Profile attachment (`progression`, synced to owner, copyOnDeath)
`level, xp, rank, unspent, stats[6], awakened(bool), path(id|null), truthsDeclared(≤3), truthsTrue(set), titles(set),
equippedTitle, latents(set), counters(map<id,long>), directives(≤3), regimen(today), lastNewThingTick, insight(map),
fractureUntil, playDay, schemaVersion`.

### 4.2 Counters
Any module calls `Progression.count(player, "awaken:<name>", amount)`. Counters drive Truths, Titles, Latents, Paths,
Directives and Regimen. Standard counter ids are listed in `progression/Counters.java`; modules add their own ids freely.

### 4.3 Home XP
Kills of overworld hostiles: 4% of a level × mob max health/20 (cap 1 level per 10 min from kills). Mining ores: 1% of a
level per ore (cap). Placing blocks: 0.05% per block (cap 1% per minute). Hard cap: 1.5% of a level per real minute
from home activity.

### 4.4 Reassessment (rank-up)
At RANK_LEVEL the Spine says "Reassessment available". Trial is taken at the Spire (hearth town) or any Reassessment
Monolith. Trials are handcrafted arenas (in the Stillpoint dimension's trial wing): D survive 3 waves; C Second Awakening
(waves + Path reveal); B boss duel; A timed descent (5 rooms, 4 min); S fight a Sovereign's echo; SOVEREIGN after the Seed.
(Since §47.4 to §47.10 every rank's trial is a Proving, D to Sovereign, and Sovereign comes before the Seed: it opens it.)
Pass → rank++, Signal Reassessment window, town celebration, new tier of gates, aura tier.

### 4.5 Truths
Data: `data/awaken/awaken/truth/*.json` `{id, text, hint?, condition, reward}`. Offered 3 at awakening and 3 at each rank
(plus emergent ones when a hidden condition is met). Declare up to 3 → "NOT TRUE YET" → condition met → TRUE (permanent).
**Since §27.13 (2026-10-30)** none are offered or declared: from level 5 each comes true by itself when lived.
Conditions (`progression/Condition`): `counter_at_least`, `streak_at_least` (counter that resets on a reset-counter),
`event` (one-shot flag), `all/any`.

### 4.6 Titles & Latents
Same condition system. Titles: equip one (perk). Latents: hidden, granted automatically, announced by a Notice, recorded in
the Codex only once found. Codex shows counts like `Latents 7 / ??`.

### 4.7 Paths (Second Awakening, C-rank)
12 paths; 6 at launch + 3 later + 3 hidden. Each has `scoring` (weighted counters normalised per hour) and `hidden`
condition for hidden ones. Offer top 3 + qualifying hidden. Evidence lines quote real counters. Pick grants a signature
power + passive + aura colour.

### 4.8 Directives
Rule tables in data `directive/*.json` with `when` (context filters), `text`, `condition`, `reward`, `expires_days`.
One new offer per morning or notable event, max 3 active, no repeats within 5 play-days, ≥1 in 4 must be "fresh".
Accept with Y, ignore and it fades. **Gone since §27.13 (2026-10-30)**: only the Registry's own, the first floor of a gate,
stays (§27.6); the Tasks page says what's next.

### 4.9 Daily Regimen
Each in-game morning: 3 drills tuned to Path (sprint distance, Flow seconds, kills, Training Grounds lap, meditate 30 s,
mine N). Reward per §2. Skip = nothing, unless Hardline (Penalty Zone: survive 4 min in a desert night arena).
**Gone since §27.13 (2026-10-30)**, the Penalty Zone with it.

### 4.10 Director
Runs every 1000 ticks per online player: gates upkeep, directive offers, new-thing rhythm, break warnings.
`/awaken why` prints the last 10 decisions with inputs. Novelty memory stored per player.

## 5. Signal (UI)

Server: `Signal.send(ServerPlayer, SignalWindow)`. `SignalWindow{kind, title, body?, rows[(label,value)], footer?,
actions[(id,label)], ttlTicks, priority}`; kinds NOTICE, GATE, DIRECTIVE, TRUTH, WARNING, REASSESSMENT, REVELATION, DAYS_END.
Client: one window at a time, top-centre glass panel, letters type in fast, chime. In combat (hurt in last 5 s or hostile
within 8 blocks) windows become a compact toast and queue. Actions answered with **Y** (accept) / **N** (dismiss).
Visual: deep glass `#0F1724` at 88% alpha, edge `#7FC3FF`, corner brackets, title white, labels pale, "NOT TRUE YET" amber
`#FFCF7A`, warnings `#FF8A7A`.

NPC dialogue (Euan, 2026-10-28; Codex, reviewed): NPC speech (`SignalWindow.Builder.dialogue()`: townsfolk, quest
givers, Wayfarers, Vael, Veil spirits) is shown as speech, the speaker's name before the line ("Hale: Hold on."), paged
in whole sentences like any story line; a speaker's choice card stays a card with its own keys. The use key
(right-click by default) goes on one step per physical press: the first press finishes the line being typed, the next
shows the next page, then the next line (a Veil spirit's next line is asked of the server, which refuses a duplicate,
stale, distant or finished request). While a press would go on, a small bobbing chevron sits beside the last line.
Speech only takes the use key inside a conversation the player started (`Dialogue.talking()`): a use on an NPC (or
Focus on a spirit) opens one for 5 s while the reply comes, and it lasts while speech is up and 2 s after. Speech that
simply arrives (a quest step finished in the field, Vael's timed lines) never costs a shield block, a meal or a bow
draw. Inside a conversation the last press is used up, so it can't also restart the talk, use an item or take a
handover; holding use and the offhand never go on twice, and a fast second click waits for the first reply (1 s).
Without presses everything still plays on its own timing. The Opening's speech goes on with use while it shows; a
citizen's reply over their head goes when you look at them (within 6 blocks) and press. Timing, rewards and handovers
stay server-owned. Test `signal_dialogue_use_once`, `veil_dialogue_continuation`.

The band (key **K**, §30): six pages, Status · Tasks · Hearth · Powers · Journal · Map (§27.13). Status shows level, rank, path,
title and XP, the stats with + buttons when points are unspent, then the Journal; Powers holds the loadout (provided by
`powers` via `StatusSections`); the Map page is the Atlas.

## 6. Powers

Slots: 4 active (Z X C V), Ultimate (R), Movement (Left Alt). Passive powers apply when owned.
`PowerType` registry (custom registry `awaken:power_type`) with code; data numbers in the same class.
Families: Kinetic, Velocity, Flight, Energy, Shadow, Mind, Architect, Tech, Spirit. Forces: HEAT, CHARGE, GRAVITY, SPIRIT,
FROST (+ SPORES, WATER, VOLATILE, MIRROR as environmental tags).
Power Cores: item `awaken:power_core` with component `{power, variant}`. Using it learns the power (or upgrades a known one).
- **Before using a known Power Core** (Euan, 2026-10-28; Codex's journal-notices, reviewed against §36): its hover says
  what using it will do for the variant you **own**: "Use: level 2 → 3 (Overshield)", then the next ladder step in its own
  words (`PowerLadder.text(power, level)`, §36 decision 12), then the numbers every level moves, before → after: energy,
  cooldown (with the ladder's `cdScale`) and the main hit's damage (+6% a level, §36.2). The numbers come from the code a
  cast uses (`Cast.dmg`, `Casting.cooldownTicks`, `Casting.effectiveCost`) with your stats and effects right now; a step's
  own changes (riders, ranges, durations) are told by its text and never re-modelled. A core of another variant adds
  "Sneak and use instead to change it to X and keep level N." At the top level a same-variant core says it does nothing
  and is kept; another variant says it changes how the power works and keeps the level. Unknown powers keep "Use to
  learn". `powers.PowerPreviews` builds the lines on the server (read-only: never casts, spends or levels); the client
  asks only while a core is hovered, at most twice a second, the server answers at most once per 5 ticks and only for a
  power you own; the client keeps 16 answers for 1.5 s, drops them on logout or when your level or variant changes, and
  shows "Reading your next level…" until one arrives.
- Learning a power keeps its New power window, a variant change its Variant changed window, a level its ladder moment
  (§36.6); each is also kept quietly in the Journal (§26.3c) with what it does, the step and the numbers at that moment.
  The old "+12% damage, -4% cooldown" toast is gone. Codex's `PowerNumbers` (a second copy of every power's runtime
  numbers, shared by the casts) was dropped in review: §36's steps change those numbers per level, so a copy drifts.

Icons (2026-10-25): 32x32 GUI sprites `power/<id>`, generated by `tools/art/specs/powers.py` (kit `powericons.py`,
glyphs `powerglyphs.py`). The frame's shape names the family: Kinetic shield, Velocity chevron, Flight ringed world,
Energy diamond, Shadow crescent cut, Mind eye, Architect notched block, Tech chip octagon, Spirit teardrop. One light
from the top-left shades every frame and glyph. A Power Core is a crystal with its power's glyph inside (item model
select `awaken:core_power` on the power's path; an emissive `_glow` layer per power; no power shows a blank crystal).
Movement powers are client-predicted (velocity applied locally, server validates and corrects).
Dashes and the movement powers are held at the edge of the land the client has (the edge hold, §28.9), whether their
velocity is set on the client or comes in a motion packet; Blink and the other steps are teleports, not velocity, so
the server's packet cap (§28.9) is their backstop.
Dash direction: a Dash goes the way you are moving, at every power level and in every variant (Blink and Double included; a
duplicate core or a mastery level only changes the distance, damage and cooldown, never the direction). The held movement keys
(forward, back, left, right) ride on the cast payload (`PowerPayloads.Cast.keys`, 4 bits) and the predictor gets them as
`strafe` (+1 left) and `forward` (+1 forward): no key or forward alone is the look's flat heading as before, back is the
reverse, left/right are 90° to it, two keys are the diagonal, opposite keys cancel. A cast with no payload (commands, tests,
fake players) reads `ServerPlayer.getLastClientInput()`. Only a forward-leaning air dash lifts with the look's pitch; sideways
and back dashes run flat. Blink teleports along the same steered line (`Moves.steer`). Test `powers_dash_goes_where_you_move`.
A blink aimed into the ground (the crosshair a little low while standing) glides along it at the last free height instead of
stopping at its first step: `Moves.blinkTarget` (Blink, Lightning Step, Shadow Step) and `Moves.phaseTarget` (Ghost Step,
which still passes walls at that height). Test `powers_blink_low_aim`.
Feel: hit-stop 40–80 ms on heavy hits (client time scale on the hit entity's render + camera kick), shake toggle in config.

Launch power list (≥45): see `powers/PowerCatalog.java` header for the authoritative list with numbers.

The Tech movement power `awaken:grapple` is shown as **Snap Cable** (2026-10-26, progression plan decision 11), so
"the grapple" only ever means the Tether; its id, and saved worlds, are unchanged.

## 7. Gates

Overworld: `awaken:gate` block structure (frame + core) at a surface position; client renders a light pillar coloured by
rank (E #F4F6FB, D #5FD08F, C #6FB3FF, B #B48CFF, A #F2A541, S #FF5A6A, Sovereign black-gold), visible up to 1500 blocks
(drawn at clamped distance beyond render distance). Our own soft light, never vanilla's beacon beam: camera-facing
ribbons with a bell-shaped falloff across their width ((1 - x²)³, nothing and flat at the edge), a near-white core and
the rank's glow added as light, a wide haze in the rank's colour alpha-blended (it carries the pillar by day), all
thinning to nothing with height; no world fog (it counts height as distance and cut the column off flat), the top kept
inside the far plane. Drawn after the level in a pass of its own (depth-tested, no depth written), never through the
level's translucent passes (with improved transparency their composite writes a translucent's depth wherever it shows,
so Lens took each ribbon's whole quad for solid and left its clouds out there: a hard-edged slab). Hidden by any land
in front of where the gate really stands, near or far (Euan, 29 Oct: "One of the gate beams is showing on top of the
cliff here even tho the gate is behind it"): a pillar drawn pulled in along its sight line was tested at the depth it was
drawn at, so chunks between there and the gate never hid it, and Far Sight's land isn't in the game's depth at all. The
pillars' own pipelines (`RigPipelines.PILLAR_HAZE`/`PILLAR_LIGHT`, shader `gate_pillar`) carry each pillar's stretch (how
many times further off it really stands), write its real depth (at the far plane past it) for the game's depth test, and
discard where far land is nearer (`compat.client.FarTerrain`'s depth and planes, while it draws and shares one; never
under Distant Horizons). A driver that can't build them draws the pillars as before. Tour `pillars-ridge` (render
distance 6; the camera due south of gate 1 at fixed spots 120 and 300 blocks off, lifted over the roofs; a stone wall 31
wide 84-87 blocks ahead to 2 under its eyes). CI runs 40815747360 (before) and 40814281481 (after) at 300 blocks: before,
the beam crosses the wall's face down to the gate; after, it shows only above the wall's top. Admin `/awaken gate frame <dist> <lift>` puts the camera on the line from the nearest gate toward
Carillon's centre, facing the pillar (tours).
Gate card shows rank, breaks-in, omen; PER ≥20 adds layout, ≥40 modifiers, ≥60 floor count; Veil scouting shows all.
A gate of another rank than the hunter's says so in a "For you" row: "above your rank", or "below your rank · pays less"
(floors below your rank pay ×0.3, `Curve.BELOW_RANK_FACTOR`; §17.25).

Dimension `awaken:gates`: cells of 512×512 aligned to region files, cell origin = ((i mod 64)·1024, (i div 64)·1024).
Floors stacked vertically: floor f at y = 200 − 32·(f−1) (f = 1..6), each floor a grid of room slots (16-block pitch).
Generation is deterministic from `GatePlan{seed, theme, layout, modifiers, twist, floors, boss, contentVersion}`.
Rooms: start, normal, elite, cache, puzzle (some layouts), shrine (floor end), boss arena (last floor).
Everything picked up inside a gate goes to the **Satchel** (no slot limit, it never refuses; + Satchel XP; §13 Gates, "Gate spoils"). Shrine: Extract (bank + return to
gate mouth) or continue via the Seal to the next floor. Boss kill: claim + exit portal.
Gate encounters (2026-10-28 playtest; Codex, reviewed): the current room and its connected neighbours are populated before doorway
entry, within the existing 40-monster gate / 60-monster arena caps. A neighbour is prepared only once its chunks are
loaded (a preview never reads or loads a chunk, §38.1); stepping in prepares a room regardless. A company's size (party
scaling) is fixed when it is prepared. If the budget is full, the unspawned part of a
company waits in saved state, with its original party scaling and spawn index. It resumes when space becomes available,
without replacing any members already killed. A capped empty arena stays open and unfinished; cavern zones wait separately.
Prepared enemies wait visibly and alive, never frozen (orchestrator, 2026-10-28: Euan reported mobs that "just stopped
moving" as a bug, so no NoAI): their AI stays on, they take no target, and `gates.run.Dormant` (a top-priority move and
look goal) keeps them idling near their spot: breathing and swaying through their own idle clips, looking about, now
and then a shuffle or a stroll of up to 2.5 blocks, and walking back if they drift more than 4. Entering their room
(or damaging one from the same gate/floor) wakes that encounter, not its neighbours. A woken enemy first has a 14-tick
wake beat (`Encounters.WAKE_BEAT`): it stops, turns toward whoever woke it (what hit it, else the nearest player) and
cannot target yet; then it takes that player as its target and fights. The goal is not saved; loading a waiting enemy
attaches it again (and clears a NoAI an earlier build saved). Caverns prepare their 16-block
zones and wake only the entered zone; cleared zones also reject reinforcements. A room/zone may target within its
own bounds plus 8 blocks beyond its doorway;
floor-wide pressure enemies target within 32 blocks on their actual gate/floor. Arena bars still close on entry; only
the first wave is prepared, and the second follows its defeat. Stealth Hall sentries retain their existing patrols.
Prepared and triggered encounters are saved separately. Gate registry schema 3 saves pending companies and the living UUID roster, including
unloaded entities. Death removes membership before the corpse animation ends; restart/load order never means an
arena is empty and never recreates a saved Lord. Schema 2 rooms already triggered count as prepared on load. Cleared encounters remain cleared across leave/re-entry and relog.
Gate pressure: after 4 min on a floor, a wave every 45 s, scaling; at 8 min the gate's Warden (elite) can arrive.
Reinforcements and the Warden spawn only in engaged, unfinished rooms, never safe, cleared or merely previewed rooms.
A Warden is announced only after successful spawning. Its bar includes “Warden” (the Hive's Swarm Mind is a Warden,
not the final Lord). Gate bars require an engaged encounter on the player's actual gate/floor, within 32 blocks and
visible or actively targeting that player; a previewed or remote-floor Lord has no bar. Echoing's one rise and a
living boss's summons remain parts of their original fights.
States: BUILDING → READY → ACTIVE ⇄ OPEN → CLEARED | BROKEN → RELEASED (cell region files deleted on server stop).
Break: spill wave + roaming Gate Lord with boss bar at the gate; blight (desaturation + grey fog) within 96 blocks until
cleared; better loot. Warning one play-day ahead when within 256 blocks of a Hearth. The Gate Stabiliser pushes a break
back by play-days. After the "Break the Signal" ending no gate breaks; after "Wake up" there is no blight.
**Seen first** (Euan, 29 Oct 2026: "way too many gates breaking that I haven't even seen yet... a gate should only start
the timer if you've been close to it"): a gate's break clock starts the first time any player comes within 64 blocks
(`Breaks.SEEN_RADIUS`, about where the vortex reads clearly over the land; 3D distance from its ground block, checked once
a second). Any player's approach starts it, owner or not (the gate stands in everyone's world and whoever is near can
clear it); a spectator's never does, and Spirit Sight or a Gate Scanner reading from afar doesn't count. The clock then
runs the play-days it was rolled with (1-4 by rank, plus any Stabiliser days): `breaksOnPlayDay = seen day + (rolled break
day − created day)`. Until then the gate waits: it never warns or breaks, `GateRecord.waiting`/`counting` say so, and
every reader shows no clock (`GateView.breaksOnPlayDay` is `Long.MAX_VALUE`, `GateHooks.waiting(level, id)` tells a
waiting gate from a calm one; the Hearth's and a village's bells, the Grey Fields, Spirit Sight's card ("Not until
someone goes near it"), the Gate Scanner and its Atlas marks, the gate card, the Atlas's gate marks (beacon flag
`WAITING`), Jade and `/awaken gate info`'s timer line ("waits to be seen"). The Director's cap (4 standing gates per owner
within 1,500 blocks) counts waiting gates, so a waiting gate nobody visits folds away quietly after 7 play-days unseen
(`Breaks.UNSEEN_DAYS`, `GateRecord.foldsOnPlayDay`): no break, no Lord, no message. Saved as `seen_day` and `folds_on`
(gate registry schema 4); loading an older save sends every standing gate that can break back to unseen, folding 7
play-days from that load, and leaves broken ones as they are.
**Where a gate stands** (29 Oct 2026, Euan's save: gates 41-46 failed in a row, gate 40 showed a beam over nothing):
a gate replaces natural ground only, and that now includes the Awakened Lands' own (fused and scorched glass, sunshard,
riven shale, faultstone, fault seam, hoarfrost, frostspar, mirepeat, the Wild Lands' trodden earth, salt licks and
wallows) and the Soft Land's step slabs (`#awaken:gates_ground`). A bottom slab of a ground material lying on a natural
block is a soft step, never a build, so it no longer refuses the spot (every Soft Land footprint has some); a top slab,
or any other slab, still is someone's build. A step is good ground to stand on. The vortex's own column (the anchor
and its cores) always forms over whatever grew there unless it is a block entity or unbreakable. A gate stands when its
anchor core holds the vortex (`Overworld.stands`); a build whose vortex can't stand fails and comes down, with the real
reason in the trace ("a Hearth within 64 blocks", "someone's build in the footprint", "wet or open ground", "its vortex
had no room"). A loaded gate whose vortex is missing (an old doorway, or the anchor that Lands ground blocked before
this) is rebuilt once per server run, checked every 10 s; if it still can't stand it folds away quietly (a broken one,
or one with someone inside, is hidden instead). Every surface that shows a gate shows only one that stands (built, not
released, not fallen: `GateExterior.shown`): the pillar and the Atlas marks (beacons), Far Sight's pillars, the Now line,
the Horizon's first gate, `GateHooks.near` (Spirit Sight, the Gate Scanner, the bells, the villages) and `Gates.near`.
The first gate's "A gate has opened N m" waits until it stands, so a failed build never announced anything.

**Trees round a gate** (8 Nov 2026, Euan: "Trees above gates are floating"): the clearing takes what crosses the pad up to
3 blocks over the opening and tells nothing round it, so a tree it cut kept its crown and the top of its trunk in the air.
Now a tree the gate cut comes down whole (`Overworld.fellCut`, every rank and every tree in the game: test
`gates_trees_fall_whole`). A log stands if a line of wood (logs, a pale oak's Creaking Heart, a mangrove's roots) takes it
to the ground or to someone's build, and only something solid counts: what grows on bark (hanging moss, cocoa) doesn't, nor
does a stalk of bamboo. A leaf stands within the game's six steps of such a log, counted through leaves as the game does. What doesn't stand, within 14 blocks past the crater, goes, with
what grew on it (vines, snow, bee nests, the top of a stalk of bamboo). A tree that still stands only loses what the
clearing took. Leaves saved as persistent (the Wild Lands' hawthorn, someone's hedge) go only
when their piece touches nothing. The crater no longer burns the top of a short trunk as if it were ground. A gate built
before this comes down the same way once, the first time all its ground is loaded (`GateExterior.fellOld`, saved as
`trees_felled`); a gate that had already closed left no record, so a crown it left stays. The two dark blue-veined rocks
round a portal are the vortex's own shards (`GateVortex.emitShards`), drawn orbiting the rim on purpose.

Themes (15), layouts (8), modifiers (14), twists (8), bosses: exactly as in `docs/plan.html` gate generator.

Arrivals (§28.9, 2026-10-29): leaving a gate (cleared, failed, lost, or its gate gone at login) and `/awaken gates
frame|hop` wait for the overworld land off the server thread through `Passage.go`; the gate's own bookkeeping (released,
unsealed, beacons) runs whether the move does or is dropped. Going in doesn't wait: the interior is made first.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 8. The Descent

The Well: landmark structure within 400–700 blocks of world spawn (a Precursor ring around a deep shaft). Jumping in (or the
Well's lift) enters stratum 1. Strata = dimensions `awaken:stratum_1` … `awaken:stratum_10`, each its own generator +
biome + one rule; drops (portal pits) lead to the next. Endless = `awaken:endless` (cells, stacking rules).
Arrivals (§28.9, 2026-10-29): Descent travel (waystones, the climb, the camps) waits for its land through `Passage.go`
in place of its own portal ticket, and a death in the Descent warms the checkpoint camp's land for the wake there.
Rules: 1 none · 2 wind gusts · 3 rising water every 5 min · 4 the dead rise once · 5 sound draws Listeners ·
6 machines wake (power puzzles) · 7 gravity flips with the tides · 8 rooms change when unobserved · 9 your shadow fights you ·
10 the Seed (finale). Waystone per stratum: checkpoint + fast travel. Strain when climbing up without the Deep Lift:
−(5% × strata climbed) to all stats for 10 min, stacking. Grave Echo on death in the Descent holds the Satchel.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 9. Lucidium, Veil, Stillpoint

Lucidium: Day Journal captures ≤10 snapshots/day (≤64 kept) as structure templates ≤16×12×16 around salient events. At
dusk a DreamPlan is built; on sleep (dream chance 40% + SPI%, +bed/Sanctuary) the player enters a Lucidium cell for 3–8
min. Lucidity 0–100: reality check (H) +12 in dreams, dream sign spotted +15, intention set at bed +10 start, WBTB
(alarm block wakes you, sleep again within 1 in-game hour) +25 start, Recall stat (journal entries) +0.5/entry.
≥50 lucid: flight, intent-manifest (hold H on a wall: door/stair/bridge from snapshot palette). ≥80 summon from memory.
Dying in a dream: wake "Shaken" (no penalty). Not ready → normal sleep. Hold sneak while sleeping: dreamless.
Arrivals (§28.9, 2026-10-29): waking from a dream and the dream rescue wait for the bed's land through `Passage.go`;
going into a dream doesn't (the cell is built first).

**Dreams remade (2026-11-03, `docs/dreams/PLAN.md`, Euan approved all 12 decisions).** A dream is now a remembered
trial with one goal and a clock. The paragraph above is history: stage 4 removed the 40% roll, the islands of memory
(`DreamPlanner.plan`, the island `BlueprintCompiler`, `Imagined`, the swaps while nobody looks), lucid flight, shaping
and summoning (`Manifest` and its payload), and the nightmare and mentor at island nodes (the Chase and the Duel took
their place, §9.5). `Dreams.enter` refuses a plan with no course; an old plan with no trial compiles as the first dream;
`dream now`, `dream plan` and `Lucidium.startShared` dream the trial waiting (startShared: or the one finished last,
§9.6). Lucidity stays as a trial's starting seconds. No `dreamsRemade` flag (PLAN §6): the old path went by the same
delivery, so a flag would only have guarded a dream nobody plays.

### 9.1 Trials

`trial.Trial`: FIRST (the Dreaming Bell's dream, 75 s), Runs WALL, LEDGE, VAULT (stage 1), CLIMB (stage 2), ROPE, LEAP,
WINGS (stage 4, §9.6), Rooms WRONG, LOOK_AWAY, HUSH, FOLD, NO_DOOR (180 s), LONG_FALL (120 s) (§9.5), CHASE (120 s), DUEL (150 s). Each has one
goal line and a small line under it. A Run's course is laid by `trial.CourseKit` from RunnerRules' own probes (read only,
§12): every wall-run, wall jump, ledge hang and shimmy, vault and slide is proved by the same checks the movement makes,
and `TrialCompiler` tries four seeded variants then a plain road, so a plan always compiles. The solver's time from the
doorway to the goal is the par; a Run's clock is max(60, par × 1.8) s. `DreamPlan` v2 carries the trial id and a ref
(`bell:dreaming`); `DreamBlueprint` v2 the course (start, doorway, rings, end, bell spot, floor, par, path, reveals).

### 9.2 When a dream comes (the ledger)

`Dreamer` schema 2 adds `data.DreamLedger`: waiting (trial, ref, since, why), finished (best ticks, medal, day, times),
`lastDreamDay`, `lastNewDay`, the Journal's choice and its day. A dream comes **only when one waits**: at most one a
night, never two nights running unless chosen that day; new dreams join at most one a play-day (the first and old-save
seeding excepted); the Dream Bell's second sleep (WBTB) takes the next one regardless. `DreamOffers` fills it from the
level road's flag `awaken:dreams` (level 12): FIRST (with the Dreaming Bell when `BellHooks.dreamBellNext` says
`dreaming`), then after it the built Runs one a day; old dreamers are seeded with FIRST and up to two Runs. Sneak while
lying down: dreamless, as before. Tasks (OUT, BELLS when a bell waits): "A dream is waiting. Sleep in your bed
tonight." / "A bell is waiting in a dream. Sleep in your bed tonight."; never what it holds. While one waits, your own
bed sheds a few pearl motes at night (client, `DreamWaiting` payload).

### 9.3 The trial dream

- **Arrive** in your room: the Day Journal's latest HOME snapshot (else a kit bedroom), a doorway of dream glass, the
  course beyond, its end glowing far off. Dream signs as before (your personal sign and one other). No lucidity meter:
  one line, "You're dreaming. Press H to take control." ("Press H." after three dreams). The dream waits up to 5 min,
  and walking out past the doorway takes control too.
- **H takes control** (first H: `first_lucid`, lucid-dream count): the doorway clears, the goal line and a crescent
  clock show; the clock is the trial's seconds plus starting lucidity as seconds (cap 60), so every old source of
  lucidity still counts. The road lays itself ahead of you (24 blocks a tick, 14 ahead of your furthest step).
- **While lucid**: H glints the true path for 2 s at a cost of 2 s, once every 4 s; noticing a dream sign gives 8 s
  ("That's not right. +8 seconds"); falling 6 below the course floor is caught: back to the last ring passed, 3 s gone
  ("The dream caught you. 3 seconds gone."), never a wake, no fall damage in a trial. Rings: gold, the next one
  breathing; passing one counts it.
- **Ends**: the goal reached → the prize line for 3 s → wake WON ("You reached the end of the dream", time, medal, what
  you kept, "Your Dream Journal has written it down."). Clock out → SLIPPED ("The dream slipped away"); Esc's "Wake up"
  button (`WakeUp` payload, throttled, server checks dreaming) → CHOSE; both leave the dream waiting. Death, logout and
  the rest wake as before.
- **Keeps**: medals by the Gauntlet's rule (gold ≤ par × 1.1 + 1 s, silver ≤ par × 1.5 + 2 s, else bronze; Runs only);
  world XP 6% of a level the first finish, 2% another day; 2 Dream Residue (held while still in the Lucidium); counter
  `awaken:dreams_finished` (`first_dream` revelation fires on it). The Dreaming Bell's dream holds the bell at the end
  ("Take the bell first. It's just behind you."): `DreamBells` lets the lucidium place it (`Lucidium.dreamBell`) and
  `Lucidium.bellTaken` finishes the dream; no lucidity gate on that bell.
- **The Dream Journal writes itself**: "Write down the dream" and its two-minute window are gone. It shows whether a
  dream waits, each finished dream (best time, medal, times), the latest dreams and the places remembered. Recall in a
  trial is two entries per finished dream (a second each on the clock, cap 10 s), or an old save's written Recall if
  more.
- **Payloads**: `TrialStart` (goal, sub, rings, end, bell, path, dreams so far), `TrialHud` (phase, ticks left, total,
  ring, a line to flash, glint) once a second and on change, `DreamWaiting` (your bed or none), `WakeUp` (C→S); the
  dream HUD's `TRIAL` flag hides the meter. Look: `TrialHud` (crescent clock, rose in the last 10 s), `TrialRings` (own
  gold bands, not end rods), `PearlMoteParticle`, the Waking Veil and dream road blocks (`tools/art/specs/dreams.py`).
- **Tests**: `dreams_runs_solvable` (every built trial's first variant passes its own solver, with a bell and without),
  `dreams_waiting_ledger`, `dreams_arrival`, `dreams_clock`, `dreams_catch_never_wakes`, `dreams_wake_button`,
  `dreams_win`. Tour `tools/autopilot/dreams-first.txt` (admin `/awaken dream offer <trial>`, `control` = H, `ring <n>`;
  past the last ring, the goal).

### 9.4 Runs: what the body keeps

- **Moves remembered**: the first finish of a Run remembers its moves for the body (`Trial.moves()`: the wall: wall-run
  and wall jump; the ledge: hang, shimmy, ledge jump; over and under: vault and slide; the climb: wall climb and grip;
  the rope, leap and wings name their Ascent tiers). `MovementHooks.remember` sets `BodyMemory.remembered` (schema 2,
  synced to its owner) and THE BODY says "Remembered in a dream." under each. The prize line: "Your body remembers the
  wall-run."; the morning card adds the move to "You kept" and says how to do it awake (`Trial.how`). The tip that
  teaches it awake counts done (`ascent/freerun`, `rope`, `leaper`, `wings`).
- **Mastery**: 50 points on the Run's Ascent track the first finish, 50 the first gold (`MovementHooks.addMastery`,
  `AscentServer.addMastery`: no chain link).
- **Ghosts**: the best run of each Run is kept (`DreamLedger.ghosts`: a sample every 4 ticks from the doorway, ≤ 750,
  packed in quarter blocks from the course's start); replays show it (§9.6).
- **The climb** (Wall Stride held): faces 5 or 6 high run up into the lip's hang (`CourseKit.climbUp`, proved by the
  body's own climb tick by tick: `climbTarget`, `wallOn`, `findEdge`; a plain jump must not reach the lip), and faces
  with a Dream Ribbon up their middle (`DreamRibbonBlock`, a climb line in `awaken:runner_climbs`; proved by
  `GripRules.find`, `climbTop`, `topLip`, then `climbOut`). The tower grows: the faces rise out of the road as you come.
  The door is at the top.
- **Tests**: `dreams_move_remembered` (the wall remembered once, the ghost kept, a sample packs and unpacks); the climb in
  `dreams_runs_solvable`. Tour `tools/autopilot/dreams-runs.txt`.

### 9.5 Rooms, bells, the Chase and the Duel (stage 3)

A Room has one dream rule, shared by everyone in the dream (`dream.RoomRules`); its layout is laid by `trial.RoomLayouts`
after the doorway (a `Course.Room`: the floor's middle and reach, where the goal first stands or null while the rule
hides it, the rule's things, no door's walls, the fold's loop, the fall's edge, the hidden place's spot). A Room's goal
may move: `ActiveDream.roomGoal`, the small Waking Door laid again where it goes, the end's light following
(`TrialGoal` payload: shown or not, where). The clock: a Room 180 s (the long fall 120 s), the Chase 120 s, the Duel
150 s. A Room won is won for everyone in it in control (phase 1).

| Rule | Goal line (no bell / with its bell) | Rule | Fail |
|---|---|---|---|
| What's wrong here (`wrong`) | "Three things in this place are wrong. Look at each one and press H." / "... Find them all, and the bell will be there." | today's place (the latest Day Journal snapshot of today or yesterday, a home only if nothing else; else a pale courtyard) in a plaza, with three wrong things on spots round it: a door a block off the ground with no wall, a floating grass block, a lantern on a chain that ends in the air. Look at one (9°, 40 blocks) and press H. Looking at the sky, H glints them | a guess at nothing costs 5 s |
| Look away (`look_away`) | "The door moves whenever you look away from it. Reach it." / "The bell moves whenever you look away from it. Catch it." | once in view (60°), out of view and over 3 away, it moves 16 to 28 from you on the plaza (8 to 16 if the plaza's too small) | none |
| Hush (`hush`) | "Something is asleep by the door. Get to the door without waking it." / "... next to the bell. Take the bell without waking it." | a nightmare (generic family, no AI, silent, breathing clouds) beside the goal; within 12 not sneaking, or 18 sprinting, wakes it: it hunts you (at most 3 awake, the oldest fades) and the goal moves, a new sleeper beside it | it comes for you |
| The long fall (`long_fall`) | "You're falling. Find a way to land." | the road ends at an edge over nothing; 8 below it, falling with your eyes down (over 40°) lifts you 10 ("The fall goes on for as long as you watch it."); eyes up (under 15°) lays a landing 6 below you and the goal on it. Caught only 60 deeper than the floor | none |
| The fold (`fold`) | "This hallway keeps coming back. Find the way out of it." | a 30-long lamp-lit hallway; past 24 you're back 18 ("You've passed that door before.", then "Try walking backwards past the door you keep passing."); walking backwards (moving against where you look) past the pane of dream glass in its east wall opens it onto a short way to the Waking Door | none |
| No door (`no_door`) | "There's no door. Make one." | a sealed room (the way in closes behind you); H looking at a wall (14 blocks) makes a door in it; the right wall's (a draft of pearl motes through it) leads to the Waking Door, the others into more wall | none |

- **The Chase** (`chase`): a road with gaps and steps; once someone's past the doorway, 2 of your fear (3 from C rank)
  spawn behind you in your room (`MobHooks.spawnThemed`, the family's theme and tags, level 80% of your content
  level), hunting the nearest dreamer. The fear is the ref's (`fear:<family>`), else the week's worst, else something
  hunting you in the dark. With the Nightmare's Bell the first carries it ("Your fear is coming after you, and it's
  carrying a bell. Take the bell from it."); felled, the bell lies where it fell; the door says "Take the bell first.
  Your fear is carrying it."
- **The Duel** (`duel`): a ring of dream glass on a plaza; step within 8 of its middle and your Path's mentor comes
  (`Mentors.start(ad, feet, player, trial)`: "Show me what you've learned."). Worn down (its blows stop at 3 health):
  "Not yet. Catch your breath, and again." 10 s gone, the mentor back 3 s later. It yields at 35% health: won for
  everyone in control.
- **Bells** (the six keep their count; `DreamBells` keeps their words and the Book's Dreamt leads): the Dreaming Bell
  is the first Run's; the Daydream Bell is Look away's, the Lullaby Bell Hush's, the Falling Bell the long fall's, the
  Nightmare's Bell the Chase's, the Lucid Bell What's wrong here's (found all three: "Now there's a bell where there
  wasn't one."). `Lucidium.DreamBell(id, at, carrier)`: `at` where it stands now (null while the rule hides it),
  `carrier` the Chase's fear holding it. `DreamBells.follow` (every other tick) sets the Sleeping Bell where the dream
  says, clears it while hidden, puts it in the carrier's hand (no drop), and sets it again for a shared dreamer when
  someone else took theirs. A bell's dream is won by striking it (no lucidity gate); the old dream puzzles stay only for
  a dream that isn't a trial.
- **Hidden places**: a Room carrying `vision:<id>` (the visions finder's place: an unvisited surface structure 160 to
  1,400 away, or an old remembered place) shows it beyond a window of dream glass at the far side, on its own island,
  undistorted. Won: "Look through the glass. That place is real, and it's in your world." Waking:
  `Visions.reveal` (the Journal's Visions, with which way it lies from your bed), `AtlasHooks.reveal` (40 round it) and
  a pearl mark on the Atlas (`DreamPlaces` payload → `MapMarks`, faded once found); "You saw a real place: <label>.
  It's on your map now. <hint>". Everyone in the dream gets it (a guest a copy of the host's). Walking up to it awake
  is found, as before (`awaken:secrets_found`).
- **Prizes on waking**: a Room "You found your way through the dream"; the Chase "You got away from your fear" / "You
  took the bell from your fear", its fear let go (`nightmares_beaten`, that family's weekly counters and death marks
  cleared, +10% of a level); the Duel "Your mentor yielded" (+20% of a level, `awaken:mentor_duels_won`). World XP and
  residue as every finish.
- **What waits** (`DreamOffers.check`, after the first dream; one new a play-day, in this order): the next dream bell your
  rank has reached (`bell:<id>` on its dream; one bell waits at a time); the next Run; a place the finder has ready, in
  the next Room in turn (`PLACE_ROOMS`: fold, no door, look away, hush, what's wrong here); the Chase once one family
  killed you twice this week (`fear:<family>`); the Duel once you have a Path, 3 play-days after the last. Stale waits
  drop: a bell you hold or one no longer next, a place shown or gone, a fear with no deaths left. A bell or a place is
  given once (`DreamLedger.given`); a waiting dream carrying something else than tonight's shared one stays waiting.
- **The Dream Journal's choice**: "Tonight I want to... learn a move / find something hidden / face my fear / find a
  bell" (the last only while one waits): the oldest waiting of that kind (run, room, chase, bell) comes first, and asks
  for a dream a night after the last. It lasts into the next play-day and is spent when a dream begins; it also counts
  as an intention (+10 s).
- **Commands** (admin, tours): `/awaken dream offer <trial> [bell:<id> | vision | fear:<family>]`, `/awaken dream solve`
  (one step of the rule as a player would: the next wrong thing named, the right wall's door, the fold walked
  backwards, the fall looked up from, the mentor coming or yielding, the carrier felled; then to the goal).
- **Tests**: `dreams_room_rules` (each rule's mechanism, the bells' API, the Chase's door, the Duel to its morning),
  `dreams_hidden_place`, `dreams_shared`. Tour `tools/autopilot/dreams-rooms.txt`.

### 9.6 Replays, ghosts and the dream's sounds (stage 4)

- **Replays**: every trial you've finished can be dreamt again, the one finished last first (`DreamOffers.replays`; the
  Dream Recorder lists eight, "The wall: best 0:42, gold", through `DreamHooks.recorded`; the Stillpoint's In door
  opens onto index 0 and glows while one is there). A replay's plan carries the ref `replay` (`DreamLedger.REPLAY`): no
  bell, no place, no fear's name; it spends neither tonight's dream nor the Journal's choice and takes nothing off the
  waiting list. Its time, medal (a first gold's mastery too) and ghost count; world XP 2% and the 2 residue only on a
  later play-day than the last finish; no fear let go or mentor's lesson again. The sub line says your best ("Your best:
  0:42, silver. Your ghost runs it with you."). Version-1 dreams in the history are no longer replayed.
- **One a night**: a dream that isn't a replay sets `lastDreamDay` for everyone who arrives in it (the ledger's "one a
  night, not two running" reads it).
- **Ghosts**: the moment you pass a Run's doorway the server sends `TrialGhosts` (the course's start and up to four
  ghosts: your best run, and in a shared dream the best runs of the others in it). The client plays each from there,
  a sample every 4 ticks interpolated: a soft standing figure of light with a short trail, pearl for yours and rose for
  a friend's, lingering half a second at its end (`TrialRings.ghost`).
- **Sounds** (`tools/art/specs/audio_dreams.py`, all mono, the dream's own): `dream.catch` (an airy swoop and two slow
  heartbeats: the catch), `dream.tick` (the clock's last ten seconds, client side: every half second slowing to every
  second, a little lower and louder each time), `dream.ring` (a ring passed, pitched up ring by ring), `dream.won` (the
  end reached: a warm rising chord).
- **The air's Runs** (each waits once its Ascent tier is yours: `Ascent.has` TETHER, LEAPER, WINGS; old worlds are
  seeded with them like the rest, §9.2). Proved like the ground's, by the Ascent's own rules at mastery 0 holding forward
  (`trial.AirProofs` over `trial.CourseSpace`, a `SwingSpace` answered from the course's blocks before any are placed),
  each also proving a plain sprint jump falls short and that the landing is on the far road, not past it:
  - **The rope** (`CourseKit.swing(len, up, ahead)`): a gap under a lantern of dream light (3 wide, 2 high, 3 deep: big
    enough for the rope's fan from anywhere on the jump), thrown at 2 and at 9 ticks into the jump (`AscentSwing.find`,
    `entry`, `travel`, then `tick` from the catch to the arc's top, every tick tried as the key's let-go with `letGo` and
    `carryStep`; the held rope, §62, lets go only by the key): both must land, the landing best in the window kept; the
    top is the last tried (where the rope once let go by itself), so a gap laid for that let-go still proves. A swing
    carries about 27 from the take-off whatever the gap, and needs open air under the arc, so the gaps are 22-24 with 9
    of road after. Layout: road 8, swing 22 (lantern 14 up, 6 on), swing 24 (14, 8), swing 22 (16, 8); par 17 s.
  - **The leap** (`CourseKit.leap(len, rise)`): the sprint jump, the double jump near its top; the air dash as it falls
    only if the double jump alone comes down short. Reach at mastery 0: double jump about 6.8 flat; with the dash 12.4
    flat, 8.9 two up, 16.5 four down; nothing three up. Layout: 6 flat (the double jump alone), 8 flat, 6 two up, 10
    flat, 12 four down; par 13 s.
  - **The wings** (`CourseKit.glide(len, drop)`): the road ends at a cliff; an island (7 wide, 14 long, clouds under its
    ends) `drop` below and `len` on, three rings of light in the air between (a fall from any is caught back at the
    cliff). Proved by falling 3 ticks, `glideCatch`, then `glideStep` looking at the island's middle until the feet
    touch it (a glide this way lands at 1.6 to 2 times its drop). Layout: 30 on and 20 down, then 40 on and 24 down; par
    12 s.
  The twists the plan named for these (anchors lighting in reach, drifting islands, updraft columns) are not built: the
  air Runs are the plain proved layouts. All three Runs' clocks are the 60 s floor.
- **The goal line** sits under any boss plates (the sleeper's and the Chase's fears are NIGHTMARE plates;
  `CustomizeGuiOverlayEvent.BossEventProgress` gives their bottom each frame) and wraps to fit between the corners'
  panels (`TrialHud.goal`), so a plate never covers it and the right-hand panel never cuts it.
- **Hush's solve** (`/awaken dream solve`): a step that lands you by the sleeper is a sneak's step; it sleeps on for 5 s
  (`ActiveDream.roomQuietUntil`) while you take the next.
- **Old saves**: a player asleep mid-dream at the update (an island dream) is woken at login where they lay, its
  flight taken back, and the ledger is seeded on the next check (the new first dream and up to two Runs the body can
  do); nothing of the old dream can be replayed.
- **Tests**: `dreams_replay` (listed, no bell, nothing spent, the time counted, nothing taken off the list, no residue
  twice a day); the air Runs in `dreams_runs_solvable`; `dreams_upgrade` (the old save's wake and seeding).

Veil: sneak + G held 10 s, still, not in combat → Body (mannequin-like entity with skin + gear, chunk ticket) +
player switched to spectator-backed spirit mode with cord radius (SPI). Awareness fog radius = PER/SPI derived. Ores and
secrets glow within Awareness (client-only highlight, server-sent positions). Only blue-tagged `veil_interactable` things
can be used. Body hit → Warning + snap back offered; body killed → player killed. Logout → snap back first.
Stillpoint dimension `awaken:stillpoint`: void + cloud sea + dawn temple platform; time ×10 slower feel (no hunger, no
mobs). Hub for stats, Truths, Codex; doors Out (Veil) and In (the dream you finished last, dreamt again; §9.6). Hosts trial arenas.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 10. Above, Hearth, Story

Above: Precursor Vaults/sky platforms/ocean labs/monoliths; Scanner reads broken machines → Codex blueprint; machines
built at home from 3–5 parts; Essence power from a reactor within 32 blocks. Machines: Gate Scanner, Gate Stabiliser,
Waypoint Pylon, Deep Lift, Frame Forge, Clone Vat, Dream Recorder, Signal Relay, Recalibrator, Observatory, Launch Ring.
Halo dimension `awaken:halo`: orbital station, low gravity, archive with the truth.

Hearth: Anchor block (crafted from first boss essence) defines a 48-block radius base. Rooms detected by contents:
Sanctuary (bed + meditation mat), Armory (anvil + forge + rack), Trophy Hall (≥1 trophy), Workshop (≥1 machine),
Barracks (role pads). Town NPCs arrive by rank: Blacksmith (E), Scout (D), Archivist (C), Healer (B), Rival (A).
Echoes: bind fallen elites/bosses (B key within 10 s, chance by SPI and rank), cap by SPI, roles at home via role pads
(Guard, Haul, Farm, Mine, Train). Costs of Hearth upgrades fall 15% per rank above the upgrade's tier.

Story: prologue (scripted Bell Crypt → death → Stillpoint "Will you accept?" → Accept/Accept), Acts I–III gated by rank,
Revelations via Signal, Codex rumour board, the Rival's beats at D/C/B/A/S, endings at the Seed (Become / Break / Wake),
then New Game+ "Ascension" tiers.

Arrivals (§28.9, 2026-10-29): pylon jumps, the Halo and its return pad, and the Clone Vat's wake wait for their land
through `Passage.go` (`Travel.teleport`); a pylon whose land isn't loaded is checked on arrival, and its essence given
back if it's gone. A Hearth trial's way home waits the same way, and a fall warms the Hearth's land for the respawn
(§28.10).

## 12. Cross-module public API (stable)

- `dev.awaken.signal.Signal` — `send(ServerPlayer, SignalWindow)`, `toast(ServerPlayer, Component)`,
  `toast(ServerPlayer, Component, Notices.Tier, String topic)`; `SignalWindow.Builder.tier/topic/moment` (§26).
  `SignalWindow.Builder.dialogue()` marks NPC speech (choices keep their action); `SignalWindow.dialogue()` reads it.
  `dev.awaken.signal.Finds` — `tell(ServerPlayer, Find)`: how a new find is told (lesson, moment, first of kind, filed).
- `dev.awaken.core.api.NoticeEvents` (§26.3c) — owning modules publish `tell(player, Event)` or
  `remember(player, Event)` when an existing scene already explains the event. `Event(id, category, name, summary,
  details, kind, colour)` carries authored semantics, not text inferred from a toast; kind is PERMANENT, COMBAT,
  DISCOVERY, REWARD or TASK. Stable ids deduplicate repeat delivery; separate reward occurrences get separate ids.
  Signal installs the server sink and owns saved history, sync, unread state and presentation.
- `dev.awaken.progression.RewardWords` — `grants(Reward)`, `describe(Reward)`, `perk(Perk)` and `perks(List<Perk>)`:
  explicit common reward/perk wording shared with the existing reward cards; unknown or currently inactive perk
  effects are identified honestly. `RewardHooks.powerName` is installed by powers alongside its existing learner.
- `dev.awaken.core.api.Notices` (§26) — `enum Tier {CRITICAL, IMPORTANT, AMBIENT}`; client: `claim(tier, topic)` before
  a module's own HUD line takes the screen, `file(tier, title, line)` into the Journal, `quiet()`, `hold(owner, bool)`.
- `dev.awaken.progression.Progression` — `profile(Player)`, `grantXp(ServerPlayer, double, XpSource)`, `count(ServerPlayer,
  Identifier, long)`, `markNewThing(ServerPlayer, String what)`, `rank(Player)`, `stat(Player, Stat)`, `contentLevel(rank)`.
- `dev.awaken.powers.Powers` — `learn(ServerPlayer, Identifier power, int variant)`, `energy(Player)`, `forcesOf(DamageSource)`.
- `dev.awaken.gates.Gates` — `gateAt(...)`, `activeRun(ServerPlayer)`, `isInGate(Entity)`, `satchelAdd(...)`, `preview(id)`.
- `dev.awaken.core.Forces` — force/environment tags on entities and damage.
- `dev.awaken.core.PlayDays` — current play-day counter.
- `dev.awaken.mobs.Mobs` — `spawnScaled(ServerLevel, EntityType, pos, level, modifiers)`, rosters by theme.
- `dev.awaken.mobs.Ritual` — the Ritual of the Bell's cast: `spawnSeated`, `spawnStatue` (stages set on the entities).
  Presentation reads `walkSeconds(Entity, partial)` (the same distance phase used by the renderer), `walking`,
  `windingUp` and `plantedFoot`; story audio never reaches into the mob renderer or changes its gait.
- `dev.awaken.gates.Gates` (ritual) — `ritualPlan(seed)`, `ritualHall(server, gateId)` (`RitualHall`: every position in
  the hall), `isRitual(server, gateId)`.
- `dev.awaken.gates.Gates` (trials) — `leaperTrialPlan(seed)`: the Leaper's Gauntlet's plan, opened with
  `openScripted(player, plan)` (§17.10). `dev.awaken.core.api.TrialHooks` — `atEdge(player, trial)`, `done(player, trial,
  ticks, medal)`, installed by the Ascent.
- `dev.awaken.body.Body` — `unlocked(Player, Move)`, `isSliding`, `isTacticalSprinting`, `isMantling`, `lastMoveTick` (both sides).
- `dev.awaken.body.ascent.Ascent` — the Ascent's ladder (§17): `enum Tier {TETHER, LEAPER, WINGS, SKYBORN, SOVEREIGN}`,
  `has(Player, Tier)` (both sides), `highest(Player)`, `grant(ServerPlayer, Tier, String source)` (grants that tier and
  every one under it, saved, synced; true when new), `onGranted(BiConsumer<ServerPlayer, Tier>)` (each new tier once,
  lowest first), `state(ServerPlayer)` (`AscentState`), `arrivedByMovement(ServerPlayer, int seconds ≤ 20)` (a third
  of the stretch in a rope, glide, flight, wall-run or hang, and no block placed: a tower never counts).
  `core.api.MovementHooks.wallRunning(Player)` / `hanging(Player)` read the Runner's moves, `stairSliding(Player)` a
  slide down stairs (§17.22; `sliding` is true too). `core.api.AirHooks`
  (`register(Source)`, `Source.airAt(Level, x, y, z, double[] out)`): moving air the free states feel (§17.6).
  `core.api.CameraHooks` (client): `installToggle(BooleanSupplier)`, `toggleView()` (the View key asks it first; with
  Shoulder Surfing it flips first person and the shoulder view, §17.13), `zoom()` / `installZoom(DoubleSupplier)` (the
  binoculars' magnification now, 1 when none, §39: Far Sight's panorama steps aside while it is over 1.05).
  `core.api.FarGround` (client): `install(Sampler, BooleanSupplier ready)`, `ground(x, z)` (the far land's ground top, NaN when
  unknown; thread-safe, sampled off the render thread), `ready()` (the far land drew lately). Far Sight installs it (§39.8).
  `core.api.Spotting` (server): `register(Source)`, `sources()`; `Source.moves()`, `gather(player, reach, Sink)`, `find(player,
  ref)`; `Sink.place(key, bounds, ref)`, `Sink.entity(entity, ref)`: what the binoculars can spot (§39.10). Fauna, landmarks
  and wonders register sources.
- `dev.awaken.terrain.api.BiomeTable` — `archetype(Holder<Biome>)` (the vanilla biome an Awakened one stands in for, else
  its own key), `tag(String path)` (the table's `awaken:` biome tags: `fauna/`, `has_lair/`, `lair_style/`, `cottage/`).
- `dev.awaken.terrain.api.CityBasin` / `CitySite` — the city basin (§15): `request(Predicate<MinecraftServer>)` (the city's
  rule, once at mod init), `site(server)` (centre, core and blend radii, street Y, the river's centre line, whether the
  basin is carved), `reserved(x, z)` (inside the core plus 48: thread-safe, allocation-free; worldgen and runtime
  placement keep out), constants `STREET_Y` 70, `CORE_RADIUS` 330, `BLEND_RADIUS` 700, `RIVER` (the city's fixed path).
- `dev.awaken.terrain.alpine.Erosion` / `AlpineSurface` — Awakened Alpine's erosion and snow-and-rock rule as pure,
  allocation-free maths (§15): `Erosion.erode(x, z, gx, gz, strength, finestCell, out)`, `AlpineSurface.snowLine/snow/
  stone/erosionStrength/strata` (`strata(x, y, z)`: the rock layer there, 0-4, which the road banks read too, §28.9). Far Sight predicts and shades with the same numbers; its shaders mirror them.
- `dev.awaken.city.City.skyline(layout, chunkX, chunkZ, worldSeed, topY[256], top[256])` — the city as planned over one
  chunk, from the plan alone (any thread): each column's highest placed block and its world y, or none where the city
  leaves the land; false outside the city. Far Sight's far skyline reads it (§20).
- `dev.awaken.terrain.city.CityBasinFunction.Shape.ground(natural, x, z)` — the basin's ground height over a column
  whose natural ground stands at `natural` (what the density mode builds), for far terrain.
- `dev.awaken.hearth.Hearth` — a Hearth's owner and members ("Together"): `record HearthInfo(owner, ownerName, anchor,
  tier, radius, members, foundedFrom)` with `has(UUID)`, `hearthsOf(MinecraftServer, UUID)` / `hearthsOf(ServerPlayer)`,
  `home(ServerPlayer)`, `isMember(ServerPlayer, BlockPos anchor)`, `isMember(MinecraftServer, UUID player, UUID owner)`,
  `hearthAt(ServerLevel, BlockPos)`; plus `anchor`, `atHome`, `hasRoom`, `isSanctuary`, `inRoom` (`ownedEchoes` went with the Echoes, §43.4).
  (W6, §28.8) `record Village(owner, name, anchor, radius, tier, people, gather, bell)` and `villages(MinecraftServer)`: homes
  grown to Tier IV+ (the festival's and caravans' hook); a home's people run on the people engine as settlement
  `hearth:<owner>`. `core.api.HearthHooks` gained `greenhouse(Level, BlockPos)` (both sides) and `study(ServerPlayer)`.
- `dev.awaken.citizens.api.Settlements` — the people engine's settlements (§28.4; overworld, server thread):
  `register(ServerLevel, SettlementSpec)` (or the running one with that key), `unregister(id)` (never Carillon),
  `at(Level, BlockPos)` (the smallest that contains it), `byId(id)`, `all()`, `bodies(id)`; `CARILLON` 0 / `"carillon"`.
  `record SettlementSpec(key, name, origin, radius, RosterSource source, plannedEvents)`. View `Settlement`: `id`, `key`,
  `name`, `origin`, `inside(BlockPos)`, `people`, `bodies`, `awake`, `standing(Player)` (RenownHooks tiers, its own
  memory), `stations(String placeKindOrLotTag)`, `district(BlockPos)`. `RosterSource.build()` → `Built(roster, graph,
  lots, water, districts)`; `RosterSource.jar()` is Carillon's; `RosterBuilder` builds one in code (nodes, streets, lots,
  places with spots, routes, smithy, wash place, lamp, bell, bakery, tavern, stall, households, groups, people and their
  days, extras).
  (W3, §28.6) `Settlements.onTalk(Talk)` (a settlement other than Carillon answers a player's talk first: `talk(ServerPlayer,
  Settlement, rec)`), `Settlements.installVoice(Voice)` (`standing(Settlement, ServerPlayer)` "stranger|known|friend|kin",
  `fill(Settlement, ServerPlayer, line)`); `Settlement.records()`, `job(rec)`, `personName(rec)`, `age(rec)`, `body(rec)`,
  `say(ServerPlayer, rec, line, ticks)`, `acquaint(ServerPlayer, amount, ceiling)`; `RosterBuilder.emitter(x, ry, z, kind)`
  (0 bakery, 1 house, 2 tavern, 3 forge, 6 mill, 7 well) and `RosterSource.Built.emitters`.
  (W6, §28.8) `RosterBuilder.Person.face(String)`: a face of their own outside Carillon, `skin:<texture>[:slim][;<title>]` or
  `as:<settlement key>#<record>` (the roster's `named` field; synced as the body's skin and the word under its name).
- `dev.awaken.village.api.Villages` (§28.6) — AWAKEN's settlements: `record View(key, name, kind, family, origin, radius,
  settlement, people)`, `settlementAt(Level, BlockPos)`, `nearest(Level, BlockPos, within)`, `all(Level)`,
  `standing(ServerPlayer, key)` (STRANGER 0, KNOWN 1, FRIEND 2, KIN 3), `addStanding(ServerPlayer, key, points, why)`,
  `damage(server, key)` (`record Damage(pos, original, day)`), `repaired(server, key, pos)`, `history(server, key)` and
  `history(server, key, line)`, `prosperity`/`addProsperity`, `mood`/`addMood` (0-100), `reserved(Level, BlockPos,
  margin)` (a settlement's ground, planned ones included: gates and Hearths keep off).
- `dev.awaken.finds.api.Monuments` (§64.3) — `near(ServerLevel, x, z, margin)`: whether a column lies on a monument's
  ground (everything within its reach) or within a margin of it. Pure from the seed, any thread, no land made; the
  first ask of a stretch of country runs the search for its monuments' spots, so a planner asks from its own thread.
  For whatever is laid across the land (a road, a yard) to keep off a monument; nothing calls it yet.
- `dev.awaken.village.api.Troubles` (§28.7, W4) — who a player brought home from a trouble: `rescued(ServerPlayer)` →
