    part, 25% a worn iron sword) and scattered bone blocks; the remains stay.
  - The Rolling Storm (day/dusk): a cell crossing 180 blocks in 4 min; visual lightning out of its rain core (within 20
    blocks of a point 12 downwind of its centre) about every 3 s; 3 damage within 4 blocks of a strike; struck sand
    turns to glass. Its look, local weather and thunder: "The Rolling Storm, as a real storm" below.
  - The Wild Hunt (full moon only, night, bands 1+): five wisp hounds and the Huntmaster (an elite four levels up,
    titled "Huntmaster of the Pale Moon") run 220 blocks; they go for anyone within 18; each hound drops 2 essence, the
    Huntmaster 6. Beast Duel (bands 1+): two named beasts fight; the winner is left at 45% health.
  - The Deep Tide (new moon only, dusk/night, 10 min): fog out of a broken gate within 300 (else open ground); while it's
    up the night's hunters, elites and camps are two levels harder everywhere (`Regions.creatureLevel`).
  - Caravan (day, weight 0.4, ×1.5 on the half moons): a wandering trader ("Caravan Master") and 2-3 trader llamas
    walk about 100 blocks of road and pass by in 75 s; trade as usual. (12 Nov 2026, Euan: it came too often and stayed
    for six minutes ringing bells round his Hearth; it was weight 1.5, ×3, 160 blocks in 6 min, bells heard to 160.) 40% are ambushed halfway by 3-4 pillagers; if the master lives, everyone within 40 gets
    0.15 of a level (budget "pulse", 0.15 per 10 min) and 4 emeralds.
- **Tells** (payload `living_happenings`: id, tell, centre, radius, progress, line direction; to players within 512
  every 2 s, an empty list once when the last goes). `living.client.PulseFx` draws them in an alpha pass (unfogged,
  reads by day) and an additive pass, the centre eased over the 2 s; past 70% of the render distance a tell is pulled
  in along its sight line and shrunk to match (as the gate pillars). The storm tell is a cell of its own (below), never
  pulled in.
- **The Almanac**: within a kind's `witness_radius` a player witnesses it once: counter `awaken:happenings_witnessed`;
  the first time a discovery `happening/<id>` (0.1 of a level), a new thing for the Director, and "Witnessed · <title>".
  The Codex tab lists them ("HAPPENINGS WITNESSED · n / ??").
- **Rumours** (`Rumours`, attachment `awaken:rumours`, schema 1, synced to the owner, kept through death): half the
  time a Wayfarer with nothing for you tells of a happening on now 160-2500 blocks away that you haven't witnessed, with
  a compass direction; it leaves a "? <title>" mark on the Atlas (MapMarks) for two play-days (at most 8).
- Dev (admin): `/awaken living happen <kind>`, `happenings`, `calm`, `strike <distance>` (a storm strike that far
  ahead of you, for tours). Tests `living_pulse`, `living_storm`.
- **The Rolling Storm, as a real storm** (Euan's playtest, 2026-10-26: the cell read as round soft discs full of
  artifacts, its rain as moving white pillars of light, and it wasn't a real storm; he liked the bolts and their sound).
  One model both sides share, `living.pulse.StormCell` (sizes match `lens_storm.glsl`):
  - **The cell, a cumulonimbus**: its base 92 blocks over the ground its centre first stood on (140-215), 300 blocks
    from base to the anvil's top. A flat dark shelf at the base (the condensation level, flat to a block or two),
    125 in radius with a ragged rim, wider than the tower that rises from it and 14-34 deep (the orchestrator's review:
    the underside read as rounded and lumpy). A broad tower (95 radius at the base, narrowing a third toward the top,
    leaning 35 downwind) of cauliflower turrets (cellular "puffs" at 50 and 20 blocks, rising 0.35 blocks a second through it,
    so it boils), its axis wandering and its girth swelling and pinching with height, big lobes on some sides; an
    overshooting dome over the updraft; a flanking line of three smaller towers stepping down upwind (170, 118, 78
    high); a flat-topped anvil plate reaching 340 downwind, 70 upwind and 185 across, 78 deep where the tower spreads
    into it and thin at its rim (underside at 230 + 58 × r^0.55, top at 308 − 3r), its edges fibrous streaks along the
    wind (ice, not puffs); 260 by 150 read as a pale blob in profile. Its rain: a core of soft shafts 58 in radius, 12 downwind
    of the centre, slanting downwind as it falls (0.3 blocks a block), to the ground. Downwind is the way it travels.
    It builds over its first 12 s and rains itself out over its last 15 (the client times the end by the storm's 240 s).
  - **Drawn by Lens 2 on Cinematic and Ultra** (§22 "Storm cells"): marched in Lens's cloud volume. Elsewhere (Lens off,
    Swift, a shaderpack) by `living.client.StormFallback`: the same shape, built off-thread once per storm into 12-block
    cloud cells, 8 blocks (96 × 45 × 96, density over 0.45), opaque and face-shaded as the game's clouds are (top 1,
    sides 0.8-0.9, base 0.62), each lit by how much cloud lies eight cells toward the sun (exp(-0.45 per cell)), the sky's
    light mostly the game's cloud brightness (30% of its hue: its sunset tint on every face read as terracotta), dim and
    cold at the base, the sun's warm colour on faces turned to it, lit from inside by its lightning, hazed toward the sky colour
    with distance (1400 blocks); only outer faces turned to the camera are sent (about 3,000-4,000 quads). It grows from the
    base up as it builds and rains out from the top down (each cell's threshold by its height and a hash; faces rebuilt
    off-thread per 32nd of strength). Its rain: nine curved sheets fixed in the world round the core (arcs at set radii
    and angles), slanting downwind, the texture `living/storm_rain` (soft streaks, `tools/art/specs/storm_rain.py`)
    sliding down at about 19 blocks a second (Euan saw it flow up at first), faded at their ends, top and foot, dark grey, in the game's own fog (the weather pipeline). No
    camera-facing discs or billboards (the old `PulseFx.storm` is gone); nothing popped in from beyond the render
    distance either: the cell stands where it is, as the game's clouds do.
  - **Its local weather** (`living.client.StormSky`): this client's rain and thunder levels rise to
    `weatherAt(d)` (full within 45 blocks of the rain core's centre, none past 110, smooth between) × its strength,
    held in sixths (`StormCell.weatherStep`: it moves to a new sixth only once the wanted weather is more than 0.65 of a
    sixth past the held one, then eases there over 0.75 s), never below the server's own weather (followed if the server changes it while overriding) and handed back as you
    leave. So under and near it the game's own rain falls on you and sounds, the sky, fog, clouds and light darken as in
    a vanilla thunderstorm, terrain's wind steadies higher (rain and thunder lift it), the world sound hears rain, and
    Lens dims its sun. Lens's cloud layer doesn't thicken for this rain (`StormSky.localRain`): the cell is the cloud
    over you. Storms show only in the overworld while the Living Wilds are shown.
  - **Its thunder**: the server's visual bolts stay (and the game's sky flash). The game sends a bolt only to 256 blocks,
    so each strike also sends `living_storm_strike` (its position) to players within 640 (`StormCell.HEARD`): a far
    storm still flashes and thunders. On the client a bolt or that word within 90 blocks of a cell is its strike (the
    second of the two for one strike changes nothing): it lights the cell from inside (a burst and up to two restrikes over half a second, 25
    blocks over the base), and its own thunder and impact (played at once, everywhere, at full volume) are silenced and
    played again late by the distance at 130 blocks a second (the world's scale: a strike on the horizon rolls in a few
    seconds later). Within 70 blocks: the crack (the impact, pitch 0.55-0.7) and the thunder; farther: the thunder lower
    and softer (volume 1.15 - d/520, pitch 0.95 - d/1400) and a long low roll after it (`ambient.storm.roll`, three
    synthesised takes). The thunder and crack are the game's own under the storm's names (`ambient.storm.thunder`,
    `ambient.storm.crack`, event references). Every 8-16 s lightning flickers inside the cloud (50-210 over the base, a
    quarter to two fifths of a strike's brightness) and rumbles far off. Each flash is a burst and its restrikes, each
    fading over 0.11 s, and nothing once under 0.02. The storm's rain roars from its core for 340 blocks
    (`living.tell.storm`, a loop; PulseSound).
  - **Its cost** (Euan, 2026-10-29: "loses a good 10 fps when it's happening and stutters"; pack/storm-perf). What it
    cost and what changed, counted from the code (scratch `perfmodel.py`: the cloud pass's rays, bands, steps, early exit
    and temporal one-in-four at Cinematic 560×315; the storm's strike and flicker timing; Far Sight's look tolerances):
    - Far Sight's cached horizon serves only while its look (rain, haze to 1e-6, sky light, fog) holds within a hair.
      The local weather drifted every tick as the cell moved, and each bolt's sky flash set the sky light to full, so
      near a storm the far land was drawn live nearly all the time. Now the weather holds in sixths (472 breaks over a
      storm passing 75 blocks off became 90 ticks of easing) and Far Sight holds its sky light while a storm's lightning
      flashes (`StormSky.flashing`, two seconds after a strike).
    - Sound Physics (the pack, 32 rays × 4 bounces, cloning the level round you when its cache is over 20 ticks old)
      processed the storm's roll and crack, about 130 sounds a storm, one every one or two seconds. As `ambient.*`
      events it leaves them alone (`evaluate_ambient_sounds=false`); the rain roar's loop is the one processed, once.
    - Lens marched every cloud pixel every frame while any flash's value was above zero, 1.2 s after each strike and
      flicker: 61% of a storm's frames at four times the pass. Now only rays passing within 180 blocks of a flash march
      every frame, only while it is bright (over 0.08), and flickers come half as often: 21% of frames; the storm's
      average reads in the pass fell from 4.75 to 2.74 million a frame watching it from 180 blocks, from 8.10 to 4.67 at
      its edge. The lightning's faint wash over the whole cell (0.1 × exp(-d/180)) is gone; its glow ends by 180 blocks.
    - The light pass's storm shadow read the full density three times a pixel (about 1.07 million texture reads a frame
      while a storm was up); it reads the cell's outline (`stormOutline`), with no texture.
    - The client's storm tick allocates nothing (the cells follow the tells when they arrive, every 2 s).
    - Under its core the game's own rain costs what any rain does (its particles grow with the rain level squared).
    - Measured on the Mac with `tools/autopilot/perf-storm.txt` (storm on, then off, one spot and view).

### 21.7 Creatures live somewhere: the ledger (Phase D, as built 2026-10-25)
- `living.population.Ledger` (saved data `awaken:living_world`, schema 1, only cells players reached): per 512×512 cell,
  made once from the world seed the first time a player is within a cell of it (one cell a tick at most), from its
  land at five points (the biome source; never loads a chunk): up to two herds (greenwild mossback, frostwild frost
  stag, sunscorch dune ray, crag crag ram, blossom honey bear; 6-10 of 12), one pack linked to the first herd
  (greenwild gloomstalker, frostwild wisp hound, canopy canopy prowler, duskwood thornling; 3-5 of 5), one roost
  (frostwild frostfinch, crag peak kite, duskwood hollow owl; 4-6 of 6). A record: kind, species, home, three pastures,
  count, max, last play-day, seed, linked herd.
- Where (pure, from seed, play-day, time): a herd at pasture (day+seed) mod 3 → the next by 2000 (dawn walk) → the one
  after from 12000-13500 (dusk walk), wandering ±10; a pack at its den 23000-13000, else 24 blocks off its herd toward
  the den; a roost at home, out circling at 40 blocks at dawn and dusk.
- Bodies: every 2 s, a population within 96 blocks of a player (its place loaded and dry) takes min(count, 12/5/6)
  bodies (tags `awaken_ledger`, `awaken_ledger_<id>`, persistent; at most 24 near a player); they walk toward where
  their population is (herds 0.9, packs 1.1; grazing within 12). No player within 128 of any body: they're discarded.
  A death lowers the count; a body loaded from disk that isn't current never joins (after a restart): its join is
  cancelled (`Ledger.stray`, first of every listener). It is never discarded while it joins: that comes before the level
  has it, so the level kept it and every client near it saw it frozen where it was saved (12 Nov 2026, Euan: "the dune
  rays here are just glitched and not moving"; the same froze the ledger's cows, pigs and sheep).
- Catch-up (when a population takes bodies after days away): herds +1 a day (+2 while their pack is wiped out), packs
  +1 per 2 days (+1 per 4 once wiped), roosts +1 a day; each night a pack lived its herd lost one (never under 2).
- Natural spawning leaves the herd species to the ledger (`LivingHooks.ledgered`, read by `FaunaRules.verdict`:
  "its herds live in the Living Wilds' ledger"); hunters and ambient creatures keep spawning as before.
- Dev: `/awaken living ledger`. Test `living_ledger`.

### 21.8 Camps and nests (Phase D, as built 2026-10-25)
- `living.camp.Camps` (saved data `awaken:living_camps`, schema 1): a riftborn camp (45%; gate creatures that got out,
  an E-rank theme: Ember Mines, Bell Crypt, Fungal Hollow, Overgrown Temple or Hive) and a hollow den (30%; the
  Hollows) seeded with each ledger cell whose centre is level 8+, and a blight nest at a broken gate nobody cleared for
  two play-days (its theme). A seeded camp finds its ground (dry, level within 2 over 5 blocks, 120+ from a Hearth, 48
  from a gate, never the city) within 48 of its seed spot the first time a player is within 160, else it never was.
- Built (`CampPainter`, natural ground and air only, every block recorded) when a player is within 96: a riftborn camp
  (coarse dirt and paths, a crying-obsidian rift scar, a palisade of fence posts and dripstone points with gaps, 1-3
  wool tents, a lit campfire, two soul lanterns), a blight nest (blackstone, sculk and crying obsidian over the scar,
  a heart pillar), a hollow den (mossy stone, bone blocks, webs); radius 3 + tier; three lights at most.
- Awake within 40: the heart (an elite of the theme, "Heart of the <camp>", +2 levels) and a wave of 2 + tier
  (max 9) at `Regions.creatureLevel(CAMP)` + 2 per tier above 1, through `Mobs.spawn` (stats at that level), tagged
  `awaken_camp`, creature kind CAMP (kill XP by role); when a wave is down and the heart stands, another, tier - 1
  more in all. Everyone gone past 104: it sleeps (its creatures go; whole again next time).
- The heart killed: cleared. Its ground turns to coarse dirt (ash), what it stood up goes, for 5 play-days; then it
  can return at tier 1. Players within 56 get 0.4 × (1 + 0.25 per tier above 1) of a level (budget "camp", 0.10 per 10 min, as
  pacing_sim's CAMP_K), counter
  `awaken:camps_cleared`, "Cleared · <camp>".
- Each new play-day: with a player within 1500, a camp grows a tier every two days (max 5; rebuilt bigger next time).
  At tier 4+ it picks the nearest Hearth or the Wayfarer camp within 800, warns players within 800 of it ("it raids
  tomorrow night"), and the next night (14000-14400) 4 + tier of its creatures come 24 blocks short of the target,
  toward it.
- Dev: `/awaken living camps`, `nest <kind> <tier>`. Test `living_camp`.

### 21.9 Crafts (Phase E, as built 2026-10-25)
- Six crafts (`living.craft.Craft`), levels 1-50, craft XP to the next level 40·c^1.3 + 40; attachment `awaken:crafts`
  (schema 1, kept through death, synced to its owner: craft XP per craft, kinds hunted). A craft level is a toast; a
  perk opening is a toast that names it, what it does is in the Crafts tab (counter `awaken:craft_perks`).
- Each paying action also pays the Hunter level 0.008 of a level (pacing_sim CRAFT_ACTION) through its craft's budget
  (forage 0.012, mine 0.012, fish 0.012, cook 0.007, smith 0.007 per 10 min, × the rank's wild share), and the craft
  XP shrinks by the same share the budget kept back, so a farm levels off on both. Hunting rides the kill's "hunt"
  budget (its craft XP divided by how worn that is).
- Sources: Hunting, a kill: 4 + 0.3 × level (+20 an elite, +60 a beast, +30 the first of a kind). Foraging: a ripe
  plant 12 (and its herb), a flower or fern 2, a mushroom 4, berries picked 5. Mining: an ore 10 (deepslate 15).
  Fishing: a catch 15. Smithing: a temper at the Forge 40 (hearth's `awaken:use/temper`, through `Quests.advance`),
  an anvil job 12, a tool, weapon or armour crafted 8, a Field Forge mend 8. Cooking: food crafted 8, smelted 6 each.
- Herbs are no new blocks: a natural plant (short and tall grass, ferns, small flowers) is ripe on a day by a pure hash
  of its column and the clock's day: 3% (6% with Root Sense). Harvested, it gives the land's herb: sunleaf (most
  lands), frostcap (frostwild), emberroot (sunscorch), moonmoss (mire), duskbloom (duskwood, canopy), spiritgrass (10%
  anywhere). Nine meals from them (shapeless recipes, a bowl back where there was one): herb broth (Regeneration 20 s),
  frostcap tea (Resistance 60 s), ember skewer (Strength 60 s), moonmoss soup (Night Vision 120 s), hunter's stew
  (Strength and Speed 120 s), forager's salad (Regeneration 30 s), miner's pasty (Haste 180 s), angler's chowder (Water
  Breathing 120 s, Dolphin's Grace 60 s), spirit tea (Luck 120 s).
- Perks (5 · 10 · 20 · 30 · 40 · 50), all live:
  - Hunting: Field Dressing (animals: a hide or more meat 33%), Tracks (client: for 30 s after the band reads a creature it
    leaves glowing amber prints, paws or cloven hooves, lying on top of grass and flowers, fading over 30 s), Weak Spot (crits ×1.15 on kinds killed 20+), Stalker (sneak attacks on a creature not targeting you
    ×1.5), Trophy (beast parts twice), Apex (×1.1 to elites and beasts).
  - Foraging: Herb Glint (client: a sea-green shimmer on ripe plants within 16), Wild Larder (+1 berries, glow berries,
    mushrooms), Root Sense (6% ripe), Seed Keeper (grass 4%: pumpkin, melon, beetroot or torchflower seeds), Bloom (by
    day among 3+ flowers, a Bloom Sprite comes, 30% each 10 s, none within 16), Wildheart (Regeneration in forests).
  - Mining (fixed by W2, §28.3): Clean Strike (ores +1 15%), Ore Sense (client: every 4 s with a pick or Hunter mattock
    in hand, ores within 6 pulse through stone as glass outlines, 3 s), Vein Sight (each ore Ore Sense finds, its whole
    vein outlined: same ore through the 26 neighbours, 20 out, 192 blocks), Deep Ear (client: underground with a pick,
    every 3 s, an open cave or Deepglass behind two or more blocks of rock within 12 plays a soft sound from where it
    is), Deepglass Cutter (Deepglass breaks ×2 and gives a shard more; replaces Deep Vein and the planned "alloy from
    deepslate"), Heart of Stone (below y 0, damage ×0.85). Mining keeps its own pace: only its Hunter-level share is
    budgeted (`mine`), its craft XP is not cut; every craft's XP is × (1 + perk `awaken:craft_rate`).
  - Fishing: Calm Water (+1 fish 20%), Shimmer (a treasure 10%: name tag, saddle, nautilus shell, book, bottle o'
    enchanting), Deep Lungs (air lasts twice as long), Storm Caller (+1 in the rain), Pearl Diver (prismarine shard 8%,
    ender pearl 2%), Leviathan Line (catches pay the Hunter level twice).
  - Smithing: Patch (anvil jobs a level cheaper), Fine Edge (crafted gear +10% max durability), Field Forge (an iron
    ingot on a lit campfire mends the off-hand item by a quarter), Masterwork (Unbreaking I 10%), Keen (weapons
    Unbreaking I 20%; it was Sharpness I until enchanting's rule, §45), Signature ("Made by <name>" lore).
  - Cooking: Hearty (+1 saturation from cooked food and meals), Campfire Feast (eating by a lit campfire feeds players
    within 6), Hunter's Stew (meals' strengths ×1.5 long), Long Meals (+2 saturation), Spirit Tea (`awaken:energy_regen`
    +0.25 for 2 min after a cooked meal), Banquet (+the food's saturation again).
  The plan's Tidewater bait, sigil slot, temper discount and an apex phase read moved out: they need other modules'
  systems; the replacements above are this module's own.
- UI: CRAFTS on the band's Powers page (§30; level, a bar, perks open, the next). Dev: `/awaken living craft <craft>
  <level> [announce]` (announce: with the level and perk toasts, for tours). Test `living_crafts`.
- Art: the 15 icons are drawn by `tools/art/specs/items_crafts.py` (16×16, our own palette, one wooden bowl shape shared
  by the bowl meals; the pasty stands on its flat side with a crimped rope; no vanilla pixels). Its `preview DIR` checks
  colour count, distinct colours and herb silhouettes.

### 21.10 The shape of danger (regions v2; plan docs/regions/PLAN.md, page https://claude.ai/artifact/MnswCydLWBrdpXzL3f84YE; Euan approved all fourteen decisions 2026-10-27, "Go with all recommendations"; decision 8 amended and 15 added the same day at his word)
Why: Euan died at the Commons' wall at level 1 (an elite, health ×4.4) and found level 72 land 20 blocks further, the first hamlet
inside it. Causes: the neighbour cap measured to a region's heart, the 5% deck rounded to one level 45-80 region in nine per near block,
no gradient, nothing placed on purpose asked the land. This section **replaces §21.2's bands, odds, deck and neighbour rule**; names,
roles, offsets, the API and the Hearth's calm stand. Decisions (numbers are the plan's):
1. **Ceiling by distance, temper by region.** The highest a land can be at distance `d` from the centre (`reach.json`, data, straight lines):
   240→1, 700→8, 1,000→12, 1,500→20, 2,000→30, 3,000→52, 4,000→74, 5,500→105, 8,000→150. Inside 700 it is the Commons' ramp. A region's
   temper (0-1: its own roll dealt per 3×3 block, a smooth 2,400-wide "mood", the biome tilt ±0.15, contrast 2.2) places a land between a
   floor (8% of the ceiling, fading in from 700 to 1,300) and the ceiling; a region is 20% worse at its heart than at its edge.
2. **Soft borders.** Every heart near a point votes on its temper, weight `exp(-(d - dmin)/240)`: no 100 blocks change by more than about 15 levels inside 5 km.
3. **A safe start.** The Commons stays 1-8 and the ring to 1,000 follows the ceiling (8-12). The first hamlet's site must be level ≤ 12, the first town's
   ≤ 22 (prefer), the Director's first gate ≤ the player's level + 5 (re-roll the bearing).
4. **Quiet vales.** One region in eight beyond 2,000 is calm (temper 0) wherever it is.
5. **Roads and settled land are calmer.** −6 levels within 24 blocks of a laid road (easing to 0 by 60); within 96 of a settlement's built ground the land is capped at
   10 (hamlet), 14 (village), 18 (town).
6. **One band system:** E 1-9 · D 10-24 · C 25-44 · B 45-69 · A 70-99 · S 100+ (`Regions.bandOf`) is the land's rank too; the deal's 1-8 / 8-20 / 20-45 / 45-80 / 80+ goes; the Atlas
   legend is 1 · 10 · 25 · 45 · 70 · 100; a region's range is what it really spans.
7. **Elites live in places:** roaming share E 0%, D 2%, C 4%, B and up 5% (`Creatures` and `FaunaModule`); dens and camps keep an elite guard.
8. **Animals** (amended 2026-10-27, Euan's idea after the plan was approved; was "a pig is a pig, no chip"): in E land exactly as before (meek, no chip, no scaling).
   In D land (level 10) and up a naturally spawned cow, pig, sheep, mooshroom or chicken (not bred, from an egg, a baby, penned, on a settlement's land or in a Hearth's
   calm) is neutral: it fights back when struck (only when struck; it forgives ten seconds after the last blow), carries its level so the chip is true, is scaled like any
   creature of that level, grows 4% a rank up to 20%, and now and then is an alpha (an elite: bigger, tougher). From C land the herd rallies when one is struck. Kill XP is
   neutral's (0.5, not passive's 0.15). One more of its food drop per rank above E. Left for later: a client overlay (tusks, scars), wild kin with their own art, a land
   that goes quiet; the alphas are the "Terror of <region>" trophies agreed with the Arms planner (Phase 3).
9. **The land owns the hunt's parts and the pull** (agreed in principle with the Arms planner): trophies and hide by land ("Terror of <region>" beside the existing named
   beasts, nothing "only here"), surface signs of metal; metal stays in lodes by depth, light stays in gates; C and up tiers open three levels before their land. Phase 3, with the Arms builder.
10. **Going above your level pays in finds,** not XP: the kill bonus stays +40%; the first step into each higher rank is a discovery (a tenth of a level); wonders and secrets rank with their land. Phase 3.
11. **The land speaks first** (client, per player, gap = the land's level minus yours): 5-9 a faint cold tint and a low bed, 10-19 stronger with an ember edge, 20+ strongest, eased over ~4 s;
    a post on a road where a land one rank higher begins. Phase 2.
12. **Warn early, plainly:** every 2 s a 150-block look-ahead along the heading; a land 10+ above you and rising gives one CRITICAL-tier toast with numbers in plain words, once per land per
    5 minutes (the cooldown is per region); the Commons' wall warns a player 5+ below the local level; nothing inside the city's reserve.
13. **Existing worlds** switch on at the next load (the field is a pure function of seed and centre); `awaken:living_regions` schema 2 adds `rules` (absent = 1: names keep the old band roll, new worlds name from their new level).
14. **Order:** Phase 1 (1-8 but the loot of 8, 12, 13), Phase 2 (11), Phase 3 with the Arms and deep builders (9, 10, the loot of 8).
15. **The plate's colour is how hard the creature is against you** (Euan, 2026-10-27): grey ten or more levels below you, blue about your level or easier (up to four above:
    easy to kill), orange from five above (a good fight that takes skill), red from fifteen above (you can win it, but only as an insane fighter; the chip pulses). The
    same for every creature, animals included. Every creature's plate shows its level chip, a meek animal in E land too (Euan 2026-10-27, "I still see vanilla passive mobs
   with no level"; `PlateRules.showsLevel`): its chip is its land's level and reads grey or blue; only an untagged creature has none.

**Phase 1 as built (2026-10-27, `pack/regions-plan`).**
- `living.region.RegionMap` is the field: the numbers are `data/awaken/awaken/regions/reach.json` (read once from the classpath: the map is pure and
  runs on worldgen threads), `ceilingAt(distance)`, `levelAt` (no allocation; about 1.6 µs a call against 0.3 µs, hearts' tempers cached per cell),
  `rankOf(level)` (`Regions.bandOf` and the Atlas use it). A region's `band` is its land rank index (the heart's level), `low`/`high` the levels
  its land spans (its heart and eight points half a pitch round it). `RegionService` is schema 2 with `rules` (a new world 2, a save without it 1):
  rules 1 names regions by the old deal's band (kept in `RegionMap` for naming only) and follows the same levels. `RegionService.rulesOnDisk(server)`
  reads the flag from `dimensions/minecraft/overworld/data/awaken/living_regions.dat` before the overworld loads, so `RoadWorld` (opened at
  ServerAboutToStart) names regions the way the live map does.
- Placed things: `FirstHamlet.search` tries spots at level ≤ 12 first (then any; the level is read with no biome tilt), `FirstTown.find` prefers
  hearts at level ≤ 22 (then ≤ 32, then any), `Director.firstGate` caps the land at `max(level + 5, 12)` (then any way, then any land).
- `village.SettledCalm` (registered in `VillageModule.init`): `Regions.addLevelExtra` drops creatures 6 levels within 24 blocks of a laid road
  (easing to 0 by 60; `RoadNet.distanceWithin`), `Regions.addLevelCap` holds them at 10 (hamlet, wayhouse), 14 (village, mining town) or 18 (town)
  within the settlement's radius + 96. Both act on creature levels (`Regions.creatureLevel`), not on `levelAt`.
- Elites: `LivingModule.eliteChance(land level)` (0 / 2 / 4 / 5% by rank), read from `Regions.creatureLevel(NEUTRAL)` at the spawn so a Hearth's calm
  counts, in `Creatures.tag` and `FaunaModule`. Dens and camps keep their own guards. The pacing sim carries `ELITE_BY_RANK` and `role_mix`; the balanced
  player is level 5 at 0.99 h, 10 at 3.90, 25 at 16.83, 50 at 51.25, 135 at 101.93, every target passing (the hunt budget caps kill XP).
- Plates: an animal (kinds PASSIVE and AMBIENT) shows its name and no level chip (`LivingPlates.shownLevel`); creatures still carry their level for XP.
- Warnings (`RegionTracker`): every pass (40 ticks per player) a look of 150 blocks along the heading (the way they walked since the last pass if 3 blocks a
  second or more, else the way they face); `aheadWarns(mine, here, ahead)` = 10 or more above and 3 or more above where they stand gives a CRITICAL
  toast "Danger · <land>" with `body(...)` in plain words ("... about six times as tough as ones at your level and hit nearly four times as hard. Turn back, or go
  in only to look."), once per land per 5 minutes (`WARNED` per player and region; it was one per player per 10 minutes at the IMPORTANT tier). In the Commons
  outside the city's reserve a player 5 or more below the land is warned too; the region caption's danger flag and the Promise now read the land under the player
  (`danger(p, land)`), and the Commons is no longer exempt.
- Atlas: six rank colours and the legend 1 · 10 · 25 · 45 · 70 · 100 (`ZoneMap`, `AtlasScreen`); a region is coloured by the middle of its span.
- Tests: `living_region_map` (ceiling, apron, slopes, tilt, determinism, rules 1), `living_region_placed`, `living_elite_by_rank`, `living_warning_ahead`,
  `living_region_rules_saved`. Prototype and numbers: `docs/regions/proto/`, `docs/regions/results/`.
- Not built yet: Phase 3 (parts and trophies by land, richer game, first-step discoveries), the Atlas's smooth shading (it colours whole regions), the quiet
  vales' name ("the Rest").

**Amendments built (2026-10-27).** `living.combat.WildKin` (decision 8: `fights`, `wild`, `growth`, `rallies`, `arm`; `Retaliate` is a `HurtByTargetGoal` that lets go after 200 ticks;
an `ATTACK_DAMAGE` attribute added to pig 3, cow 3, mooshroom 3, sheep 2 and chicken 1 through `EntityAttributeModificationEvent`; goals are put back at every join since they are not
saved), `Creatures.tag` (a wild spawn in D land or up is tagged NEUTRAL, scaled, grown, an alpha at `eliteChance`), `GameDrops` (richer game for animals that can't hurt you and for
these), `PlateRules.heat` and `LivingFx.heatColour` (decision 15). Tests `living_wild_kin`, `living_plate_heat`, `living_game_drops`.

**Phase 3 as built (2026-10-27, after the Arms builder finished; `pack/arms-progression` A to G and the base are merged into `pack/regions-plan`, the two road-file conflicts kept both sides).**
- Decision 9, the land owns the hunt's parts: an alpha (decision 8) is titled "Alpha of <region>" and always drops hide of its land's tier (`GameDrops.alphaHide`: one, one more
  from B land, two more from S, from the gear tier's `#awaken:hunter_hide_<tier>` tag); so the next tier's hide is where the harder land is. The named beasts keep their species
  trophies and their "Terror of <region>" title exactly as they were (Arms' `#awaken:hunter_core_d` is a list of species parts; nothing was removed or made "only here").
- Quiet vales are named like shelters ("Willow Rest", "the Heron Hush": `Names.quiet`), in worlds made under rules 2 only.
- Not built, and why: **a generic "Terror" trophy item** (Arms' D part is the species list; a new item needs Arms' `sources.json` line, JEI and tests, which are Arms' to extend),
  **surface signs of metal** (a worldgen feature over Tectonic; metal stays in lodes by depth per §28.0.7, the pull is Arms' part jobs and "What waits"), **shard scaling for
  vanilla creatures** (Arms' shard economy and pity are calibrated without it), **the Atlas's smooth shading** (the client does not have the field), **tusks and scars, wild kin
  art, a quieter land** (art), **wonders and secrets ranked by land** (Living Wilds Phase F is unbuilt).

**Phase 2 as built (2026-10-27): the land speaks first.**
- `LivingNet.LandMsg(level)` (`living_land`): the level of the land under the player, sent from `RegionTracker.tick` when it changes (-1 away from the overworld). Client
  `living.client.DreadFx` turns the gap (land level minus the player's level) into `DreadRules.strength(gap)` (0 under 5, 0.15 at 5, 0.45 at 10, 1 at 20), eased in over
  about four seconds and out a little faster, as a Lens place look over the world's own and the volume of a looping bed. Per player and client side; setting `dread`
  in `awaken-living-client.toml` (on). It stays on with `awaken:pure_survival` (atmosphere, not a plate).
- Lens `PLACE_LAYERS` is 3: layer 2 is `awaken:dread` (`looks_living.json`: the colour cools and drains, shadows blue, an ember haze gathers at the edges, the corners darken).
- Sound: `living.dread`, `amb_living_dread.ogg` (`tools/art/specs/audio_living.py`: 8 s, every tone a whole number of cycles in the loop and the air periodic, so it
  loops without a seam; D 73.4 Hz and a twin beating once a loop, a fifth, a cold octave, a dark breath of air; -29 dBFS RMS). Played looping, relative, at
  the land's weight × 0.85. Listening is for the Mac.
- March posts (`village.road.Waymarks.marches`, from `Highroads.lay` for highroads): where a road first passes into land a rank above the land behind it, a post on
  the walker's right (from each end) with one arm: "<land> · Lv 10–24". A boundary must hold for 32 blocks; bridges wait for dry ground; clear of the settlements'
  posts. Painted by the waymarker painter like any marker (new chunks only).
- Dev: `/awaken living dread <gap|off>` (admin) forces the gap for tours; tour `tools/autopilot/regions-dread.txt` (CI).
  CI tour 40444955175 (reviewed 2026-10-27): the tint eases in and out as designed (blue sky at gap 0 to a grey lavender at 25), but the first values read only as a slightly greyer sky, so
  the look was strengthened (saturation 0.5, exposure 0.84, vignette 0.75, haze 0.4, ember mix 0.75) without a second tour (one a hand-back); the next playtest judges it. The sound is for the Mac's ears.
- Tests: `living_dread_gap`, `village_march_ranks` (a synthetic road: a post for each rise, none for a flicker).


### 21.11 The Wild Grows Teeth (plan docs/regions/PLAN-2.md, page https://claude.ai/artifact/LhA8jeGxTmYTktau4mmgia; Euan approved all sixteen decisions 2026-10-27, "Go with all recommendations", and said to do the work without sub-agents)
Continues §21.10's numbering (16-31). The long form is PLAN-2.md; this is what builders hold to.
16. **Five forms.** Every common creature in D land or higher (level 10 up) wears one of five forms (rung 1-5 = ranks D, C, B, A, S): a new body, one new move, a new voice. E land and the first hour are vanilla.
17. **First drop species:** zombie (husk), skeleton (stray), spider (cave spider), creeper, pig, cow (mooshroom), sheep, chicken; enderman, slime, witch and drowned in a second pass.
18. **One kit on the vanilla bodies, no mixin.** `living.client.FormLayers` adds a layer to each species' renderer: a skin overlay (the parent model drawn again with `textures/entity/forms/<layout>/o<rung>_<family>.png`), the kit (a second model of the vanilla class whose own cubes were cleared and replaced by the
    kit's pieces, `assets/awaken/forms/kit.json`, drawn with `k<rung>_<family>.png`), and an emissive glow (`g<rung>.png`, a white mask tinted by the rank's colour: D gold, C orange, B red, A violet, S indigo, the Atlas's). The biome family (green, sun, frost; from the biome's base temperature) sets the material.
    Client setting `forms` (awaken-living-client.toml): FULL, LITE (no kit) or OFF. The plate chip stays relative to the viewer; the glow is absolute rank.
    **Superseded 2026-10-28 by §21.13** (form bodies from C; the kit, `kit.json`, the overlays and `forms_geom.py` are retired; D keeps the vanilla body with the forms' eyes).
19. **Moves (Build 2):** one telegraphed move per rung (a second on alphas from C), tells 1.2 s (D) down to 0.7 s (S), damage at most 1.3 times a normal blow, delivered with `Strikes.deliver` naming its class.
20. **Voices (Build 2):** `PlayLevelSoundEvent.AtEntity` lowers the pitch and layers a growl by rung; each move has a tell sound.
21. **First sight** of a form is a discovery (a tenth of a level, `form/<species>/<rung>`), an Almanac line, no toast stack.
22. **The mix:** a creature's rung is its land's rank 70% of the time, one below 25% (50% in the first three levels of a rank), one above 5% (D land and up only: the foreshadow). Alphas wear the land's rung at least, and the crown piece (mark bit 1).
23-31. A quieter land, signs and ambient by rank, the Atlas's smooth shading, wonders, surface secrets and treasure maps, legends, the rest of the chains and happenings, order: Builds 3 to 6 (PLAN-2.md sections 6-9 and 11); recorded here as each is built.

**Build 1 as built (2026-10-27).**
- `living.combat.Forms` (pure rules and the assigner): `rungFor(landLevel, random)`, `Species` by entity type, `family(biome)`; attachment `awaken:wild_form` (`LivingContent.FORM`, `Forms.Form(rung, family, marks)`, rung -1 = not rolled yet, saved and synced to trackers), rolled by `Creatures.tag` for a levelled vanilla monster or a wild kin and, for creatures from before it existed,
  once on join. Only creatures the Living Wilds tagged MONSTER or wild NEUTRAL get a form (never AWAKEN's own, never a settlement's or a Hearth's calm: those are below D).
- Art: `tools/art/specs/forms.py` writes the overlays, kit textures, glow masks and `forms/kit.json` (one source for the Python painter and the Java model builder).
- Dev: `/awaken living form <species> <rung> [family]`, `/awaken living formparade [family]` (every species, rungs 0-5, in rows, still), tour `tools/autopilot/forms-parade.txt`.
- Tests: `living_form_mix`, `living_form_state`. CI tour 40454849731 (forms-parade, 14 shots) reviewed: every species' rungs read as an escalation in the real game (tusks, horns, helms, spines, crests, the rank's glow at the eyes); the kit follows the animation.
  Offline look: `tools/art/forms_preview.py` renders the kit on the vanilla bodies (the vanilla textures are read from `.ref` for the preview only).

**Build 2 as built (2026-10-27): moves and voices.**
- `living.combat.Moves` (the table and the shapes), `MarkGoal` (the goal, priority -1, flags MOVE and LOOK: a roll every few ticks only with a target; wind-up standing still and facing,
  strike once, a lunge or a charge carried through, a rest), `MarkEvents` (a revenant's rise, spider webs taken away, voices). Armed at every join (`Creatures.onJoin` -> `Moves.arm`; goals are not saved).
  Tells run 24 ticks in D down to 14 in S (`Moves.windup`); a tell is a ring or a line of dust in the rank's colour on the ground and a sound; damage is the creature's attack times `power` (at most 1.3)
  delivered with `Strikes.deliver` naming its class (a lunge or a charge GRAB, a stomp PERILOUS, a bash HEAVY, shots LIGHT). A crowned creature from the third rung has the rung below's move too.
- Shapes: LUNGE, CHARGE, STOMP, BASH, RALLY, ROAR (slows or blinds, no damage), VOLLEY and SNIPE (arrows), BLINK, SPIT (a ray with poison), WEB (a cobweb at your feet, taken away after 8 s), SUMMON (never past eight of a kind
  within 24 blocks), PULL; RISE (a zombie form from the fourth rung stands up once at 40%, `Forms.RISEN`, in `MarkEvents.onDeath` at highest priority) and RETREAT (a first-rung skeleton gets an `AvoidEntityGoal` for players).
  Pig: Gore, Root-up, Trample, Quake, Roar. Cow (and mooshroom): Back-kick, Charge, Stomp, Storm charge, Bellow. Sheep: Headbutt, Charge, Spark, Charge, Bleat. Chicken: Flap-jump, Crow, Burst, Flap-jump, Screech.
  Zombie (husk): Groan, Shield bash, Pounce, Rise, Dread call. Skeleton (stray): Retreat, Marksman, Volley, Wraith step, Volley of five. Spider (cave spider): Web, Drop, Spit, Brood, Pull.
- Voices: `PlayLevelSoundEvent.AtPosition` (mob sounds are played at a position): a formed creature within half a block of the sound has its pitch lowered 8% a rung (S: 0.6) and its volume raised 5% a rung.
- Not built, and why: the creeper's moves (the explosion is vanilla's; its five forms are bodies only), a growl layered under the voice and custom tell sounds (the tells use vanilla sounds repitched; `tools/art/specs/audio_living.py` is the place),
  Arms' tell glint for a form's wind-up (`Strikes.installTells` is install-once and the mobs module holds it; chaining it is a change in `core.api`), the "unless you finish it fast" clause of Rise.
- Tests: `living_form_moves`.

**Rise and the tests (2026-10-27, after CI).** A revenant rises from a lethal blow that is not a finishing one (`MarkEvents.shouldRise`: at least its health, under two health bars, 400 to 900), in `LivingDamageEvent.Pre`
(the blow is spent, as a totem's), not from every death. Game rule `awaken:wild_forms` (default on; the GameTest server starts with it off, like `living_herds`) switches forms off for a world: older tests that kill a zombie
outright in far land (where forms are the rule) failed on CI when a revenant stood up. The form tests roll and set forms themselves.

**Kit placement rules (2026-10-27, after Euan's screenshots: tusks over the face, spines floating over the back, claws hanging off the fists).** Every piece of a kit is checked when the art is built
(`tools/art/forms_geom.py`, called by `tools/art/specs/forms.py`; a violation stops the build with the piece named): **attached** (it touches the vanilla body or a piece that does; a horn is a chain
whose segments start where the last ended; only up to six marked floating shards in the top rung may hang free, within 9 blocks); **off the face** (the eye band from the face plane forward is a
keep-out: tusks, horns and crowns go round it, marks are never painted on a head's front); **seen** (not hidden inside the body); **in reach** (7 blocks at D to 13 at S). Geometry is the
vanilla bodies' own (`BODIES`, from the 26.3 ModelPart definitions), checked at rest. Pieces are placed on named surfaces (a ridge stands on the body's top plane, a tusk starts inside the cheek,
a claw starts at the end of the arm and points along it). Looks are reviewed offline from four angles (`python3 tools/art/forms_preview.py OUT.png 0 <layout> --angles`) before any tour.

**Build 3 as built (2026-10-27): the land, the quiet, the Atlas.**
- **Signs** (decision 24): `living.signs.Signs` (thirteen kinds: wallow, bone pile, boulder and rust outcrop in D; skull post, cold camp and broken cart in C; snag and ribs in B; graves and a black spire in A;
  a weeping stone and a ring of them in S; vanilla blocks by biome family) and `WildSignsFeature` (`awaken:wild_signs`, step vegetal_decoration through `neoforge:add_features`, `data/awaken/worldgen/*/living/signs.json`):
  per new chunk 0.25 signs in D, 0.5 C, 0.9 B, 1.3 A, 1.6 S (none in E), on natural ground only, flat enough, never in water. The region map is warmed at ServerStarted so worldgen threads
  (`RegionService.mapIfReady`) never touch saved data; chunks made before it exists (a new world's first, in the Commons) get none. The rust outcrop is the surface sign of iron (a pull; iron stays by depth). Not consulted
  at generation: a settlement's or a road's reserve (only the natural-ground rule keeps signs off built ground).
- **A quieter land** (decision 23): `living.combat.QuietLand`: natural animal spawns are turned away by wildness, not rank (since the Wild Lands, §41.4: kept
  Tamed 70%, Pasture 90%, Wild and Deep all; `FinalizeSpawnEvent.setSpawnCancelled` in `Creatures.onFinalizeSpawn`; never a settlement's land or a Hearth's
  calm, bred or egg animals, or the ledger's own bodies), wild kin avoid a player who is not sneaking (`AvoidEntityGoal`, 10 blocks in D to 26 in S, below the fight goals), and the wild life
  layer's dial is multiplied by the rank (`Wildlife.dialNow`: birds and insects 80%, 50%, 30%, 8%, 2%).
- **Ambient air** (decision 25): `living.client.AmbientFx`: a few specks a second drifting through the land you stand in (D dust, C ash, B embers, A violet motes, S almost none; snow in the cold), off with the `dread` setting.
  Not built: a sound bed per rank (needs `audio_living.py` work) and a colour grade per rank through Lens (the gap's dread look stays).
- **Atlas smooth shading** (decision 26): `AtlasNet.WireTile.levels` (a level byte per explored cell, `Discovery.levels`), `ZoneMap.View.level` (blended between the four nearest cells' middles in the log), `rankRamp`
  (the rank colours blended between the ranks' geometric middles) and `heatRamp` (the plate's colours blended at -10, +5, +15), `AtlasMesh` colours a region column by its level, **H** switches between the land's rank and
  how hard it is for you (the legend follows). Test `atlas_levels`.
- **First sight** (decision 21, done in Build 6's place): `MarkEvents.onPlayerTick`: once a second, a formed creature within 24 blocks in plain view is a discovery (`form/<layout>/<rung>`, a tenth of a level) and one
  line ("New form · Tusker: Watch for its gore.", `Forms.nameOf`). The Almanac's Forms page is not built.
- Tests: `living_signs` (density by rank; every kind builds one piece standing on the ground, under 90 blocks, in all three families), `living_quiet_land`. Two older tests set their zombie's form to vanilla: the test land is
  far out, in S land, where a revenant would stand up from the kill.

**Builds 4 and 5 as built (2026-10-27): Phase F, the part that stands in the world.**
- **Wonders** (decision 27): `living.wonder.Wonders` (a region's wonder: its kind by the rank of its heart's land, its site 70-200 blocks from the heart on dry, flat ground inside the region, its plan of blocks from a seed;
  all a pure function of the seed and the region, cached), `WonderFeature` (`awaken:wonders`, step surface_structures, data `worldgen/*/living/wonders.json`: each new chunk writes the share of every wonder within 38
  blocks, only inside itself, building the ground up under the foot). The ground is the chunk generator's own `getBaseHeight`, so every chunk and the server later agree. Six kinds: the Bell Tree (E-D; a real bell hangs
  in it), the Boar Throne (D-C), the Statue Field (D-B), the Web Cathedral (C-B), the Gravefield of the Revenants (A: a black house and rows of graves, some open), the Weeping Stones (S). `WonderWatch`:
  warded (no hostile spawns within 44 blocks), found by standing within 30 blocks (a discovery of 0.15 of a level plus 0.07 a rank, a "New wonder" line, the counter `awaken:wonders_found`, the player's list
  `awaken:wonders` kept through death) and drawn on the Atlas through `MapMarks`. The region map is warmed at ServerStarted and worldgen asks `RegionService.mapIfReady`.
- **Surface secrets** (decision 28): `Secrets` and `SecretFeature` (`awaken:secrets`): three per region (a cairn over a brushable cache, a cold camp with a barrel, a marked mound over a chest), 150-400 blocks from the
  heart on flat dry ground, each cache filled from its rank's loot table (`data/awaken/loot_table/chests/living/secret_0..5.json` and `archaeology/living/secret_0..5.json`: emeralds, iron, gold, essence shards, diamonds,
  from a netherite scrap in S). Finding one is walking up to it (6 blocks): the "Secrets found" counter, a line, a small discovery for the first of each kind.
- Review of the first real-generation tour (CI 40458312323): wonders generate through the feature as intended (statues, ring stones, a black house with graves, found by walking up with the toast); it showed a wonder on a Precursor ruin's floor and one on stilts
  at a cliff, so a wonder's site keeps three chunks clear of any structure that may start (`Terrain.structureNear`, from the generator state's structure sets), a secret one chunk, a column whose real ground is more than three blocks from the
  heart's level is left out, the foot is built up at most four blocks, and what grows through a wonder's ground (leaves, logs, tall grass: `Kind.clear` blocks round the heart) is cleared. Not handled: a road passing through a wonder.
- **Ground others stand on** (Euan's playtest 11 Nov, build 5c930ea6d: "a camp here that is broken... a ton of things are floating"): a cold camp at (-1543, 77, -584) in
  his New World V20 stood at the noise's ground over a hillside a delve mouth had already cut away (the mouth is a structure at `underground_structures`, before
  any surface feature), and a cairn at (-1031, 67, -648) over a carver's pit. The noise still says ground where a cave place, a carver, a road or a settlement
  has changed it or will. So:
  - A **secret** stands on the ground of each of its columns: every column's own noise ground, no more than 2 over or under the heart's (steeper gives the spot
    up for the next attempt), its blocks and cache moved with it (`Plan.foot`, `columns`). And it is written whole or not at all: `SecretFeature.keepsOff` is
    asked by every chunk under it and reads only what each of them holds alike (a secret is 13 blocks wide at most, so its chunks lie beside each other), and
    keeps it off when (1) a wonder's ground is within reach (38 + 2) of it; (2) any structure referenced from its chunks (or those beside its blocks within 2,
    that all of them hold) has a piece whose box crosses its blocks plus 2, from 6 under its lowest block to 12 over its highest; a piece that says which land it
    uses (`core.api.GroundPiece`: road legs and settlements, whose boxes are their whole rasters) is asked that instead, with a road's 8 of banks; (3) a start
    one of its chunks can't read (past the 8 chunks the FEATURES step holds) is named; (4) a column's ground block is air, water or ice, or not a whole
    block, or the block under it is air or water (a carver's pit, a pond: carving is part of the terrain step, done in every chunk beside). One that kept off is
    simply not there: `WonderWatch` counts a secret found only when at least half its plan's blocks stand in the world.
  - A **wonder** keeps off a cave place open to the sky (a mouth, a sinkhole, a mine's adit) whose box crosses its footprint and cleared ground plus 3, from 6
    under to 12 over its ground: `Terrain.cut`, through `delve.api.CaveGround` (§34.1, each nearby candidate start's own site search), and tries its next
    spot. Its sites are a full terrain's (`WonderFeature.terrain`, worldgen and the server); `quickTerrain` (no probes) is for a census and a command's first
    look, cached apart (`Terrain.seesCuts`). The server thread asks `Wonders.near(..., wait false)`: a region not worked out yet is worked out on a background
    thread and counts from the next ask (the ward and finding start a second later), so a region's first look never stalls a tick. `wonder list|goto` pick
    regions by the quick look, nearest first, then ask each as worldgen does.
  - New chunks only: a secret or wonder an old world already holds stays as written; one whose site moves under the new rule may be written in part where
    the old and the new land meet. Not handled: a road passing through a wonder (as before), and a carver's pit under a wonder (its columns are left out, as before).
- Dev: `/awaken living wonder list|goto <kind>|build <kind>`; tours `tools/autopilot/wonders.txt`. Tests `living_wonder_sites` (sites inside their regions and ranks, the same every time, the Commons has none; every kind's plan
  is one piece standing on the ground in all three families), `living_secret_sites`.
- **Chains** (Build 6, the part done): five more for the lands the first nine skip (`data/awaken/awaken/quest/`): Silk on the Road (band 2, Pell, spiders on a road), Iron in the Ranks (band 2, Gus, zombies in scrap iron), Ash on the Wind
  (band 3, Wren, archers below a ledge), The Bell at the Crossing (band 3, Pell, the dead and a bell), Crowns in the Dark (band 4, Gus, a bone crown on a crag). They use the engine's own objectives and what the land's forms already
  drop; no new relic.
- **Not built, and why**: ten of the sixteen wonder kinds (Frozen Gate, Glass Sea, Upside-down Falls, Giant's Arch, Singing Canyon, Sunken Spire, Petrified Herd, Star Crater, Chain Bridge, Mirror Lake: each is a
  structure of its own and wants its own look), wonder effects and Codex pages (the Bell Tree's bell rings as any bell does), per-player caches, **treasure maps** (an item with its own art and a clue
  reader), **the legendary beasts** (Old Greymane, Hush, the Glass Wyrm: they need bodies and a place in the beast registry, the fauna module's), six of the **eleven chains** and all **nineteen happenings** (Build 6), a sound bed and a
  colour grade per rank, the Almanac's Forms page, moves for creepers, Arms' tell glint for forms. Signs and wonders consult no settlement's or road's reserve (only natural ground keeps signs off built ground).

### 21.12 The wide world (regions v3; Euan 2026-10-27: "I don't want to be blocked from exploring if you're still rank E or D or C"; approved "go ahead with all of it")
Why: under §21.10 danger was a ceiling by distance, so low land ended about 2.6 km out: a level 1-5 player had about 9 km² to
explore, a level 20 about 36 km², and a region was crossed in three and a half minutes. Euan wants Minecraft's go-anywhere
exploration at any level, bigger regions, a mix where calm land turns up far out, and still more danger the further you go.
Numbers below were measured on a script copy of the field (two seeds, 32 km across) before it was built.
1. **Rules 3, new worlds only.** `RegionMap.RULES` is 3; a world made before keeps the rules on its record (its roads and settlements
   were laid on 900-block regions). The GameTest server's world is made under `TEST_RULES` 2 (`RegionService.newWorldRules`): the road,
   village and wonder tests were written on 900-block regions; the wide world's own test builds a rules 3 map directly.
2. **Bigger regions:** hearts 1,600 apart (`pitch()`, data `wide.pitch`), about six minutes' walk across; borders warp 380 over 1,300-block waves.
3. **A rank by odds, not a ceiling.** Each region rolls its rank from odds that shift with its heart's distance (data `wide.odds`, straight lines
   between rows, flat past the last): 1,300 all E · 2,500 E 55 D 35 C 10 · 4,500 E 30 D 30 C 25 B 12 A 3 · 7,000 E 14 D 24 C 26 B 21 A 12 S 3 ·
   11,000 E 5 D 13 C 20 B 24 A 22 S 16 · 18,000 E 3 D 8 C 14 B 23 A 25 S 27. The roll is dealt in nine strata per 3×3 block (every block holds the
   spread), tilted by a 6,000-wide mood (`u^exp(-1.6(mood-0.5))`, which keeps both ends reachable) and by the biome (±0.12, 40% of regions). Inside its
   band a region sits higher the further out (`push` 2,000 → 12,000); B, A and S start 10%, 30%, 50% up their band so a border's slope does not wear
   them into the rank below. A region is 10% worse at its heart and 10% calmer at its edge; neighbours blend with weight `exp(-(d - dmin)/240)`.
4. **Calm ways.** Along every border of a province (three regions wide, 4,800, jittered) runs a wandering valley of E land (levels 3-8 by noise), about
   220 blocks wide (wobbling ±50%), warped 900 over 3,200-block waves and 260 over 800. Its edge eases into the land round it over
   `180 + 4 × (level − calm)` blocks, so beside S land the climb takes about 650 blocks. The ways join into one net: a level 1 player can walk
   calm land to the edge of the world.
5. **The safe start.** The Commons' ramp inside 700 as before; 8-9 to 1,000 (camps and dens still seed by the wall); regions with hearts inside
   1,300 are E (3-8), easing into the mix by 1,600. Calm regions beyond 2,000 are named like shelters ("Willow Rest"); §21.10's one-in-eight quiet vales
   are not rolled in the wide world (the calm ways and rolled E regions replace them).
6. **Measured.** The real field (`living_region_wide` logs its census; seed 1234): calm land walks from the wall to 12,000 out (the test's
   edge); 11-15 km out E 18%, A and S 24%, S 6% (S keeps growing past 15 km); mean level 15 at 3-5 km, 45 at 11-15 km; inside 5,000 no 100
   blocks change by more than 25 levels, nowhere by more than 50. The plan's script copy (before borders were softened to 240), two seeds: share of land by rank 0.7-2 km E ~90%; 2-4 km E ~60 D 23 C 12; 4-7 km E 30 D 28 C 25 B 11 A 4 S 1; 7-11 km E 20 D 23
   C 21 B 20 A 11 S 6; 11-16 km E 15 D 12 C 17 B 22 A 18 S 15. Land a player can walk to on land no more than four levels above their own, out to
   16 km: level 1-5 from 9 km² (2.6 km out) to about 165 km² (16 km out); level 10 from 18 to about 200; level 20 from 36 to about 310. First S
   land about 6.3 km out (was 5.2), first A about 3.5 km (was about 4).
7. **What follows the size.** Roads join neighbouring regions' hubs, so the highroad grid is now about 1,600 apart (`w.regions.pitch()` in
   `village.road`); a region holds a town at 0.35 (was 0.22, `RoadNet.TOWN_ODDS_WIDE`); the settlement grid (640) leaves half its cells empty
   besides the usual tenth (`SettlementGrid.WIDE_EMPTY`): about one settlement every 900 blocks. A region keeps nine secrets (three of each kind,
   150 to 0.42 × pitch from the heart; was three); one wonder per region as before.
- `RegionMap.levelAt` in the wide world costs about the same as before (25 hearts' cached levels, nine province hearts, a few noise samples). Test
  `living_region_wide`; `living_region_map` pins rules 2.

### 21.13 Forms, rebuilt (plan docs/forms/PLAN.md; Euan 2026-10-28: the levelled forms "look rushed"; approved all five decisions: real form bodies, animals and spiders grow while walkers stay under two blocks and gain bulk, the land's crystal in the rank's colour at A and S, two-hit attacks from B with the alpha's roar and the creeper's moves, F0-F3 straight through; "animations on par with Fresh Animations' zombie")
Replaces §21.11 decision 18's kit. Built 2026-10-28 by one builder, no sub-agents.
1. **A body of its own from C.** A formed creature at rung 2-5 (C-S) is drawn as a hero rig of ours instead of the vanilla body:
   `RenderLivingEvent.Pre` is cancelled and `living.client.forms.FormRenderer` (a `MobRenderer` over `HeroRenderState`, one per rig, built in
   `EntityRenderersEvent.AddLayers`) submits the body at the same place. A render state modifier on `MobRenderer` fills a per-entity `FormBody`
   (weak map, reused, no per-frame allocation) after vanilla's extract, so name tag, fire, outline, shadow and the vanilla state the layers need
   stay vanilla's. No mixin. D (rung 1), a baby, setting LITE, and a rig that failed to build keep the vanilla body with the forms' eyes
   (`FormLayers`, `textures/entity/forms/<layout>/o1, g<rung>`); OFF is vanilla. A failure to pose is logged once and that creature falls back.
2. **Rigs.** `living.forms.FormRigs`: `form_<body>_<rung>` for the eight bodies (zombie, skeleton, spider, creeper, pig, cow, sheep, chicken) at
   rungs 2-5, 32 rigs, generated data (`FormData`, from `tools/art/specs/forms_bodies.py` with `_forms_hostiles.py` and `_forms_animals.py`;
   build `python3 tools/art/build_all.py forms_bodies`). Husk, stray, cave spider and mooshroom wear their family's rig with their own paint (a
   cave spider at 0.7); the biome family (green, sun, frost) is a paint per species. Textures: `textures/entity/forms/body/<rig>_<species>_<family>`
   (+ `_shut` for the blink, `_glow` emissive) and the coats; about 1.7 MB in all. Every rig passes `check_rig` at build time (every cube attached
   to its bone's chain, nothing floating, nothing over the face's eye band, whole pixels, in reach). `HeroModel` gained an overload
   `HeroModel(ModelPart, HeroRig, LifeProfile)`; its graph is unchanged (the boss plan's).
3. **Ladders.** Zombie → ghoul (hunch, open jaw, long clawed forearms, ribs; A knuckle-walk, S crystal crown and grave cape). Skeleton → bone knight
   (ribcage of bars, a heart light from B, jaw, horns, pauldrons, greaves, tasset; S bone cloak). Spider → brood stalker (coxa-leg-shin legs
   solved to the ground, fangs, lit sac, plates, bladed legs, an eye crown at S). Creeper → bloom (a sepal ring and petals round the head, the
   front left clear; veins glow from B; the petals flare to 78° as it swells; S crown petals). Pig → boar (hump, spines, plates, tusks).
   Cow → aurochs (hump, lyre horns as their own bones, boss plate; mooshroom's mushrooms painted only for it). Sheep → ram (curling horns, wool
   on gear bones). Chicken → fighting cock (upright, spurs, crest, sickle tail). Posture and mass tell rank before colour.
4. **The gear-bone rule.** Core bones (`head`, `torso`, `arm_r/l`, `leg_r/l`) hold only their core cubes; growth hangs on child bones named
   `gear*` at the parent's pivot. `FormGear` sizes vanilla's armour meshes to the union of each core bone's cubes (only the torso stretches
   tall; a skeleton's limbs measure against 2-pixel bones) and poses them from the body's composed bones; held items stand at `hand_r/l`.
   Life roles come from bone names (head, jaw, torso, arm, leg; skirt, cape, chain dangle), so gear names avoid those tokens.
5. **Clips** (per rig, additive, the life layer on top): idle, walk, run, angry, bite (the melee swing), hurt, death (each body's own fall:
   a skeleton crumples and its skull rolls, a spider rolls onto its back, animals fall on their side), roar, and per move `<kind>_windup` and
   `<kind>_strike` (or one `once` clip). A blade skeleton stands in `angry_melee`; a bow skeleton aims with `angry`. Chicken has `air`.
   The walk is driven by ground distance so a cycle covers its stride; the zombie keeps Fresh Animations' rhythm (arm sway, head bob) with
   our own variation, and every other body follows the same weight.
6. **Cue.** `LivingNet.FormCue(entity, move, startTick, holdTicks, windupTicks)` to trackers when a move winds up (`MarkGoal`), an empty move
   when it is cut short, and for the creeper's moves (`Combos`). The client stretches the wind-up to the move's real length, then plays the strike;
   a late joiner computes the phase from `startTick`. A lost cue loses only the acting: the ground tell and sound still warn. D sends none.
7. **Eyes.** Lit in the rank's colour (D gold, C orange, B red, A violet, S indigo), set in modelled sockets; they close with the blink, flare in
   a wind-up and go out over the fall. A soft additive halo round each (`textures/entity/forms/halo.png`, `RenderTypes.eyes`): faint by day,
   strong at night, swelling in a wind-up, within 48 blocks.
8. **True size** (`living.combat.FormShape`, `EntityEvent.Size`, both sides from the synced form, `refreshDimensions` when set or loaded): width,
   height in blocks for C, B, A, S: pig 1.0/1.0, 1.2/1.15, 1.4/1.35, 1.6/1.5; cow 1.1/1.55, 1.3/1.75, 1.5/1.95, 1.7/2.15; sheep 1.0/1.4,
   1.15/1.55, 1.3/1.7, 1.45/1.85; chicken 0.5/0.85, 0.6/1.0, 0.75/1.25, 0.9/1.5; spider 1.6/1.0, 1.9/1.1, 2.2/1.25, 2.5/1.4; creeper 0.65/1.8,
   0.7/1.95, 0.8/2.1, 0.9/2.3; zombie 0.7/1.95, 0.8/1.9, 0.9/1.85, 0.9/1.98; skeleton 0.65, 0.7, 0.8, 0.85 wide at 1.99. Applied as factors over
   vanilla, so the elite scale attribute and eye height carry over. Walkers stay under two blocks (doors).
9. **Two blows from B** (`Combos`): a formed creature's melee hit (B, A, S; never a creeper) is followed `SECOND_AFTER` = 10 ticks later (the
   target's hurt cooldown) by a second blow of 0.5/0.6/0.7 times its attack (never more than a normal blow), a LIGHT strike through
   `Strikes.deliver`, only if the target is still in reach and sight: stepping back is the answer. One follow-up at a time per creature.
10. **The alpha's roar.** A crowned creature (mark bit 1) from C roars once, the first time it turns on someone in sight within 16 blocks
    (`MarkGoal.ALPHA`: a 16-tick wind-up, no blow), and its kin nearby take up the hunt.
11. **The creeper's moves** (§21.11's "not built" closed): at the start of a swell, at most once each 8 s: C a sidestep hop (so a lined-up shot
    misses), B a seed left where it stood that bursts 1.5 s later (power 1.6, no block damage), A lights the fuses of up to two creepers within
    6 blocks of you (each takes its own full swell), S drags you toward it while it swells (within 7 blocks). The explosion stays vanilla's.
12. **Tells by class, not rank.** A tell's dust says what to do: LIGHT white, HEAVY amber, PERILOUS red, GRAB violet; a move that is no blow
    keeps the rank's colour (`Moves.tellColour`).
13. **Coats.** A sheep's wool (dyed colour, gone when sheared) and a pig's saddle are drawn as a coat layer over the body
    (`forms/body/<rig>_<species>_<family>_wool|saddle`, tinted by the wool colour); the base skin leaves those cubes clear.
15. **A gradual change** (Euan 2026-10-28, after the first renders: "from one level to the next it looks like a completely different
    animal"; keep the bodies, slow the texture change). Each paint runs from the vanilla creature's own colours (our palettes, read off the
    vanilla look) to the form's by `DRIFT` = C 0.18, B 0.42, A 0.7, S 1.0 (`forms_bodies.toward`): a C pig is still pink, a C creeper bright
    green, a C zombie still wears the cyan shirt, a C sheep a pale face, a C chicken is white. Rot, cracks, bristle and curls grow with it,
    a spider's chevron fades in, a cock's hackles and sickles colour a rank at a time and its wing bows two ranks later; a mooshroom keeps its
    pale patches. The shapes are unchanged.
16. **Falls along the blow** (with Fight Feel, §25). A form body that a blow killed turns as it starts to fall, over 0.2 s, so its
    own death clip falls the way the blow went (`FormShape.fallTurn`, from `CombatFeedback.blowOn`): at most 100° (a blow from the front
    tips a forward-faller onto its side, never into the striker). The walkers fall forward; the creeper, the chicken and the beasts onto
    their left; a spider rolls over in place and does not turn. A vanilla body at D keeps its glow's fade though Fight Feel's own fall
    clears the state's `deathTime` (the layer reads the fall from its own render data).
17. **With Fresh Animations, its moves 1:1** (Euan 2026-10-29: "for all vanilla mob upgrades, literally just use the fresh animations 1:1, they are
    perfect already"; he chose to keep the rung's size, eyes and extras). When EMF is loaded and the resource packs hold a model for the
    species (`minecraft:optifine/cem/<id>.jem` or `emf/cem/`), read on each renderer rebuild, a form from C up keeps the vanilla body, which the
    pack animates, at the rung's height (`state.scale *= FormShape.heightFactor`, about the feet; the walkers stay near vanilla's height in their
    wider box). Nothing of the pack is shipped or read beyond that check: its terms forbid redistribution and our repo is public, so the moves
    come from the player's own install (a modpack may bundle FA by its terms). The rig's extras ride the vanilla parts (`living.forms.FormFit`,
    pure): every bone that isn't the body (body = base, hips, torso, head, neck, abdomen, tail, spinner, legs, shins, arms, forearms, hands,
    coxae, ears, wings, eyes, jaws, fangs) is anchored to the vanilla part its body bone maps to (walkers: torso and hips on `body`, `arm_r` on
    `right_arm`...; beasts and the chicken: `neck` and `head` on `head`; spider: torso on `body0`, abdomen on `body1`) and moved from the form's
    box onto vanilla's grown to the rung: a point outside keeps its distance from the face it's beside, one inside spreads with it; plates on a
    body bone move cube by cube, a chain (crowns, horns, claws, petals, crystals) moves with its root. Vanilla rest boxes are read from 26.3's
    models (FA keeps vanilla's joints). `living.client.forms.FormExtras`, one layer per species' vanilla renderer, draws each part's pieces as
    one baked model, carried by that part's pose from its own fields times the inverse of its vanilla rest (not `translateAndRotate`, which EMF
    moves to the hand on an arm), in the form's skin and glow. The form's own clips, cued moves, life layer, halos and fall don't run then: FA
    acts it all. The forms' eyes are `FormLayers`' as at D. LITE and OFF, no EMF, or no model for a species: as before.
14. **Perf.** Per entity one `FormBody`, created on first sight, reused; no allocation per frame; halos past 48 blocks skipped; the life layer's
    springs past 32 as elsewhere. Rigs: at most 60 bones (tested). Server: one cue per move, one dimension refresh per form change.
- Not yet (F3 follow-ups): presence motes at A and S and heavy footfalls, distance LOD for sub-pixel growth, a voice layer per family
  (`audio_living.py`), the wind-up light trail at S, a gallery command. The vanilla cow and pig variants (warm, cold) are not read: the form's
  own family paints them.
- Dev: `/awaken living form <species> <rung> [family]`, `/awaken living formrow <species> [family]`; tour `tools/autopilot/forms-parade.txt`.
- Tests: `forms_bodies` (every species and rung has a rig that passes its checks, its clips, its paints and coats), `forms_fit` (with a model pack every non-body bone rides a vanilla part, none lost, each by its part), `forms_size` (the hitbox follows the form on the server),
  `forms_cue` (the cue codec round-trips; the second blow's caps), plus `living_form_mix`, `living_form_state`, `living_form_moves`.

## 22. Lens 2 (cinematic light on Vulkan and Apple Silicon; Euan's brief 2026-10-25, three steps, one builder)

Lens's Cinematic and Ultra tiers become a light model of their own: shadows, contact darkness and warm/cool light
without rendering the world a second time from the sun, built for the M4's tile GPU (few full-size passes, the heavy
work at reduced size, temporal accumulation). Target: his reference (a golden-hour valley), dialed down a little.
Swift is unchanged. L1 light and shadow (this section, below); L2 atmosphere and a look per gate theme; L3 water and
magic.

- **Tiers** (client config `lens` = OFF | SWIFT | CINEMATIC | ULTRA; chains `awaken:lens_swift`, `lens_cinematic`,
  `lens_ultra`). Budgets on the M4 at 2560×1440, Vulkan, RD 32: where Lens off holds 120 fps, Cinematic 90+ and Ultra
  60+. The Look switch's Ultra tier is now Lens Ultra (no Iris: Iris is OpenGL-only and its Sodium pin crashes on
  NeoForge 26.3.0.95), selectable on every backend; its budgets are Cinematic p50 ≤ 11.1 ms / p99 ≤ 20 ms and Ultra
  ≤ 16.7 / ≤ 25 ms. With an Iris shaderpack on, no tier is current and Lens steps aside as before.
- **Rain** (Euan, 2026-10-28: replace the blue rain with restrained rain that fits Lens): an original 64×256 RGBA
  texture at `minecraft:textures/environment/rain.png`, generated by `tools/art/specs/lens_rain.py`. Twenty-eight
  narrow one-pixel streaks, 8-22 texels long, silver-grey RGB 194-218 with tapered alpha below 145; transparent between
  drops, no blue pigment, opaque bands or extra rain veil. It replaces the texture in the game's existing weather batch.
  The vanilla lightmap, world/storm rain strength, roof/ground heightmap clipping, dry biomes, weather radius setting,
  snowfall, sound and splash rules remain vanilla; Lens grades the same frame afterwards. Lens off still gets neutral
  rain under vanilla lighting; an external resource pack may override this texture normally. Rolling Storm's distant
  rain shafts/curtain are unchanged. **Splash** (Euan, 2026-10-30: the splash on the ground was still blue): vanilla's
  `minecraft:rain` particle shares `minecraft:splash`'s deep-blue sprites, so `minecraft:particles/rain.json` now names
  `awaken:rain_splash_0..3` (same generator): 8×8, one to three fully opaque pixels (the particle draws on the opaque
  layer), a crown of grey 200 over a body of grey 170, the streaks' grey without their fade. The water splash
  (`minecraft:splash`: swimming, fish, a bobber) keeps vanilla's blue. No mixin, custom renderer, shader change, scene
  copy, extra particle, draw or post pass. Static incremental work: the same 64 KiB base texture, samplers, vertices and draws; no new per-frame CPU work.
  Lower alpha does not reduce the existing quad overdraw, so no frame-time saving or measured GPU cost is claimed.
  `lens_rain_texture` checks the packaged dimensions, neutral colour, sparse coverage and opacity, and that the rain
  particle names the four grey splash sprites, each opaque and neutral. Offline contact-sheet
  inspection covers overcast, forest, night and lamplight; roof/dry/snow/settings preservation follows from leaving the
  extraction/rendering path unchanged. No client, GPU timing or in-game visual acceptance was performed.
- **Chain** (Cinematic, Ultra): far-depth probe and trust (two 1-px passes) → **sun map** (`lens_sunmap.fsh`, L2) →
  **light** (`lens_light.fsh`, 960×540 on Cinematic, 1440×810 on Ultra since the L2 tour; uniform `LensConfig.Quality`
  1 or 2) → blit
  into the persistent `awaken:lens_hist` → Lens's bloom and shafts passes → **composite** (`lens_composite_lit.fsh` =
  the Swift composite's body, `include/lens_composite.glsl`, with `LENS_LIGHT` defined) → blit. 13 passes against
  Swift's 9; full-size passes stay two (composite and its blit), as before. Measured at L1 (no sun map yet), the extra
  cost barely changed between Cinematic's and Ultra's light buffer, so it's per-pass and full-size work, not tracing:
  L2 folds volumetric light into the light pass and the fog glow into the composite instead of adding passes. 26.3 post targets are RGBA8 only and fixed-size (or screen-size), so values that need precision travel in
  float textures (below) and the light buffer packs its distance into two bytes.
- **Frame texture** `awaken:lens_frame` (`LensFrame`, 24×1 RGBA32F, written in `RenderLevelStageEvent.AfterLevel`,
  just before the post effects, nothing allocated): 0-3 inverse view-projection, 4-7 view-projection, 8-11 last
  frame's view-projection (all camera-relative; the projection the world was really drawn with, below), 12 the camera
  in the heightfield ring (x, z modulo 1024; y absolute; w a frame counter), 13 the camera's
  move since last frame and whether history is usable (not after a teleport over 24 blocks, a gap over 0.25 s, a new
  dimension or the chain starting), 14 toward the light and its strength, 15 the heightfield (size, highest surface,
  trusted radius 496 blocks), 16 zero-to-one depth, moon, rain, near plane, 21 the sun on screen (uv; z 1 ahead of the
  camera: the shafts and the halo use it on Cinematic and Ultra, Swift keeps the parameter texture's). Layout in
  `shaders/include/lens_frame.glsl`.
- **The world's own projection** (`WorldProjection` in `dev.awaken.lens.client`, `core/world_projection.fsh`; Euan
  2026-10-27: strafing and flying with Camera Overhaul, "I can visibly see shadows moving around ... the ground itself
  becomes darker and moves as I move"). `GameRenderer.renderLevel` multiplies its bob pose stack into the projection,
  and a camera mod may add to that stack: Camera Overhaul rolls it by up to about 10° as you strafe, turn and fly, and
  sways it at rest (at the head of `bobHurt`, so before the game's own bob). That matrix exists only in the level's
  projection uniform buffer (no CPU copy, no event hands it out), so every CPU rebuild of it (the game's bob, hurt tilt
  and nausea) missed the roll. In Lens, every pass that rebuilds a position from depth (sun shadows, contact shadows,
  AO, normals, volumetric light, clouds) and the temporal reprojection worked with a camera rolled differently from the
  picture, and the shading slid and darkened across the ground as the roll changed; Pixels' steady pass ghosted; the
  Holo HUD's panels rolled with the world.
  - **The pass.** On a frame a user asked for it (`WorldProjection.want()` before the level draws: Lens on Cinematic or
    Ultra, Pixels' steady pass, a Holo panel showing; nothing runs otherwise, Lens off or not), a highest-priority
    `AfterLevel` listener takes the bound projection (perspective only; the buffer is the level's, written once a frame
    before the world draws) and a one-row pass (18×1 RGBA32F, two targets in turn, the projection block bound as
    `Projection`) writes: 0-3 the inverse view-projection, 4-7 the view-projection, 8-11 last frame's, 12 the sun on
    screen, 13-16 this frame's NDC to last frame's clip space with the camera's step (Pixels), 17 the roll a camera mod
    adds (`inverse(camera projection) × world projection × inverse(game's bob)`, its angle about the view axis). History
    holds across ordinary frames (not a teleport over 24 blocks, a gap over 0.25 s or a frame without the pass).
  - **Users.** Lens copies texels 0-11 and 12 over its CPU estimate in the frame texture (texels 0-11 and 21) and in
    Tiles' uniform block (four GPU copies); the shafts and the lit composite's halo read the sun from texel 21 (Swift
    keeps the parameter texture's). Pixels' steady pass copies texels 13-16 into its uniform buffer on the GPU when both
    its own and the pass's history hold. The Holo HUD reads the roll back to the CPU (a 16-byte copy, four buffers in
    turn, a frame or two late; ignored once 0.25 s old) and puts it before the game's bob in what it undoes, so its
    panels stay level under the roll (during a quick change of roll they trail it by those frames).
  - The game's own bob (`WorldProjection.vanillaBob`) is one copy shared by all three. No mixin, no access transformer;
    the cost is one 18-pixel draw and a few copies of a few hundred bytes (not yet measured on the M4: the Lens bench runs
    on the Mac, not on CI). Where the pipeline doesn't compile, or the bound projection isn't perspective, each user's
    CPU estimate stands, as before. Development: client command `/awaken lens projection off|on|check` (off: every
    user's CPU estimate, for A/B; check: the latest roll read back).
- **Heightfield** `awaken:lens_height` (`LensHeightfield`, 1024×1024 RGBA16F since "Shadows beyond the block map"
  (b a roof's underside, a the floor under it), mips 1-4 hold the max of their 2×2 (the min for b); about
  5.6 MB on the GPU and the same off-heap mirror): from the client chunks' own heightmaps (26.3 sends MOTION_BLOCKING
  and MOTION_BLOCKING_NO_LEAVES to the client): r the top of everything that blocks motion (leaves included), g
  without leaves. **The heightfield sees every solid block** (`LensHeights`, Euan 2026-10-29: "in a closed room the
  shadow on the wall moves with me instead of staying where it is. It's the shadow of the light coming through the
  door"): 26.3 builds those heightmaps from `#minecraft:blocks_motion`, which holds the game's blocks and only the mod
  blocks a tag adds, so a room of Carillon's city bricks under clay tiles read as open sky. Lens lit it as it lights
  the street, and only the screen-space contact shadows (the door frame's, at most 3 blocks long) shaped that light,
  so it slid with the view. Each column also takes in, from its highest block of any kind down to the heightmap's own
  top, the first block the tag skips that the game still counts as solid (`isSolid`: a collision box most of a block,
  or a whole block high; never leaves, which the tag holds) as the top of both. Only sections whose palettes hold such a block are
  walked, so land without one costs one palette check a section and a chunk read. Swift's camera cover (texel 21)
  takes the same rule at the camera's column. A room of any block now reads as covered: the model's fade under cover
  and the 85% floor hold inside it, and its light no longer rests on the screen-space contact shadows alone, so it
