  stays put as you walk. Since 2026-10-30 every solid Awaken block is in the tag (§1, "Blocks that stop motion"), so
  the walk catches only another mod's untagged block; the kinds vanilla leaves out (signs, webs, layers) are no roof
  here either. GameTest `lens_heights_skipped_roof`;
  tour `tools/autopilot/lens-door-light-look.txt` (the same room in stone bricks and in city bricks under clay tiles,
  a door toward the morning sun, from four places across it).
  A ring addressed by world block modulo 1024, a 64×64-chunk window centred on the camera's chunk: a chunk
  entering the window clears its slot and is read nearest first (40 a tick), a loaded chunk is read when it arrives
  (`ChunkEvent.Load` on the client), the 5×5 chunks around the camera are re-read every 10 ticks and the rest of the
  window 12 a tick in turn (block changes show within about ten seconds; halved for the CPU after L3), and a slot uploads only when its hash changed,
  as the changed chunks only: a tick's changes as one box per level when they fit in 64 chunks (a recentre's new
  column or row), else up to 8 rows a tick, each the span of its changed chunks (packed through one staging buffer;
  whole-width strips cost 320 barriered copies per step east or west, docs/perf/CITY-FPS.md). Built only where the dimension has the overworld sky.
- **Light pass** (per pixel of the reduced buffer, from the full-size depth): position and normal from depth (of the
  two neighbours per axis the one continuing the centre's plane; a normal within 0.9 of an axis snaps to it, since
  block faces are axis-aligned), then:
  - **Sun shadow from the heightfield**: from the surface (nudged 0.06 along its normal) toward the light, in two
    parts. Near: every column the ray crosses, cell by cell, for the first 10 cells on Cinematic / 16 on Ultra, each
    tested at the ray's lowest point over it (where it enters, since it climbs), so a step's or a wall's shadow is
    whole and crisp to its far edge. Far: 15 / 24 steps from there, each longer than the last (to about 250 blocks, the
    same reach as before), steps testing a whole max cell (mip by the stride) so a stride can't skip a ridge. Solid →
    shadow; through leaves the light fades (exp(-0.9 × the length through the cell or the stride)) for flecks under
    trees. Stops above the window's highest surface or past the trusted radius. A heightmap counts a slab, stair or
    fence as a whole block (a carpet not at all), so a surface's own column only counts from a block above it; a point
    more than a block under its column's solid top (a roof, a cave) gets no sun.
    Why the near part (Euan 2026-10-29, "shadows break in the corner of my screen"): with point samples alone, a
    one-block step's shadow came in two strengths. Toward its far edge the ray is under the step's top for only a
    short wedge, and the strides there (0.6 to 0.75 blocks) jumped it about half the time, so the shadow faded out
    partway, with a stepped edge against the stretch beside the step's corner that the march still caught. The near
    walk costs about what the steps it replaces did (10 + 15 lookups on Cinematic for 24).
    The ray leans across a sun disc about 1.4° wide (0.012 radians in radius), by each pixel's noise each frame, so a
    shadow's edge is a penumbra that widens away from what casts it and the frames smooth it below the light buffer's
    texels. A crisp edge at 960 × 540 would show as four-pixel stairs on a 4K screen.
  - **Contact shadows**: 6 / 12 steps through the depth buffer toward the light, 0.35 to 3 blocks (longer far off):
    mobs, grass, slabs and block edges the heightfield can't hold. Within 96 blocks. A hit within 4% of the screen's
    edge counts less, down to nothing at the edge, so they fade out there rather than end in a line where the march
    runs off the screen. Whatever is off the screen is the heightfield's, which never depends on the screen.
  - **The small shade's reach** (12 Nov; `lens_light.fsh` `texelArt`, `smallKeep`; frame texels 30 to 33 w). Euan,
    playing at 4K over a meadow of tall grass: "there's so much going on in such a small area of view ... can we
    change the logic of how shadow is on swaying grass so that it just makes it look less shimmery? Because like
    right now I'm on native 4K and it still just looks very shimmery". The contact shadows are made from the light
    buffer's own depth, one sample a texel, and in a meadow what casts them is a blade or a stem one or two of the
    art's pixels wide. Far off a texel spans several blades and the gaps between them, so its one sample lands on a
    blade in one frame and on the ground behind in the next as the camera breathes and the plants sway, and the
    shade flips: dark flecks to the horizon. So the contact shadows are kept while the buffer can see what casts
    them and let go as it can't: whole where a light texel is up to **0.6** of an art pixel wide on the surface,
    gone by **2.2** (a smoothstep between; at a 90 degree view 10 and 37 blocks, where the crisp light near the eye
    also starts to go over to the smooth read). The measure follows the view: a wider view lets go sooner, a
    spyglass keeps the shade of the far grass it brings near. Past the fade the march is not run at all (one
    unprojection a pixel is the whole cost of the rule). **The ambient shade keeps its own reach** (the composite
    fades it from 48 to 96 blocks): measured, it darkens grass evenly and adds no flecks, and far buildings keep
    their corners. Trees', hills' and the block map's shadows are untouched.
    Measured on a built meadow (tools/autopilot/steady60-meadow-ci.txt, tools/lens/meadow.py; runs 43166685979 for
    the stills by part and 43173148812 for the rest; 2880x1800, the bands by where a row's ground lies, within a
    tenth: a spectator's view is a little wider than its setting). Stills: the contact shadows add about 40% to the
    grass's local contrast at every distance (8.8 to 10.7 against 6.1 to 7.4 without them) and darken it by 17 to
    20%; the ambient shade darkens it by about 14% and adds none. With the camera drifting half a pixel a frame and
    the plants held still, mean change between frames in 8-bit steps and the share of pixels changing by more than
    12 (two bursts each, within 5% of each other):

    | about | as it was | with the reach | no contact shadows | Swift (the game's own grass) |
    |---|---|---|---|---|
    | 5 to 11 blocks | 4.48, 8.7% | 4.43, 8.5% | 3.07, 4.8% | 2.69, 5.3% |
    | 11 to 23 | 5.96, 12.9% | 5.24, 10.2% | 4.24, 7.1% | 4.28, 9.2% |
    | 23 to 53 | 6.32, 12.2% | 4.96, 7.3% | 4.86, 6.8% | 5.77, 11.6% |
    | beyond | 2.62, 3.5% | 2.11, 2.4% | 2.05, 2.3% | 3.15, 3.8% |

    With the plants swaying in a held breeze as well: 11 to 23 blocks 7.67, 19.2% to 6.14, 13.4% (none 5.58, 12.3%);
    23 to 53 blocks 5.80, 10.0% to 4.41, 5.4% (none 4.67, 6.2%). In the stills the grass 23 to 53 blocks off is 28%
    less busy (local contrast 10.9 to 7.8, none 7.7) and 12% lighter; 11 to 23 blocks 13% less busy and 5% lighter;
    nearer, unchanged. What is left is the game's own: Swift's grass, with none of Lens's light, flips 9 to 12% of
    its pixels 11 to 53 blocks off under the same drift (cutout blades thinner than a pixel), which no shade of
    Lens's can go under. A first reach of 1 to 3 art pixels (17 to 51 blocks, run 43170794805) calmed 23 blocks and
    beyond the same and left 11 to 23 as it was (12.1% against 13.3%). The real wind with Camera Overhaul's sway
    (run 43168733918) could not rank anything: the same setting measured twice differed by 60% with the gusts.
    In play: `/awaken lens small <contact from> <to> <ambient from> <to>` (art pixels a light texel; the answer
    gives the blocks at the view in use; an end not past its start: no fade; `setting`: the built-in reach), so
    `/awaken lens small 0 0 0 0` is the picture as it was.
  - **The edge's hold** (12 Nov; `lens_light.fsh`, the contact shadows' `known`; frame texel 34 w). Euan, playing:
    "on the very left edge of my screen, I can see the shadows disappearing basically as I turn my camera. And the
    closer the thing is to me, the more obvious that is ... even with a smaller FOV, that still happens ... I can see
    them basically disappearing and then reappearing." A block's, a tree's or a hill's shadow is worked out in the
    world and never depends on the screen. A flower's, a grass tuft's, a fence's, a chest's or a mob's is a contact
    shadow, made from the screen's own depth: when what casts it slides off the screen its shadow, still in view, had
    nothing to be made from, and the march that ran off the screen answered "lit". Near the eye those shadows are a
    block and a half long, so the strip that lost them along the sun's side of the screen was wide. The march now says
    how far its answer is known (0 where it ran off the screen, the old 4% ramp for a hit at the very edge), and what
    is not known is what it was: last frame's light for the surface over this frame's light without contact shadows is
    the share they took, which is kept and let go by 0.12 a frame before the buffer's own mix (about a second in all
    at 60 frames a second), so a turn carries its shadows out with it and a mob that walked off leaves none standing.
    No history, no hold: the unknown is lit, as before. No extra samples (the history is already read).
    Checked (tools/autopilot/steady60-edgehold-ci.txt, run 43188196485; fence posts and poppies two to four blocks
    round the camera, a turn of a degree a tick away from the sun's side, one shot at the end of each turn): after 14
    and 20 degrees the poppy's shadow lies on the ground with the poppy off the screen, where without the hold the
    ground is bare; five seconds later, at rest, it has gone in both (`edge-hold-before-after.jpg` in
    docs/perf/steady60/play-2026-11-12). The first run of that tour (43186252840) shot during the turn and showed
    nothing held: a screenshot stalls the runner past the 250 ms the light buffer keeps its history for.
    **What it cannot do**: a shadow whose caster has not come onto the screen yet is still unknown (it comes in with
    its caster, over the edge's ramp), and at rest the strip on the sun's side is without small shadows once the hold
    has let go. Only casters held in the world would cure those (plants and small blocks in the block map: not built).
    `/awaken lens edgehold off|on|setting` for A/B in play.
  - **Ambient occlusion**: 6 / 10 cosine-weighted samples in a 0.9-block hemisphere against the depth buffer. Within
    96 blocks. A sample off the screen counts as open, so the screen's edge is a little lighter. Averaging only the
    samples on screen was tried (2026-10-29) and made the edge darker than the middle instead (the samples left on
    screen there lean toward the occluded side).
  - **Temporal accumulation**: each frame uses fresh noise (interleaved gradient noise stepped per frame) and blends
    into last frame's result reprojected by the frame matrices (0.14 new on Cinematic, 0.1 on Ultra); of the 2×2
    history texels only those that saw the same distance count (disocclusion), dithered into 8 bits so slow changes
    still move. Out: r sun, g ambient occlusion, b volumetric light (L2), a the distance in one byte (log2(d+1)/13,
    about 3.6% steps; 0 for sky); texels of the history and of the upsample count when within 1.5 steps.
  - Never within 1.25 blocks (the first-person hand, whose depth 26.3 merges into the main depth while post effects
    run, and the holo glass at 0.62 m): not shadowed, never an occluder.
- **Composite light** (before the haze; the frame is display-encoded, so a multiplier m on linear light is applied as
  √m): the light buffer upsampled by distance (of its 2×2 texels the ones that saw this surface), the normal again at
  full size (from screen derivatives where the pixel's 2×2 quad lies on one surface, the four-tap version only across
  an edge), then a warm key where the sun reaches (noon (1.04, 1.02, 0.97); golden hour, by the sunrise colour's
  strength × `keyWarmth`, (1.30, 1.03, 0.72); the moon (0.93, 0.98, 1.08)) and a cool shade where it doesn't
  (`shadeTint` × (1 − `shade`), deepened 30% at golden hour and up to 35% with distance, 24 to 160 blocks, so long
  shadows stay readable across the land; warmed a little at golden hour by light bounced off sunlit ground). Sunlit
  colour gains up to 16% saturation at golden hour, and the distance haze takes a share of the sunrise colour, so a
  golden-hour vista reads warmer and richer, not greyer (the orchestrator's note on L1's sheet). Faces turned from the sun shade only as it lowers (none
  at noon, when Minecraft's sun is straight overhead and the game's own face shading stays; all by golden hour). The
  model fades out under solid cover (1 to 7 blocks of it: a ledge is shade, a roofed room is left as the game lit it,
  torches and all; a column with open sky in one of its four neighbours counts that neighbour's cover, so the ground
  under an eave or a gable's rake takes the lawn's shade instead of a room's, with no step along the roof line: Euan's
  cottage, 2026-10-28; four more heightfield reads, only where the column is covered), toward the end of the render distance (85-100%), in the game's thick fog (as the haze does) and
  within 1.45 blocks. Strength: the sun's height (none at the horizon crossing), a faint moon (0.4) by night, rain
  (−85%) and thunder (−50%); 0 where there's no overworld sky. Golden hour is the more of the sunrise colour's strength
  and the sun's height (full below sin 0.1, none above 0.5; the sunrise colour alone only peaks as the sun touches the
  horizon). Ambient occlusion applies everywhere, by day and night,
  fading out from 48 to 96 blocks. It only darkens, so the never-lift rule holds.
- **Filmic curve** (`filmic`, in place of the plain contrast clamp): past white, colour runs toward white instead of
  clipping its hue; the top tenth rolls off with tanh (white itself within 3% of white); contrast is an S around
  mid-grey with the look's slope there, then a black point of 0.45 × (contrast − 1), as deep as the plain contrast's,
  so night and shade keep their depth. Not on the open sky, where the sun's glow keeps its soft blow-out (a shoulder
  there showed the sun's square disc).
- **Under cover, never darker than the game** (Euan, 2026-10-29, mining: "Shaders whole mining are completely broken,
  my tool is black, shadows are broken"): every tier, after the grade and before the story's crush, the focus dim, frost
  and the vignette. Under solid cover a pixel keeps at least 85% of what the game drew there, per channel, fully for
  the game's darks (luma up to 0.05) and easing out by 0.22, so the mids and lights keep the look's contrast. Without
  it the grade's black point (0.45 × (contrast − 1); the cave looks run 1.08-1.16) and the cool shadow tint took a
  cave at light 0 (the lightmap's ambient on Bright, about 6% grey on stone) and a hand or tool held there to pure
  black, so every face the light didn't reach read as a hard black shape. A cave stays as dark and moody as the game
  made it, never a black void; a Lightless gate is still as dark as the game draws it. Cover: Cinematic and Ultra per
  pixel, 0.5 to 1.5 blocks of solid heightfield (`g`) over the air in front of the surface (its point 0.3 blocks
  toward the camera, so a trunk's or a cliff's own column never counts as its cover; a dark doorway seen from the
  street does count; not the open sky, far terrain or Holo plates; not past the heightfield's trusted reach); Swift by the
  camera (texel 21 r: the client's MOTION_BLOCKING_NO_LEAVES top, with the blocks it skips, above the eye + 0.5, eased over about a sixth of a
  second). The open land, by day and by night, is untouched.
- **Within arm's reach, never darker than the game at all** (Euan, 2026-10-29, "some more shadow issues with
  underground torches held here": the torch in his hand was dark): every tier, right after the cover floor, a pixel
  within 1.25 blocks of the eye (your hand and what it holds, a wall at your nose) keeps at least what the game drew
  there, whatever its brightness, easing out by 1.45 blocks as Lens's light eases in (Lens 2's light already leaves that
  reach alone). The cover floor's 85% eases out by luma 0.22, so a handle lit by its own flame (about 0.15) still took
  the cave look's grade, about 35% darker than the game drew it. Lens may still lift it (the grade's highlights), never
  lower it. Not the sky or far terrain. With it the held light gives its bearer its whole level (§28.3), so the torch,
  the hand and the tool in the other hand read as lit by the flame they hold. The black faces in the same report were
  the held light's, not Lens's (a torch pressed to a block flooded from inside it, so the face looking at you kept the
  game's light 0; §28.3); Lens's shade and ambient occlusion take a face to about 45% at most, never to black. Tour
  `tools/autopilot/held-light-faces-look.txt` (a block row at arm's length, a cave mouth at sunset and a sealed room).
- **Look fields** (looks*.json, inherited from `default`; texels 17-19): `light` 1.0, `shade` 0.32, `shadeTint`
  [0.86, 0.93, 1.14], `keyWarmth` 0.8, `ao` 0.65, `filmic` 1.0; L2: `mist` 0.5, `mistHeight` 48 (blocks), `fogGlow`
  0.15, `skyGlow` 0.3. Texel 19: r mist, g mistHeight/256, b fogGlow/2, a skyGlow.
- **Debug views** (`lensdebug`, Cinematic/Ultra): 5 the light buffer (r sun, g AO), 6 normals with direct sun, 7 the
  light alone (grey 0.5 = unchanged), 8 the classic Cinematic (no Lens 2 light, plain contrast) on the same frame, for
  before/after shots.
- **Not used**: mediump. Desktop GLSL 330 through shaderc and SPIRV-Cross gives MoltenVK no half-precision path, so the
  bandwidth savings come from RGBA8 targets at reduced size instead. A real shadow map (rendering the world from the
  sun) is out of scope: the heightfield covers terrain, trees and buildings; contact shadows cover mobs.
- Tour: `tools/autopilot/lens2-l1.txt` (a lab plot with trees, pillars, a gazebo, slabs, carpets, mobs and a torch-lit
  room; Carillon at golden hour into and away from the sun; noon; night; the holo menu; debug views; a frame-time bench
  of off / Swift / Cinematic / Ultra at 2560×1440, RD 32). L1 measured (busy Carillon vista at golden hour, p50/p99
  ms): off 10.59/15.30, Swift 11.20/17.18, Cinematic 13.01/17.95, Ultra 13.16/18.36: Cinematic +2.4 ms over off,
  Ultra +2.6 ms, inside both budgets. A four-way diagnostic (`lens2-diag.txt`, one pillar, the light buffer facing N, E,
  S, W) proved the shadow direction from every side.
- The heightfield's scattered uploads go round the ring from where the last tick stopped (8 rows a tick), so a row
  that keeps changing near the camera can't starve the rest.

**L2, atmosphere**
- **Sun map** (`lens_sunmap.fsh`, `awaken:lens_sunmap`, 512×512 cells of 2 blocks on Cinematic, 1024×1024 of 1 block
  on Ultra, rebuilt every frame): for each column of the heightfield ring, the height above which the sun reaches it
  (the highest ridge, roof or canopy toward the sun less the light's drop over the distance), solid in r/g and with
  leaves in b/a (two bytes each, -256..768 blocks in 1/64 steps). Its march (24 / 32 steps, max mips by stride) stops
  as soon as nothing further toward the sun could rise above what it has, so most stop in a few steps.
- **Volumetric light** (in the light pass, its blue channel; it replaces adding a pass): along each view ray to the
  surface (or 192 / 320 blocks into the sky), 8 / 16 jittered samples of the sun map (lit, in a shadow, or under
  leaves at 35%) in a mist lying on the land: thickest at the height of the ground under the camera (its heightfield
  column; sea level 63 where unknown) and thinning above it, exp(-(y - ground) / mistHeight), so valleys fill and the
  air over a mountain stays clear (at sea level only, it vanished wherever the land is high); optical depth 0.0016 per
  block × `mist` × the look's `shafts` × the light's strength, sent toward the eye by a Henyey-Greenstein phase (g 0.6,
  plus a 0.06 floor), so beams show strongest toward the sun and the air away from it stays clear. Accumulated over
  frames (0.2 new on Cinematic, 0.15 on Ultra). The composite adds it (screen) in the light's colour × 1.6, and keeps
  the screen-space shafts at half (0.7) for what the sun map can't hold: clouds crossing the sun. Classic (view 8)
  shows the old shafts alone.
- **Fog glow** (lights glowing in haze, the gates' light pools): the shafts pass (quarter size, its g/b/a) spreads the
  wide bloom layer again over two rings of six taps (3.5% and 7.5% of the screen out) and the centre; the composite
  adds it tinted toward the haze colour, × `fogGlow` × 3. (At L2's tour it sat in the full-size composite with nine
  taps a pixel: too costly, and too diffuse to read as light pools.)
- **Sky scattering**: the sky, and the haze over terrain, brighten around the light's direction (pow(μ, 8) × 0.25 +
  pow(μ, 48) × 0.35 in the light's colour, × `skyGlow` (0.3 since L4: wider, it washed half the golden-hour sky
  white), warmer at golden hour). Clouds are in the depth
  buffer, so they take the key and shade like terrain (their sunlit tops warm, their undersides cool).
- **Gate looks**: each theme's biome (`awaken:gate_<theme>`) has a look of its own, `biome:awaken:gate_<theme>` in
  `assets/awaken/lens/looks_gates.json` (all 15 themes; the camera's biome picks it as for any biome, so no new sync).
  Every field is written out (a biome look inherits from `default`, the overworld). No sun in gates (`light` 0, `mist`
  0); their magic is the grade, haze toward the theme's colour, `ao` 0.5-0.85 and `fogGlow` 0.3 (Sky Archipelago) to 1.3
  (Lantern Night Market). Swift uses the same looks for its grade and haze (fogGlow and ao need Cinematic).
- **Ambient particles** (`LensParticles`, types `awaken:lens_mote|ember|frost|spore|wisp|breath` registered by
  `LensModule` on both sides, sprites from `tools/art/specs/lens_fx.py`: smooth white light sprites, tinted per place,
  never vanilla's): spawned on the client within about 12 blocks of the camera (more ahead), only on Cinematic (half)
  and Ultra, scaled by the Particles setting (Minimal: none), never during a story scene. Each gate theme has its mix
  (Ember Mines embers and ash, Fungal Hollow teal and violet spores, Hive honey spores, Frost Monastery falling frost,
  Spirit themes wisps, Drowned Archive rising motes, ...); the Nether has embers; the overworld by day has dust that
  spawns only in sunlit air (a CPU march of the heightfield mirror toward the sun) and glints when it's between you and
  the sun. Your breath shows every 3-4 s in first person in the Frost Monastery and wherever it snows. Embers, spores,
  wisps and dust are full bright (Lens's bloom picks them up); frost and breath take the world's light. Gate rates are
  ×1.5 the table's since the L2 tour, and every kind half as big again (they read as specks).
- L2 measured (same vista as L1, p50/p99 ms): off 9.00/13.61, Swift 8.94/14.12, Cinematic 13.13/23.75, Ultra
  16.14/23.66. Ultra holds 60; Cinematic (+4.1 ms) missed 90, so after that tour: the fog glow moved to the quarter-size
  shafts pass, normals from screen derivatives, Cinematic's light buffer 960×540 (24 sun, 6 contact, 8 volume steps),
  Ultra's 1440×810. Measured again in L3's tour.

**L3, water and magic** (looks: `water` 0.6, `heat` 0, `frost` 0, `glow` 0.6 by default; texel 20: r water, g heat,
b frost, a glow; the frame texture's texel 17 x is seconds, wrapping hourly)
- **Water**: the heightfield marks open-water columns (a solid top at the block's base + 0.75, exact in half floats up
  to y 512; the occluder loses nothing). A pixel whose surface lies on such a column's water level (base + 0.889) is
  water; where water draws without depth the pixel shows what's under it, and the reflection sits where the view ray
  crossed the water's surface. Rippling normals (two sines each way, by world position and time), Schlick Fresnel
  (F0 0.02). The reflection: the frame where the reflected ray meets open sky on screen, else the fog's colour; on
  Ultra a 20-step screen-space march of the reflected ray against the depth buffer (nearest first, fading at the
  frame's edge) reflects the scene itself. The sun's glint (pow(R·L, 240) × 5, none in the water's own shade) in the
  light's colour: the reference's glinting river. × `water` and the fog fade. Only where the heightfield is built (an
  overworld sky).
- **Emissive glow**: AWAKEN's glows (bright, saturated, not a warm hue: runes, vortices, the Signal's blue, eyes, the
  gate pillars) bloom up to 2.5× as much as lit surfaces of the same brightness (the prefilter, by `glow`; all tiers),
  and keep their light in Lens 2's shade (the shade's weight × (1 − glowness × `glow`)). They glow through fog
  because the bloom is made before the haze and the fog glow spreads it. No creature was repainted.
- **Heat shimmer** (`heat`: the Nether 0.45, Ember Mines 0.55, Glass Desert 0.4): the frame is read through rippling
  offsets (up to about 0.2% of the screen, more in the lower frame), Cinematic and Ultra only.
- **Frost** (`frost`: Frost Monastery 0.6): frost creeps in from the frame's edges (a band up to 11% of the height ×
  frost, deeper at the corners, crystalline refraction in it and a pale rime with fine streaks over it).
- `glow` 0.9 for the Spirit and Charge themes and the Mirror Palace, 0.8 for the Ember Mines.
- Tour: `tools/autopilot/lens2-l3.txt` (a pool in the lab into the sun, glowing creatures at dusk and night,
  Carillon's river, the Ember Mines' shimmer, the Frost Monastery's frost, the bench).
- L3 measured (with L2's fixes; same vista, p50/p99 ms): off 8.00/12.39 (122 fps), Swift 7.93/11.94, Cinematic
  11.02/16.67 (about 90 fps), Ultra 12.99/19.79 (77 fps): both tiers on budget. The tour harness's `gate interior
  enter` landed in other themes' gates, so heat and frost weren't in its shots.

**L4, volumetric clouds** (Euan, 2026-10-25: "the blocky clouds just aren't it")
- On Cinematic and Ultra Lens draws its own clouds wherever the game would draw clouds (the frame's cloud colour has
  alpha and the player's Clouds setting isn't Off) and the look's `clouds` (cover, default 0.45; 0 keeps the game's) is
  above 0. In `ExtractLevelRenderStateEvent` Lens takes the frame's cloud height and colour and clears that colour's
  alpha, so vanilla's clouds skip that frame; the setting itself is never touched (Swift, Off and a shaderpack keep the
  game's clouds). Rain thickens the cover by up to 0.4. Frame texels 18-19: base height (0: none), cover, the camera's
  x and z plus the wind's drift (0.04 blocks a game tick east) modulo 30720; the cloud colour.
- Shape (`include/lens_clouds.glsl`): a cumulus layer from 6 blocks under the game's cloud height, 84 blocks thick.
  Cover 0.45 leaves most of the sky open between distinct clouds (a coverage threshold of 1 − 0.72 × cover, edges 0.1
  wide), closing into an overcast deck toward 0.95; the threshold rises with height (0.16 × h²), so each cloud narrows
  upward into a dome and only the thickest rise tall (flat 2D cover read as vertical curtains). One tileable noise
  texture, `awaken:lens_cloud_noise` (256×256 RGBA, made in the frequency domain by
  `tools/art/specs/lens_clouds.py`: r coverage, g shape, b billows, a wisps), sampled at 3072, 960, 256 and 120 blocks
  a repeat (all dividing 30720) for where clouds stand and their outlines; their billows are two octaves of a cheap 3D
  value noise in world space (46 and 17 blocks on Ultra, one octave at 38 on Cinematic; flat noise slid with height
  drew vertical streaks), skipped deep inside a cloud. The cover slides up to 45 blocks with height (two noise channels,
  opposite ways; only in the main march, not the light-step and shadow look-ups), so a cloud's sides lean and break
  up instead of standing as straight walls. Flat-ish bases,
  domes that rise where a cloud is thick, billows eating the edges.
- Pass `lens_clouds.fsh` (560×315 on Cinematic, 800×450 on Ultra; then a blit into the persistent
  `awaken:lens_clouds_hist`): each ray marched through the layer (20 / 32 steps, up to 800 / 1100 blocks of it, never
  past nearer terrain), lit by 3 / 5 steps toward the light (doubling from 6 blocks): two octaves of Beer's law (the
  second, at 35% and a quarter of the extinction, stands in for light scattered many times inside, so bases stay soft
  grey-white), σ 0.03 per block, a powder term (thin sunward edges glow, dense cores darken), a phase of 0.85 + 0.9 × HG(0.6) (white from every side, a modest silver
  lining toward the sun; stronger forward lobes blew the sky round the sun out into one white mass), the sun's colour (warm at
  golden hour, the moon's at night) and the sky's light on them (a cool blue with a third of the horizon's colour, by
  the game's cloud colour but never below half and up to 1.95× toward overcast, so a grey sky stays bright grey; 60% at
  the base to 100% at the tops; the sun's light on them × 1.05). Distant cloud melts into the
  fog colour from 1500 blocks and is gone at 5000, so the deck never ends in a line. Accumulated over frames (0.15 /
  0.12 new), reprojected where the ray entered the layer. Out: rgb their light (premultiplied), a
  what shows through.
- The composite lays them over the sky and over anything farther than where the ray enters their layer, before the
  haze. The bloom prefilter (`lens_prefilter_lit.fsh`) folds them into the sky, so bright edges bloom, and the sky's
  alpha (what the screen-space shafts and the sun's halo read) carries 60% of their transmittance: rays break through
  gaps and the halo dims behind a cloud (all of it streaked the whole sky like rain curtains; the shafts also drop to
  0.35 in the composite). The shafts read the open sky's own brightness, not the clouds' (bright cloud tops seen from
  above streaked into rays). The light pass darkens the sun on the land under them (to 28% under thick cloud, along
  the light ray through the layer's middle) and, on Ultra at half strength, in the volumetric beams: moving cloud
  shadows and beams through gaps.
- First tour (bad8a542, 480×270, 20 steps, the first cover curve; p50 ms off 7.74, Swift 7.85, Cinematic 10.73, Ultra
  13.20: the clouds cost no net frame time, since the game's are no longer drawn): too much cover (a stormy deck),
  dark bellies, a hard line toward the horizon, a noise grid; tuned as above.
- Tour: `tools/autopilot/lens2-l4.txt` (Swift's clouds against Lens's: noon, golden hour into the sun, cloud shadows
  over Carillon, above the deck, rain, night; the bench). Final (f53b8bf4, p50 ms): off 6.80, Swift 6.79, Cinematic
  9.96 (100 fps), Ultra 13.46 (74 fps).

**Storm cells** (the Living Wilds' Rolling Storm, 2026-10-26; §21.6): Lens 2 marches each cell in its cloud pass.
- `living.client.StormSky.lensCells` hands Lens up to two cells a frame (as `HoloWorld.lensPlates` does the plates):
  frame texel 20 y their count; texels 42-47, three a cell (`lens_storm_frame.glsl`): centre x, z camera-relative,
  base y, strength; downwind x, z, the ground under it, noise time; the latest flash camera-relative and its strength.
  `LensClient.drawsStormCells()` says whether Lens draws them this frame (Cinematic or Ultra under an overworld sky);
  otherwise the fallback does. Storms draw whether or not the game's clouds are on.
- Shape (`lens_storm.glsl`, §21.6's numbers): cheap cellular puffs (the nearest of 8 jittered points; one octave on
  Cinematic, two on Ultra), the body's wobble, girth and lobes from the cloud noise texture, the anvil's fibres from its
  wisps channel. Light steps (and the land's shadow) keep the big forms only.
- March (`lens_clouds.fsh`): a ray meets a cell in bands, marched in the ray's order, each its own steps by its length:
  rain (ground to base; 18 / 16 blocks a step, at most 10 / 12), body (12 / 10.5, at most 22 / 26), anvil (8 / 7, at
  most 10 / 12), Cinematic / Ultra, so the thin anvil is never stepped over. A turret's surface turns solid within 4
  blocks (9 read as a soft ball at 200 blocks); σ 0.085 a block (a solid mass); 3 light steps (6 blocks, ×2.3); Beer's
  law with a weak multiple-scatter floor (0.22) so the base and the shadowed side go dark; the layer's phase; the sky's
  light as a cool grey-blue of the layer's ambient brightness (its sunset hue turned the shadowed side brown), by height
  from 0.16 at the base (cold and bruised, bluer) to 1 on the tops; rain σ 0.016, its colour that sky light × 0.4 (a
  grey veil, darker than the sky), fading in from 16 to 40 blocks from the camera (nearer, the game's rain falls).
  Lightning lights the cell from within: 3 × exp(-d/55) × exp(-τ) of a cool white from the flash, fading to nothing
  from 130 to 180 blocks (`FLASH_REACH`), where τ is the cloud between the flash and the point (its density at their
  midpoint × d × σ × 0.35, one sample, only while a flash shows), in the cloud and (half) in its rain; with temporal
  Lens a ray that passes within 180 blocks of a flash marches every frame while the flash is over 0.08 (every ray did
  while any flash was above zero: §21.6 "Its cost"), the rest one frame in four; the core round the bolt glows and the cell's shape still
  reads (an even glow over the whole cell blew a night strike out to a white disc); while a flash shows, the pixel takes up to 85% of this
  frame instead of 12-15%, so it lights at once and fades as an afterglow. The layer's clouds thin to nothing within
  330-450 blocks of a cell (it clears the sky round it), so the layer's march can skip the cell's bounds without a cut.
  History reprojects where the ray first met cloud (was: where it entered the layer). A ray that met none looks up
  `historyDepth` (`lens_clouds.fsh`): where cloud would be on it (the layer's entry, `stormGuess`: tight cylinders round
  the body, shelf, anvil plate and rain core), or the terrain's own point when nearer. Never a block ahead (what a miss
  took before 2026-10-27: its parallax carried the history across the screen as the camera moved) and never the cell's
  bounding volume (hundreds of blocks in front of its surface: the storm swam against the world as you walked; Euan's
  report 2026-10-27, "the storm goes crazy while I move").
- The composite lays the cloud buffer over anything farther than where the ray enters a cell's bounds (320 radius
  round 60 downwind of its centre, ground to 48 over the top; the anvil band 245 round 150 downwind, from 72 under
  the top), never nearer than 16 blocks; the light pass darkens the
  sun on the land under a cell, sampled where the light ray crosses three heights of its outline (`stormOutline`: body,
  shelf, flanking towers and anvil with soft edges, no noise and no texture; long shadows at dusk).
  Its bright, flashing edges bloom and cut the screen-space shafts like the layer's clouds.
- It builds from its base up (the density cut at a height rising with its strength, softened over 40 blocks) and rains
  out from the top down, as the fallback's cells do; its rain starts once the base has formed (strength 0.1-0.4).
- Lens dims its sun by the world's own weather, not the storm's local rain (`StormSky.serverRain/serverThunder`): the
  sun still lights its towers and the land beside it, and the cell's own shadow darkens the land under it.
- **Wet surfaces** (Cinematic, Ultra; any rain, the storm's local rain included): in the composite, a surface open to the
  sky in its column (the heightfield's top with leaves; under leaves 40%) gets wet by the rain level: 16% darker, 10%
  richer, and what faces up a dull sheen of the haze colour at glancing angles (Schlick-like, power 4, × 0.22).

**Holo world plates** (the Living Wilds' creature plates, 2026-10-25): plates write their depth at a creature's
distance (4-40 blocks), beyond the 1.25-block rule that keeps the panels and the hand out. `HoloWorld.lensPlates`
hands Lens the plates drawn this frame (up to 6: centre, half-width and half-height vectors, camera-relative); the frame
texture carries them (texel 20 x the count, texels 24-41, three a plate; it grew to 48×1), and a surface point within
0.15 block of a plate's plane and inside its rectangle (`onPlate` in lens_frame.glsl) gets no shadow, AO, key or shade
and no haze. With the K panel open they dim with the rest of the world (the focus dim stays).

**Lens on Apple** (orchestrator brief 2026-10-26 from Euan's "maybe there's a way to massively improve them to really
optimise for macOS"; docs/perf/LENS-APPLE.md):
- **Measured** (Roost at noon; MacBook at Euan's 4.7 MP world; GPU world pass). Swift costs nothing over Lens off. The
  lit composite was ~4 ms of Cinematic's ~3.6 over Swift, everything else under 0.6 ms a pass. Inside the composite:
  - its light, 1.15 ms;
  - the cloud blend, 0.45 ms;
  - the scatter, 0.5 ms.
  A pass of one texture sample costing 0.45 ms pointed at its ~70 per-pixel fetches of values every pixel shares.
- **Tiles** (Turbo, `dev.awaken.turbo.tiles`, `awaken.tiles.mixins.json`, setting `lensTiles`, default on;
  autopilot `lens tiles`). Vanilla gives every post chain target a full-size D32 depth buffer, clears colour and depth
  each frame in a pass of their own, and opens every pass LOAD/STORE on both; on a tile-based GPU each is a trip
  through memory for the whole target. For `awaken:lens_*` chains only:
  - per-frame targets have no depth and no clear pass;
  - histories have no depth (their clear when made stays);
  - passes open CLEAR with no depth attached.
  Every Lens pass is a full-screen triangle with no blend or discard, and no post pipeline tests depth, so the picture
  is the same (look tour lens-apple-look). It is version-locked, logs a probe line, and is off on failure.
- **The uniform block** (`LensBlock`: LensF[48], LensP[32], LensUse; include lens_block.glsl, tools/lens/block.py;
  autopilot `lens block`):
  - The Lens chains declare it with zeros on every pass whose shader reads F() or P().
  - Lens writes the same values to a live buffer each frame (the parameters as byte/255, what the texture fetch
    returns), and Tiles' PostPass hook binds it.
  - With LensUse.x at 0 (not bound), F() and P() read the textures as before.
- **The Tiles twins** (Steady 60, 12 Nov; tools/lens/block.py writes `lens_cinematic_tiles` and `lens_ultra_tiles`,
  composite `lens_composite_lit_tiles.fsh`; autopilot `lens twin off|setting`):
  - Why: with the block bound every value is one constant load, but each F() and P() still chose per pixel between
    the block and its texture, and a value that may come from a texture is a per-pixel register: some 60 of them were
    held through the whole lit composite. A shader that size runs only as fast as its registers let the GPU keep
    pixels in flight, so the composite ran slower for code it never reached (the Dell at 4K, his settings: leaving out
    the near clouds' walk saved 2.2 ms where nearly every pixel leaves it at once, the water 1.5 ms with no water in
    view, and the parts summed to more than the 11.5 ms the composite cost; tools/lens/regs.py).
  - Each lit chain has a twin, written from it by block.py, whose composite reads the block alone (LENS_UNIFORMS),
    has no development views (LENS_NO_DEBUG) and none of Lite's paths (LENS_NOT_LITE: these chains never run as Lite,
    LensParams writing texel 25 as framed && !lit; 0.1-0.2 ms more, bit for bit against the twin without it, twin
    check `_notlite`). LensClient runs the twin while Tiles has handed the block over and
    still would (`Tiles.blockLive`), no development view is on and `lens twin` isn't off; else the chain as written.
  - Same picture, to well under the scene's own noise: with the block bound the composite already read every value
    from it, and the twin makes the same reads of the same block. It is not bit for bit: once the Metal compiler
    knows a value is the same for every pixel it orders some sums differently, and a pixel balanced on a threshold
    can land the other way, chiefly far leaves where the light buffer's nearest-distance pick ties (upsampleAt).
    tools/lens/twincheck.py, both composites of one frame from the same inputs at 4K, six views: 0.13-0.53% of the
    shot marked (marks three pixels wide: about 1,200 to 4,900 pixels of 8.3 million differ). The composite as
    written with its own values one bit up (`_nudge`) marks 0.4-1.8%; two frames of the scene as written one tick
    apart differ in 76-80% of pixels, by over 4 steps in 24-32%. Without the development views alone it is bit for
    bit (0 pixels; `_nodbg`). GLSL's `precise` on every sum leading to that pick (PROBE_PRECISE, twin check
    `_precise_twin`, `_both`, `_self`; tour steady60-perf12-k, six views) leaves the twin's marks as they were
    (0.13-0.46% against 0.15-0.45%) while it moves the composite as written by at most 0.0024%: the rounding comes
    in wherever a block value meets arithmetic, not in one sum, so there is no cheap way to pin it. Left as it is.
    In a frame that loses the block mid-way (Tiles off on a failure) the twin draws the game's own picture, and the
    next tick runs the chain as written.
  - Never edit a twin: edit its chain and run block.py. probes.py builds the probe chains from the twins (the twin's
    own composite alone).
  - **The calm composite** (`lens_composite_lit_tiles_calm.fsh`, LENS_CALM; autopilot `lens calm off|setting`): each
    twin carries a second composite, just before its own, without the paths that are off in a calm frame: rain's
    wet, storm cells (in the composite and its cloud walk), heat's shimmer, frost's rime, the motion smear, a holo
    panel's focus, the tear and the old water (only without the Air). Both draw the whole of swap from the same
    inputs; every frame Tiles leaves one out (`Tiles.skip` asks `LensClient.leftOut`; the PostPass hook already
    cancels a pass at its head): the calm one, unless `LensBlock.calm` finds every one of those switches off in the
    block it has just written, then the twin's own. The test is each path's own (`f16.z > 0 && F(15).x > 0`,
    `P(20).r > 0 && airOn() <= 0`, `P(20).g` or `.b > 0`, `P(16).r > 0.004`, `int(F(20).y + 0.5)`, `P(14).r > 0`,
    `P(13).r > 0`) on the floats the composite reads, none in the texels the world's matrices are copied over, so a
    frame never runs the calm composite where a path it lacks would have drawn anything. No chain switch, so the
    histories carry on. With the skip hook gone both run and the twin's own, drawn last, is what stays. block.py
    places the two at LensClient's CALM_AT and FULL_AT and fails if they move. The Dell at 4K, his settings
    (tour steady60-perf12-h, the twin's own against the calm one, two pairs each): 0.76 ms where he stood (14.32 →
    13.55), 0.83 at the tree (13.81 → 12.98), 0.87 running (15.63 → 14.76).
  - Same picture: on a calm frame the two run the same code, less the paths that draw nothing there.
    tools/lens/twincheck.py `_calm` (the twin's own composite and the calm one on one frame at 4K, eight views:
    the tree, where he stood, the sky, west at morning and dusk, the sky at night, Ultra at the tree and where he
    stood): 39 to 241 pixels marked of 8.3 million (marks three pixels wide: some 5 to 27 pixels differ, each by one
    step of 8 bits, but for one pixel in two of the views), the compiler's last-bit ordering again, a hundredth of
    what the twin itself shows. In rain the frame is not calm and the twin's own composite runs (`lens calm` says
    which the last frame was).
  - Steady 60, measured (12 Nov, his world, pack and settings on the Dell at 4K, borderless; tour steady60-perf12-i;
    docs/perf/steady60/perf-2026-11-12): the chain as written against the twin with its calm composite, GPU world pass:
    where he stood 18.66 → 13.7 ms (49 → 60 fps, the cap), the tree 18.24 → 12.83, turning 19.62 → 14.45 (47 → 59.8
    fps), running 19.98 → 14.99 (45 → 57.5 fps; the terrain itself costs 0.6 ms more running). What is left would cost
    quality and is not applied (the report's list: Pixels 0.80 or 0.75, the Sun Pass off). Running's slow frames (tour
    steady60-perf12-j, each frame's GPU time beside what Lens did in it, tools/lens/slowframes.py) are the stretches
    looking west, the morning sun behind: there the game costs 1.2 ms more (Lens off 4.5 → 5.8) and Lens 1.5 more
    (8.6 → 10.2), every frame of that view; 95-98% of the slowest 5% fall there. None of Lens's periodic work (the lit
    air's upload and sweep, the sun map's rows and sweep, heightfield and block map uploads and reads, the 150 µs tick
    budget) is more common on the slow frames than on the rest, and frames with it are within 0.3 ms of those
    without, so there is nothing to spread.
- **Together, measured** (GPU world pass, old path → new; frame p50):

  | Look | GPU world pass | frame p50 |
  |---|---|---|
  | Swift | 7.71 → 7.13-7.20 ms | 9.59 → 9.1 ms (105 → 111 fps) |
  | Cinematic | 11.51 → 10.06 ms | 13.26 → 11.8 ms (75 → 85 fps) |
  | Ultra | 13.33 → 11.8 ms | 15.04 → 13.65 ms (66 → 73 fps) |

  The look is unchanged. The composite's volumetric term also reuses the light buffer's upsample (identical output).
- **Measurement tools (dev only):**
  - probe chains `awaken:lens_probe_<tier>_<group>` (tools/lens/probes.py: one pass group swapped for lens_null);
  - composite sub-probes (lens_composite_probe_<part>.fsh, PROBE_NO_* defines);
  - autopilot `lens chain <name>|off`.

**Temporal clouds and light** (Euan, 2026-10-26: "Start all three ideas now", docs/perf/IDEAS-26OCT.md B; setting
`lensTemporal`, default on; autopilot `lens temporal on|off|setting`):
- Why: at the Roost, Lens Cinematic cost ~5.4 ms of a ~21 ms frame (docs/perf/PERF-26OCT.md). Its marches (the clouds
  at 560×315 / 800×450, the light buffer at 960×540 / 1440×810) already blend into a reprojected history, but every
  pixel marched every frame.
- The clouds: a pixel marches one frame in four, a 2×2 pattern of 8×8-pixel tiles turning with the frame counter
  (frame texel 12 w). Whole tiles, so the GPU's SIMD groups skip together: the first, per-pixel pattern left a marching
  pixel in every group and saved nothing (Cinematic 13.22 ms off, 13.25 on).
  - On the other three frames it keeps last frame's clouds, reprojected to where cloud would be on its ray (`historyDepth`:
    the layer's entry or a storm's body, the terrain's point when nearer; 150 blocks when the camera is inside the layer).
  - A march blends in at 1 - (1 - f)^4 of the old weight f, so the clouds answer over time as before.
  - It marches anyway with no history (a cut, a teleport, a long gap), off screen, or while lightning flashes.
- The light buffer (sun visibility, contact shadows, AO, volumetric light): a checkerboard of 8×8 tiles marches each
  frame, alternating.
  - On its off frame a pixel keeps its reprojected history where at least 0.4 of the 2×2 taps saw the same distance.
  - A new surface (disocclusion) marches.
  - A march blends in at 1 - (1 - f)^2.
- Frame texel 17 y carries the switch; with it off, both passes are exactly as before.
- Measured (perf tour `tools/autopilot/lens-temporal-perf.txt`, 26 Oct; MacBook at Euan's 4.7 MP world, the Roost,
  noon, a quiet machine; GPU world pass p50):

  | | off | on |
  |---|---|---|
  | Ultra | 17.02 ms | **15.12 ms** (frame p50 19.4 → 17.3, 51 → 58 fps) |
  | Cinematic (paired windows) | 13.95, 13.53 ms | 13.70, 13.13 ms (−0.25 to −0.4) |

  - Lens Swift is 9.29 ms, so the whole of Lens Cinematic is ~4.2 ms over Swift and the marches are a small part of
    it. The rest is the full-size passes; time them per pass next.
  - Look tour `tools/autopilot/lens-temporal-look.txt` (CI): no smear and no tile blocks, at rest or in a 180° turn.

**Steady Light** (Euan, 2026-11-10: "nearly on par with immersive VFX ... a stable 60 but extremely high quality"; plan
docs/perf/steady60/PLAN.md, page https://claude.ai/artifact/4UjwicVDJEoS9vceUanMyQ, state docs/perf/steady60/STATUS.md).
ImmersiveVFX's look, made in Lens inside a frame budget. Measured on his Dell (4K at 120 Hz, the world at 2880x1620,
RD 16): ImmersiveVFX needs 16.7 ms of GPU time flying, most of it a shadow pass redrawn every frame; Cinematic 8.7.
- **The Air** (Cinematic and Ultra under an overworld sky; client `lensAir`, default on; autopilot `lens air`).
  `include/lens_air.glsl`, frame texels 22 (toward the sun, under the horizon by night; w the Air's strength) and 23
  (the game's sky colour, its star brightness).
  - **Sky**: Lens's own, in the composite for sky pixels: a violet-blue gradient by day (zenith (0.33, 0.41, 0.86), mid
    (0.53, 0.61, 0.95), horizon (0.83, 0.86, 0.98)), rose and gold toward the sun and violet away from it at dusk and
    dawn (from sin 0.50 of sun height down to -0.32), near-black blue by night, a glow round the sun, greyed by rain.
    The sun, the moon and the game's stars are kept as what the frame held over its own sky colour.
  - **Night sky** (`airNight`, from sun height sin 0.06 down to -0.20, not in rain; Euan 2026-11-10: "ours has
    basically no stars ... like a fantasy shader"). It turns with the sun about the world's z, as the game's stars do.
    Stars in four sizes, each a square of the game's own kind with its own brightness, tint (blue-white to warm) and
    slow twinkle: a dust of faint ones (a grid 230 cells across the sky, 7.5% of cells, up to 27.5% along the galaxy),
    small (140, 8.5 to 18.5%), middling (70, 8.5%), and the few bright ones (27, 8.5%) with four thin points. The
    galaxy: a soft band (pole (0.32, 0.47, 0.82), `exp(-13 b²)`) of blue to violet noise with dark lanes and a warmer
    heart. A shooting star: one chance in two every nine seconds, 0.9 s long. A wide halo round the moon.
  - **Wisps** (`airWisps`): a second, high layer 680 blocks up, over the sky and under the block clouds: feathered
    streaks of noise (26-block cells, longer east-west so they gather toward a low sun, bent by two slow drifts so
    none is a ruled line), drifting 2.2 blocks a second. White at up to 34% by day, rose and gold at up to 50% at dusk
    and dawn, none by night (they drew dark lanes through the stars). No march: one plane, three noise reads.
  - **Fog**: land fades into the sky that stands behind it (`airFog`: the sky's colour in the pixel's own direction,
    the horizon's from above). Far: `1 - exp(-3.2 t²)` over the render distance (five times that while a far renderer
    draws), a little thinner 40 blocks and more above the eye. Near: `1 - exp(-(d - 4) / L)`, L 280 blocks by day to 150
    at dusk, dawn, night and in rain, so each line of trees is paler than the one before; thinner only well above
    the eye (130-block scale: a haze that thinned over a tree's height left dark crowns on vanished trunks). It is the
    air along the view: only a camera under cover (parameter texel 21) looking at a covered point is left out. Gates
    and underwater keep the game's fog (the environmental-fog factor, as the haze had). The old haze is off under it.
  - **Clouds**: the game's own shapes, soft. Twelve-block cells in one to three tiers of seven (taller toward the
    middle of a group), where the cloud noise at 1536 and 384 blocks a repeat clears `1 - 0.72 cover`. The noise repeats
    every 128 cells, so the whole field of cells is one fixed 128x128 texture (`awaken:lens_cloud_cells`, 16 bits a
    cell, made by `tools/lens/cloud_cells.py` from the noise): a cell is one exact read by cell number modulo 128. Walked cell by
    cell (exact entry and exit), sigma 0.95 a block
    (solid: at 0.16 and 0.34 the cells and tiers behind showed through as the sections a cloud is built from, Euan
    2026-11-10), one even tone: lit by three steps toward the sun (`max(exp(-0.16 od), 0.30 exp(-0.03 od))`) and a
    little by the face the ray came in by (0.75 to 1; a joined block keeps the first face), the sky's light 86% on an
    underside, 91 to 98% on a side, whole on a top. Their shade is the sky overhead and at the horizon mixed, 52% toward
    white by day (the sky's own blue read as the sky seen through); the sun's share 0.40 (to 0.70 at dusk), the moon's
    a tenth. They take the fog's colour from 260 blocks and thin from 520. Drawn whatever the Clouds video setting says.
    - **Near and far**: the clouds within 640 blocks (`CLOUD_NEAR`) are walked at the frame's own size (at first in
      a pass of their own, since "The trim" inside the composite): every pixel walks its ray every frame against its own
      depth, so an edge is true to the pixel and a tree in front keeps its own; ground is out after one depth read,
      the walk ends at the first cloud (up to 80 cells), and the colours are worked out only for a pixel that met one.
      The composite lays it over everything, with no test. The far ones stay in the small cloud buffer (800x450 on
      Cinematic; `blockPiece` from 640 blocks on for up to 600 more, 800 on Ultra), walked every frame with nothing
      carried from the frame before. Before, all of them lived in that buffer, a tile in four refreshed each frame and
      the rest carried along: stretched 3.6 times they were soft and stair-stepped, and they crawled ("they don't look
      like clouds", Euan 2026-11-10). The drift (0.04 blocks a tick) follows the frame's own share of the tick.
    - Storm cells were still marched in the small buffer as soft vapour, a tile in four with their history, until
      Euan saw one beside the blocks (2026-11-11: "the custom storm is still the old clouds. Let's fix that so it's
      the new clouds and looks great without costing much extra performance"). **The block storm**
      (`lens_storm_blocks.glsl`): the same cumulonimbus, by §21.6's own numbers (the shelf, the leaning tower, three
      flanking towers stepping down upwind, the overshooting dome, the anvil far downwind), built of the layer's own
      cells, twelve blocks across and seven high, solid and flat-faced. The grid rides with the cell and is turned to
      the world's axes. A turret's swell is a hash three cells across with each cell a little ragged, so the tower
      is a cauliflower of blocks and holds its shape as it drifts (nothing boils: a block that flickered in and out
      would read as a fault). It is walked once a ray in the composite, to the pixel and afresh every frame, and at
      half size in the bloom prefilter so a storm in front of the sun cuts its glow and rays. Cost is kept down by
      three tight bounds walked each on its own (shelf and tower; flanks; dome and anvil), a cell test that is
      arithmetic and two hashes with no texture read and rejects open air before the hashes, a walk that ends at
      the first block, and colours worked out only for a ray that met one; the soft storm's whole march leaves the
      cloud buffer, which keeps only the rain (a soft veil under the base). Light: the sky's light by height, dark
      blue-grey at the shelf paling to the layer's white at the dome and anvil, a face that looks down darkest; the
      sun only on faces turned to it, less where three samples toward the sun find more of the cell in the way; the
      lightning's glow from within, round the flash. The layer's near clouds clear round a storm (within 330 to
      450 blocks, as the far ones always did) and those behind it are not walked. Without the Air the soft storm
      is drawn as before. A sunlit face is kept under white with its hue (a soft knee from 0.84): past white the
      tower was paper at golden hour and its blocks ran together. Under Lite the blocks are the whole storm: the soft
      rain belongs to the cloud buffer Lite leaves out. Tour: `tools/autopilot/steady60-storm-ci.txt` (the cell from
      460 blocks at three hours and by night with a strike, from 230, and from under the shelf; `living near` goes to
      480 for it, inside the 512 a happening's tell reaches). Last run 42959983512; sheet
      `docs/perf/steady60/play-2026-11-11/storm-blocks.jpg`. Not measured: its frame time, which needs the Mac; and
      no shot has caught a strike at its brightest.
  - **Sunlight**: key (1.24, 1.17, 0.98) by day. The shade has weight (Euan 2026-11-10: "more black ... more
    cinematic"): its depth 2.5 times the look's under a high sun (capped at 0.9), easing to 1.5 as the sun sinks to
    sin 0.10 and by moonlight (a morning forest went black under a bright sky). The sun's light fades into the shade
    as it sinks (sin 0.55 to 0.05), and its disc widens (0.2 to 3 times), so dusk is one soft light and not long
    streaks. A shadow keeps the texture's pixels close to the eye, and holds still: within 10 blocks
    (fading out by 18) the composite reads the sun's light, and only that, at the centre of the pixel's own 1/16-block
    texel (`upsampleAt`), and the light pass gives such a texel one unchanging answer (along the sun's own line, with
    no disc, and a march jitter fixed to the texel), so a texel is wholly lit or wholly shaded and the edge runs along
    texel edges. The soft shade and the mist are always read at the pixel's own place. (First the whole sample was
    held across the texel out to 72 blocks: the mist and the soft shade, new every frame, made each grass texel
    flicker as a block, and the sun's disc sampled once a texel made a shadow's edge a dither of light and dark
    texels that changed every frame: "the floor was shimmering ... a grid style where the shadows were broken", Euan
    2026-11-10. Checked with `steady60-still-ci.txt` and `tools/steady60-flicker.py`: frames of a still scene
    compared.) With the Air on
    the clouds and light are always spread over frames (`lensTemporal` as if on).
  - **Life** (`LensParticles`, on the spore sprite, no new particle type): fireflies from sun height sin 0.32 down
    through the night, low over open ground, none in snow or rain; pollen in sunlit air near the ground by day; twice
    the sunlit dust, which stands only where the lit air (below) says the sun reaches, under a canopy too. Lens's
    particles are light, not things: they draw through their own pipeline (`awaken:pipeline/lens_particle`, the
    particle pipeline without a depth write), so no shadow, contact darkness or haze of Lens's falls under them (in the
    depth they cast blocky little shadows, Euan 2026-11-10), and one within 1.2 to 3.4 blocks of the eye fades out. The sunlit mist is 3.4 times as strong in the composite and up to 2.6 times denser under a low sun.
- **A power's look** (12 Nov; `LensClient.accent`, `Looks.shift`, powers' `CastLens`, §36.5). Euan, playing, with
  two pictures of the same deck, one while holding a beam: "is intentional, that everything is way less bright when
  you're using the power." It was not. A cast's look (`looks_powers.json`) went through the moment channel
  (`LensClient.override`), which is a story scene's: it replaces the place's own look (the biome's, a cave's, a
  dimension's) with the look as written, and it switches the player's grade off for its length. So for as long as a
  beam was held, his Vivid grade (the azure sky, the bright greens, the lifted shade) was gone and the land wore the
  overworld's default look with the beam's numbers, although the beam's look is written to lift the light. Now a
  power's look is an **accent**: read as what it changes from the default look (the one a look's missing values come
  from): a ratio for exposure, contrast and saturation, a difference for every other number (`Looks.shift`); that is
  laid over the place's look after the place's own slow easing (so it arrives with the cast, at its own pace), and
  the player's grade goes over the result as always. In the overworld's default look a cast draws exactly the
  numbers its look was written with; anywhere else the place keeps its own character and takes the same change; the
  grade never leaves. Numbers that would go under zero stop at zero (warmth may). A story moment's look still
  replaces everything and plays as authored: Lens hides the accent for that moment's length and brings it back if
  the cast outlasts it. One accent at a time (the last set); only while Lens draws. Lens's own drifting motes and
  the view's motion feel, which a story scene stops, now carry on through a cast. Arms' perfect dodge
  (`awaken:arms_breath`, twelve ticks) and the Living Wilds' level moment still take the moment channel: they are
  written as a beat in which the world drains, and are left so.
  What it looks like: the same world, with the cast's own colour over it. The looks written to change the world
  (Flow and Red Hour drain it, Void Maw and Legion darken it) still do, by the same amounts, from wherever you
  stand. The beam's own look lifts exposure 3% and softens contrast and colour by 4% and 7% (as written; under the
  old way that softening was hidden inside the larger loss).
- **A Look switched back to** (12 Nov). Euan, playing: "I also turned off cinematic mode then back on, and the
  shadows broke". Each chain keeps its own histories (the light buffer's, the clouds'), which stay as they were when
  it last ran. Switched from Cinematic to Lite and back, the frame values never stopped (Lite reads them), so
  Cinematic took its light of a quarter of a minute ago, from wherever the camera then looked, for last frame's:
  stale shade for a moment after the switch. A chain that starts or comes back now starts its histories afresh
  (`LensClient.ran`, `LensFrame.reset`). That is the one fault found. His own order of switches on CI
  (`tools/autopilot/steady60-lookswitch-ci.txt`, `tools/lens/samecheck.py`, run 43201767617: Cinematic, Swift nine
  seconds, Lite five, back; again; each alone; quickly) gave the fresh start's ground and shadows every time: what
  differed was what moves anyway (the high cloud, leaves, motes). In his screenshot the orange lattice is leaf
  litter and the two hard dark stripes are, as far as the log shows, the contact shadows of the ropes he had thrown
  (a thin rope casts as if half a block thick): not confirmed by him, and not changed here.
- **The Sun Pass in play, a part at a time** (development; client commands, nothing saved): `/awaken lens sunpass
  off|on|setting` (the block map's walk; off leaves the heightfield's answer alone), `/awaken lens rays off|on|setting`
  (the lit air, and with it the shortcut that spares sure pixels the walk), and `/awaken lens paths on|off`, which
  marks on every sunlit surface which part answered it, over the answer itself and in the world's own blocks: plain
  where the heightfield found nothing over the ray or a block stopped the walk, lines across the sun's way where the
  lit air was sure, lines along it where the walk left the map in the open, a checker where the walk met a section
  not read yet (frame texel 29, w). For a shadow that changes with where you stand, the mark under it names the part
  that changed its mind.
- **The Sun Pass** (client `lensSunPass`, default on; autopilot `lens sunpass`): `LensBlocks`, a block map. 128 blocks
  across and high, a ring by world block modulo 128; one RGBA8 texel (128x1024) a column of a section, two bits a
  block: open, stops the sun (solid render, a full occluding shape, a stair, a near-whole footprint), leaves, a lower
  half (a slab); all ones is a section not read yet. Up to 14 sections read a tick nearest first, 6 looked at again,
  the 3x3x3 round the camera every 10 ticks, 6 chunks uploaded a tick; frame texel 17 z the trusted reach (46 blocks),
  w the lowest y. Where the heightfield says shade and the point is inside the map, the light pass walks the map
  toward the light (`blockRay`, up to 72 blocks, never the block it starts in): a block stops it, three texels in ten
  of a leaf face pass it, a lower half stops it under half height; out of the map in the open, the heightfield
  carries on from there. Inside the map every face is asked and the turn of a face decides nothing (deciding by the
  face lit the one-pixel sides of path plates and block lips while the ground lay in shade: bright rims at dusk, Euan
  2026-11-10); under cover the key shows where the map says the sun comes in. Contact shadows near the eye are a block
  and a half long in 16 even steps from the texel's centre. Cinematic's light buffer is 960x540. Before it walks, the
  light pass asks the lit air (below) at the point, half a block off its face: three slices, each smoothed over four
  cells, all over 0.996 is a walk that would meet nothing, so it is skipped and the heightfield carries on from where
  the walk would have stopped (`walkEnd`: the trusted box's edge or 72 cells). Everything else walks. The lit air
  never shades a surface itself: it reaches farther than the walk, and where it called a block dark and the walk
  beside it found the sun, the difference lay on open grass as a patchwork under a low sun (Euan 2026-11-10).
  - **The walk's reads** (Steady 60, 12 Nov): under the block map, rows 1024 to 1031 are its open map, one texel a
    4x4 of columns within a chunk, one bit for each four levels of each of its eight sections, set where all 64 blocks
    are read and open (a section not read yet is all ones, so never open). It goes up with the chunk's block texels,
    from the same cells, in the same call. The walk reads the open texel when it enters a new 4x4, steps through an
    open level's cells without reading their block texel, and fetches a block texel only when it moves to a new one
    (one texel is a column of a section, sixteen blocks). The cells it visits, their order, the arithmetic and every
    answer are as before: `tools/lens/walkcheck.py` ran the walk as it stood at 5a1f0582b beside it on every pixel of
    ten frames (four suns, three views, 3 to 50% of pixels walking) and not one differed in status, exit distance or
    answer, bit for bit. 0.2 ms at the tree (the world pass 17.49 to 17.28 ms, the Dell, his settings).
- **The sun's rays** (on with the Sun Pass and the Air; autopilot `lens rays`). Two parts.
  - **The lit air** (`LensLit`): how much of the sun reaches every block of air in the block map's window, 0..1, as an
    R8 texture `awaken:lens_lit` (2048x1024: 128 slices of 128x128, x across and y up, sixteen slices a row), addressed
    from the volume's own corner (frame texels 15 w, 20 zw and 28 w: whether it is there and the camera's place in
    it). **The corner's z rode in texel 21 until 12 Nov**, and the world's own projection (`WorldProjection`) copies
    its sun over the whole of texel 21 every frame, w and all, as 0. The shader then took the camera to stand on the
    volume's z edge: a surface less than two blocks to the camera's +z was "outside the volume" and walked (right),
    and every surface farther to its +z was judged by a slice of air some 64 to 79 blocks to its north, open sky as
    a rule, so the lit air was "sure of the sun" there and the walk never ran. A tree's shadow was whole from the
    south, gone from the north, and cut along a straight east-west line two blocks ahead of the camera in between;
    the sun's rays in the air were read from that far slice too (Euan, playing, 11 and 12 Nov: "the shadow moves as
    I move", "on one side of the tree the shadow is perfect, then if I go to the other side, the shadow is gone ...
    its for ALL trees"; found with `/awaken lens rays off`, which brought every shadow back, and `/awaken lens paths
    on`, which drew the lit air's mark across the trunk's own shadow). Rule: a frame value never rides in a texel
    another writer replaces (texels 0 to 11 and 21 are the projection's, whole). The sun travels in the world's x-y plane, so each z-slice is its own flat problem: a worker thread (one,
    lowest priority) sweeps each slice once from the sun's side, column by column under a low sun and row by row under
    a high one, every cell taking the light of the two cells its ray came through (mixed by the ray's slope), cut by
    what it holds: a block 0, a lower half 0.43, leaves 0.33, one leaf block in three 0.91 (a canopy's shade is
    dappled in whole blocks), a section not read yet 1. Beyond the window the air is lit: the volume holds only what
    its own blocks do, and the land out there is the light pass's to judge. A volume takes 8 to 11 ms of the worker and 0.2 ms to upload, every
    20 ticks at rest and every 5 once the camera is 5 blocks off the volume's middle; none where the light leaves the
    x-y plane or sits under sin 0.02. The light pass's mist march spends its first 60 blocks in it (12 steps, 18 on
    Ultra, linear in x and y, dithered in z; weight `1 + 0.30 / max(phase, 0.12)` so a shaft shows from the side), each
    step times the sun map's answer at the point where the sun's ray leaves the volume (the same far shade the ground
    gets), and the rest in the sun map as before (5 steps, 10 on Ultra).
  - **Rays on the screen** (`lens_shafts.fsh` under the Air): the light is the sky round the sun itself
    (`exp(-14 d²)` of screen heights), gathered in 40 jittered steps along each pixel's line to the sun, so a cloud, a
    crown of leaves or a ridge on that line leaves a dark lane and the gaps between stand out as beams fanning from
    the sun; fainter with distance (`exp(-1.9 r)`). The prefilter's sky mask under the Air is the open sky whatever
    its colour, cut whole by Lens's clouds. Composite strength 0.95 of the look's shafts (0.35 without the Air).
- **Lens's own tick work** (the heightfield, the block map, the lit air's hand-over; autopilot `lens cost`): each has a
  time limit of 0.5 ms a tick on top of its counts (what waits is read on the next tick, nearest first), and the
  re-reads of the terrain round the camera go in turn, a few a tick (the heightfield's 25 chunks three a tick, the
  block map's 27 sections three a tick), where they went all at once every 10 ticks: those ticks took 2 to 5 ms.
  Measured in flight after: heightfield 0.15 to 0.2 ms a tick (worst 1 to 2), block map 0.3 (worst under 1), lit air
  0.02; the worker's sweep 2.5 to 8.5 ms, its upload 0.06 to 0.5 ms.
