- **The wild's and the city's walkers** (2026-10-29; a cross-module edit the orchestrator approved: client code only,
  the wildlife module's `WildModel` and `WildRenderer`, the citizens module's `CritterModel` and `CritterRenderer`; no
  server, entity, spawn or data change). Each model binds `CreatureLife.rig(root, temperament, rig.id)` (§12); a rig
  with no `motion.json` profile behaves exactly as before. The renderer sets `grounded` (not flying or landing, a city
  cat not mid-leap), `legsFree` (a perched bird, a sitting animal, a swimming duck, or any clip but idle, walk, trot,
  sniff, listen, peck, caw and call: a sit, a loaf, a groom, a pant, a pounce, a hop, the fox's bolt keep their legs),
  `gaitRun` (a trot clip's weight, or the speed between the rig's `runFrom` and `runFull`, whichever is more) and
  `bodyScale` (the model's own scale, so the feet land where it is drawn). Profiles: the **fox** (`wild_fox`; `mixed`:
  8 px one-bone forelegs stiff, the hind leg and hock bending) and the city **cat** and **dog** (`city_cat`,
  `city_dog`, the same build at 7 and 9 px) a ripple walk and a trot (duty 0.66/0.45, 0.66/0.42, 0.64/0.42; strides
  0.6/0.9, 0.55/0.95, 0.7/1.2 blocks), the cat's crouch 1.1 px (its hind feet are drawn 1 px off the ground); the
  **crow** (`wild_crow`) and the city **pigeon** and **gull** (`city_pigeon`, `city_gull`; rigid 3 and 4 px legs whose
  toe plates put the foot 1 px ahead of the hip, so a forward step runs out of leg first: a deeper crouch, 0.5 to 0.6
  px, and the pigeon's duty 0.5/0.45 keep the hips within their drop) an alternating walk (0.34 to 0.5 blocks; the
  feet never take a cycle under 0.2 blocks, so a pigeon at 0.6 can't go shorter). Not planted: the **city horse** (its
  walk clip bends knee and hock in time with the cart; `fknee` and `hhock` aren't leg names, and rigid legs would lose
  that), the **heron** (it wades: its feet would reach for the bed under the water), and the hoppers and climbers
  (songbird, woodpecker, squirrel, rabbit, frog), whose clips are their gait. Test: `creature_fauna_feet` (every walker
  here has its gait, its rig in its module's sources, and every leg plants); `creature_motion_feet` checks their
  strides with the rest.
- **Flight** (`Flight`, plain math checked on the server; a `fly` block, by rig id or, for a hand-built body, by its
  creature id): while airborne or swimming (or `always`, for a body always under way: serpents, the ray) the body noses
  into a cruise (`tilt` at `fast` blocks a second) and pitches along its path's climb or dive (`climb`, the share), banks
  into a turn (`bank`, radians per radian a second of turn at a full cruise, capped 0.7), and rides its wings: the wings'
  height above their own mean (read from the pose, the roots named in `wings`) lifts the body as they sweep down
  (`heave` px per radian, 50 ms behind). A flier keeps all of its stroke climbing or hovering, glides down a dive
  (`glide`, the stroke's share kept, about the wings' mean), and at a cruise beats and glides by turns on a slow wave of
  its own (about six seconds). A body whose clips only glide (the owl's `air`) gets the layer's own beat (`flap`: radians,
  cycles a second, the tips' trailing share): down in 40% of the cycle, up in 60%, quicker climbing and hovering (x1.15,
  +0.4 per radian of climb), slower in a cruise (-0.35); the tips (`tips`) trail it by an eighth of a beat. The spine
  (`spine`, the links behind the body, front first) carries its swim stroke stronger with speed (`wave`: the stroke's
  scale at rest and at a full cruise, about each link's mean) and curves into a turn (`bend`, radians over the whole
  spine per radian a second, the tail to the inside of the turn); fins (`fins`) fold back at speed (`tuck`); the head
  holds level against the pitch and bank (`level`). Hand-built bodies beat on the life layer's paced clock (the moth's
  wings, the ray's ripple, the serpent's wave), so a change of pace never jumps the phase.
  The **Hollow Owl** beats 0.7 rad at 2.4 a second (tips 0.5) round its glide pose, heave 2, glide 0.12, banks 0.18,
  climb 0.6. In the air its body lies forward along the line of flight (75° off its upright stance, a 2° rock), and a
  cube-less `yoke` at the shoulders turns back by as much under the head and wings: the face still looks ahead, the wings
  still spread level and beat up and down about the line of flight (a wing hung from a pitched body would row); the legs
  trail under the tail, which fans straight back. Before this it flew upright, a perched owl hung in the air; the **Bogwick** (clip beat) heave 0.6, glide 0.6, tilt 0.25; the **Empress Moth** (its clip heaves) glide
  0.45, bank 0.16; the **Plumed Coil** wings heave 0.8, glide 0.4, spine of ten bending 0.25, wave 0.7/1.2; the **Dune
  Wyrm** spine of nine bending 0.3, climb 0.7, wave 0.7/1.25; the **Glimmerfin** tail and caudal fin wave 0.55/1.3, bend
  0.3, pectorals tucking 0.6, climb 0.7; the **Lantern Maw** wave 0.6/1.2, bend 0.25, bank 0.12; the **Tidesteed** tail
  and fluke wave 0.6/1.3, bend 0.25; the **Brook Otter** swimming, tail wave 0.6/1.3, bend 0.3; the **Lumen Moth** and
  **Petalwing** heave 0.9, glide 0.7 and 0.4, tilt 0.3 and 0.25, bank 0.25; the **Dune Ray** heave 0.8, bank 0.3, its
  tail bending 0.35; the eels (**Deep Eel**, **Tide Eel**, **Cord-Eater**) bend 0.45 over six segments, climb 0.6.
  The Breathbell's bell pulses as its clip has it (a jelly drifts; no bank or pitch).
- Test: `creature_motion_feet` (every motion.json entry with a gait names a rig; every gait finds two-bone legs on a body bone that
  carries the head; every foot can reach its stance on its crouch and sunk to stalk; the IK lands each foot within 0.05 px of its
  home, a step ahead and behind, the top of a step's arc and the crouch, checked by forward kinematics; the hip's turn
  survives its ZYX Euler angles; a straight leg whose knee can't hide 20° of bend is rigid (the four-legged walkers all
  are, so no knee of theirs breaks either way), and a rigid leg's foot lands within 0.05 px of each spot within 97% of
  its length with its top kept inside the body (no further fore, aft or down than its room, no more than 70% of its
  length up); at least 68 rigid legs; every gait's stride, walking and running,
  sweeps its planted feet no further than the hips can vault to; every gait's feet, on flat ground through a stand, a
  sudden walk (a cycle a second), a sudden run and a stop, never plant further ahead of home than a steady stride's
  landing plus 10% of a stride or trail further than its lift point plus 40%, and a rigid leg never swings past 35°
  walking or 45° running (about its pivot `shoulder` above the hip); then turned on the spot at 120° a second as a
  client sees it (the body held until its facing is 50° ahead, then dragged along 50° behind, the body bone twisted its
  share of that look), no planted foot is more than four `settle`s (+1 px) off its spot under the twisted body nor a
  rigid leg past 25°, and stood 1.5 s after it every foot is back within a `settle` (+0.75 px) (the old feet failed 22
  gaits); the forms' rigs
  are looked up too); `creature_motion_flight` (every flight names a creature and, on a rig, bones it has, wings with a
  side; the beat sweeps down in under half a cycle and never jumps; a right turn banks right and curves the spine right;
  a climb noses up and keeps every beat, a dive noses down and glides, a hover beats, a cruise glides between beats; a
  climb beats faster than a cruise; the body rises as the wings sweep below their mean). Tours walk still (NoAI) creatures with
  `/awaken admin stroll <targets> <blocks per tick> <ticks> [degrees per tick] [climb, blocks per tick]` (each call queues a leg; the server moves
  them every tick, so a busy runner can't turn a scripted walk into a crawl the way a tp a command did), load the studio's
  chunks first (`forceload`) and fill its floor twice. Tours on CI (PACK=perf,feel; a vanilla spider under
  Fresh Animations beside each): `tools/autopilot/mob-anims-lurker.txt` (clips run-autopilot/clips/lurk_*: idle, a walk
  into a run, a stop and a turn, a blow, a death, the hunt), `tools/autopilot/mob-anims-spiders.txt` (spid_*: the forms'
  row from vanilla's rungs to S, a walk side by side, a blow, a death, a hunt) and `tools/autopilot/mob-anims-crawlers.txt`
  (crawl_*: the thousandfoot, wickling, hushling and weaver queen); `tools/autopilot/mob-anims-fliers.txt` (fly_*, swim_*:
  each flier on a set course, NoGravity, beside a parrot, a bee or a cod under Fresh Animations: a cruise, a U-turn
  each way, a climb, a dive, a hover; a blow and a death in the air; the swimmers in a tank);
  `tools/autopilot/mob-anims-close.txt` (close_*: each grazer and the spider side on at leg height, a spectator camera
  gliding beside it, first vanilla's under Fresh Animations then ours at rung 3 on the same walk, trot, stop and half
  turn; then the two at rest side by side for half a minute); `tools/autopilot/mob-anims-beastclose.txt` (bclose_*:
  the sow, the stag and the ram the same way, after vanilla's pig under Fresh Animations, each then half a minute at
  rest); `tools/autopilot/mob-anims-flyclose.txt` (fly_*, swim_*
  close and at half speed (`/tick rate 10`): each flier hovers, then circles a spectator camera at its own distance, a
  cruise lap and half a slower one, the camera's eye at the body's middle turning with it from the circle's middle,
  a parrot, a bee or a cod a little further round the same circle). A NoAI fauna creature refreshes its pose
  bits every tick (`FaunaMob.tick`), so a tour's still flier shows itself aloft (the first fliers tour's owls hung
  upright in the air, perched).

- **Pollen Grazer** (`pollen_grazer`, Amber Reach, SPEC 50.7; six two-bone legs, a bee as much as a yak): ripple-alternate,
  duty 0.74/0.52, steps 2.6/4.2 px, stride 0.8/1.2 blocks, reach 0.55, a heavy body's bob 0.45 and roll 0.035, the front
  leading (`lag` -0.18), head level 0.45, twist 0.18, shift 0.8, nod 0.05, land 1.3. Knees stand out and up like a beetle's
  (thigh 7 px at 55°, running a pixel past the knee to hide the joint). The rig's bones carry the life layer's names
  (`neck`, `head`, `jaw_*`, `antenna_*`, `wing*`, `abdomen`, `tail`, `crest`, `mane_*`, `shag_*`), so the look, breath and
  springs reach it. Its folded wings grow from a chitin knuckle inside the ruff, at any angle a clip or a spring can reach,
  and lie within the body's width. It breathes by pumping its abdomen, chews off and on, feels the air with one antenna at a
  time, and its old wings shiver now and then, a side at a time; when it runs they come open and buzz, no use at all.
  Grazing, its neck and head go down to the moss, the mandibles scissor and the antennae feel the ground. A blow clenches
  the abdomen and flares the wings; it dies on buckling knees, rolls on its side with a bounce, the legs curling in one by
  one and twitching afterward, and the last thing it moves is the wings.
- **Wax-folk** (`wax_folk`, no legs): the pool and skirt are a `base` of their own, flat on the ground whatever the body
  above does. The body rocks over them in a tired waddle and each step squashes the skirt and pushes the pool toward the
  side it leans; chest, head and hands take the rock a moment later and the flame streams back. A real sigh in the idle,
  hands rubbed together, a look at one hand as if it were shorter today, beads of wax that swell and let go. Drips, arms
  and the wick and flame swing on the life layer's springs (the flame carries on when the body stops). A blow all but puts
  the flame out and it comes back too far; death is the flame going out, then a slow slump into a puddle.
- **Amberfly** (`amberfly`): flies always (`fly`, always, glide 0, four wing bones), hanging in a slow figure of eight
  with the bead pulsing and the head scanning; going somewhere it noses down, the bead drags on its waist and the six
  thread legs trail on springs. A blow spins it round; it dies on its back, a small bounce, the legs curling in.
- **On real ground** (Euan's playtest 9 Nov: the Drip Lurker's legs ran down the face of a gravel step). A foot goes only where it can stand:
  `LegSurface.footing` reads the surface in that foot's own column, and refuses a wall (higher than a step), a drop (more than a step
  down) or a spot with something solid right above. `Legs.fit`, run every time a foot lifts, takes the full stance if the column will
  take it, the leg can reach it (off flat ground, 1.05x its length) and a straight line from hip to foot clears every block; otherwise it
  draws the foot in towards the body in steps (0.8, 0.6, 0.45, 0.3, 0.15), and that place becomes its home, so it doesn't keep re-stepping. A
  swinging foot re-aims with the same rule, and one planted foot a frame re-checks its leg. Flat ground behaves exactly as before.
  `creature_motion_feet` (via `LegBlockTrial`) stands every rig against a wall, a corner, a kerb, a step down and a two-block drop.

## 24. Hands: the first-person system (plan docs/anims/PLAN.md, page https://claude.ai/artifact/5dQodY76zUGpn536Z34Lpy; approved 2026-10-25)

Euan: "right now for basically everything there is no first-person animation". One owner for everything drawn in first
person, as the Feel Director is for the camera (module `anims`; public face `core.api.FirstPerson`; built in phases P1-P6
of the plan). No mixins.
- **World layer**: your body in first person, posed in the world (`anims.client.WorldBody`): a `WorldPose` source fills a
  `FirstPerson.Rig` (each limb from its root toward its tip, its front, a weight; `Rig.reach` slides a rigid limb's root
  so its fist or foot lands on a spot); the highest priority source that poses this frame wins (movement 100,
  interactions 200, combat 300). Limbs are parts of a private copy of the player model (vanilla's own is posed by every
  player in the frame and drawn after submission), with your skin, sleeves and pants. Legs are drawn in the world with
  real depth (`SubmitCustomGeometryEvent`). Arms are viewmodels (P1 tour: a fist a third of a block from the eye filled
  half the frame): drawn in the hand pass, each fist where the world puts it on screen but at 0.85 from the eye, the arm
  rising to it from under the frame's corner on its side (view (±0.5, -0.85, -0.1)); vanilla's hands step aside. No
  torso (from inside the head it is only a slab under the camera). Never in third person. Like vanilla's hands, none of
  it shows with the HUD hidden (F1). It draws from your eyes, the furnace station's lowered view, or a scene's own camera
  standing in for them (`FirstPerson.camera(owns)`, read only when the view isn't your eyes: the War Anvil's, §46.3).
- **View layer** (`anims.client.Hands`, the one owner of `RenderHandEvent`, first for each hand and last for the off
  hand): every `ViewPose` stance adds moves (view space: x right, y up, z toward you, blocks; then pitch, yaw, roll in
  degrees) for both hands, the main or the off hand; the body's stances (sprint, slide, hang, mantle) and the rope's
  arm moved here from their own hand listeners. The casts (powers) still draw their own arms until P3.
- **View clips**: `assets/awaken/fp_clips/*.json` (`anims.FpClipSet`, schemaVersion 1) written by
  `tools/art/specs/fp_moves.py` (edit there; `preview DIR` draws vanilla's arms from the eye); keys in ticks eased by
  `anims.Ease` (the same curve names as the third-person clips), authored right-handed and mirrored for a left main arm;
  a one-shot ends at rest; `FirstPerson.play(name[, speed])`, `stop` (a 3-tick fade), `playing`; keyed events reach
  `FirstPerson.listen` listeners (sounds, hit-stops). Combat's animations use the same three layers.
- **Fists** (P2): a view clip (`"fists": true`) or a stance may key where each EMPTY hand is on screen (view space)
  instead of moving vanilla's arm by offsets: its arm is drawn rising to the fist from under the frame's corner (from
  view (±0.48, -0.84, -0.53), vanilla's own arm start), so a hand can be lifted anywhere without its forearm floating into
  view (offsets that lift a vanilla arm show its end: the P2 preview). Vanilla's resting fist is
  `FirstPerson.View.REST_FIST` (0.744, -0.455, -1.072); a clip's fists replace a stance's for that hand; a hand holding
  an item ignores fists (vanilla draws it) unless a cast or a climb puts the item away (below). A fist clip gives the hands back at rest (or the off hand out under the
  frame), or, marked `toStance`, where its stance holds them (the hang's ledge jumps).
- **Grips** (Arms 2026-10-26, Euan: "it feels like the weapon is just floating and attacking on its own"): a source may
  key where a hand that HOLDS something closes on it (`View.gripMain`/`gripOff`, view space, weighted as fists): that
  hand's arm is drawn rising to the grip from under the frame's corner exactly as a fist's (after the moves for both
  hands, so it sways with what it holds), and the held thing still draws (a grip never hides the hand). Unset (weight 0)
  nothing changes. Arms keys them every frame a styled weapon is held: at rest, through each swing's turn, the guard
  and the equip rise, the off hand's on a pair's twin. Test `arms_grip`.
- **Put away** (Euan 2026-10-27: "climbing while a weapon is out doesn't hide the weapon, so it looks really weird"):
  whenever the hands grip the world, what they hold goes out of view and the fists take its place. Asked by a cast clip
  (`View.stow`, `"stow"`: at once, as before), by a climb (`View.climb`: the hang and its shimmy and every move between
  holds while `RunnerMoves.hanging()`, a wall climb, the Ascent's rope, zip line and rappel; and the clips marked
  `"climb"` in fp_moves.py: `fp_grab`, `fp_lower`, `fp_ledge_up`, `fp_ledge_side_l/_r`, `fp_mantle` (every mantle and
  climb out, a fence or wall climbed onto), `fp_rope_fire`), and on each side the world layer has an arm (the pipe's
  grip, a crossing's planted hand, the slide's trailing hand, a hard landing's palms). Each hand eases separately
  (`Hands.STOW`): going away it sinks 0.6 down the view (vanilla's equip drop) over 2.5 ticks (smoothstep; its grip arm
  sinks with it) while that hand's fist comes up into place from 0.8 under it, then is hidden; once nothing asks, it rises
  back over 3 ticks while the hand's last fist sinks 0.8 away (a world arm lets go in the world instead). A pair's twin
  goes with the off hand. Letting go of the lip (a drop, `fp_ledge_back`, a wall jump), the rope (`fp_rope_release`,
  `fp_rope_launch`) or the line brings the weapon back at once; a climb out keeps it away to the end of `fp_mantle`. The
  tactical sprint, slide (its main hand), roll, wall-run, vault and hop keep it in hand.
  Third person (2026-10-28): both held items, including a pair's twin, are hidden during a ledge hang and moves between
  holds, pipe/ladder grip, vertical wall climb, mantle/climb out, climbs over or onto rails (`HIGH`, `ONTO`, `OVER`),
  and the Ascent's rope, zip and rappel. `body.client.BodyHeldItems` clears only the extracted hand meshes and stacks,
  after Arms has populated them; the player's equipment never changes. The next extraction restores current equipment
  as soon as climbing ends, including after an interrupted mantle or climb-out.
  Dimension/respawn reset first ends tactical sprint, slide and vault through their normal cleanup paths, so removing
  transient movement state cannot strand a sprint speed modifier or forced crawl pose. The local player uses movement
  prediction; observers use the server's current transient `body_stowed` Boolean attachment (updated only on change,
  after movement validation, and sent on initial tracking too). It works without the animation library. A climb-out's
  server window is the same 10 ticks as its path plus the existing 6-tick Runner grace, ended sooner by the client's
  completion/interruption; other windows retain their existing motion limits. Death/replacement, logout and dimension
  changes retain no stow state. No save schema changes. Tests: `body_climb_stow` (state, ends, isolation, resets) and
  `tools/tests/body-held-items.py` (actual modifier, both hands, paired-item appearance, prediction and next-frame restoration).
- **Look-lag** (P2): the hands trail fast turns of the view on a damped spring (up to 0.06 sideways, 0.045 up, 4° of
  roll), halved with reduced motion (`FirstPerson.reducedMotion`, the body's setting).
- **Near legs** (P2): a foot nearer the eye than 1.15 is drawn in the hand pass, pushed out along its line of sight to
  that distance, as the arms are; farther legs stay in the world. (No source puts one there since P2.1 cut the slide's
  legs: from eyes 0.4 up they could only be a slab across the frame.)
- **Clean fists** (P1.1; Euan, 2026-10-25): the hands are vanilla's own blocky fists, never modelled fingers (finger
  boxes read as loose bricks). A world arm rises to its fist from under it on its own side (its root follows the fist
  across by `WorldBody.RISE` 0.45), not from the frame's corner, so a hand high in the frame never drags its sleeve
  across it. A world rig sets `handDistance` (nearer reads bigger: touches 0.75, both hands 0.85, stations 0.8, the
  pipe 0.85, the slide and landing 0.78), `held[]` (an item at the fist: a plucked flower, food being laid) and `glow`.
  Vanilla's hand steps aside only on the side the world body has an arm (a touch with one hand leaves the sword in the
  other); what it holds sinks away first (§24 "Put away"). In the hand pass the frame shows y down to about 0.7·|z|: keep keyed fists inside it.
- **The Runner's Kit in first person** (P2, `body.client.BodyFp`): each move's view clip starts from the same event as
  its third-person clip (BodyAnims hands the clip's name over): `fp_roll`, `fp_mantle` (and every climb out),
  `fp_grab`, `fp_lower`, `fp_ledge_up`, `fp_ledge_side_l/_r`, `fp_ledge_back`, `fp_walljump_l/_r` (the run's wall side),
  `fp_vault` and `fp_leap` (the free-run), `fp_slide_jump`, `fp_land_soft` / `fp_land_hard` (a fall over 0.55 b/t,
  hard over 0.95; never over a roll), `fp_stair_bump` (each half step a stair slide passes). Stances: the tactical
  sprint's lowered hands pumping in step (empty fists pumping up into the lower frame in turn, P2.1), the slide's brace, a
  wall-run's wall-side fist at the frame's edge brushing the wall with each footfall, a wall climb's fists slapping up in
  turn, a hang's fists on the lip (`BodyFp.HANG_*`, swaying; shimmying hand over hand). The wall jump's shove is well
  in the frame. World (source `body_moves`, 90; P2.1): the slide's trailing hand (the off side) on the
  ground where the eye's ray through view (±0.42, -0.34) meets it (the step under it on stairs), skimming it with a
  friction shake; a hard landing's fists slapped onto the ground under view (±0.2, -0.3) (down 3 ticks, held to 7, back
  by 12) instead of `fp_land_hard`;
  feet to the wall in a hang. No legs in a slide. The stair slide tips the view 9° down the run (`BodyCamera`).
- **The Ascent in first person** (P3, `body.ascent.client.AscentFp`): moments, each where the Ascent gives the Feel
  Director its beat: `fp_rope_fire` (the main arm flings the rope), `fp_rope_release`, `fp_rope_launch`, `fp_wings_open`,
  `fp_wing_beat` (every beat, the one that takes flight too), `fp_barrel_roll`, `fp_boom` (hands up against it),
  `fp_double_jump`, `fp_air_dash` (the lead fist punches through), `fp_dive` and `fp_slam_land` (fists up for a dive slam
  or the Judgement Fall, smashed down on landing), `fp_sovereign_ascend`. Stances: on a rope the main fist holds it at
  view (0.3, -0.02, -0.72), where AscentRender now starts the rope in first person, the other hand joining to pump
  (forward) and climbing over it to reel (sneak); a zip, both hands on it; flying free, arms out low for balance (fists
  up in a dive slam); wings, arms out flat at the frame's edges trembling with speed (swept out of the frame folding into
  a dive); flight, one fist forward on a boost, palms down in a hover, arms sweeping up to climb, swept back cruising; in
  the Sovereign's form the arms are tinted gold (`FirstPerson.View.tint`).
- **Reaches** (P4.1, `anims.client.Reaches`, world source `anims_touch`, 200): a touch's hand goes to the thing and does
  it there. Each touch is a few keys (tick, s across, u up, n out toward you) about where the hand meets the thing (its
  anchor, followed as it moves: a creature's flank, a lid's edge), from and back to rest under the frame's foot,
  smoothstepped; drawn at 0.75 (both hands 0.85). A door's palm meets it where you clicked (vanilla's door is open by
  then) and pushes on through. The player never moves (Euan, 2026-10-25: walking you to the thing
  would take control): past 2.5 blocks the hand only gets an arm's length (1.3) toward the thing, and while a hand is out
  the view narrows ×0.95 (a lean; off with reduced motion). A chest's screen waited 4 ticks for both hands to reach its
  lid until §65.7 (it now opens at once and the hands go up with the lid). The fist clips below stay for books (no world thing).
- **Touches** (P4, `anims.client.Touches`, `anims.AnimsClips`): quick hand moments from the game's own interaction
  events (client side), so every module's blocks get them by what they are: a door, trapdoor or gate (`DoorBlock`,
  `TrapDoorBlock`, `FenceGateBlock`) pushed with a palm (`fp_push`), a lever thrown (`fp_lever`), a button pressed
  (`fp_button`), a chest, barrel, ender chest or shulker box's lid lifted with both hands (`fp_lid`; the screen opens at
  once and covers it in single player), berries or a plant that breaks at a touch (no hardness, no collision: flowers,
  ferns, grass, the Living Wilds' herbs) pinched and plucked (`fp_pluck`), an animal stroked with an empty hand
  (`fp_pet`), a meal from a bowl held up with the free hand under it (a stance while eating); P5 adds the Forge (block
  id `awaken:forge`, not its class) or an anvil hammered three times (`fp_hammer`, 18 ticks: holding the blade being
  tempered, the off hand strikes) and food a campfire takes (`RecipePropertySet.CAMPFIRE_INPUT`) laid on it by the hand
  holding it (`fp_lay`). P6 adds: a palm pressed to a stone and held while the light answers (`fp_palm`, 18 ticks; the
  hand lit from within, `View.glow`, and cooled a touch, 5-18) on Awaken's waystone, conduit, ascent stone, Hearth anchor,
  rest and Stillpoint shrines, gate entrance, seal and rune (by id) and vanilla's lodestone, respawn anchor and beacon; a
  notice torn off the Spire board (`fp_tear`); a grindstone cranked (`fp_crank`); a page turned at a lectern, an
  enchanting table, or as a book or the Dream Journal opens (`fp_page`); the smithing table hammered (`fp_hammer`); both
  hands set to a stonecutter, loom, cartography table or brewing stand (`fp_set`, two-handed like the lid); any
  `awaken:*_cache` lifted like a chest. The Ritual of the Bell (`story.client.RitualFp`, a view stance): kneeling in the
  bow both palms go flat to the floor (eased in over 6 ticks), as the eyes open the main hand comes up against the bloom
  (50-132), at the End both hands rise palms out, shaking harder as the light drains (30-195), and drop at the error. At most 9 ticks each; the
  action never waits; a swing cuts them; with the main hand full the off hand does it (each has an `_off` twin), with both
  full nothing. Settings (feel): `firstPersonMoves` (P1-P3) and `firstPersonTouches` (P4), both on.
- **Station scenes** (P5, `anims.client.station`): at a crafting table (used within 10 ticks of its screen opening, not
  sneaking: sneak + use is the plain screen) the screen is replaced by `StationScreen` (kind `TABLE`), the vanilla
  crafting menu with its grid and result drawn on the table in the world instead of on the screen. Each
  ingredient lies flat, centred on its drawn square (the texture's: 2-pixel squares a square every 3 pixels, middles on
  pixels 5, 8 and 11 of 16, so `CELL` = 3/16 and the grid 9/16 across; row 0 the far one; the way in snapped to an
  axis; a flat item 0.16 across, a block half that), the result lies flat on the top's near border (0.41 in from the
  middle toward you, 0.17 across, turning slowly where it lies), inside the table's own block so it never reaches into a
  wall, and flat it never hides a square (it once floated over the far edge and went into the wall behind; over the
  middle it hid the far middle square), the square under the cursor (and every square a drag has passed over,
  showing what it will get) is outlined (Holo blue).
  - **Layout** (`anims.station.StationView`, common so the tests run it headless): your inventory is a glass strip at
    the foot of the screen (vanilla's image, `top` = screen height - 165, the strip over its rows), the hint over it
    (wrapped to the room's width, centred), and above the hint the *room*: the middle half of the screen's width with
    JEI loaded (at least the strip's width), else the screen's width less 8 each side, from 6 px down to 4 px over the
    hint. The screen reports room and strip as its area (`getLeftPos`/`getTopPos`/`getImageWidth`/`getImageHeight`),
    so JEI's list and bookmarks keep to the sides. Hints: "Works just like a crafting grid. Sneak as you open it for the
    usual screen." and the furnace's.
  - **The view** frames the station: from your eye, the yaw, pitch and vertical field of view that fit every slot (a
    grid square ±3/32, the result ±0.085, a furnace's opening) inside the room, 6 % to spare, turned so they sit in its
    middle (`StationView.frame`, recomputed each tick; at most 100° or 1.5× your FOV setting). It eases in over 12 ticks
    (6 coming back within 12 s), out over 10; the player's own look never moves. Standing 1 to 4 blocks from a table at
    any GUI scale the framing stays under 100°; pressed right against it (under 1 block) the near edge can reach the hint.
  - **Clicks are vanilla's**: the scene screen is vanilla's own container screen, and a station slot is under the
    cursor where the world shows its square (`isHovering` answers from a ray through the view as drawn; the slots'
    old screen places are never hovered or drawn). So every mouse and key rule of the crafting grid holds: left click
    lays the held stack or takes it, right click lays one or takes half, left-drag splits evenly, right-drag lays one
    per square, double-click collects, shift-click on the result crafts all it can into the inventory and a plain click
    takes one craft, number keys, Q and the pick key work on the hovered square or slot, shift-click from the inventory
    moves into the grid; all through the menu's own clicks, which the server checks. Only a point inside the room picks
    a square: a click on the strip, the hint or a side panel never reaches the station. A click outside the room and
    the strip drops what you carry, as off any container screen. Your hands (world source `anims_station`, 200) rest off the table's near corners and one goes out to every
  square whose contents change (and to the result as it is taken), over 9 ticks; moving, jumping, E or Esc leave.
  A hand moves only within 6 ticks of your own click on a slot, so a furnace cooking on its own moves none; taking a
  result moves the hand to the result only.
  - **Furnaces** (kind `FURNACE`: vanilla furnace, smoker and blast furnace; Codex's furnace-interior, reviewed
    2026-10-28): the view drops to the mouth's height (block y + 0.57) where you stand; your body and your look are not
    moved. A client-only camera entity (StationCamera, unregistered, like the opening's OpeningCamera) carries the
    lowered view, eased in and out like the table (12/6 ticks in, 10 out); the field of view is set through the
    final-FOV hook, since a camera that is not the player gets no FOV-modifier event. The scene opens only from the
    front, 0.85 to 4.5 blocks from the block's middle, and only while the far item's edge still shows through the mouth
    (0.30 either side of it); from the side, the back, too close, or with something in the way you get the plain furnace
    screen. Eight rays 0.12 out from the eye's corners keep the drop from passing through a floor, wall or low ceiling;
    they are cast when the scene opens and again every tick (never every frame), so a block placed into the path while
    you work gives the view back and shuts the screen. Moving, jumping, E or Esc, another camera, death, a new level and
    logging out also give it back. Your own body is hidden from the lowered view; the hands rest beside it, by the
    shoulder (0.35 under the eye, clear of the floor), and only a working hand reaches into the frame.
  - **A real mouth:** every furnace, smoker and blast furnace in the world gets a block model with a recessed mouth
    (all four facings, lit and unlit): the five outer faces and a stone frame stay, the cavity is x 3–13, y 2–13, z 0–9
    model pixels with soot-dark walls and back (vanilla's cobbled deepslate, by name) and a coal bed, and a lit one glows at
    the back of the coals. The cavity's faces are lit from the air in front of the mouth (cullface north, so vanilla's
    block renderer reads the light there instead of inside the solid furnace, which is always 0; Sodium unchecked): an unlit furnace
    reads as a deep sooty hollow, not a black hole, and the cavity is culled when a solid block covers the front. Items sit
    3/16 inside the mouth at scale 0.24: what cooks on the left, the finished result on the right (±0.15, y + 0.57),
    the fuel on the coals (y + 0.26). They stay still while vanilla's flame, smoke and cooking go on. Each slot is
    picked within 0.16 of its middle and gets the front-facing outline; the cooking (Holo blue) and the fuel left (fire)
    still run as two thin lines over the strip; fuel is the off hand's, the rest the main hand's. The hint reads "Cook on
    the left, add fuel below, and take finished items on the right. Sneak as you open it for the usual screen."
  - **What's inside, screen shut:** the server sends each player read-only copies of the three slots of nearby
    furnaces (FurnaceContents, payload `furnace_contents`): the nearest 64 within 16 blocks, found every 40 ticks in the
    nine loaded chunks around them (`getChunkNow`, never a load), compared every 5 ticks, and only changes and
    removals sent. Using a furnace sends its contents at once, before the menu opens. Leaving range, an unloaded chunk,
    a replaced block, a new dimension and logging out drop a view; coming back reads it fresh. Nothing is saved and
    nothing in the furnace is changed. The items are drawn only within 16 blocks and from in front of the mouth, depth
    tested behind the opaque cavity walls (never through a wall); everyone nearby sees them whatever their
    `stationScenes` setting, which only turns the scene on or off. Recipes, fuel, taking items, XP and saves stay
    vanilla's. (A hacked client could read the contents of a furnace behind a wall within 16 blocks; a furnace shows
    its contents openly anyway, so this is accepted.)
  - **Other mods and packs:** no mixins. Only a plain single-variant cube furnace model is replaced; a resource pack's
    or mod's non-cube or wrapped model is left alone, and then the furnace has no scene and no items in its mouth (the
    plain screen opens). A mod that gives furnaces their own block-entity renderer keeps its look the same way. The
    models use vanilla's own textures by name; no Mojang file is copied. Setting `stationScenes` (feel), on.
- **The lens** (P5): the hand pass draws at a fixed 70°; anything the world anchors (arms on a pipe, at a table; near
  legs) has its view x and y scaled by tan(35°) / tan(world FOV / 2), so it lands where the world shows it on screen even
  with the view narrowed or widened (a station's zoom, the speed FOV). The lowered furnace camera uses the actual HUD
  FOV from the render state for that ratio, because its final-FOV hook affects both projections.
- Test: `anims_fp_clips` (the file reads, every clip the body and the touches play is in it, every one-shot gives the
  hands back). The table scene: `anims_station_frame` (seven GUI sizes from 320×240 to 1280×720, with and without JEI,
  standing 1 to 4 blocks off each side: every slot lies inside the room and a click on its middle picks it),
  `anims_station_cells` (each way in: every ingredient on a drawn square's middle, row 0 far, the result on the near
  border, all inside the table's block, a click straight down picks each),
  `anims_station_panel_click` (a square under the strip while leaning in: a click there picks nothing), and the clicks
  vanilla's screen sends on a real crafting menu: `anims_station_right_click`, `_right_drag`, `_left_drag`,
  `_shift_result`. Furnace regressions: `anims_furnace_camera_pick` covers all four facings, high/low player eyes,
  approach distances/offsets, small and large GUI layouts, all slot picks, and wall/near-plane collision rejection;
  `anims_furnace_contents` uses real vanilla smelting and save/reload, two viewers, inventory mutation, range/rejoin
  and removal; `anims_furnace_recess_geometry` checks the six packaged models have an open mouth and opaque backing.
  These are headless checks; rendered appearance, camera feel and third-party renderer combinations need in-game
  verification. Tours: `tools/autopilot/anims-pipe.txt` (P1), `anims-runner.txt` (P2), `anims-ascent.txt` (P3),
  `anims-touch.txt` (P4: filmed with the pilot's clip recorder, since a command reaches the client a few ticks late),
  `anims-station.txt` (P5), PACK=feel, HUD on. Pilot lines `use`, `attack`, `usehold <ticks>` press the real keys;
  `station <slot> [button]` clicks a slot of the open station scene.
- P1-P6 built (P5: the crafting table and furnace scenes, the Forge and campfire touches; P6: the rest of the touches, books, the Ritual's hands). Tour P6: `anims-p6.txt`. The casts (powers) still draw their own first-person
  arms (`CastAnims`); folding them into Hands is the powers module's step, coordinated with the combat plan.
