## 25. Arms (weapons and combat; plan docs/combat/PLAN.md, page docs/combat/plan.html; Euan 2026-10-25)

Euan: "Massively level up the weapons and combat system." Approved: "Go ahead with the full plan", every §7 decision
as recommended (i-frames on the dodge only; dodge = sprint + back/left/right/none; guard on right mouse; Hands grows to
weapons; vanilla swords get the verbs only; PAL optional; weapons carry an item level; a Lord-forged weapon goes to the
hand; S0 and S1 first). Then: "Do anything you can for the highest quality bar without me": the builder decides and
writes each decision here. Module `arms` (`dev.awaken.arms`), docs/modules/arms.md. Built so far: S0, S1, the sound kit.

**S0: every blow is told and has a class** (`core.api.Strikes`, §12).
- Classes: LIGHT (deflect, block or dodge), HEAVY (deflect or dodge; it breaks a guard), PERILOUS (dodge only), GRAB
  (dodge only), NONE (fire, falls, poison, the void: nothing answers it). An untold melee or projectile is LIGHT, a
  blast with an entity PERILOUS.
- Our creatures' melee is told (`MobGoals.ToldMelee` replaces `MeleeAttackGoal` everywhere): the body stops and winds up
  for 8 ticks (elites 9; bosses, wardens, breaks and nightmares 10), then swings; a target that stepped out of reach is
  a whiff. Big bodies make every third swing a HEAVY (+6 ticks, ×1.5 damage, transient `mobs_haymaker`). The flier's
  dive is told the same way (LIGHT). The tell is synced (`AwakenMob.DATA_TELL`) so the client can draw it by class.
- Abilities have a class (`Ability.strike()`): a heavy-flagged ability is PERILOUS; BOLT, ARROWS and NOVA LIGHT; SLAM,
  LEAP, CHARGE, BLINK, CONE, FANGS and FANGS_RING HEAVY; areas, beams, clouds, pulls, roots and darkness PERILOUS;
  summons, heals, guards, decoys and frenzies NONE. Every boss blow is told for at least 8 ticks (test).
- A mob's held weapon is only a look (`AwakenMob.gearStack` strips its attribute modifiers): a creature's damage is its
  def's, never its def's plus a diamond sword's.
- A broken stance staggers (`Strikes.stagger`): ours end the wind-up and stand still; any other mob is slowed to a stop.

**S1: the three verbs** (every `_sword` item and our `*_blade`s fight as the Longsword until their own style lands).
- One timing table, `data/awaken/arms/archetypes.json` (schemaVersion 1, read from the classpath on both sides at
  start: the server judges and the client predicts by the same rows, so it is not datapack-reloadable on purpose). Per
  style: guard, dodge, chain, mastery chain, input buffer (5) and late press (6); per move: wind-up, active, recovery,
  cadence window, motion (damage ×), posture, arc, reach, hit-stop ms, finisher, window, boss cap, charge, the
  first-person swing (from/to yaw, pitch, roll and lunge) and `swish` (light by default, heavy, thrust). The Longsword is
  the PLAN §4.2 table exactly; recovery scales with attack speed (×0.6..1.6 of the row).
- **Strike** (attack key): tap = the chain (strike 1, 2, 3; strike 4 with mastery); a press inside the cadence window
  earns a rhythm step (+8% damage and +1 posture each, up to 3); a press just early is buffered to the window and
  earns none; far ahead it counts for nothing. **One press is one press** (S2 fix, Euan's first play, 2026-10-25: a
  diamond sword showed nothing or one frame and a held heavy shook in place): vanilla asks again every tick the key
  stays down over a block (its mining, `Minecraft.continueAttack` through `onClickInput`), and each of those was taken
  as a new press, restarting the swing every tick; now only a press the key was not already down for counts, and the
  repeats are swallowed. Every new press strikes wherever it points; outside a fight (100 ticks) a block the weapon
  cuts faster than a bare hand (a log or planks with an axe, a web, bamboo or leaves with a sword; never in creative)
  is still mined. The old rule (any block under the crosshair outside a fight is mined) meant a click at the ground
  mined with no swing at all. **Only a fight opens the window** (Euan 2026-10-29: "I can't use a normal axe to break
  trees because it charges the hit like an attack"): every strike opened it, so one swing that missed a log, or hit
  leaves (an axe cuts them no faster than a hand), made every press for the next 5 s a strike, and each one kept it
  open. The window now opens only on something that means a fight (`ArmsRules.meansFight`):
  - a press at a creature: locked, under the crosshair, or the mark within the style's longest blow plus its step in
    (`ArmsRules.markReach`; a cow marked across a field is no fight);
  - a blow either way, a guard's answer, a dodge, or a blow landing on you.
  A strike at the air or a block still swings but leaves the window shut, so the next press on a log chops it. The
  HUD's busy look, the combat camera and the dodge still count any swing (`ArmsPredict.busyAt`). A hold goes on as its
  press began (`ArmsRules.attack`): a strike's hold stays the strike over a log, and a mining hold keeps mining whatever
  the crosshair slides onto, as vanilla does. `arms_attack_key` holds the rule, and checks that every fighting axe and
  sword (vanilla's and ours) cuts logs and planks, or webs and bamboo. **The chop** (Euan 2026-10-29: "Even without the
  timer, when it does cut, there is no animation"; the hands were posed only from Arms' own moves, so vanilla's mining
  wave never showed): while vanilla mines with a fighting weapon, the hands cut in a loop of their own, baked per style
  by `tools/art/swing_choreo.py`'s lever (`tools/art/swing_chop.py` into `fp_swings.json`'s `chop` and `hack`,
  `FpSwings.Loop`):
  - the chop (any axe, `minecraft:axes`, 8 ticks): set high on the hand's side, driven down through a mark just under
    the crosshair, stopped in the wood with a small kick back; the hack (a blade, 6 ticks): a quicker diagonal from low
    on the hand's side that carries on through. Each loop starts and ends on its blow and is entered on the way up
    (3 ticks in, 2.5 for the hack); it eases out to rest over 4 ticks when the mining stops (`ArmsChop`).
  - Each blow lands on the frame the block breaks (the last frame before the tick vanilla breaks it): every tick the loop's rate is solved from the block's own break
    time (the progress vanilla's `MultiPlayerGameMode` adds a tick, read through `BlockState.getDestroyProgress`,
    counted only on ticks it adds some: its 5-tick wait after a break is kept until the next mining spends it) so
    the next blow, or the one a loop later, lands then, held to 0.6-1.7 of its pace; between blocks (vanilla's 5-tick
    wait) and in third person it runs at its own pace. An iron axe's log and wait (16 ticks) are two blows.
  - A blow plays the block's own hit sound, louder and lower than vanilla's tap, an axe on wood adds `hit_wood`,
    chips fly off where the blade struck, and the first-person view kicks a little; the drive's whoosh as it leaves
    the set. Vanilla's own hit sound (every 4 ticks, out of step with the blows) is hushed on a block a chop is
    showing (NeoForge's `PlaySoundEvent`).
  - Third person: the body plays `arms_chop` / `arms_hack` (loops with `_end` settles, `ArmsClips`; posed for
    vanilla's hold, the item square to the forearm: the axe cocked high beside the head and driven down until its
    head points into the wood, the blade set out at the side clear of the head and cut down across the front), each
    clip's tick 0 where the hands enter the loop, so the body's blow lands with the sound; it starts again on the hands' next
    entry after the view turns to third person. Everyone else's chop is read from what every client already sees: a
    miner's arm swing (sent every few ticks while it mines; one swing alone, a block placed or a log stripped, is no
    chop), a fighting weapon in hand, no move of theirs in the last second, their look on a block it cuts; their
    blows play at the block on the clip's clock. No packet, no server change. Held = a heavy (charges from 6 ticks, full at the glint, 16;
  a release on the glint or any time after is the full blow: motion 2.4, posture 20, 110 ms hit-stop; held on to 24
  with Resonance full it is the Art). **The glint is the full charge** (Euan 2026-10-29: "the yellow ting happens before
  the full charge, and then nothing different happens for that attack sometimes"): it was a window of 2 ticks either
  side of the glint with the ting at its middle, so a release on hearing it came after the window shut, and the charge
  arc went on filling to 24 past the ting. Now the arc is full and gold at the ting and stays so; the server counts a
  tick short as full (`ArmsServer.GLINT_GRACE`: its count starts when it hears the charge, a tick or so late). **Tap or hold**
  (Euan 2026-10-26: "when you long click to power up your attack... on the first click, before letting go, it already
  attacks"; 2026-11-09: "it should go straight into an animation... the moment you start clicking long... it brings the
  weapon into its charge like form. But right now it just glitches into its form, or sometimes it starts an attack and
  then cancels the animation midway"). **The draw** (`ChargeDraw`): someone drawing a weapon back doesn't begin a light
  blow and swap to a heavy one; every press starts the same pull back, and letting go early just looses it sooner. Rounds
  of 2026-10-26, 10-29 and Swing Studio's round 8 each moved where in the light strike a held press waited (its hit, then
  its `set`), so every hold still showed 300 ms of a light attack and then swapped clips at the mark; the fault was showing
  the strike at all. Drawing from the press's first frame (9 Nov, first try) was wrong the other way (Euan 2026-11-09: "it
  just sometimes thinks you're going into a heavy hold or like a heavy strike when you're not, and it makes it look
  glitchy"): every click showed the start of the heavy's pose and then snapped into the strike, by an amount that depended
  on how long the finger happened to stay down, on every weapon. No capture saw it: at a tenth of play's speed it was a slow
  small dip, and at real speed on the slow runner a click's ticks ran inside one frame (`tap drawn` was 0 on all 99 clicks).
  Now **until a press has outlasted a click nothing on screen knows about it** (`ChargeDraw.GRACE`, 4 ticks, 200 ms;
  `ArmsPredict.undecided`): the hands and the view's lean go on with what they were doing, the move that was running
  playing on to its end (`underMove`, `underTime`) or the stance holding. After the grace it is a hold, and the hands
  leave for the heavy's drawn pose (its clip's first key, the very pose it is loosed from) on one curve (`ChargeDraw.ticks`,
  `SwingBlend`'s quintic: 0.6 of the weapon's glint, 7.8 ticks on the Daggers to 12 on the Maul, there before the glint),
  from wherever they are. The draw and the charge are one source of the hands (`ChargeDraw.source`), so the mark (6 ticks
  down, `PRESS_CHARGE`) moves nothing; the arm's strain grows from nothing after it (slow, about 3 Hz: the old 8 Hz tremble
  read as a glitch), and the charge's meter fills from the end of the grace to the glint, so a tap never lights it and it
  doesn't jump. **A release** gives the hands 1 tick to reach the loosed heavy from a full draw and up to 3 from one barely
  begun (`releaseTicks`). The press still begins the chain's strike on both sides (`ArmsPredict.waitHit`,
  `ArmsServer.waitHit`), so a tap is never queued behind a decision, but it is out of sight: its clock stands at 0, and the
  hands, the view's lean, its ribbon, swish, arc, step in and body clip all wait until the press is a tap. A press landing
  in another blow lets it land first (`handsFree`): the hands leave once it has, and the mark waits for it too; one landing
  in a recovery plays that recovery on through the grace, its strike unseen or still queued. **One chain** (Euan 2026-11-09: "the combo stops being the usual one", "it just switches to something else"): the two
  sides time the windows on their own clocks, more so with a busy server, so left to decide alone they disagree on a window's
  edge: one counts a strike the other never played, and the combo repeats a strike or skips one. Only the hands decide. The
  press carries what they did (`Press.claim`: the move they began, or `CLAIM_NOTHING` for a press too early to count) and the
  server plays that: never a strike they don't show, and never another in its place. A strike they began is kept however early
  the server's clock calls it, and waits for the server's own window (`ArmsRules.HEARD_BUFFER`), so nothing strikes faster than
  the rules allow. A press that only repeats the strike already queued says so (`CLAIM_AGAIN`), so it can't count as another. A claim must still be legal (`ArmsRules.follow`: starting again, or the strike after the last within 60
  ticks; a move off the chain only if the server saw its deflect, dodge, slide or fall, give or take `HEARD_SLACK`). A move off
  the chain it can't grant lands no blow and starts nothing else. The server's reply never changes the strike the hands are in
  or the step they count from; only what they couldn't know (an execution on a heavy's release) takes over. Any real difference
  is logged (`[arms]`), and each session logs what the hands played (`strikes played`). In a development run the last minute or so of the hands, every frame, is written to `logs/arms-blackbox.tsv` on leaving the world (`ArmsBlackBox`). **The blend's clock is a double** (found with the black box, Euan 2026-11-09): the hands' clock counts from the machine's boot, and as a float it moved in steps of 268 ms on a Mac up 34 days, so each `SwingBlend` sat frozen and then snapped, and about one strike start in four flashed the pose of up to 268 ms earlier for one frame (the draw into a charge "teleported" the same way). Test machines boot fresh, so no tour could show it. **A tap** (let go before the mark, `PRESS_TAP`,
  read every frame by `ArmsPredict.frame`, not on the next tick) starts the strike that waited, from where the hands
  are: its clip from its first key with its wind-up at twice speed (`TAP_RATE`), the hands carried onto it by its
  hit (`launchTicks`: half the wind-up, at least a tick, so a one-tick strike's way out lasts three frames and isn't a flash, and up to a tick longer the further the draw has come, so a
  late tap from nearly full draw doesn't snap across). That is the one trade: the blade reaches its hit 9 to 25 ms later
  than when the wind-up played under the press on a 60 ms click, 17 to 44 ms on a 100 ms click (the Daggers, which struck on
  the press until now, 38 and 85 ms); the server's hit is where it was. A tap with no strike of its own (one still queued,
  or a press too early to count) hands the blade back to what was running. While a strike waits, the client's chain clock
  waits as the server's does (its start a tick later for every tick past the wind-up, as `ArmsServer.moveTick`), so both
  time the next press alike: unmoved, the client ran each strike a tick or two ahead of the server, cut the last
  strike's carry short, and took presses the server's buffer refused, so strikes never landed and the chain fell out
  of step (the server's MOVE then swapped the clip mid-swing). A hit's hold freezes the hands only while the strike it
  came from is still on them: a late one froze the next strike mid-swing. Still down at 6 ticks and the strike is dropped
  unlanded and unseen and the charge begins (`PRESS_CHARGE`; a strike the same press queued mid-combo is dropped too). The
  charge holds at full for as long as the key is down, trembling, and goes only on the release (no auto-release; held past
  full it counts as full); the heavy's clip begins on the pose the hands are in, so the release has nothing to carry. The
  server never holds a blow on the client's word alone: with no tap or charge heard it lands `ArmsServer.HOLD_WAIT` (4)
  ticks after the charge's mark. In third person nobody near sees a waiting strike (`ArmsServer.shown`): no swing, no
  swish, no clip. The fighter's own body starts its held draw with the hands, over the same ticks, and a tap's strike clip
  takes it over; everyone else's copy of it starts on the server's word at the mark, over 5 ticks (`ArmsBodies.SEEN_DRAW`,
  was 2), and the weapon's wrist comes round with the clip (`ArmsWrist`; it snapped on at once). A riposte, Slipcut,
  Undercut or Plunge starts as it always did, and a press held on through one draws after its blow.
  Tests `arms_tap_or_hold`, `arms_dagger_click` and `arms_draw_smooth` (every style, from rest and from each chain strike's
  recovery: no frame steps further than the curve or the motion it came in on). A block under the
  crosshair outside a fight (100 ticks since the last) is still mined. A move strikes each creature in its arc and reach
  once, through vanilla's own attack at full strength (crits, enchantments, momentum and every damage listener still
  apply), scaled first by the move; vanilla's immunity is cleared between one fighter's blows; it never sweeps. A sweep
  only takes the aimed creature, hostiles and anything hunting the player: never a player, a villager or a pet. **What
  isn't alive** (Euan 2026-10-26: "rifts can only be broken at the core with your hands"; vanilla's own attack, which
  Arms stands aside from for its weapons, was the only way to strike one): what vanilla's attack would strike
  (`isAttackable`, not `skipAttackInteraction`: a rift's core, an end crystal, a boat, a minecart, an item frame) is
  struck when aimed, and in the arc only when tagged `#awaken:struck_by_sweeps` (the anomalies: the rift tear, the
  shimmer, the falling star), through `damageSources().playerAttack` at the move's strength (`ArmsServer.strikeThing`),
  with the impact sound, the hit-stop and the ribbon's flash; the thing decides what a blow does (a core loses a hit).
  Test `arms_strikes_things`.
- **Guard** (use key, the `blocks_attacks` component Arms gives every weapon that fights with a style: no delay, a front
  within 120° of where the head faces, vanilla's `horizontal_blocking_angle`; the Shieldblade 150, the Gauntlets 100): the first 4 ticks
  after the raise deflect a LIGHT or HEAVY (no damage, the attacker's stance takes 18 or 26, Resonance +20, a riposte
  for 12 ticks); after that LIGHT is blocked (70% less), HEAVY breaks the guard (50% less, the guard drops, 15 ticks
  before it can rise); PERILOUS and GRAB pass through. A raise within 8 ticks of lowering one that deflected nothing can
  only block (spamming is not deflecting). **Latency grace**: a guardable blow on an unguarded fighter waits up to
  latency/2 ticks (0 under 50 ms, at most 3) for a raise already on its way. **Untold blows** (Euan 2026-10-26, of
  zombies: "you don't know when it's going to hit you... so it's very hard to time a parry"): a creature's own melee
  (it strikes with its body, the direct attacker) with no wind-up to read is untold: anything not ours (every Awaken
  creature tells its blows) and not in `#awaken:told_melee` (the iron golem, the ravager, the warden): a zombie, husk,
  drowned, spider, cave spider, silverfish, endermite, piglin. Its deflect window is `ArmsRules.UNTOLD_DEFLECT` (4)
  ticks longer (the Longsword's 4 → 8; only on the early side: a raise after the blow still lets it land), and its
  deflect pays `UNTOLD_REWARD` (0.6) of a told one's Resonance and stance. Told blows keep the tight window, so reading
  a tell stays the skill; shots and players are never untold; nothing on screen foretells a blow. The combat sim's
  untold table (`combat_sim.py --untold`, docs/combat/untold-parry-2026-10-26.md): a Parrier against zombies, deflects
  40% → 70% and damage taken 117 → 58 per 100 blows once they raise into the wider window (Resonance per blow 8.0 →
  8.4); no Gate Lord or summon is untold, so the Lord table is unchanged. Test `arms_untold_parry`.
- **Shots** (Euan 2026-10-27: "Add blocking for arrows or projectiles, so if I have a weapon I can block the shot").
  Why a raised weapon seemed to stop nothing: the guard did judge shots, but past its first ticks it only took 70% off
  and the arrow still reached the body (it stuck in you, its tipped effect and fire took, the hurt thump and kick
  played); a blaze's or a ghast's fireball counted as fire (Strikes' NONE) and passed every guard and dodge unanswered;
  and the front was judged by the point on the body a shot reached. Now:
  - **Which weapons guard**: everything that fights with a style (every sword: vanilla's, other mods' `_sword`, the
    Hunter blades; every axe; the mace; every forged weapon: daggers, spears, glaives, the War-staff, twinblades and
    the rest) gets the guard, unless another mod gave it its own. Vanilla's spears and the trident keep their own right
    mouse and raise nothing.
  - **What a shot is** (`ArmsServer.shot`): a projectile struck, or the damage is `#is_projectile`: arrows, tridents,
    fireballs, wither skulls, wind charges, llama spit, our creatures' bolts, other mods' projectiles. A shot is at
    least LIGHT (`ArmsServer.kind`; Ability BOLT and ARROWS are LIGHT), so a fireball's hit is answered like an arrow's.
    A blast stays PERILOUS (a ghast's fireball, a wither skull and a firework burst through a guard: dodge them), and a
    bolt fired by a HEAVY or PERILOUS ability keeps its class (a HEAVY one breaks the guard and lands at half).
  - **Its front is its own path**: it comes from the way it flies, flat, whoever loosed it and wherever they stand;
    straight down, by where it meets the body. The guard's angle as for any blow; from outside it, the shot lands as
    ever, and sticks.
  - **In the window it glances off** (the style's deflect ticks, 3 to 5): no damage, nothing sticks, no effect or fire.
    The arrow is set just off the blade, clear of the body, and knocked up and aside back the way it came (0.18 back,
    0.16 to the side it came in on, 0.26 up, blocks a tick) to drop a few blocks off, harmless: its damage is spent. A
    bolt or a fireball breaks on the steel by its own hit; anything else with no weight to fall by breaks on it. It pays
    as a deflect (Resonance, Mastery III's charge, the Weave's beat), but opens no riposte and takes no stance: there's
    no one in reach.
  - **After the window it's blocked**: the shot stops on the blade (nothing sticks, nothing takes) and drops at your
    feet, and only its share (1 minus the style's reduction: the Longsword's 30%) comes through at the tick's end, with
    no hurt thump: the guard's own answer says it. The share already carries every scaling the shot had (a creature's
    level, a power's cut), so `ArmsServer.onIncomingPinned` (LOWEST) pins it back after the listeners' second pass.
  - A shot is never held for the latency grace: holding it would stop it at your body at once and land it after.
  - **Unanswered on purpose**: a piercing arrow (a Piercing crossbow) goes through any guard, vanilla's rule for
    shields; a damage type in `#bypasses_shield` (another mod's own choice); a shot that does no damage (a snowball on
    a player; a thrown potion breaks and splashes as on anyone).
  - **How it shows**: in first person the guard jolts (knocked back toward the eye, up and away from the side it struck,
    the tip thrown back 9°, ringing out over 9 ticks; the hands go with it), a spark off the blade back the way it came
    (`FxClient.guardSpark` on the effects engine, drawn at sword's length from the eye: a white-hot flash, a ring off the
    edge on a deflect, sparks in the weapon's light), the view's kick and, on a deflect, a smaller snap of the field
    than a blade's. Its own sound, `arms.glance` (tools/art/specs/audio_arms.py: a lighter, higher ring than a blade's
    deflect, sparks, the ricochet whining away); a blocked shot plays the block at ×1.2 pitch and 0.8 volume. Everyone
    near hears it, sees the body's jolt (the clip `arms_guard_jolt`, 6 ticks, then the guard held again) and the spark
    at its guard (`ArmsPayloads.SHOT`). On an onlooker's screen vanilla ends its own copy of an arrow at the guard, so
    they see it stop at the blade, not fall. Test `arms_shots`.
- **Dodge** (sprint pressed with back, left, right or no direction, on the ground; sprint + forward still runs): 6
  ticks, 2.6 blocks, client-predicted, server-validated (position within 1.5 blocks, charges, not in a wind-up or blow:
  a recovery can be dodged out of, which drops the rhythm). Ticks 0–4 evade any class (**the SPEC amendment: the only
  invincibility in AWAKEN**); a blow in ticks 0–2 is a perfect dodge: the attacker alone runs at half speed for 8
  ticks (every other tick; the plan's 0.45 rounded to the tick clock), Resonance +15, a Slipcut for 6 ticks. Two
  charges, 24 ticks each. A refused dodge stops the body where it is.
- **Context moves** (no input of their own): Riposte (strike ≤ 12 ticks after a deflect), Slipcut (motion 2.5, from
  1.2: the sim's reward for a dodge; strike ≤ 6 ticks
  after a dodge), Execution (a heavy on a broken creature in reach: motion 4, capped at 8% of a Lord's max health),
  **Undercut** (a strike out of a slide, the body module's own state: a low sweep, 160° wide, posture 8; the slide's
  trip still happens), **Plunge** (a strike in a fall of 2+ blocks arms it: the hands hold the blade high, the client
  dives, and it strikes all round where the fighter lands, motion × 1 + fall/6, at most × 2.8, the landing taking half
  its fall damage; it gives up in water or after 5 s).
- **The Art** (the Longsword's default): a heavy held through to full charge (2 ticks' grace) with Resonance full is
  the Art, not a heavy, and spends the whole meter (so holding past the glint is a choice). A great level sweep whose
  reach grows 2 blocks a tick through its 4 active ticks, out to 10, striking each creature once as the wave passes:
  motion 7 (3 as first built: the combat sim showed the Art dealt less than plain chaining in the same time, so a
  full meter made a fight longer; at 7 it pays), posture 30, 150 ms hit-stop, capped at 12% of a Lord's health. Its arc burns gold, a golden wave rolls on
  along the ground, and the kit's `arms.art` replaces the swish (the steel's ring swelling through the wind-up, the
  release, a wave of air rolling out). Lord-forged and legendary weapons bring their own Arts later (S8).
- **Posture** (creatures only; no player stamina): normal 20, elites, wardens and beasts 40, bosses, breaks and
  nightmares 100 (`CreatureTag`, `MobRole`). It drains at 6/s (Lords 8/s) after 2 s untouched; full, it breaks for 50
  ticks (Lords 40), then cannot break again for 6 s. On the struck creature only (the patent rule holds). Not saved.
- **Resonance** (per player, 0–100, not saved): deflect 20, perfect dodge 15, break 25, a finisher 6, a finisher in
  full rhythm (every press of the chain in its window: a cadence equal to its step; "rhythm 3" as first written was
  out of the 3-strike chain's reach) 12 more; drains 2/s after 5 s out of a fight. Full: the Art (S2).
- **Soft focus**: the creature you last struck turns your strikes toward it by at most 15°; looking more than 60°
  away from it for a second lets it go (server and client by one rule, `ArmsRules.lookedAt`).
- **Stances on the plates** (`core.api.Stances`, §12, read by the living module's plates): every stance change sends
  its snapshot (value, hold, broken ticks) to players within 48 blocks, the fighter included; their clients drain it by
  the server's own rule (`ArmsRules.drained`), so nothing is sent while it only recovers. Under the health bar, once
  strained: a thin amber strip filling from both ends to the middle (white-hot past three quarters), pulsing gold
  while broken. The fighter's focus wears the plate's bright rim.
- **Feel** (`core.api.CombatFeedback`, §12; one freeze for every blow, Powers' hits included): the struck body freezes
  and trembles for the move's hit-stop, the striker's hands and view hold for the same beat (the move's clock skips
  it), and the view kicks along the swing (≤ 2.4°) and settles; at most one freeze per 4 ticks in a sweep. A deflect
  holds both for 100 ms; a break freezes the body for 160 ms. Visual only: the game's clock never stops. Kicks follow camera shake.
- **The camera's voice and comfort** (S2, `ArmsFeel`, `ArmsComfort`: `config/awaken-arms-client.toml`). Arms owns the
  fight's camera: the kicks above, and the big moments as the field of view's push and pull, in fast over the first
  fifth and home on a long ease, a bigger moment taking the view from a smaller one: a deflect snaps in 3.5% (9
  ticks), a guard broken widens 2.5%, a break leans in 5% (16), an Execution 7.5% (22), the Art's release opens 6%
  (16), a perfect dodge breathes out 5% (18) and, with Lens on and no story moment playing, drains the frame for 12
  ticks (`awaken:arms_breath` in `lens/looks_arms.json`: colour at 0.42, cool, closed in; `LensClient.overriding()`
  says whose moment is on). Under 30% health (clear again over 36%) the heart beats (`arms.heartbeat`, 28 ticks a beat
  at 30%, 16 near nothing) and the frame's edges cool and darken (from 0.6 of full at 30% to full near nothing) (our own texture, `textures/gui/arms/low_health.png`
  from tools/art/specs/arms_hud.py), tightening on each beat; a Lens look was rejected for it: a look replaces the
  whole place's look and would flatten minutes of play. In the shoulder view the action camera takes a COMBAT pose
  while you fight (a blow either way in the last 3 s with a fighting weapon in hand, `CombatFeedback.engaged`): 0.45
  closer and 0.18 lower, the guard no longer read as an aim. Comfort, one switch per layer: `hitStop`, `viewKick`
  (0..1), `moments`, `combatCamera`, `lowHealth`; reduced motion is the body's one setting (`FirstPerson.reducedMotion`)
  and halves every kick and moment (and now the body roll's 32° dip and its twist too); Awaken's camera shake still
  turns every kick off.
- **The blow is centred on the hit** (S2): the server's sweep lands on the first active tick, so the blade's blow
  starts half the active before it (`ArmsHands.blowStart`: never before half a tick) and the recovery takes up the
  difference; the move ends when its row says. In first person, in third person (`arms_moves.py` keys the cocked pose
  there too) and in the trails. Before, the hit, its freeze and its red flash came while the blade was still cocked.
- **First person** (`ArmsHands`, a source on Hands' view layer, `FirstPerson.view`, every styled item; Euan
  2026-10-26: "like you're waving the sword instead of slicing... a bit too high"): every move plays a swing baked by
  the animation lab (tools/art/anim_lab.py `bake` -> `data/awaken/arms/fp_swings.json`, read by `FpSwings`): keys every
  0.25 ticks of the hand's move from vanilla's rest and its turn about its own place. A cut is a lever, the arm and
  blade turning as one about a pivot low and right of the view (0.80, -0.64, -0.48 from the eye), in the plane that
  holds the blade and the cut's direction on the screen (the row's swing.from -> swing.to: a slash flattened 0.6, a
  chop down, a rising cut up), the blade's flat across that plane so its edge leads (its cutting side toward the motion
  for an axe, a scythe or a glaive; a symmetric blade takes the side that turns least). On the hit tick (the server's
  first active tick; mid-blow for a released heavy) the blade crosses the target, a point just under the crosshair
  (0, -0.10, -1.20), at 78% along its length: seen along its length rising from the frame's lower right, not down it
  from the hilt. Drawn back to 50-74 degrees before it (heavier rows further), accelerating into the hit, the edge
  biting and slowing 14-22 degrees past it, a follow-through, then home. Thrusts drive straight along the aim, the flat
  level. The keys are for the style's forged weapon; a vanilla item in the style takes the same targets from its own
  hold (`vanilla` turn and grips in the file). A held heavy waits at its drawn-back start and trembles; an armed
  Plunge at the Plunge's; mirrored for a left main arm. Without keys a move falls back to the row's own slide (the old
  model). Lab numbers (the review set, 2026-10-26): every slash and chop crosses within 0.11 of the half-frame of the
  crosshair (most within 0.05; the Chain-blade's and War-staff's long blades +0.11..0.13), edge lead 0.87-1.00 through
  the blow (before: Longsword strikes 1 and 2 at 0.41 and 0.17, crossing 0.45 above). Test `arms_fp_swings`.
- **Forms** (tools/arms/forms.py writes them into archetypes.json's swing rows; Euan 2026-10-26: "a dagger should feel
  like you're actually stabbing forwards... a hammer... from up to down, or side to side... the big thing first...
  everything is just being swiped... very floaty"): every strike is done as its weapon is really used. Cuts turn the
  arm and weapon about the pivot: slash, chop (raised above the view, down), slam (the hammer raised overhead, crashed
  down head first), swing (level, a hammer's or axe's head leading), rise, whirl (the 360-degree finishers), reap (the
  scythe), lash (the chain-blade: the wrist whips twice as hard). Thrusts drive the point along the aim to the target
  (stab: a straight line, from below, overhand, or reverse-grip edge-down); the gauntlets punch (jab, hook on an arc,
  upper); the twinblades and war-staff spin about their middle; the shieldblade bashes with its shield. The combos:
  Daggers stab, rising stab, a reverse-grip rip, an overhand plunge, a spinning backhand (heavy: a deep stab); Maul an
  overhead slam, a head-first side swing, a ground-shaking slam, an uppercut; Axe a diagonal chop, a level backhand, an
  overhead chop, a wide swing; Longsword forehand, rising backhand, overhead chop, thrust; Greatblade a diagonal cleave,
  a level sweep, a whirl, an overhead chop; Spear and Rapier thrusts with a haft sweep or a flick cut third; Katana a
  level draw cut, a rising cut, a chop, a thrust; Glaive wide swings and a whirl; Scythe reaps, an overhead reap and a
  whirl; Gauntlets jab, cross, hook, uppercut, straight; Chain-blade lashes and a lasso whirl; Shieldblade cut, shove,
  chop, stab; War-staff swings, a chop and spins; Precursor Arm cuts and a thrust. A stab, jab or bash strikes narrow on
  the server (arc at most 30 degrees, the thrust's whoosh; the Daggers' stabs became single-target, their rip and
  backhand 90 degrees). Weight by style (snap: Daggers, Rapier, Gauntlets; blade; heavy: Axe, Maul, Greatblade, Glaive,
  Scythe, War-staff): how much of the wind-up reaches the cocked pose and how long it hangs there creeping back (heavy
  70%), the drive's curve (progress to the power 1.25 snap, 2.2 blade, 3.4 heavy: a heavy blow starts slow and
  arrives explosively on the hit), how far it carries past (0.45 / 1 / 1.5), the wrist's whip (6 / 18 / 7 degrees), the
  step in (0.04 / 0.07 / 0.13 blocks), how it comes home (snapped back, eased, hauled back after a beat). The view leans
  with every blow (FpSwings' camera keys, first person, scaled by the kick setting): a slam pitches it down on the
  crash (4.5 degrees heavy), a cut turns and leans it the way the blade travels, a whirl turns it furthest; heavy blows
  draw it the other way first. The third-person body of each move is picked by its form (arms_moves.py styled()).
- **First person, the hold** (tools/art/specs/arms_holds.py; Euan 2026-10-26: "a spear should still feel like you're
  holding a spear. Right now in first person, it just looks like a sword"): every style is held as that weapon really
  is, written in view terms (where the business end points: degrees left of ahead and up; its roll about its length;
  where the hand closes, from vanilla's resting hand; for an axe, a glaive or a scythe the side its working edge faces)
  and solved for each weapon from its own mesh, so each is seated in the hand. One scale for all (0.5, the Longsword's;
  the Daggers 0.575 so their blade reads): a spear is as much longer in hand than a longsword as in F5 and a dagger as
  much shorter, and a long point may leave the view. **Edge first** (Euan 2026-10-26: "You're never going to hold an
  axe on its side like that. You're going to hold the sharp ends downwards, similar to a sword"): the Longsword, Greatblade,
  Axe, Glaive and Daggers are held as the Katana is, turned a quarter about the length (roll 90), the working side down
  and toward the foe (`arms_holds.DOWN`), the flat to the side and never to the eye; the Rapier, Chain-blade and
  Precursor Arm are turned the same, an edge down; the Scythe's blade still reaches in across the top. **Standing as a
  vanilla sword stands** (Euan 2026-11-09, of the Longsword turned to roll 135 by the weapon audit: "it looks like it's being
  held the completely wrong way", "a vanilla sword ... actually feels like it has the sharp edge like forwards"): vanilla's
  `item/handheld` turn stands the blade up, leaned about 20 degrees back toward the eye, edge straight ahead, flat to the
  side, and because the hand is to the right of the eye the flat still shows. The Longsword, the Shieldblade's sword, the
  Axe, the Katana and the Greatblade now stand that way (`arms_holds.STANDING`, `FORWARD`; yaw 180 is the lean back), the
  Glaive keeps its line with its edge square down (roll 90). A swing's blade is solved in view terms, so a new hold moves
  only the rest and the way to and from it, never where a blow lands (`anim_lab.py bake`).
  Longsword standing, 72 up (size 0.85); Rapier en garde, the point forward at the target's height
  (20, 18); Katana two-handed at the right shoulder, standing, 78 up (size 0.9);
  Spear the shaft across the lower view, gripped part way, the head forward and up (46, 13); Glaive the same with the
  blade higher (54, 22); Scythe the snath up, the blade reaching in across the top (8, 64); War-staff at its middle
  across the body (58, 28); Greatblade two-handed, standing near the middle, 82 up (size 0.75); Maul two hands low on the haft,
  the head up (6, 58); Axe standing, its bit ahead, 80 up (size 0.75); Daggers short, the
  point forward (14, 42); Twinblades at the middle, the blades either way across (62, 34); Chain-blade the head forward
  on its chain (18, 38); Shieldblade a sword in the hand and the shield on the other arm ("The Shieldblade"); Precursor Arm forward like a
  drawn arm (14, 24); the Gauntlets keep their worn hold. `python3 tools/art/specs/arms_weapons.py
  holds` rewrites only the holds; the old check that kept every point inside the view (it shrank every style to the
  Longsword's outline) is gone. The swings are baked from these holds (they start and end at rest), and the lab's
  holds sheets (docs/combat/anim-lab/holds-*.png) show each style before, after and in F5.
- **The wrist and the arm** (Euan 2026-10-26: "it should actually turn it like as if you had a wrist... or a forearm
  that's turning... if you're gonna do an uppercut, you kind of turn it 180 degrees"): every cut turns the weapon about
  its own handle as the swing gathers and back square just as it lands (a slash 35 degrees, a chop 40, a slam 75, a
  hammer's swing 85, an uppercut 170: the head turned right over to drive it up), the wrist cocked so a heavy head
  trails the hands (16 degrees at least) and whips through. The arm that holds the weapon is drawn to its grip
  (§24 "Grips"): the hand closes where the style's hold puts it (arms_holds.py's grip, baked as fp_swings.json's
  `handGrip`), a vanilla item's on its sprite's handle. The lab's `strip` shows one move frame by frame (a turn in the
  hand reads there, not in an onion-skin).
- **A pair, and the left hand** (Euan 2026-10-26: "the left hand... looks like it's just floating near the hand"; "the
  gauntlet should be on the hand"): the Daggers and the Gauntlets are pairs (ArmsOffHand: the main hand's twin worn or
  held in the empty off hand, first and third person; in first person it rises and sinks with the main hand's equip, and
  the view counts that hand as full (`FirstPerson.offHandShows`), so a stance's fist never takes the twin's place: both
  daggers stay in hand through the tactical sprint's pump, a wall-run or a touch. Euan 2026-10-27: "you can't just make
  one disappear". A two-handed weapon sprints with one hand, the off fist pumping); the Gauntlets' combo alternates fists (jab, cross, hook, the other
  fist's uppercut, a straight; heavy both) and each fist closes inside its gauntlet (the mesh's centre), so the arm wears
  it rather than holding it. Every weapon's left-hand hold is its right hand's true mirror (arms_holds.mirror_display):
  26.3 mirrors any left-hand transform as it applies it (x translation, y and z rotation), so a left transform written
  pre-mirrored, as old vanilla JSON was, came out unmirrored and the twin sat beside the hand the arm reached for. A
  weapon's frame is its design's (along the item's diagonal, its flat across z), never a guess from its outline: a
  maul's head is longest along its striking faces, so the outline's thinnest direction was the way it strikes and its
  emblem side led; now the gold face leads in every direction it swings.
- **Working parts** (Euan 2026-10-26: "when it's a blade, it's the sharp end that's cutting. When it's a dagger, it's the
  sharp end that's stabbing. When it's the hammer, it's that end... think logically"): every move strikes with the part
  of its weapon that does the work, and the lab's `audit` holds it to that at the hit, on every weapon of the style in
  its own hold and in the hand that strikes (the off hand's twin in its left-hand hold, the move mirrored): a blade's
  edge, an axe's bit, a hammer's faces (never its emblem flat), a staff's ends, a point for a thrust, the knuckles for a
  punch, the shield's face for a bash, and a scythe's inner edge drawn back through. Which side cuts is read from each
  design (arms_holds.EDGES), never guessed from the outline: the katana's edge is on the outside of its curve, the tip
  curving back toward the spine, and the glaive's fluke weighs down its back, so the old guess (the heavier side) had
  every katana and glaive cut leading with the spine. Single-edged: Katana and Glaive (+x), Axe (the bit, -x), Scythe
  (the blade, -x), Twinblades (each blade's leading side, so the pair spins tips trailing), the Beastbound Longsword and
  Greatblade (tusk cleavers), the Wildhide skinning knife, the Beastbound tusk (honed on its inside) and the Veilwoven
  talon. A style whose forged (C) weapon is double-edged but has single-edged tiers (Longsword, Greatblade, Daggers)
  cuts with the side its hold's cut turns down toward the foe, and each single-edged tier is turned so its edge is
  there: one baked swing cuts with every tier's edge (the wrist turns a backhand over, as a single edge needs). A turn
  can mirror only two of a weapon's three ways, so a single-edged weapon's left-hand hold keeps its length and its
  edge mirrored and shows its other flat (before, the Wildhide twin's off-hand cut led with its back). The scythe is
  swept round, its blade's point leading, until the blade is past the target (0.12 blocks out), then hauled back 0.34
  blocks through it on the hit, its inside edge drawn through what it hooked; its blade, at the snath's top, is what
  crosses the target. Every punch lands knuckles first, square to the fist's travel (a jab and a hook palm down, an
  uppercut palm to the face, an overhand driven down); the Gauntlets' shared moves are punches too (riposte and undercut
  uppercuts, the dodge's cut a hook, the Art a straight, the plunge and execution overhands; their server blows kept;
  `ArmsClips.OWN_SHARED`: the Gauntlets play their own Slipcut, Undercut and Plunge clips, where every other style shares
  the Longsword's).
  The bash shoves the shield straight at the foe, its face square to the shove. Every move has a form in its row
  (tools/arms/forms.py writes the shared moves' too, read from their path as the lab always read them), so first and
  third person do the same thing (a spear's Art is a thrust in both).
- **One-faced heads** (Euan 2026-11-11, the Bell Warden's Toll: "facing the wrong way and hitting with the wrong end"):
  a head that works one way, in a style whose forged weapons strike with either side (the Maul's two hammer faces, the
  Chainblade's dart), declares its side like a single edge (arms_holds.EDGES: the Toll's bell mouth -x, its crown and
  hanging loop +x; the Beastbound tusk hook, the Veilwoven sickle and the Lantern Broker's Due, each hook curling to -x
  with its back, and the tusk's barb, to +x). Undeclared, each was held as drawn and the audit took either side as a
  hit: the Toll's mouth faced the eye in the right hand and its backhands landed with the crown; the hooks' plunge and
  execution landed with the hook's back, and in third person their three chain strikes and riposte. `arms_weapons.py
  check` holds every Axe, Maul and Scythe head to it from its boxes: a head not mirrored about its haft must declare a
  side, and the side it declares is the one its mass leans to. Its holds turn that side to the front
  (arms_holds.FACES: the side a style's one-sided heads are held with, the Maul's +x and the Chainblade's -x), and on
  each blow the style's baked keys land with the other side the weapon turns half round about its own length in the
  fist on the way in, whole just before the hit, and back as it comes home; the hand and the arm never turn. First
  person: FpSwings' per-move `turn` (half turns a key, signed the way round that keeps the head away from the eye; the
  Maul's strike_2, strike_4, riposte, slipcut and undercut, the Chainblade's plunge and execution), played by
  WeaponRenderer about the item's diagonal through its grip on the hands' own clock and carried across a change of
  source like the hands (ArmsHands.roll). Third person: `wrist3t` and `wrist3st`, the move's wrist keys with the turn
  in them (the Maul's strike_2, strike_4, slipcut, undercut, the carry onto the body landing its riposte square; the
  Chainblade's strike_1 to 3 and riposte), for the weapons `faced3` names; the Toll, its mouth the other side from the
  forged mauls' front face, is turned over in its hold too (`flipped3`). `anim_lab.py faced` writes both from the keys
  as they stand, and bake, splice, rerig and the rig's inject run it; the audit counts a one-sided head's own side
  only. GameTest `arms_fp_swings` holds the Toll's mouth away from the eye in both first-person hands, names the four
  in faced3 and holds every turn home by its move's end.
- **Third person, the wrist** (Euan 2026-10-26: "hold third person to the same working parts"; then "it's
  literally going through his body"): vanilla's third-person hold sets a weapon across the fist, square to the
  forearm, and a vanilla arm has no wrist, so the forearm's roll swings the blade round rather than turning its edge,
  and the shared poses swept long blades through the head, the body and the legs (a chop led with the other side of
  the blade from a forehand, a katana's wind-up crossed the torso). Now through each move's clip the weapon turns in
  the fist, about its grip (`ArmsWrist`; FpSwings' `wrist3` keys: a quaternion per arm every 0.25 ticks, in the forged
  weapon's item frame; a weapon turned over in its hold, `flipped3`, takes them turned over too): about its own length,
  so its edge, bit or face lies square into the blow, and bent in its own plane and out of it (15-degree steps, 90 and
  60 at most), so it stays out of the head, the body, the legs and the other arm. The lab solves it per move and arm
  (`wrists`, `bake`): a path through the bends at every quarter tick (Viterbi; at most 45 degrees a quarter tick, held
  still through the hit, from the hand's rest and home to it; a heavy loosed from its held draw starts turned), the
  working part's lead at the hit before everything, then no weapon of the style (every tier's outline at once) more
  than 0.3 px into the figure in the straight clip and its bent twin (Bendable Cuboids, in the pack: the item rides
  the bent forearm), looking ahead or down, then the least bend. The fighter's hand items are resolved again marked
  with their arm while a move turns them (the player's render-state modifier, last), so only a hand's weapon in third
  person turns, never one in first person, the hotbar or a frame; a left main arm keeps its hold (the keys are
  right-handed). A single-edged tier on the other side from its style's lead (since the edge-first holds, the
  Beastbound Daggers; before them the Beastbound Longsword and Greatblade and the Wildhide and Veilwoven Daggers) is
  turned over in its third-person hold. The Gauntlets are worn in third person
  too (`arms_holds.worn_third_person`: the knuckles down the forearm, the back of the hand out, the cuff round the
  forearm, 0.7 scale), never held out in front of the fist, and punch their own clips, each found in the lab (knuckles
  first at the hit, the bent twin 0.8 or more, nothing into the head or body): a jab with the arm level and the body
  lunging along it, an overhand angled down with the body dropping in behind it, an uppercut from a low bent fist
  rising, a hook with the elbow bent at shoulder height, the chest turning it round. The thrust keeps its arm and
  chest on the line from cocked to through, leans in less than it lunges and bends its elbow only a little (a turn, a
  lean or a straightening forearm swept a long point's tip off its line); the shield bash raises the shield square in
  front of the chest. The lab's `audit` holds every clip to the working part on every weapon in the arm that strikes
  (the bent clip at the bar; without Bendable Cuboids the straight one at least leading with it) and measures how
  deep any weapon goes into the figure (`body` compares it with no wrist); `wrist` draws a move's blow in third person
  with and without the turn. Measured over every weapon, both clips, looking level: moves putting a weapon more than
  1.5 px into the figure went from 99 of 179 without the wrist to 53 (the Katana, Glaive, Scythe, Spear, War-staff
  and Gauntlets none). What still goes in: a few designs' own bulk at rest (the Hive Regent's glass-wing knuckle guard
  along the forearm, the Gearwright Colossus's fist against the hip) and the wind-ups of the shared one-handed sword
  poses for the longest and widest weapons (the Greatblade's, the Twinblades' far blade, some Longswords): those need
  their own third-person poses and two-handed grips, not a wrist. The scythe leads point first in third person; its haul back through
  the target is first person's.
- **Third person from first person's blade** (the Katana, Greatblade, Maul, Spear, Glaive, Scythe, War-staff and
  Twinblades; the Scythe since 2026-11-03 from its own keys, "Hand-keyed moves" below; Euan 2026-10-26: "how are we gonna get that exactly the same as first person... so that it genuinely
  looks really, really good", then "roll the blade-first third-person rig out to the maul, spear, glaive, scythe,
  war-staff and twinblades"; tools/art/specs/arms_rig4.py). First person is designed from the blade (its path, the edge
  leading, through the target on the hit); third person was designed from the arm (a few poses per kind, the weapon
  wherever the hand put it), so long blades swept through the body and two-handed weapons were held in one hand. Now
  third person takes each move's weapon from first person's own baked keys (the grip's place and the blade's turn
  every quarter tick) and the body follows it: first person's arc about its pivot is carried onto a point before the
  chest (its middle for a two-handed grip; a spear's or glaive's lower, at the hip), turned as a whole so its line into
  the target runs from there to a point before the face, its lever scaled to the figure's reach, level with the view
  (a slide's or a fall's lean doesn't tilt it). Through the drive, the hit and the cut the weapon is exactly first
  person's; in the wind-up and the follow-through only, the move may be turned as a whole about the pivot (+36 to -30
  degrees: first person cocks an overhead chop back past the top of the view and carries a long blade down out of the
  frame, which in a figure are through the head and the legs). The grip shifts a little where it must (out, ahead, up,
  in toward the middle), chosen over the whole move at once (Viterbi): a blade by the face counts most, then any
  weapon in the body, then both hands reaching; the Scythe's held still about the hit, so its haul back through the
  target is first person's to the pixel. The chest turns with the lever, half a tick ahead of it (a style's share,
  at most 55 degrees). Two hands: the sword hand on the grip, the off hand on the hilt toward the pommel (swords, the
  Maul) or up the haft (polearms), by IK, elbows bent (Bendable Cuboids) or, for the straight clips, solved straight
  with their own wrist keys (`wrist3s`; `ArmsWrist` plays them when Bendable Cuboids isn't loaded); an arm may graze the
  body, never go into it. Polearms (Spear, Glaive, Scythe, War-staff) are fought side-on (the chest turned 20-30 degrees
  so the off shoulder comes forward: a figure's arm can't reach up a haft held square before it), the off hand sliding
  along the haft to where it reaches, on one side of the sword hand for the whole move (the side whose solved arms keep
  both hands on longer). Where the off hand still can't reach (a follow-through carried round to the far side, the low
  sweep out of a slide) it lets go cleanly, never floats beside the hilt. The Twinblades are swung in one hand at their
  middle, the other free. **A haft is held down it** (`arms_holds.HAFT3`: Maul 3.5 px, Spear 10, Glaive 5, Scythe 6,
  War-staff 5, at the third-person scale): their third-person hold moves the item along its length so the fist closes
  that far toward the butt, and the wrist turns the weapon there (`arms_holds.grip3`; `FpSwings.grip3`, WeaponRenderer),
  so the haft behind the hands doesn't run back through the chest (held at the item's grip, a Spear's 12 px of butt
  went through it on every move). These styles play their own Slipcut, Undercut and Plunge (`ArmsClips.OWN_SHARED`) and
  hold their own heavy's first pose while charging (`arms_<style>_heavy_charge`, `ArmsClips.charge`; its settle goes to
  the move's rest, the off arm out before the body), so the release never snaps. Measured (`arms_rig4.py bake`, the
  lab's audits, every tier of each style, looking level and down): every move but one leads with its edge, bit, face
  or point at the hit (the Veilwoven Spear's second thrust leads at 0.74 of the 0.8 bar); both hands on through 81-100%
  of each Katana move, 73-100% Greatblade, 90-100% Maul, 83-100% Spear, 80-94% Scythe, and most Glaive and War-staff
  moves (their thrust, plunge and slide moves mostly one-handed); the blade more than 1.5 px into the head, body or legs
  in 17 of the 89 moves (23 before: the Greatblade's from up to 3.7 px to about 1.3, the Maul's and Scythe's to none).
  What still touches: a two-handed sword's pommel by the belly (a figure's arms meet at most ~4 px before its chest, a
  hilt reaches 5-9 px behind the hands), the War-staff's rear end (1.3-1.9 px), the Twinblades' far blade in the
  spins; with them, 39 moves have some part of the weapon past 1.5 px (24 before, held one-handed at the side); and the
  Executions' first quarter tick out of rest, where the blade passes the head looking down. Review set:
  docs/combat/anim-lab/third-<style>-blade-first.png (shipped against new, every move from behind-right) and
  fp-third-<style>-<move>.png (first person over third person from behind-right and the side, at the same moments).
- **The animation lab** (tools/art/anim_lab.py; SPEC §25, Euan's ask for a way to see the motion): `sheet` / `all`
  draw each strike's first-person frames as the game composes them (the swing, Hands' view layer, vanilla's rest, the
  weapon's hold and mesh, 70 degrees) as an onion-skin with the blade tip's path (wind-up blue, blow gold, recovery
  grey), the hit ringed and the crosshair; under it the tip's height on screen and the edge lead over the move; beside
  it top and side views of the grip and tip paths against the view cone (`--model old` shows the row's slide).
  `third` draws the body's clip (arms_moves.py) with the blade in its hand as vanilla's ItemInHandLayer holds it, two
  views and the third-person edge lead (a thrust: the point lead). `audit` checks every move's working part ("Working
  parts" above; exit 1 when one fails). `film` overlays the game's own frames (the clip
  recorder's, in a tour) the same way. Sheets for the review set in docs/combat/anim-lab/.
- **The arms film** (`arms film <name> <ticks> [gap] [downscale]`, autopilot only; `ArmsFilm`, `FilmLog`; the dagger and
  scythe audit, 2026-11-02): a fight filmed as the game draws it, into clips/<name>/: a picture every `gap` ticks of game
  time, and for every frame drawn a row of `track.tsv` (the hands' clock, the move, the press, the hold, the hit-stop, each
  blade's base and tip where it is drawn: both views in the camera's place with the world's axes) and in
  `events.tsv` what happened between frames on both sides (press, buffer, begin, tap, the server's press heard, begin,
  wait over and hit, its MOVE, REFUSE and HIT reaching the client, the swish, the source change, the third-person clip).
  `arms strike [hold]` holds the key that many ticks. Every blade of ours is logged each frame, the one not laying a
  ribbon too (the twin's own first-person draw is marked while it runs). Tours `tools/autopilot/arms-film-daggers.txt`
  and `-scythe.txt` film slow, combo and spam takes with the world at 2 ticks a second; `tools/art/arms_film.py` reads a
  take (each press by its number: begun, released, the blade on the target on screen, the server's hit, the impact
  shown; tip speeds and spikes; marked strips; stamped videos at a set pace, timed by the film's clock, cropped for
  third person). Speeds are timed by real time, as the hands' clock runs: inside a runner's stutter the client's ticks
  bunch and the frames' game time lags the hands, which read as false jumps; a press seen through a frame drawn over
  250 ms after the last is marked and left out of the summary. A server stalled at world start (its roads) ran a
  tour's `cmd` set-up in one tick before the ground had loaded, so the set-up waits on the server: `arms studio <item>`
  builds the studio on the server's own thread with its chunks loaded, `arms waitserver [n]` holds the script until the
  server has ticked n times, and `arms rate <r>` sets the world's pace and holds until this client runs at it (the
  core autopilot retries an `arms` line that answers null). The feel's clock (`ArmsFeel.nanos`: the hands, the hit-stop, a struck
  body's freeze and recoil, the ribbons) runs at the world's pace, so a slowed film shows a 35 ms freeze as 0.7 of a tick,
  as play does; at 20 ticks a second it is real time. Each row ends with `rib`, which of our blades lays its ribbon that
  frame (1 the main's, 2 the twin's), and `arms_film.py gates <clip dir>...` reads every take against the audit's gates,
  pass or fail: the impact within 17 ms of the blade on the target (the first impact of the move once ours has begun:
  fights' stage 0 shows it on the predicted hit, which can come before the server's on the film's clock), the freeze on the hit tick, the press to the blade
  within the wind-up, a stab's point within 0.15 of the crosshair and its blow three times its return, the dagger's free
  hand travelling, one ribbon a swing (the scythe), the scythe's blade in view through the wind-up, and a chain's hands
  never home between strikes.
- **What play showed about the rigged moves** (Euan 2026-11-09). *No dip on the way home:* a move whose hand is already home
  when its follow-through ends has nothing left to do, so `swing_studio.cut_pose` returns the rest there; the recovery's rise
  used to run anyway, and the War-staff's strikes 1 and 3 and the Spear's strike 3 sank and came back up after settling.
  *The Maul's uppercut* keeps its face to the front: a two-headed weapon has no reason to turn over, and the 170 degrees it
  unwound about its haft while rising read as a spin glitch (`tools/arms/feel/maul.json`, form `rise`, `roll0` 16). *The
  Greatblade's heavy* is a chop, not a rise: charged high in view, tip up, grip right of centre, and brought down across the
  crosshair. The rise it shared held the blade off the bottom of the screen for the whole charge (0% on screen, now 100%);
  its server row is the same chop (`archetypes.json`, form `chop`, dir [-0.3, -1]). *The Katana is held edge down in third
  person* (`arms_holds.EDGE_DOWN3`): vanilla's handheld hold puts a design's +x side up as the arm hangs, so it is turned
  half round about its length, and the rig solves each move's wrist from that hold, so the edge still leads every blow.
  *The Gauntlets are the arm* in first person ("as if it was like your entire hand, basically like a glove"): no arm rises to
  them (`ArmsHands.worn`), because a bare fist was showing round a smaller gauntlet, and each runs on past its rim into a sleeve
  of its own cuff and metal, banded every 8 texels, out of the view however far a punch carries it (`<id>_arm.mesh` and
  `.png`, drawn by `WeaponRenderer` in first person only; `arms_weapons.gauntlet_sleeve`). From outside the cuff already runs up
  the forearm, so nothing changes there.
- **Hand-keyed moves** (the dagger and scythe audit's rebuild, Euan 2026-11-02: "Go with all recommendations"; never
  tuned by a script, the Swing Studio's sixteen rounds read worse each time): the Daggers' and the Scythe's moves are
  written pose by pose in `tools/art/arms_keys.py`: the fist placed on the screen at a depth, the point drawn at a
  screen place for the blade's length (0.627 for all four daggers, weapon-designs 7bbc8f78; the scythe's snath top,
  0.656 from the fist, with the blade's way out from it), the edge's way, for both hands; each blow's key on the tick
  the server counts its hit (the first active tick; a loosed heavy's and a landed
  Plunge's 0.3 in). Between keys a hand travels on a cubic, stopping only at a key that says so, its turn eased the
  same way. `bake` splices the keyed styles into fp_swings.json (schema 7) and leaves every other byte as it was;
  `check` proves that against git and holds the data to the GameTests' rules; `strip` and `chain` draw a move or a chain
  as play strings it. A keyed style's entry carries `"by": "tools/art/arms_keys.py"`, and anim_lab.py's bake keeps it.
  - *The stance* (schema 7, a style's `stance` [dx, dy, dz, qx, qy, qz, qw]): where the hands rest between moves,
    a pair's off hand its mirror while the twin shows; let go as the guard comes up, never while the weapon cuts. A
    keyed style's moves start and end there (arms_fp_swings: "ends in its stance").
  - *The Daggers* (Euan 2026-11-09, after the first stabs-only rebuild: "barely even hitting", "add the slash back in", "a similar
    animation to before, just polished up with everything we've learned and without the glitches"): a forward grip in both hands.
    Strike 1 the right stabs, strike 2 the left, strike 3 the right slashes, strike 4 both stab at once, strike 5 (mastery) the
    left slashes. A stab drives the fist forward and in, the point travelling up the screen toward the crosshair, because a
    point that stays put on the screen reads as nothing moving however far it goes (that was "barely moving forwards"). Every
    blow is one stroke: from a stop, through the hit, to one stop a little deeper, then a slower way back. Nothing chambers
    first: a chamber, a blow and a follow-through inside 1.3 ticks was the jitter. At every blow the fist stays low and on its
    own side, no higher than -0.55 on the screen and no nearer the middle than 0.26 ("the hands still go way too upwards"); a
    slash carries the fist across the middle and stops by 0.06, where the old one threw it to -0.30 ("way too much to the left
    side"). The hand not striking draws back into its guard (0.54, -0.92) while the other drives, so each blow starts where
    its hand already is; before the slash the right has turned its edge out and waits, cocked out to the right with the blade
    showing its length, through the whole window a press can land in, and before the finisher both gather low at the hips. The
    view leans a hair with a stab and rolls with a slash. The heavy charges at the hips and its release is both stabs in half
    a tick. The riposte is the chain's stab at full reach. The slipcut (wide, a little low) and the undercut (at the legs) are the
    slash. The server's rows are the slashes' again: strike 3 and 5 arc 90, the slipcut 120, the undercut 160, each with the light
    whoosh. The Art and the blows driven down (the Plunge, the Execution) keep their own keys. `arms_keys.py check` and the test
    `arms_dagger_stabs` hold the rules (which strikes slash, the fist low and on its own side at the blow, never crossing over).
  - *The Twin Blades* (Euan 2026-11-09: "way too fast", "no spinning animation or anything that makes it look really like
    cinematic and awesome", "too much movement, so it makes the trail ... take up too much of the screen"; replaces round 5's
    figure-eight): one double-ended blade twirled in one hand. Every strike is whole turns about the true middle of the shaft
    (`handGrip`, where the fist is), and the fist moves very little: the spin is the motion, so the ribbon is a thin line near
    the tips at 60% light. A light strike is one turn: half of it arrives on the hit, with the upper blade at the crosshair,
    and the second half brings the same blade home, the hit's speed carried through it so there is no stop inside. Strikes 1
    and 2 turn opposite ways, strike 3 is near flat, strike 4 (and mastery's 5) are two turns with the hit after the first.
    Slower than before, about the same damage over a combo: the chain takes 37 ticks where it took 24, and each strike's motion
    is higher to match. The turn is written as a turn, an angle against time (`Spin` in `tools/art/arms_keys.py`) and not as
    poses to blend between, because a turn between poses takes the short way and can't go past half. Third person's wrist
    (`_spin_wrists`) is the same turn about the weapon's flat, leaning onto first person's plane by the hit; solving it from
    where the blade points flips each time the blade passes the far side of its axis (179 degrees in a key). The two moves
    that don't spin (plunge, execution) reach for whichever end is nearer.
  - *The Shieldblade* (Euan 2026-11-09: "reinvent that one from scratch"; "when you push with it, it doesn't feel like a push";
    "it feels like it's hitting the wrong side"; "the blocking with it doesn't even block with the shield side"; "it just looks
    like a tiny dagger swung out of a shield"): one item that is two things. A sword as long as a Longsword in the main hand, a
    shield with a front and a back on the other arm. The item's mesh for inventories and stands is the two together; the hands
    draw them apart (`<id>_blade`, `<id>_shield`): the shield is a copy of the stack in the free off hand with its `ITEM_MODEL` set
    (fp_swings `off.model`). With something in the off hand no shield is drawn. In first person you see the shield's inside; it has
    its own rest and guard (`off.stance`, `off.guard`), and the sword stands as a Longsword does, edge ahead (arms_holds.STANDING). Its cuts (strike 1, the slipcut, the undercut) run on the Longsword's own line: the point travels straight through the crosshair on the hit with the blade square to the way it goes (Euan 2026-11-09: "it reads as just waving the swords instead of swinging it blade side"; the old keys laid the blade over, so the point went over the top of the frame and off to the far left and never crossed the target). The second strike and the heavy are the shield alone (`hand: off`, form `bash`, no ribbon): gathered out to
    the left with its face turned aside, driven across to the middle of the view and squared to the front, held a moment, because depth
    alone doesn't read and a shove must cover what it hits. The body lunges behind it (0.9, the heavy 1.3), it holds longer on the
    hit (85 ms, heavy 130), and a target is thrown back (`BASH_PUSH` 2.6 where a thrust is 1.15; a Lord isn't moved). The heavy is
    charged with the shield gathered further still. The guard is the shield: raised to the middle of the view with the crosshair
    over its rim and the sword held back at the side; in third person `arms_shieldblade_guard` lays the arm across the front and
    `off.guard3` turns the shield square to the front (a left-handed player's isn't turned, as for every third-person wrist). Through the
    sword's cuts in third person the shield stays on its arm's clip and no wrist turns it; it leaves the clip only when it does
    something (`shield3`, its own weight in `_shield_weight`), and its wrist is the whole frame, never the shortest turn to a line,
    because which way a shield's front looks is the point of it. Reaches now match the Longsword's (3.0, 2.8 for the shove, 3.2,
    3.6).
  - *The Scythe* (decisions 8 and 9): two hands in both views, the main fist low on the snath and the off fist on its
    peg (weapon-designs' second grip, design (4, 6.5, 0); fp_swings `offHand` is that point in the main hand's frame,
    ArmsHands closes the empty off hand there). Every strike's wind-up is in view: strike 1 draws the snath back up
    over the right shoulder, the blade high in the view's right, and reaps across the crosshair on the hit tick, carried
    down and round to the left and held low there; strike 2 turns the blade over on the way up (never in less than a
    tick) and reaps back from the left; strike 3 lifts the snath overhead and behind, hooks down on the hit and hauls
    back through, then settles (by tick 10) into a ready stance, the snath across the body and the blade low before
    the feet, before it goes home: decision 9 keeps its full 20 ticks of recovery but shows them as a stance, not a
    pause; strike 4 reaches far out to the right and sweeps round. The moves keep their old lengths. The ribbon lays
    over the cut only (`trail`, from a fraction of a tick before the hit to about a tick after it), so the return
    lays none. `arms_keys.py check` holds every strike's point inside the view at its set.
  - *Third person from the same keys* (decision 7; `arms_keys.py third`, written to `tools/art/specs/arms_keys3.json`,
    which `arms_moves.py` builds into each keyed move's clips, `arms_daggers_<move>` and `_bent`, with the heavy's charge

    drives the Scythe.
  - *A charge is held in view* (Euan 2026-11-09, of a heavy charged under the view: "you can't even see the blade anymore"):
    a heavy's first pose is what a charge holds for as long as the press lasts, so its draw back is cut until the blade's
    middle sits at most 0.75 of the way to the frame's edge (`swing_studio.HEAVY_SET`), an overhead's too (one that rose out
    of the frame left a strip of haft on the screen; a filmed Longsword showed nothing at all). The Longsword's heavy, a rising
    cut loosed from below the frame, is now a high diagonal chop in first person and pins as a chop does; third person's
    `arms_heavy` is still the rising cut.
  - *The Maul's charge is held raised* (Euan 2026-11-11: "it's just holding it in front of the character instead of actually

    upright and leaning 29 degrees ahead of fists low in the corner: a hammer presented, not lifted. A raised head can't be

  - *A charge goes the way its blow will* (Euan 2026-11-11, of the other heavies that come down: "If they go in that
    direction when doing a charged hit then yeah. It should actually charge in the direction it's about to go in"). Every

- **Swing Studio** (plan docs/weapon-anims/plan.html, page https://claude.ai/artifact/NZVvwxBumfRvcwRiiA45co; Euan
  approved all six decisions 2026-10-28: "go ahead with the entire plan... so that it genuinely feels extremely
  satisfying"; his notes: swings aim too far up, the katana is floaty, "each strike starts from rest... it kind of feels

  - *Feel specs* (`tools/arms/feel/<style>.json`, read by `tools/art/swing_studio.py`): the knobs a round changes
    (weight fields, the cut's pivot, target, draw, drive, carry, exit, rise; per form and per move; the camera's decay;
    the bite; the swish's lead; the off hand's gap). No spec: the style bakes exactly as before (round 0 rebakes
    today's keys bit for bit). `bake [--round N] [--out PATH]` keeps third person's wrists from the game's file (a
    first-person round never moves them; `--solve` solves them again). Schema 5 adds per move `swish` (the tick its
    swish starts), `swishSound` (the studio's sound in place of the row's), `bite` [rate, ticks]; per style `offHand`
    and `vanillaOffHand`; the file's `round`.
  - *The second-generation cut* (a spec's `cut`): a lever about a shoulder-like pivot (0.62, -0.52, -0.30) through a
    target at chest height (0, -0.24, -1.15); loaded with an eased draw to a set at the frame's edge, held a moment,
    driven explosively (progress^power over `drive` ticks) so the hit is the fastest moment; then one continuous fall of
    speed (1 - (1 - x)^k, k matched to the drive's end so nothing stutters) carrying the blade on and down out of the
    frame, where it waits for the chain's next press (the cadence window's start) before rising home from below. A
    whiff flows through; a landed hit's resistance comes from the runtime (hit-stop, then the bite).
  - *The report* (`swing_studio.py report [style ...] [--json OUT]`): per move the contact height (the blade's middle on
    screen at the hit), the share of the cut's fast motion above the eye line, the speed at the hit against the peak,
    the drive's length, how soon it slows after the hit, slow motion left in view after it (drift), the swish's peak
    against the hit, the view swinging back past level, hands on; each against its class's range (cuts: contact
    -0.45..-0.10, above the eye at most 40%, the hit at least 0.85 of the peak; drift at most 50/75/100 ms for
    snap/blade/heavy; swish within 35 ms). `strip60` draws a move at 60 fps, `ab` a move from an older file over
    today's. Rounds are logged in docs/weapon-anims/ROUNDS.md.

  - *The runtime*: a change of source (a chained strike, a move ending or refused, the charge taken up) never jumps:
    `SwingBlend` carries each hand's shown pose and the view's lean into the new one (inertialization, Bollo GDC 2018:
    the gap and the old motion along it decay on a quintic over at most 1-2.5 ticks for a strike, 3 to rest, never past
    it). The hands' clock follows the server's tick rate (`TickRateManager.nanosecondsPerTick`). The bite: after a landed
    blow's hit-stop the hands run at `biteRate` for `biteTicks` (snap 0.5 x 0.5, blade 0.35 x 0.75, heavy 0.25 x 1.25),
    then make the time up by the move's end (`ArmsPredict.viewTime`; the server's clock never bites; off with hit-stop
    off). The swish plays on the blade's clock, its whoosh peaking as the blade crosses (the fighter's on the frame it
    falls due, those near on the server's tick, `ArmsState.swishAt`); a blow landing before the row's sound could peak
    plays `arms.swish_quick` (its pass 38 ms in), the katana's cuts `arms.swish_katana` (thinner, a clean high whistle,
    56 ms). Two-handed weapons (katana, greatblade, maul, spear, glaive, scythe, war-staff, twin blades) close the off
    hand on the handle below the main (0.11 to 0.40 blocks down it; the Scythe up its snath on the peg, "Hand-keyed
    moves") when the off hand is empty, through every swing and the guard;
    a stance's own off fist still takes the hand.
  - *Live tuning* (`SwingTuning`; `/awaken swing tune on [path] | off`, `ab`, `blind`, `note <words>`, `last`; the
    state kept in `awaken-arms-client.toml`): while on, the swings come from `<folder>/fp_swings.json` (the folder: the
    path given, else `AWAKEN_TUNING`, else /Volumes/MEDIA/Awaken-tuning if present, else `awaken-tuning` in the game
    folder), looked at once a second, read on a worker and put in use only between moves. A newer schema or a round
    older than the jar's is refused with a line in chat. `prev.json` beside it is the A/B; blind mode names the two X and
    Y at random; notes go to `notes.jsonl` with the style, move, round and version that was playing. Off: the jar's.
  - Tests: `arms_swing_blend` (no jump, no overshoot, the new pose by the end, the lean carried), `arms_swing_reload`
    (a set read whole, swapped in and out, a newer schema refused), `arms_feel_rules` (every swish starts by its hit,
