- **Fight Feel** (plan docs/fight-feel/plan.html; Euan 2026-10-28: "Go ahead with the fight feel plan", all eight
  recommendations yes: walls stop blows, wall hits are feel only, sweeps cut wild grass, counters at x1.5 posture,
  knockback follows the swing, the strike step on by default, overworld fight music after its listening page, built in
  four stages, each merged after its tests and Euan's play). Every blow gets an answer that matches what the blade did.
  - *The blow* (`arms.Blow`): one description of each landed hit, built in `ArmsServer.hit` and packed into HIT's aux2
    (29 bits; arms_result and arms_seen are unchanged): the move, KILL, LAST (no other creature within 16 blocks has
    the striker as its target), STRONG (a finisher, a perfect heavy, an Execution: weight x1.3), the bodies this move
    has struck (the cleave), the lift (-1 pins: chop, slam, over; +1 lifts: upper, rise; read from the swing's `form`,
    now in `Archetype.Swing`), the push's world yaw (a byte) and the cut's sideways share on screen (-7..7).
  - *Stage 1, the blow lands* (built 2026-10-28):
    - Knockback follows the swing (`ArmsRules.push`, `LivingKnockBackEvent` while the hit resolves): away from the
      striker along the line to the body, turned along the cut by 45% of its sideways share (a full side cut 55% away,
      45% along the blade's travel, never toward you; a left-handed striker's screen is mirrored). A thrust (stab, jab,
      bash, any thrust swish) pushes straight away x1.15; a pinning blow x0.7 and its rise taken away; a lifting one
      +0.18 blocks a tick (less by knockback resistance). Vanilla's strength, enchantments and resistance otherwise
      stand. A Lord's body (150 health and up) keeps vanilla's push, as a player's lift does (vanilla sends and puts
      back a struck player's motion). A kill is thrown x1.6. Switch: `directionalKnockback` (awaken-arms.toml; off:
      vanilla's push).
    - The recoil (`ArmsRecoil`, every client): once the freeze ends the body springs (omega 18, zeta 0.45: out to the
      shove in 70 ms, back past rest by a fifth, settled by 0.4 s; `ArmsRules.recoil`): shoved along the blow by
      0.04/0.06/0.09 blocks (snap/blade/heavy, `ArmsRules.heft` as the swings weigh them; x1.3 strong; half under
      reduced motion), up for a lift and down for a pin by half that, turned 6-12 degrees with the cut and tipped 4-8
      degrees away (by weight), all scaled by size (1.5 / (width x height + 0.3), from a quarter to double: about 1 for
      a zombie; half under reduced motion; at once with hit-stop off). A blow landing mid-recoil adds its spring to the
      one still settling (its clock held through the new freeze), so the body never snaps back to rest first. The
      shove and the turn ride the render state; the tip and the fall a pose pushed in
      `RenderLivingEvent.Pre` at the lowest priority and popped in Post (a body another listener draws itself cancels
      Pre and is left to its own clip). Skipped for our own creatures (they play their clips from `CombatFeedback.blow`,
      now fed the server's direction), Lords and the camera's own body. 32 slots, no allocation, nothing at all once
      the last recoil is over.
    - A body a blow killed falls the way the blade went: vanilla's flip zeroed and our own fall about the flat axis
      across the killing blow, held upright through the kill's freeze, then on vanilla's timing (the square root over
      20 ticks), so it still sinks and puffs out as before.
      Switch (both): `recoil` (awaken-arms-client.toml).
    - The kill moment, for the one who struck (switch `killMoment`): the freeze 40 ms longer to at most 160 and never
      shorter (`ArmsRules.killHitstop`, added by the viewer so the switch is theirs; a freeze the 4-tick gap skipped
      stays skipped), the view's kick x1.3, `arms.kill` over the impact (a low body drop under a steel ring, pitched by
      what falls: stone and slime low, bone, armour and a spirit higher), the ribbon flares toward white for 160 ms,
      and the last foe lets the view breathe out (field of view +2.5% over 14 ticks). Observers see the same freeze
      and fall.
    - The freeze lets go instead of jumping (`ArmsFeel`, every struck body, also before Fight Feel): it trembles along
      the blow (0.045 blocks, easing to 40% through the beat; diagonal when the blow's way isn't known), and when it
      ends, what the body moved while held (the push, its walk and animation clock) is caught up over 110 ms on a cubic
      ease-out, so it launches out of the hit rather than appearing where the push had already carried it (more than
      2.5 blocks is shown as it is). A body struck while still held keeps its hold; struck while letting go, its new
      hold starts where it is shown.
    - The cleave: the one freeze of a sweep grows by 12 ms for each extra body it strikes on that tick (up to 3), the
      kick by a fifth per extra body (up to x1.6), and each extra body plays `arms.cleave` a semitone higher. Feel only:
      no extra damage or Resonance.
    - Sounds: `arms.kill` (3 variants, -13 dBFS) and `arms.cleave` (3, -15) in audio_arms.py, Kenney CC0 layers and
      the kit.
    - Tests: `arms_knock_dir` (a right-to-left cut throws a zombie left, 30% sideways at least; a thrust straight back;
      a chop lifts it under 0.05; the rise lifts it; a Lord is pushed as vanilla pushes it; the blow packs whole),
      `arms_kill` (a hit that doesn't kill is neither KILL nor LAST; a sweep through three hunting wolves sends KILL
      and CLEAVE 1, 2, 3 with the freeze growing 12 ms a body, LAST only on the third), `arms_recoil_spring` (peak 1,
      back-swing under 30%, settled by 0.4 s). The frame cost (budget 0.05 ms with 20 struck bodies) is not measured
      yet: builders run no tours.
- **Third person** (Player Animation Library, optional, through `core.api.PlayerClips`; `ArmsClips`, `ArmsBodies`):
  a full-body clip per move from tools/art/specs/arms_moves.py, its keys on the timing table's rows (cocked at the
  wind-up's end, through at the active ticks' end, home by the endTick), each with a bent twin; the guard held while
  it is up, the heavy's draw held while it charges (a blade-first style's own: its heavy's first pose), the dodge back
  or to a side by its way (mirrored for a left
  hand). The fighter's own from their prediction, everyone else's from `Seen` MOVE, CHARGE and DODGE. Every clip is
  checked for an arm through the head or body (under 1.25 px). Without the library: vanilla's arm swing.
- **The blade's own ribbon** (S2, `BladeTrail`; PLAN §4.8's SWEEP): while a blow is in the air the blade lays a
  ribbon over its outer part (the outer quarter of a vanilla blade in first person, where the blade fills a third of
  the view; ours from 78% of the way along to the point), sampled every frame from where it is drawn: the fighter's own in first
  person (any styled weapon; a vanilla sword through `item/handheld.json`'s display transform and its sprite's blade,
  pixel (5.5, 10.5) to (15.5, 1.5); ours from the mesh, the corners half way along to the furthest one), and our
  weapons in anyone's hand in third person. The samples live in the world 150 ms (a turn of the head leaves the ribbon
  behind), run on a Catmull-Rom curve between frames, and the head is carried on along the blade's last motion to the
  present frame so it never trails the steel. Drawn in two passes: a shade (the colour at two fifths, alpha-blended,
  `arms_trail_shade`) under the light (additive, the weapons' glow pipeline), so it reads on a noon sky as well as at
  night (additive alone vanished by day: the frozen-ribbon tour showed the geometry right and the light invisible);
  alpha 0.55 + half the rhythm's brightness, nothing at the root, a soft rise, a crisp whitened strip along the tip's
  path, out with age. `arms trailfreeze on` (autopilot) holds ribbons still for a frame; `arms ribbonlog N` logs
  samples and then draws them flat red to check the geometry. The hand-arc crescent below stands aside wherever a
  ribbon is laid; it stays for vanilla blades seen from outside. The first tour on the Mac showed the crescent floating
  off the blade ("laggy", Euan).
- **Trails and sparks** (`ArmsFx`, on the powers module's effects engine: one budget, one settings page). As a
  blow starts (the end of its wind-up), its arc: a crescent following the hand's own arc about the shoulder, pushed
  out 1.5 blocks ahead of the eye so it faces whoever looks (an arc in the plane of the look is seen edge-on, a line:
  found in the tour), nothing at the hand, a tinted body and a crisp bright rim along the blade's visible middle,
  its head crossing in the move's active ticks on the hands' curve, its tail chasing it. A thrust is a straight
  streak. The weapon tints it (diamond cyan, netherite violet, gold, copper, iron, stone, wood; our blades Holo blue),
  each rhythm step brightens it, a perfect heavy and an Execution burn gold; the fighter's own is softer in first
  person. Where a blade lands, on the body's near side: a small white flare and sparks by what it met (warm off plate
  and stone, pale chips off bone, brown off wood, wisps through a spirit, green spatter from slime, dark red from
  flesh). The fighter's from their prediction and the HIT result; everyone near from `Seen` MOVE and HIT (observers
  also see the struck body's freeze).
- **HUD** (`arms_hud`, above the crosshair layer): a 15-dot arc under the crosshair for Resonance or the heavy's charge
  (full and gold at the glint, the full charge), the dodge's two pips beside the sprint line, and a red shard on a ring round the
  crosshair pointing to where the last blow on you came from (any held item; 24 ticks). Nothing at rest.
- **Network**: `arms_press` (strike, charge, release; seq, look, aimed id), `arms_dodge`, `arms_result` (to the
  fighter: move, hit, deflect, block, guard break, perfect dodge, evade, break, refuse, dodge, resonance, hurt) and
  `arms_seen` (to players within 48 blocks). The client predicts every move and takes the server's word.
- **Config**: `awaken-arms.toml` `enabled` (server, synced; default on). Off: vanilla melee, and the guard Arms gave a
  sword never rises (a sword another mod made to block keeps its own).
- Off while riding, sleeping, projecting, meditating, flying or gliding; Arms never runs a spectator's melee.

**Weight in the Hand** (the polish pass on the weapons' motion and the fight's feel; page
https://claude.ai/artifact/7myPKAY51tmf9kCzryQdVw, its source docs/weapon-feel/plan.src.html with the measuring scripts in
docs/weapon-feel/harness/; Euan 2026-11-10: "the animations are still decent... what's the kind of small polish pass that we
can do to massively bring it to the most extreme and awesome level", then "Go ahead with all": all six decisions as
recommended).
- **What it is.** Every one of the 179 first-person moves is kept. The pass adds what is round them: hits that are honest,
  sounds that can be heard, a blow whose direction is the blade's, weight in the freeze and after it, a guard that eases, a
  draw for every weapon, a world that answers. Measured before anything was built (the page's section 2): 99 of the 334 hits
  his game showed in fifteen sessions (4 to 9 Nov) were never confirmed by the server; the hits on flesh and armour, the blunt
  hit, the kill and the Execution carry 80 to 98% of their sound below 300 Hz (the block's old fault, §47.3); 36 of the 102
  weapon sound files hold the thin tone he calls a synthetic ding; the view's kick and the knockback's side read the timing
  table's old `from`/`to` and disagree with the baked blade on 28 of 139 cuts, eleven thrown the opposite way (the page's
  first count, 17 and nine, had not mirrored the off hand's moves); the fast part of
  a cut is about three frames at 60 a second, and after its freeze the blade is at a dead stop within 60 ms; the guard drops in
  one frame; a changed weapon stays below the frame for its attack cooldown (vanilla's `FirstPersonHandsAndItems`), 9 ticks
  filmed for the Katana; Fight Feel's stages 2 to 4 (above) were never built.
- **The rules of the pass** (from the sixteen Swing Studio rounds, which tuned to scores): no script score is a target; no
  weapon's motion changes until he has flagged it in play; every feel layer is built for the Longsword and the Maul first and
  he picks between it and today's in the game before it goes to the other fourteen; his play log is read before any theory.
  Every layer is drawn by the client from what the hands already decided, on the hands' own double clock, has its switch in
  `awaken-arms-client.toml` (off: today's picture, frame for frame), and never moves a hand that is at rest.
- **The decisions** (2026-11-10): the layers, not a re-make (1); stage 0 is built before he plays, so one session gives his
  first feel of the 9 Nov round and the ghosts' causes (2); the fourteen sounds that failed are remade from Minecraft's own
  recordings named in `sounds.json`, after a listening page, with the draws' new sounds, and the swishes stay (3); blows stop
  at walls, with the glance (4); counter-hits are not in this pass: their rule goes to the fights' owner, who places it with
  the bosses' minds (5); the Katana rests lowered at the hip with no new model (6).
- **Code first** (Euan 2026-11-10, after stage 0: "The whole plan is approved. Just go ahead and actually do everything and
  code everything... prioritize coding over testing... code at the best possible level of code... and then do a test"):
  stages 1 to 5 were built in one run with their first values and one test pass at the end. Where the plan said "after your
  play" the best call was made and its switch and its measurement kept, so his play corrects it: the ghosts' fixes without
  his log (the ghost report stays on), the sounds on the listening page's first pick for each row (the page stays), the
  weight layers on for all sixteen weapons (one command flips them: `/awaken swing weight on|off`). Stage 6 needs his notes.
- **The stages**: 0 truth; 1 honest hits, and the blow's direction
  from the baked blade; 2 sound; 3 weight (the shake in the freeze, the settle where the blade stops, the living hold); 4 the
  guard, the draws, the Katana's sheath, the look-lag by weight; 5 walls, the glance, grass; 6 his notes weapon by weapon, by
  hand as the Daggers were, then third person against first.
- **Stage 0, truth** (built 2026-11-10; nothing a player sees or feels changes). *The ghost report*, development runs only
  (the black box's switch, `!FMLEnvironment.isProduction()`): the server keeps, per press and body, the nearest it came to
  landing a blow (`arms.HitWhy`, fixed arrays, written only while a development client in the same JVM has it on, as
  `FilmLog` is): what it did with each press (the hands said nothing, too early, a move it couldn't grant, queued, run), and
  for every foe within 4 blocks past a sweep's reach that the sweep left unstruck whether it was out of reach (the gap and the
  reach), outside the arc (the degrees) or out of the height's band, and for every body struck whether damage landed (with the
  damage cooldown vanilla saw). The game notes each blow it plays (`ArmsGhosts.shown`: the press, the body, the gap it saw, the
  reach), and when the ledger counts one as never confirmed (`HitLedger.ghosts`) the server's record gives its cause
  (`HitWhy.explain`): out of reach, outside the arc, out of height, struck with no damage, landed under another press (a blow
  on the same body within 1.5 s under a different press: the same blow filed differently, which the game then played twice),
  nowhere near, the press ran no move, landed and the word not matched, or no record (a server in another process). Each is
  a line of the play log (`[arms] ghost: seq 212 strike_2 on minecraft:husk: shown at gap 2.91 (reach 3.30); out of reach: on
  the server it was 0.82 beyond reach ...`) and an E row of the black box, with `shown` and `confirmed` rows beside the
  `impact` one; on leaving the world `[arms] ghosts by cause, N of M blows shown: ...` follows the old count. Test
  `arms_hit_why` (the nearest call is kept, each cause is told apart, nothing is kept while off, the ledger tells each ghost
  once, the real sweep and blow write the record). *The listening page* (`tools/art/weapon_listen.py`, written to the
  gitignored `run-autopilot/weapon-listen/` and served to the browser pane; it plays Minecraft's own recordings from this
  machine's asset cache, so it is never hosted or committed): each of the fourteen sounds and the five draws in a scene at the
  game's own timing, today's sound beside three picks made of named recordings, his mark for each saved to `picks.json`
  there. *The baseline film*: `tools/autopilot/arms-feel-baseline.txt` (CI run 42788877636).
- **Stage 1, honest hits and the blade's own direction** (built 2026-11-10).
  - *The direction.* `tools/arms/blows.py` writes each cut's travel on the screen at its hit into its swing row of
    archetypes.json as `blow` [x right, y up] (`Archetype.Swing.blow`, optional), read from the blade the baked keys draw: the
    blade's middle over the half tick round the hit, mirrored for a move the off hand strikes, the two together for both
    hands; a hand-keyed move keeps the direction its own bake worked out (its `kick`); a thrust has none. `ArmsRules.blowX`,
    `blowY` and `side` read it (the row's `from`/`to` only where a move has none), so the knockback's side, the struck
    body's recoil and a kill's fall follow the blade, and so does the view's kick (`ArmsPredict.impact`: a thrust now nods
    the view in as the hand-keyed stabs do, `THRUST_NOD` 0.6, and a left-handed fighter's kick is mirrored as their screen
    is). `blows.py check` fails when a row is more than 20 degrees off the bake: run it after any re-bake. Test
    `arms_blow_dir`.
  - *A blow always lands whole.* `ArmsServer.hit` clears the struck body's damage cooldown before every Arms blow, whoever
    hurt it last (it was cleared only after the fighter's own): vanilla's half second of immunity after fire, a fall, a
    pet's or another fighter's blow swallowed or shrank blows the game had shown. Each move still strikes a body once.
  - *One blow, one press.* The two sides can file a strike under different presses (a queued strike pressed again moves to
    the newer press on each side's own clock, and a HIT sent in between carries the older number): its impact then played
    twice and one copy was a ghost. `HitLedger.confirm` matches the server's word by the press, then by the body and the
    move (the oldest such blow still waiting, `reconciled` counted in the log's line); `HitLedger.struck` keeps the hands
    off a body the server already struck with the same move under another press (`SAME_BLOW`, 12 ticks); and a HIT is held
    for the blade by the move, not the press (`ArmsPredict.early`), also for a strike still queued behind the one on the
    hands (the server ran ahead), never longer than `QUEUE_WAIT` (8 ticks).
  - *The hands' word.* The game draws a creature about three ticks behind where the server has it (26.3's stepped
    interpolation, by the entity type's update interval), so one just knocked back can look in reach and be a block further
    on. When the hands play a blow they say so (`ArmsPayloads.PRESS_HIT`: the move's press, the body, the move's
    ordinal), and the server lands it by their word (`ArmsServer.claimed`, `grantClaims`) when its own sweep left that body:
    only a creature its sweep would look at (a foe or the aimed one, never a person), once a move, only while the move they
    name runs here (from 3 ticks before its first active tick to 6 after its last; a word that comes before its move waits
    up to 20), and only within `CLAIM_REACH` 1.25 blocks and `CLAIM_ARC` 20 degrees past the move's own reach and arc, and
    never through a wall. The damage, the push and everything after are the server's own. Switch `claimedHits`
    (awaken-arms.toml, on); `[arms] N landed by the hands' word (x past the server's reach on average)` in a development
    run's log says how much it is used. Test `arms_claim`.
  - *Struck, no harm.* A blow that strikes and does no damage (an invulnerable body, another mod's refusal) is answered
    (`ArmsPayloads.DULL`): Minecraft's own weak-attack sound, and the ledger counts it answered, not a ghost.
- **Stage 2, sound** (built 2026-11-10 on the listening page's first pick for each row; his ear is still the judge, and
  the page stays). Fourteen sounds play as mixes of Minecraft's own recordings (`ArmsSounds.mix`, `Voice`), each recording
  named as an event of its own in the merged sounds.json (`fight.*`, `"type": "event"`, so it follows the game's own
  variants and no file of Mojang's is in the repo), layered in code on both sides (`ArmsSounds.play`, `ArmsAudio.play`):
  a hit on flesh the strong attack over the kit's thump at 0.45; a heavy one the critical hit (pitch 0.85) and the knockback
  hit (0.7 at 0.8) over the thump at 0.5; the Maul's the mace's own blow (0.8) over its thump; armour an iron golem struck
  (0.9 at 1.2) with the strong attack (0.6); a spirit a breeze hurt (0.8) with a sweep of air (0.6 at 1.2); a blow on you
  the knockback hit (0.9 at 0.8) over the thump; the parry an anvil landing (0.45 at 1.6) over the shield block (at 1.1);
  the glance a breeze turning a shot; the charge a crossbow drawn (0.8 at 0.8) and its glint the crossbow locking (0.9 at
  1.2), a wooden click in place of the ting; the kill the critical hit (at 0.8) over the body drop; the cleave Minecraft's
  own sweep; the Execution the mace's heaviest ground blow (0.9) with the critical hit (0.9 at 0.7); the perfect dodge a
  dragon's wingbeat (0.6 at 1.7). The swishes, bone, wood, stone, slime, the block, the tells and the Art are as they were.
  Switch `recordedSounds` (awaken-arms-client.toml; off: the 25 Oct kit).
- **Stage 3, weight** (built 2026-11-10; `arms.SwingWeight`, plain maths, drawn by `ArmsHands` over the same keys; test
  `arms_weight`). By `ArmsRules.heft` (snap / blade / heavy):
  - *The shake* (`weaponShake`): while a landed blow of the move on the hands is frozen, the striking hand shudders along the
    blow's own direction, 0.005 / 0.008 / 0.012 blocks at first (about 5, 9 and 13 pixels at 1080p), dying to nothing by the
    freeze's end, its sign turning every 16 ms. Added after the blend, so it is never carried into the next move.
  - *The settle* (`weaponSettle`): where a baked move's hand stops after its hit (`SwingWeight.stop`: the first key under
    6% of the move's fastest, found once a clip) it carries 0.015 / 0.025 / 0.04 blocks and 1.5 / 2.5 / 4 degrees past, along
    the way it came in, peaking 0.9 / 1.4 / 2.2 ticks after the stop and back to nothing with no second swing (x e^(1-x)).
    A stop within 0.05 of the pose the move ends on is the rest itself and is never settled: 138 of the 179 moves have a
    stop, the rest go home in one motion.
  - *The living hold* (`livingHold`, off under reduced motion): a held weapon rises and sinks 3 mm once in 4.5 s, and the
    hands trail the view's turn by the weapon's weight (`FirstPerson.lagReach`, `lagRate`, §12, read by Hands' look-lag:
    0.75 of the reach and 1.3 of the rate for a dagger, 1.45 and 0.65 for a Maul).
  - Reduced motion halves the shake and the settle. `/awaken swing weight on|off` flips the shake, the settle, the living
    hold, the draw and the guard's ease together.
- **Stage 4, the guard and presence** (built 2026-11-10).
  - *The guard* (`guardEase`): it comes up on an ease-out that seats with a small settle, in the server's own two ticks
    (past nine tenths by a tick and a half), and lowers over three, from wherever it is (`SwingWeight.guardUp`,
    `guardDown`). On film it rose in a straight line and was back at rest one frame after the key came up. Only the
    picture: the windows are the server's. A deflect throws the blade at the blow and back, a third harder than a block's
    knock (`ArmsHands.parry`).
  - *The draw* (`weaponDraw`): a change of the fighting weapon in hand (its item or its slot, seen each tick) plays its
    family's sound (blades Minecraft's iron armour going on, pitched by the blade; hafted weapons an axe biting wood; the
    Chain-blade a chain; the Gauntlets leather; the Precursor Arm a conduit waking; `ArmsSounds.draw`, those near from the
    server on the equipment change) and the weapon comes up on the draw's own clock, 6 / 8 / 10 ticks by weight on an
    ease-out that seats a hair above its place, its wrist turned in 22 degrees at first (`SwingWeight.drawSink`,
    `drawTurn`). It replaces vanilla's rise for a fighting weapon: vanilla raises a changed item only as its attack cooldown
    refills (the item swap scale, cubed), a cooldown Arms never uses, so the weapon was out of view for nine ticks on film
    with the Katana and by that rule over twenty with the Maul, and a strike thrown meanwhile was drawn that far under the
    frame. A strike begun during a draw brings the weapon up within 2 ticks from where it is. A power's stow never draws.
    The hand's own transform takes the stack vanilla's hand drew last tick when it is the same item as the one held: a
    slot the server re-sends (wear, any sync) is a new object until the next tick, and told apart by identity the weapon
    fell back to vanilla's place and sink for those frames (the proof tour's film: out of view for 0.4 ticks mid-draw).
  - *The Katana's rest*: rested as long as its drawn cut asks (`drawIdle`, 40 ticks from the last move's end, the count
    the server grants the cut on: a press, a hold not yet a move and a dodge leave it be, so the hands show the cut
    exactly when it will be given), it is lowered across the body: the hand just under the frame's edge, the blade low
    with its point to the off side, its edge down and its flat turned up to the eye, the guard showing (`ArmsHands.HIP_D`
    (-0.15, 0.04, 0), `HIP_Q` 88 degrees over, 3 forward, rolled 80 about its length; the first value, back past the
    hip, hid the blade and laid a forearm across the frame, and the second showed the re-cut blade from its spine, a
    grey line). The pose is picked offline with `tools/art/swing_studio.py` `lead_points`, which matches the game's own
    blade within about 6 degrees.
    It lowers and rises over 6 ticks on the hands' own clock from wherever it is (`SwingWeight.lowered`, `ArmsHands.hip`:
    the rest pose itself moves, so the strike that draws it is carried out by the blend, and nothing that starts or
    breaks the rest moves the hand in one frame), with a soft click on the way down. A change of weapon is the one place
    it is set outright, and only unseen: the weapon going away keeps its pose while it sinks, and the one coming up
    takes its own rest on its first frame, still under the frame, so a rested Katana rises straight to this rest. The drawn cut has its own sound over the swish (a rasp and a ring) and a
    ribbon half again as bright. No scabbard (decision 6).
- **Stage 5, the world answers** (built 2026-11-10; `arms.ArmsWalls`, one set of rules for the server's sweep and the
  client's prediction; tests `arms_walls`, `arms_cut_grass`).
  - *Walls stop blows* (`wallsStopBlows`, awaken-arms.toml, on): a body is struck only when a line from the eye to its
    nearest point, its middle or its top is clear of every block a body can't pass. Three points, so a creature half
    behind a door frame still counts; glass, fences and leaves stop a blade, tall grass doesn't. The hands' word is held
    to it too. Things that aren't alive (a rift's core) are struck as before.
  - *The glance* (`glance`, client): a strike that has struck no body by a third of a tick past its hit, and whose blade
    meets a block within the move's reach (three lines 14 degrees either side of the look; a pinning blow one more, 25
    degrees down), glances off it: the block's own hit sound, lower and louder, with a ring over stone and metal; its
    chips (three); sparks off stone and metal (warm, `FxClient.guardSpark` at size 0.85, under the size that adds a
    deflect's ring) and duller ones off wood (0.5), started 0.08 blocks off the face and thrown out of it along the
    blade's way. They are the guard's near-eye sparks and not a body's: a wall is struck within a blade's length of the
    eye, and the effects engine shows no glow inside 1.5 blocks and only part of one inside 4, so a body's sparks at a
    wall were never seen (two proof tours, 10 Nov). The blade is knocked back against its cut for two and a half ticks;
    the view kicked one degree against it; a 30 ms hold off stone and metal. Leaves, wool and what a hoe mines only rustle. The
    block isn't harmed and the chain goes on. Those near hear the block's hit from the server on the move's last active
    tick.
  - *Grass* (`cutGrass`, awaken-arms.toml, on): each active tick cuts the plants tagged `#awaken:cut_by_sweeps` (short
    and tall grass, ferns, dead and plain bushes, dry grass) in the sweep's arc and reach, as a player's break
    (`CommonHooks.fireBlockBreak`, so a claim can refuse; drops as vanilla's), at most 12 a blow; never where the
    fighter can't build, at a Hearth, in the city or in a village.

**Styles** (S5 batch 1, the timing table's rows beside the Longsword's; PLAN §4.5): every style has the full set of
moves (a three-strike chain and a mastery strike, the heavy and its glint, riposte, slipcut, execution, the Art,
undercut, plunge), its own guard and dodge numbers and its base speed (recovery scales with the item's attack speed
against it, so a vanilla item plays its designed tempo).
- **Axe** (0.9; vanilla's axes): chops on a 3-tick wind-up, a finisher cleave from overhead (motion 2.0, posture 18),
  a hooking mastery strike; the heavy is a guard-breaking hew (posture 24, 34 on the glint); its Art a whirl all round.
- **Maul** (0.7; the mace): slow heavy swings (wind-up 4), the finisher a slam all round (arc 360, posture 26), the
  heavy an overhead crash all round (posture 30, 44 on the glint), a plunge that hits harder (motion 1.3); its Art the
  Earthbreaker's wave. Its blows land blunt (`arms.hit_blunt`) on every body but a spirit.
- **Spear** (1.1; our forged spears; vanilla's spears and the trident keep their own right mouse, the charge and the
  throw, until the style can share it): thrusts at 4.2 blocks on a 25° arc, the finisher a wide sweep, the heavy a
  lunge to 5 blocks; its Art a thrust whose wave runs 12 blocks.
- **Greatblade** (1.0): wide heavy cleaves (arc 130, reach 3.4), a spinning finisher all round, an overhead mastery
  strike; its Art a great sweep.
- **Rapier** (1.8): quick thrusts at 3.6 on a 20° arc, a slash finisher; a riposte of motion 3.4 and posture 24 with
  a 16-tick window, the deflect window 5 ticks: the parry weapon.
- **Daggers** (2.2): a four-strike chain (two cuts, a stab, a wide finisher) and a fifth stab with mastery; the
  shortest dodge (5 ticks, 2.2 blocks, recharging in 16) and a Slipcut of 2.8 with an 8-tick window; a blow from
  behind (the striker more than 120° round from where the body faces) lands ×1.8.
- **Katana** (1.5): a sweeping chain from the draw; the first strike after the blade has rested 2 s (40 ticks since
  the last move ended) is drawn from the sheath: ×1.7 motion, ×1.8 posture. The deflect window 5 ticks. Its first
  strike winds up 3 ticks and recovers 5 (1 and 7 as first built: Euan 2026-10-26, "it starts off low, and then all of a
  sudden he's already to the right side"; the cut from the right now reads before it lands, the move as long as
  before). Every style's first strike was checked: each slash winds up 2 ticks or more; only the thrusts and jabs
  (Rapier, Daggers, Gauntlets), short in travel, keep 1.
- **Twinblades** (2.0, a double-ended blade): a fast four-strike chain on tight rhythm windows closing on a spin all
  round, a fifth spinning back with mastery; its Art a whirl. Its first strike winds up 2 ticks and recovers 3 (1 and 4
  as first built: a wide slash in one tick was a blur).
- **Glaive** (1.0): sweeping arcs of 160° at 3.8 for crowds, a finisher all round, a thrust with mastery.
- **Scythe** (0.9): wide reaps (150°) that rise and fall, a finisher reaping down across; a spirit struck ×1.6 (it
  cuts the Veil's spirits).
- **Gauntlets** (2.4): fist strings (a four-punch chain on 1-tick wind-ups, an uppercut finisher, a fifth with mastery),
  a dodge of 5 ticks recharging in 18; a riposte that throws the body (knockback 1.3).
- **Chain-blade** (1.3): lashes at 5 blocks, a thrust to 6, the heavy to 6.5; each blow landed reels the body up to 2
  blocks in.
- **Shieldblade** (1.4): block-first, the guard taking 85% (70% of a HEAVY), 150° wide, broken for only 10 ticks; the
  second strike and the heavy a shove with the shield that throws its target back; the riposte a stab from behind the shield that
  throws (1.0).
- **War-staff** (1.2): sweeping two-handed blows; each blow landed gives back 3 power energy (`Powers.restoreEnergy`),
  so a staff fighter's powers come round faster.
- **Precursor Arm** (1.5, Tech): an energy blade whose reach grows half a block with each step of the chain (2.6 to 3.6
  by the finisher), the heavy at 4; its Art a wave to 14 blocks.
- Style traits (`Archetype.Traits`, optional per style in the table): `backstab`, `drawIdle`, `drawMotion`,
  `drawPosture`, `spirit`, `pull`, `energy`, `reachPerStep`, `riposteThrow` (`ArmsRules.behind`, `ArmsRules.drawn`;
  the server applies the rest as the blow lands; a Lord, 150 health and up, is neither reeled in nor thrown; test
  `arms_style_traits`).
- Third person: `arms_<style>_<move>` clips on each style's own ticks, generated from the authored poses by the move's
  kind (a side cut, an overhead, a thrust, a sweep round), heavier styles leaning and sinking further; the slide's,
  the fall's and the dodge's strikes are every style's. Strike 1's follow-through passes out in front (a waypoint) so
  the arm never crosses the chest, and finishes out past the off side so the blow reads from behind.

**Sounds** (`ArmsSounds`, 26 events `arms.*`, 76 files; tools/art/specs/audio_arms.py).
- Hybrid by design: CC0 recordings (Kenney's Impact Sounds and RPG Audio, `tools/art/sources/kenney`, CC0 1.0, licence
  files kept) for the physical transients and bodies synthesis renders thin; the audio kit for the air, the steel's ring
  (inharmonic modes), the weight, the shimmer, the rooms and the tells' language. Every event is layered (transient,
  body, tail, sweetener) and has 2–5 seeded variants.
- Loudness category `arms` in audio_mix.py: −14 dBFS gated RMS ±3, true peak ≤ −1 (vanilla's own strong attacks sit at
  −11..−14 and its shield block near −9.5: at AWAKEN's general −20 a blade would sound weaker than a wooden sword).
  Every render is checked: loudness and true peak after encoding, a blow's transient in its first 6 ms (it meets the
  hit-stop's frame), no click at either end, no 2–5 kHz harshness past its family's, variants spectrally distinct. The
  checks catch a broken sound, not a dull one: the listening page (`tools/art/arms_listen.py` →
  `docs/combat/listening-<date>.html`: nine scenes at the game's own timing, read from the table, and every sound
  alone, each with keep / remake / cut) and Euan's ear are the last gate.
- Which sound a blow makes is chosen in one place for both sides: the swish by the move's `swish`, a semitone higher
  per rhythm step; the impact by what the blade meets (`core.api.BodyMaterial`, §12: flesh, armour, bone, wood, stone,
  spirit, slime; flesh lands heavy from motion 1.4: the finishers, a heavy, a riposte; a heavy on a hard body plays a
  little lower); an Execution is a blow of its own. The fighter hears their own client's copy on the frame it happens;
  everyone else the server's (`playSound` excluding the fighter). Vanilla's attack sounds are silenced while an Arms hit
  resolves. Deflect, block, guard break, break, perfect dodge, dodge, the heavy's draw and its glint each have theirs.
- **Tells by eye** (S3, `ArmsTells`, from the synced tell, `Strikes.tell`): LIGHT, a white glint on the striking
  hand 5 ticks before it lands (the deflect window is 4: a tick to see it, then the press); HEAVY, an amber flare and
  ring as the wind-up starts, then the hand burning amber, brighter as it nears; PERILOUS, a big red flare at the hand
  that keeps its red, the hand glowing, and a red rune ring flat on the ground under the creature for the whole wind-up,
  tightening from its reach to the body's own width as the blow nears (over the head, the first plan, it hid behind
  the name plate); GRAB the same in violet. The striking hand is ahead of the body
  at its reach, toward its main arm. On the effects engine with the new `FxPool.NEAR` (drawn even inside 1.5 blocks of
  the eye, where every other sprite fades: a blow is told at sword's length; the fighter's own first-person motes use
  it too), `FxClient.tellMark`.
- **Tells by ear**: each class has one voice on every creature (`Arms.tellSound`: light a bright rising tick, heavy an
  amber swell, perilous a two-tone shriek nothing else makes, grab a creak of reaching): the mobs module plays it with
  every told blow; a NONE ability keeps the mob's own wind-up (`mobs.telegraph`).
- **Hurt**: a blow of any class landing on a player plays a blunt body thump to that player only (`arms.hurt`, no
  voice), with the shard and a small view jolt from where it came (vanilla's own tilt stays).

**Weapons** (`ArmsItems` from the generated `ArmsData`; tools/art/specs/arms_weapons.py, its catalog the source).
- The six forged Longswords, one per Hunter tier (Wildhide, Beastbound, Gatewrought, Veilwoven, Lordscale, Sovereign):
  the tier's Hunter blade plus half a point of damage (4.5 to 9.5 over the player's 1), its uses, rarity and
  enchantability, the Longsword's speed (−2.4), mended by the tier's repair tag. Each fights with its row's style
  (`Arms.plainStyle` reads the row before the name rules), is in `#minecraft:swords` (vanilla's sword enchantments)
  and lights its swings in its tier's colour (the row's `trail`).
- Until the Forge's blueprints (S7), each is crafted from its tier's Hunter blade between the tier's core and bind
  (a column: core, blade, bind); the recipe unlocks when the blade is held, like every AWAKEN recipe.
- **Built to Euan's reference** (`/Volumes/MEDIA/arms-ref/weapon-style-ref.webp`, a Minecraft-Dungeons-style hero
  with a great hammer; the look bar for every Arms weapon). Two passes came before it: plain JSON cubes ("still very,
  very blocky... push it to the maximum") and lofted sculpted meshes at 4 texels a unit (2835ede4: "too thin and
  noisy against his reference"). Now (2026-10-26, `tools/art/voxel.py`): **designed box construction at the player's
  own density**, 1 texel = 1 item unit (a skin pixel), each face its own chart, buried texels dropped and visible ones
  merged; the style rules every archetype follows are in `docs/combat/weapon-style.md` (density, construction from
  bold parts and whole-angle turned boxes never staircases, a longsword about 36 texels with seven tenths blade,
  painted bevels as one-texel bands lit toward the painted light and dark away with contact shadows at joins, three
  or four hue-shifted ramps with one dark and one warm, a few deliberate marks per part and no per-texel noise,
  stones in 45° frames standing proud with concentric painted faces, emissive by flow hilt to tip). Each weapon still
  writes the same `.mesh` (`WeaponMesh`: item-space corners with normal, uv and how far along the weapon each lies;
  the points that glow; then, under header flag 1, the streams of light that lift off it), 244–510 triangles (budget
  6,000, `ArmsTests.MESH_BUDGET`); `check()` repeats `arms_assets` and fails on two faces sharing a plane on different
  texel grids (they z-fight). Review: `python3 tools/art/specs/arms_weapons.py sheet OUT.png` puts the reference beside
  every weapon in three-quarter, back, hilt close-up, first person at rest and in vanilla's hold, night and the icon
  (`docs/combat/weapons-voxel-2026-10-26.png`).
- **The weapon polish pass** (Euan 2026-11-10: "some of the blades to me look a bit fat... the Maul is really, really
  good... the Katana is decent, but I think can still be slightly improved... I don't want to completely scrap
  everything"; plan docs/weapon-polish/PLAN.md, page https://claude.ai/artifact/EZkCwbGng9aNhA6rB4t6rC, approved
  "This is great go ahead with the full plan"). The cause: the look was built from a hammer, so every blade had a
  hammer's body, a post 3 wide and 3 deep down a blade 5 wide, and since the swords stand edge ahead (9 Nov) the eye
  looks straight at it. A first answer, blades ground to a slanted bevel and a smooth point, he turned down: "it
  doesn't feel like MC at all anymore... it has to stay that voxel style. Just extremely well polished voxel style."
  **So weapons are boxes at whole-texel sizes and the whole-angle turned boxes they already had, nothing else, ever.**
  Inside that: every straight blade 4 or wider takes the Rapier's cut (a slab one texel thick with a ridge one texel
  wide, three on the Greatblades; `blade()`), points step finer and longer and end one texel square (`point()`), the
  Katana is one texel thick on an even curve with its point stepped up to the back, the Glaive and Scythe are a thin
  flat with a back three deep along the spine (`curved()`), the tusk and talon Daggers and the tusk Twinblades lose a
  texel of depth, and the Shieldblade's sword is the Longsword's width with its lit fuller as its ridge. 63 of the 111
  change (docs/weapon-polish/changed.json: 57 forged, 6 Lord-forged); the Maul, War-staff, Precursor Arm, Gauntlets,
  Rapier, Axes and the Chainblades' tusk hooks do not. No weapon's length, grip, width, edge side, hold or swing
  changed (each end within half a texel), so nothing was re-solved. The build was checked corner for corner against
  the drafts he approved (docs/weapon-polish/fingerprint.py).
- **The weapon audit** (Euan 2026-11-02, of the Longsword in first person: "not long enough... it almost looks like a
  small dagger... the two blocky things at the bottom look very, very chunky, and you can barely see the blade
  itself"; the hammer "perfect right now"): every weapon measured and graded against the Maul (session weapon-designs,
  concept page with the grades and rules per style). The Longsword was the proof: at 28 texels it was shorter than
  every other bladed style but the Daggers (Rapier 33, Katana 37, Greatblade 40; the Maul 36 to 43), its guard
  ornaments climbed 5 to 8 texels up an 18-texel blade, its hilt parts were 7 to 9 deep against the blade's 3, and
  the hold shows a blade by its edge (roll 90), so in first person the hilt read as blocks beside a sliver. Now all
  six are about 36 texels, the blade 25 of it (y 5 to 30), the grip 5 (y -2 to 3), the guard at most 11 across (wings
  and crowns 14) with its ornaments out to the sides and about 4 up the blade (never beside its root), and nothing
  on the hilt deeper than 5 (a stone and its frame 6); each tier keeps its materials, story and motifs. The hold is
  turned an eighth further about the blade (roll 90 to 135, decision 2 of the audit): at 90 the guard showed its end
  on (the "blocky things"); at 135 the blade shows its face and the guard spreads across, the edge still down and
  forward toward the foe (37 degrees off the cut, was 20). The Longsword's swings are baked again from the new hold
  (`anim_lab.py bake`, the third-person wrists kept); in the lab every blow leads with the edge as well or better
  (0.85 to 0.98, was 0.71 to 0.98). In the game it reads better (CI tour `arms-longsword-turn`: the blade's face and
  the guard's spread at rest, every blow with the hand on the grip), so the Greatblade has the same turn (batch 1;
  every blow 0.79 to 0.99, was 0.72 to 1.00), the Katana and Glaive too (batch 2; the Katana's blows unchanged at
  0.96 to 1.00, its curve now showing at rest; the Glaive's 0.91 to 0.98, was 0.89 to 0.98), and the Axe (batch 3;
  every blow 0.73 to 0.96, was 0.63 to 0.90; at rest the bit shows, where at 90 only its eye did), each checked in
  the lab first (the Daggers and Scythe are dagger-scythe's).
- **Proportions per style** (the audit's rules; Euan 2026-11-02 approved the whole plan, "Go ahead with the whole
  plan"; each line lands with its batch, in texels): every style keeps the hilt off the blade's root, nothing near the
  hand deeper than the working part, one framed stone as the focus, and no two weapons with one outline.
  - Longsword: about 36, the blade 25, the guard at most 11 (wings 14), at most 5 deep (a stone 6).
  - Daggers: about 18, a blade about 11 (y 3 to 14 over a 4 grip); the curved Beastbound and Veilwoven stay about 16,
    their curve carrying the length. The Hive Regent's Sting is already 21 with a 13 sting, so it stays.
  - Greatblade: about 43, the blade 26 (y 8 to 34, six tenths), 9 to 11 wide; the grip 8 (y -5 to 3), the guard
    (y 3 to 5) and the ricasso (y 5 to 8) at most 6 tall together, the guard at most 15 across (today 9 to 13), its
    ornaments out to the sides and at most about 2 up the blade, nothing on the hilt deeper than 6 (a stone 7). The
    tusk's hook, the fork's tines and the window's crystal are the blade's own outline, not ornament.
  - Twinblades: about 40, two blades of 15 (y 5 to 20 each way) on one grip of 8 (y -4 to 4); at each blade's root
    only a slim collar (at most 7 across, 1 or 2 tall), and one hub at the grip's middle round the stone; nothing
    deeper than 6 (a stone 7). The Sky Leviathan's Fins: each fin 15, its rays two short ones off the root (were
    three long ones along it).
  - Precursor Arm: about 35, the light 24 (y 7 to 31) in its three stages, over the cased hilt (y -4 to 7); nothing on
    the case deeper than 6 (a stone 7; Beastbound's gear and Veilwoven's lens were 8 and 9, the lens now 6 across).
    Unit Zero's Countdown: its light 25 (y 9 to 34), the countdown emitter a texel shorter.
  - Scythe: about 38, the snath y -13 to 21 with the blade off its top; the blade a crescent of six or seven turned
    links, 5 broad and 3 deep at the heel stepping to a point 1 wide (was 3 broad and 2 deep, so in hand it read as
    a cane), each tier its own sweep and its own mark along the back (flakes, teeth, a brass spine, a mirror
    crescent, gold ribs, a beard); the collar 3 across and 4 deep; the second hand's peg stays at y 5 to 9. The
    Sporemother's Reaping is built the same, its gill blade 6 broad with gill ridges standing off both faces.
  - War-staff: about 37, the staff y -12 to 17 and the head above it as deep as it is wide (9 to 15 across, was 5
    and flat): four arms of turned links round a stone 4 across (E antler beams, D tusks curling over it, B mirror
    crescents, A gold claws between its wings, S arms before and behind its gold diamond) or C's brass cube, so the
    head reads from the edge as well as the face. The Root Saint's Reliquary: its shrine 7 across on a gold plinth
    under a stepped roof 9 across, pillared and open at the front (was 5 and 7).
  - Axe: about 34 (was 28 to 33), the haft 3 to 6 longer above the grip so the head sits a quarter to a third of
    the height up its top (`lengthened`); the bit and eye 12 or more across (Wildhide's flint 12, was 8; Gatewrought's
    bit 10 from a 5-wide eye, was 7 from a 7-wide one; Veilwoven's spirit edge 2 taller; Lordscale's bit a column
    broader and two steps lighter than its haft, which it melted into); nothing at the eye deeper than 6 (a stone 7;
    Sovereign's frame was 9). The Ember Tyrant's Cleft stays as it is (31, its bit 22 across).
  - Spear: the head 7 or more wide (Wildhide's, Lordscale's and Sovereign's were 5 and Veilwoven's 6, so edge-on in
    hand the head vanished into the shaft): Wildhide's leaf with antler lugs both sides (was a barb on one), Veilwoven's
    wave 7, Lordscale's leaf 7 under smaller wings, Sovereign's spire 7 over a gold frame 6 with its stone. Beastbound's
    and Gatewrought's were already 7 and 9.
  - Gauntlets: the fist kept (7 across, 5 deep, a cuff and rim), and each tier's own outline standing 2 or more proud of
    it (all six were one box with a stone): E antler spikes off the knuckles (to 4 out) and tines curving back off the
    cuff, D boar tusks rising off the fist's sides and curving forward past the knuckles, C a gate on the back of the
    hand (slate posts and a tie, a brass lintel 9 across, the crystal inside) and lit pylons off the cuff, B mirror
    crescents sweeping back off the knuckles to spirit tips, A gold claws off the knuckles and a gold wing off each
    side of the cuff over the ember seam, S a crown of gold points, the stone 3 across in a raised gold diamond and
    ivory plates stacked down the cuff. The Gearwright's Grip: its gear a dark wheel with eight brass teeth past the
    fist's sides and over the knuckles round a brass hub and the furnace core, and two exhaust stacks along the cuff's
    back past its rim, their mouths lit.
  - Chainblade: about 35 (32 to 34), the head 12 or 13 long and 7 or 8 across (was 8 or 9 long and 4 to 6, lost at
    the chain's end), on a chain of ten links (was twelve) in the same S, face-on and edge-on in turn: E a broad flint
    leaf, D a great tusk hook with a horn barb on its back, C a gate-steel dart with its circuit and brass flights, B a
    Veil sickle tipped in spirit light, A a molten-edged arrowhead barbed in gold, S a straight ivory blade with its
    runes over a gold crown. The Lantern Broker's Due: its hooked blade 4 across at the cage and about 12 long (was 2 and 7),
    the three lanterns on turned links.
- **Hilt cuts** (the generated `ArmsHilts.CUTS`, for the War Anvil, §46.3): for each sword-like weapon (Longsword,
  Greatblade, Rapier, Daggers, Katana), where its blade, guard and grip begin along its mesh, {blade, guard, grip, 0}
  in the mesh's own along (0 the pommel's end, 1 the point): the blade's lowest corner (its back, teeth and ricasso
  with it), the grip's top and the grip's foot. A design without a blade or a grip part has none; the anvil then
  keeps its own fallback.
- **Drawn by our shader** (`arms_weapon` pipeline; `WeaponRenderer`, the `awaken:weapon` special item model): vanilla's
  two item lights partly banded (painted light, not plastic), metals reflecting a soft studio (a cool sky, a warm
  floor, a strip light), a gloss highlight, a rim of the weapon's accent, the world's light on all but what glows; a
  sheen runs hilt to tip every five seconds; emissive parts pulse in order along their flow (runes light in turn up the
  blade, the circuit climbs, the molten edge runs to the point, the spirit edge flows); an enchantment is our own
  violet shimmer. Optional pipelines: if a shader pack or driver can't build them, the same mesh draws with vanilla's
  entity light. The stones carry a soft halo (additive, facing the eye, its falloff in the vertex colours) that
  breathes slowly and feeds the Lens bloom.
- **Light that lifts off it** (S2, `WeaponMotes`; the mesh's streams, below): Lordscale's molten edges shed embers
  that rise, slow and cool from white-hot through its gold to a dull red; the Veilwoven's spirit edge lets go of wisps
  that swell, curl and fade; motes hang round the Sovereign's stones and drift up off its burning rune channel (and
  round the Veilwoven's heart stone). The lower tiers shed nothing: the light is a reward of the high ones. Each stream
  lets particles go at its rate, two and a half times more at a full charge, from points along its line through the
  very transform the weapon is drawn with, into the shared effects engine (`FxClient.weaponMote`: its pool, budget and
  particle setting; our own EMBER, WISP and MOTE sprites), so a swing leaves them hanging behind the blade. In first
  person a point on screen is carried out to where the world's own field of view puts it (the hands draw at 70°).
  Nothing while a screen is open or the game is paused.
- **It carries the fight**: the fighter's own blade fills with its accent's light as a heavy charges, flares on the
  glint and on a perfect heavy, and hums while the Resonance is full (the Art ready); its halos swell with it.
- **First person**: a hold of its own (`<id>_in_hand.json`, which draws nothing itself; scale 0.5 for the voxel
  blades, whose points ran off the top at the lofted ones' 0.6): the whole blade standing at the right with its point
  in view, its flat turned a little to the eye (vanilla's sword sits so close a longsword
  shows a fragment); the swings move the hand as for any sword. Third person: vanilla's handheld hold. Size: a fifth
  longer than vanilla's sword (`SCALE` 0.9 of sword units).
- **Inventory icon** (32×32; `items/<id>.json` selects on the display context like the trident: the icon in the
  inventory, on the ground, in frames and on shelves): rendered from the same mesh, painted clean (no dither or
  grain), each pixel the surface's colour at its centre, the silhouette by coverage, vanilla's dark outline.
- Checked before writing (each weapon: budget, inside the item box, atlas fits, icon present); `arms_assets` reads
  every mesh with the game's reader (budget, bounds, whole normals, texels in the albedo half), the items, recipes,
  files and that the hands route to the weapon renderer. tools/art/mesh_render.py renders any weapon with the shader's
  own terms (turntables, close-ups, and first person with vanilla's exact hand transforms and 70° projection, which
  matches the game frame); tools/autopilot/arms-weapons.txt is the in-game tour.

**The combat sim** (S3, `tools/sim/combat_sim.py`, report `docs/combat/sim-2026-10-26.md`): every Lord at its home
rank against four profiles (Tank, Dodger, Parrier, Expert) and a diamond-sword Parrier at D, the numbers parsed from
the sources at start (timing table, bestiary, scaling), seeded. It found three bugs, fixed: every blow lands as the
class it was told as (a bolt carries its ability's class, our fangs are HEAVY, hazard and aura pulses PERILOUS,
through `Strikes.installClassifier` and `Strikes.deliver`; before, Force bolts landed as NONE and could not be
answered at all); an answered blow (deflected, evaded, blocked whole) brings none of its burn or effects; a broken
stance starts no ability until it stands. Tuning for the whole game's pacing (Lord damage by rank, Lord health,
fliers in reach, vanilla's flat burn and fang, per-Lord health) is recommended there and waits for Euan's three-Lord
session (PLAN §6.4 S3 gate): it moves powers players' fights too.

**Weaves** (S8, `ArmsWeaves`; `core.api.WeaveHooks`, §12: the powers module asks it for a cast's energy and tells it
of each landed cast): for 12 ticks after an opening the blade earned (a deflect, a perfect dodge, a Break, a finisher in
full rhythm) a power cast fuses with the weapon and costs 30% less. Four openings × nine families = 36 Weaves, each
named (the deflect's Ripostes: Iron, Gale, Weighted, Ember, Umbral, Mirror, Bulwark, Arc, Soul; the dodge's echoes:
Quake Step, Slipstream, Falling Star, Flashpoint, Afterimage, Phantom Step, Glass Wake, Ghost Circuit, Wisp Echo; the
Break's: Sundering, Whirlwind Break, Collapse, Meltdown, Eclipse, Shattered Will, Keystone, Overload, Severance; the
rhythm's edges: Hammer Rhythm, Tempest Edge, Heavy Hand, Burning Edge, Night Edge, Thought Edge, Mason's Edge, Charged
Edge, Spirit Edge). The opening is the shape: a deflect bursts a 4-block ring off the meeting of the blades (the
fighter's attack ×1.2, knocking back); a perfect dodge leaves an echo where the dodge began that strikes 6 ticks later
(3 blocks); a Break sends the power through the broken body (×1.6, at most 3% of a Lord's health) and holds the Break
a second longer; a rhythm finisher charges the next three blows within 5 s with 40% more as the power's force. All
scale a little with the power's level (+8% a level). The family is the element (the power's own Force, else the
family's: Energy and Tech Charge, Flight and Architect Gravity, Shadow, Mind and Spirit Spirit) and the look (the
effects engine's style of the family). The first time each is woven the System names it ("WEAVE · Ember Riposte", a
toast); after that the action bar does. Kept in `awaken:arms_memory` (schemaVersion 2, saved, kept through death; the
Codex's Weaves page counts it as N / ??, never naming the rest). Test `arms_weave`.

**Lord-forged** (S7, `LordForged`, hand-written beside the generated ArmsData rows): one weapon for each Gate Lord, in
the style that fits it, a step above the forged weapon of its home rank (that weapon's damage + 1, its speed, rarity
EPIC; it only drops, never crafts). A Lord killed by a player (the death event; a decoy's role is NONE, so a reflection
gives nothing) gives its weapon 35% of the time, and certainly on the third Lord in a row without one (the Power Cores'
pity; the count, `lordsWithout`, is in `awaken:arms_memory`, schemaVersion 2). The reveal comes on the next server
tick, after the kill is tallied (so a kill with an empty hand still counts as unarmed): a pillar, a ring and a nova of
the Lord's family light round the fighter, the totem and beacon sounds, the System's toast "LORD-FORGED · <name>", and
the weapon in the main hand if it is empty (else the inventory, else at the feet). Its Art is the style's own and then,
on the Art's first active tick, the Lord's signature move: a shape on the effects engine in the family's look, the
Lord's Force, a reach, ×power of the fighter's attack, what it leaves, and a pull in or a throw out (never on a body of
150+ health, and a Lord takes at most 5% of its health from one). The fifteen (home rank, style, Art): Bell Warden (E,
Maul, Grand Peal: a 9-block Spirit ring that slows), Mother of Spores (E, Scythe, Spore Rain: poison), Ember Tyrant (E,
Axe, Eruption: a Heat slam that burns and throws), Hive Regent (E, Daggers, Royal Dive: a poisoning cone), Root Saint (E,
War-staff, Root Lance: a Gravity ring that roots), Drowned Archivist (D, Spear, Tidal Page: a blinding cone that washes
them back), Gearwright Colossus (D, Gauntlets, Piston Slam: a Charge slam that staggers), Glass Serpent (D, Rapier, Glass
Storm: weakness), Lantern Broker (D, Chain-blade, Last Light: a Heat nova that burns and reels in), Abbot of Frost (C,
Glaive, Glacial Vow: a Frost nova, deep slow), Mirror Knight (C, Shieldblade, Reflections: a Spirit ring that marks),
Unit Zero (C, Precursor Arm, Zero Point: a Gravity vortex pulling in), Sleeper (C, Katana, Waking: a Spirit ring that
all but stops them), Sky Leviathan (B, Twinblades, Storm Eye: a Charge nova that lifts them), Hollow Herald (A,
Greatblade, Event Horizon: a Gravity vortex, darkness, the strongest pull). Test `arms_lord_forged`.
Each Lord-forged weapon also carries one Mark of its Lord (Bell Warden Rebuke, Mother of Spores Feast, Ember Tyrant
Chain Reaction, Hive Regent Windrunner, Root Saint Steady Breath, Drowned Archivist Echo Return, Gearwright Colossus
Earthsplitter, Glass Serpent Counterspark, Lantern Broker Harvest, Abbot of Frost Parry Ward, Mirror Knight Mercy, Unit
Zero Overcharge, Sleeper Phantom Cut, Sky Leviathan Crescendo, Hollow Herald Sunder).

**Mastery** (S7, `ArmsMastery`): five steps for each style, from the kills made with it (20, 60, 150, 350, 800; a kill
of a foe with the style in the main hand; kept in `awaken:arms_memory` `kills`, schemaVersion 3). Each adds to the same
presses: I the chain's mastery strike (the style's `masteryChain`, the 4th or the 5th: a press from 2 ticks after the
finisher's blow until its recovery ends chains on, a chain in full rhythm staying in it, so that strike can be a
full-rhythm finisher too), II a Slipcut window 3 ticks longer, III a charged deflect (posture to the attacker and the
deflect's Resonance ×1.5), IV every Resonance gain ×1.2, V the Art at 80 Resonance instead of 100. A new step is named
by the System ("MASTERY · Longsword II · a longer Slipcut"); the steps go to the client (`arms_mastery` payload, by
style index) for the prediction of I, II and V, and show under a weapon's name. Dev: `/awaken arms mastery <style>
<kills>`. Test `arms_mastery` (and `arms_timeline`'s mastered finisher).

**Marks** (S7, `Marks`): 48, every trigger with every effect, in `data/awaken/arms/marks.json` (written by
tools/arms/marks.py; read once on both sides, like the styles). Triggers: a landed hit, a finisher in full rhythm, a
deflect, a perfect dodge, a Break, a kill, a blow guarded (blocked, not deflected), a perfect heavy. Effects: a rider (×
the fighter's attack as a second blow of the weapon's attuned Force, else the Mark's own, else plain; on a Lord at most 2%
of its health), posture (points; a Break's: the Break held longer), a heal (share of max health), power energy, Speed I
or Resistance I (ticks). A kill's rider and posture go to the foes within 4 blocks. A weapon carries at most two, with
its attunement, in the item component `awaken:arms` (`Marks.Instance`, schemaVersion 1, saved and synced, moves with the
item). Until the named weapons (S9), an Elite a player kills drops a forged weapon of its rank (the content level's) in a
style at random 4% of the time (a Warden 10%), glowing, with one Mark (a second 20% of the time), and the System names
it ("MARKED · Gatewrought Glaive · Rebuke"). Tooltips list each Mark and what it does. Dev: `/awaken arms mark <id>`.
Test `arms_marks`.

**The Forge** (S7, `ArmsForge`): sneak and use Hearth's Forge (any placed `awaken:forge`; a plain use stays Hearth's
tempering and upgrades). Holding one of our weapons: attune it to a Force named by the catalyst in the off hand (since
W2, §28.3: Sunshard Heat, Frostspar Frost, a Fault Seam Gravity, a Copper Ingot Charge, a Deepglass Shard Spirit) for 6
essence, a Core Shard and the catalyst; re-attuning replaces it. An attuned weapon's Mark riders take its Force, and it primes both
ways: a landed hit makes the next power within 3 s cost 15% less (with a Weave's 30%: ×0.7×0.85), and a landed power of
its Force makes the next blow within 3 s land ×1.25 with the Force's touch (Heat burns 3 s, Frost slows, Charge 6
posture, Gravity lifts, Spirit heals 1.5). With an empty hand: the Blueprints, one design each use in turn, each for 4
paper, a lapis (ink, since W2) and an essence shard. Every style but the Longsword needs its Blueprint at the crafting table: the
Blueprint sits in a free cell of the style's own shape (tools/art/specs/arms_weapons.py `blueprint_pattern`; `python3
tools/art/specs/arms_weapons.py recipes` rewrites only the recipes) and comes back out of the grid. Blueprint art: the
style's Wildhide silhouette in white line on blueprint paper (tools/arms/blueprints.py). Dev: `/awaken arms attune
<force>`. Test `arms_forge`.

**Item level** (PLAN §7.7, decided by the sim): a weapon's level is its tier. The forged Longswords' damage climbs by
tier (4.5 to 9.5) and melee already rises with the player's strength, so on-level melee keeps pace with a Lord's
health; scaling weapons by level as powers scale (sim `--item-level on`) broke the ordinary fight (normal creatures fell
in 1–2 hits from D up) and let a Tank win at C and A. No extra level is carried.

**Tests** (`arms_`): timeline, defence rules, strike arc, damage stack, deflect, deflect latency, dodge, posture break,
kill switch, sounds, stance rules, clips, the Art, the Plunge, assets; `mobs_held_weapon_damage`, `mobs_told_melee`, `mobs_ability_classes`, `mobs_body_materials`;
`audio_events_resolve` covers the kit's files and subtitles. S2/S3: `arms_hand_pose` (the swing on Hands' view layer),
`arms_assets` (the streams), `mobs_bolt_class`, `mobs_answered_no_burn`, `mobs_broken_idle`.

**Arms progression: where weapons come from** (plan docs/arms-progression/PLAN.md, approval page https://claude.ai/artifact/DA4J66cpZkKinGbm6X18ML; Euan
2026-10-27: "go ahead with everything else that's recommended", his changes folded in; built in seven commits on
`pack/arms-progression`). The rule: **the gates give the pattern, the world gives the materials**; a pattern is never in a plain chest.
- **Data**: `data/awaken/arms/style_homes.json` (schemaVersion 1; read on both sides by `ArmsHomes`): each style's gate theme and
  rank, its master Lord, an early teacher, Hale's rack price by rank (E 4, D 6, C 8, B 10, A 12, S 12 essence), the village smith's
  price (E 6, D 10, C 16, B 24, A 32 emeralds), the level bands (E 1-9, D 10-24, C 25-44, B 45-69, A 70-99, S 100+; one function,
  `ArmsHomes.rankOfLevel`, to change if the regions plan moves them), the boss-weapon rates and the Marked rates.
  `data/awaken/arms/sources.json` is written by `tools/arms/sources.py` from the recipes and creature loot tables (`--check` for CI);
  a hand-written line (`awaken.source.<ns>.<item>`) covers what a creature table can't say.
- **State**: attachment `awaken:arms_progress` (`ArmsProgress`, schemaVersion 1, kept through death, per player): styles known, the issue
  taken, the shard no-drought count, the weapon and Marked pity counters, the tracked weapon, the gates (last 64), people and
  Pattern Stands that have already taught this fighter. Cross-module calls go through `core.api.ArmsApi` (hooks installed by `ArmsIssue`).
- **B, the first hour**: Hale's issue (pick Daggers, Axe or Maul on a card screen; the finished Wildhide weapon, its Blueprint and a spare
  Fang; once), Ilse hands it over at the camp if Hale was missed, the Now line at priority 70; Moth Lights pays 2 shards and Marta's Wheel 1;
  the first-shard card; **shard pity**: the 5th awakened kill in a row with no shard drops one (per player).
- **C, the Armoury** (`ArmsArmoury`): one list, three doors (Hale's rack by sneaking and talking to him, a Forge with an empty hand, the
  band's K > Powers > THE ARMOURY): styles you know and the ones your rank opens at Hale's rack, six tier cards with have/need and where each
  need comes from, buy a pattern with essence, draw a copy of one you know at the Forge (the random cycle is gone), **Track** one weapon on
  the task card and the Now line (priority 52).
- **D, the gates teach** (`ArmsPatterns`): on a main gate's first floor the first elite (else the third creature) is the **bearer**: it
  wields the gate's style weapon with a faint glint, and its death gives every fighter near it the Blueprint straight into the pack
  (never the Satchel), once per gate per player; the Lord's hoard is the fallback. A style you know gives an unknown style of the same
  rank, a whole rank known gives essence. A riftborn camp's heart is a bearer. Six people teach early at the end of their jobs. The gate
  card names the pattern ("The first floor carries a pattern: Daggers"); it does **not** show a Lord's weapon (Euan).
- **E, boss weapons, rarer the cooler they are** (`ArmsSpoils`, `LordForged`, `MarkedDrops`, `ArmsRaise`): each fighter in a Lord's hoard rolls
  Spoils (a Marked weapon of the Lord's style at the gate's tier, two distinct Marks) at E 60%, D 45%, C 30%, B 22%, A 15%, S 40%, with a
  pity (the sixth Lord without any weapon is certain); a Lord-forged weapon replaces the Spoils (unchanged, pity 3). The Lord wields its
  Lord-forged weapon, glinting. Guardians 30%, Sovereigns 40%, named beasts 15%. `tools/sim/gear_sim.py`: Lords per weapon E 1.3, D 1.5, C 1.7,
  B 1.8, A 1.9, S 2.4. Marked: elite 4%, Warden 10%, camp heart 10%, certain on the 25th, the first from a Warden or heart certain.
  **Raise** at a Forge: a Marked weapon becomes the next tier's (Marks, name and attunement kept; the next tier's parts spent; level gate);
  a Lord-forged weapon keeps its body and gains +1 damage per raise (`awaken_raised`). The Armoury lists FINDS; JEI has Boss drops.
- **F, tiers announced** (`ArmsTiers`): the next tier's lock says what it waits for, the ones beyond only after you hold one of their parts
  (then "What waits" files it, `Promises`); at the tier's level a toast names the job; **a part job per tier from D up is first on Hale's
  board** (`bounty/part_job_*.json`, `featured` and `keep`: Hale looks at the part and hands it back; done once). Oren's rank lines point at the forge.
- **G, villages and stands** (`ArmsStands`, `PatternStandBlock`): the village smith's rack sells two patterns of its land's rank (the region
  level at the village) for emeralds, never one you know, standing in the price (`VillageService.talk`, `ArmsApi.villagePatterns`); a Hearth
  forge stands beside every village anvil as an Armoury door (`VillagePainter`). The **Pattern Stand** (`awaken:pattern_stand`; makes rack,
  lectern, plinth, bier; emissive Blueprint-white line; the tier's weapon turns above it) holds one pattern drawn from its rank's band by the
  structure's seed; taken once per fighter (the stand's position is the claim id); a style you know pays its rack price in essence; a fighter
  within 7 blocks who hasn't taken it gets the find cue. Placed through `ArmsApi.placeStand` by Precursor vaults (the door's rank), monoliths,
  ocean labs, sky platforms and spire crowns (`RuinBuilder.Sink.stand`), hero-tree crowns (`HeroCrowns.rig`) and surface lairs
  (`LairBuilder.Sink.stand`). A stand placed with no rank (`""`) takes its land's rank on the server thread when someone first comes near,
  because the region map must not be read during world generation.
- **Tests** (`arms_`): `arms_sources`, `arms_recipe_unlock`, `arms_issue`, `arms_shard_pity`, `arms_rack`, `arms_armoury`, `arms_gate_pattern`,
  `arms_homes`, `arms_boss_weapon`, `arms_marked_pity`, `arms_raise`, `arms_tier_cards`, `arms_stand`, `arms_village_patterns`.
- **Hale's rack** (physical): two Pattern Stands of the rack make (style `hale`) stand three blocks from Hale, turned to face him, hanging the five Wildhide weapons (three hooks each); using one with an empty hand opens his first-weapon pick while it waits, else his Armoury, like speaking to him while sneaking. `Scenes.haleRack` asks `ArmsApi.placeHaleRack` once Hale is in the world and a player is near; it finds an existing rack after a restart and adds none.
- **Not built / unverified**: stands in camps' hollow dens (a camp is cleared and
  repainted, so a stand would vanish with it; the heart's bearer pays instead); the camp-name caption for the bearer; every client screen
  and the stand's look and turning weapon, because the client was never launched (a tour is the next check); retrofitting stands into
  structures already generated in an existing world.
