## 26. How AWAKEN tells you things (the notification director, discovery, the rift; Euan's playtest 2026-10-26)

Euan, at level 3 in a forest: a lair rumour, "Something tore open nearby" and a "New creature" toast whose hint named a
plant arrived seconds apart; he hadn't looked at anything, barely heard the rift and could hardly see it. The audit
(26.6) found ~400 Signal call sites, a dozen client HUD channels that ignore each other, and no global pace at all.
The rules below replace that.

### 26.1 Principles
- **World first, HUD second.** A happening announces itself in the world first: sound with distance and direction,
  light, motion. Text is the last resort. A rift's word follows its tear by 2.5 s (`AnomalyDirector.WORD_AFTER = 50`).
- **One director.** Every System message that isn't a decision, and every module's own HUD line that wants the
  player's eye, goes through the Signal client's `Herald` (pure pacing logic in `signal.ui.Pace`, GameTested).
- **Discovery is earned and understood.** Intent, never proximity alone; the first find teaches; the rest are quiet.
- **Nothing is lost.** What isn't shown is filed in the Journal (K), and finds stay in the Codex for good.

### 26.2 Tiers, pace and context (`core.api.Notices`, `SignalWindow.tier/topic/moment`)
- **CRITICAL** bypasses everything: a decision (any window with an action), a WARNING kind, a GATE panel, a dangerous
  region's caption, a level-up pane, an Ascent gift scene (those two claim the moment so what follows waits its gap).
- **IMPORTANT** (the default for everything else) is paced. **AMBIENT** never interrupts at Standard: filed with a cue.
- A **moment** (`Builder.moment()`): a first of its kind, a wonder, the first rift. Shown as the centre banner
  (`signal.client.Moment`: spaced label = the window's footer, a line of light, the name ×1.8, ≤2 lines; ~5 s +6 ticks a
  word, at most +6 s; sound `awaken:ui.moment`), at 20% of the screen height; shows at every density.
- **Pace** (ticks; density `notifications` in `awaken-client.toml`, `AwakenConfig.Client.NOTIFICATIONS`):

  | density | gap | calm gap | burst / window | ordinary waits | moment waits | IMPORTANT | AMBIENT |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | MINIMAL | 600 | 900 | 1 / 2400 | 600 | 3600 | filed | filed |
  | STANDARD (default) | 160 | 280 | 3 / 1800 | 900 | 3600 | shown | filed |
  | GUIDED | 80 | 120 | 5 / 1200 | 1200 | 3600 | shown | shown |

  Calm = no fight for 60 s. Waiting messages of the same `topic` merge into one toast ("Mossback · +2"). A message that
  waited past its wait is filed, not shown late. Moments go first, then the higher tier, then the oldest.
- **Held** (nothing paced shows): any screen open, a fight (hurt in 5 s or a hostile within 8), `UiHooks.focus > 0.2`,
  a choice card or info panel up, a moment up, a scene holding (`Notices.client().hold`, the Ascent gift scene), not yet
  awakened, or the world's first 5 minutes (`Herald.SETTLE`; onboarding speaks through story lines and its own HUD).
- **Responses and runs stay live.** An *untagged* message (IMPORTANT, no topic, not a moment: most of the ~400 call
  sites) that arrives within 60 ticks of the player's own click (attack/use/pick, or a click in a screen) answers it and
  shows at once; inside a gate run the server raises untagged messages to CRITICAL (`Signal.send/toast`). The pace is
  for what arrives unasked.
- **Look and place per tier:** CRITICAL = the choice/warning card or panel (right slot) and the warning sound;
  IMPORTANT = the System toast, top right, chime; moment = the centre banner; AMBIENT = the find cue (below).
- **Client lines through the director:** `Notices.client().claim(tier, topic)` before showing (true counts as shown);
  `file(...)` what can't wait. The region caption claims IMPORTANT (CRITICAL when dangerous), waits up to 200 ticks,
  then files "Entered · <name>"; the dangerous region's toast is IMPORTANT, topic `danger`.
- **Fleeting** (`Builder.fleeting()`, 2026-10-26): shown now or never. A fleeting message that waits past its wait is
  dropped, not filed: the System's first contact ("[ERROR] … candidate found.", the opening's and the prologue's), which
  in the Journal read as a real bug. The awakening's first moves ("Your body remembers") are no longer a toast at all:
  the checklist teaches them (§27.10). The Signal's quips (`signal_line/lines.json`, `story.Beats.lineOnce`: "That's your
  first power. Try it out once you're outside the city.") are fleeting too: a reaction read later in a list, out of its
  moment, meant nothing ("There it is."). Nothing is filed for the city's own region while you're inside its walls
  (§27.6).

### 26.3 Discovery (`signal.Finds`)
- **Intent.** A creature is studied when the crosshair rests on it (its angular size + 3°) for 3 looks in a row, 5
  ticks apart (~0.5 s), within 24 blocks (48 for a named beast), in line of sight; or when it is hit or touched
  (`AttackEntityEvent`, `EntityInteract`). Proximity alone never counts, except something big in plain view: a named
  beast or a creature ≥2.5 blocks tall, within 16 blocks and within 60° of the view (`Sightings`). Biomes and
  happenings are big and in plain view: standing in one, witnessing one counts (but they never carry the lesson).
  Lairs (reach the den), landmarks and gates (reach them) are found by going there. **Through the binoculars** (§39.10),
  holding the glass on a creature, lair, landmark, gate or wonder you haven't found for 2 s finds it from afar.
- **Telling** (`Finds.tell(player, Find)` after `Progression.discover` returned true):
  1. the first find ever made on purpose (`intent`) is the **lesson**: a moment with the name, its hint, and "A
     discovery. You studied something new: it pays a little XP, and what you learned is kept in your Journal and Codex
     (K). Look closely at what you meet." (counter `awaken:finds_taught`);
  2. a **big** one (a named beast; later wonders) is a moment with its own label;
  3. the **first of each kind** (`awaken:finds/<kind>`: creature, biome, happening, lair, landmark, gate) is an
     IMPORTANT toast ending "kept in your Journal (K)";
  4. **every later one** is AMBIENT: filed with the cue.
- **A find made on purpose shows the moment it's made** (Euan, 2026-10-29: a glimmerfish's card came 5-10 s after
  he studied it). An `intent` find (looked at, touched, gone to) answers what the player just did, so `Finds` marks its
  window `immediate` (`SignalWindow.Builder.immediate()`, codec key `immediate`, default false): the lesson, a big
  moment and the first-of-kind toast skip `Pace`'s gap and burst limit and go first in line. They still wait while
  nothing can show (`Herald.blocked`: a screen, a fight, a scene's hold, a card or moment already up, not awakened),
  and still expire after `maxWait`/`momentWait`. A new world's `SETTLE` (its first 5 minutes) does not hold them: a
  creature studied in those minutes shows; ordinary messages stay held. The density still decides whether a find shows
  at all (MINIMAL files the first-of-kind toast as before). Finds without intent (a biome stood in, a happening
  witnessed) stay paced; later finds are filed with the cue at once, as before. Test `notice_find_shows_at_once`.
- **The find cue** (`signal.client.FindCue`): a small diamond blooms 13 px right of the crosshair with the name in a
  whisper beside it (5 + 34 + 16 ticks), and `awaken:ui.find` at 0.32 (at most every 60 ticks); several at once read
  "N finds · Journal".
- **The Journal** (`signal.client.Journal`, the band's Status page right under the stats, and its Journal page, §30): filed lines newest first ("◆" unread), 60 kept per
  session, "JOURNAL · N NEW" until the K screen has shown them. The Codex keeps the finds themselves.
- A lair rumour ("Heard of · …") is AMBIENT, topic `lair` (the Now tracker points at it).

### 26.3b The city is not a discovery (Euan, 2026-10-26)
Carillon is where you start, not something you find: inside its walls (`CityHooks.inCity`, the wall included) nothing
counts as a discovery. One rule, `Finds.counts(player)`, checked by every source before it records anything, so the
first find outside is still a first:
- **Biomes** (`BiomeDiscovery`): no first steps inside; the remembered biome is dropped there, so the first step past
  the wall into the same biome is the discovery (the Commons' caption is the moment).
- **Creatures** (`Sightings`): the city's animals and citizens are never studied, by look or by touch.
- **Landmarks and gates** (`LandmarkWatch`): the city's own gate and places are not landmarks found.
- **Happenings** (`Pulse`): one seen from inside the walls isn't witnessed; stepping out while it runs still is.
- **Anomalies** (`AnomalyDirector.discovered`).
What the city keeps, because the city needs it: the Registry's band and licence, the first power, the city's own places
on the Atlas (its discovery and bells), the opening's story lines and revelations, Carillon's quests and requests, region
captions (a place name is not an achievement). Ores and lodes are found by mining, not by standing there, and stay.
The K menu in a fresh world, by this rule (checked 2026-10-26): Journal and Codex creatures empty until the first step
outside; Almanac empty; Truths none (they wait for level 5, `LevelRoad` flag `awaken:truths`); "Your body remembers"
never plays in a fresh world (old worlds only, from rank B); Records (time awake) and Recent messages (the opening's
own words) stay. Test `notice_city_discovers_nothing`.

### 26.3c Readable notices and saved recent events (Euan, 2026-10-28)
Euan asked what combat notices such as "Severance" mean, for a brief explanation immediately, and for a way to
read the detail later in the existing Journal rather than adding an important keybind.

- A meaningful event shows its plain name/category and one short functional summary, followed by **Press K to read
  more in your Journal** (the player's bound Status key; "this and 2 more" when a burst merged several; unbound, it
  says to set a Status key in Controls). It uses the current
  compact toast style, two-toast budget and burst coalescing. No new key, automatic combat modal or damage-tick
  feed. Both System and Classic mode tick these saved-event toasts. Remapped-key hints wrap rather than hiding
  the binding. The owning module supplies the semantics; Signal never guesses a mechanic from a rendered string.
- The existing Journal merges a server-saved **RECENT EVENTS** list with its ambient session log. The Status
  preview links to the Journal even with only a few entries. Recent events sit near the top of the Journal and
  remain visible under every filter. Expand an entry (**Read more**) for what it does and how to use it, its permanent/temporary/
  discovery/reward/task label, conditions and relevant durations. The existing scroll/Show all controls apply.
  Merely viewing the short Status preview does not acknowledge the saved history; viewing Journal and closing
  the screen acknowledges up to the shown sequence. Ordinary ambient discoveries still use the session diary
  and their existing durable Codex records; this is not another encyclopedia.
- `signal.NoticeHistory` stores immutable per-player attachment `notice_history`, **schemaVersion 1**, newest
  **120** semantic entries (at most 4096 UTF-8 bytes each). Each has a monotonic sequence, overworld game time and bounded Event. Equal repeat
  deliveries produce neither a new record nor a toast; changed same-id facts replace the old record and become
  unread. Independent reward occurrences retain separate ids. The attachment copies through death and saves
  through relog; absent data starts empty without fabricating past rewards. Login/respawn sends a bounded quiet
  snapshot, new events send a single-entry delta, and a client's read acknowledgement is clamped to its own
  current server sequence. Clients cannot add events, award rewards or read another player's history.
- Adapters cover learned/upgraded/swapped powers and power mastery; weapon-style mastery; elemental reactions; all 36 weapon/power
  weaves; learned crafting patterns, first essence guidance, Hale's weapon, dropped Marks, gate spoils,
  Lord-forged weapons and Forge attunement; levels and level-road unlocks; available/fulfilled Truths, titles,
  latents, rank and Path results; directive/regimen progress/completion; and taken/advanced/completed Living
  quest chains, bounty acceptance/readiness/payment, and completed teaching steps. Generic `RewardHooks.apply` grants are saved quietly alongside their originating event, with
  exact item/stat/XP wording and no claim that merely applying a Reward activates its perk list. Titles are equipped and Truths declared on the existing Truths page; the Journal explains the event. Title perks
  require equipping; fulfilled Truth and latent perks do not. Existing choice/ceremony flows keep their controls.
- Power events (learned, levelled, variant changed) are kept quietly (`remember`): their own window or ladder moment
  already shows them (§5, §36.6). An expanded entry's button reads "Read more" / "Show less".
- **Severance** is BREAK × SPIRIT, a temporary combat weave. Cast within **12 ticks / 0.6 s** after a posture
  break: the triggering power costs **30% less**; the still-living broken target must remain within **16 blocks**.
  The extra strike is attack damage × `(1 + 0.08 × power level)` × **1.6**, capped at **3% max health** on targets
  with at least 150 max health, and extends an existing break **20 ticks / 1 s**. It does not add an equipped
  power. Repeating a known weave does not spam identical records. An old save that already knew it receives the
  explanation on its next use. The other openings explain their actual burst, delayed echo or three-hit window.
- **Wording, read aloud (Euan's rule, 2026-10-28).** Every adapter's summary and details are plain speech, short, the
  way a person would say them, with each entry's facts kept and no lists of numbers. A detail never repeats the
  summary (the Journal shows both). Rewards are said through `progression.RewardWords`, shared with the Status
  screen's reward cards: a share of a level in words ("a tenth of a level's worth of XP"), a stat by its name
  ("+1 Strength"), perks as phrases with their caps said briefly ("power cooldowns 10% shorter (up to half off in
  all)"), joined with "and"; a reward with nothing to count is "just the recognition". Marks are said whole in the
  Journal (`Marks.say`: "When you land a hit, the target takes an extra 20% of your attack as Heat damage."); the
  item tooltip keeps the short form (`Marks.describe`). A power's levelled entry says its numbers in one sentence
  (`PowerPreviews.numberSentence`); the Power Core hover keeps its before → after lines. A directive says how many
  days are left, not a day number. The last drill of the day is filed quietly, since the day's reward toast tells
  it. The Journal's kind labels read Lasting change, Short combat effect, Discovery, Reward, Task. Test
  `progression_reward_words`.
- Validation: saved history/codec/sync/read-bound/per-player/bounded-retention lifecycle; actual Severance damage,
  break extension, opening expiry and repeated-proc dedup; real core consumption/owned-variant handling and
  barrier strength/lifetime/cooldown parity; healing/passive/cooldown/boss caps and bounded round-trip previews
  for every catalogued variant/upgrade. Headless evidence does not establish in-game visual fit or responsiveness.

### 26.4 "Nearby" alerts and the rift
- Anomaly words are IMPORTANT, topic `nearby` (merged, paced, never several at once), sent 50 ticks after the anomaly's
  own cue, and dropped if it ended meanwhile. The first rift a player meets is a moment ("Something tore open", label
  "Rift", what it is and how to close it).
- **The tear's sound:** `anomaly.rift_open` is our own `sfx_rift_tear` (tools/art/specs/audio_discovery.py: air pulled
  in, a falling rip with crackle, a sub boom 62→27 Hz, glass splinters, a crackling tail; mono), a fixed-range event
  heard to 128 blocks with linear falloff (`attenuation_distance` 128). Before: vanilla respawn-anchor sounds that a
  variable-range event at volume 3 sent only within 48 blocks of a tear that opens 32–96 away.
- **While open:** the near crackle bed (40 blocks, as before), a new far bed `amb.rift_rumble` (`amb_rift_rumble`,
  started within 72 blocks, attenuation 72), the hum, and a hush of birds and insects within 40 blocks to 20%
  (`Soundscape.hush`, renewed every 40 ticks).
- **The look** (`world.anomaly.client.RiftGlow`; the CityGlow way: one additive lightning-blend pass, depth-tested, no
  depth written, Lens-friendly; replaces the 0.8 × 3.6 textured quad and the vanilla portal particles): a jagged crack
  7 blocks tall (16 nodes whose edges crawl) in three ribbons (violet glow ×2.8, magenta body, white core ×0.3), four
  flickering side cracks, a halo of radius 6.5, a violet pool of radius 11 on the ground, a faint column 56 blocks into
  the sky (so it reads against the sky from 60 blocks by day), 28 motes spiralling in, the core at its foot. It opens
  over 30 ticks with a flash and a ring running out along the ground, flares when struck, folds as it closes. Drawn to
  160 blocks.

### 26.5 Tests
`notice_pace_gap_and_burst`, `notice_critical_bypasses_queue`, `notice_ambient_files_to_journal` (signal),
`notice_discovery_needs_intent` (fauna: beside the crosshair is never a find, a glance isn't, a rest is; the first find
teaches), `notice_city_discovers_nothing` (wilds: walking the city finds no biome; one step past the wall, it does). `fauna_sighting_discovery` studies for `Sightings.DWELL` looks.

### 26.6 The audit (2026-10-26) and what is still outside the director
Routed: every Signal toast/panel/window (server tier tags: anomalies, creatures, biomes, happenings, lairs, landmarks,
gates, crafts, the danger toast; the rest default IMPORTANT/CRITICAL by kind), the region caption, the level pane, the
Ascent gift scene. What Euan saw: reaching level 3 (and a first sighting) queues lair rumours for every family met
(`Lairs.onLevel`) → a toast "Heard of · <lair>"; a rift opened (toast at once, sound to 48 blocks only); a creature
in the 60° cone at 24 blocks counted as a sighting and its toast's hint named plants ("Plants mushrooms", "Crops it
hovers over grow"). Not yet routed (follow-ups): the vanilla action bar (102 server call sites, three throttled), boss
chat lines, the XP pop, Ascent notes and the Vow scene, citizens' speech; TipHooks has no implementation (the onboarding
spec's `TipHud`/`TipRules` were never built), so Carillon's and the Ascent's tips show nothing today.

## 27. The Way Forward (progression and guidance; plan docs/progression/PLAN.md, page https://claude.ai/artifact/RjzQ2SNdst8vbXPrZrvx1P; Euan approved all of it 2026-10-26)

Euan, in survival: "I just got out of the city, I go into the forest, and I'm like, okay, so what's next?" The rules: every
lock is seen before it opens and names what it waits for (a rank, a level, a rung by its in-world name), never how to
play it; the world remembers the locks you met and calls you back once when you hold the key; three goals at all times
(Now, Next, Far); the world pulls first and the HUD confirms. Builds on §26 (the notification director) where it lands.

### 27.1 Promises (`core.api.Promises`, `progression.PromiseKeeper`, `PromiseBook`)
- **The book** (attachment `awaken:promises`, schema 1, saved, kept through death, synced to its owner): at most 64
  entries `{key, dim, where?, need kind, need value, what, answeredAt}`; the oldest go. A key is one per place
  (`door:x,y,z`, `landmark:ruin:x,z`, `wing_core:x,y,z`, `stratum:n`, `region:id`, `halo`, `possession`).
- **`seen(player, key, where, need, what)`**: recorded once, only for an awakened player who doesn't already meet the
  need. Silent, except the first lock a player ever meets: one NOTICE toast "Saved for later · <what>: you'll need
  <need> first. Your band (K) keeps a list of things like this, and you'll get a reminder when you're ready." (flag
  `awaken:promise_taught`). The band's list is **SAVED FOR LATER**, each row "<what> · needs <need>" ("· ready now" once
  answered); the call back says "<what> is open to you now". (Until 2026-10-26 it was "What waits · The Commons waits
  for level 4", which Euan couldn't read; plain words now, §27.6.)
- **Needs**: `rank:<label>` and `level:<n>` answered by progression; `tier:<tether|leaper|wings|skyborn>` answered by the
  Ascent (`Promises.addAnswer`). Words: "D-rank", "level 20", "the Tether".
- **The call back**: on a rank-up, a level reached or a rung granted, every waiting lock the player now meets is
  answered. The nearest one with a place in this dimension leads one NOTICE toast "Ready now · <line> · 640 m NE" (+
  "and N more in your band (K)"), and for 10 minutes (`RAISED_FOR`) the Horizon line raises it over everything near
  (a raised site, same line). `markNewThing("promise_answered")`.
- **The line says what it is, and where** (Euan 2026-10-27: "the Sky Vale · answers you … here, but there's nothing
  here"): an answered lock reads `PromiseKeeper.ready` in plain words, "<What> is open to you now" ("A sealed vault is
  open to you now"), and for a land (`region:`) "<The Sky Vale> is no longer too dangerous for you"; never "answers you".
  A region's place is only where the player first met its danger, on its edge, so with the player standing in that land
  (`PromiseKeeper.inside`) the lock is off the Now line, the Horizon and the toast's compass: nothing to walk to.
  Every way to a place counts height (`signal.NowWay`, one place for the Now line's arrow, the band and the toast):
  **"here" only within 4 blocks across and 6 up or down**; straight over or under you it says "60 m above you" / "below
  you"; elsewhere "↗ 58 m · 30 above" (the height past 8, rounded to 5). Test: `progression_lock_line`.
- **`kept` / `keptAll(prefix)`**: a rank door opened (`door:`), a spire's crown climbed (`landmark:ruin:`), Wings from
  a sky core (`wing_core:`).
- **Sources today**: the Tether Vow's stir and every rank door's reading ("A sealed vault" / "A sealed door", the door's
  rank), a Tether Spire or sky platform reached without the rope (`LandmarkWatch.reach`: "A Tether Spire's crown" / "A
  sky platform", need the Tether), a sky core refusing a climber under C ("A sky core's wings"), a sealed Descent stratum
  ("<name>, in the Descent", its rank), the Observatory's Halo line ("Something past the sky", B), Veil possession
  refused ("Wearing a creature, in the Veil", C, no place), a dangerous region ("<region>", the level at which it stops
  being dangerous).
- **In the band** (K › Journal, §30, "WHAT WAITS", order 5, `progression.client.WaitingSection`): up to 8 rows, answered
  first then nearest: a chip with the need in its colour (rank colour; the Horizon's green for a rung) or READY, what,
  and "640 m NE". The same locks are pinned on the Atlas (`MapMarks`), coloured by need.
- **Far** (the next rank's promise): under "Next rank: D at level 10…" in the Spine section, "D-rank opens what waits
  for you: A sealed vault · Gardens, in the Descent." Only locks the player has met; never a list of spoilers.
- Test: `progression_promises`.

### 27.2 The band's Ascent page (`body.client.AscentSection`, K › Powers, §30, order 28)
"Runner · yours from the start"; each rung held with how to use it (keys in the player's own bindings,
`signal.client.KeyText`); the next rung as "◇ The Tether · next" with where it comes from ("A Precursor vault keeps a
line for a hunter it opens to: its door's rank, D at the least."); the rest "???". What a rung does is only told once
it's yours.

### 27.3 The ladder (decisions 1-2; details in §17.7, §17.9, §17.10, §17.19)
Tether at the vault's door rank, D at the least (~5 h, balanced); Leaper at D with Tether mastery 4 (~8-12 h); Wings
at C from a sky core (~20-25 h); Skyborn at A; the Sovereign form with any ending. Wren's Rope (`requires`
`tier:tether`, a new requirement token answered by the Horizon's reach) is no longer offered before the rope, so it
can't block every later found scene. Rungs, Lord-forged weapons and first Weaves now count as new things for the
Director's rhythm.

### 27.4 The Horizon line says why
A landmark's site name carries a few words of why (`LandmarkKind.why`): "Sealed Vault · something waits inside", "The
Well · the way down", "Tether Spire · a crown at the top". The sky's need reads "· needs a rope or wings" (the rig's
rings are a rope ladder), the Tether's "· needs the Tether".

### 27.5 Locks that hold and speak (phase 3)
Built by the locks builder on `pack/locks` (the orchestrator's split, 2026-10-26): climbs refusing the first block and
naming their key, the cache's inner seal, a relog keeping a built visit, the hero trees' canopy wards, the crown and core
by the line, door colours, gate cards comparing ranks, refusals on first contact. It uses `core.api.Promises` (§27.1)
and answers its "Show me" card through `Progression.BAND_ACTION` ("band:ascent", `ProgressionPayloads.OpenBand`).
A first draft of it is on `pack/progression-p3-wip` (48d09e19).

### 27.6 The first thread (phase 1)
- **Registered** (`core.api.OpeningHooks.onRegistered`, fired from `OpeningModule.afterOpening` when the opening ends or
  is skipped): Bram's errand, **The Last Delivery**, starts by itself and is tracked (`living.FirstThread`; once;
  never for a player who has it or did it). At the end of the Registry (its step `LETTERS`, after the Directive) Bram
  says what a hunter is for ("Oh, and one more thing. As a hunter, your job is to protect the city from whatever is out
  in the wilds, beyond the walls.") and where to go first ("Ilse runs a camp for new hunters up the north road. Take
  these letters to her, and she'll explain the rest."; 2026-10-30: between them the bells and the gates, §43.15), and holds out **Letters for Ilse** (`awaken:ilse_letters`, an
  errand item; Bram's prop "letters"), which you take from his hand the way you took the band ("Take the letters").
  A player who skipped the Registry is given them at registration. The steps: take the letters from Bram (done the
  moment they're in your pack; it keeps the old first step's place, so saves hold), out through the High Gate, to the
  Wayfarer camp up the north road, deliver them to Ilse by her fire ("Deliver the letters · 0/1"; she takes them from
  your pack), and take the ember she gives you (the Ember, §28.2). The thread lets go there: its Now line ends once
  Ilse's step is done, and the Hearth's own line ("Place your Ember where you want your home", `hearth:ember`) takes
  over; the chain's last step (a `hearth` objective: done when you have a Hearth) waits in the Journal. Kestrel's
  word-from-the-square opening and return were cut (Euan, 2026-10-26: Bram hands you the letters). After it the player
  chooses: it is one errand, not a chain that keeps leading (BotW's "lines" railroaded 80% of testers). Euan, after
  playing it (2026-10-26): guide them exactly to the Ember, then let them go and explore.
- **Chains on the Now line**: the tracked chain's current step (else the first chain's), priority 68 (over points to
  spend 55 and the next level's unlock 15; under a waiting Reassessment 72, rifts and danger), with a compass to its
  place: a "reach" step's marker; a "talk" step's person (Kestrel: the Roost, `OpeningHooks.place("roost")`; Hale: his
  quartermaster spot; Ilse and Hettie: the camp; a Wayfarer: their scene). Before, tracked chains never reached the HUD.
  Since §27.11 (2026-10-27) the corner shows the step's place from the task card (the quest step's `place`, its
  compass), not this suggestion; the suggestion stays in the band's lists.
- **The camp is findable**: its marker falls back to its nominal spot until someone has come near (the compass knows the
  way); a Horizon site "Wayfarer camp" until the player has stood within 24 of it (counter
  `awaken:camp_reached`); and a signal fire on a bale by Ilse (`Scenes.campFire`), its smoke a column seen from the High
  Gate (vanilla smoke rises only near you, so the client draws its own column to 1000 out, 110 blocks tall to clear the
  Lumen canopy: `LivingNet.CampSmoke`, `PulseFx.campfire`), lit once a player is within 256 and lit again if it's gone; the camp itself is now founded within 256 (it was 112,
  so from the gate there was nothing there yet).
- **The Registry's Directive fits** (`Directives.opening`, reason "opening"): "Clear a floor of any gate.", accepted for
  the player (4 play-days; since §27.13 "Your first job", never fading), "Your first gate will open somewhere outside the city walls." Accepted Directives show on the Now
  line with their progress ("· 50%", priority 58). Before, the Registry's was a random roll offered quietly, its waiting
  line gone in 30 s, and accepted ones never showed outside K.
- **The first gate, on purpose** (`Director.firstGate`, SPEC §21.0.14 finally built): a player's first gate waits until
  level 3 or about half an hour after awakening (36 Director passes), and until they're out of the city (or an hour),
  then forms 250-400 blocks further along the bearing from the city's centre to them (north from its middle; any way
  if that way is sea, a river or a beach), at their own rank, with "A gate has opened 320 m N · clear its floors to get stronger" (IMPORTANT, topic `gate`); the
  Horizon raises it ("First gate · E-rank") until they've cleared a floor. Before, the first gate
  was rolled the moment they awakened, in the infirmary, at random 300-1500 out, unannounced.
- **Out through the walls** is a moment: crossing the city reserve outward shows the region's caption ("THE COMMONS ·
  1-8") once a play-day (the Commons spans the city's edge, so leaving had none). Inside the walls no region caption,
  warning or promise is sent at all, and the Commons, the land everyone starts in, is never a "danger" region (it was:
  a level-1 player read "Danger · The Commons" and "The Commons waits for level 4" in the Journal before leaving the
  city). **The first time out through the High Gate, its shot names the land**: as the view lifts over the gate the
  title "THE COMMONS · THE LAND AROUND THE CITY · CREATURES LEVEL 1 TO 8" (the region at the camp, from the server),
  then the camp's caption ("THE WAYFARER CAMP · UP THE NORTH ROAD · 181 M AWAY · YOUR NEXT STOP"); the region caption
  is skipped that time. A danger region's warning says it plainly: "The creatures here are level 20 to 28. That's well
  above you, so be careful."
- **The High Gate's shot** (`living.FirstScenes.gateShot`, filmed by `living.client.FirstFilm.GateShot` with the
  opening's camera and letterbox through `opening.client.Cinema`): the first time a player goes out through the High
  Gate on the errand (the step "Out through the High Gate" completes), ten seconds, letterboxed, hold jump to skip: a
  breath in your own eyes turning to the smoke, then the view lifts over the gate (the first clear spot of a fan, up to
  15 up and 8 on) and narrows (FOV x0.6) onto the Wayfarers' smoke, which reads stronger while it's filmed; the lower
  bar names it ("THE WAYFARER CAMP · UP THE NORTH ROAD · 330 M AWAY") while Hale says his line; then back down into
  your eyes, left facing the camp. Once a player (counter `awaken:first/gate_shot`). Before the camp is founded the
  smoke rises from its nominal spot at the generator's height. The step's done line is said in the shot, not as a
  story line (`QuestEngine.Stager`: a scene that stages a step's ending takes its lines).
- **Ilse's scene by the fire** (`FirstScenes`, `FirstFilm.IlseShot`): coming within 7 of Ilse with the letters (or
  talking to her) starts it instead of a bare click. Letterboxed, over your shoulder on the side away from the fire, a
  slow push while she talks; her lines one at a time in the Registry's speech (name above, the line under it): she asks
  for the letters (the lower bar: "LETTERS DELIVERED 1/1"), sits you down, says why you'll want a home of your own ("It's
  getting dark, and nights out here are dangerous"), then holds an ember from
  hers out in her hand and brings it over to you (to within about two blocks). The view comes back to your own eyes
  facing her, the HUD stays out of the frame, "Take the ember" with the use key (within 3.6), and your hand takes it from
  hers (the Registry's hand-over, `HandOver`, now for any item): the step ends as your hand closes on
  it, and its reward is the Ember (W1's rules kept: one a player, kept through death, Ilse or Hettie give a lost one
  back). Her last line says plainly what it does ("Once it's placed, you can rest there, and if anything happens to you out
  here, that's where you'll wake up."), the bars lift, and the Now line says "Place your Ember where you want your home"
  (the Hearth's). About 20 s to the coal; hold jump to skip to it; after 30 s with her hand out she
  presses it into yours. Someone with a Hearth or a coal already is told "Looks like you already have a home fire" and the step ends there. Walking
  off (18 blocks) ends it; it starts again when you come back. Nothing hunts or hurts a player while either moment plays
  (target changes cancelled, damage cancelled but for what bypasses invulnerability; the gate's for 14 s).
- **The camp** (`living.wayfarer.Camp`): laid once round its fire when a player is within 96 (`Scenes.campBuilt`, saved,
  optional field): what lies on the ground within 5 cleared (grass, flowers, mushrooms, moss and carpets: anything
  that gives way underfoot), each piece set on the real ground under it, the ground within 3.5 trodden to coarse dirt
  and path; two
  **Wayfarer's Bedrolls** (`awaken:wayfarer_bedroll`, our own block on `AbstractBedBlock`, texture from
  `tools/art/specs/camp.py`) feet to the fire, west and south; stripped spruce logs to sit on (north, east); a barrel of
  packs with a lantern, a log of firewood; and the **Camp Pot** (`awaken:camp_pot`) hung by a chain from a bar on two
  A-frames over the fire. Only on open ground: a trunk or a rock where something goes, and it's left out. Neither block
  drops or has an item. **Its ground is safe**: no monster spawns (natural, chunk generation, patrols, reinforcements)
  within 32 of the fire; a monster within 30 stops hunting and is sent back out past the edge (every half second); no
  monster takes a player within 32 as its target. A **bedroll** sleeps the night through like a bed when it's dark (the
  rule `WHEN_DARK`), never sets your spawn (that's the Hearth's), and when a step you're on needs the dark (a quest step's
  `night`, e.g. Moth Lights' "The Lumen Moths only come out at night.") it says "You can't sleep yet. ..." instead. At night
  Hettie lies down on the far bedroll and gets up at dawn; Ilse keeps the fire.
- **Plain words, start to finish** (Euan, 2026-10-26, after playing it: "make it more human-like... not some poetic
  riddle"): every line in the first sequence says plainly what it means, the way a person would say it: the infirmary
  (Sun, Bram), Bram at the Registry and its cards, the ritual's prompts, the System's acceptance, Kestrel, Hale, Ilse,
  Hettie, the clerk, the crier's news of the wilds, the first tips, the Ember's messages and tooltip, and the toasts
  and captions on the way (e.g. Ilse: "Here, take an ember from our fire. Carry it with you, and when you find a spot
  you'd like to live, place it there. That'll be your home."). Lines that grew got time to be read (Bram's briefing:
  28 s, a line every 7; Ilse's beats 90 apart).
- **Control comes back** (Euan, 2026-10-26: "right after the cutscene, you can't move"; he had to /kill). Every scene
  that holds the player still goes through one lock, `core.client.InputLock` (bookkeeping `core.InputHolds`): the camera
  shots, the Registry's waits, Ilse's ember, the ritual. The real input is saved once, by the first holder, and put back
  only when the last lets go; a holder never saves another's stand-in. (Ilse's hand-over saved the camera's empty
  stand-in, the camera then gave the real keys back, and the scene's end put the stand-in back for good.) Every hold has
  a deadline (a shot's own length + 2 s, re-asserted while it plays; Ilse's ember 45 s; a shot of unknown length 2 min):
  past it the lock lets go and logs `[input]`. A respawn's new player object is held in turn and given its own keys; a
  logout lets everything go. Ilse's scene also ends server side on walking off (18 blocks), death, logout or her being
  gone, and her hand empties. Tests: `core_input_holds`, `progression_first_scene_exits`; tour `camp-exit.txt` walks
  away after the scene.
- **Held means held** (Euan, 9 Nov: "cinematics don't stop you so you keep walking forward or even jumping during it").
  While the camera is on anything but the player the game doesn't read the input at all (`LocalPlayer.applyInput`), so
  swapping the input left whatever was held as the view left latched in `xxa`/`zza`/`jumping`. The lock clears those as it
  starts and every tick after (`InputLock.stop`; the player's momentum still runs out on its own). Scenes that take the view
  to a camera of their own all hold through the lock: `OpeningCamera`'s shots (the opening, the High Gate's, Ilse's), the
  Registry's, Ilse's ember from her first line, the ritual, the furnace's lowered view, the Forge Song's and the anvil's,
  each with a deadline of its own. Binoculars, the map and combat cameras are not scenes and take no lock; the map only
  clears the latch (`InputLock.stop`) so you don't walk on behind it. Raw key reads respect the lock (`JetBoots`, a landing's roll).
- **The camp's ground** (Euan, 9 Nov: "Isle appeared in a huge hole in the ground once"). `Scenes.campSite` takes the nearest
  ground to the nominal spot, out to 160, that is dry, level, under open sky, walkable in a straight line from the road's end
  (26 short of the spot) and seen from it, and at the height of the land round it: of 32 looks at 10, 18, 28 and 40 blocks in
  eight directions, at most 8 may stand more than 3 above it or fall more than 5 below (`offLand`). A pit, ravine, basin or
  cave mouth has land above it on most sides. All the land it reads must be finished chunks, which is also why nothing can
  carve it afterwards: a chunk is finished only when its neighbours have been through features, and sinkholes and cave mouths
  are structures built during that. With someone within 64 of the spot and nothing good enough, the dry ground that sits best
  in its land, so Ilse is never missing. A camp founded before this and more than half surrounded by higher land (over 16 of
  the 32) is moved once, the first time someone comes within 64: Ilse and her fire go, the old bedrolls stay in the hole.
- **The far smoke is far only**: the column (`PulseFx.campfire`) fades out within 48 blocks of the fire (gone at 48,
  whole from 96), where vanilla's campfire smoke is the real thing. Drawn up close its puffs, up to 15 blocks across and
  110 up, read as a dark dome over the camp and a pale facet in the sky (Euan, 2026-10-26).
- **Quest fields** (`QuestDef.Step`, schema 1, both optional): `tally` shows a step's count even when it's one ("· 0/1");
  `night` says why a step needs the dark. Objective type `hearth`: done when the player has a Hearth.
- Dev and tours: `/awaken living first gate|letters|ilse|took|camp`; tour `tools/autopilot/first-scenes.txt` (CI).
  `letters` and `ilse` work from a brand-new world (Euan 2026-10-27: "skip the whole start"). An unfinished opening is
  skipped as `/awaken opening skip` does it: registered, Bram's letters, his errand. Then you're taken to the camp, and
  once Ilse is there (up to 30 s, the camp's 5 s tick) the errand jumps to her step and you stand 10 blocks off her
  (`letters`, you hand them over yourself) or 5 with her scene begun (`ilse`).
- Tests: `progression_first_thread`, `progression_now_priorities`, `gates_first_gate_on_purpose`,
  `progression_first_scenes` (the gate's shot once; the letters counted; Ilse's scene to the coal; the Ember; the thread
  letting go), `living_camp_keeps` (laid round its fire; nothing hunts there; a monster sent out; the bedroll's rule; a
  step that needs the night).

### 27.7 Tips, switched on, and the Signal's thread (phase 4)
- **Tips** (docs/carillon/m4/onboarding.md §1, finally built; `TipHooks.install` had no caller, so every tip in the
  game, the Ascent's, the Living Wilds' and the free-run's, showed nothing):
  - Rules (`signal.ui.TipRules`, pure): one tip at a time, the highest priority whose context has held 6 ticks; 80 ticks
    between any two; `cooldown` between showings of one; retired after `retire_after_done` dones or `retire_after_shown`
    showings; the `short` text (just the keys) once it's been done.
  - Client (`signal.client.Tips`, `TipHooks.Client`): data from `assets/awaken/tips/<group>/<name>.json` (reloaded with
    resources), `{key.<mapping>}` in the player's own bindings (`KeyText`), other placeholders dropped; counts per person
    in `config/awaken-tips.json`; shown only when the notification director allows (`Notices.claim(IMPORTANT, "tip")`)
    and never over a screen, while held (`hold(owner)`: the Ascent's scenes) or while the director is quiet. Drawn
    centred above the story line's slot, one line (two at most), in the System's glass; it fades when its context ends,
    at once when done. Client option `tips` (on).
  - Server (`TipHooks.Server` in the signal module): `offer` and `done` are one small payload (`signal_tip`); a server
    offer waits up to 5 minutes for a quiet moment (the director holds tips in a fight, a scene or the world's first
    minutes; those first minutes don't count against the 5, or a tip offered at registration lapses as the world
    settles), then shows for its `show_for`.
  - The first stretch (`assets/awaken/tips/first/`): `band` (registration + 6 s: "K opens your band: what you hold, what
    waits for you, and the way up."; done when K opens), `now` (registration + 26 s: "The top left of your screen shows where you're heading, with an arrow. To go
    somewhere else, open your map with M and click a place.", §27.11), `atlas`
    (the first way out through the walls; done when the Atlas opens), `power` (the first power chosen; done at the first
    cast), `level` (a level-up with points; done when a point is spent: "You grow by finding new things, hunting, and
    clearing gate floors."), `gate` (the first gate placed; done on entering a gate), `night` (the first dusk outside
    the walls, once).
- **The Signal's thread** (`NowClient.thread`): toward the Now line's place, a thread of the Signal's light runs low
  along the ground, 26 blocks in a little over a second (`AscentFxBridge.threadMote`, two motes a tick), once when that
  place is new and once more if the player stands still outdoors for 8 s with it; at most every 2 minutes, never in a
  screen, never within 12 blocks of the place. No key, nothing that stays on screen (Ghost of Tsushima's guiding wind,
  in our blue).

### 27.8 People who point (phase 4)
- **The crier names real places** (`CityEvents.wildsNews`, lines in `tools/city/lines.py` → `citizen_lines.json`
  `news.wilds_*`): the nearest standing gate within 900 of the city ("Hear ye! A gate's light stands past the High Gate,
  to the north!"), else the spawn vault ("…hums again! Its door reads a hunter's rank, they say!"), else the
  Wayfarers' camp. Before, every line in the city was flavour.
- **Kestrel speaks** before you click her (`named.kestrel`: "Runner! You still haven't told me what happened in the square.").
- **"Anything for me?"** (`progression.Advice.next`, after Terraria's Guide): a free Registry clerk you right-click says
  the one next step that fits you: a Reassessment waiting, a lock that is open to you now, points to spend, the Directive
  you've taken, else the next rank and what it opens for you ("D-rank at level 10. It opens a sealed vault for you, and
  more.").
- **A level-1 found scene**: Marta's Wheel (`quest/martas_wheel.json`, band 0, a road scene): eight sticks for her
  wagon, paid in road news (gates' light, vaults' doors, the camp). Found scenes all needed level 8, so a new player
  never saw a flare; now the first one can rise in the first quarter hour.
- **One Journal**: the Living Wilds' chains read "JOURNAL · CHAINS" beside the System's filed finds ("JOURNAL").

### 27.9 The long middle (phase 5)
- **The capability clock** (`Progression.CAPABILITY_AT`, set inside `markNewThing` for things you can *do*: a power
  learned, a rank, a Path, a rung, a Lord-forged weapon, a first Weave, a machine or blueprint, an Echo, a Hearth or its
  tier, a latent, a townsperson; never a sight or a core). After 75 minutes without one, outdoors and out of a gate, the
  Now line offers the nearest one in reach: a lock that is open to you now, with its place (57), else "D-rank opens at
  level 10: gate floors give the most XP" (50).
- **The Reassessment says where**: "Your D-rank trial is ready: take it at the Spire in your town" with a compass to your
  Hearth, or ": craft a Reassessment Monolith and use it" without one.
- **The level road goes on to 135** (it had two steps in levels 51-135): The Precursor Foundry (52), The Halo (55, goal:
  see it from an Observatory), Wings you know (58), The Inverted Sea (62, a core), A-rank trial (70), The open sky (73,
  goal: the Sky Leviathan's trial), Any creature (77), The Dreaming Stratum (80, a core), The Sovereigns (90, goal: one
  falls), S-rank trial (100), The Court opens (105, a core), Half the Court (112, goal: four), An empty court (122, goal:
  eight, a core), The Seed (135).
- **Weapon mastery** is wired by Arms S7 (`ArmsMastery.strikes`); Wilds content past level 20 belongs to Living Wilds
  phase F.
- Test: `progression_capability_clock`.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### 27.10 The current task, top right (Euan's playtest, 2026-10-26)
"Every time you have a goal and things to do, you actually have a small checklist top right." One small card tucked
into the top-right corner (`signal.client.TaskHud`; the Now card's margin, 4 GUI px), in the Now card's glass, at about
half its size (Euan, 2026-10-26, after the first version: "WAY too big, 2x smaller and closer to the corner"): 0.45 of
the System scale, never under two screen pixels a font pixel, widest line 185 px before a step is shortened. Its title
and done/total, then only what matters now, one line each: the current step bright with ▸, the next two dim, and a step
that just ticked (a soft green flash, then it fades out over 2.5 s); a long step is shortened with "…" (the Journal has
the whole of it). Keys are drawn as key caps from "{key}" in the words, a count where a step has one ("0/10"), and a
compass to a hint nearby ("↗ 9 m", the ledge). While the System's toasts are up it eases down under them, and below
a boss bar it would reach (on a narrow screen). Hidden with the HUD. The Now line, top left, keeps the where (§27.11):
a step that sends you somewhere carries its place (`Row.at` and `Row.place`, the name the Now line gives it: null for
the step's own words, "" for a hint nearby, which stays the card's), and its compass is the Now line's, not the card's.
The quest step's optional `place` names it ("High Gate", "Wayfarer camp", "Ilse"); the task payload carries the
dimension it was sent from.
- **The top-right stack** (Euan, 2026-10-27: "let's move the floors to the top right where the current active things
  to do are"): the task card heads it and the gate's run panel (`gates.client.RunHudLayer`, the floor HUD that sat on
  the left at mid-height) sits 3 GUI px under it, or takes the corner itself when there is no task; the same margin,
  look (`HudLook` projected or flat glass, accent red in a Red Gate) and scale (`UiHooks.topRightScale`). The run panel
  steps down under the toasts and below boss bars it would reach (`UiHooks.topRightBelow`; the layer draws after the
  boss overlay, which counts the bars afresh each frame), moves down at once when the task card arrives and eases up
  into the room when it goes. It keeps everything: rank and gate name with the floor beside them ("Deeper · Floor 1/4",
  a ✓ when cleared), Satchel stacks and XP, kills and the floor clock with the pressure word (stirring, awake, Warden),
  the Noise bar under Silence, the collapse countdown and the twist's hint (shortened with "…"); widest line 215 px,
  narrowest card 96. Never dims; hidden with the HUD, under F3 and, like all of Awaken's HUD, while any screen but
  chat is open (§12 `UiHooks`). Its strings are built only when the server's run update changes. Test
  `signal_layout_every_gui_size` (the stack's maths at every GUI size: never over the card, a toast or a boss bar).
The server decides (`progression.Checklist`, sent only when it changes, payload `signal_task`; nothing while the
opening runs):
- **Your body remembers** first, from the awakening: "Hold [Shift] as you land to roll", "Double-tap [Ctrl] to sprint
  harder", "Hold [Shift] while sprinting to slide", "Press [Space] at a ledge to climb it",
  each ticked the first time you do it (the body module's counters `awaken:body_roll`, `_sprint`, `_slide`, `_mantle`);
  the ledge row points at the nearest chest-high ledge within 10 blocks while it's current (every 2 s: a two-block step
  up from standing ground with room on top). All four done: the list stays ticked for 4 s (`awaken:first/moves_done`),
  then goes for good. It replaces the "Your body remembers" toast, which the director filed unread.
- **Then where you stand** (`Checklist.registerHere`): your home's first steps while you're in its land (§28.2, "Your
  home").
- **Then the tracked chain** (`Checklist.register`; the living module's `FirstThread.task`): its title, its steps ticked
  as they're done (at most six: the last done, the current, what follows), a count on a step that has one or a `tally`.
  The first thread reads: Take the letters from Bram, Leave the city through the High Gate, Take the letters to the
  Wayfarer camp up the north road, Deliver the letters 0/1, Place your Ember where you want your home. Before it (it
  registers first) **Your first power** while the choice waits (`powers.Starter.task`): "Press [K] to choose your first
  power" (the Status key, drawn as a key; the cards come back on login, and K opens them instead of Status). After it a
  weapon you track (arms, "Making: …").
- **Last** (`Checklist.registerLast`): what waits until nothing else is on the card: your home's first steps from afar.
- Test: `progression_checklist` (the moves tick one by one, then a first power still to choose, then the errand takes
  the card); `powers_starter_chosen_once_and_equipped` (the first power's card and its key, gone once chosen).

### 27.11 The Now line shows only where you're going (Euan's playtest, 2026-10-27)
"I also don't like how the top left is pulling me in so many directions. This should only appear when a checklist is
active and requires me to go somewhere, or if I choose a destination on the map." (His screen: "◇ E-rank gate · 270 m"
over "△ Sealed Vault · a sealed… ↘ 381 m", two places two ways.)
- **The corner shows at most one place** (`signal.NowCorner`, drawn by `signal.client.TrackerHud`): the destination
  you chose on the Atlas (§16.8), "◆ E-rank gate  ↖ 270 m" in white; else the current task step's place when it sends
  you somewhere (§27.10: a row with a place name), "◇ Wayfarer camp  ↗ 120 m"; else nothing. Its compass counts height
  (§27.1) and only in the place's dimension. A step's place that moves less than 24 blocks (Ilse walking) is the same
  place: no fade, no new thread.
- **Gone from the corner:** what the Now tracker suggests (the nearest gate, the best idea, a lesson, a rift, a request,
  the way home underground) and "N decisions waiting · K" (the K menu's badges count them). The suggestions are still
  collected and synced (`NowSync`): the band's Now section and the Journal's "Anything for me?" list them.
- **The Horizon line** under it is a client setting, off by default (`horizonLineShown`; a new key, so a saved
  `horizonLine = true` doesn't keep it on).
- **The Signal's thread** (§27.7) runs toward the corner's place, not the top suggestion: once when a place is new (a
  destination the moment the map closes, even if a thread ran lately), once more on standing still 8 s with it.
- **Urgent lines** (priority 90+, `NowSync.URGENT`) no longer have the corner: each is said once as a fleeting toast
  when it first comes up (not filed). The opening's own (`opening:` ids) aren't: "The gate is opening · waiting for N
  hunters" is the square's own line (`OpeningHud`), and Bram walks you to the Registry and says so. The others today are
  the ritual hall's ("Go through the doors", "Waiting for N hunters…").
- **What wasn't a place moved to the task card** (Euan, 2026-10-27, on "Use your fire for a guide": "I have NO CLUE what
  that means"): the Hearth's first steps ("Your home", §28.2) and the first power ("Your first power": "Press [K] to
  choose your first power", §27.10), which a player who closed the cards had only the corner to learn from.
- **Plain words** (the same day): every Now suggestion says what to do, what to press or where to go, for someone who
  doesn't know the mod. The K menu's lists show `{key.…}` placeholders in the player's own keys (`KeyText`); a line of 90+
  (a toast) never uses one. Among them: "Press [K] to spend 3 points", "Your D-rank trial is ready: take it at the Spire
  in your town", "D-rank opens at level 10: gate floors give the most XP", "At level 13: …", "Talk to Hale: he has a free
  weapon for you", "Right-click the Rest Shrine to leave with your loot, or the Seal to go deeper", "Floor 3 of 3 · the
  Lord is on this floor", "A Lord got out of a broken gate · 120 m", "Close the rift · 40 m NE", "Open the spirit cache ·
  12 m", "A star fell · 60 m NE", "Right-click the fallen star to open it", "Walk into the shimmer grove · 40 m SW",
  "Hunt the Old Antler · 120 m NE", "Find the lair of the Briar Sow · 1.2 km NE", "Tame the … 20 m N: sneak
  up and feed it …", "Use a Hunter's Bridle on your …", "Your … is 300 m NE: use your Hunter's Whistle to call it",
  "Mire Hide 3/8 for a request at your Anchor" (all in hand: "right-click your Anchor to hand it in" / "take it home to
  your Anchor"), "Go back into the Bell Crypt for floor 2", "You can craft a Wildhide Vest at a crafting table", "You
  have everything for …: make it at a Forge", and the level road's goals ("Defeat all eight Sovereigns", "In a lucid
  dream, hold H at a wall", "Defend your Hearth from a gate break", …, still within the road's 200 px check).
- Tests: `signal_corner_nothing` (no task, a step with no place, the ledge hint: nothing), `signal_corner_task_place`
  (the current step's place, named, in the task's dimension; an unnamed one says its own words),
  `signal_corner_destination_wins`; with §16.8's `signal_destination_arrival` and `signal_destination_saved`.

### 27.12 A done goal never shows (Euan's playtest, 2026-10-30)
"Lampwing was already flying near me and even after taming it, the task still shows to find it top left." "I've already
set my fire but it's still a choice in my tasks." "Overall the task system is broken and shows stuff you've already done.
This needs to be fixed for ALL the game." The rule: whatever is in front of the player as a thing to do goes the moment
it's done, by any route, including one met before the line appeared or one the line didn't expect. A checklist may keep a
done row ticked beside its open ones (the card's tick and fade, a tier's list); nothing done is ever a current step, a
suggestion, a rumour, a lead, a decision waiting or a destination.
- **The top left had the Track** (`KinPage.track`): "Where Lampwings live (roughly)" was a destination, cleared only on
  arriving within 16 blocks, so a Lampwing met or homed anywhere else left it there for good. **A destination now carries
  its goal** (`Destinations.set(p, target, goal)`; saved as `goal` in `signal.Destination.Saved`, an optional field,
  schema 1), and the signal module drops it quietly (no "Destination reached") within a second of its owner saying the
  goal is met (`Destinations.doneWhen`). Goals: `kin/<kind>` (one met anywhere, or one living with you; one that settles
  at your fire is filed as met there and then, `KinHome.settle`, so the goal holds if the home later ends), `kin/<kind>/home`
  (back to where you met one: one living with you), `bell/<n>` (the bell held), `metal/<metal>` (the Delvers' mouth: the
  home no longer short of that metal), `raid/<pos>` (the raid's chest emptied or gone), `stilled/opened:<settlement>` (the
  key's chest opened), `stilled/done:<figure>` (the keepsake shown to its family). A place picked on the Atlas has no goal
  and clears on arrival as before.
- **The first fire's Lampwing has no Track**: its need row says it's by your fire (Track pointed at a wild site instead).
- **Trails**: in a linear trail a step is done once any later step is (`TrailEngine.latch`). Set Your Fire's "Find open,
  level ground" was manual, so after the fire was set from Ilse's coal it never ticked and kept the trail on "What you can
  do now"; it also reads `hearth` now, and The Training Grounds' course reads a lap run. A trail whose every step is done
  when it opens opens quietly (no "A new trail" toast) and finishes at once.
- **Saved for later**: a land answered and then stood in leaves the list (`PromiseKeeper.walkedIn`, every 2 s); a sealed
  stratum is kept on arriving in it (`stratum:<n>`), the Halo on being seen (`halo`), the Veil's creature on wearing one
  (`possession`).
- **Bell Book**: a held bell's lead is never listed. **Tips**: one still waiting for a quiet moment is dropped when you
  do the thing first.
- **The sweep** (`core.api.Shown`): each module registers the lines it shows as things to do: `card` (the task card's
  open rows), `now` (the Now suggestions the band lists), `destination`, `choices` (decisions waiting), `saved` (Saved
  for later), `trails` ("What you can do now"), `hearth` (the Hearth page's needs with rumours, the Kin list's rumours),
  `bells` (the Bell Book's leads). Tests: `trail_done_never_shows` (every source is swept; the fire set as the coal sets
  it finishes Set Your Fire and nothing anywhere still asks for the Ember), `kin_done_never_shows` (a Track is done on
  meeting one anywhere; the lesson Lampwing has no Track; once it lives with you its Track goes by itself and nothing asks
  for a Lampwing). Its test home stands on a real Anchor block: Hearth upkeep drops a record whose Anchor is gone (every
  20 ticks, at an offset from the owner's id), which made the test pass or fail by the mock player's random id.
- **The Hearth guide's green is true** (Euan, the same day: "the door isn't green ... kitchen already has a crafting
  table and furnace green, but that's not even in the kitchen"). A room card ticks only the pieces standing together in
  one closed room, the one holding the most of that kind (`Guide.card`; before, any piece anywhere in the radius lit
  up), and names it (`RoomCard.room`). The door-icon item reads "in a closed room" and is green once the pieces stand in
  one, not only once the kind is built. One room can be several kinds (`Room.types` is a set; a bed, a furnace, a
  crafting table and a barrel make a Bedroom and a Kitchen), so a card whose pieces stand in a room that's already
  another kind says "It stays your Bedroom too" (`RoomCard.roomKind`). The Meditation Mat's recipe line, its guide
  card and its tooltip say where amethyst comes from first: a geode underground (every land has them; the recipe is
  unchanged). Tests: `hearth_guide_one_room` (real blocks: the bedroom's table and stove tick for the Kitchen, a loose
  barrel outside doesn't; a barrel inside makes the room a Kitchen and still a Bedroom), `hearth_guide_matches_roomtype`
  (loose furniture ticks nothing).

### 27.13 One Tasks page, a tab per goal (Euan, 2026-10-30; page docs/tasks/page.html, https://claude.ai/artifact/RbQNkY1tvFB6QKcP2n3NWU)
Euan: "one single tasks tab which contains all the things you can do right now", and his moment: back home with the
Hearthfire set and a bed built, what next? Approved in full with two changes: "The kin should be part of the hearth tab"
(no Beasts tab; kin steps and the kin list, rumours and wants live on the Hearth) and "The armour tab should show a real
preview of each set too". This changes §43.5's "the help is never stated" for the main path: what to do next and where
each piece comes from is said plainly; what the world holds beyond it is still found. Phase 1 as built:
- **The band has six pages:** Status · Tasks · Hearth · Powers · Journal · Map (`StatusSections.Tab`). The Truths page's
  sections stand on Status (the path choice 700, the Truths 710-730, the road 735, titles 740, latents 750:
  `StatusSections.placed`); the Codex's board, the Atlas list, the Almanac and the Bell Book stand on the Journal (600-640;
  phase 3 gives each its category). The holo rail has six nodes (`BandLayout.PAGES` 6); Tasks carries a badge for steps you haven't seen.
- **Goals** (`core.api.Goals`, §12): a module says what a player can do now as `Step`s under one of six goals (Hearth,
  Armour, Weapons, Bells, Gates and rank, Out there), each with its needs (an item, a tag or a condition, have and
  need), a place, a place on the main path, optional or not, choices (the armour sets) and the Now suggestions it
  covers. The main path: start 0, the fire 10, a first room 20, the Armoury 30, the first armour 40, the first gate 50
  (for its Lord's Heart), the Anchor 55, the Forge 60, a War Anvil 62 and the first weapon forged on it 64 (§46.4), the
  trial 70. An optional upgrade (the Sanctuary) is never on top.
- **The book** (`tasks.TaskBook`, cached 10 ticks): every module's steps and every Now suggestion (`tasks.NowMap` maps a
  suggestion to its goal and place on the path by its id: `kin:` and `request:` go to the Hearth) as one list, one row
  per key (two of one key: the one with more needs or choices, the place from either), nothing a goal step covers twice.
  Order: the path, then priority, then key. On top: something urgent (priority 90 and up: the opening, a ritual's
  doors), else the pinned step, else the path's next that isn't optional, else the most pressing of the rest.
- **The page** (`tasks.client.TaskTabs`, `TaskPage`): tabs NOW, HEARTH, ARMOUR, WEAPONS, BELLS, GATES (Q / E; a dot on
  a goal with a step you haven't had in front of you for 1.5 s). Now: "Do this next" in full; "Also open to you", the
  first open step of each goal with how many of its needs are ready and Open ›; "Out there" (suggestions no goal
  claims); "When you want" (optional upgrades). A goal's tab: every step in order, each need with its icon, count, a tick,
  and under a missing one where it comes from (`WhereFrom`: the page's own line `awaken.where.<ns>.<path>` or
  `awaken.where.tag.<path>`, else the Armoury's `awaken.source.*`, else the creatures that drop it with their land, and
  "Some live round here." in their land); a place as "About 310 blocks north-east." **Pin** puts a step on the task card
  (one pin for everything: pinning stops a followed trail). An armour step shows each set as a tile (its four pieces,
  name, role and armour, materials ready, Choose); **See them worn ›** opens `SetPreviewScreen` over the band: a vanilla
  `ClientMannequin` per set wearing its pieces, turning to the cursor; click one to choose it, Esc goes back. The set
  chosen is saved and the card then lists what that set still takes.
- **The task card:** the pinned step leads it (`Checklist.registerLeading`); with nothing else on, the step on top shows
  last when it has needs. Swept with every other place a goal shows (`Shown` source `tasks`, §27.12).
- **Sync:** `tasks_view` (server → client) when it changes, looked at every 20 ticks while the page is open and every 100
  otherwise; `tasks_act` (client → server): PIN, UNPIN, OPEN, CLOSED, SEEN (a goal's ordinal or one step's key), CHOOSE
  ("step|choice"). Saved: attachment `awaken:tasks` (`TaskState`, schema 1: pinned, seen (the last 256), chosen), kept
  through death. `/awaken tasks` lists the page, `/awaken tasks pin <key>`, `/awaken tasks unpin`.
- **The Armoury** (`RoomType.FITTING`, label "Armoury", id `armoury`): a Fitting Stand and a crafting table in one closed
  room, your first workshop, right after a bed (`HearthNow.ORDER`: Shelter, Bedroom, Armoury, then the rest). An anvil,
  the Forge and an armour stand in the same room make it the Forge too (one room, both kinds). `Furniture.FITTING_STAND`
  is appended (saved counts go by ordinal). Its gift: armour finished at a Fitting Stand inside an Armoury lasts a quarter
  longer (`MAX_DAMAGE` × 1.25, `ArmourForge.ARMOURY_WEAR`; the stand asks `HearthHooks.armoury(level, pos)`, §12; the
  tooltip says "Made in your Armoury: it lasts a quarter longer"; `ArmourForge.fromArmoury` reads it off the stack).
- **The Hearth's steps** (`hearth.HearthGoals`): Build your Armoury (its pieces ticked where they stand in one closed room,
  as the guide ticks them); Clear your first gate (at the Hearthfire: the nearest enterable gate within 600 blocks, for
  its Lord's Heart) or, with a Heart in the pack, Set the Lord's Heart on your fire; Grow your Armoury into a Forge;
  Make your Bedroom a Sanctuary (optional); Grow your home to the next tier (its rules, the rank, the price).
- **The Armour's steps** (`armour.ArmourGoals`): until every piece you wear is your rank's, "Choose your first armour"
  (on the path) or "Make your X-rank armour", its choices your rank's known sets with what the pieces you don't own
  still take, summed; once you wear your rank's, when the next comes.
- **The Hearth page** (phase 2, `hearth.client.HomePage`, replacing the old Hearth section): your home at a glance (name,
  tier, the Forge, Comfort as pips, style, town, trophies, "Rooms and upgrades ›" to the guide); NEXT FOR YOUR HOME, the
  Hearth's first step in full with "Everything for your home (N more) ›" to the Tasks page's Hearth tab
  (`tasks.client.HearthNext`); ROOMS, every room kind as a tile in `HearthNow.ORDER`: built (green), started (amber, its
  pieces counted), open, the Sanctuary dashed (optional), and "?" for a kind whose rare piece (a trophy, a machine, a lode
  heart, a vent stone, a perch, a crucible, a drop, a ledger) you've never had at home or in your pack; click a tile for
  its pieces, where each comes from and the closed room it needs; MAKE IT LOOK GOOD, each room (weakest first, up to 8)
  with its grade, kinds, its six readings as pips (the weakest amber) and the one thing that lifts it. Then the kin
  sections as before (your beasts and nooks, the kin list, rumours and wants). Sent in `HearthView` as `tiles` and
  `looks` (optional fields, so an old client's view still reads).
- **The beasts' steps** (`kin.KinGoals`, Hearth goal): the home's first two needs (`KinPage.NEEDS` order) with no beast of
  that kind living there yet, while a nook is free. A kind you've met or heard of is named ("Bring a Burrowbun home", the
  need and where: "You've met one: ..." or the rumour you already have, with its place); one you haven't stays the need
  itself ("Nothing lights your yard at night."). Looking never learns a rumour: it reads `Kinship`, never asks
  `KinSpawner`.
- **The Bells' steps** (`bells.BellGoals`): a step per lead in the Bell Book you don't hold yet, newest first, up to 4
  ("Find the Barrow Bell" once seen or narrowed, else "Find where that bell's note came from"; its last line; its place as
  Track had it), and the tower's next step when it's yours to do (set the frame down at home, clear room for the belfry
  or the stone tower, raise the Great Belfry, ring the Hundred Peal). A tower that only wants more bells adds nothing:
  the leads are that. Reads the Book, never changes it.
- **The beasts' wants** (phase 3): a want you've read by watching a beast three times is a plain Hearth step ("Give the
  Burrowbun what it wants", its third watch line, "Help one three times and it trusts you; then it follows you home"),
  until one of its kind lives with you; the first fire's Lampwing, before you've watched it, is "Watch what's been
  watching your fire". Both under `kin.KinGoals`.
- **Truths come true by themselves** (phase 3, `Progression.truthDue`, `truthsCatchUp`): from level 5 (the road's
  `awaken:truths`), a Truth whose rank has come, whose emergence (if any) has happened and whose deed is done is true,
  its reward unchanged; no offers, no declaring, all 32 can be earned. Lived before level 5 or before its rank, it comes
  true at the flag, the rank-up or the next login, told in one line. Status shows TRUTHS · n OF 32 (yours, green) and
  CLOSEST TO TRUE (the three you're nearest, with what each takes and gives, a bar). The Truths offered toast, the
  Declare and Withdraw buttons and the `declare` / `undeclare` actions are gone; an old save's offered and declared lists
  drop at its next catch-up (the saved fields stay so old saves read). Two Truths counted removed systems and get new
  deeds: "I keep my word." is ten helps to beasts you meet (`awaken:kin_helped` 10, +3% XP in place of the Directive
  slot), "I choose my path." thirty floors past your comfort (`awaken:floors_pushed_past_comfort` 30). The Titles
  Keeper of Promises (seven helps to beasts) and The Regimen, now The Drilled (ten Gauntlet runs), and the hidden
  Wanderer path (25 landmarks reached) move the same way.
- **Directives and the Daily Regimen are gone** (phase 3): no morning offers, no gap offers, no drills; `Regimen.java` is
  deleted and Hardline's Penalty Zone retires with it (a pending one is cleared at login). Only the Registry's own stays,
  "clear the first floor of a gate" (§27.6), taken on at the opening, never fading, paid as before, shown on Now and
  folded into the Hearth's "Clear your first gate" step (`covers("progression:directive/")`). An old save's other
  Directives and its Regimen drop quietly at login (`Directives.retire`). The Journal's DIRECTIVES and DAILY REGIMEN
  sections and the Directive glossary entry go. The pacing sim drops their sixth of a level a day (phase 4).
- **Anchor requests are gone** (phase 3, as JOURNEY part 9 said): none is offered; one waiting is withdrawn; anything
  handed in for an open request comes back to your pack (a tag's first item); Forge credit already earned still pays;
  the Journal's request section goes. Core Shards still drop from C-rank gate floors. Tests:
  `hearth_requests_retired`, the saved state and the shard fusing; the offer tests go with the offers.
- **The Signal Relay** (phase 3): near your Hearth, once a play-day, Listen (its Essence cost unchanged) put the
  nearest sleeping bell within 1,500 blocks you don't hold and haven't heard in your Bell Book as a heard note, one
  bearing from the relay (`BellHooks.relay`, `Bells.relayed`). The +1 Directive slot and `awaken:relay_linked_day` go.
  **Retired the same day by §43.16** (no bell lies in the open, so there's nothing to hear): `Bells.relayed` is false
  like the Chimewrens' and Snufflets' leads, the panel offers no Listen and spends nothing, and says plainly that every
  bell is kept somewhere now. `AboveData.relay_day` stays in the save, unread. The relay has no job left; a new one is
  Euan's call.
- **Trails fold into Tasks** (phase 3, `trails.TrailGoals`): each open trail you haven't finished or hidden gives its next
  step (key `trail/<id>`, optional, its trail and "n of m done" as why, its place) under its area's goal: home → Hearth,
  weapons → Weapons, gates, powers and the body → Gates and rank, the rest Out there. Pin replaces Follow: the trail card
  and its Now line go, and an old save's followed trail becomes the pin if nothing is pinned. The Journal's TRAILS
  section and its All trails browser go; trails still open, tick, hide and finish (with their share of a level) as before.
- **One pin** (`Goals.Pin`, installed by tasks: `pinned`, `pin`, `pinIfFree`): the Bell Book's Track is Pin now (its
  lead's step `bell/<no>` leads the card; a lead found by a letter pins itself only when nothing else is pinned).
- **The Journal is a catalogue** (phase 3, `progression.client.Catalogue`, `JournalFilters`): a tab per category along
  its top with how many you've found (Q / E step through them; they wrap on a narrow band): CREATURES (every overworld
  creature in the bestiary, `CreatureCodex.slots`, found once seen, with its egg), BEASTS (the kin kinds that live in the
  world, found once met; read off the Hearth page's words, `KinPageSection.slots`), LANDS (biomes found, a count),
  PLACES (landmarks, lairs, wonders and secrets found, a count), GATE WORLDS (the Atlas, found / total), CAVE REGIONS
  (`RegionCodex.slots`), BELLS (the Hundred's own board is the slots; the tab counts held / 100), LORE (the Codex board
  without its Creatures and Cave regions, which have their own; found entries counted), HAPPENINGS (the Almanac, a
  count: the kinds are the server's data, so the client can't number them), ORES (the twelve of
  `ProgressionModule.OreXp`, found once mined, with what each is for) and YOUR STORY last (the log, Records, the chains,
  Saved for later, Recent; its tab says "n NEW" while the log has unread lines). A fixed category shows every slot numbered; one not
  found is a "?" with its number and nothing else, never a name, a picture or a hint; click a found one for what you've
  learned. A category with nothing to show yet says in one line what it keeps (`Catalogue.Empty`). The Hundred's board
  shows from the start; a bell you know nothing of hovers as its number only (no name, no rank). A section says its
  category (`Section.shelf()`, YOUR STORY by default); a note link to the Journal opens on
  the linking section's category (`StatusSections.follow`: the Status page's "ALL n ›" opens Your story). The Now list
  leaves the Journal (Tasks has it; Recent's links go to Tasks). Autopilot: `journal <category>`. Not moved: the chains
  and Saved for later stay under Your story rather than on Tasks.
- **Track is Pin on the kin list too** (phase 3): a kind with a step on the Tasks page (`kin/need/<id>` or
  `kin/want/<id>`) pins it; one without falls back to the rough bearing as before. A kin step's place is that rough
  bearing (`KinSpawner.rough`), never the spot. The Armoury's weapon Track stays its own (no weapon steps yet).
- **Pacing** (phase 4, `tools/sim/pacing_sim.py`): without the Regimen and the daily Directives (about a sixth of a level
  a play-day) the balanced player reached level 50 at 62 h and 135 at 115 h (targets 50-60 and 95-105). Gate floors make
  it back: `Curve.WILDS_TRIM` 0.80 → 0.94 (0.90-0.94 keep every target; anomalies and camps priced from a floor follow).
  Now level 10 at 3.8 h, 25 at 17 h, 50 at 57 h, 135 at 101-105 h (the sim varies a few hours run to run); the first
  hour, power mastery and the gate death targets hold.
- **Tests:** `tasks_book_rules` (order, the top rule, covers, merge, NowMap, the saved state), `tasks_choose_and_pin`

  Sanctuary optional; the Hearth page's tiles and looks, the beasts' first need as a step; built, the armour is on top and
