sandstone under flat roofs in the desert, whitewash and blue shutters by the sea. Lower and plainer than the city (one or
two storeys, no jetties or shopfronts), with the same climbing grid. Every house is enterable (panes, real doors of the
land's wood) and **furnished** by `CityInteriors` from who lives there (`SettlementPaint.Interior(adults, children,
trade, seed)`): a bed each (a couple's double, the children's upstairs), a hearth under the chimney, a table and seats,
storage, the trade's blocks (the smith's anvil and blast furnace, the inn's bar, tables and guest beds, the scribe's
lectern and shelves, the miller's sacks), rugs, pots; a real staircase (five steps, the floor cut over it) or a ladder;
at most two lights a house. Generic over plots, for Carillon's B4 to adopt.

**The people** (`VillageRoster` on W0's `RosterBuilder`): a graph from the streets (a node every four blocks, lanes
joined at their branch), a door for every building, places for the work (each field's edge, the pen's gate, the forge,
the well's trough, the bell, the benches, the green's play, the woodlot, the pier's end, the mill, the inn's taproom
inside its door with the guests' floor found by painting the inn alone, the lamps, the Watch's posts and the roads
out). Errands spread over the whole place, never round the well: the board, the benches, the stall (buying), every other
home's door (a visit), the green itself and a corner every sixteen blocks of street. A place holds as many people as it
has spots (past them they'd stand in a heap), so the children's game spreads over twelve spots of the green, the green
holds ten, the stall's front four, the board three. Households of 1-3 adults and 0-3 children per home, 8-16 people in a hamlet, 20-50 in a village. Village jobs
appended to `Roster.JOBS` (21 farmer, 22 shepherd, 23 woodcutter, 24 miner, 25 fisher, 26 hunter, 27 carter, 28 elder,
29 scribe) beside the city's smith, tavernkeeper, miller, washer, lamplighter, bellringer, Watch, healer, stallkeeper
and children. **The day** (0 = 06:00): the bell at dawn and dusk (the ringer at the bell 05:18-06:42 and 17:30-18:36;
it rings six with Minecraft's own bell sound); work 07:00-11:30 and 12:50-17:50 (farmers hoeing, the woodcutter's axe,
the smith at the anvil, the fisher at the pier with his rod, the shepherd leaning on his crook); the midday meal at home;
from half past six half the grown-ups at the inn or on the green till ten; hunters and miners out by the road at dawn and
back at dusk, the hunter with a kill on his pole; the carter's round of the barn, granary, inn and mill with a crate;
the lamplighter's round lighting the lamps at 18:10 and putting them out at 05:00; the Watch at the posts and walking
the edge 17:30-04:50; the elder on a bench and, of an evening, at the inn. Clothes from the city's trades by hash (a
farmer wears a porter's, a fisher a boatman's, a scribe a clerk's). Ledger cost with a village of 38 awake: 0.003-0.005
ms a tick (`village_day`).

**Speech** (`data/awaken/village/village_lines.json`, 729 lines, read by `citizens.Lines` under `village.`): greetings by
job and standing (`village.greet.<job>.<stranger|known|friend|kin>`), calls at work, news of the village and the region,
trade, the board, the inn's offer, room and rumours, the scribe, the elder, the bell, and what people say when struck,
robbed or their fields trampled; `{village}`, `{region}`, `{elder}`, `{gate}` (the compass way to the nearest gate) filled
by the village's `Settlements.Voice`. Talking to a trader opens their goods (`Settlements.Talk`); the elder tells news.

**Trade in emeralds** (decision 5; `Trade`, `Emeralds`): `EconomyHooks` is installed with the emerald (balance,
charge, and pay once per claim id; the claims are kept in `awaken:villages`). Every trade sells what it makes and buys
what it needs (vanilla's merchant screen); every land's villages make something of their own (the frost's furs and
berries, the desert's glass, the mire's slime and clay, the highland's copper, the coast's ink, prismarine and nautilus
shells, honey in the heartland...). The scribe sells three enchanted books a day (the tradeable enchantments, 9-25
emeralds by level), paper, books, maps, name tags. Prices show standing on the screen itself (the old price struck
through): a stranger pays one over on anything of three or more, a friend a fifth under, kin a third under; what a
village buys asks a stranger an eighth more goods and kin a fifth fewer, and is capped a play-day per player (nothing
ever locks for good).

**Standing** (`VillageState`, per settlement and player): points, Known at 10, Friend at 35, Kin at 80; a trade +1
(four a day), a filled notice +4 to +8, a night at the inn +1, two blocks of a house broken -1 (three a day); the
people's own recognition (W0) lifts a stranger to Known. Rising, every one of its people knows you better
(`Settlement.acquaint`) and a line says so.

**The notice board** (`Requests`, `client.NoticeBoardScreen`): right-click the board on the green: a timber board with up
to three pinned notes from the village's real state (damage: timber and stone to mend it; a smithy: iron; the inn:
bread; fields: bone meal; a pen: wheat; a frightened village: torches for the edge; a bell: copper; a pier: string;
lamps: glass; leather), renewed every other play-day, kept six days at most, counts shown, "Hand over" gives what you
carry; filled, it pays its emeralds once and its standing, lifts prosperity and mood, and goes into the history.

**The inn** (`Inn`): the innkeeper sells a room for three emeralds (the key is the receipt): the inn's guest bed becomes
where you wake if you fall, once (given back after you wake there, or after two play-days), and the night's rumour is
told over the fire.

**Sound and light.** The ambience slot in a settlement (`MusicLayers`, priority 90, under Carillon's):
`awaken:village/day` (birds over a murmur that grows with the people out of doors) and `village/night` (crickets, the
inn's voices till late), AmbientSounds' players the same without our birds and crickets; beds made from the city's
stems. The client sounds the forge's hammer through the working day, the mill wheel and the inn of an evening
(`citizens.client.VillageSound`), and puffs smoke from every chimney the grammar built (the roster's emitters, by hour
as in the city). Street lamps are the citizens' lamp heads (no light block; their light drawn, decision 26).

**Saved** (`awaken:villages`, schemaVersion 1): each settlement met (key, name, kind, land, origin, radius),
prosperity and mood (0-100), each player's standing, damage (every block broken in its planned ground by a player or an
explosion, with the block that stood there and the day, up to 2,048), buildings added, a short history (32 lines), the
board's notices, the day's counts; the paid claims; tonight's inn beds. The people's records are W0's.

**API** (§12): `dev.awaken.village.api.Villages` — `settlementAt`, `nearest`, `all`, `standing`/`addStanding`,
`damage`/`repaired`, `history`, `prosperity`/`addProsperity`, `mood`/`addMood`, `reserved(level, pos, margin)`. Citizens
gained `Settlements.onTalk(Talk)` and `installVoice(Voice)`, `Settlement.records/job/personName/age/body/say/acquaint`,
`RosterBuilder.emitter(x, ry, z, kind)` and `RosterSource.Built.emitters`. City gained `PlanView`, `SettlementPaint`
(`Layout`, `Canvas`, `Interior`, `paintChunk`, `sweep`, `standingCells`, `chimneys`, `dump`), `VillageStyles`.

**Measured.** Planning on real overworld noise: 0.3-0.6 s a hamlet, 0.9-1.3 s a village, once per settlement on the
worldgen thread that meets its start (the first hamlet's search at server start: a few tries). Painting: 0.35-1.5 ms a
chunk (about 1,600 cells; the grammar, the rooms and the ground), at most 4 light sources a chunk. Ledger with a village
awake: 0.0008-0.005 ms a tick. On GitHub's macOS runner (slower cores) the first hamlet planned in 5.2 s and a village
in 2.2 s; look tour 40313778099.

**Decisions taken here** (none of the plan's 13): the own pack and flag (above); the 640 grid and its odds; the first
hamlet's search order; the structure's step and the plan rebuilt from its anchor; the clearing of six; beards on the
streets and two past each house; half steps in the paving; spots spread over the green; styles keyed 16 + land x 4 + wealth;
two lights a house; the standing thresholds and the price rule; the board's needs; the inn's one fall; the claims kept
in the villages' file; village jobs appended to the city's list; the day's hours; the kit's civic blocks (they drop
nothing) used in village walls and furniture; gates 64 and Hearths 8 off a settlement's ground.

**Left.** W4: troubles (W0's director, `plannedEvents`), growth (prosperity raising buildings, `added`), the Rebuild
from the damage record, the history in the Journal, festivals. W6: settlers to the Hearth (Friend and Kin), a refugee or a
cured villager settling. W7: towns, mining towns, roads and caravans between settlements. Smaller: the Mire's houses
want stilts and the caravanserai a courtyard (styles only today); village clothes are the city's; a house smokes by the
hour, not by who is in; `/locate` can't find a settlement (`/awaken village list` does).

### 28.7 W4 as built (troubles and growth, 2026-10-26)
Branch `pack/world-depth-w4`. Packages `village.trouble`, `village.growth`, the troubles' client in `village.client`;
module doc `docs/modules/village.md` ("Troubles"). Tests `village_trouble_taken`, `village_burning_rebuild`,
`village_director_caps`. Tour `tools/autopilot/world-depth-w4.txt` (CI): `/awaken village trouble` moves each trouble
along by hand, `view <name>` stands at a framing (the eye moved as little as it takes to one with sky over it, room to
stand and nothing between it and its mark), and `site` stands you past the village's edge on even, open ground facing out,
so a lair built in front of you (`/awaken fauna lair place`) is in a Taken's reach. The Deep Mine waits for W7's mining
towns.

**The director** (`TroubleDirector`, saved data `awaken:village_troubles` `TroubleState`, schemaVersion 1). Every 10 s,
for each village that is awake (a player within its radius + 192): its festival's calendar first; then, unless the world
option is on, the world is in its first two hours of play (`PlayDays.playTicks`), the village is already in trouble, its
last ended under two play-days ago, it stands inside a Hearth, or some player within 1,500 of it already has two troubles
within 1,500, the first cause the world holds, in order: a gate within 500 due to break in one or two play-days (the Grey
Fields); its bell gone, a gate broken within 600 (cracks it, once per gate), or a riftborn camp of tier 2+ within 800 on
one night in eight (the Bell); a surface lair within 400 whose beast is home, else a Hollows den or riftborn camp within
400, on one night in four (Taken); a storm at dusk, one in three (Gone Missing); 24+ blocks of damage (the Rebuild). The
Burning comes from the camps (below). Each trouble runs on its own play-day clock (`due`) and ends without you when it
runs out, unless someone is mid-deed (carrying someone home, at the lair, the raid's night, the masons at work, a bell
being cast); its plot ticks each second while its village is awake (its once-in-a-while beats, a line said, the runner,
the smoke, counted in seconds of the world's clock, so a loaded world's clock offset never silences them). **World option**: game rule `awaken:calm_villages`
(off by default; in the world screen's rules): no troubles; festivals and growth go on.

**Found, never listed.** The call is in the world: the village bell rings the alarm fast and is heard to 256 (a new
event `village.alarm` played at volume 16 from the bell the ringer pulls; players 256 out get a quiet AMBIENT line naming
whose bell it is); scouts at the treeline; smoke columns over burned roofs sent to 512; the bell silent at dusk; lanterns
and the jig. While nobody has said Help, a villager (a hunter, farmer or carter) runs to the village's edge toward a player
the village knows (Known or better) coming within 180, waves, and tells them (`Runner`). The one who asks shows a choice
card (Help / Not now). The Journal holds a trouble only once you said Help: a row on the band's Journal page through
`living.api.Quests.addJournal` (the newest tracked), and the Now tracker points the way (for Taken the trail's next point,
not the lair). Up to three villages where you're Known show their latest history line in the Journal.

**Always paid** (`TroubleDirector.pay`): emeralds once per trouble and player (EconomyHooks claim), standing, XP through
the new budget `village` (0.5 of a level per 10 minutes), a keepsake (`awaken:keepsake`: named and inscribed), counter
`awaken:village_troubles_helped`, the village's prosperity +4 and mood +10. **Multiplayer**: saying Help counts the party
within 48; a payout reaches every helper and any party member of one within its radius; a raider felled, a flame beaten or
a person cut free counts you in whether you said Help or not.

**Taken** (`Taken`). At night the beast takes a child (else a young one) whose household has a grown-up: their record goes
away from the village's day (`Settlement.away`), the bell rings the alarm (36 strokes, again every 100 s up to three
times), the parent weeps by the well with the household round them, the Watch and neighbours stand at the green's edge
with lanterns and halberds looking the way it went. From dawn the parent stands in the square pointing that way and asks.
The trail: points every 6-8 blocks from the village's edge to 7 short of the den, wandering ±4 (seeded), laid as their
ground loads: two or three scuffs of drag marks along the way (`awaken:drag_marks`, flat, four looks, facing the trail) and
every fifth a strip of their clothes (`awaken:torn_cloth`, four colours); use a clue to read it ("A strip of Bren's
clothes, caught here. The way runs north-east."). With the Tracks perk (hunting 10) the trail glows for its helpers:
paired smears in the perk's teal every 1.3 blocks, a pulse running along them toward the lair. Within 56 of the den the
taken one is in the nest beside it, bound (arms tied behind, head down, tugging now and then, calling for help) in
cobwebs. They can't be cut free while the beast (its lair's resident, alive within 64) or the den's heart stands ("Not
while the Old Antler is here"). Holding use cuts the bonds (0.12 a use: about a second and a half; cobweb bits and shears),
then they **hold on to your back**: drawn behind your shoulders, legs round your waist, arms round your neck, leaning in
on your shoulder; you're 15% slower, can't sprint, and the body's moves stop (`core.api.MovementHooks.burdened`); your
arms reach back under their knees (the carry arm pose, `AWAKEN_CARRY`); in first person only their hands show at your
chest. Sneak a second to set them down: they walk behind you, climb a Runner's rope or ladder after you (they wait at
the foot and say so when there's none), and wait where they are if you go too far; use them to take them on your back
again. In the square they run to their parent's arms, the green cheers round them, a ring of light runs out; paid (14
emeralds a hamlet, 20 a village, standing +25, half a level, a keepsake: the child's carved whistle or the family's
knot), the village's history, the lair cleared for good (its beast never comes back: `Troubles.lairSealed`, read by
fauna's `Lairs.wake`; a den sealed by `Camps.sealForGood`), a carved token (`awaken:carved_token`) by the family's door
with your name on it, and from then on they greet you by name the first time you speak each play-day. Missed (three
play-days): they get out alone days later and the family leaves for Carillon (its people away for good, the house
empty), mood -12, prosperity -6, and whoever said Help and didn't come loses 4 standing.

**The Burning** (`Burning`; Living Wilds' camps, §21.8). A camp at tier 4+ whose nearest target within 800 is a village
asks the village (`Troubles.raidComing`): it takes it as its Burning unless calm, already troubled or crowded (otherwise
the camp raids a Hearth or the Wayfarer camp as before). The camp records `raid_village` and leaves the raid to it. The
ladder: the warning a play-day ahead (an IMPORTANT line to everyone within 800 and the history; the elder at the green
looking the camp's way, asking), scouts at the treeline at dusk (three of the camp's creatures 30 past the edge, slowed,
gone after 80 s), then the raid's night (13,600). If a player is within 90 of the green: the alarm, the camp's 4 + tier
creatures from 34 past the edge toward the green, the Watch lining the green facing out with halberds and lanterns; every
10-15 s while raiders live a fire arrow (a real flaming arrow) sets the nearest house's roof alight (up to four): up to
seven flames (Carillon's `city_fire`) on its ridge that grow on their own (+9 a second to 1,000), a bucket line of six
forming from the well to its door (Carillon's bucket pass, the bucket in hand) holding it back (-2 a second each: a full
line only slowly wins, a short one loses; a player in the line with a bucket counts twice), and beaten out by players
(-140 a flame: the player decides it); a fire at full for 20 s eats the roof, at 40
s guts the house. It ends when the raiders are dead and the fires out (paid by how many houses stood: 18 or 10 emeralds,
standing, a bucket token) or at dawn (the rest withdraw and what burns burns). Missed (nobody there, or the village not
awake: then it burns when it next wakes): the 2-3 houses nearest the camp (3-5 at tier 5) are charred (`Char`: roofs fall
in, timber blackens to stripped dark oak, basalt, coal and blackstone, glass, doors and cloth gone, floors to ash; stone
stands but soot blackens its walls and roof (not the paving), a sixth at the footings rising to most under the eaves,
into its deepslate or tuff kin, shape kept; burned footings up, so a charred remnant only stands on what's under it, never
floating; chests untouched; every block into the damage record with what stood there), a fire smoulders in each gutted
house (a signal campfire on its ash floor: Minecraft's own tall smoke, seen from far off; cold once the smoke's days are
done, cleared by the Rebuild), smoke columns rise over them for three play-days, the survivors camp by the well (a
campfire and bedrolls, sitting at night) until the Rebuild, mood -25, prosperity -12.

**The Rebuild** (`Rebuild`): 24+ blocks of damage (after a Burning, or any). The elder at the board asks; three notices
go up first on it (timber: the land's logs, a fifth of the wooden blocks lost, 12-64; cobblestone, a quarter of the rest,
12-64; iron, 3 + 2 a house, 4-12), filled by anyone. Then the masons raise scaffolding round each damaged house (corners
and every third block of the long sides, to the eaves) and put it back over three play-days, footings up, 40 blocks a
second at most, caught up when the village wakes, exactly as it stood (blocks someone else put there since stay); three
villagers at the house hammering and laying by day. Done: a beam of your colour over each charred house's door (the
lintel in the terracotta of your dye, by UUID), the first family that had left for Carillon comes back, the survivors'
camp is struck, mood +15, prosperity +6, a ring of light. Missed (five play-days without the materials): the village mends
what it can and the worst house stays a shell (its damage kept: a later Rebuild can still come). W3's own mending notices
now put back 24 blocks each (they had only forgotten the damage) and wait while a trouble runs.

**The Bell** (`BellTrouble`): the bell (Minecraft's own, in the tower or on the post) is taken down. At dusk the ringer
pulls at the empty rope and says so; the elder at the tower's foot asks. Stolen: once the camp's heart falls the bell lies
in its ashes (`awaken:village_bell`, named for its village). Either way the smith casts a new one from five ingots of bell
bronze (W2: copper and amethyst) handed to him: twelve seconds at the forge (sparks, the anvil) and it's in your hands.
It's heavy (slowed while in a hand: haul it up the tower yourself). Used in the belfry it hangs, rings, and a ring of light
runs out 160 blocks over the land at 20 blocks a second (three golden bands on the ground with a veil of light rising off
them, thinning as they go, CityGlow's pools under them nearby). Paid (16 emeralds, standing +20, the bell-pin keepsake). From then on: gate breaks within 600 of the
village are warned two play-days ahead (IMPORTANT, within 500), and the Grey Fields' blight keeps off its fields. A missing
bell rings nothing (citizens' peal checks the block). Missed (six play-days): the smith casts a thin one himself
(prosperity -8). Night hunters' boldness is left to Living Wilds (not built here).

**Gone Missing** (`Missing`): a storm at dusk and someone out (a hunter, woodcutter, miner, shepherd, else a child) doesn't
come home: away from the village, somewhere 50-180 out at the foot of the deepest drop (5+) the land shows, else in the
woods. The search party (five, with lanterns) at the village's edge that way calling the name; the parent at the well.
Clues: three strips of their clothes on the way; what they carried (a bow, an axe, a pick, shears, a lantern) dropped where
they fell. Within 40 they're there, sitting hurt; on your back or (sneak) walking behind you up a rope. Home as Taken
(Friend standing +30, 10 emeralds, a lucky stone; recorded for `Troubles.rescued` as "missing"). Missed: they limp home at
dawn two days on.

**The Grey Fields** (`GreyFields`): a gate within 500 due to break in one or two play-days. The elder at the green's edge
facing it asks ("It breaks tomorrow."). Cleared or released: nothing happens, the best ending, and they say so (14
emeralds, standing +15). Broken: the fields grey (farmland to coarse dirt, crops withered to dead bushes or gone) and two or
three grown-ups are Hollowed (abed: away from the day), mood -20, prosperity -10. The cure: an herb remedy
(`awaken:grey_remedy`, shapeless from sunleaf, moonmoss and a glass bottle) given to the healer or the elder brings one
back (standing +6); the last one back and the fields are tilled and sown again. A village whose bell a player hung keeps
the blight out.

**The Festival** (`Festival`, `Race`): every ten or eleven play-days per village (the first two to six days after it's met),
at dusk: the harvest, the first snow in the frost, the bell's day where a hunter hung its bell. Five or six poles round the
green (a fence post four high, a lantern on top) with paper lanterns on strings between them and across the green (drawn
on the client like Carillon's square, `village_festoons`; lit from dusk with CityGlow's halos and pools), a bonfire across
the green from the board, a jig on note blocks (flute over guitar, a bass drum and a hat: 48 eighths in D, heard to about
55) played from the musicians by the fire, ten of the village ring-dancing round it (the new `dance` clip), children
running the green's edge, the old cheering from the benches; fireworks at 14,500 and 16,200. The elder judges the fishing
and cooking (hand him your best fish or dish: fish by rarity and cooking, craft meals most; the best wins 8 emeralds,
standing and the village's ribbon). The rooftop race: the village's best runner at the well offers it; five roofs round
the green in order and back to the well (gold columns of light, the next one tall; the clock in the action bar), against
their time (the route at 5.5 blocks a second plus three); beat it for 6 emeralds and standing. Over at 18,600. Calm
villages keeps festivals.

**Growth** (`village.growth.Growth`): prosperity 72+ (it costs 14), no trouble, six play-days since the last, at most two
new houses a hamlet and three a village: past the end of a lane, on free level ground within the village's radius + 22,
the smallest house of the village is copied (its blocks read from the world, chests empty) turned to face the lane. The
plot is fenced with a gate and the land cleared, timber and stone stacked in it; the next morning scaffolding goes up at
its corners and the masons build it over 2.5 play-days, course by course from the floor; a path is laid to the lane.
Then a carter brings the family's cart to the door and the family (three) walk up the lane and in. From the village's
next waking (it restarts once nobody is within its radius + 80) they live there on the people engine: a door, a household,
two grown-ups and a child, records after the plan's own (the settlement's saved people reset with the new roster: its
standing is the village's and is kept). Saved in the trouble state's memory (`growth`).

**The person you bring home** (`Rescuee`, `awaken:village_rescuee`): wears their record's own skin (`Settlement.look`),
a child at 0.68; never hurt; saved; modes BOUND, CARRIED, FOLLOW, WAIT, HOME, EMBRACE, LOST; says lines over their head.
Players can't be ridden in 26.3 (the player's type is never saved, so `Entity.startRiding` refuses it as a vehicle on the
server): on a back they're held in place each tick behind the carrier's shoulders, and each client draws them from the
carrier's own position that frame. Their trouble gone (a body in an unloaded chunk), they go.

**History**: every trouble and its ending go into the village's history (W3's 32 lines): taken, warned, burned, rebuilt,
cast, festivals and their winners, families leaving and coming back.

**API** (§12): `dev.awaken.village.api.Troubles` (`rescued`, `settle`; `raidComing` for Living Wilds' camps;
`lairSealed` for fauna's lairs).

**Other modules touched (small, additive)**: `citizens` (api `Settlement`: `stage`, `away`/`isAway`, `alarm`, `where`,
`look`; `Roles.AWAY`; `CityEvents.stage` by record and `away`; the village alarm's far sound; a missing bell rings
nothing; more props by name; staged villagers answer talk; acts `DANCE`, `EMBRACE`, `WEEP` with their clips in
tools/art/specs/citizen_clips.py), `living` (`api.Quests` Journal rows, QuestEngine appends them (16 at most); `Camps`:
village raid targets with `raid_village` saved, `resolved`, `raidDay`, `byId`, `heartStanding`, `sealForGood`,
`placeAt`, `raidAt`), `world.fauna.Lairs.wake` (one line: a sealed lair), `body` (`BodyServer`, `ClientMoves`,
`AscentMoves`: `off()` reads the burden, one line each), `core.api.MovementHooks` (`addBurden`, `burdened`),
META-INF/enumextensions.json (`AWAKEN_CARRY`).

**Decisions taken here** (none of the plan's 13): the director's cause order and odds (one night in four, one in eight,
one dusk in three); two play-days' rest after a trouble; the young-world rule read from play time; the runner's 180 and
Known; a party member within 48 counts; the `village` XP budget at 0.5 per 10 minutes and the payouts above; a cut needs
the guard down; the held carry instead of riding (26.3 can't ride players) and its 15% slow; sneak to set down; the
nest within 56 of the den, cobwebs for every lair; the lair cleared for good through `Troubles.lairSealed`; missed Taken
sends the family to Carillon (the house empty) and costs the no-show 4 standing; a raid on a village is the village's
Burning (the camp hands it over); raids needing someone within 90 to be held, else burned (when next awake if asleep);
four fires at most, fire numbers above; char palette; the Rebuild's counts, three play-days and the beam in terracotta
by UUID dye; mending notices put blocks back; the bell taken down (not a cracked block); five bell bronze, cast in 12 s;
the bell's warning two days ahead within 600; Gone Missing from storms only; the Grey Fields' cure as an herb remedy (no
Sun's Cure exists yet) and the Hollowed as away from the day; festival every 10-11 days, its contests and race as above;
growth by copying the village's own smallest house, its thresholds, and the roster reset on growth.

**Left.** The Deep Mine (W7's mining towns). Night hunters bolder round a silent bell (Living Wilds). A hamlet becoming a
village through growth (W7's towns). The Hollowed's grey look on their bodies (they're abed instead). Settlers choosing to
go home with you at a festival, and your Hall's festival (W6 reads `Troubles`; a festival hook for the Hearth is W6's). A
GameTest for growth (its mechanism is exercised by `/awaken village grow`).

### 28.8 W6 as built (your village, 2026-10-26)
Branch `pack/world-depth-w6`. Package `dev.awaken.hearth.settle` (and `hearth/stage`, `hearth/kit`, `TierRules`); module doc
`docs/modules/hearth.md` ("Your village"). Tests `hearth_settler_moves_in`, `hearth_tier_reading`, `hearth_mine_head` (and the
kit's `hearth_home_kit`). Tour `tools/autopilot/world-depth-w6.txt` (CI).

**Who comes** (`Settlers`, PLAN 4.7, decision 2). Three things true: **you know them**, **a spare bedroom of Snug or better
stands**, and **their trade has its room**. Known (sticky, saved in the Hearth's `folk`, learned every 10 s from the household
online): the townsfolk by the household's rank as before (Oren E, Mira D, Teodor C, Sun B, Vael A until S), each a rank early
once Carillon's renown knows you (`RenownHooks` Known: "Trusted", §16 decision 8); a Wayfarer whose own chain you finished
(Ilse `moth_lights`, Hettie `ten_sheep_short`, Wren `wrens_rope`, Pell `pells_message`); one person from each village where
you're a Friend, and one from the city once its renown knows you (named from a seeded list, their work decided when they
come: your shaft if no one works it, your fields if no one tends them, else a hand); the rescued (W4's `Troubles.rescued`, read by
`settle/Rescued`: the grown-ups only, a child goes back to their family; a miner, farmer or shepherd, or smith keeps the
trade, anyone else finds work at move-in; the face they wore in their village, read from `Settlement.look` while it runs;
on moving in `Troubles.settle` once, through the household member who brought them home, so the village's history says
so). Rooms:
the townsfolk, Wren and Pell want only a bed; Ilse a Greenhouse; Hettie (and a farmer) a field or a pen; a miner a Mine head
no one else works; a village smith a Forge. A spare bedroom is a read Bedroom of Snug or better that isn't a settler's, isn't
the bed a member of the household last woke in at home (`folk.ownBeds`, from `PlayerWakeUpEvent`), and isn't the best one
kept for a member who hasn't slept here yet. One at a time, the first known who can, into the best spare (nearest their
work). **Caps** by tier: 0 / 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 / 12 (Hearthfire to Town). Waiting is said plainly: the guide's TOWN lists who
lives here (name, trade, "Ilse's room") and who waits and why ("waits for a bed", "needs a Greenhouse", "Tier II"); the Now
line (52) "Oren will come when there's a bed for him". A settler whose bed goes stays, between rooms, and takes the next spare
first. Vael leaves at S with a note.

**The walk up the road** (`Arrival`). The household is told ("Ilse is coming to live with you · On the road from the Wayfarer
camp with her things. She'll take the fine timber kitchen."). With one of them within 128, the newcomer appears on the
ground at the edge of the land toward Carillon (or the player's side) and walks in at an easy pace (a townsperson's body,
`TownNpc`, in their own face; the bundle on their back: the city porters' back layer with the vanilla bundle) through the
door to the bedside; vanilla pathing, 160 blocks, repathed every 2 s; stuck 12 s or on the road 2 min, they're in anyway.
There the room takes their name ("Ilse's room", in the caption, the room panel and the guide), the household hears "Ilse
moved in", a wool thud and embers at the bed. Nobody near: they simply move in. Arrival bodies are never saved.

**On the people engine** (`HomePeople`, PLAN 4.7: "your Hearth registers as a settlement through W0's API"). A Hearth with
people runs as settlement `hearth:<owner>` (origin the Anchor, radius the Hearth's, no planned events), rebuilt when the people,
their beds, the rooms or the yard change. Its places are read from the rooms you built: each bedside (a door place: going home
is going to bed), Oren's (or a smith's) spot beside the Forge's anvil (`anvil`: he hammers), Ilse's beside the Greenhouse's
soil (`wash`: her hands at work), Teodor's at the Study's lectern (he reads), Mira's at the Lookout's window, Sun's in the
Sanctuary, the miner's beside the hatch (a door place: going in is going down), Hettie's at the field's edge (farmland outside
rooms, from the scan's new `Scan.Yard`) and outside the pen's gate (away from the beasts), meals standing at the Hall's
table (`stand`: a floor cell beside a fence or wall with something on it, a top slab or an upside-down stair, facing it, eight
spread along it; with no table, beside its benches; the engine has no seated pose and someone stood on a bench reads wrong),
else the Kitchen's, else beside its stove, else the fire, the fire's ring by the Anchor of an evening (`tavern_out`: they lean and
talk), the yard's edge for Mira's watch at dusk (`post`, a lantern), errands round the doors. **The street graph** is walked
over the real blocks (`HomeWalk`): breadth-first from the yard over cells someone can stand in (feet and head clear or a carpet,
something 0.5-1.0 high under the feet that isn't farmland, a bed, fire, magma or leaves; wooden doors pass; steps of one up
with head room, two down; diagonals only past clear corners; at most 30,000 cells, 8,000 reads a tick), then each path pulled
straight where a line keeps to walkable ground at one height (sampled a body's width either side, a corner at least every 12
blocks), with corners on both sides of every step and doorway. **The day** (`Days`, 0 = 06:00): home; breakfast 06:20; work
from 07:00 (Hettie's pen from 09:50); the midday meal 11:24; work 12:30; supper 17:18; Mira's watch 18:12; the fire 18:18;
bed from 20:12 (each start nudged ±150 per person). The miner goes down the shaft at 06:54 and comes up at 17:18 with the
haul; Wren, Pell and the hands go about the place. Wooden doors on their way open as a body reaches them and close once the
doorway's clear; the hatch opens as the miner goes down and comes up. **Faces of their own** (a seam in citizens, additive:
`RosterBuilder.Person.face(String)` writes the roster's `named` field as `skin:<texture>[:slim][;<title>]`;
`CitizenBody` syncs `DATA_SKIN` and the word under the name; `CitizenRenderer` draws it):
Carillon's own named faces for the townsfolk (`townsfolk/oren`), the Wayfarers' (`wayfarer/ilse`), the rescued their
village's, a generated Carillon face of their trade for the rest (by id). Named bodies stay out of the city's events, as Carillon's named do. **Their voice**: a
`Settlements.Voice` wrapping the villages' (installed at server start) makes the household **kin** (the villages' warmest
greetings, `{village}` the home's name) and anyone else known.

**What they do** (`Work`, `HomeTalk`; talking goes through `Settlements.onTalk`; a chain waiting on them by name goes first,
except at Oren's forge with its business in your main hand: something to temper, or an ingredient of the piece he'd make).
**Oren**: tempers what you hold (as before); **commissions**: with a Forge, the best piece you carry the makings of (a weapon or
armour from any crafting recipe without a Blueprint, AWAKEN's first, then the bigger recipe) on a choice card; he takes exactly
what the recipe picks and the piece is done the next play-day, tempered I, in the chest nearest his anvil (else he keeps it for
you); without a Forge he asks for one. **Hettie** (and a farmer): every 30 s of work hours six ripe crops of the home's fields cut
and replanted (a seed kept back), the harvest in the chest nearest (else kept for you); once a play-day after 09:50 two of each
kind of beast in the pen breed while there are fewer than ten. **Ilse**: the herbs you hold (up to 16) become tonics by the next
play-day, two herbs a tonic (sunleaf and emberroot broth, frostcap tea, moonmoss soup, spiritgrass and duskbloom spirit tea),
home-cooked, in the greenhouse's chest. **The miner** (or a Mine Echo): below. **Mira, Teodor, Sun, Vael**: as before (rumours,
reading and identifying, mending), at home. **Wren**: once a play-day a rope line between two of your buildings at their eaves
(`Ropes`: the city's `awaken:hang_line`, a runner goes across hand over hand; rope and bunting by turns, sagging toward its
middle; across 3-14 blocks of air three above the ground, wall to wall, never within two of another; nearest the Anchor first;
six at most), and the first time you talk to her a Start Gate, four Checkpoint Rings and a Finish Gate ("Lay a line over the
roofs. I'll race your ghost."): the Training Grounds' ghost on your own route. **Pell**: once a play-day a letter (from the
village that knows you best, its own history's latest line; else the Association) and a rumour. What's kept for you comes
with the next talk. Trophies are commented on by the nearest who lives here; a rank-up's window has their lines.

**The Mine head** (`RoomType.MINE_HEAD`, `MineHead`, PLAN 7.7, decision 8). A closed room with a **hatch** (any trapdoor in its
floor) over a shaft at least 16 deep of air and what you climb (ladders, scaffolding, vines, chains, the runner and city
ropes: at least half of it), measured to 96 under up to four hatches (`Tally.F_SHAFT`, `F_SHAFT_X/Y/Z`, facts 12-15). The
shaft cuts a lode when a lode block (`Lodes.nearest`, radius 3) lies by it anywhere down it (the richer when two). Each evening
at 17:18 (once a play-day, `folk.haulDay`) each shaft worked (a miner who lives here or a Mine Echo on duty, one a shaft,
deepest first) brings up the ore of its foot's depth: ≥ y 40 coal and copper; 16-40 coal, copper, some iron; 0-16 iron,
copper, coal, now and then lapis; -24-0 iron, gold, redstone, now and then lapis; deeper redstone, gold, iron, lapis, 15% a
diamond; and the cut lode's ore (3-5, gold and Deepglass 2-3, diamond and emerald 1-2) until the mine has taken half the lode's
blocks. Into the chest nearest the hatch within 10 (else kept), dust and a thud at the hatch, a quiet toast to the household at
home. **The Mine Echo's dice are gone**: a Mine pad's Echo works the Mine head (no Mine head: nothing, and its pad says so); the
JEI page shows the haul by depth.

**Tiers grow from the home** (`TierRules`, PLAN 4.8). Beside the rank and the materials each tier already asked (iron at II,
gold and amethyst at III, diamonds at IV, diamonds, obsidian and a Lord's Heart at V): II Steading four rooms, one of them Fine,
and a field or a pen; III Hall a Grand room; IV Village a bell tower and four people living here; V Town eight. Shown ticked on
the upgrade card and the guide ("The home grows first"), checked again on building. Radii 24 / 48 / 56 / 64 / 80 / 96. The
Anchor's flame shows the tier (`HearthAnchorBlock.TIER` 1-5, kept in step by upkeep: five models from `tools/art/specs/hearth.py`,
a fire-bowl in the Anchor's top with the Lord's Heart in it: I a low ember flame, II steadier and taller, III gold with a gold
rim, IV bell-gold with the side runes lit, V a block of white-gold flame and a crown of light; particles and the fire's
crackle by tier; light 15 from IV). **At Tier IV your village is named**: on the Atlas (a `MapMarks` mark, "Ashford · your
village"; "· your town" at V) and in the place caption ("ASHFORD · your village"). The rise is told to the household.
`Hearth.villages(server)` (§12) is the hook W4's festival and W7's caravans use.

**Fixes found on the way**: a stair counts as a seat from the cell over it whichever side the reading meets it first (a hall's
benches could go uncounted). After the first CI tour: the townsfolk's bundle stack is made on first use (a static stack built
before item components are bound broke the client's first resource reload: tours hung at world creation); the walk graph's nodes
are offsets from the Anchor like the rest of a roster (they were world coordinates, so every walk between places failed and the
engine set people down at their places: `hearth_settler_moves_in` now reads the graph back); the arrival walks a given road to
its end first (the stage's).

**Commands** (admin): `/awaken admin hearth people | know <who> | arrive <who> | talk <who> | tier <n> | evening | wren | harvest
| stage [settle | miner | clock <who> breakfast|work | time <tod> | follow <who> | view <name>]` (the staged village for tours: `hearth/stage/HomeStage`, a home grown round its Anchor,
built from the Hearth's own cottages and simple shells; every room reads as any build does. It finds its own ground first, read from the
generator's heights without generating (`HomeStage.search`): candidates every 48 blocks out to 16 rings (768); each sampled on a
coarse grid over the 50-block disc and its 16-block rim (no water, nothing below the sea, no settlement or planned village),
then every 6 blocks for water; the least rise wins (14 at most; a ring of distance costs a block), and one rising 6 or less
ends the search; nothing fits, it builds where you stand. The first tour started on a coast (ocean east and north, ridges
west, Carillon south-west) and found nothing within 320 with the shore excluded, hence the reach. The disc is levelled, the
rim eased back to the land's height, trees the cut reached taken whole, the land's own beasts cleared. `view walker` frames
whoever is walking in from behind their shoulder, `follow <who>` a settler out of doors the same way; the clock only moves on
(a day's work and the haul follow it): `miner` to four seconds before the miner comes up with the haul, `clock <who>
breakfast|work` to three before a settler sets out, `time <tod>` to the next such time). Oren's commission card names the
piece in its title (a choice card shows only its title and choices).

**Decisions taken here** (none of the plan's 13): townsfolk want only a bed (their room makes them work there); "Trusted in
Carillon" is a townsperson a rank early; a village Friend or the city sends a new person, never one of its own records (no one
lives in two places); one settler a bedroom, one miner a shaft; the caps 0/1/2/4/8/12; the own bed by waking; arrivals walk only
when someone's near; the settlement keyed `hearth:<owner>`; the walk's rules above; the day's hours; the household is kin; Oren's
commission takes the best piece you can make, done next play-day at temper I; Hettie's six crops a half-minute and two of a kind a
day; Ilse two herbs a tonic, home-cooked; the haul table and half a lode; Wren's lines at the eaves and her course gift; Pell's
letter from the village's history; seats from above; meals standing at the table; the forge's business before Oren's chain.

**Left for W7** (and after): caravans on your road (Tier IV's other reward); the festival comes to `Hearth.villages` (W4);
a rescued settler still walks in their village too (the village
keeps its roster; W4's history says where they went), and a party member who also brought them home could take them in as
well; settlers sleeping in their beds visibly (today going to bed
is going in at the bedside, as in the villages); Pell's deliveries to villages you've helped; the Lookout's settler at the
Atlas; Carillon's own Oren, Mira, Teodor and Sun stay in the city as well (one person in two places, as the townsfolk always
were); the stage is a tour's, not a building tool.

### 28.9 W7 as built (roads and towns, 2026-10-26)
Branch `pack/world-depth-w7`. Packages `village.road` (the network, the planner, painting, the Atlas record), planners
in `village.plan` (`TownPlanner`, `WayhousePlanner`, `MinePlanner`, `TownPainter`, `MinePainter`),
`village.world.MinePiece`, the Deep Mine in `village.trouble.DeepMine`; module doc `docs/modules/village.md` ("Roads and
towns"). Tests `village_roads`, `village_town_plan`, `village_deep_mine`. Tour `tools/autopilot/world-depth-w7.txt`
(CI). Built by one builder with no sub-agents (Euan's instruction). New worlds only, like W3: the **Awakened Villages**
pack carries the road structure (`awaken:road`, set `awaken:road`, placement `awaken:road_lattice`); old chunks never
repaint.

**The network** (`RoadNet`, `Highroads`): planned per pair of neighbouring regions from Living Wilds' region map
(`RegionMap.cellRegion/heart/swallowed/roll`, made public for it), pure from the seed and the generator's estimate of
the land (`RoadWorld`: seed, centre, one `GenTerrain` per thread, its own `RegionMap`; made at `ServerAboutToStart`
right after the first hamlet is found, gone at stop). Each region outside the Commons has a **hub**: its **town** (about
one region in five, `TOWN_ODDS` 0.22, on the best site within 192 of its heart; never within 520 of the first hamlet),
else the grid settlement anchored nearest its heart within 300, else a **wayhouse** (an inn on a crossroads at the
heart, so inns stand a region apart: about 900 blocks, a day's walk), else a bare crossroads on dry ground within 128 of
the heart. Grid settlements within 360 of a town's region heart stand down. A **highroad** joins the hubs of every two
4-neighbouring regions, through the settlements near the straight way (between an eighth and seven eighths of it, within
a fifth of its length or 200 to one side; in at one end of a main street, out at the other); Carillon's three **ports**
(north from the Wayfarer camp, past its fire and the first hamlet; east and south from the painter's reach, 336 out) run
to the nearest hub within sixty degrees of their way out (up to three tried); every other settlement has a **lane** to
the nearest road point within 650 (with a waymarker at the fork). Each road is made once by whichever thread asks first
(`once` futures) and cut into **legs** of at most 72 points whose structure starts sit on a lattice of chunks (every
eighth chunk each way), so a chunk off the lattice answers at once; minimum-priority planners ("Awaken road planner N",
`RoadPlanners`) lay the roads within 1,100 of each player ahead of them, sixteen lattice chunks a pass (see Cost).

**The line** (`RoadPlanner`): an A* over a 12-32-block lattice inside an ellipse round the ends (stretch 1.45, 40,000
nodes at most), costing grade squared, refusing cliffs (over 0.6), open water (only narrow crossings with land on both
sides) and deep sea, with a small price on height so it takes low passes; corners cut (Chaikin twice); laid every 4
blocks; its profile the land's own height smoothed over three points each side, never more than a block a point (two
where the land is that steep), held at the ends and level over water. The road north out of the camp (the one every
player follows), where no narrow way is found, tries again allowing wide water (land within 48 on both sides; the deep
sea still refused). Bridges at surface + 2 (timber, or stone near a town and on a highroad's spans of 6+), boardwalks
over the mire's shallows, causeways over brooks. It keeps off a settlement's **built ground** (houses, streets, square,
walls, landmarks, three round them) but may cross its fields; each settlement keeps a way **14 wide clear past every
street end** a road leaves by (`VillagePlanner.keepExits`: no field, pen, garden, tree or house there; W3's villages
read this too, so their fields shift a little in new worlds).

**Painting** (`RoadPiece`, `RoadPaint`, `RoadMarks`, `Waymarks`): each leg paints the chunks it touches through the
settlement painter (fell the trees within reach, sweep what hangs over, fill to rock, `CityWriter`), pure per chunk;
thin-beard markers under every dry point ease the land to the road's heights (the pieces themselves take no beard, so a
bridge never dams a river). **Tall things keep off**: a road or settlement only clears a few blocks over its ground, so a
spire it meets lost a slice and its top hung in the air, and a neighbouring chunk's feature can land before the paint as
well as after it, so no sweep afterwards could be safe. The placement modifier `awaken:clear_of_settlements` (`reach`, last
in the placed feature) drops a feature whose reach, plus 8 for a road's banks, touches land a road or settlement referenced
from its chunk or those beside it uses: frost spires and glass shards (13, small 8), floating shards (16), boulders and
shale boulders (6). New chunks only. It reads only what the region decorating the chunk holds (vanilla's FEATURES step:
references in the chunks beside it, starts out to 8 chunks): the chunks under the footprint, no further out than those
beside the centre (whatever could cut the feature's own blocks is named there), and a start a reference names past 8
chunks (a road leg reaching 8 chunks from its lattice start, named from the chunk beside) keeps the feature off rather
than being read (reading it crashed world generation, CI tour 10 Nov: "Requested chunk unavailable during world
generation"). A layout is asked in its own plan coordinates (offsets from its origin, as the painter asks it); asked in
the world's, the first version saw no real road or settlement. Tests: `village_tall_things_keep_off`,
`village_tall_things_keep_off_region` (a region built as the FEATURES step builds it, far from the world's origin).
**Ground others stand on** (11 Nov, §21.11): `RoadPiece` and `VillagePiece` are `core.api.GroundPiece`s, answering
`usesGround` with the same layout test plus the banks, so a surface secret asks the land they use rather than their boxes. The carriageway is a two-track country road in the land's own ground: a crown grown over
between two worn wheel tracks and, on a highroad, rougher shoulders, each band mostly one ground so it reads along the
road (grass between dirt-path tracks in the heartland, podzol in the elder woods, gravel and coarse dirt in the frost,
gravel and stone in the highlands, sand and sandstone in the desert, mud and packed mud in the mire; cobbles and setts
near a town), 5 wide for a highroad, 3 for a lane, an earthen half step (mud brick; cobble in the frost and highlands,
sandstone in the desert) wherever it climbs a block; lantern posts every fourth lit point for the last 18 points into a
settlement. **Waymarkers**: a stripped-log post on a stone foot with a lantern, one hanging- sign arm per way out of its
side, the place's name and distance on both faces (waxed; white ink on dark woods); one a little way out of every
settlement (the next place and the one behind), one at every fork; at the crest where the first town comes into view, a
cairn of field stones.

**Viaducts** (`RoadPlanner.viaducts`, `RoadPaint.viaduct`; Euan, 2026-10-27: he likes the raised road over a valley, "it
adds a sense of fantasy", but its support was one plain grey post): where the graded road stands 8 or more over dry land
(`VIADUCT_RISE`, against the land at the point) it crosses on a viaduct. The planner flags the run and one point either
side (the abutments, on the land) VIADUCT (32), and PIER (64) on the abutments and evenly between, 2-4 points apart
(about every 12 blocks), so each span is one arch. A piece keeps 4 points either side of its leg (was 2), so every span's
piers are in its window. The painter, across the deck (the carriageway and a block past it):
- **Deck**: the road's own paving on dressed stone, no earth bed; a dressed edge of stone bricks with a parapet of stone
  brick wall (a quarter mossy) joined along the edge; a cornice of top slabs a block out, one under the road.
- **Piers**: three blocks thick and the deck's width at each PIER point, carried down to the ground by the plate (at most
  48 blocks, like any fill); a rib a block out up each face, under a slab cap; a lantern on the parapet over each pier.
- **Footings**: round each pier's foot the fill builds up from the ground only (`Mound.rise`): 5 high a block out, 2 high
  the next, rough stone (cobble, mossy cobble, mossy stone bricks).
- **Arches**: between two piers a round arch from face to face, its crown three blocks under the road, a chiseled
  keystone; open under it, so the valley keeps its own floor (no road markers' beard under a viaduct).
- **Stone**: stone bricks, cracked here and there, mossier the lower it stands (about 5% under the deck to 45%), a course of
  polished andesite every eight blocks; in the desert cut, smooth and chiseled sandstone. Every face has a grid and
  courses that read up close (a plain stone face with no seams read as stretched).
- Waymarks, lane joins and lantern posts keep off viaducts. New chunks only. Test `village_road_viaduct`.

**Banks** (`RoadPaint.bankDrop`, `CityWriter.fills`; Euan, 2026-10-27, "the cliff needs to look a bit more natural"): where
a road stands over lower land short of a viaduct (a rise under 8, or a hillside falling away beside it), the painter
raises a bank out to 26 blocks past the verge instead of leaving a sheer wall under the footprint. The bank comes down in tiers: each a rise of 4-8 blocks over a
face 0.7-1.7 blocks out, then a ledge of 0.9-2.5 blocks, the tier sizes from value noise (13-15 blocks a cell) and the
edge wandering about 3 blocks, so faces break and step, and one column in seven or ten pokes up or dips a block. Ledges
and the top take the road's turf (grass; podzol in the elder woods, sand in the desert) over 2-3 of dirt; steps of 2-3
get grass, coarse dirt, moss or rock; faces of 4 or more are rock with moss (10%) and mossy cobble (8%), and every face
foot gets a toe of gravel, coarse dirt or (mossy) cobble. The rock in the banks and in the plate under the road follows
the strata (`AlpineSurface.strata`: stone, andesite, tuff, granite, calcite bands; sandstone in the desert), so a face
reads as layered rock, not one flat stone sheet. A fill passes a solid crust up to 3 thick with air under it (the thin
road-marker beard over a valley) and stops on the ground below, so no stretch of road floats on a slab; a dry fill that
meets water stops, as before. The rim stays walkable: the road's own width plus verge is untouched. No bank on bridges,
boardwalks, causeways, viaducts or in towns. The banks reach new chunks only. Test `village_road_banks`.

**Towns** (`TownPlanner`, `TownPainter`; `Kind.TOWN`): a raster of 112 round a site near the region's heart (broad,
gentle, dry, water near). A wall ring of mean radius 64 (planned again at 76 where the land fits fewer than 25 homes,
the one with more homes kept) that follows a wavy line (8 high, merlons, a walk, towers about every 30 blocks and two
flanking each gate, 12 high with loopholes and pyramid roofs or crenels); a market square (super-ellipse, half-size 11)
where two main streets cross, squared to the compass (within four degrees), each out through a gate (arched passage,
portcullis bars, lanterns, banners) with a Watch post; straight lanes off the main streets every 24 blocks (they end at
the next street, T-junctions only) and a lane round the inside of the wall; a slot every 3 blocks of frontage so houses
stand shoulder to shoulder; 30-43 homes asked (the test valley fits 33, 113 people; a site under 18 is refused; the
survey's 15 sites all plan, 25-50 buildings and 69-120 people), the inn, the hall, the scribe's shop and the smithy
nearest the square, the granary and barns at the edge; districts by quarter (stone and slate round the market, timber
further out, the poorest by a gate); the square's fountain, a 5x5 bell tower, the notice board, benches and up to six
market stalls (a stall keeper each, goods by the land); fields, pens and the mill outside the walls. People 60-120 (two
Watch per extra gate, a carter, a healer, farmers outside). The first town is placed on purpose (`FirstTown`): of the
regions north of the first hamlet (420-1,700 on), the first whose land takes a town, preferring one with a rise between:
its road crests it there (the pass's cairn), and the town lies below.

**Wayhouses** (`WayhousePlanner`; `Kind.WAYHOUSE`): a crossroads square with four streets out (each an exit), the inn
(13x9 or 11x9: W3's tavern keeper, a room and respawn once, a meal, the night's rumours), a stable (a barn) and a horse
paddock, a carter (horses, leads, saddles, hay), a well and notice board; 4-9 people.

**Mining towns** (`MinePlanner`, `MinePainter`, `world.MinePiece`; `Kind.MINING`): a grid settlement rolls mining (a
village one in three, a hamlet one in ten) and plans as one where a mountain rises at least 26 from its edge (16
directions); else it plans as a village. At the mountain's foot the **shaft head** (7x7: timber headframe, sheave wheel,
chain, winch drum with its grindstone and lantern), the **assayer's store** (job `assayer`, id 30 in `Roster.JOBS`: raw
iron and copper, coal, ingots, gold nuggets, lapis, lantern; buys torches; a **lode map** for 8 emeralds, read with
lapis, W5's `CaveItems.map()`), four to six miners down the shaft each day. The workings: the shaft (lined, a ladder on
the town side, a roped piton line on the cross side) down 24 to the first level, a timbered gallery 3 wide and 4 high
with sets every 4 and rails, to the landing and a winze (ladder) 16 down to the second level, driven to a lode (W2's own
within reach, else a seam of the land's ore) and behind its face the cavern the Deep Mine breaks into; fluids walled
off, lode cells never cut.

**The Deep Mine** (`TroubleKind.DEEP_MINE`, on W4's framework): caused once per mining town, after it's been worked
three play-days, on a morning (1,500-5,000) one in four; never again once sealed. The mine bell (the alarm at the shaft
head, 36) and up to three miners' kin at the mouth with lanterns. Go down (ladder, rope, gallery, winze); near the
cavern (28) the nest wakes: 4-5 Hollows (Bestiary, normal tier) round the miners in its far corner; clear them (none
within 24), the miners follow you back along the second level while the roof comes down behind (W2's cave-in: cracks,
dust, falling stone, `CAVE_FALL`), then climb after you; home at the head. Paid (`TroubleDirector.pay`): 16 emeralds,
standing 20, XP 0.5, the keepsake "The Miners' Lamp"; the town's mood +14, history "... The mine's working again.", the
miners recorded for `Troubles.rescued` ("miner"). Missed (two play-days): the town seals the shaft with planks for good
(`mine_sealed`), the miners get out through old workings hurt, the assayer stops selling the mine's ore and maps.

**Caravans** (`RoadHooks`, `RoadAccess`; Living Wilds' `People.Caravan`): the World Pulse's caravan asks for a stretch
of a laid road 50-160 from the player, about 160 long, bound for a settlement (arriving at its edge when it's in reach),
and walks it; when it comes in, the village gains prosperity (+2, +4 if someone stood with it through an ambush), its
history says so, its stalls take the caravan's goods from where it set out, and players within 200 get an AMBIENT line.
Without the roads (old worlds) it walks open ground as before. **Tier IV** (W6 merged into this build): a home grown to
Tier IV (`Hearth.villages`) within 400 of a laid road is the caravan's first choice near it (`HearthRoutes`, installed
through `RoadHooks.installHearths`): along that road from its longer side to the point nearest the village, then over
the land to where its people gather, arriving there (an AMBIENT line to players within 200; keys `hearth:<owner>`).

**The Atlas** (`RoadAtlas`, attachment `awaken:road_atlas`, schemaVersion 1, kept through death; payload
`village_road_atlas`): every second, the stretch of road a player stands on (within 6; eight points of it) and the
settlement they're in; 3,000 stretches and 400 places at most; the whole on login, then only what's new. Settlements
are marks labelled with "· town", "· mining town", "· inn". The walked stretches are kept but no longer drawn on the map
(Euan 2026-10-29: "Let's remove this trail from the map"); `MapMarks.Line`/`registerLines` stay for any line a module
wants later.

**API** (§12): `dev.awaken.core.api.RoadHooks` (`Route`, `Access.stretch/arrived`, `install`, the Hearth call site);
`MapMarks.Line`, `LineSource`, `registerLines`, `lines`.

**Other modules touched (small, additive)**: `living.region` (`RegionMap.cellRegion`, `swallowed`, `heart`, `roll`;
`RegionService.land` public), `living.pulse.People` (the caravan on a road), `core.api.MapMarks` (lines),
`atlas.client.AtlasScreen` (draws the lines first), `citizens.Roster` (`ASSAYER` 30).

**Cost** (Mac, seed 26102610, real noise): planning a road 285-355 ms on a planner (about 107k land reads; ~80 roads
within 2,400 of the centre), painting a road chunk 0.9-3.1 ms (cold); a town planned in 0.36-0.93 s on real land (the
slower ones planned twice, the second with the wider wall; 48 ms on the test valley), painted at about 0.3 ms a chunk
over ~75-110 chunks, at most 6 lights a chunk. On Euan's terrain (Tectonic with the Awakened preset, the city basin) a
land read is a whole noise column (26.3 samples it all), 0.63 ms on the M4 (3x vanilla) and ~2.7 ms on CI's runner, so
the land is nearly all of the cost and the only lever is reading fewer columns. What keeps it down (every cut exact: the
same roads and plans for a seed, the bench's fingerprint unchanged):
- one shared reading of the land (`SharedLand`, behind `RoadWorld.terrain()`: 64 stripes of 4,096 recent columns and
  4,096 older ones), so a site search, the plan on its site, a village's fallback hamlet, a town's wider wall and the
  roads over it read each column once;
- planners (`RoadPlanners`: half the cores, one to six, always two cores left for the game, `-Dawaken.roadPlanners=N`;
  minimum priority, which macOS ignores, so the cap is what leaves the server its cores) sharing a lattice chunk's work
  as jobs ranked urgent (world generation waits for it), soon (a site search the server thread asked for) and ahead
  (nearest first): its settlements' plans, its highroads' hubs, then their pieces and Carillon's roads, then the lanes;
  each piece is still made once by whoever asks first, and no thread waits for a job still queued. A job ahead of the
  players starts between the server's ticks or within a tick's first 40 ms (`RoadTimer.serverLate`, from the server
  tick's start and end; held a second at most, so the queue keeps moving). Land comes first (`core.api.LandFirst`, §12;
Euan's Mac, 12 Nov: five planners used 4.6 cores while he flew over new land, and Tectonic's land came in half empty):
while new land is coming in round a player only the jobs for that land run, two at a time (a third goes back in the
queue in its place and the planner rests 50 ms before it takes the next): world generation's own, and the pieces of a
lattice chunk within the ring world generation makes structure starts in (the view distance, the generation pyramid's ten chunks
round a full one, `ChunkLevel.RADIUS_AROUND_FULL_CHUNK`, and one lattice spacing past it). The rest (a job further ahead, one a search asked for) is held
aside and queued again in its order once the land is in. Holding the near lattice chunks too had left world
generation laying their legs itself (run 43209363904: 15 s in 30 on the road starts thread, one chunk 5 s), where the
planners had laid them first (run 43205566659, the same flight before Land first: 11 ms). The pass ahead queues a
lattice chunk again nearer the front of the queue as a player comes closer (a job is queued again only when it's more
urgent), and the copy further back finds a newer one queued or run and does nothing; the lode plans'
and the Horizon's sinkhole workers, the village planner and the optional searches (the pick's trail to an adit, the
Hearth's mouth for a metal, a region's wonder, the Well's site, now on `LandFirst.later()` instead of the game's own
worldgen pool) wait before each job, at most a minute. No road, village or place is left out: each only comes later.
The road timer's line counts the jobs put back or held and the chunks in view not made yet. The pass ahead (`RoadNet.ahead`, on the
  server thread twice a second) only queues: a lattice chunk's fan-out (the region map and the grid, a few ms) runs
  on a planner. The laid roads' index by chunk is read without a lock (copy-on-write lists, a batch's points filed in
  one copy): a creature's road distance on the server thread had waited 31 ms for a planner filing a batch.
  `village_tick_holds` holds it: a wave of ~360 lattice chunks queued 2,400 out and world generation waiting on a cold
  lattice chunk beside it, then 15 s of the server thread's road calls for a player flying 40 blocks a second over new
  land. On the Mac (five planners, another build sharing the cores): no wait, the most work in a call 0.45 ms of CPU
  (19 ms by the clock: the cores were shared), the longest tick 196 ms, the planners busy every tick. It and
  `village_road_starts_wait` hold their 250 ms limit on a tick less the garbage collections inside it (the pause time
  the JVM's collector beans count, ZGC's and Shenandoah's concurrent "Cycles" left out), and say in the line how much of
  the longest tick was a collection: in the full suite on CI the longest tick swung 35-642 ms with the road work in it
  under 1 ms of CPU, so a collection must not fail the test, only a wait;
- a lattice chunk lays a lane only if it can reach it, judged from the roads the lane may join that are laid already:
  a lane runs from a street end to the point of those roads nearest the settlement's middle and keeps inside its
  search's ellipse (every point within 1.225 (δ + E + 24) + 44 of that street end, δ the nearest laid point or 650, E
  the farthest street end);
- a highroad is a way (its hubs, the settlements it rides through, each piece's two ends and what it keeps out of)
  worked out once, its pieces laid one by one: a lattice chunk lays only those whose ellipse comes within its legs'
  reach (100 each way), a lane only those that start or end at its settlement or could still hold a point nearer it
  than the nearest found (nearest first). Carillon's roads out are laid the same way: which region one heads for
  turns on whether its way there has any piece at all, so its pieces are laid in order only until one is (once, by
  whoever asks first) and the rest where they're needed. Commands, framings and the survey still lay whole highroads;
- a settlement beside a highroad that can't ride on it wherever its site moves (46 blocks at most, 91 for the first
  hamlet) is planned only when a piece's search probes within reach of its ground;
- the server thread never waits for a town's or wayhouse's site search: its searches ask the planners and pass the
  anchor by until it's known.
The bench (`roadbench_` with `-Ptests=roadbench_`, M4; cold lattice chunks 2,400 out, then the ~490 lattice chunks
within 1,600): W7 on Tectonic 51 s on average (26-83 s), the area 345 s (348k columns; 85 roads at 1.55 s, 108 plans at
1.19 s); now 11.2 s (3.6-18.8 s), the area 76 s (176k columns; 42 roads, 79 plans). On vanilla land: W7 13.1 s and 50 s
(242k columns); now 3.1 s and 22 s (131k). On CI's runner (three cores, two planners), the roads-perf tour
(`tools/autopilot/roads-perf.txt`, flying and teleporting over new land): W7 laid a highroad's piece in 3.35 s and
planned a settlement in 3.55 s on average (96 and 86), a world's spawn took 320 s (Carillon's pregen of 1,725 chunks
waiting for the roads round it) and the worst lattice chunk 81 s; now (run 40442457153) a piece 4.2 s and a settlement
3.4 s (45 and 70: the runner's cores are shared with world generation, and a piece's time now holds the plans its
search probes beside it), the spawn 274 s, the worst lattice chunk 84 s; with Carillon's roads out laid piece by
piece (run 40448865954) a piece 3.56 s, a settlement 2.67 s, the spawn 184 s (the runner's spread: the bench below
lays the same). The bench's counts are the measure: the runner reads a column several times slower than the Mac under
that load. The bench's last phase times the city's land cold (the lattice chunks within 374 of its middle, what
Carillon's pregeneration waits for): on Tectonic 26 lattice chunks, 12 roads and 32 plans (74k columns) in 40-47 s
whether the roads out are laid whole or piece by piece, the region each heads for being decided by a piece near
the city; on vanilla land 9 s (22 plans, 49k columns). What the spawn waits for is the highroads round the city and
the settlements at their far ends, up to ~2,900 blocks out.
What still stalls: 26.3 runs a chunk's structure starts inline on the level's one "worldgen" executor, so a lattice
chunk waiting for its roads holds all of the level's chunk generation, and the server thread blocks on any chunk it
loads meanwhile (on the runner: progression's ledge finder, Lithium's collision sweep for a spectator flying into new
land, a vault): the tour's "Can't keep up" (W7: 2, 4.5 and 38 s, the last at the first teleport, the camp's road north
laid already, then a near-freeze; then 2 s at the start and 33 s at the first teleport, the watch's stack in the ledge
finder reading a chunk still generating, then one tick of 4.5 minutes in it; the ledge finder now reads only chunks
already whole). A watch on the server thread (`RoadTimer.watch`) logs any tick (or task between ticks) over two seconds
with its stack, always (a player's log says what held the server; on a tour over one second, sampled 20 times a
second), again every 10 s while the same tick runs, each time with the first frames of every thread not waiting for
work, of any name (a stack's first 24 frames, then when they don't reach the tick the rest from the first frame of ours
on, else the last ten above it: a density function's frames alone filled the 24 of Euan's 32 s stall at a join, 12 Nov,
and the caller was cut off) (a chunk the server thread waits for waits on one of them; those waiting for work counted), Road
starts' lattice chunks not given back with what each waits for (its roads, the worldgen dispatcher to take it up, its
step) and how long, each level's worldgen and light dispatchers (queue head, asleep, both executors' state), its light
tasks, generation tasks not yet run and chunk tasks for the server thread, and the chunk under each player followed to
what it waits on (`ChunkWaits`: its status, the step it started, its ticket and queue levels, its generation task; then
the neighbour furthest behind what its next step needs, and that one's, down to a step started and not finished or one
whose neighbours are ready and that never started; read only, from the watch's thread, the fields widened by the access
transformer; `village_stall_watch_reads`). Run 40709834352 is why: the flight waited 6.6 minutes in vanilla's fall-damage
fluid check (`EntityFluidInteraction.hasFluidAndLoaded`, a FULL `getChunk` that doesn't load but waits on a chunk under
way) with every world generation, IO and Awaken thread idle and no roads being laid. A tick counts from the players' packets on (26.3 handles them before `tickServer`, and a move into land not
generated yet waits there in NeoForge's `Entity.setPosRaw`). It logs any chunk the server thread had to wait for further than view distance from every player in its level,
with the chunk's own tickets and who asked (once a minute a caller; a chunk without a getChunk's own "unknown" ticket
rode in another chunk's wait, so the stack names that wait, not who asked for it). The camp command (`/awaken village road camp`) never lays a road on the server thread: a
thread of its own lays what it needs (not the planners: their queue can be minutes deep after a pregen) and the server
stands the player on it once it's laid (run 40448865954: at once). Still left, on the runner only: a spectator flying
24-40 blocks a second over new land freezes the server for minutes (that run: a 10.4 s tick, then two ticks in four
minutes), vanilla's own movement check (`handleMovePlayer`, fall damage, the fluid under the player) blocking on a chunk
whose lattice chunks' roads world generation is laying itself while the two planners fall behind. On the Mac a cold
teleport waits ~11 s and the planners keep 1,100 blocks ahead. Road starts (below, Turbo, built 2026-10-28) free world
generation while a lattice chunk waits; the chunks that need that one still wait for it. The minutes-long flight freeze
is not the roads' (runs 40715105903 with Road starts off and 40716396298 with it on and the deeper watch, both on
a1d5816c's code, both froze 6-7 minutes the same way): the server's tick never came. 26.3 handles every queued packet
before each tick (`PacketProcessor.processQueuedPackets`, `while (!queue.isEmpty())`), and a client has no chunk gate
(`LocalPlayer.tick`), so a player moving faster than the server generates land sends move packets into chunks not
made yet. Each one waits on the server thread for the chunk under its position (NeoForge's `Entity.setPosRaw`, then
vanilla's fall-damage fluid check), and the client keeps sending, so the one tick runs the queue for minutes (the
chunk under the player moved from 50,11 to 201,-117 within it, each one finished in turn) until the client stops (the
quit). The level's one worldgen executor was busy all along (features, structure starts' site and height reads; the
terrain noise runs on the background pool), Road starts gave every lattice chunk back (184 of 184, the longest 22 s
waiting for its roads, 7 s for the dispatcher), and the worldgen, IO and Awaken pools were otherwise idle. The quit
hang that follows such a freeze (run 40716396298's watchdog dump) is the same freeze's: the client's
`IntegratedServer.halt` queues a task for the server thread (`executeBlocking`, after its `isRunning` check) and joins
it, but the server, held in that tick, handles the host's disconnect first, stops itself ("Stopping singleplayer server
as player logged out") and never runs the task, so the Render thread waits forever (the world is saved). Both fixes
are built (Euan, 2026-10-28: "Do both: hold fast movement at the edge of generated land now, and build the Turbo
mixin that caps packet handling per tick as a backstop"): the edge hold and the packet cap.
**The edge hold** (core, `core.EdgeHold` for the math, `core.client.EdgeHoldClient` for the hook, 2026-10-28). Fast
movement never carries a player into chunks their client doesn't have. Once a client tick, the local player's
horizontal velocity is capped. The hook is the last listener to `MovementInputUpdateEvent`, which fires in
`LocalPlayer.aiStep` just before `travel`. It reads the path 25 ticks (1.25 s) ahead, chunk by chunk: one lookup in the
client's chunk storage per chunk the path crosses (`getChunk(x, z, FULL, false)`), no allocation, out to the render
distance less one chunk. Where a chunk on the path is missing, the speed is capped at the distance to it over
25 ticks, so the player arrives as the land comes in. The cap falls at most 12% a tick from the speed the player
had, which feels like thick air or a headwind, never a wall. It never drops below 0.1 blocks a tick (2 b/s) until
the last block before the edge; over that block it eases to nothing and the player stops short of the missing chunk
(the orchestrator, 2026-10-29: "drop it at the edge"; in run 40741943440 a crawl at the floor walked into unmade land
and one move packet waited 44 s). The player's middle stays `EdgeHold.BODY` (1.35 blocks) from it: the box's
half-width and the block past it that vanilla's fluid check reads (`EntityFluidInteraction` reads one block beyond
the box, and a FULL `getChunk` that doesn't load still waits on a chunk under way). Each tick the cap is also at most
half the room left, so the player nears that line and never crosses it. `travel` adds the mover's own acceleration
after the cap, so a guard at the end of the player's tick (`PlayerTickEvent.Post`, before `sendChanges` sends the
position) puts back any step that came nearer than `BODY` to a missing chunk, on the axis that crossed, and zeroes
that axis's speed. A player already nearer (just arrived, the land still coming) isn't held there. The headwind and
the mist carry the meaning (the cue, below). It lifts the tick the chunk arrives. Vertical speed is the mover's own. Every fast mover moves the
player by their velocity, so the one hook holds them all:
- Skyborn's flight and its boosts (§17.1, §17.8, §17.19);
- glides and windways (§17.1, §17.12);
- the Tether's launch, zip and swing (§17.7, §17.31);
- dashes and the movement powers (§6), whether set on the client or by the server's motion packets;
- the pilot's `glide` (§13, Tours);
- vanilla's elytra, firework boosts, riptide and creative or spectator flight.
A mover that sets velocity later in a tick is held from the next tick, a tick's travel well inside the 1.25 s look.
Riding is the mount's movement and isn't held. Teleports (Blink, the steps, commands) aren't velocity: Awaken's own
travel waits for its land (Arrivals, below), and the packet cap is the backstop for the rest. A hold of a second or more logs one line when it ends, at most every 10 s (`[edgehold] held N ticks
at the edge of the land this client has, slowest S blocks a second`). In multiplayer it keeps a player's own move
packets inside land the server has already sent them, so the server has made it.
**The cue** (`core.client.EdgeHoldCue`, 2026-10-29; the orchestrator, from the runner's 55 s crawls: "if a held glide
ever crawls that long it'll feel broken"). While the hold eases a player, the world says it is catching up, not
lagging. Both parts follow one eased strength (`EdgeHoldClient.shown`): in over about half a second, out over about a
second once the land comes, holding 10 ticks past the last tick held so a crawl at the floor stays one hold. It runs
from 0.3 for an edge 48 blocks ahead or more up to 1 at the edge.
- A headwind: its own loop, `edge.headwind` (`edge_headwind.ogg`, `tools/art/specs/audio_edge_hold.py`, events in
  `src/main/merge/core_edge`). It's air pushing back in your face, not the Ascent's rush past the ears: a soft wide
  breath in slow swells, low pressure under it, a thin hiss on the swells, and a faint glassy shimmer at a swell's peak
  (the land forming ahead). It plays at the listener up to 0.6 volume, a little higher in pitch as it presses.
- A mist at the edge: in air only, the fog closes in on the eased edge distance. It's whole 4 blocks past the edge and
  clear for the first quarter of the way. The far plane comes in geometrically from vanilla's 1,024, so it eases
  instead of appearing at the end. Its colour leans up to 35% toward a pale, faintly cool glow of the sky's own light,
  so the land ahead fades into haze instead of ending at a cut. It composes with the other fogs (Far Sight before it,
  Lens reading after it).
`core_edge_hold_math` checks the path's edge straight, through a corner, west of the origin and from a chunk that's
missing. A flight at 40 b/s toward land missing beyond 40 blocks eases by at most 12% a tick and never holds below
the floor short of the last block. It never crosses before the land comes, and it's back to full speed within two ticks
of it. When the land never comes, it eases to a stop within the last block and never comes nearer than `BODY`.
**Packet cap** (Turbo, `dev.awaken.turbo.packetcap`, 2026-10-28). The server's queued packets are handled in order for
at most 50 ms a tick (`PacketCap.BUDGET_NS`, a tick's time, the first packet always), and the rest wait for the next
tick. The hook is a HEAD inject in `PacketProcessor.processQueuedPackets`, for the server's processor only
(`server.packetProcessor()`); the client's is never capped. A flood, or a move packet waiting on a chunk, now holds a
tick only as long as its own wait, and the tick runs: mobs, time and the server's tasks with it. Packets take
microseconds in play, so only a flood or a wait meets the budget. Ticks that leave packets log one line at most once a
minute (`[packetcap] N ticks left packets for the next tick (the longest handling M ms)`).
It also closes the quit race. Once `stopped` is set, just before `stopServer`, a new task runs on the caller's own
