## 31. The Soft Land (seams, steps and detail on the ground; plan docs/terrain-immersion/PLAN.md, page https://claude.ai/artifact/EHXyQyds2wzL7dGfox8gnz; Euan approved all of it 2026-10-27)

Euan: "a bit less rough terrain, a bit more cinematic and natural look (stones etc.), more foliage feeling ... the priority
really is IMMERSION", and "less like just block per block gaps, while STILL keeping it feeling like minecraft". Module
`ground` (package `dev.awaken.ground`, client half `ground.client`). The plan's audit, alternatives, failure register and
fifteen decisions (D1-D15, all recommended and approved) are in docs/terrain-immersion/PLAN.md; this section records what
is built. The measured finding that shapes it: the one-block steps are the block grid, not the noise (43.1% of
neighbouring column pairs differ by one block on a 35° hill; the same with the erosion's finest octave at 16 or 64 blocks),
so Tectonic and the erosion stay as they are (D7). `docs/terrain-immersion/proof/` holds the bench and the renderer.

**The line (D3):** blocks, pixels, half-block steps and light. No eighth-block layers to sculpt the ground, no bent
or smoothed terrain faces, no texture above 16×16.

### 31.1 P0 Seamless ground (built; client only, every world, setting `ground_seamless`)
- **Rules** (`ground.SeamlessRules`, pure on a `BlockGetter`, held by `ground_wrap_mask` and `ground_creep_mask`): a grass
  block, podzol or mycelium wraps on a side when the block beside it is open (not `isSolidRender`) and the ground just
  under that is sturdy (a one-block riser), or the block beside is one of our soft slabs (`#awaken:ground/soft_slabs`,
  empty until P1); a covered block (something solid on it) or a snowy one wraps nothing; a two-block riser keeps its dirt
  face. Paths, dirt, coarse dirt, rooted dirt, gravel, sand and red sand get grass creeping over a top edge where bare grass
  lies beside them at the same height (sky open over both), and a corner where only the diagonal is grass.
- **Drawing** (`ground.client.SeamlessModel`, a `DelegateBlockStateModel` like `terrain.client.WavingModel`, wrapped in
  `ModelEvent.ModifyBakingResult` by `GroundClient`): `collectParts(level, pos, ...)` on Sodium's meshing threads. WRAP:
  the masked sides' base quad is re-made with the top quad's sprite and tint (each corner keeps its place in the sprite)
  and the overlay quad is dropped; converted parts are cached per source part and mask. CREEP: up to eight unculled overlay
  quads 0.002 above the top face (a path's top is 15/16), from our sprites `block/ground/creep_edge_0..2` and
  `creep_corner_0..1` (grey, `tools/art/specs/ground.py`), turned to the side by their UVs, cut-out layer, no tint index:
  the neighbouring grass block's colour (`BlockTintSource.colorInWorld`, drift included) is baked into the quad's colours.
- **Lawn drift** (`ground.LawnDrift`, pure of (x, z); `ground_drift_range`): the grass colour moves about ±9% red, ±3%
  green, ∓7% blue by a noise of 26-block patches plus a 7-block grain (farsight.glsl's `farHash`, so far ground can lay the
  same). `GroundClient.drift` wraps the grass layer of `grass_block`, `short_grass`, `fern`, `bush`, `tall_grass`,
  `large_fern`, `pink_petals`, `wildflowers` in a `BlockTintSource`; City Sight's per-biome probe (position 0, 0, 0) and
  items keep the plain colour. Setting `lawn_drift`.
- **Settings and commands**: `config/awaken-ground-client.toml` (`ground_seamless`, `lawn_drift`, both on); `/awaken ground
  status | seamless on|off | drift on|off` (client; saves and redraws the chunks). Off, the client draws as vanilla.
- **Fresh sides** (`ground.FreshSides`, `ground.GroundFresh`, `ground.client.FreshView`; Euan 2026-10-27: a dug lawn's
  neighbour was green down its new face at once). A grass side bared a moment ago shows its own face (vanilla's dirt and
  fringe) and grows green, where the shape rule alone would wrap it on the first frame; a riser the world was made with has
  no record and wraps as before. **Recorded** when it happens, never by scanning, on the server: a player's break of a
  hider (`isSolidRender`) whose ground under stays sturdy (`BreakBlockEvent`, lowest priority), an explosion's hiders
  (`ExplosionEvent.Detonate`, minding the blocks it takes beside and under), a sturdy block placed under the open block
  beside a grass block (a cliff's face becomes a riser's), and a grass block placed beside open ground. Placing a hider
  beside drops the side's record at once; breaking the grass block drops its four. Not caught (they wrap at once, as
  before): pistons, endermen, fire, other mods' block changes. **Kept** per chunk in the attachment `awaken:fresh_sides`
  (key = block in chunk + side, value = lit ticks; `schemaVersion` 1; saved while not empty; never loads a chunk to write
  one). **Grows** every 100 ticks over the loaded chunks that hold records: a side whose open block beside has
  `getMaxLocalRawBrightness` >= 9 (vanilla's own rule for grass to spread) gains 100 lit ticks; dark or roofed it waits.
  **Stages** by lit ticks: 0 bare dirt (0), 1 grass a third of the way down (2,400 = 2 minutes of light), 2 most of the way
  (6,000 = 5 minutes), wrapped at 12,000 (10 minutes of light, about a day with nights): the record goes and the side is a
  riser like any other. A side that stops being a riser's face (filled, its ground under gone, its grass gone) loses its
  record on the next growth. **Sync**: each record's stage (not its ticks) to every player who sees the chunk, sent the
  moment it changes, so all players see the same stage and a stage change redraws one section. **Client**: `FreshView`
  keeps an immutable key-to-stage map per chunk (Sodium's meshing threads read it; nothing to look up when no chunk has
  records); `SeamlessModel` leaves a fresh side unwrapped and, on a grass block, lays a quad 0.002 out over the side with
  our sprite `block/ground/creep_side_0` (stage 1) or `_1` (stage 2), grey and tinted as the grass (tint index 0, drift
  included). While the local player mines a hider beside grass, the sides it would bare count as stage 0 for two seconds
  (`PlayerInteractEvent.LeftClickBlock`), so the hole is dirt the frame it opens, not green until the server's word.
  Tests: `ground_fresh_dig` (dug: dirt; lit: stage 1, 2, wrapped; roofed: stays dirt; filled: record gone; dug again),
  `ground_fresh_natural`, `ground_fresh_saved`.
- **Not yet** (P0's own follow-ups): City Sight's wrapped sides (`VoxelLooks`) and Far Sight's drift (`farsight_terrain.fsh`,
  `FarColumns`): near and far differ by a few per cent of colour and a one-block riser's colour until they land.
- **Tour**: `tools/autopilot/ground-p0.txt` (CI look tour): a control scene (step, pillar, path, coarse dirt, gravel, sand
  beside grass) on and off, five biomes at eye height, the drift on and off.

- **The pack** (skeleton, so every later phase shares it): `datapacks/awakened_ground` behind the feature flag
  `awaken:awakened_ground` (declared in META-INF/feature_flags.json; `GroundModule.PACK_ID`), the way Lands, Alpine and
  Villages are: a world created with the flag loads it, an older world never does. P1, P2 and P4 put their worldgen in it
  (P3 extends Awakened Alpine's own pack and flag).

### 31.2 P1 Soft steps (built; new worlds only: pack `awakened_ground`, flag `awaken:awakened_ground`)
- **The rule** (`ground.SoftRule.foot`, the bench's: docs/terrain-immersion/proof/SoftBench.java): a column takes a half slab on
  top of its ground when a cardinal neighbour is exactly one block higher, none is lower, and none of the eight is two or more
  higher. It only adds; it reads ground heights only. Measured on AWAKEN's own erosion: one-block risers -97% on rolling land,
  -42% on a 35° hill, -4% on a 58° flank (cliffs untouched by design); 3.5 ns a column.
- **The pass** (`ground.SoftStepsFeature`, feature type `awaken:soft_steps`, a placed feature with no placement added to
  `#minecraft:is_overworld` by `neoforge/biome_modifier/ground/soft_steps.json` at step `local_modifications`): once per
  chunk. Heights are the chunk's and its one-column ring's `OCEAN_FLOOR_WG` heightmaps (read from the nine chunk objects; no
  noise column, so Tectonic's cost is unchanged), dryness `WORLD_SURFACE_WG == OCEAN_FLOOR_WG`; only this chunk's columns are
  written, so a chunk comes out the same in any order. Skipped: wet columns, cold columns (snow layers can't lie on a slab),
  a block or plant over the ground (not air), a ground with no slab. Grass and podzol under a slab become dirt at once.
  **Order**: roads and settlements paint at `top_layer_modification` (`awakened_villages` structures `road` and `settlement`),
  after this pass, and overwrite their own columns (streets and yards clear `g+1..g+4`), so no half-slab can survive in a
  street or a yard (`ground_soft_before_painters` holds the two steps); vegetation (`vegetal_decoration`) comes after it too,
  and plants and saplings refuse the slab (not in `#minecraft:supports_vegetation`), so nothing floats.
- **The slabs** (`ground.SoftSlabs`, `SoftSlabBlock extends SlabBlock`, generated by `tools/content/ground_content.py`): turf
  (grass), dirt, coarse dirt, podzol, mud, gravel, sand, red sand; stone, andesite, granite, diorite, tuff, sandstone and red
  sandstone steps use vanilla's own slabs. All in `#awaken:ground/soft_slabs` and `#minecraft:slabs`, shovel-mineable,
  monsters spawn on them (`isValidSpawn`), the turf slab in the animal spawn tags. Breaking gives the slab (a turf slab gives a
  dirt slab unless silk-touched); no recipe. The turf slab's side shows the top half of the grass side texture so its fringe
  sits at its top; double slabs show vanilla's full block models. Unhandled in P1: our Lands grounds (hoarfrost, mirepeat,
  riven shale, faultstone, fused glass) and snow country (cold columns are skipped).
- **Tufts**: `TurfSlabBlock.TUFT` (0 none, 1 short grass, 2 tall grass, 3 fern, 4 flower, 5 bush; chosen by `SoftRule.tuft` from
  the seed and column: about 45% carry one) draws a plant inside the slab's own block from its top up; tinted as the grass is
  (`GroundClient` registers the grass block's drifted tint for the slab); sways through `PlantSway.SLAB_TUFT` (rooted at y 0.5).
  A turf slab under a solid block decays to a dirt slab on a random tick; it does not spread.
- **API**: `ground.api.GroundTop.standingY(level, x, z)`: where a body really stands over a column (a heightmap counts a slab
  as a whole block). Use it for anything placed on the ground after generation (camps, anomalies, Hearth pieces, gates); the
  callers of `getHeight(` in other modules are not changed in P1 (an audit list for the owners: a thing placed by heightmap alone
  floats half a block over a foot column).
- **Ascent**: no change. A half slab is under the step height (0.6), so walking up needs no jump; a descending run of half
  steps is a run for the stair slide (§17.22: it slides down a soft hill); a wall topped with a slab has a ledge at its top
  (`ground_soft_hill_body`).
- **Tests**: `ground_soft_rule` (plateaus, one-wide stairs, cliffs, tufts), `ground_soft_steps_paint` (the pass on real
  blocks: foot columns take slabs, grass below turns to dirt, plants and blocks stay, standing height), `ground_soft_slab_rules`
  (spawning, no vegetation support, decay), `ground_soft_before_painters`, `ground_soft_hill_body`.

### 31.3 P2 The floor (built; new worlds only, the `awakened_ground` pack)
- **Palette table** (`tools/terrain/ground_palette.py`, the one source; run it to rewrite `datapacks/awakened_ground/data/awaken/
  worldgen/{feature,placed_feature}/ground/` and `neoforge/biome_modifier/ground/floor_*.json`, and `datapacks/awakened_ground/palette.json`):
  per group of biomes (forest, birch and Elderwood, Lumen Forest, taiga, hills and mountains, plains and meadow, savanna, desert,
  badlands, swamp) a list of placed features, each with a `ranks` slot (E, D, C, B, A, S; all for now; P5 will fill it from the regions
  plan). Added at `vegetal_decoration`. Patterns: `drift` (a chunk in `rarity` gets `count` of them within `spread` blocks of a spot:
  a cluster, never an even scatter; the air-over-a-whole-block filter keeps them off slabs) and `single` (one where a chunk picks).
  Vanilla pieces reused by name: `fallen_oak_tree`, `fallen_birch_tree`, `fallen_spruce_tree`, `moss_patch`, `bush`. Our Lands
  biomes already have their own fallen trees; Lumen Forest gets boulders and pebbles but no oak twigs or logs.
- **Pebbles and twigs** (`ground.GroundCover`, `cover.PebblesBlock` kind 0-3 stone/andesite/granite/diorite and 1-3 stones;
  `cover.TwigsBlock` wood 0-2 oak/birch/spruce bark, four ways): `VegetationBlock`s that need a whole block's top under them
  (never a slab), no collision, broken by a touch, replaceable, not swaying; models are small boxes on the 16-grid with the game's
  own stone and bark textures (no new art), generated by `tools/content/ground_content.py` (`cover_assets`). Twigs drop sticks.
- **Boulders** (`ground.BoulderFeature`, feature type `awaken:boulder`, config `palette` and `min_radius..max_radius`): a rounded
  ellipsoid of its palette's rock (forest: mossy cobblestone, stone, cobblestone; highland: stone, andesite, granite, tuff; plains;
  desert: sandstone; badlands: red sandstone), half sunk (two blocks for radius 3 and up), crowned with the rock's own half-block
  slabs where the height has a half left; never over water, logs, leaves or a non-natural ground. Radii: forest 1-3, highland 2-5,
  plains 1-2, desert and badlands 1-3.
- **Wild life**: bare stone is a ROCK perch (`wildlife.client.Sites`); boulders count: `#awaken:ground/perch_rock` (mossy cobblestone,
  cobblestone, sandstone, red sandstone and their slabs) joins `BASE_STONE_OVERWORLD` there. Fallen logs are trunks as they are.
- **Footstep tags** for later: `#awaken:ground/litter`, `brush`, `gravel`, `small_things`.
- **Not in P2** (listed in the plan, deferred): three own grass heights and clover (they need new art), roots at tree feet (hero
  trees have their own), rank palettes (P5).
- **Tests**: `ground_floor_data` (every palette entry's files exist, boulder configs and every placed block state decode),
  `ground_floor_blocks`, `ground_floor_boulder`.

### 31.4 P3 Mountains (built; new worlds only: Awakened Alpine's own pack and flag `awaken:awakened_alpine`)
- **Slope-led ground for every steep slope** (`terrain.alpine.AlpineSurface`, D8): scree and rock reach lower (`SCREE_SLOPE`
  1.45 -> 1.15, `ROCK_SLOPE` 1.8 -> 1.5, rise per block; the same numbers in `farsight.glsl`, held equal by
  `ground_mountain_far_parity`), and `LOOSE_FROM` 0.7: soil that is steepening shows patches of coarse dirt and gravel
  (`AlpineSurface.loose`, 7-block patches that grow with the slope). The scree band is no longer all gravel: its noise
  (`pocket`, 6-block cells) leaves grass pockets where low (under 0.22) and rock showing where high (over 0.78).
- **Every steep land, not only Alpine biomes**: the rock rule (`awaken:alpine/slopes`: rock, scree, coarse, gravel; no snow)
  is prepended to `minecraft:overworld/biome_surface` for `#awaken:upland` at any height (`lithostitched/worldgen_modifier/alpine/
  slopes_surface.json`); the full rule `awaken:alpine/surface` (which adds snow) still runs for `#awaken:alpine` and for upland above
  y 150. Far Sight's shader already drew scree and rock by slope in every biome, so near now matches it.
- **Strata** (`AlpineSurface.strata`, material condition `awaken:strata` = `StrataCondition`): the rock block follows layers of
  three blocks in a cycle of eight (stone, andesite, stone, tuff, stone, granite, stone, andesite) and a thin calcite band (two
  thick, one in 31), tilted by a slow noise (about 4 blocks over 40) so cliffs have dipping strata and the vanilla ore blobs
  (white diorite streaks) are covered. Far Sight keeps its per-biome stone colour (the layers are too fine to show from afar).
- **Snow in layers** (`terrain.alpine.SnowDriftsFeature`, feature type `awaken:snow_drifts`, added at `top_layer_modification` to
  `#awaken:alpine` and `#awaken:upland`): in the band of about nine blocks under the snow line, in patches and thicker toward the
  line, never on ground steeper than 1.3, one to three of vanilla's snow layers where vanilla lets one survive
  (`AlpineSurface.driftLayers`; reads the chunk's heightmap ring, skips chunks under y 130).
- **Scree skirts and ledges** come from P1: gravel and stone grounds take their half slabs on the foot of every step.
- **Tests**: `ground_mountain_bands`, `ground_mountain_strata`, `ground_mountain_drifts`, `ground_mountain_far_parity`;
  `terrain_alpine_snow_and_rock` updated for the new slopes.
- **Not in P3**: gully planting (the Soft Land's P2 pebbles and boulders, vanilla spruce and the treeline filter cover it).

### 31.5 P4 Roads that sit in the land and P5 (blocked)
- **Built: bands** (`village.road.RoadPaint.paving`, held by `ground_road_bands`): the carriageway's ground was drawn block by block
  from a coin toss (`pct(wx, wz, 50)`); it now draws once per four-by-four patch (`pct(wx >> 2, wz >> 2, 50)`) with a ragged edge
  (one block in seven draws for itself), so the crown's grass and the wheel ruts' path read as bands along the road, and a town's
  setts stay a mix. The paving tables, the planner and the half step where a road climbs are unchanged (the road bench's
  fingerprint is a plan and does not move). The grass creeping over the road's edges is P0's.
- **Built: shallow cut and fill banks** (`village.road.RoadBanks`, new worlds with `awaken:awakened_ground`): past the
  1.6-block verge, grade toward the original land over seven blocks, rounded to half-block surfaces. Turf, podzol, sand,
  gravel (frost/highland) and mud (mire/jungle) take their Soft Land slabs. Only dry columns with at most seven blocks
  between the land and road are graded; steeper land retains the rocky embankments of §28.9. Streets, verges, town
  approaches, water crossings and viaducts keep their existing surfaces. The existing fringe and verge flowers remain.
- **Planned clearance, independent of paint order**: each chunk's complete structure references supply persisted road
  geometry and the other structures' bounding boxes before painting. No bank or its tree-clearing extension may enter
  another road's carriageway/verge, a waymark's two-block margin, or any other structure's box (conservatively including
  a settlement's whole raster, yards and fields). Where banks overlap, the nearest carriageway edge owns the column;
  ties use road key then leg index. The same mask guards the older rocky embankments. This replaces the proposed
  per-leg free-side flags: it uses the generation planner's saved footprints without laying extra neighbouring roads,
  rebuilding settlement plans, changing saved road data or depending on which planning cache is warm. Road lines,
  profiles, flags and their plan fingerprint are unchanged.
- **Natural height contract**: the canvas's optional `Land` is an immutable snapshot of this chunk's `OCEAN_FLOOR_WG`
  and `WORLD_SURFACE_WG` maps, which 26.3 stops updating at `TERRAIN`; the settlement writer refreshes only the final
  heightmaps. No noise columns or adjacent chunk height reads. Missing WG maps leave the old grading in place, without
  lazily priming from already-painted blocks. Flag off uses the unchanged old painter entry point.
- **Tests**: `ground_road_bank_ownership` covers a saved crossing road and a settlement yard across chunk boundaries,
  both structure orders, bank ownership ties and no added noise columns. `ground_road_bank_profile` holds cut/fill
  half-step profiles (at most one block per column on the tested four-block rises/falls), chunk order, frozen heightmaps,
  no bank slabs in a level carriageway/verge, flag-off equivalence and missing-height fallback. Existing road bands,
  rocky embankment and viaduct tests stay in force. No client or look tour was run; irregular steep land and kerb/pebble
  dressing remain a visual follow-up, not a claim of in-game approval.
- **P5**: the habitats (boulders are rock perches) and the footstep tags are built (§31.3); the rank palettes wait for the regions
  plan's level field (SPEC §21.10, on `pack/regions-plan`): `datapacks/awakened_ground/palette.json` already carries each
  entry's `ranks` slot, so the table is ready for it.

### 31.6 Where things stand
P0 (client, every world), P1 soft steps, P2 the floor and P3 mountains are built and tested. P4 has bands and protected
shallow banks; its kerb/pebble dressing and visual acceptance remain open. P5's rank palettes are open. New worlds only for P1-P5 (flag `awaken:awakened_ground`; P3 rides Awakened Alpine's).

## 32. Power casts (plan docs/power-anims/PLAN.md, page https://claude.ai/artifact/KBCT1me9LHaDXeUmGS5Xak; Euan approved all of it 2026-10-27: "Go with all recommendations")

Euan, playing, 2026-10-27: the beam "doesn't even come out of the core place it should... it's more so coming from the wrist";
the stamp "doesn't feel like you're actually stamping, with your foot... a small animation and a thump". The audit (59 casts,
mean 8.8 of 18) found one fault under all of them: family poses, effects at constant offsets, first person outside Hands, the
effect on the press tick, three camera paths, vanilla-remix sounds. Decisions D1-D14 are in the plan (section 6); all taken as
recommended: the whole system with a proof first (D1, D14: Euan's look at the proof before the families), the beam from the palm
fed from the core (D2), a 3-6 tick wind-up for 14 heavy powers (D3), the effect on the body's release frame on your screen for
the rest (D4), a stylised boot in first person (D5), one camera director (D6), authored layered sound (D7), small Lens light (D8),
a signature per power (D9), PAL and Bendable Cuboids stay (D10), mirrored for left hands (D11), PvP tells (D12), one comfort
setting (D13).

**P0, the proof (built 2026-10-27, branch pack/power-anims-plan): the stamp and the beam.**
- **Cast profiles** (`powers.fx.CastProfiles`): per power, its wind-up (server ticks), release tick, third-person clips (begin, hold
  loop and when it takes over, end), first-person clips and the vanilla fallback pose. Today: `shockwave` (wind-up 5, release 5,
  clip `stomp`, `fp_stomp`) and `beam` (release 5, `beam_gather` -> `beam_hold` -> `beam_hold_end`, `fp_beam_gather` -> `fp_beam_hold`).
  On the wire a profile id and a beat (BEGIN, RELEASE, END) ride the FxEvent's high flag bits (values from 128 up; below that is a
  `CastAnim` ordinal): `FxEvent.profile()`, `beat()`, `Builder.profile(id, beat)`. `Fx.at` marks a power's wind-up kind BEGIN and its
  release kind RELEASE; `Fx.end(.., 0)` marks END; `Fx.pose(c)` sends a new FxKind `POSE` (a beat with no particles). Tests:
  `power_cast_profiles` (every clip in both files, the release tick a key in both, the wire), `power_cast_windup`.
- **The stamp** (`KineticPowers.shockwave`): the press starts the knee (POSE BEGIN, sound `power.stomp_lift`) and a `shockwave_windup` Running
  (5 ticks; energy and cooldown on the press); the wave (`shockwaveRelease`) leaves when it ends, aimed where you look then, with the
  sound `power.stomp_plant`, a 50 ms hit-stop on the first body struck. Third person: clip `stomp` (power_casts.py: coil on the off leg,
  knee to hip height, a one-tick hang, plant at tick 5 = 250 ms, rebound; straight and bent twins). First person (`fp_casts.py`):
  `fp_stomp` (hands up, flare, drop with the plant) and a Hands world source `powers_stomp` (priority 350, `client.fx.CastLegs`): the
  stamping leg comes up from under the frame, hangs at its bottom edge and drives down on the plant; authored on screen in the hands'
  view space (a real stamp is out of frame). `FxRecipes.cone` starts the wave under the planted foot (`Anchors.PLANT`) with a flare, cracks,
  rubble, dust and sparks, and `CastFeel.thump`: the view dips 2.6 degrees (Arms' `CombatFeedback.kick`, 9 ticks), the field narrows 3%, and your
  hands and view hold 55 ms (`CombatFeedback.hold`). Any power's hit-stop now also holds the caster's own hands and view (`ClientPowers.onFeel`).
- **The beam** (`EnergyPowers.beam`): the gather pose and the light at the palm begin on the press (sounds `power.beam_gather`, then
  `power.beam_loop` every 10 ticks from tick 5, `power.beam_end` on release); the beam FX is deferred on the client to tick 5, the arm
  arriving on the aim (`FxClient.defer`, decision D4); a micro-recoil (`CastFeel.beamStart`) as the hold begins; the hands glow
  (`View.glow`) while it is held. Third person: `beam_gather` (both hands to the sternum, the main arm to the aim at tick 5), then
  `beam_hold` (braced, the off hand at the wrist, trembling), `beam_hold_end`. First person: `fp_beam_gather` (fists, `stow`) -> `fp_beam_hold`.
- **Cast points** (`client.fx.Muzzles`, `MuzzleLayer`): `Anchors.HAND` first asks `Muzzles.palm`: your own first person = the clip's fist
  (`FirstPerson.LAST_FIST_MAIN`, written by Hands each frame) plus a hand's depth, put into the world with the lens factor; a drawn body
  = the posed model's palm sampled by `MuzzleLayer` (like Arms' `BladeTraceLayer`: `translateToHand`, the torso and the main-side leg's
  sole for CORE and FOOT); an undrawn body = the stance's baked numbers (`proof/numbers.json`). Anything else keeps the old constant offsets.
  Every HAND-anchored effect of every power now starts at the drawn palm while a cast pose shows it.
- **Instant casts let go** (Euan, 2026-10-28: Snap Cable left both hands raised): a first-person hold loop belongs only
  to a channelled power. Snap Cable and Void Maw use the aim/reach gesture's finite version: after release the hands
  settle to rest over 6 ticks, and the clip ends one tick later. Landing, a missed target or a refused prediction needs
  no channel-end message to free the hands. Railgun and Telekinesis keep their held gestures until their channel ends.
  The runtime permits a hold hand-over only while a channel's held cast is live. `power_cast_profiles` checks the power
  mode, profile and first-person clip lifetime together.
- **A held pose has an owner** (Euan, 2026-11-09: two bare fists stuck up in a fight while he swung a weapon). A hold loop runs
  until something stops it and hides what you hold, and the record of "your cast" is one per entity, so tapping another
  power over a held Charged Shot left letting go aimed at the wrong cast, and the loop ran for good. `powers/fx/HeldHands`
  now owns it: each power key remembers the held cast it went down on, letting go ends that cast and no other, and one
  loop plays at a time. It lives only while a key or a running cast of the server's holds it (checked every tick), and a
  reset clears the keys. The server's end of a held cast always carries the END beat, on every way it can end
  (`Fx.end`, `Fx.chargeEnd`), so a charge that runs out with the key still down lets go too. Only a held cast's `hold1p` may
  be `loop: true` in the first-person clip files. `power_hold_pose_has_an_owner` runs every order of press, release,
  hand-over, server end and tick; `power_held_casts_say_they_ended` checks the end on the server's real path.
- **Hands additions**: `FpClipSet.FILES` also reads `fp_casts.json`; a clip may be `stow` (its fists are drawn even when a hand holds
  something, so a held weapon is out of view while you cast); `FirstPerson.View.stow`, `FirstPerson.LAST_FIST_MAIN/OFF`, `lastFistNanos`.
- **Sound**: `tools/art/specs/audio_powers.py` renders `sounds/powers/power_{stomp_lift,stomp_plant,beam_gather,beam_loop,beam_end}_*.ogg`
  (CC0 transients and the audio kit, audio_arms' mastering, window `power` -16 +-4 dBFS) and merges their events into
  `merge/powers/.../sounds.json`. Not yet listened to by Euan.
- **Tour**: `tools/autopilot/power-casts.txt` (`tools/tour-ci.sh ... PACK=feel`): both casts in first person, third person from the front and
  from behind, clips `pc_*`, filmed at `/tick rate 4` (the runner renders a few frames a second, so at full speed a 15-tick cast is two
  frames; the game's own tick rate slows the animation, the effects and the hit-stop together). It skips the opening and waits for the
  chunks before it builds its platform (the first runs toured the opening's balcony camera, then the sea). Run 40460497291, shots in
  `docs/power-anims/proof/p0/`: the beam leaves the main fist in first person and the palm in third person (halo orb at the hand, the
  fists lit); the stamp's hands rise and flare, the boot comes up into the bottom of the frame (it hid behind the hotbar, so its keys were
  raised afterwards: not re-toured), the wave starts at the foot with a flare, cracks, rubble and dust, and in third person the knee comes up
  and the foot plants before the dust. The held item leaves the frame the moment a stow clip starts (a pop, not a lowering).
- **Not in P0** (plan phases P1-P6): profiles for the other 57 casts, sound played on the clients at the muzzle, the Lens pulse and looks, the
  action camera's drop in the shoulder view, the off-hand/CORE light line, the release on the clip's frame for casters with latency, one
  "Cast animation" comfort setting. The weapon pops out of view when a stow clip starts (a lowering is polish).

**P1-P6 (built 2026-10-27, same branch): the other casts and the system under them.**
- **The table is data.** `tools/art/specs/power_cast_table.py` has one row per power (gesture and accents in third and first person, wind-up,
  screen moment, Lens look, origin, begin sound); `power_gestures.py` (third person, figure-term poses, straight and bent twins, the clipping check)
  and `fp_gestures.py` (first person: fist clips that stow what the hands hold, offset clips for quick casts) register the clips as `p_<power>`,
  `p_<power>_hold`, `p_<power>_end` and `fp_p_<power>`, `fp_p_<power>_hold`, with a `release` event on the profile's release tick;
  `power_gestures.write_table()` writes `data/awaken/powers/casts.json`, which `powers.fx.CastProfiles` reads (ids are the rows' order). 54 profiles;
  left on their family poses: `ground_slam`, `meteor_dive`, `hover`, `flight` (already designed) and `leap` (its landing slam is an explicit pose a
  profile would replace). 208 third-person clips (547 KB), 62 first-person clips.
- **Wind-ups run in `Casting`** (`windUp`): a profile with `windup` > 0 sends the pose beat (`Fx.pose`) and its begin sound on the press, spends energy
  and cooldown, and runs the power's own behaviour `windup` ticks later (a `<id>_windup` Running) aimed where you look then. The 14: Shockwave, Spire,
  Frost Nova 5; Terrain Rip, Collapse, Rampart, Legion, Citadel, Void Maw, Storm Call 6; Thunderclap 4; Brace 3; Gravity Flip, Drone Swarm 5.
  `windup` must equal the gesture's release tick (the generator asserts it).
- **Everything lands on the release frame, on every client** (D4): `FxClient.defer` holds each effect, beam and sound from a caster whose profile pose has
  not reached its release tick until it does (a ring of 64; the pose, the gathering light and the let-go never wait). An observer's first event of an instant
  power (its RELEASE beat) starts the pose, then the effect waits the same ticks. `Cast.sound` for a profile power sends an `FxKind.SOUND` event
  (`Fx.sound`: registry id in colour, volume in scale, pitch in aux) that each client plays at the release frame (`ClientLevel.playLocalSound`), so the
  server no longer plays those sounds on the press tick. `Fx.Emit.anim`/`noAnim` do nothing for a profile power (a family pose would replace its own);
  `Casting` adds a pose beat if a cast sent none.
- **The screen moment** (`CastFeel.MOMENTS`: thump_heavy, thump_light, recoil_light, release_big, push, breath, lift, none) plays on the release tick
  (`CastAnims.tick`) and at a channel's let-go (`endMoment`): your view kick and hold through Arms' `CombatFeedback`, the field of view through `FxScreen`, a
  flash and a Lens bloom pulse on the big ones; others feel it by distance (16 blocks). Reduced motion halves it; the camera shake setting turns the kicks off.
- **Lens** (`lens.client.LensClient.pulse`, `assets/awaken/lens/looks_powers.json`, `CastLens`): your own cast's look for its length (Flow, Foresight, Overload,
  Legion, Citadel, Void Maw; the beam and Prism Lance while held), laid over the place's own look and under your grade (`LensClient.accent`, §22 "A power's look",
  12 Nov: until then it replaced both, and the world dulled for as long as a beam was held), hidden while a story's or Arms' moment plays, only while Lens draws.
- **Beams from the core** (`origin: "core"` in a profile; Prism Lance): `Anchors.CORE` (the sternum sampled from the model; in your first person a point low in
  the view); its orb and beam start there.
- **Sound** (`tools/art/specs/audio_power_kits.py`): the 43 vanilla-remix `power.*` events are now authored (115 files, 1.4 MB): Kinetic weight, Velocity air,
  gravity low pulses, Energy rising light, Shadow ink, Mind pads, Architect set stone, Tech clicks and lasers, Spirit bells; `fail`, `learn` and `danger` stay.
  Not listened to by Euan yet.
- **Comfort** (D13): Full is the default; Reduced is the body's reduced-motion setting (halves the boot, the kick, the field's push and the tremble); Off is the
  existing "Cast animations" setting (no profile pose, no boot).
- **Tests**: `power_cast_profiles` (every name in both clip files, a key on the release tick, wind-up = release, moments, Lens looks, begin sounds),
  `power_cast_windup`, `power_cast_beats` (every profile power sends its beat and no family pose beside it); `power_fx_reach_matches_hits` gives the
  wind-up powers their ticks. Tour: `tools/autopilot/power-casts-2.txt`.
- **Open** (needs the game or Euan): the first-person gestures are authored from the numbers, not yet seen except the stamp and the beam; the weapon pops out of
  view on a fist clip; the sounds are unheard; `ground_slam`, `meteor_dive`, `hover`, `flight` and `leap` first person and the Lens look timings are untouched.

**Charged Shot: the ball between the hands (Euan 2026-10-30: "hands higher and ball shoots from them ... the sounds are so underwhelming").**
It is one of the starter powers, so it is a first impression. Its charge is now a ball of lightning held up between both hands, and the shot leaves
from that ball.
- **One point for the server and every pose** (`powers.fx.CastPoints.ball`, profile `origin: "ball"`): from the eyes, 0.58 along the look and 0.17
  down the view's up, centred. The bolt (`Bolts.fire`), the muzzle burst and the let-go flash all start there, at every charge and pitch; the old
  `EnergyPowers.hand` (0.35 to the right) is no longer used by Charged Shot.
- **First person** (`fp_gestures.py` `lightning_ball`): the fists cup low, then lift to `BALL` (±0.25, -0.17, -0.48 in the hand pass's view
  space; at ±0.15 the tour showed the fists meeting in the middle and hiding the orb, since the hands draw over the world). The palms' midpoint (`Muzzles` adds 0.10 of depth) is exactly the ball point, and it sits about 40% down from the centre of the screen,
  clear of the hotbar. The hold trembles (`fp_p_charged_shot_hold`). A new profile field, `end1p` (`fp_p_charged_shot_end`), drives both fists
  straight out on the let-go; `CastAnims.release` plays it in place of the hold.
- **Third person** (`power_gestures.py` `lightning_ball`, `BALL_HOLD`): both arms follow the look (aimed). The palms are 0.34 apart and their
  midpoint is the ball point at a level look, within about a sixth of a block at 20 degrees up or down; the arms turn at the shoulders, not the eyes.
  This was fitted with the rig's forward kinematics at the 0.9375 player scale. Levels 3 and 5 keep the same hold: level 3 adds the family accent,
  level 5 a lower, wider stance and a two-handed spear's hurl as the let-go. The level-5 body line now reads "Both hands drive the ball out like a
  thrown spear, the whole body behind it." A profile's third-person let-go now starts on the release tick (it used to wait 2 ticks for a release
  cast that profiles never send), so the push lands with the bolt. While a ball profile plays, whatever the hands held is not drawn
  (`CastAnims.emptyHands`, a render-state modifier registered last, after Arms fills the hands; the inventory is untouched), and for 10 ticks
  after, while the push settles. In your own first-person view the orb at the ball counts as held in the hand (`FxRender.ownHand`): drawn small
  and never faded for being near the eye (the near fade had hidden it whole, 0.58 from the eye).
- **The orb follows the drawn hands** (`Anchors.BALL`, `Muzzles.ball`): your fists' midpoint in first person, the sampled palms' midpoint on a drawn
  body, otherwise the server's point at the frame's look. Ladder looks placed `"at": "hand"` (Coil's orbit, Thunder Lance's sigil) follow a
  profile's origin (`LadderFx.anchor`). At a field of view other than 70, your first-person orb (drawn by the 70-degree hand pass) and the world
  point drift apart a little, as with any hand-anchored effect.
- **Sound, layered** (`audio_power_kits.py`, `power.lightning_*`, original synthesis):
  - `lightning_charge`: a 1.8 s build that rises about 14 dB to full at 1.5 s and then holds. A climbing arc hum, a rising whine, crackle that
    thickens from a few sparks to a storm, air and a sub swell. A new profile field, `holdSound`, plays it from the ball on every client through
    `HoldSound`, which follows the hands and cuts it with a two-tick fade on the let-go.
  - `lightning_full`: a bright ring and snap one tick before full.
  - `lightning_release`: a crack, torn air, a zap and a push thump, louder and lower the more it was charged.
  - `lightning_boom`: added under a release past half charge.
  - `lightning_sizzle`: the bolt's hiss along its flight (`Bolts.Bolt.fly`, every 3 ticks).
  - `lightning_thunder`: a crack and two or three rolling swells where it lands (`Bolts.Bolt.hitSound`, louder with charge; it takes the place of the
    blast sound).
  - Volley fires from the ball too and uses the release and a lighter thunder.
- **Tests**: `power_cast_ball`: at pitch -30, 0 and 30, after 6 and 30 ticks, the muzzle burst is at the ball and centred, and each bolt's first
  step starts there. `power_cast_profiles` also holds `end1p`, `holdSound` and the origin names.
- **Tour**: `tools/autopilot/charged-shot.txt` (a CI look tour, PACK=feel) films the charge and the shot in first person, from the side and from
  three quarters in front. Third person is turned round the player by the tours-only client command `/awaken fx sidecam <degrees>` (0 is off): it
  turns the camera angles before third person pulls back along them, so the camera orbits the player.
- **With cast animations off**, your own key press now starts the profile as well, the way it already did for everyone watching you. Its fallback
  pose, held sound and screen moment run; the first-person clips still follow the setting, and the boot checks the setting itself. The held sound
  starts with the charge orb (`FxRecipes.startCharge`), so Volley, which never charges, has none.

### 32.N The next level (plan docs/powers-next/PLAN.md, build ledger docs/powers-next/BUILD.md, page https://claude.ai/artifact/W1U5AFoQMizBjLxbUg8VHv; Euan approved all of it 2026-11-10: "Go ahead with the full thing")

The film of 10 Nov (`tools/autopilot/powers-next-before.txt`, 17 casts in first person) showed why casts read weak: the arm was one
straight box, wind-ups happened off screen, a weapon popped out of the hand and back, and most powers ended as the same ring and flash.
What follows replaces that. Nothing here changes what a power does to a number unless it says so.

**The arm** (module `anims`; clip schema 2, `FpClipSet.SCHEMA`; schema 1 files still load).
- A fists clip may say `"arm": true`: each fist key's three spare values are then how the arm would lie (pitch and yaw, degrees, view
  space, 0 0 straight ahead) and the wrist's roll. **The arm drawn is still vanilla's: one straight box, its sleeve end out of sight**
  (Euan, 10 Nov 2026, on the first film, where an elbow and a separate upper arm read as a broken arm: "keep the arms closer to vanilla
  style and not break them"). It comes to the fist from under the frame's corner on its own side (`side * 0.48, -0.84, -0.53`), as it
  always did; the keyed lie turns it toward itself by at most 38 degrees and never so far that the far end of the box would show; a fist
  held too high for that is reached by drawing the same arm longer, at most 1.6 times, about its shoulder (`WorldBody.drawFist`). There
  is no elbow joint and never a second piece. The roll turns the arm's front. Without `arm` the arm is exactly as before.
- `"mainMoves"` / `"offMoves"`: that hand's track is offsets (it moves what the hand holds) while the other hand is fists. This is the
  left-hand cast: the off hand acts, the main hand keeps the weapon and lowers it into a guard. A weapon's grip follows the move.
- `"ease": true` with `"stow"`: a two-handed cast puts the weapon away over 2.5 ticks and brings it back over 3, never a pop. The weapon
  session's draw never plays when a cast gives the weapon back.
- `"light"`: `[tick, chargeMain, heatMain, chargeOff, heatOff, ease]` keys. `FirstPerson.View` carries `armMain/armOff` (pitch, yaw,
  roll, weight), `lightMain/lightOff` (charge, heat, weight) and `stowEase`.
- **Arm layers** (`anims.client.ArmLayers`, public): anything may draw on the first-person arm after its skin, in the arm cube's own
  space (x from `x0/16` to `x1/16`, y `-2/16` at the shoulder end to `10/16` at the hand, z `±2/16`). `ArmLayers.add(Layer)`;
  `Layer.draw(Arm, PoseStack, SubmitNodeCollector)`; `Arm` says which arm, whether it holds something, and the light keyed on it.
  The arm's armour (§44.1, `core.client.FirstPersonDress`) is drawn first, stretched with the arm, and `Arm.dressed` says it was:
  what a layer puts on the skin may be under a plate. A layer's `prepare(Arm)` runs before the arm is dressed.
- **The light on what you wear** (`powers.client.fx.ArmourLight`; Euan, 10 Nov 2026: the light must "map to the shape of the armor
  itself and the arm, instead of sitting below it and looking glitchy", with "custom styling for each armor piece for the different
  powers"). On an arm that wears armour the light is never drawn on the skin. Two things pass through `FirstPersonDress` (§12):
  - `glow(rgb, amount)`, set by the light before the arm is dressed and cleared after. The armour answers in its own shader: for that
    draw its accent is the type's colour and it flares by the amount (`ArmourClient.dressArm`), so the piece's edges and what glows of
    itself take the colour.
  - `surface(limb)`: the shape of what the limb wears (the armour gives the worn chestplate's arm mesh, its texture and the set's id).
    The light cuts it into cells, one a texel of every face, once a shape. Each cell plays a part read from the set's own texture
    (its colour half and its material half): **cloth**, **plate**, a **line** (a trim: bright glossy metal, or the set's accent
    colour wherever it is painted, that is a rim or a strip a texel or two wide; the middle of a wide one is plate or cloth again)
    or what **glows of itself** (material blue over 0.25). Each cell knows how far down the arm it is (0 at the shoulder end, 12.5 at the fingertips) and where it sits across its
    own face.
  The light is drawn cell by cell on the faces themselves, 0.003 off them (faces turned from the eye left out), with a soft additive
  spill round the lit lines only (when every lit cell spilt, the spills added up to a pale wash over the whole arm). Lines cover 0.18 + 0.55 of their light, 0.78 at most, and go no more than 0.7 of the way from the type's colour to its
  white core until a release (a line that is a wide plate, lit white by a passing pulse, was a blown-out patch); cloth and plate
  are tinted, never painted out (0.62 of
  theirs, no floor), and take the light by their own painting (times 0.5 + 0.65 of the texel's brightness, or of its darkness for a
  set whose grain is -1), so the piece keeps its own colours. The armour's own answer is small while the light is on (0.12 of the
  heat: its edge light takes the type's colour) and flares only at a release (1.2 for each point of heat over 0.9). Two films
  taught this: in the first every lit cell spilt glow and the arm washed pale; in the second the armour flared all through a cast
  and wide cuff plates, being lines, were painted out. Rule for every type: **the set's lines carry the type, and the type's motif lies on the rest one
  face at a time**, moving the way it moves on bare skin (to the fist, or back from the hand). Kinetic: the lines pulse, a seam
  wanders down each face. Heat: the hand's end burns, the lines glow hot, embers in the rest. Velocity: streaks down every line and
  one lane a face. Flight: motes, the lines pale. Gravity: falling bands, ink at the wrist with the lines lit over it. Energy and
  Prism: a pulse down the lines, a forking vein a face. Charge: lightning crawling the lines in jumps. Shadow: ink from the hand, the
  lines lit in it. Mind and Soul: rings round the wrist across all they cross. Architect: the lines inked in, a rule every third row.
  Tech: the lines lit and a scan row sweeping. Spirit: tongues from the hand, taller on the lines. Frost: rime on the lines first,
  then crystals across the rest.
  **A set's record** (`ArmourLight.SETS`, one for each of the 29 since every arm was finished on 11 Nov 2026) says how its
  materials take the light. Four gains, for cloth, plate, lines and glowing parts, and seven ways:
  `lead`, how many rows its lines run ahead of the rest (metal conducts); `soak`, how much its cloth holds a glow where the light has
  been (hide and cloth); `shimmer`, how much what glows of itself flickers (crystal, a signal); `grain`, +1 its bright texels take
  more light, -1 its dark ones (the light sits in bark's cracks and bone's hollows); `tips`, how much the parts that stand off the
  arm light late and bright (a cell more than four texels from the arm's middle is a fin, a feather or a spur: the light has to run
  out along it, 0.8 of a row a texel, and it burns up to 0.35 brighter); `ripple`, how much a wave of shade runs down its plate and
  cloth (rows of scales and feathers); `glitter`, how often an unlit texel where the light has been catches it for a moment (mail's
  links, rivets, star metal). The records, by what each arm is made of:
  E: Wildhide (hide: soak 0.22, lead 0.5), Bellguard (bell bronze, rim after rim: lead 2), Rootwarden (bark: grain -1, resin 1.3),
  Amberwing (a jerkin: soak 0.14). D: Beastbound (bone: grain -1, tips 0.7), Cleftrunner (cloth under strips: soak 0.16),
  Lanternlight (a robe over mail: glitter 0.6, glass 1.3), Bladeward (rivets: glitter 0.35, lead 2), Hornlord (horn: grain -0.6,
  lead 2). C: Gatewrought (lead 1.5, soak 0.12), Vaultbreaker (steel: lead 2.5), Frostwalker (hide: soak 0.2, shimmer 0.6), Sunward
  (cloth under gold: soak 0.14, shimmer 0.5), Shardcrown (crystal: shimmer 1, glow 1.3). B: Veilwoven (a veil of threads: lead 2,
  lines held to 0.65 so they don't flood), Deepcarapace (shell: grain -1, tips 0.8), Cloudrunner (feathers: tips 1, ripple 0.6),
  Tidebreaker (wet mail and fins: tips 0.8, ripple 0.4, glitter 0.5), Hollowheart (bone: grain -1, tips 0.7). A: Lordscale (scales:
  ripple 0.6, lead 2, seams 1.3), Leviathan (fins: tips 0.9, ripple 0.4), Galewing (feathers: tips 1, ripple 0.6), Halo Choir (ivory
  and gold: lead 2, shimmer 0.5, glitter 0.3), Dreamsteel (shimmer 0.8, tips 0.6). S: Sovereign Weave (its threads carry it: lead
  2.5, ripple 0.3), Starfall (star metal: glitter 0.8, lead 2), Riftwalker (plates off the sleeve: tips 0.8, glitter 0.4),
  Nightcourt (court leather and a half-cloak that hangs: soak 0.18, tips 0), Signal's Echo (the Signal runs through it already:
  its glow at 1.0 and shimmer 0.7, so the light flickers and never doubles). Living parts on an arm (Lanternlight's lanterns,
  Veilwoven's ribbons) are lit where the arm's own mesh has them at rest, which is how first person draws them.
  `tools/art/arm_light_preview.py` draws the same cells and rules off line, a sheet a set; its `light` and
  `ArmourLight.light` are kept line for line. A dresser that gives no shape gets the stopgap: the skin's light drawn 0.16 nearer the
  eye along the line of sight.
- **The light** (`powers.client.fx.ArmLight`, an arm layer): the power's type shows on the skin itself. One procedural pattern a style
  (15), drawn on the skin's own pixel grid (4 x 12 a face, 3 wide on slim arms) 0.004 above it, running toward the fist as the charge
  climbs, with a soft halo. A cast with no light track gets one from its age against its release tick. Powers that sit on you (Barrier,
  Mend, Brace, Nanite Skin, Cloak, Bulwark, Overload, Hoarfrost Lances) keep the arms lit for as long as they last, and hold a resting
  fist in view when the main hand is empty. Blocky fists, no fingers.
- Authoring: `tools/art/specs/fp_casts2.py` writes `assets/awaken/fp_clips/fp_casts2.json` (read last, so a clip there replaces the
  older one of the same name). One-handed casts key only the left fist. Its rules are checked on build: every pose held two ticks is
  on screen above the hotbar; no hand sits in the middle fifth of the view for more than two ticks; two hands never start on the same
  tick; a strike overshoots and settles. 77 clips authored (207 with takes). The three held aims (Charged Shot, Prism Lance, Railgun)
  keep the fist places their first clips gave them, because the ball, the core and the rail's line are measured from the hands; only
  Shockwave's standing stamp is still its earlier clip (a stamp is the foot's, and its run and air ways are authored).

**Takes.** Every authored cast has three takes (`_t2`, `_t3`: the same cast with its path and timing a little different, never its
release pose). The client picks one that isn't the last one it used for that power and sends it with the cast, so everyone sees the
same take.

**Ways** (`powers.fx.Ways`: STAND 0, RUN 1, AIR 2). The client says how the body was moving at the press; the server keeps the claim
if it was true within 5 ticks (`Casting.WAY_GRACE`). The cast payload's `keys` carries the way in bits 4-5 and the take in 6-7; an FX
event's flags carry them in bits 12-13 and 14-15. A way picks its own clip (`base__run`, `base__air`, falling back to the base) and may
change the power's shape, never its damage:
- Shockwave: at a run 35% longer and 40% narrower; stamped down out of the air, a ring all round you at 60% of the range.
- Haymaker: at a run the body is thrown 35% further and flatter; out of the air it is driven into the ground and those within 2.6
  blocks are thrown back.
- Spirit Palm: at a run it reaches 6 blocks (4.5) and throws 30% further; out of the air the body goes down and the print bursts under
  it for half on everything within 2.5.
- Nova: out of the air it goes off beneath you, 15% wider, and lifts you.
- Frost Nova: at a run the ring lands three blocks ahead; out of the air it is 30% tighter and holds half again as long.
- Updraft: cast in the air, the column starts at the ground beneath you and still carries its full height above you.
There is no timing in any of this: the way is whatever you were already doing.

**The press buffer.** A power key pressed within 3 ticks of its cooldown's end is kept and cast on the first tick it can be.

**A moment each** (`CastFeel.POWER`): 57 powers have their own screen moment at the release (view kick with yaw, field of view,
hold, flash) in place of the eight shared ones. Camera shake and reduced motion still scale them.

**Signatures** (`powers.client.fx.Signatures`): after a power's shared recipe has drawn, its signature adds the one thing only that
power has. Built so far: Frost Nova (rime runs out along the ground and stands up as crystals), Thunderclap (lightning along the floor),
Telekinesis (a line of force from the palm, the ground lifting round what is held), Spirit Palm (the handprint goes through the body and
out the far side), Barrier (a curved plate of hexes that turns with your look), Mend (petals climbing round you), Shadow Step (your shape
left behind in ink), and the five earned powers (§50.11). The rule for the rest: no power's main effect may be only a ring, a flash and a
number. Signatures are drawn, never real, inside the effect budget, and off at the Minimal effects level.

**Open** (in the ledger): third person has no takes or ways yet; the remaining powers' signatures.

## 33. Trails (optional guidance for everything; plan docs/trails/PLAN.md, page https://claude.ai/artifact/QvuzZLthjqdy1dmXFgNit4; Euan approved all ten recommendations 2026-10-27)

Euan: "...the moment you place your hearth, you unlock a whole hearth discovery program, ... that you don't have to follow.
... you can click it, and then it creates the side checklist ... so that whenever you don't know what to do at all, you can
always go in there and find ... the things that are available for me to do right now ... not just for the hearth, really
plan this for everything." Module `trails` (`dev.awaken.trails`), `core.api.TrailsApi`, docs/modules/trails.md.

- **A trail** is one JSON file, `data/<ns>/awaken/trail/<id>.json` (schemaVersion 1, `TrailDef`): `title`, `area` (home, weapons,
  gates, powers, body, world, deep, story), `blurb`, `weight` (catalogue order), `opens` (tokens, all must hold), `after`
  (trails to finish first), `order` (`free` or `linear`), `steps` and a `finish` (a line and a share of a level, 0.05 by
  default, paid once through the Discovery XP source). A step has an `id`, `text` (at most 76 characters), `done` tokens, optional
  `show` tokens (hidden until they hold), `where` (a kind of place for the compass), `hint` (at most 140), `tip` (a tip id offered
  once when the step is current) and `manual` (a step with no `done` must be manual: the player marks it).
- **Tokens** (`Conditions`): the `Requirements` tokens, `holds:<item>`, `count:<counter>:<n>`, `a|b` alternatives, and the families
  other modules add through `TrailsApi.condition(prefix, test)`. The Hearth's (`HearthTrails`): `room:<kind>`, `rooms:<kind>:<n>`,
  `grade:<snug|fine|grand>`, `hearth_tier:<n>`, `forge_tier:<n>`, `settlers:<n>`, `pads:<n>`, `duty:<n>`, `cottage`, `named`,
  `tip:<marker>`, `furniture:<name>`, and the place `hearth`. Arms' (`ArmsTrails`): `style:<id>`, `styles:<n>`, `arms:issued|marked|lordforged`,
  `armstier:<n>`, and the place `quartermaster` (Hale). An unknown token is never met; `trail_defs_valid` fails the build on one.
- **State** (`TrailState`, attachment `awaken:trails`, schemaVersion 1, kept through death, per player): trails opened, finished,
  hidden, the followed one, and `latched` steps ("trail|step"): a step seen done stays done. Progress is read from the world, so
  a step done before the trail opened is ticked at once.
- **The engine** (`TrailEngine`): every two seconds per player, staggered, it opens the trails whose tokens hold (at most
  **2** announced a play-day, one IMPORTANT toast "A new trail: X. Open the Journal (K) to follow it.", topic `trail`; the rest open
  quietly), latches done steps, finishes a trail when every step is done (an AMBIENT toast filed in the Journal, the reward, the
  Director's new-thing tick), and sends the screen's copy (`TrailPayloads.View`) when it changed. A trail whose only unmet
  tokens are a rank or a level shows as a silhouette ("Opens at D-rank") and files a "What waits" entry; any other lock keeps it unseen.
- **Where it shows**: K, Journal page, **TRAILS** (order -38, under TRACKING): "What you can do now" (at most 3 rows, each the next step
  with Follow), and **All trails ›** opening a browse view in the same section (area chips, a card per trail with its pips, Steps,
  Follow, Not for me, silhouettes last). Following puts the trail on the **task card** (`Checklist.registerLeading`, asked before even the first-hour moves card: the trail,
  every step done plus up to four to do, a linear trail two; the card counts the done ones; a step longer than the card wraps over up to three lines, `signal.ui.TaskWrap`, with key caps kept in the line, seen on the third tour) and its current step on the **Now line** (priority 55). Only Follow changes the HUD;
  one trail is followed at a time, and the Armoury's Track gives the card up (`TrailsApi.unfollow`). "Anything for me?"
  (`Advice`) names the best next step.
- **Catalogue shipped** (25 trails): Home (7): Set Your Fire, Your Hearth, A Room for Everything, Your Village, The Forge, Trophies and
  Echoes, The Training Grounds. Weapons (4): Your First Weapon, Finding Patterns, Making Your Next Weapon, Boss Weapons. Body (3):
  Moving Like a Hunter, The Line, Wings. Gates (1): Your First Gate. World (2): Out in the Commons, Wayfarers and Camps. Deep (5):
  The Veil, Dreams, The Precursors, The Well, The Delver's Pick (§34.4). Not yet written: Powers, Story, Villages, Beasts and Lairs, Digging Down, Rumours.
- **Counters added** for steps (docs/COUNTERS.md): `rested`, `armoury_forge`, `armoury_opened`, `blueprint_copies`, `weapons_attuned`,
  `weapons_raised`, `patterns_bought`, `patterns_from_gates`, `patterns_from_people`, `patterns_from_stands`, `patterns_from_villages`.
- **Admin**: `/awaken admin trails list | open <id> | follow <id> | done <id> | reset`. Autopilot: `trails now|browse [area]|open`,
  tour `tools/autopilot/trails-journal.txt`.
- **Tests** (`trail_`): `trail_defs_valid` (every shipped trail passes the checks, and the checks catch what they should),
  `trail_progress_derived`, `trail_open_once`, `trail_follow_card`, `trail_silhouette`, `trail_hearth_tokens`.
- **Seen** (CI tour `trails-journal`, 2026-10-27): the TRAILS section in the Journal (what you can do now, Follow and Stop, the browse view by area with
  steps and hints), and the rail's unread count rising as trails open. **Not built / unverified**: the task card and Now line with a followed trail on a real
  screen (the first tour caught the first-hour card covering it; fixed, and the second tour showed the trail on the card ticking as steps were done; the card's count was off until every done step was sent, fixed and tested, not re-toured; the Now line shows the followed step below the Hale and camp lines, as designed at priority 55); a step's `{key}` caps; a `tip` (none shipped yet); several
  followed trails; the Powers, Story and the remaining World trails; the Armoury's Track as a step type.

## 38. Gate Worlds (every gate floor a world of its own; page https://claude.ai/artifact/T6AdCwtMo7vvpDiNA2wJRf; Euan approved all seven recommendations 2026-10-28: "Go with all recomentations, this is great")

Euan: gates feel like block rooms; make each floor feel like entering a new world, "holy shit, jaw dropped", every kid's dream
RPG. The plan: 90 worlds (per theme two everyday, a deep one, a wonder and a secret one, plus 15 rare), four moods each,
about 230 new blocks, the seven-layer atmosphere checklist, a different world on every floor, darker shaped light, Gate Air in
Lens (built by the Lens owner from this section), an open-sky gate dimension (Stage 3), per-world looks for each theme's
monsters plus 15 signature creatures (through the mob forms work), and the RPG layer (the Atlas of Gates in the Codex,
keepsakes, title cards, the journey down, a rule per world, secrets, rarity, theme mastery). Built in stages, each merged and
switchable on its own: 0 foundation, 1 the Bell Crypt complete (Euan's go or stop), 2 the other E themes, 3 D themes and the
open sky, 4 C themes, 5 B and A themes and the rare worlds, 6 polish. Module `gates` (`dev.awaken.gates.worlds` and
`dev.awaken.gates.world`). The fights, keys, shrines, Lords, twists and modifiers inside stay what they are.

### 38.1 Room for height: plots (content version 6)

- `GatePlan.CONTENT_VERSION` is **6**. A version 6 gate gives every floor its own **plot** (`Plots`): the cell's four
  256 x 256 quadrants, each an upper tier (y 128..255) and a lower tier (y 0..127), eight plots for the six main and two annex
  floors a gate can have. The dimension stays 256 tall. Version 5 and older gates keep the stacked 32-block bands
  (`Cells.floorY`, `Cells.floorAtY`) exactly; nothing they built moves.
- **Assignment** is a function of the saved plan only (`FloorBuilder.plotFor`): floors in order (main 1..n, then annex 1 and 2;
  the ritual and the trials have one), tall worlds first get a whole quadrant column (y 0..255) while every floor still fits
  (n floors with k tall use n + k tiers of 8, at most 4 tall), earliest first; the rest take upper tiers, then lower ones.
  Whether a floor is tall is saved with its pick (`FloorWorld.tall`), so plots never move even if a recipe goes away.
- **Today's rooms in a plot**: a floor with no world builds exactly the rooms version 5 built (same seed, same rooms, same
  blocks), standing at its plot's bottom + 48 (`Plots.ROOMS_BASE`) with its grid at the quadrant's slot + 1. Unentered version 5
  gates are rebuilt as version 6 on the next start, as every gate update has; a gate someone entered keeps its version.
- **Finding things**: `GateLayout.floorAt(x, z, y)` (cell-local x and z, absolute y) checks the plots on version 6 and the bands
  before. `FloorLayout` carries its `plot` (null before 6), the y range it paints (`yLo`, `yHi`, `paints(y)`; tests and tools
  filter a chunk's blocks by floor with it), and on a world floor its `places`, `world`, `mood`, `biome`, `air` and `model`.
  `Where` asks `roomAt(x, y, z)`. The fall check is unchanged (below y 0 puts you back at the floor's entrance).
- **An instance keeps to itself** (checked 2026-10-28 after a 42 s freeze on Euan's server, likely overworld planning around
  a gate's coordinates; the roads work audits that side): a world floor is built and lit only from its saved plan, inside its
  cell, in the gate dimension. Worlds call no other module with a position, add no chunk tickets of their own (a gate's
  build still loads 7 x 7 chunks at its entrance and 5 x 5 at the next floor's, as before), and never read or load a
  chunk that isn't loaded (the Flood fills a chunk when it loads). World biomes have no features, carvers, spawns or tags,
  and the gate generator places no structures, so nothing else plans in them. A floor plans in under 50 ms and carves a
  chunk in under 4 ms on average (tests). A new gate takes the **lowest free cell**, not the first freed, so live gates
  stay close to the dimension's origin (cells are 1,024 apart, 64 to a row).
- **The place map** (`PlaceMap`): which place (room) holds a floor-local spot, in 4-block cells, each with a ground place and
  optionally an upper place from a split height (a gallery over an aisle). World floors answer "which room is this?" with it;
  rooms floors keep the 16-block slot grid (`PlaceMap.ofSlots` gives the same answer, cell for cell). Places are `Room`s, so
  `Where`, `Rooms`, `Pressure` and the Rig keep their answer type; a place's `gx..gh` are its bounding slots.

### 38.2 Worlds, recipes and engines

- **A recipe** is `data/<ns>/gate_worlds/<theme>/<world>.json` (`GateWorld`, `schema` 1), id `<ns>:<theme>/<world>`:
  `theme`, `name`, `line` (the Atlas line, plain speech), `tier` (everyday, deep, wonder, secret, rare), `rarity` (common 10,
  uncommon 4, rare 1, mythic 0.2 as weights), `kind` (the engine), `tall`, `roles` (`floor`, `boss`), `mastery` (floors of the
  theme cleared that open it early; default deep 4, wonder 10, others 0), `weight`, `enabled`, `biome`, `moods` (`id`, `name`,
  `weight`, `biome`), `params` (numbers for the engine) and the dressing (`blocks` by role, `hero`, `life`, `residents`, `sound`,
  `events`, `rule`, `secrets` with `leads_to`, `keepsake`, `signature`). The loader (`GateWorlds`, a server reload listener)
  skips a recipe with a problem and logs why; `gateworlds_recipes` fails when any file doesn't load or names a biome that
  doesn't exist or the gates dimension doesn't list.
- **Shape is stable**: a released world's `kind`, `params` and `hero` never change. A new shape is a new world (or a content
  version), because a floor someone stands on is rebuilt from its recipe after a restart.
- **Engines** (`WorldEngine`, by kind; `WorldEngine.of`): a pure, deterministic sculptor. `plan(Ctx)` turns the plan, floor,
  plot, recipe, mood, seed and variation (0..2) into a `FloorLayout` with its places, place map, light, Gate Air data and a
  `WorldModel` that carves any chunk of the plot on worldgen threads. A plan that can't make a floor complete on foot (every
  place, key, cache and the end reachable from the arrival) returns null: the next variation is tried, and after three, or on
  an exception, or for a kind this build has no engine for, or a role the recipe doesn't hold (a Lord's floor needs `boss`),
  the floor is today's rooms in its plot. Stage 0 ships no engines (every floor is rooms); Stage 1 adds the Bell Crypt's.
- **Biomes per world** (`GateBiomeSource`): on version 6 a floor's plot shows its `biome` (the mood's, else the world's, else
  the theme's), sampled by height, so fog, sky, particles and sound follow the world with nothing synced. Every world biome is
  listed in `data/awaken/dimension/gates.json` and gets a Lens look (`looks_gates.json`, by the Lens owner).

### 38.3 The world director and the Atlas

- **When**: `GateService.create` dresses every new plan (`GateWorlds.dress`) before the gate is recorded, and the start-up
  rebuild of unentered older gates dresses the rebuilt plan; picks are saved in the plan (`worlds`: `area`, `floor`, `world`,
  `mood`, `tall`). Never dressed: plans before version 6, the story's ritual, the Ascension trials, plans already dressed.
  Server switches: `gateWorlds` (default on; off, new gates build rooms), `gateWorldsOff` (world ids never picked) and
  `gateOpenLands` (default off since 12 Nov: no open world is picked, 38.11).
- **Picking** (pure: same plan, Atlas and catalogue give the same picks; its own random stream, so the Director's rolls are
  unchanged): per floor, the open worlds of the floor's theme (the annex's floors use the annex theme): enabled, not switched
  off, not secret, holding the floor's role, and open to the gate's rank (the theme's rank + 1 for deep, + 2 for wonder) or by
  mastery (the owner has cleared that many of the theme's floors). From B rank a rare world replaces the pool on about one floor
  in 25. Never the same world twice in a gate while another fits, never the world you were last in; weight = recipe weight x
  rarity x 1 / (1 + times you've been there)^2; the mood the same way by mood weight and times in that mood. A floor nothing
  fits stays rooms. Secret worlds are reached by finding their secret, never rolled.
- **The Atlas** (`GateAtlas`, attachment `awaken:gate_atlas`, schema 1, kept through death, per player): per world the first
  play-day, arrivals, arrivals per mood, secrets found and the keepsake; floors cleared per theme (mastery); the last 12
  arrivals (world#mood); creatures met. Filled on arrival (`WorldsLive.arrive`) and on an ordinary floor cleared
  (`WorldsLive.cleared`). The director reads the gate owner's (online) Atlas; friends each fill their own.
- **Arrival** (`WorldPayloads.Arrival`): on arriving on a floor the client is told its world, name, mood, rarity, tier, line,
  whether it's a first find, and its Gate Air data with the world position of its floor-local origin (an empty world clears).
  `GateWorldClient` holds it: `current()`, `air()`, `origin()` (null and empty off a world floor or outside the gates).
- **Gate Air data** (`FloorAir`, floor-local, sent with the arrival): lights (position, colour, reach, strength; at most 96),
  shafts (from, to, radius, colour, strength; 24), mist layers (height, thickness, colour, density; 6) and still water planes
  (height and rectangle; 12). Lens's Gate Air reads it each frame: mist takes the colour of the nearest 32 lights, 12 shafts
  are marched, still water reflects; at most 1.5 ms a frame on Cinematic at 1440p on the M4, off on Swift and with Lens off.
  Every world must pass the atmosphere checklist without it.

### 38.4 Tests and where things stand

- **Tests** (`gateworlds_`): `gateworlds_plots` (every floor of 400 varied plans inside its own plot and found again at its
  arrival; no shared plots; version 5 bands unchanged; tall plots granted only while every floor fits; a Double Gate's annex
  floors show the annex theme), `gateworlds_same_rooms` (version 6 builds version 5's rooms on every floor and paints the same
  blocks, moved; a few room pieces pick a block's variant by its height, such as bookshelf or sodden shelf, ore, obsidian and honey, so
  only those pairs may swap on a moved floor of a new gate, and gates already open never move), `gateworlds_place_map`, `gateworlds_recipes`, `gateworlds_director` (determinism, back to back, twice in a
  gate, Lords' floors, secrets, mastery opening the deep world and the wonder, worlds switched off, saving plans and the Atlas).
- **Stage 0** (built 2026-10-28): plots, the frame, the place map, recipes and their loader, per-world biomes, the engine
  interface, the director, the Atlas and the arrival payload. No recipes ship yet, so every floor is today's rooms in its plot.
- **Stage 1** (built 2026-10-28; its gaps closed the same evening: the swinging bells, the air, the Bell Tower set, the
  signature hook): the world floor contract (38.5), the Bell Crypt's blocks and its four floor worlds (38.6); tests
  `gateworlds_bell_recipes`, `gateworlds_belfry`, `gateworlds_ossuary`, `gateworlds_field` and `gateworlds_shaft`; the
  arrival, the journey down and the Atlas page (38.7), test `gateworlds_atlas_view`; the live layer (38.8): events, the
  bell rule, the Ringer, residents' looks, secrets, keepsakes and the catch, tests `gateworlds_live` and
  `gateworlds_catch`, and every world's test also checks its marks (each handbell stands where it's marked, each secret
  has something to find, the Flood's basins are dry and walled in) and that each of its recipe's secrets is placed on
  some floor.
- **Stage 2** (built 2026-10-28): the cave engine, the four cave themes' blocks, dress, rules, events, nooks, secret places,
  twenty worlds, sets, biomes, sound and paintings (38.10); tests `gateworlds_<world>` for each of the sixteen, and
  `gateworlds_touch`.
- **Stage 3** (built 2026-10-28): the open sky's dimension, open land and streets, the four D themes' blocks, dress, props,
  rules, events, the Festival, twenty worlds, sets, biomes with their skies, sound and paintings (38.11); tests
  `gateworlds_<world>` for each of the sixteen and `gateworlds_sky`.
- **Stage 4** (built 2026-10-29): islands, the endless plain, the fold and the mirrored underfloor on the cave engine, the
  four C themes' blocks, dress, props, rules, events, moments, twenty worlds, sets, biomes, sound and paintings (38.12);
  tests `gateworlds_<world>` for each of the sixteen and `gateworlds_repeats`.

### 38.5 The world floor contract (Stage 1)

- **The programme** (`FloorBuilder.programme`): a world floor first lays out today's rooms for that floor exactly as a rooms
  floor would (same seed, layout, room types, monsters, keys, puzzles, caches, Rig, the Lord's arena), then an engine hosts
  each programme room on a place of the world (`WorldPlan`). Same fights and rewards, a different world. `WorldPlan.host`
  gives a room its own place, `merge` puts several plain rooms (normal, elite, hall, shaft) in one long place, `extra` adds a
  place the programme doesn't have (a stair, the Rope Shaft, a secret world), `join` connects two places and `anchor` says
  where a room's features go. `finish(Walk, Look)` carries everything over: types, monster counts and spots (only where the
  engine's `Walk` says you can stand), features snapped to the nearest free spot you can stand on within 10 blocks (the
  Lord's spot and inner gates are placed by the engine), and returns null, with a reason (`WorldEngine.WHY`, logged), when a
  room has no place, the Lord's arena changed size, or the end can't be walked to from the start.
- **Built rooms**: the Lord's arena and every Rig room keep their programme size and are painted as today (in the band
  4 below their floor to 28 above), with the world carved round them. A world floor's rooms sit on the plot's 16 x 16 slot
  grid in slots 1..14 (the edge slots are the world's margin).
- **Sculpt** (`Sculpt`): an engine's carve is an ordered list of operations, each in its own box and bucketed by chunk:
  `carve` (open space by a signed distance field, with a 3-block solid shell behind it so nothing past it is ever seen),
  `mass` (solid), `fill` and `fillOpen` (a block inside a shape, anywhere or only where open), `box`, `openBox`, `put`,
  `putOpen`, `stamp` and `op` (any per-block work). Shell blocks are skinned last by what they face (floor, ceiling, wall).
  Built once at plan time and frozen (`seal`); each worldgen thread then paints through its own buffer. **Thresholds**: every
  doorway between two places is carved through with its own shell, and a door into a built room gets a frame of the world's
  trim. **Screens**: where a world's open space (air or water) meets the edge of the band, a wall closes it.
- **Blocks by role** (`WorldMats`): a recipe's `blocks` map names a block per role (`wall`, `floor`, `trim`, `bronze`...);
  an engine asks for a role with a fallback, so one engine builds many worlds.
- **Budgets**: a world floor plans in under 50 ms and carves a chunk in under 4 ms on average, 40 ms at worst (measured by
  every world's test from its second plan on: the first warms up class loading and the JIT, which alone can pass 40 ms;
  a chunk over 10 ms is carved again and the faster run counts, since a collector's pause or a compile on a shared CI
  machine isn't the carve's).
- **World tests** (`WorldCheck`, `GateWorldBellTests`): each world is planned over many gates (every layout, rank, twist and
  mood), every chunk carved, and walked on foot from the arrival (stairs, ropes and shallow water included; a Rig room is
  crossed by its mechanism, from its way in to its way on): every monster spot, key, cache and feature reachable, every room
  enterable, no water that would flow, and every step on the way to the end lit to 7 or more outside built rooms. Set
  `AWAKEN_WORLD_DUMP=<dir>` to write plan, section and view pictures of the first floors and any failing floor.

### 38.6 The Bell Crypt (Stage 1)

- **Its 15 blocks** (`GatesRegistry.WORLD_BLOCKS`, textures `tools/art/specs/gate_worlds_bell.py`, all mined with a pickaxe
  outside gates): crypt limestone, worn and crumbling; carved tracery; flagstone and wet flagstone; patina bronze (the
  bells; strike it and the world's rule answers); crypt candles (1 to 5, lit or out, 3 light each lit); moon glass (light 10,
  the lancets); rose glass (five hues, light 6); a bone niche (light 5, faces a wall); a drowned vestment (hangs on a wall,
  no collision); bell rope (climbable); a lily candle (floats on water, light 6); a handbell (bronze in a stone yoke,
  standing on the floor where anyone can strike it, faces one way, no collision; 38.8).
- **The worlds** (`data/awaken/gate_worlds/bell_crypt/`): the Sunken Belfry (everyday, `hall`), the Ossuary Ways
  (everyday, `passages`), the Bell Shaft (deep, `drop`, tall), the Field of Bells (wonder, `void`, floors only), and
  Bellmaker's Rest (secret, `rest`, reached only through the Belfry's odd rope). Each has the moods Still, Tolling, Requiem
  and Storm with their own biome (`awaken:gate_world/<world>[_<mood>]`, written by `tools/art/specs/gate_worlds_biomes.py`
  and listed in the gates dimension); sound events are `awaken:gate.world.<name>` (38.9).
- **The Sunken Belfry** (`HallEngine`): a drowned church along the plot's middle. The arrival is a narthex with two stair
  turrets; a candlelit causeway (5 wide) runs down a flooded nave (the water one step below the causeway, so a fall is never a
  trap; on a world with the Flood the tide is out when you arrive, see 38.8) between pointed arcades, with a gallery above and dark aisles behind the piers. The programme's spine becomes nave
  bays (plain rooms merged, three at most, in runs of rows); the hub or the arena takes the Great Bell (you walk under it,
  its lip just over your head), a calm bay later takes the drowned choir (stone singers waist-deep, facing the causeway);
  branches become side chapels and crypts off the aisles; a puzzle or cache wing can take the Rope Shaft (a tall shaft hung
  with bell ropes, climbed to Bellmaker's Rest on the odd rope); the end is the chancel under the rose window. Built rooms
  sit centred on the causeway so their doors open onto it. Light: candle clusters every 4 blocks along the causeway, a
  hidden light every slot, lancets of moon glass whose light lands on the water, small bells hung with lamps inside. Moods:
  Tolling adds a monster to each fight room, Storm breaks some lancets open to the dark, Requiem and Still are the quiet
  ones.
- **Chains** (`ChainLayout`, shared by the passages and void worlds): the spine winds across the plot as places joined by
  one-slot links (a seeded, bounded search; first with rock round every place, then allowing places to touch; a spine too
  long folds plain neighbours into one place). A built room is crossed straight through, in line with its way in, so the
  Rig can rebuild it; branches hang off their parent through a link of their own, or open straight off it, or off the
  nearest place with room. A floor whose Rig room doesn't rebuild tries its next variation.
- **The Ossuary Ways** (`PassageEngine`): the crypt under the Belfry where the bell-ringers were laid. Rooms are rounded
  chambers under low domes, joined by winding passages three wide (a gentle S, or a quarter turn round a corner). Every
  wall is banded like a real ossuary: a worn plinth, bone ends, a row of skulls and candles set into the wall above head
  height, bones laid lengthwise, bone ends again. The arrival is a chamber at the foot of a stair that climbs away into the
  dark you came down; the hub is the Bone Rotunda (a round domed hall, a pillar of skulls with candles at its foot, two
  skull bands and a ring of lit niches); a quiet chamber halfway holds the charnel well (a round shaft to black water, a
  lamp on a chain inside it, a bell rope down for anyone who falls in); long rooms are the Lantern Row (burial shelves,
  lamps hung down the middle); the end is the ringers' tomb (a raised sarcophagus, candles all round); other chambers
  have bone heaps, a coffin or bone pillars. Light is the candles plus hidden light (12) four apart and at every doorway
  (`WorldPlan.doorLights`). Moods: Tolling adds a monster to each fight room, Requiem lights every candle, Still leaves
  some out, Storm wets the floors.
- **The Field of Bells** (`VoidEngine`, floors only): black water seven deep with no shore and no roof (its edges and
  sky are black), bells of every size hung over it from nothing with a lamp lit in each, a few sunk to their shoulders.
  Rooms are islands of flagstone level with the water, joined by causeways at the surface (the chain's links) edged with
  floating lily candles; anyone who falls in swims to an edge and steps out. A stair of floating slabs comes down out of the
  dark to the arrival island; a bell hangs low over every other island; the Still Bell (the biggest, its clapper still)
