- **The ground grid.** An engine that gives its places ground sets `WorldPlan.ground` before `finish`: where you stand
  over each of the plot's 256 x 256 columns, in whole blocks above the floor line (a half slab's column counts the
  block over it). The floor keeps it (`FloorLayout.ground(x, z)`, 64 KB a floor, rebuilt from the saved plan like the
  rest of the layout; nothing new is saved). Null on a flat floor, so every version 6 floor and every room floor reads
  0.
- **Spawns and features stand on the ground.** `GateService.roomFloor` adds the ground, so every monster, spot, Lord,
  NPC, flood and fallback that asks for a room's floor stands on it; the entrance and the vault bars read their
  feature's column; the painter sets shrines, seals, caches, runes, lanterns, sigils and updrafts on it. Features keep
  their own heights over it.
- **Tests.** `gateworlds_depth` measures every world's places as the plan page measured them (columns you can stand
  in, the share at the floor line, half-step heights per place as the median of places a chunk or more big, surfaces
  that aren't full blocks, walls plumb from feet to head, the roof's spread, what stands per 100 floor blocks, and the
  plan's cost) and logs them; worlds whose ground is built (`GateDepthTests.DEEP`) are held to the dry caves' targets
  (flat 55% or less, 8 heights or more, 12% partial, 65% plumb or less, roof spread 6, detail 35). The world tests'
  reach checks read the ground.
- **Shaped ground (`Relief`, stage 1).** A cave world whose dress says `depth()` (the Hive so far) and whose floor is
  enclosed (not an open land, isles, sea, plain or hall: stage 2) gets a height field in half blocks, -4 to +8, solved
  at plan time after the dress (so it knows where the dress set things down) and before the lights; one column
  operation per place lays it at carve time. The field: a roll everywhere (+-1.8 blocks); away from the way (the line
  from each doorway to the middle and on to the anchor, faded in over 1.8 to 5.8 blocks) terraces climbing toward the
  walls (up to 4 blocks, their edges ragged), mounds, hollows, and the ground standing a slab higher on the whole, so
  the way reads as a path worn into it. On the way's core half a step up at most, within 3.5 of it a block either way;
  in a fought place's middle (`q` < 0.5) half a block down to a block up, rolling half again as much off the way (half
  steps you run over without a thought). No specks: a rise or a hollow needs four of
  its eight neighbours rising or sinking with it (a wall counts with it; two passes), or it's flattened, so no lone slab
  lies on the floor like a dropped tile and no small pit reads as a hole. Never closer than 3.5 under the roof (or
  under what the dress hangs low: `Dress.headroom`). **Flat pads** stay at the floor line and are never shaped:
  each doorway (4 deep either side of its wall, across the opening), 3 round the anchors, a lake's water, 1 past each blocked spot, 2 round each hand spot, the
  dress's centre pad (`Dress.pad`: the Comb's honey pools 3.4), and every small mark (49 blocks or less, 1.5 round it:
  nooks, bells, props, touchstones; an event's or a basin's wide box isn't one). **Steps**: no step over a block, half
  a block where it's gentle (the way's margin and a fought middle); the rises and the hollows are each only lowered
  toward the floor line until no step is too steep (eight neighbours), and where a rise meets a hollow each comes to
  within half the step of the line, so nothing is ever raised to meet a pad.
- **A world's own depth numbers** (optional, in its recipe's `params`, 1 the usual; they only shape version 7 floors, so
  a released world's version 6 floors are untouched): `depth_ground` (how bold the ground is away from the way: the
  terraces, mounds and hollows), `depth_things` (how many things stand in its places: clusters times it, 0 none),
  `depth_lumps` (its walls' lumps, times the theme's `Dress.lumps`), `depth_ledges` (how often a tall wall steps back,
  times `Dress.ledges`), `depth_roof` (how far the roof swells and dips), `depth_shelves` (the high ledges, stage 4). The
  Root Warrens and the Last Room set `depth_roof` 1.9 and 2.2, the Root Halls 1.5 and the Pipe Maze 1.3 (their low
  roofs spread too little otherwise). Whatever the dress hangs from the roof (`Dress.hang`: roots, icicles, chains) and
  the Fungal tunnels' roots stop as far over the highest ground within 3 as over the floor line before, so raised ground
  never makes one a ladder. In Upward Rain mud (it stands 7/8 of a block) gives way to moss beside a half step up: from
  mud onto a slab is a jump.
- **The walk guarantee** (plan time, `Relief.ease`): every doorway and the anchor must be joined over the place's
  ground (round what the dress blocked) with no step over half a block. Where they aren't, the place's ground is
  halved, and if that's still not enough, flat; either is logged (`[gates] <world> place <id>: no way through without a
  jump`). On the Hive it never has to (`gateworlds_depth_ease` holds the rule on a ridge a block high, halved, and two
  blocks high, flattened).
- **Tunnels** swell slowly along the way, up to a block, never a step over half a block (a slab between), flat 2.5 round
  each doorway; their arch rises with the floor and vaults and dips along the way (-0.7 to +3).
- **Laying it** (`Relief.column`): under a raised floor full blocks of the theme's bank (`Dress.ground(BANK)`, the
  Hive's wax with every third layer dark), its top skinned as floor; a half step is a stair facing up a straight ramp,
  else a slab (on the Hive's pollen a pollen drift four layers deep); a hollow is opened with a shell under it. What grew
  on the floor line is moved up onto the new ground; elsewhere a drift at a rise's foot or in a dip (55%, one or two
  layers) or bits (by how wild it is: below).
- **Soft steps at walls and roof steps** (`Relief.soften`, after the ground is laid): off the way (wild 0.3 or more),
  about half the wall feet that rise sheer from a full block get the theme's stair (`Dress.ground(STAIRS)`), its back to
  the wall; where the roof over a column is a block higher than beside it (on one side only), the theme's roof stair
  (`Dress.ground(ROOF)`, the Hive's wax stairs) hangs upside down under it, stepping down to the lower roof, where the
  roof is 4 or more over where you stand. Never on a pad; a column at a chunk's edge is left.
- **Walls and roof over shaped ground.** A groove 1 high is cut into the wall's foot at the local ground (0.9 to 1.7
  deep, the wall's first 2 blocks), so walls aren't plumb from feet to head. The roof rises with the terraces (the
  terrace's height is added to it: no trench at a wall's foot), swells and dips away from the walls (+-7.5) and opens
  into chimneys here and there (up to 12 higher, `CaveEngine.CHIMNEY`; the carve reaches 19 over a place's roof).
- **Thin blocks are open** (`Sculpt.thinOpen`, every version 7 floor): a palette block that isn't a full solid cube and
  holds no fluid (a slab, a drift, crumbs, a carpet) gets the shell's skin under or over it as floor or ceiling, as air
  does.
- **Lights** over shaped ground hang at head height over where you stand, and a place's lights reach 2 blocks into its
  wall's foot. **Spots** a live thing is put on (`walk`) need their 3 x 3 level on shaped ground, on a whole
  block (never a half step).
- **Depth blocks** (`gates.block.DepthBlocks`, art `tools/art/specs/gate_depth.py`, the same table): slabs and stairs
  cut from a theme's blocks wearing their texture (soft when cut from a soft block, else they want the stone's tool),
  a drift that piles in layers like snow (you stand a layer under its top, mobs path over four layers or fewer), and
  bits underfoot (no collision, broken at a touch). The Hive's: wax slab and stairs, dark wax slab, packed wax floor
  slab and stairs, capped comb slab, pollen drift, wax crumbs. Every other theme (stage 2) gets two
  slab and stair pairs, one cut from its walls and one from its floor, a drift where its floor is soft and bits drawn
  for it: Ember basalt and slag, ash drift, cinders; Temple stone and tiles, moss drift, fallen leaves; Archive stone
  and tiles, paper drift, scraps; Foundry iron and brick, shavings; Desert sandstone and tile, sand drift, shards;
  Market cobbles and boards, confetti; Frost stone and tiles, snow drift, ice chips; Palace marble and checker, shards;
  Lab panel and floor, moss drift, screws; Dream wood and boards, plush drift, feathers; Sky rock and marble, turf
  drift, pebbles; Abyss shrine stone and tiles, wax stubs; Fungal rock and loam, moss drift, spores (82 depth blocks in
  all). They join `#minecraft:slabs` and `#stairs` (blocks and items); a double slab drops two.
- **The Hive's dress over shaped ground.** Drips hang thicker and longer (12%, up to 5). **Comb sheets** hang from the
  roof as a real hive's comb does: at most one in each 6 x 6 patch (the Comb 75%, the Swarm 55%, others 40%), a wall of
  cells a block thick and 5 to 9 long, deepest in its middle (up to 7), its lower edge dark wax; never within 4 blocks
  over where you stand, never within 1.5 of a wall (4 round the Brood Hall's ledges), never in a boss's room. The Brood
  Hall's great place keeps 6 of head room under its lowest ledge (`Dress.headroom`).
- **Walls that change as they rise** (`CaveEngine.Cave.wall`, in each shaped cavern's carve). Lumps over every wall and
  roof face, taller than wide (up to 1.3 blocks in or out, bigger the higher; the theme scales them, `Dress.lumps`: the
  Hive's comb bulges 1.3 times); where a wall stands tall it leans in or out as it rises (up to 2.2) and here and there
  (about a third of it) steps back 1.6 at a ledge 5 to 9 over the ground (`Dress.ledges`). All of it starts 2.5 over
  the highest ground or standing piece within 3 (`Relief.near`, raised by each outcrop, fallen piece and heap:
  `Relief.lift`), past a jump, so no wall is a stair to its roof. Under the roof it bulges a block down at most
  (headroom stays over 2), and it's never worn back nearer than 2.5 to the place's box, so the rock between two places
  stays whole. Tunnels keep their own swell and vault.
- **The way and the wild.** Each shaped column keeps how wild it is (0 on the way's core, rising to 1 away from it; a
  fought middle a third as wild; a tunnel wild only at its sides) and how far in from the wall it is. Where it's
  wildest (over 0.55) the theme's growth creeps (`Dress.creep`, the Hive's capped comb) over the floor and up the foot
  of the walls beside it (up to 4 high, thicker the wilder; never on a pad); drifts bank against the wall (wild over
  0.45, within 3 of it, deepest at its foot, up to 7 layers); bits lie by how wild it is (`Dress.bits` x wild: the
  Hive's crumbs at most about one in 12 floor blocks, none on the way); the dress's growth thickens with it (0.2 to 2
  times). A wall nook's crawl mouth is kept clear (1.5 round it), so a banked drift never seals it.
- **Things standing in the space** (`Formations`, once the ground is solved, before the lights). In each shaped place's
  wild (never a boss's room) a chunk's cavern gets one or two pieces and a bigger place up to three clusters of two to
  four (one more cluster per 150 wild spots): a **pillar** from the ground to the roof (only a cluster's first, 2.5 or
  more from the wall where the roof is 7 or more over the ground; slimmest a little under halfway, flaring into the
  ground and wider into the roof), an **outcrop** half sunk and lumpy with slabs where its top steps up, a **fallen
  piece** 4 to 7 long lying along the ground half sunk (each end on the ground under it), a **heap** with a drift
  slumped round it. A piece's footprint is wild ground (0.35 or more) or the wall (an outcrop may lean on it), never a
  pad or the way; each is blocked, so nothing spawns or stands in it. The theme cuts them (`Dress.formation`; null is
  the shell's own skin): the Hive's wax pillars banded dark with a honey cell here and there, wax mounds crusted with
  capped comb, fallen comb with its cells broken open, heaps of dark wax. About half the Hive's small caverns get
  something, and every bigger place.
- **No jump on the way, no climbing the walls.** `gateworlds_depth` also walks each built world from the arrival to the
  end without a jump (no rise over 0.6 of a block by what you stand on: a slab or a stair is a step, a full block a
  jump) and fails a world that needs one (`jumps`, 0 in all three); and counts the columns where the walk (jumps
  allowed) got more than 4 over the ground (`climbs`): a built cave world must have none (0 in all three).
- **Every theme's caves (stage 2).** Every enclosed cave world of every theme shapes its places by the Hive's rules,
  in its own pieces (`Dress.kit`, `Dress.pieces`): a half step is a slab of the floor (on a soft floor its drift four
  layers deep: Ember's ash, the Temple's moss, the Glass Caves' sand everywhere, Frost's snow, the Lab garden's moss,
  the Fungal moss and all of the Bloom), a ramp the floor's stairs; the wall's stairs stand at a wall's foot and hang
  where the roof steps, the wall's slab crowns an outcrop (`Relief.FOOT`, `Relief.CAP`: null falls back to the floor's
  stairs and slab, so the Hive is as it was). Growth creeps where it's wildest in Ember (magma crust), the Temple
  (mossy stone), the Glass Caves (sand), Frost (snow), Dream (plush), the Lab (moss in from the garden) and the Fungal Hollow (glowing
  moss); the Archive, Foundry, Market, Palace and Abyss stay bare. What stands in the wild: Ember basalt pillars banded with glowing
  cracks, cooled lava humps, a collapsed frame in the mine, slag heaps; the Temple columns banded with carving (roots in the Great Tree and
  the Root Halls), mossy outcrops, a fallen column; the Archive shelves floor to roof banded with written stone, a
  toppled bookcase, book piles; the Foundry pipe bundles banded with brass, scrap iron with gears in it, a fallen gear
  half sunk, scrap heaps; the Glass Caves sandstone pillars, glass outcrops glowing here and there, a half-buried column; the Broker's Vault timber
  posts and heaps of cobbles; Frost ice pillars banded with glowing ice, ice boulders under snow, a fallen icefall; the
  Palace marble columns banded with gilt, a toppled gilt frame, a heap of broken mirror; the Lab frames banded with light, racks, a
  heap of panels; Dream bedposts, heaps of sheets and plush; the Abyss pillars banded with runes, a fallen pale column;
  the Fungal Hollow mushroom stems floor to roof, rock crusted with moss, a fallen cap, heaps of loam (the
  plan page's table, as near as each theme's blocks allow). Not shaped: a world under a
  glass floor (`mirror`: the Inverted Palace, the Reflection: the world below copies it), the Simulation (its lines are
  everything), the White, the Sleeper's Dream (its void blocks would skin a raised island's sides) and the Endless
  Hall (a fold that reads the same both ways).
- **Open lands, islands and seas** shape their places too (the Market's Rooftops keeps its line: you stand on roofs
  there). Under the sky nothing hangs where a roof would step and no pillar stands (nothing to hold up; not over an
  island either). An island's (the isles, a sea's islands) ground is half as bold and makes **hummocks** instead of
  terraces: rising between its middle and its edge, back to the floor line at the drop, so no rim stands at it;
  nothing stands out over its edge; its bridges and causeways stay flat. The Sky's pieces: marble slabs on its ruins,
  turf drifted four layers deep elsewhere, rock stairs at its cliffs, rock outcrops under turf, fallen ruin stones,
  pebbles; turf creeping.
- **The rare worlds** take the ground of the look they wear (`BorrowedDress` passes every depth hook on), but the
  Other Gate keeps its line (its colours turn only on full blocks, so slabs would show true colours) and so does the
  Endless Stair (its landings are the same landing again). The rare lands in their own clothes (the Quiet, Upward Rain,
  the Aurora Steppe, the Lantern Orchard, the Last Campfire) step in the Soft Land's slabs of the soil underfoot (turf,
  mud, coarse dirt, podzol: SPEC 31.2), mossy cobblestone stairs at the hillsides, snow drifted on the Steppe, pebbles
  and twigs, moss (snow on the Steppe) creeping, mossy boulders, fallen trees and heaps of earth. A fallen piece's log,
  stem or column lies along it (its axis).
- **Doorways stay at the floor line**, 4 deep either side of the wall across the opening (`Relief.doorway`, what the
  doorway test checks; a door's lintel is set for the floor line: a Rig room's way out, a tunnel's mouth), and the groove
  at a wall's foot isn't cut there (it would open only the wall's bottom block). Over shaped ground a light may sit up to
  5 over its column, on top of whatever stands there, or in the column beside it where a wall's bulge fills its own; an
  isle's rim keeps its lights in the air just off it. **Bits lie in patches** (`Relief.litter`: a quarter as thick between
  them, up to 2.75 times in them, about as many on the whole), as the plan asked (clusters, not an even scatter), and a
  third as thick on the way as off it (0.35 + 0.65 of how wild); the themes that grow little else lie thicker: the
  Archive's pages 0.5, the Palace's glass 0.45, the Foundry's shavings, Dream's lost things and the Abyss's wax 0.42,
  Ember's cinders 0.34, the Glass Caves and the Lab 0.3, the Market's confetti 0.25, the Quiet lands 0.15, Frost 0.12,
  the Temple and the Fungal Hollow 0.1 (the Hive and the Sky 0.083). The roof's swell over shaped places is +-9 (was
  7.5), up to 1.6 times that under a low roof (11 over its roof height: a low roof can't dip, it stops 3.5 over the
  floor); a tunnel's vaults over shaped ground rise up to 13 over the floor line (9 before), +-4.5 along the way. The
  Fungal Hollow's walls bulge 1.15 times (shelf fungus), the Bloom's 1.5 (its gills fold).
- **Shores, cloisters and vaults.** An island's shore never sinks (no hollow within 3 of its edge: the sea or the drop
  stands level with it). Under the Cloisters' roofed walks the ground stays at the line (`FrostDress.headroom` 3.5).
  On content 7 a feature that finds no level spot near takes the nearest free one, so a vault's bars never close round
  a touchstone or a handbell. The tests' light check lets light into layers (snow, a drift) as the game does.
- **The Bell Crypt's own engines (stage 3)** keep their architecture, and the years show on their flagstones
  (`CryptWear`, content 7, made after each engine's carve and before its handbells): the stones sink half a block in
  patches (a flagstone slab where the noise is under 0.38) and where a patch sinks deepest (under 0.24, every stone round
  it sunk too) a wet hollow opens a block down onto wet flagstone, moss on a third of it and a hidden light in every
  other stone (it's a block under the floor's lights); rubble from the vault lies at the walls' feet where the place is
  three clear out from the wall (crumbling limestone in a corner, a limestone stair with its back to the wall, one in
  eight a fallen piece of tracery, a limestone slab a block further out); limestone dust drifts one to three layers
  against half the walls' feet; bone shards lie in patches; moss grows round the hollows; and one bell lies toppled on
  its side (`crypt_bell_toppled`: the swinging bell's model turned over, its mouth to its facing) in the floor's biggest
  place, off its middle, slabs and dust round it. Doorways (the threshold and a block past it, 3 round the middle),
  handbells (3.5), every mark of 49 blocks or less and every basin (with 2 or 3 round them) stay as built, and each
  engine keeps its own: the Hall its bays' pits and causeway (13.5 either side of the nave's axis) and the Rope Shaft
  and the rest, the Passages the Charnel Well, the Field of Bells everything within 3 of an island's shore, its
  causeways and its landings. A spawn or a feature stands only where no stone in its three by three has sunk and 3 or
  more from the bell. The crypt's depth blocks: limestone and flagstone slabs and stairs, Limestone Dust (a drift of
  worn limestone) and Bone Shards (bits).
- **High ledges (stage 4)** in the big caverns of the cave worlds (a great cavern two, a cavern of four chunks or more
  one, times the recipe's optional `depth_shelves`; never an open land, an isle or a sea): a shelf against the wall, 3
  or 4 blocks up (even odds), 3.5 to 5 either side of where it's set and about 4 deep (its edge ragged), with a stair of
  one-block steps, 2 along the wall and 3 deep, down from one end, so it's reached a jump at a time. A shelf is tried
  every 15 degrees round the place's middle, 2.5 in from the wall where the way is 6 or more off, farthest from the way
  first, then its stair the other way round; it stands only where every column of it and its stair is in the place,
  unpinned, 3.5 or more off the way, 3 or more from anything the dress set down and under the dress's head room with
  3.5 to spare, a doorway at least its half length and twice its height and 4 away, another ledge 20, with 12 columns on
  top and 2 on the bottom step. The ledges stand as set (the specks, the steps' rule and the walk guarantee pass them by;
  the ground beside them never sinks), the roof lifts by the highest ledge within 2, and nothing is placed on one or
  beside it: no spawn or feature on a ledge or its stair (the nearest free spot for a feature skips them too), no
  formation within 2. A quiet place to stand and look out, not a place to fight. The floor keeps their columns
  (`FloorLayout.high`, not saved) for the test (`gateworlds_ledges`: the Brood Hall, the Glowing Deep, the Working Mine
  and the Atrium have them, 85% of their columns or more reached on foot, nothing on them).
- **Held to the targets** (`gateworlds_depth`): 32 dry caves of every theme (`DEEP`) as above, and none with a way up a
  wall it didn't have at version 6 (`climbs` no more than version 6's on the same floors); 28 open lands, isles and seas
  (`LANDS`, each measured at version 6 too on the same floors) to twice their partial surfaces, as the plan set, and
  more detail than before; and every world with no jump on its way (the test logs where a way needs one). Held to what
  they measure instead (`FLAT_MOST`, `DETAIL_LEAST`, `PARTIAL_TIMES`): the Swarm and the Forge Below 59% flat (many small
  fought places, 58.6% and 58.5%), the Forge Below's and the Stacks' detail 33 (both 35.0 at version 8, counting
  litter on half steps and, in the Forge, crystals stood upside down under the roof; version 9 measures 33.6 and 33.3,
  38.16), Upward Rain's partial 1.4 times (its mud counted as partial at version 6), the Gates' Heart's 1.9 (1.97 at
  version 8, 1.92 at 9: a half step under what grew there is made whole). Not held: the
  Bloom (61% flat, 69% plumb: its folds are its walls) and the worlds that keep their line.
- **Measured** (`gateworlds_depth`, 2026-10-29 with every stage in). The 32 dry caves: flat 43 to 59% (mean 50), 11 to
  15 heights, partial 14 to 22% (18), plumb 20 to 47% (40), roof spread 6.1 to 9.8 (7.1), detail 35 to 51 (41); the Comb
  54%, 13, 19%, 38%, 6.4, 38; the Brood Hall 46%, 14, 22%, 40%, 7.3, 42; the Swarm 59%, 13, 16%, 36%, 6.6, 43 (today's
  rooms: flat about 98%, plumb 97%). The lands, isles and seas: partial 2 to 50 times version 6's (the Sky's isles about
  3.3, the Abyss's steps 2.2, the seas 2.3 to 35), detail 1.5 to 7.5 times, flat down from 88 to 99% to 41 to 61% on the
  lands, 27 to 30% to 11 to 17% on the seas. The Bell Crypt (its own engines, not held to the caves' numbers): the Sunken
  Belfry flat 68 to 51%, partial 2.1 to 12.8%, detail 10.3 to 16.4; the Ossuary Ways 92 to 79%, 9.8 to 15.3%, 10.2 to 14;
  the Bell Shaft 91 to 66%, 0.8 to 19.1%, 11.5 to 21.4; the Field of Bells (black water between its islands) 14 to 13%,
  1.4 to 2.7%, 2.5 to 3. A gate's four floors plan in 8 ms (median, warm) to 50 ms (the Fungal Hollow's, with other
  builders on the machine), the ledge search under 2 ms of it, so a floor stays well inside its 50 ms.
- **Tour `gate-depth-hive`** (CI): the Comb, the Brood Hall and the Swarm at version 6 and at version 7 on the same
  floors, each floor 1's biggest place and its second. Its tools (game master, tours): `/awaken gate open <rank>

  layout, four floors), so a world's two versions are the same floors; `/awaken gate interior goto place|place2` stands
  just inside a world floor's biggest (or second) place where you walk in (else a doorway), a block over the ground,
  facing its middle. The tour starts 6,000 blocks out (no gate forms in Carillon's reserve) with the HUD off,
  and waits for the land there before its first gate; a gate made by `gate open ... world` stands where it's opened,
  even over a village's edge (a tour can't pick another spot); `gate interior enter` takes the gate opened last when
  it's ready (`GateService.lastOpened`, not saved), not a gate that formed by itself beside it since, and while
  that gate is still forming it says so and enters none (a tour's shots would show another world), and the same when
  it never stood (its build failed on wet ground or someone's build: one tour's "Root Halls" shots were the Forge
  Below again); `gate open` with no
  dry ground within 30 looks 30 to 120 out, then 120 to 300 (a tour's hop can land on a coast). Tours
  `gate-depth-themes-a`, `-b` and `-c` (every other theme's cave worlds at 7), `gate-depth-lands` (seven lands, isles and
  seas at 6 and 7) and `gate-depth-crypt` (the Bell Crypt's four at 6 and 7) are the same on CI, and wait 1,000
  ticks for their first gate (CI's first took 666 once). `gate interior goto over` (`over2`: the second place) shows
  the same place hovering 8 over the highest ground within 4 of where you walk in (at most 3 under an open land's lid),
  looking down at its middle, flying if you may. The lands tour uses it for the Dark Steps and the Honey Lake, where it
  reads well; in the open lands (kind `open`) its shots show only sky and fog on CI, with Lens on or off, though the
  plan puts the camera 10 over an open plaza looking 28 degrees down (cause not found), so those keep `place`, which
  faces a bank or a house there (and an isle's stands in the cloud).

### 38.15 Room for the Lords (content version 8; boss-plan's measure of the true-size bosses, sent at Euan's request 2026-10-30)

Every boss now has its own body drawn at true size, so the room a Lord needs is set by its body, not its hitbox.
boss-plan measured each body in every clip (shared notes `boss-plan-boss-space.md`, from the rigs in
`assets/awaken/kit/rigs`): the **sweep** is the furthest any part of it reaches from its centre (strikes, tails, its
death), the **tallest** the highest any part reaches. Version 8 builds every Lord's arena round those numbers.

- **The sweep each arena keeps clear** (`PiecesArenas.sweep`, rounded up): 10 for the Ember Tyrant (the Forge) and the
  Sky Leviathan, 9 for the Glass Serpent, 7 for the Gearwright Colossus, the Bell Warden and the Root Saint, 6 for the
  Lantern Broker and the Abbot of Frost, 4 for the rest. It's set on the boss room as `Room.space` from version 8 (0
  before) and carried to a world floor's built arena.
- **Cover and props stand a block clear of it.** A ring at `R × k` whose props reach `half` either side moves out to
  `space + half + 1` when that's further (`PiecesArenas.cover`), the same in the painting and in `blocks` (the walk
  map). In the full 3x3 arena (radius 22) that moves only the Forge's six basalt columns (from 9.9 to 12, still inside
  the lava moat at 15.4) and leaves out the Root Saint's four pillars on the grid's axes at 7. In the keeper's 2x2
  arena (radius 14) the Bell Warden's statues move from 8.4 to 9.5, the Hive Regent's comb pillars from 7.7 to 9.2
  (their canopies reach 4.2), the Mother of Spores's caps from 8.1 to 8.9 and the Hollow Herald's candles from 3.5 to
  5.5.
- **The room's own props stay out too:** nothing from the room's decoration (floor props, clutter, the Nightmare's
  floating things, hanging props) is placed inside the sweep and a block past it (`Ctx.inLordSpace`), nor the Sky
  Archipelago island's lamp posts or the Sky Leviathan arena's floating stones.
- **Over the Forge:** its overhead chop reaches 11.1, so the timber beams across its vault go from 13 to 14 over the
  floor (the lanterns under them from 12 to 13).
- **Height:** each arena is clear from the floor to the top of its Lord's body plus one, plus three over the five that
  fly (the Mother of Spores, the Glass Serpent, the Hive Regent, the Sky Leviathan and the Hollow Herald), who rise
  on top of their body's height. The full arena stays 17+ high; within the sweep 13 to 26 is clear overhead (13 over
  the Forge, under its lanterns).
- **Arenas in a world:** a world floor never hosts its Lord on one of the world's places. Its boss room is always built
  (`WorldPlan.built`): painted by the rooms painter at the plan room's size and height (17+) in its own band, with the
  world carved round it. So a cave, a sea or the islands give every Lord the full arena's headroom.
- **The inner gate's keeper:** Gate within a Gate's annex Lord floor keeps the small 2x2 arena, except for the four
  Lords that would swing through its cover: the Ember Tyrant, the Sky Leviathan, the Glass Serpent and the Gearwright
  Colossus get the full 3x3 arena (`FloorBuilder.smallKeeper`, `PiecesArenas.needsFullArena`). The 2x2 arena is 13
  high, and the tallest keeper left in it (the Hollow Herald, 6.7 and three more flying) has 18 clear.
- **True-size hitboxes:** the first six Lords' boxes now cover the main body (without the limbs) and are as tall as the
  whole body. boss-plan set them at 5e72de99 with Euan's OK: the Forge 3.6 × 8.25, Unit Zero 1.0 × 4.3, the Mother of
  Spores 1.8 × 5.8, the Colossus 1.5 × 8.4, the Root Saint 1.8 × 5.4, the Bell Warden 2.8 × 4.6. They fit: the
  medallion and its band reach 3.0, the Forge's clear disc is 10 with 13 clear over it, and
  `gates_interior_arenas_fit_lords` checks the spawned Lord's real box (a block round it, one over) at its spot. A Lord
  never leaves its arena, so doors needn't fit it.
- **Versions:** version 8 is `GatePlan.CONTENT_VERSION`. Entered gates keep their version. A version 7 arena is
  unchanged, since everything above keys on `Room.space > 0` or the plan's version. With `gateWorldsDepth` off, new
  gates are still made at 6 with their arenas as they were. `gateworlds_same_rooms` now compares version 5's rooms
  with version 7's, because 8 changes arenas on purpose.
- **Test `gates_interior_lord_space`:** checks every theme's Lord in its main arena and as the keeper, at 7 and at 8.
  At 8, nothing solid may be inside the sweep from the floor to the body's top, big keepers must get the full arena,
  and full arenas must be 17+ high. Version 7 is measured beside it for the report. At 7 the Forge had 21 blocks in
  its sweep (columns and lanterns), 83 as a keeper. The Glass Serpent as a keeper had 26, the Hive Regent as a keeper
  13, the Root Saint 9 (pillars), the Sky Leviathan 3 (an island post), and the Bell Warden, the Colossus and the
  Mother of Spores had some as keepers. At 8 every arena has none.

### 38.16 Placement: nothing hangs in the air (content version 9; Euan 2026-11-03, playing a gate: "a lot of floating things in gates instead of placemement all being thought out")

Props go where a set dresser would put them, on a surface, an edge, a corner or the roof, and a spot that can't hold
a thing gets nothing. Nothing is put there to fill the gap.

- **What holds what** (`Holds`, one rule per block state):
  - A plant, a prop, crumbs, a candle, a carpet, a cache, a rune or the seal stands on a face that holds it. That is
    the top of a full block, a top slab or an upside-down stair (`isFaceSturdy(UP, CENTER)`). A tall plant's top
    stands on its bottom.
  - A lantern, hanging roots, cave vines or a spore blossom hangs from such a face, from a chain, or from a string of
    lights.
  - Roots, kelp, a bell rope, a drip or a fall of light is held at one end.
  - The entrance is a tile set in the floor, so it's part of the floor.
  - A vestment, a torch, a banner, a ladder or a coral fan is held by the wall behind it.
  - A string of lights or prayer flags is tied at both ends to something solid, and each block of it touches the next
    face to face.
  - Solid things joined face to face, with the chains and lamps hung among them, reach the ground, a wall, the roof,
    water, or a held thing with a flat top (a vault's lid on its cache). A lump of under 2,048 blocks that doesn't is
    floating.
- **How each placer keeps to it (version 9):**
  - Bells: a hung bell's chain runs up to the roof (`BellPieces.chainUp`) in the Void, the Halls and the Shaft. The
    Void's stair has a column under each step. A lamp hung from a bell frame's canopy has its chain run up to it.
  - Chandeliers, the Lords' crowns, mirrors, gears, spores and the jelly crown take their height from the roof over
    their middle (`Pieces.apex`). Their arms join with spokes, and their rings are 0.75 wide so the blocks meet face
    to face. A room chandelier hangs at its middle's height over its middle's floor, and an arm's tip goes only where
    the arm reaches it. Roots hold nothing up, so the Fungal Hollow's caps hang on a mushroom stalk and spread on gills.
    Nothing else hangs from the roof over a chandelier's pieces.
  - Strings: lights and prayer flags run wall to wall (`Dress.strung`), placed after the ground is solved
    (`Dress.later`) so they tie to the rock that's really there. A string that can't be tied isn't hung. A shrine
    pole's flags run down to a peg on the ground, and the ground under them stays level. Market lanterns under a vault
    each hang on their own chain, their lengths following the old sag.
  - The Festival's great lantern stands on four timber legs. Under the open sky there is nothing to hang it from.
  - Beams cross a vault only where both ends rest. They carry on over a room's set piece and are left out of the
    Lords' arenas.
  - Stairs: a flight off an edge gets a sloped soffit (the Abyss's dark steps, the Dream's stair going nowhere). The
    Abyss's flight goes only where its top step meets the island, and its candles stand on pale posts at the ends of
    every third step (a stair's top doesn't hold a candle). A rare world in another theme's dress runs that dress's
    placements that wait for the ground too (`BorrowedDress.late`: the Gates' Heart's flights, borrowed strings).
  - Upside-down furniture is carried up in its own stuff to meet a roof that isn't flat (`DreamDress.shim`). The
    Nursery's mobile hangs on a chain.
  - The Shrine and the Seal, the two blocks you click to leave or go on, always stand on something solid (Euan 8 Nov:
    "those are still floating sometimes"). A terrace Shrine room sets them a block up, for its dais; a world floor takes
    a room's features but not its dais, so a quarter of them stood a block in the air. There the painter sets a plinth
    of the theme's pillar under each. A chunk already painted is never painted again, so `Rooms.enter` fills what's
    missing under either one, down to something solid within 8, on any floor of any version, when someone walks in. The
    Bell Crypt's wear leaves every feature's column as the engine laid it (`CryptWear.keepUnder`).
    `gates_placement` also rolls 600 gates the Director's way and reads these two blocks' columns: its own worlds are
    all Spiral Towers, whose Shrine room is always round.
  - Features stand on a whole step: a half step under a cache or a rune is made whole (`Relief.level`). In a built
    room a feature stands on the floor under it, up a terrace's dais or down in a pit (`RoomGeometry.featureLift`, read
    by the painter and by `GateService.feature` for every use: the rune you press, the lantern you take, the shrine's
    spot), and the net never leaves out a gate piece (a shrine, a seal, a cache, a rune, a lantern, an updraft:
    `Holds.settles`). A dais's edge under a feature stays a full block, not a stair (`Ctx.standsOn`). In a room of sky
    islands a feature over the gap moves to the nearest island column within 6, off the way through the doors
    (`FloorBuilder.ashore`). An isle's waterfall pool is never dug under a feature (`Dress.featureAt`).
  - Nothing grows or lies on a half step. Where something grew on the floor line the half step there is made whole.
    What would have lain on a half step is kicked onto a whole step within two, the foot of the rise first, never onto
    a pinned column (`Relief.kick`), and litter gathers on a whole step beside half steps, half again for each
    (`Relief.gather`): it collects at the foot and on the lip of a rise. The Forge Below and the Stacks keep 91% of
    what lay about at version 8.
  - Mushrooms grow only where the room is clear. A hive pillar stands whole or not at all, and its canopy only round
    a pillar that stands. Market awnings rest on posts and join their counters face to face. The conveyor's press
    hangs from the gantry on its ram.
  - Cave roofs: up a chimney the shell follows the roof's slope (`CaveEngine.Cave.roofD`), and the carve reaches over
    the highest swell.
- **The net** (`Sculpt.Buf.crumbs`, `GatePainter.Band`), run after a chunk's operations:
  - A lump of rock or solid things under 2,048 blocks is left out unless something holds it: water, the band's ends,
    a held thing with a flat top, or being marked as floating on purpose.
  - A lump that runs over a chunk side is followed into the chunks next to it. Those chunks are carved by their own
    operations, up to 8 of them, so every chunk the lump crosses reaches the same answer. Their carves are kept per
    thread (the last 12), so neighbours carving one after another don't carve each other again (the Honey Lake's worst
    chunk 8 ms, not 60).
  - A lump that touches water, face to face or in the chunk beside, is held by it (a pool's rim stays).
  - Then `Holds.settle` drops anything whose spot doesn't hold it, so a plant on a lump goes with the lump. If the
    settle drops a chain, the net runs once more.
  - A room's chunk does the same within its band.
- **Floating on purpose** (`Sculpt.afloat`, `Ctx.afloat`). These stay, and the census counts them apart:
  - the Sky's far isles and the Wind Stair's floating steps;
  - the Endless Stair's and the Twist's landings;
  - the Sleeper's furniture, the Wrong Room and the Nightmare's floating clutter;
  - the Sky Leviathan's stones;
  - the Rig's collapse-run tiles and the Gauntlet's course and walls over the drop;
  - the Sky Archipelago's updraft pads.
- **Test `gates_placement`.** It plans every world in every theme (412 floors: every floor of the 75 worlds, and
  rooms plans of every theme, layout, twist and set piece). It builds each floor block by block and checks every
  placed thing against the rules.
  - It counts by placer: the code that set the block, found by re-planning with `Sculpt.TRACE`.
  - Designed floats are counted on their own line.
  - Knobs: `AWAKEN_PLACEMENT_VERSION` measures an older version, `AWAKEN_PLACEMENT_ONLY` takes one world, and
    `AWAKEN_PLACEMENT_COLUMN` dumps columns.
  - The world tests' light model (`WorldCheck`) lets the sky through layers short of a full block (snow, a drift), as
    the game does. Before, the Aurora Steppe's way read as lit only from the side, past snow lying on slabs, which
    version 9 drops.
  - Before, at version 8: 239,318 of 350,358 placed things weren't held up, on 372 of the 412 floors. The biggest
    groups:
    - 120,450 blocks of cave rock in 9,203 lumps;
    - 57,905 things lying on half steps;
    - 35,407 blocks of bells and their frames hung on nothing;
    - 4,609 of the Abyss's dark steps;
    - 4,356 from the Lords' arena pieces;
    - 3,048 from room chandeliers and beams;
    - 2,807 from the Market's strings and the great lantern.
  - After, at version 9: none of 331,172 (the litter kicked off half steps and the gate pieces the net no longer drops
    are counted now). 7,601 blocks in 464 lumps float on purpose.
- **Tour `gate-placement`** (`tools/autopilot/gate-placement.txt`): six worlds before and after (the Stacks, the
  Cloisters, the Rooftops, the Dark Steps, the Open Chasm, the Upside-Down house), each pair from one spot:
  `/awaken gate interior goto float` hovers where the floor's biggest thing not held up at version 8 is in view, worked
  out from the version 8 floor at any version (`PlacementTests.floatView`; `float2` the next biggest, 24 blocks off).
- **Versions:** version 9 is `GatePlan.CONTENT_VERSION`. Entered gates keep their version. A version 8 floor carves
  as before (`gateworlds_depth_v6_golden` still holds version 6 block for block).

## 34. The Singing Deep (mining, caves and the pick; plan docs/mining/PLAN.md, page https://claude.ai/artifact/Jp3EjBR1Cb4XqBjSN6zU9x; Euan approved all of it 2026-10-28: "Go with the full plan")

Builds on §28.3 (W2) and §28.5 (W5); the plan's audit (`docs/mining/proof/`) is what it was designed against: Tectonic
seals noise caves within ~12 blocks of the ground, so the sky-open mouths are unmarked slots (median 106 m from any
spot in Euan's world); 99% of iron was vanilla's scatter; the Hearth never said where; our sparks were round dots over
vanilla's crack particles.

### 34.0 Decisions (approved)
1. Caves are where metal lives, and the trip is a story. 2. New land: vanilla's scattered iron, copper, coal and gold at
35%; early lodes open onto cave walls. 3. Our own frequent mouths (hill mouth, Delver adit, doline, cleft) about every
200 m with tells (breath, draught, cairn); Tectonic untouched. 4. The Hearth points to the nearest mouth with the metal
it lacks ("Mark it on my map"), honest when it knows none. 5. The strike rebuilt: chips of the block's texture, spark
streaks, a breath of dust, new cracks; vanilla's crack particles replaced. 6. True strikes on ores. 7. The Delver's
Pick and its six verses replace the tool ladder; Hunter mattock recipes retire. 8. The pick is pulled from the stone at
the first adit (handed over at the Hearth when no adit is near). 9. Cave air (bands, Lens haze, motes, shafts, the Deep
breathes). 10. Delver lamps. 11. Strike and cave sounds from CC0 recordings (each download listed to Euan first).
12. The Hollows in every cave by depth, drawn by strikes, wary of light. 13. One session, P1 (the first iron trip)
first, then P2 (pick, lamps), P3 (air, dark), P4 (styles, more mouths).

### 34.1 Mouths (built, P1d: hill mouth and adit; P4: cleft and doline)
- **Place** `awaken:delve/mouth` (`delve.cave.Mouth`, `CaveKind.MOUTH`, appended so older kinds keep their ordinals),
  structure set `delve/mouths`: random spread 10/3 (160 m a candidate; 12/4 before 8 Nov), salt 734018553,
  `#minecraft:is_overworld`, new land only. Spec at the lip's floor, rot forward = into the hill; p: form, throat length,
  its drop, arch width, height, the lode's heart (x, y, z), its ore + 1, the cairn's side, its look (index 10, 1 for
  mouths laid since 8 Nov; 0 for a saved mouth keeps the blocks it built, no worn ground, the old cairn).
- **The promise, on the ground** (Euan's playtest 8 Nov, "I'm really struggling to find a cave entrance"): one mouth about

  the worn ground below). So the candidates are closer together, a doline takes gently tilted ground as well as flat

  dry land (`mouths-deep` tour 42591161111, before the way needed ground under it and wound as a spiral; vanilla noise with
  the final rule, `delve_mouth_density`: one every 197 m). A candidate tries every form at up to five spots within 20 of
  its chunk's middle.
- **What keeps a mouth away**: the city's reserve (90), water or land at or below sea + 1, a biome off the list, and (from
  the seed alone, since 8 Nov) a settlement's ground: within 120 of a grid settlement's or the first hamlet's anchor, or
  in the land a town's region keeps round its heart (`RoadNet.nearTown`). A road is laid after the mouth: its bed fills

- **Ground others stand on** (11 Nov, §21.11): a cave place is cut at `underground_structures`, before anything at the
  surface, so the noise still says ground where a mouth, a sinkhole or an adit has opened the hill, and a thing set there

- **The joint, since 9 Nov** (Euan's playtest 9 Nov, "maybe 10 blocks deep, and then it just stops"): the joint must be a
  real cave. Until then any floor with three of air over it counted, so open ground did: the tunnel of his mouth at -472
  181 -2424 came back out on the hillside 20 blocks round, with a real cave 4 blocks under its floor. In his save 16 of
  the 21 mouths that could be judged had a joint in the open and 1 a tiny pocket; only 4 led on. Now:
  - **Rock over it** (every kind's search, `CaveSites.floors`): the air's top stays `ROOF` (4) under the column's ground.
    Air under water counts: it has rock between it and the water, or it would be full.
  - **How far a mouth looks** (hill mouth, cleft, doline; `CaveSites.joint`): rings 8, 14, 20, 27, 34 of 8 columns each,
    down to 3 for every 1 out, to 50 under the throat's end, nearest first, 4 floors at most. Tectonic's caves lie 8-20

  - **Cave goes on from it** (`roomy`): 2 or more of the 8 columns 6 out hold air near its height with rock over them, and
    none of the 8 is open ground at its level (an overhang on a hillside has rock over it too). On 420 random roofed floors
    in his save the count of 2 keeps 89% of the real caves and halves the small ones.
  - **The way winds** (Mouth p `SWING` 11 and `LEGS` 12, 0 on a straight way and on a saved mouth): a cave too deep to walk
    straight to (past `JOINT_SLOPE` 0.8 down in 1 along) is reached by a spiral ramp, its bends on a circle through both ends
    (radius |`SWING`| 4 to 18, its sign the way it turns), 3 to 6 legs, the fewest legs and smallest circle that give the
    length, every leg as steep as the rest and no steeper than 0.8, no bend turning more than 110° (a leg doubling back
    over the last cuts away its floor, and it can't be climbed: 12 of 54 ways stuck that way). Each bend
    opens into a small landing. The way is read every 4 blocks on the noise's cells, turning either way, and must keep rock over its bore (3 + `ROOF`), ground under it (a drop of 2 at most, `WAY_DROP`, one a body can climb back, until the last 5 of its fall, already in the cave) and stay dry, or
    that floor is passed over. So a tunnel can't break out of the hill or end high on the wall of a natural hall, the first
    tour's fault (2 of 7 mouths on Tectonic). Where natural air has still eaten the rock under the bore it lays rubble (`Carve.tunnel`'s `floored`), the bore's full width and down to 3 deep (§42.4 "Settled", a way's floor), so a way is always a floor to walk on. The piece's box holds the bends.
  - `delve_mouth_joint` holds this on real noise on his seed and walks every fifth way there and back with the real ground
    round it (53 of 53), `delve_cave_routes` walks a staged winding way both ways,
    and `/awaken delve way` walks the last `goto`'s mouth on the world's real blocks and says how much cave lies past
    the joint (tools/autopilot/mouths-deep.txt, the only way to see it on Tectonic).
  - Slope probes still read the noise's 4-block cells so the forms share columns. A mouth saved before this keeps the
    way it built.
- **Delver adit** (tried first): an iron or copper lode within 72 whose heart is at y 24 or above, a hill over the
  drift, an open front, dry; drift 14-28 long, falling 0 to a third of its length, timber sets every 3, rails, ends at

  end (the Delver's Pick in the stone, P1d's next part), a barrel there.
- **Hill mouth**: 8+ of rise in 16, open front, arch 5/7/9 wide and 6-11 high (an ellipse, a rough top, roots and vines
  over the lip), throat 16-40 falling about one in two (a drop of two where the hash says), ground over the end, dry; a

- **Nothing hangs** (11 Nov; Euan's V20, "floating blocks at a cave entrance again, exactly like the camp", by The Capped
  Well): the hill mouth's rule asks for its rise 16 in, so on a gentle slope the hill at the lip stands a block or two over
  the floor and an arch 11 high is open to the sky. Its brow (two courses of rock at arch top + 1 and + 2 out over the
  lip, the new look's collar) was laid anyway and hung 12 over the grass (his mouth at -1656 88 -136). Now each brow
  column at lz -1 is laid only where the hill itself stands at the brow's top course (`h + 2`) in that column, the outer
  course (lz -2) only in front of an inner one; the vines down the face hang only under it (or, in the old look, under

- **Order by the ground** (P4): an adit, else a cleft, else a hill mouth, else a doline.
- **Cleft** (P4): a cliff, 9+ of rise in 6 and 14+ in 14, open in front; a slot 2-4 wide (p W), 16-28 long, its floor
  level through the first 4 then falling one in three to the end; open to the sky (p H: the cliff's height over the lip
  + 2, 8-40) for the first 65% of its length, then the roof steps down to a passage four high; the walls rough and
  leaning apart a little upward, the slot wandering up to about a block each way once inside; vines down both walls,

  holds it on both sides within 5), moss carpet on the floor; ground over its end, dry; a joint to cave air is required.
- **Doline** (P4; gently tilted ground too since 8 Nov): six points round at r + 3 within 4 of the middle (`Mouth.TILT`:
  8 of rise in 16 is a hillside, the hill mouth's) and the hole turned so the near side, where its ledge starts, is within
  1 of the middle; its air now stands 6 above the middle so the high side's ground doesn't roof it; r 3-5 (p W = 2r + 1, 7-11 across),
  10 to min(25, 4r + 5) deep (p DROP, and p H the same); spec at the middle, level with the ground, forward = the way out
  at the bottom. A round hole with a rough edge, the turf's lip overhanging by one with hanging roots under it, vines
  down the walls; the floor fallen rock, coarse dirt and moss; a ledge of fallen rock (cobble, mossy cobble, coarse
  dirt) two wide down the wall from the near side, the fewest half-turns-and-more that keep it no steeper than one down
  in 1.6 along it (so every step is a walk or a jump), reaching out to the lip at the top; a way out of the side at the
  bottom 3 wide and 3 high, r + 3 long, toward the cave air it joins (required). The tells: the breath rises straight
  up out of the hole, the draught's streaks climb its walls, its light shaft falls straight down.
- **Site packing** (P4): the client site's depth is turn | form << 2 (two bits) | height << 4.
- **Names and words**: dolines "The Fallen Floor", "The Sunken Ring", "The Well of Roots"...; clefts "The Narrow Way",
  "The Split Rock", "The Slot"...; the Hearth's line "There's a sinkhole in the ground 180 m south of your home. The cave

  into a cave that runs past iron."; the map mark "The sinkhole" / "The gorge".
- **Cairn** on the open ground in front: stacked cobble walls and an iron-bar spike; at an adit a fence post with a
  lantern. A mouth laid since 8 Nov (p look 1) heaps a 3 x 3 base of cobble and stacks the walls 4-6 high with the spike

- **Worn ground** (since 8 Nov, p look 1, no change to a mouth already saved): what makes a mouth a mark on the land from
  afar, in every biome. In front of a hill mouth, an adit and a cleft a fan of bare ground runs 16 out from the lip,
  widening and ragged at its end, and the shelf of ground in front loses cells at its outer edge; round a doline a ragged ring out to r + 3.5..7 with a few leaning boulders. Soil
  (dirt, grass, sand, snow, clay) wears to rock or scree in soft patches (gravel, rubble, tuff, andesite, the depth's
  rock; a sand country's stays sandstone), two deep, its small plants cleared; so trees and grass can't grow there and
  a log or a build stops the wear. A hill mouth also gets a collar: soil within 3 of the arch, three blocks into the hill,
  turned to rock, and a two-course brow of rock over the arch with roots under it (a dark hole in a grey ring).
- **Tells** (client, `CaveFx`, from the place's site in `CavePlaces.near`: lip, arch width, and turn | form << 2 |
  height << 3): the **plume**, a column of slow mist climbing 25-35 blocks over a mouth (out of a cleft's slot, off the
  arch's lip, straight up from a doline), its own particle `awaken:delve_plume` (quads 2.2-3.6 across, 12-17 s, swelling as
  it rises, thinner close by), one every few ticks by day and thicker at dawn, half as thick again past 110 m (a quad
  there is a few pixels and pale on a pale sky: at the near rate a column was plain at 70 m and all but gone at 130),
  drawn to 220 m (`MOUTH_NEAR` in
  `CavePlaces`, 220, sends a mouth's site that far), so a mouth shows over the treetops from a long walk off; it needs
  only a site, so every mouth already in a world gets it too (mist, plume and breath draw on their own pipeline that
  tests depth but never writes it: Lens's depth haze otherwise fogs each whole quad in the biome's fog colour); the
  **breath**, mist exhaled from the arch's upper half and
  drifting out, strongest at dawn (to 1500, fading to 4000), for 3 minutes after rain, 0.14 by day, 0.35 at dusk, seen
  to 160 m; the **draught**, streaks out of
  the throat within 28 m; the **cold air heard** within 32 m (the breath-of-air loop at the nearest mouth, pitch 0.78;
  to be re-voiced from a recording). Far mist goes straight to the particle engine (the level's own path drops
  particles past 32 blocks; the sinkhole's mist had the same fault and now does the same), never at Minimal particles.
- **The Hearth points** (`delve.cave.MouthPointer`, a task-card source; `HearthHooks.metalNeed`, filled by

  your home. The cave behind it runs past iron." (distance to 10 m, eight ways, the mouth on the card's compass as a

  found: "I don't know of any old workings near your home. Iron shows in cave walls: find a cave and follow its walls."

- **Tests**: `delve_cave_routes` walks every kind (the mouth staged as each form in turn by its seed: adit, hill mouth,

  overworld's noise, biomes and caves (24 x 24 cells, his seed), at least one mouth every 215 m of dry land (the test

  `delve_hearth_points` (the four forms' lines, which mouths lead to which metal, the honest line on flat land, the card's
  3/16 row).

### 34.2 Metal lives in the caves (built, P1c)
- **Wall lodes** (`LodePlans.walls`, on top of each region's existing lodes, which are unchanged so old worlds agree):
  per 256 region 3 iron (y -16..60), 2 copper (0..64), 2 coal (8..72). Each tries 16 columns of the base noise
  (`ChunkGenerator.getBaseColumn`, no carvers; `LodePlans.columns(seed, ...)` installed on overworld load): air you
  could stand in within the ore's band (nearest the rolled height, up to four spots), then out up to 10 cells to the
  first rock at head height with rock behind; the seam then follows the wall's face both ways (each step settling on
  the rock cell with air on its cave side, two in or out, a cell up or down at 12% each), a cell behind or above now and
  then, at most 56 blocks. Not laid without a wall. On seed 3405691582's vanilla noise, 4 regions: 16 of 28 laid (10
  iron), 86% of their blocks face air (`delve_lodes_air`). A wall lode planned into chunks generated before this
  build doesn't exist there.
- **Thinning** (`awaken:thin_ores`, a biome modifier at AFTER_EVERYTHING on `#minecraft:is_overworld`): in each biome's
  underground ores, vanilla's ore_iron_upper/middle/small, ore_copper(_large), ore_coal_upper/lower, ore_gold,
  ore_gold_lower, ore_gold_extra are swapped for `awaken:thinned/<name>`, the same feature at 35% of the count (90→31,
  10→4, 10→4, 16→6, 16→6, 30→10, 20→7, 4→1, 50→18; ore_gold_lower keeps its count behind a rarity filter of 3).
  Diamonds, redstone, lapis, emerald untouched; generated chunks keep theirs. Test `delve_thinned_ores`.

### 34.3 The strike (built, P1a/P1b)
- **Particles** (`delve.client.StrikeFx`, `StrikeChip`): client extensions on every block `delve.StrikeBlocks` names
  (vanilla's `*_ore`, the rock list, the loose-ground list, our lode hearts and Deepglass), claimed last on our bus and
  only where `isBlockRegistered` is false. `addHitEffects` returns true (vanilla's per-tick crumbs gone); the bite is
  drawn from `playHitSound` (the server's progress event 2020, every fourth tick, so onlookers see it too); the sound
  stays vanilla's until the recordings. A bite: 2-4 chips (1-2 decreased, none minimal); a break: 8-14 chips (4-7) and
  3-5 dust wisps in the block's map colour (2). Chips: a 3/16 square of the block's particle sprite, tinted as vanilla's,
  shade 0.72-0.82, size 0.034-0.07, tumbling (the leaf technique), world light read every 4 ticks, one bounce off the
  floor when falling faster than 0.09, then lying flat 0.6-1.6 s and shrinking out. At most 48 chips from mining.
- **Streaks** (sparks): fixed arrays, at most 24; additive lines (the lamp's glow pipeline) from the head back 1.5 ticks
  of flight, white-gold cooling to the ore's tint, life 4-8 ticks, skitter off full blocks (axis bounce 0.4). Only off
  pickaxe-mineable blocks of hardness ≥ 1 struck with a mining tool: 2-6 a bite, 6-10 on the last blow, +4 and hotter on
  a true strike (halved when decreased). The heavy strike's sparks are streaks too. The old round spark and grit
  sprites stay only for vents, cave-ins and blocks we don't draw.
- **Cracks**: `minecraft:textures/block/destroy_stage_0..9` redrawn (`tools/art/specs/delve_cracks.py`): one crack tree
  that grows from the strike's point, branches and widens, chips spalling in stages 8-9; dark 58 / 34, lit lip 166 on
  the upper-left. The ore's warm glow in the cracks is not possible (the crumbling blend multiplies), so it was dropped.
- **True strikes** (`delve.TrueStrikes`): the seam on (pos, face, n = true strikes so far) is a seeded point 0.22-0.78
  across the face with an angle; a bite whose hit point lies within 0.22 of it is true. The client predicts, sends
  `delve_true_strike` (pos, face, n); the server accepts when the block is an ore of `Ore`, within reach + 1, n matches
  its count, ≥ 3 ticks since the last, and its own `pick` from the eye hits that face within 0.32; otherwise it sends
  `delve_true_strike_sync` with its count. Speed: × (1 + 0.35 n), at most × 2, on both sides through `BreakSpeed`
  (LOWEST, after Veins' two blows); the server's progress (speed × ticks) is never below the client's sum, so a
  predicted break is never refused. A break within 6 ticks of a true strike: 25% one more of the first drop
  (`BlockDropsEvent`). The seam is drawn while a mining tool looks at an ore (tapered additive line, the ore's tint
  toward white, breathing); the chime `delve.true_strike` (synth, the magic layer) at the Tuning Fork's ore pitch, a
  whole tone up for each true strike in a row (up to three).
- **Dig motion** (`delve.client.DigMotion`, first person): keyed to the client's bites (contact at phase 0): pick recoil
  to 0.16, wind-up to 0.68 (+17° pitch, back 0.07), strike eased in to the next bite (−15°); a shovel thrusts and lifts,
  drawn back low. Eases out within 3 ticks of letting go; 0.4 with reduced motion. A view nudge of 0.22° a bite (0.45°
  true) through `CombatFeedback.kick`. Third person keeps vanilla's swing.
- **Settings** (`awaken-delve-client.toml`): `strike_particles`, `true_strikes` (both on).

### 34.4 The Delver's Pick (built: asleep P1d, the verses and their gifts P2)
- **Item** `awaken:waking_pick`, "Delver's Pick" (the cave module's relic keeps `awaken:delvers_pick`, the Delver's Old
  Pick, carried for the fork's reach). Asleep it is a stone pickaxe (1 damage, -2.8 speed), rare, in
  `#minecraft:pickaxes` (so the dig motion, the strike and enchanting take it). Kept through death (`WakingPick.onDrops`
  and `onRespawn`, as Relics do).
- **The pick in the stone** `awaken:waking_pick_stone` (no item, unbreakable, immovable): a mound of cobbled deepslate
  with the pick's head driven in and its handle leaning out, at the adit's "pick" mark before the end face. Use it:
  your own pick if you don't carry one ("You already carry the Delver's Pick. This one stays for whoever comes next."
  otherwise); the first pull counts `awaken:delve/pick_pulled` and shows a moment: "It's asleep, but it still knows
  metal. Hold it and it hums when its head points at a lode nearby."
- **No adit near home**: when the Hearth's search finds no adit (none at all, or a hill mouth), the Hearth hands the
  pick over once (never pulled, not carried): "There's no old adit near your home, so your Hearth kept this for you".
- **Hum**: twice a second while it's in your main hand the server finds the nearest lode block within 16 of your eyes
  (any ore; a lone broken heart doesn't count) and sends `delve_pick_hum` when it changes; the client (`PickSong`) hums
  at the ore's fork pitch ×2 (to 2.0), from nothing outside 40° off your view to full facing it, louder nearer
  (0.7 × 6/(6+d)), round the listener. The deep hum's loop for now; to be re-voiced from a recording.
- **Art** (`tools/art/specs/delve.py`): the icon (worn dark-iron head, ash handle, leather grip, an unlit Deepglass
  thread on the head's spine) and the stone's parts sheet.
- **Test** `delve_waking_pick` (one pick per carrier, the stone stays, the pull counted, stone-tier drops, the hum's
  16-block reach).
- **Verses** (`PickVerses`, component `awaken:pick_verses` = `{schemaVersion 1, verse}` on the item, synced): each sets
  the pick's `tool` (what it can't take, its speed), `max_damage`, attack modifiers and `custom_model_data` (floats
  `[verse]`, read by `items/waking_pick.json`'s `range_dispatch`, seven icons: the spine's Deepglass thread lights
  ember, then blue; Tempered turns the edge blue-white; Glass violet; Hush darkens the head; Call gilds it):

  | # | Verse | Wakes when (deed counter or rite) | Can't take | Speed | Uses | Blow |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 0 | Asleep | pulled / handed over | `#incorrect_for_stone_tool` | 4 | 131 | 1 |
  | 1 | I · Kindle | a lode's heart breaks with it on you (`awaken:delve/deed_heart`) | iron's | 6 | 400 | 2 |
  | 2 | II · Echo | you light a Delver lamp with it on you (`deed_lamp`) | iron's | 6.5 | 500 | 2 |
  | 3 | III · Tempered | your Forge, 3 diamonds | diamond's | 8 | 1561 | 3 |
  | 4 | IV · Glass | you cut Deepglass with it on you (`deed_deepglass`) | diamond's | 8.5 | 1800 | 3 |
  | 5 | V · Hush | a seep falls quiet with you in it, carrying it (`deed_seep`) | netherite's | 9 | 2031 | 4 |
  | 6 | VI · Call | your Forge, a starmetal ingot | netherite's | 10 | 2600 | 4 |

  A deed is counted once (only while you carry the pick); after any deed or rite, every carried pick wakes verse after
  verse while the next one's deed is done (a deed done early waits for the verses before it; a rite always stops the
  run). Each wake: the tier, a low ring, light gathering round the hand (`delve_pick_woke`), a moment window ("The pick
  wakes: I · Kindle" and the gift in words). `awaken:delve/verses_woken` is the furthest verse woken: a pick given
  later (pulled, handed over, re-forged) comes at it. The tooltip shows the verse, each gift woken, and "Next: ...".
- **Trail** "The Delver's Pick" (`trail/the_delvers_pick.json`, area deep, linear; Euan 2026-10-28: "add the Delver's Pick
  to the Journal and Trails, so it's findable before you have it and shows the next step after"): opens with a home or a
  pulled pick; step one is the pull (`counter:awaken:delve/pick_pulled`) with the place `adit`, then one step per verse on
  `count:awaken:delve/verses_woken:<n>`, the Forge rites pointing at `hearth`. `cave.PickTrail` registers `adit`: the nearest
  adit (any ore) within 400 of your home (of you, with no home, asked again once you're 96 away), searched off the server
  thread as the Hearth's metal search is; a home with no adit in reach is handed the pick, as the metal card does, so the
  first step can always be done. Test `delve_pick_trail` (one step per verse in order, the place, the hand-over on flat land).
- **Gifts** (`PickGifts`; client `PickFx`):
  - *Kindle*: sneak and start striking bare rock (strike family ROCK): an **ember** sticks in the air cell on that face
    for 5 minutes, three a player (a fourth puts out your oldest), none within 5 of another of yours. Drawn light, no
    block: saved in `DelveData` (schema 2: `embers` = light cell, rock face, until, owner), sent to the level's players
    on change, login and dimension change (`delve_embers`); `TorchGlow` draws each within 48 as a light of its own
    (level 12, `#FF9A50`, flickering, no floor pool; with held light off in the settings they don't show), with sparks.
  - *Echo*: sneak and use the pick on bare rock while still (server's known movement < 0.05 a tick): a ring through
    the rock; for 4 s ores (full blocks, their ore's tint; any `#c:ores` warm gold) and the open air of caves (a 2-block
    lattice of points, not under open sky) within 12 light as the ring passes (0.8 blocks a tick) and glow through
    everything (pipeline `delve_through`, depth always-pass), at most 320 ores and 900 points. 20 s rest. The server
    sends only `delve_pick_sight` (kind 0, the struck block); the client reads its own world.
  - *Tempered*: true strikes' aim radius 0.22 → 0.32 (`TrueStrikes.radius`, both sides).
  - *Glass*: a heavy strike released on the glint while looking 30° or more up does not bore: for 5 s the rock in a
    cone before your eyes (cos ≥ 0.78, 22 blocks) turns to glass to your eyes: hidden cave air (rock between it and
    your eyes), ores, and living creatures (their boxes, live) show through. 40 s rest. Client-only: the server names
    no block (`delve_pick_sight` kind 1).
  - *Hush*: the pick in hand cancels the `minecraft:block_destroy` game event from you (no vibration: sculk, wardens;
    the deep's noise rule asks `PickGifts.hushed`); sneaking, it mines at full speed off the ground (x5) and with your
    head in water (÷ the submerged attribute).
  - *Call*: a heart broken with it: the lode's blocks still standing within 8 of the heart (nearest first, at most 24,
    each one a heavy strike may take: no ward, civic ground or anyone else's Hearth) crack one after another over
    3 s, their drops going straight to you (`delve_call_answer` draws the ore flying home).
- **The Forge** (right-click an `awaken:forge` not inside anyone else's Hearth with the pick in hand; the Forge's own
  use is skipped): the next rite if you carry it (3 diamonds wake Tempered; a starmetal ingot wakes Call), else an
  iron ingot mends a quarter of its uses, else it says what's next. With 3 iron ingots in hand, no pick on you and one
  pulled before, it makes another at your furthest verse ("The Delver's Pick, again").
- **Not done**: the Hunter mattock recipes still craft (retiring them touches gear's and Arms' rows: the gear
  module's call); the pick keeps vanilla's sounds.
- **Tests** `delve_pick_verses` (each wake once and in order, an early deed waits, the rite takes 3 diamonds, tier
  and uses follow, a mend, a re-forge at your verse), `delve_pick_hush` (no block-destroy event), `delve_pick_call`
  (the 24 nearest of that lode within 8, nothing further or not of the lode, the ore to the player).

### 34.5 The air below (built: motes P1e; bands, cave air, the breath, shafts, the Hollows by band, strike noise P3)
- **Motes in your light** (`delve.client.Motes`, particle `awaken:delve_light_mote`: the mote's frames, lit by the world
  so it shows only where light falls): underground (`under` ≥ 0.3, not in water), carrying a light in either hand
  (`HeldLight`, the offhand's when it wins) or wearing the miner's lamp (12, flame), dust hangs in the air within 70% of
  the light's reach of your eyes, three in four in front of you, only in air; spawned at 30/90 a tick × `under` so about
  30 live (life 70-110 ticks, size 0.018-0.038, alpha 0.6, a slow wander, barely falling), tinted 35% toward the
  light's colour from dust grey; half at Decreased particles, none at Minimal.
- **Bands** (`delve.api.Bands`, pure): **the Shallows** (y ≥ 40), **the Middle Dark** (0-39), **the Deep** (< 0), each
  with an air colour (`#8FA3B8`, `#B08A58`, `#5A3C7A`). The client (`Depths`) knows your band while `under` ≥ 0.5 and
  shows its caption the first time you enter it each play-day ("THE MIDDLE DARK", "warm, still air"; CaveHud's
  caption). A plain cave's Lens place look (layer 0) is now its band's: `awaken:shallows` (cool blue-grey),
  `awaken:middle_dark` (amber, lights glowing gold), `awaken:deep` (ink and violet, deeper corners), in
  `looks_delve.json`; `awaken:underground` stays for when no band is known. Cave biomes keep their own looks.
- **Cave air** (`Depths`, client setting `cave_air`, on): under the rock the game's own atmospheric fog is drawn in,
  by `under`: from about 8 blocks out to about 52 (16 to 60 where you stand in block light), never under water, in
  lava, snow or a status effect's fog; its colour goes 85% toward the band's air × 0.16 (coloured dark, not black). It
  works with Lens on or off (Lens grades the frame over it). Lens's own cave-air look fields (`caveAirNear`,
  `caveAirFar`, `caveAirTint`) are still only names: when Lens reads them they should override these numbers per
  look (the gate-worlds plan sets them for its worlds, which the overworld's `Depths` doesn't reach). Not built here:
  it's the Lens module's code.
- **The Deep breathes** (`Breath`): every 3-6 minutes while `under` ≥ 0.7 (not in water) an exhale runs toward the
  nearest mouth's lip or sinkhole's rim the server has named (else the way you face): the cave breath's sound, low
  (pitch 0.55), from 10 behind you and again 14 ahead, and dust (`delve_draught`) streaming along the floor within 8
  for 4 s, most in its middle; in the Deep the hum swells with it (`delve.deep.hum`, 0.6 pitch).
- **Light shafts** (`Shafts`): while the sky isn't dark or rainy, up to 3 shafts at the nearest mouths and sinkholes
  within 64: down a sinkhole's throat (its depth, at least 8; width 0.45 × its radius) and slanting in under a mouth's
  arch along its way in (9 blocks); each three camera-facing additive ribbons in pale sunlight, bright at the top,
  gone below.
- **The Hollows by band**: `delve_hollows_bands` adds drip lurkers (10), chime crickets (12) and hushlings (8) to every
  overworld biome but the cave biomes (`neoforge:and` with `neoforge:not #c:is_underground`: dripstone caves, lush caves
  and the deep dark keep fauna's own Hollows, never twice); terrain's `terrain_biome_table_parity` rows carry the three;
  fauna's own rule (cave ground under a roof, dark, the role caps) still decides, and asks
  `Bands.allows` (no hushling in the Shallows). Higher levels in the Deep are fauna's levels as they are.
- **Strikes are noise** (`StrikeNoise`): rock or ore (not loose ground) broken under the rock by a player calls every
  mob in `#awaken:delve/hears_strikes` (hushling, drip lurker) within 24 that has no target: it paths to the block.
  A Hushed pick makes none; a player's call rests 40 ticks.
- **Recorded sounds** (Euan approved four CC0 BigSoundBank recordings by Joseph Sardin, 2026-10-28; sources, licence
  and the rebuild in `tools/art/sources/delve/README.md`, cut by `tools/art/specs/audio_cave_recorded.py`; files in
  `sounds/delve/`, events written by `audio_caves.py` into merge/delve_sense):
  - **The band's room tone** `delve.band.room` (Cave #1, a 12 s crossfaded loop, its hiss eased above 5.2 kHz): round
    the listener while under (`Depths`), level 0.55 / 0.7 / 0.8 and pitch 1 / 0.88 / 0.76 for the Shallows, the Middle
    Dark and the Deep, times the square root of "under" and the Conductor's nature level, half in the deep dark, none
    under water; streamed.
  - **The breath re-voiced** `delve.cave.breath` (Cave #1's lows under 700 Hz, a 10 s loop); the synthesised
    `amb_cave_breath` is gone.
  - **Stone settling re-voiced** `delve.cave.settle` (the four loudest separate falls in Fall of Stone); the
    synthesised `amb_cave_settle_*` are gone. CaveSound plays them as before.
  - **"The cave answers"** `delve.cave.answers` (`CaveAnswers`): 30 ticks after a heart breaks, from 18 blocks off in a
    direction fixed by the lode at the heart's height, a hammer's knock (Hammer fall on concrete) and then an anvil's
    last strike (Anvil #1) slowed to 0.6, in a convolved cave room, 6.6 s; volume 3 (heard within 48), pitched to the
    ore: coal 0.75, copper 0.84, iron 0.89, redstone 0.94, gold 1, lapis 1.06, emerald 1.12, diamond 1.19, Deepglass
    0.67.
  - Drips stay synthesised (none of the four is a drip).
- **Not done**: lights don't lean or dim with the breath; nothing heard in game yet.
- **Tests** `delve_bands` (band by height; hushlings not in the Shallows), `delve_strike_noise` (a hushling 13 off is
  called and paths; a Hushed pick calls none; a second strike within the rest calls none), `delve_band_sounds` (the
  four events registered, their sounds.json entries name shipping recordings under 400 KB; an answer waits, then
  plays).

### 34.6 Delver lamps (built, P2)
- **Block** `awaken:delver_lamp` (`lit` false/true; light 3 dead, 14 lit; iron, immovable, cutout model: a clouded
  crystal in an iron cage with cap and hook; breaks for 2-4 iron nuggets). Hung from the roof on one or two iron chains:
  over a seep's hall and a grotto's room (`Carve.lamp`), and in natural caverns by `awaken:delve/lamps`
  (underground decoration, one chunk in three, three tries a chunk for air with a solid roof over 8+ of air and 6 clear
  each way at half height, y -48..48).
- **Strike** a dead lamp with anything in `#minecraft:pickaxes` (left-click; it doesn't start breaking): it lights
  (bell and chime), counts the Echo deed for whoever struck it, and floods: a breadth-first walk through air from it
  (euclid ≤ 40, at most 24,000 cells, an unloaded chunk is a wall), sharing 1 ms a tick with every other lamp. Then
  the lattice: per 6³ cube of reached air, the cell nearest the cube's middle; the 120 nearest the lamp. The wave goes
  out at 0.8 blocks a tick: each lattice cell becomes `minecraft:light` level 11 as it's reached (only if still air),
  the lamp saved with its lights as they're set (`DelveData` schema 2, `lamps` = pos, lights, name). Nearby players
  see each light bloom (`delve_lamp_lit`) and the caption "THE IRON HALL · lamp lit" (the cave place's name, else the
  nearest lode's ore within 32, else a name by depth). Lit lamps are pins on the Atlas (`delve_lamps_known`).
  Lattice 6 and level 11 leave every reached cell some block light, so no monster spawns in the hall.
- **Broken**, the lamp takes back every one of its lights that is still a light block.
- **Not done**: a flood cut off by a server stop isn't resumed (the lamp stays lit with what it had set); the way home
  doesn't count lit halls yet.
- **Test** `delve_lamp_lattice` (lights only in the reached hall, ≤ 120, none in a sealed pocket, every hall cell
  lit, all gone with the lamp).

### 34.7 Cave styles from the land above (built, P4)
- **Decoration, no cave biomes**: the feature `awaken:delve/styles` (`delve.CaveStyleFeature`, underground_decoration,
  every overworld chunk) reads the biome over the chunk's middle (`CaveStyle.of`, OCEAN_FLOOR_WG height) and makes 20
  tries for a pocket of cave air from y -56 to 10 below the ground, dressing its roof, floor or a wall. Only bare stone,
  deepslate, tuff, granite, diorite, andesite and calcite are dressed (lodes, ores and places stay). New chunks only.
- **Styles** (`CaveStyle`; an underground biome, ocean or river gives none):
  - **Roots** (forests, taiga, jungle, Elderwood, Lumen Forest): rooted dirt in the roof with hanging roots, glow
    berries on cave vines 2-5 long (berries on every other), moss and moss carpet on the floor.
  - **Sunshard** (Glass Steppe), **Frostspar** (Frost Spires): a growth on the floor (a crystal base in the rock, one to
    three crystal blocks standing on it, its cluster on top, a few small ones round it); with no floor, a seam.
    **Fault seam** (Shattered Highlands): a seam of 4-7 blocks in the nearest wall at chest height. The crystals are the
    Lands' own blocks by id (none when the Lands pack is off); mined, they're the Forge's catalysts (HEAT, FROST, GRAVITY).
  - **Sand** (deserts, badlands): smooth sandstone and sandstone patches on the floor, sandstone in the roof, a band of
    cut sandstone round the pocket's walls.
  - **Ice** (snowy and icy lands): packed ice patches in the floor (a blue ice heart now and then) and roof, ice hanging
    one or two from the roof.
- **Its air** (client, `Depths`): once a second while under, the style of the camera column's land (WORLD_SURFACE);
  the cave air's colour leans half way from the band's to the style's (roots 0x4E6B3A, sunshard 0xB07A2E, frostspar
  0x4A7FA8, fault seam 0x6A4C8C, sand 0xA8783A, ice 0x3E78A8), and the motes in your light take the style's dust (amber
  under sand, pale blue under snow, green-gold under woods).
- **Test** `delve_cave_styles` (which land gives which style; each style dresses a stone room's roof and floor).

## 35. Bosses, levelled up (the Creature Kit and the Boss Plate; plan docs/bosses/PLAN.md, page https://claude.ai/artifact/RG6JGgiSwrTvg53WACTqhY; Euan approved all fourteen recommendations 2026-10-28: "Go with all recommendations")

Euan: bosses should look, move and fight like Elden Ring's, through a system that every creature can reuse, and they
should show a boss bar of our own. What he approved (PLAN §7):
1. **The Creature Kit**: body plans, a move library, a signature move for each boss, and moves the server sees.
2. Every boss gets **its own body at true size**, never a scaled vanilla one.
3. The look: **chunky blocks, one oversized feature, and one light story** (core, eyes and cracks that change with the fight).
4. **A showcase first**: the Ember Tyrant, Unit Zero and Mother of Spores. Euan looks at them in game before the roll-out.
5. **The Boss Plate** replaces the vanilla bar for all our bosses and Wardens. It lifts off the boss's head when the fight starts.
6. **Colour means one thing**: the bar and level chip show heat against the viewer's level, and the boss's own colour is on the rim only.
7. **Phase lines leave the chat** and appear under the plate. Signature moves show their name for a moment.
8. **The Lord retune** from the combat sim, re-run with the move tables.
9. **Delayed blows only on HEAVY moves**, at most 0.6 s, and only where the held pose is unmistakable.
10. **Every creature moves onto the kit**, in waves after the bosses.
11. **The colossus** waits behind a probe. Then one prototype, in a test arena reached by an admin command only.
12. Climbing the colossus comes later, with its own OK.
13. This session builds phases 0 and 1. Euan decides on splitting the roll-out after that.
14. Euan checks in game whether Fresh Animations reaches our vanilla-bodied gate monsters.

### 35.1 The Boss Plate (`living.client.BossPlate`, data through `core.api.BossPlates`)
- **The server keeps its `ServerBossEvent`.** That keeps the rules for who sees a bar: same storey, and gate rooms
  through `GateHooks.showsBossBar` once Codex's gate-room work lands. When a player starts tracking a bar-carrying mob,
  the mobs module sends a **bind** (`BossPlates.bind`). The bind carries:
  - the bar's UUID and the entity id;
  - the plate kind (`LORD` for bosses and nightmares, `WARDEN`);
  - the phase marks (the health fractions where phases begin, from `MobDef.phases`);
  - the boss's glow.
