    tooltip says it ("Inlaid with Frostspar: +0.25 toughness").
  - **Fold (A and up).** After the shaping the netherite is doubled over and struck in pairs: three folds, each two
    strikes on one mark (`foldMarks`, down the middle of the piece), to the Fold's own rhythm (`FOLD_RHYTHM`, 4 ticks a
    step, "xx......": quick-quick, then a rest), counted in like the shaping. Its strikes follow the shaping's in the same
    list (`ForgeWork.stageFrom`/`strikesNeeded`); the fold's mark is their mean (`ForgeWork.fold`). They ring low (pitch
    0.8). The metal flares back up a little with each fold.
  - **Starfire (S).** After the fold the heat goes white: a fast chain of eight marks scattered over the face
    (`starfireMarks`, new each time from the stage's start, each well away from the last) to `STARFIRE_RHYTHM` (4 ticks
    a step, "x.x.x.x."); the screen shows only the next few, white, and a struck mark is gone. Its mark is the mean
    (`ForgeWork.starfire`); they ring high (1.2). The strikes' mean the quality weighs stays the shaping's.
  - **Tune (B and up).** The cold Deepglass rings true at one spot on the piece's face (`truePoint`, from the stage's
    start: -0.5..0.5 across, -0.6..0.6 along, in the face's half-widths). Tap it (TAP: the tap's number, x and z; the
    client finds the spot under the cursor): each note is clearer and nearer its pitch the nearer the spot (`clarity`,
    1 - distance / 1.1); the screen marks each tap in its colour and says clearer or duller than before. Within 0.15 it
    rings true: the tune is 1, the piece is marked rung true ("Its Deepglass rings true") and the tuning ends. Otherwise
    the best of five taps counts; left 600 ticks, what was found.
- **Stepping away.** The work lives on the stand (`ForgeWork`, schemaVersion 2: the P3 tune, taps and inlay and the P4
  fold and starfire optional, the judged list growing to heat, cut, quench, tune, inlay, fold, starfire;
  synced to everyone near so they see the bar glow and the shape form). It only moves while its smith is at it (`ArmourForge.AT`, not saved): Esc, logging out
  or walking 12 blocks away holds it; coming back restarts the stage (counted in again).
- **Finishing** fits the piece onto the stand (the piece there before goes to your pack) with its `awaken:forged`
  story (§44.7). All four of one set on the stand wakes it (a flare and a sound); the first time you make a set whole
  the System names it and what wearing it does (a Revelation window with its set bonus lines). Sneak-use takes the suit.
- **Client** (`armour.client`): `FittingStandRenderer` draws the suit on its form and the work: a squat blank glowing in
  the Forge's mouth, then laid face up on the anvil drawing toward the piece strike by strike and cooling (the armour
  shader's heat mode: overlay bit 9, heat in the energy channel, dull red to white, lit from within). `ForgeCamera`
  (a client-only camera entity, as the opening's): wide on stand, anvil and Forge while choosing, over the shoulder at
  the fire, still and close above the metal for the strikes, low for the quench, down on the works table, a slow turn
  round the stand for the fit; hands, block outline, your own body and the HUD (bar subtitles and chat) step aside.
  `ForgeScreen` (the list) and `ForgeSongScreen` (the gauge, the marks projected onto the metal with approach rings, a
  beat lane, pips per strike, the cut line, the helper's off-beats, the result card). The smith's client plays its own
  pull, strikes, notes and quench the moment they happen (the server plays them to everyone else), the count-in and a
  soft tap on each beat. Neither screen pauses the game.
- Sounds `awaken:forge.*` (`tools/art/specs/audio_forge.py`, from CC0 recordings): a strike for each metal (hide,
  copper, iron, diamond, Deepglass, netherite, starmetal by rank), bellows, pull, quench, count, note (a bell at C5,
  pitched per note), cut, fit, wake, miss.
- Progression counters `awaken:armour_started`, `awaken:armour_forged`.
- **Patterns (P2).** The Hunter sets come with rank and the E sets are known from the start; every other set needs its
  pattern (the stand lists it greyed, "Pattern not found", and says where patterns come from). A pattern is an item
  (`PatternItem`, stacks to 16): use it to learn the set for good (`ArmouryMemory.patterns`); one already known says so
  and can be given away. Patterns drop from gate creatures (`ArmourPatterns`, needs a player's kill and a gate id on
  `MobRole`): an elite 20%, a warden 50%, the gate's Lord always. The set is one of the gate's rank (its content level as
  `ArmsApi.rankOfLevel`) whose pattern the killer doesn't know; a Lord gives its rank's Lord-forged set first, other
  creatures never give one (at A and S the Lord-forged sets are Hunter sets and need none, so a Lord gives one of its
  rank's other four). Nothing drops once you know them all.

**44.5 Set abilities (P2).** `ArmourAbilities` (server; state `awaken:armour_state`, unsaved: a relog starts empty).
A made set's own pieces: **two** give its archetype's half bonus, **four** its archetype's ability and its own twist
(§44.6). A Hunter set keeps its own bonuses (`gear/SetBonus`) and, whole, gains its archetype's ability too; the
Lord-forged have no archetype ability, their twist is the Lord's move. Only one set is ever whole. Every piece is
counted on each equipment change.
- **Half bonuses** (two of a made set; one each even with two sets): Bulwark +1 heart; Strider falls hurt a third less
  (fall damage multiplier -1/3); Channeler powers +10%; Duelist +6% attack speed; Lord-forged +1 heart and +0.2
  knockback resistance. A Channeler piece adds its +3% power damage worn alone.
- **The fight's moments** come from `FightMoments` (§12): arms' HIT, FINISHER, DEFLECT, PERFECT_DODGE, BREAK, KILL,
  GUARD, PERFECT_HEAVY and powers' CAST.
- **Bastion** (Bulwark): a charge to 100; a guarded blow +20, a deflect +30, a blow taken +8. Full, the next deflect,
  guard or perfect heavy bursts: everyone hostile within 3.5 takes the ability's blow (4 + 2 a rank above E), is thrown
  back (1.1, lifted 0.35) and staggered 30 ticks; a shockwave and a quake.
- **Flow** (Strider): a perfect dodge +35, wall-running +2 a tick, sliding +1 a tick. Full, the next blow that would land
  (any blow a fighter could answer: `Strikes.of` not NONE) strikes an afterimage instead, and you run 30% faster for
  40 ticks. (The plan's "the dodge carries twice as far" needs the Runner's insides; this is the same promise kept from
  outside.)
- **Edge** (Duelist): a deflect +35, a finisher +30, a clean hit +6, a perfect dodge +20. Full, your next hit sends a
  wave along its swing: everyone else within 5 blocks and 50° of your heading takes 80% of your attack damage.
- **Runes** (Channeler): each power you cast puts a rune circling you, up to three, each lasting 400 ticks from the last
  cast. A cast with three overchannels: the runes fly at the three nearest foes within 8 (the ability's blow, as
  magic), and your powers hit 35% harder for 40 ticks.
- An ability's own blow on a body of 150 health or more is held to 3% of it (at least 2): a Lord is never burst down by
  armour.
- **By rank (P3).** The ability grows with the set's own rank (a Hunter set's too; the set's lines say what it does):
  - C: Bastion: a landing from 4 blocks or more with Bastion full bursts it. Flow: foes within 3 of the afterimage swing
    at it and are staggered 20 ticks (the plan's "wall-runs last longer" is the Runner's insides; this is the Strider's
    C step from outside). Runes: each rune stops one arrow or bolt (a projectile's blow cancelled, a rune spent). Edge: a
    perfect dodge with Edge full cuts the wave at once, toward the creature dodged.
  - B: Bastion: the burst carries the Force of your last power hit (its damage type, so the Forces' reactions follow;
    its slam in the Force's colours). Flow: an afterimage left in the air rushes you on along your look (1.1, lifted
    0.25). Runes: an overchannel gives back a quarter of your energy. Edge: those the wave cuts bleed, 1 every 10 ticks
    for 60.
  - A (P4): Bastion, Flow and Edge hold a **second charge** (filling to 200; a release spends 100, the rest waits); a
    Channeler gathers a **fourth rune** and overchannels four.
  - S (P4): everything the ability does **reaches half again as far** (`S_REACH` 1.5: the Bastion's burst, Edge's wave,
    the runes' reach and the foes who reel from an afterimage).
- **The look.** The charge and runes go to the wearer and everyone tracking them (`Charge` payload: entity, charge,
  runes, flash; sent when the charge moves 5, fills or empties, the runes change, or something is released, and to
  anyone who starts tracking). On the armour (`ArmourGlow`): as the charge fills its glowing parts brighten and its rim
  takes the accent (energy up to two thirds); full it breathes (1.4 s); a release flares the whole set for 450 ms. A
  Channeler's runes are its set's own little mesh (`armour/<set>/rune.mesh`: amber seeds, little lamps, Veil-stones)
  circling at the chest once every 64 ticks, growing in over 300 ms, drawn full-bright.
- **Sounds** `awaken:armour.*` (`audio_forge.py`): charged, bastion, flow, edge, rune (three notes of one chord, rising
  as runes gather), overchannel, ring, rooted, gore.
- **Mastery** (P2 to III; IV and V P3): blows dealt or taken with a whole set on +1, an elite's or a warden's kill
  +5, a gate Lord's +60, written onto every worn piece of that set in tens (`Forged.mastery`). Steps at 0, 300, 1200,
  3000, 6000 (I to V; `Forged.MASTERY`). The tooltip shows it ("Mastery II (420 / 1200)"); the System says when a set
  grows into a new step. II: the trims catch more light. III: what glows of itself glows more, and when the wearer is
  under 35% health it beats with their heart (a double beat about seventy a minute), seen by everyone. Shader: the
  overlay's bits 10-12 the step, bit 13 the wearer is low. IV (P3): each piece at IV grows its set's awakened parts,
  drawn over its own (the kit's `awake` geometry, written as `<piece>_<bone>_awakened.mesh`: longer horns, a further
  crest, a longer cape, a set's own). V (P3): with all four of one drawn set at V its aura moves about the wearer
  (`ArmourAura`: tiny full-bright motes worked out from the time alone, nothing spawned or kept), each set its own way:
  rising off the shoulders, falling from the face, circling the head, drifting about the body, ringing out from the
  chest in a heartbeat, winking on the plate, or streaming back as if in wind. Stands and everyone else show it too.

**44.6 Set twists.** Each set's own full-set twist on top of its archetype's ability (§44.5).
- **Wildhide: Pounce** (P0, replaces Hunter's Sense, which outlined creatures through walls). Crouch at least 10 ticks,
  then jump: you leap along your look's heading (0.95 forward, 0.62 up; the jumping client applies it, movement being the
  client's). The server sees the same jump (vanilla replays it) and holds the leap for 50 ticks: the first melee hit in
  that time deals +50% and shoves the target 0.7 along your heading, with crit sparks; then the leap is spent. 60 ticks
  cooldown. Numbers in `gear/SetBonus` (`POUNCE_*`), logic in `gear/Pounce`.
- **Bellguard: Ring.** A deflect rings the armour like a bell: everyone hostile within 3 staggered 20 ticks; 60 ticks
  cooldown.
- **Rootwarden: Rooted.** A cast while standing still on the ground: no knockback for 40 ticks, and you mend half a
  heart; 40 ticks cooldown.
- **Amberwing: Tempo.** A deflect or a perfect dodge: +15% attack speed and +10% speed for 60 ticks (the plan's "rhythm
  steps last twice as long" needs arms' insides; this is the same tempo from outside).
- **Cleftrunner: Slipstream.** Coming out of a wall-run or a slide: +25% speed for 30 ticks.
- **Lanternlight: Kindle.** While your runes burn, anyone who strikes you in melee within 4 catches fire for 60 ticks.
- **Bladeward: Parry Ward.** After a deflect, blows that land in the next 40 ticks do half.
- **Hornlord: Gore.** Sprint on the ground for 25 ticks and the horns lower (the set's glow fills as they do); the first
  foe within 1.6 in front of you is gored: 6 + 2 a rank above E, thrown (1.5, lifted 0.45), staggered 30 ticks; 100
  ticks cooldown.
- **Vaultbreaker: Vault Wall.** A guarded blow glances off: its striker is thrown back (1.0) and staggered 15 ticks;
  10 ticks cooldown.
- **Frostwalker: Rime Path.** Still water under your feet freezes as you go (frosted ice in a disk of 3, as vanilla's
  Frost Walker), and a perfect dodge breathes frost: foes within 3 are slowed (Slowness II, 60 ticks) and frosted.
- **Sunward: Noon.** An overchannel flares the sun at your back: foes within 5 burn 80 ticks; you and allies within 5
  mend a heart.
- **Shardcrown: Shatter** (the C Lord's move). A blow that takes you under half health bursts crystal out of the
  armour: foes within 3.5 take the ability's blow and are thrown (1.2, lifted 0.4); for 60 ticks blows do a third less;
  600 ticks cooldown.
- **Deepcarapace: Shell.** Crouching and standing still closes the shell: blows do 40% less and fill Bastion twice
  (16 each).
- **Cloudrunner: Featherfall.** Falls never hurt; crouching while falling in the air you drift down (Slow Falling, no
  particles, renewed while you crouch).
- **Tidebreaker: Undertow.** The cutting wave drags those it cuts toward you (0.7) instead of throwing them back; in
  water or rain the Edge fills twice as fast.
- **Leviathan: Abyss Pull.** Its Bastion first drags everyone hostile within 6 toward you (0.9), then bursts 8 ticks
  later (the charge is spent at the pull). Under water you never run out of breath (Water Breathing, no particles,
  renewed while under).
- **Galewing: Gust.** A perfect dodge beats the wings: foes within 3 are thrown back (0.9) and you lift (0.35); 40 ticks
  cooldown.
- **Halo Choir: Hymn.** While three runes circle you, blows do a fifth less; an overchannel rings the halo, staggering
  foes within 5 for 30 ticks.
- **Dreamsteel: Mirror.** A deflect throws half the striker's attack damage back at them (as thorns); 20 ticks cooldown.
- **Starfall: Meteor.** Falls never hurt you; a landing from 6 blocks or more strikes like a falling star: foes within
  4 (6 at S) take the ability's blow as Heat, burn 80 ticks and are thrown (1.2, lifted 0.5); 100 ticks cooldown.
- **Riftwalker: Riftstep.** When the afterimage takes a blow from a creature within 12, you step out of the rift 1.5
  blocks behind it, facing it (if there's room), and run on faster.
- **Nightcourt: Riposte.** After a deflect, your next blade blow within 40 ticks lands 60% harder.
- **Signal's Echo: Echo.** An overchannel comes again 20 ticks later: its runes fly out once more at three quarters.
- **Hollowheart: Hollow Pulse** (the B Lord's move). Every fifth blow you land the caged heart beats (the set's glow
  fills a fifth a blow): foes within 4 take the ability's blow and you mend half a heart for each struck (four at
  most).

**44.7 A forged piece's story.** `awaken:forged` (`Forged`, schemaVersion 2): the set, quality (0-3), mastery (§44.5),
a flaw, twin-struck, and who made it; from 2 (P3) the inlaid Force's name (empty: none), the look it wears (a set id,
empty: its own), its accent (ARGB, 0: its set's own) and whether its Deepglass rang true. A schema 1 story reads with
those empty. The tooltip says it plainly ("Masterwork, twin-struck", "Forged by Name"). A
Hunter piece made before the Forge Song gains a Plain story the first time it's worn.

**44.8 Looks and accents (P3).** Cosmetic: never a number. At a Fitting Stand, Looks (the button by the title, or L)
lists what you wear piece by piece, with you turning beside it. Each piece can wear the look of its own set or of any
set you've forged whole (`ArmouryMemory.forged`) in the same slot (LOOK: the slot, the set's ordinal + 1, 0 its own; the
server checks the set). `ArmourLooks.drawn` is what every renderer draws, worn, on a stand and on the arm: the look's set
if it is made, else the piece's own; its numbers, ability and mastery stay the piece's. An **accent** colours what glows:
an inlay gives its Force's colour; one dye you carry colours the whole worn suit (ACCENT: the dye's id + 1, the dye used
up); the first swatch gives each piece its own back (its inlay's colour, if it has one).

**44.9 Settings and pacing (P5).** Client settings (`ArmourClientConfig`, `config/awaken-armour-client.toml`, in the mod's
settings screen; also `/awaken armour sculpted on|near|off`, `/awaken armour camera cinematic|first`,
`/awaken armour motion true|false` and `/awaken armour movesound <0-100>`):
- **Sculpted armour** ON (default) / NEAR / OFF. NEAR draws the sculpted look within 24 blocks of the camera and the flat
  painted look beyond (the rank's Hunter look stands in for a set without its own; lighter with many armoured figures in
  view); OFF always draws flat, and the first-person gauntlet with it. The Fitting Stand always shows the sculpted suit
  and the work. (The plan's far meshes are not built: every set is 600-1,000 triangles, well under its 2,500 budget, so
  NEAR is the fallback until the Mac's perf pass says more is needed.)
- **Forge camera** CINEMATIC (default) / FIRST_PERSON: first person keeps the eye at yours, at your own field of view,
  and turns it to each shot's subject (the stand, the Forge's mouth, the metal, the stand for the fit); the marks project
  the same way.
- **Mastery pacing** (`tools/sim/armour_mastery.py`, from the Java's numbers): about 23 XP a minute of fighting in a whole
  set (blows dealt and taken, the odd elite), 26 running gates (a Lord every 20 minutes): mastery II in a quarter hour,
  III within the hour, IV in about two hours and V in about four.
- **Armour motion** on (default) / off: whether a set's living parts move (§44.10). Off: every part is rigid on its
  bone, exactly as before the Finish.
- **Armour movement sound** 0 to 100 (default 60; 0 off): the soft sound a set makes at each stride (§44.12).

**44.10 Living parts (the Finish, stage 4).** One or two things on a set that should never stand still move: a halo, a
marker, a plume, lanterns, wings. Twelve sets have them; the rest stand still on purpose (a Bellguard or a Beastbound
that fidgets would be wrong).
- **How it is made.** A living part is some of a bone's own boxes, named in the kit (`tools/art/specs/armour_finish.py`,
  `LIVE`: the piece, the bone, the part names, the motion, a pivot and an axis in the design's own texels). The kit writes
  those boxes as a mesh of their own (`<piece>_<bone>_live<k>.mesh`), the rest of the bone as `<piece>_<bone>_still.mesh`,
  and the numbers as `assets/awaken/armour/<set>/live.json`. The whole bone is still written as before
  (`<piece>_<bone>.mesh`): first person, the Hall of Arms, the forge's work and a client with motion off draw that.
- **Six motions** (`ArmourLive.pose`, the same maths as the kit's `pose`, so the kit's pictures are the game's):
  **turn** (round its axis, degrees a tick), **tilt** (leans round and round, never spinning), **sway** (swings on its
  axis: a slow idle swing, a share of your stride, and a share of the wind), **drift** (wanders a fraction of a texel on
  three slow sines), **pulse** (swells on a double beat) and **glitch** (jumps a texel along its axis and back for two
  or three ticks, in about a third of its slots of 31 to 53 ticks; which slots and which way come from a hash of the
  slot number, so every client shows the same jump with nothing sent; with the set's ability fired it tears back and
  forth every two ticks). Any of the first five may bob up and down.
- **What moves it** is the frame's render state alone: the wearer's age, stride and stride phase, and the wind, which is
  1 in an elytra's glide, else the cape's rise in a fall (`capeFlap / 32`) or its lean past a walk
  (`(capeLean - 50) / 100`). Nothing is kept per wearer, nothing is sent and nothing is saved, so every client shows the
  same and a server never knows. Armour stands and the Fitting Stand's suit move by time alone.
- **The sets.** Signal's Echo: the marker turns and bobs, and the four slices of robe that sit out of line (on the
  body, the cape and both skirts) glitch, each on its own clock, so one jumps somewhere every couple of seconds. Sunward: the rays turn slowly behind the disc. Halo Choir: the
  halo tilts and bobs, the small wings breathe. Lanternlight: the brow lamp and both shoulder lanterns swing with your
  stride. Bladeward and Nightcourt: the plume sways and streams back in the wind. Galewing: the cape's primaries open in
  a fall, a glide or a sprint (up to 30 degrees) and stir when you stand. Dreamsteel: the crown's shards drift, odd and
  even apart. Riftwalker: the rift's tear and glow shiver. Hollowheart: the caged heart beats, about once a second.
  Leviathan: the frills breathe. Veilwoven: the arm ribbons swing.
- **A check the kit runs** (`sweep`): every living part is moved through its whole range (age, stride, wind) and may not
  pass through the rest of its set, except where it is joined to a part or allowed through one by name (the plume
  through its own ridge, the rays behind their disc).
- **Mastery IV grows in.** A piece's awakened parts no longer pop: they grow from their own middle over half a second
  the first time they show on a wearer (`ArmourLive.Wake`, client only, per entity id, forgotten when you leave).
- **Fallback.** No `live.json`, a mesh missing or a name the game does not know: the set is drawn whole and rigid, and
  the log says so once.

**44.11 Moments and marks (the Finish, stage 6).** Getting a set and how it was made both show on the body.
- **The wake.** When the last piece goes on and the four are one set (`ArmourAbilities.whole`), the server tells the
  wearer and everyone within 80 blocks (`ArmourPayloads.Whole`: entity, set, first). The armour lights feet to crown:
  each piece flares 160 ms after the one below it, a 100 ms rise and a 760 ms fade (`ArmourGlow.flash(glow, piece)`,
  the shader's own flash, raised from 0.18 to 0.34 of the accent on plain plate so it reads on a set with nothing
  that glows; an ability's release flare is the same term and reads better for it), on the body, on your own first-person arms and legs
  and on the Status figure. It sounds the set's three notes (§44.12). Not for what you log in wearing, and at most
  once in ten seconds (`WHOLE_COOLDOWN`), so swapping a piece in and out stays quiet.
- **The first time** a player wears a set whole, the System says one line in the set's rank colour: "Bellguard is
  whole on you. Ring: deflect a blow and your armour rings like a bell, staggering everyone close to you." (the set's
  own twist, else its archetype's ability). Remembered in `awaken:armoury` (`ArmouryMemory.worn`, schema 3; a schema
  2 save reads it empty). No window, no toast.
- **Forge marks.** A forged piece shows how it was made, as weapons do (§46.7), in the armour shader, a texel at a
  time, on its steel only (`ArmourLayer.marks`, three spare bits of the overlay: bit 15 of x, bits 14 and 15 of y):
  a **scale flaw** (`Forged.flaw`) leaves patches of dull blue-grey scale; on a set that is folded in the making (A and
  S, `ForgeSong.folds`) a piece that came out **Masterwork or better** shows the fold's ripples in its steel; a
  **Flawless** piece carries its **maker's mark**, a small hollow diamond cut dark with the set's own light breathing in
  it. The kit leaves room for the mark (`armour_finish.maker_marks`: four texels that glow nothing but carry a flow of
  1, on the plainest place near the back of the helm, the outside of the right forearm where your own eyes see it, the
  right thigh and the right boot); a piece with no plain place carries none. Worn, on the Fitting Stand, in first
  person and held.
- **A piece in the world is the piece.** The 23 sets with items of their own draw a piece as its real meshes in a hand,
  on the ground, in an item frame and on a shelf (`ArmourPieceRenderer`, special model `awaken:armour_piece` {set,
  piece}; each bone at rest as on the stand's form, measured once so the whole piece, crests and wings and all, just fills
  a block, with its cape left off; base `awaken:item/<id>_held` on `armour_piece_held`, a block's own display
  transforms). The inventory keeps the flat icon. It carries its mastery, accent, enchantment light and marks.
  The six Hunter sets' items are the gear module's and keep their icons.
- **Icons.** Greaves stand like an A (each leg turned 7 degrees out from the hip, seen nearly straight on) and read as
  legs; boots stand apart with the background between them and read as a pair (`ICON_VIEW`, `ICON_SPREAD`,
  `ICON_SPLAY`).
- **The Status line** is offered, not built: `ArmourBonus.statusLine(entity)` gives "Lordscale, whole. Mastery III" or
  "Lordscale, 3 of 4" (null with nothing of ours on) for the K menu's owner to place under the name.

**44.12 Sound (the Finish, stage 5).** Every armour sound is one of Minecraft's own recordings, named in sounds.json
(Euan 2026-11-09: built sounds read fake). No audio of ours is added, and none of Mojang's is in the repo.
- **One table** (`tools/art/armour_sounds.py`, `ROWS`): 45 sounds, each with three picks, a pick a recipe of recordings
  (one of Minecraft's events, a volume, a pitch, a start in ms). Pick 1 is the best guess and what the game plays until
  Euan has listened; `tools/art/specs/armour_sound_picks.json` holds his choices (1, 2, 3 or "today"), written by
  `apply` from his marks. `build` writes armour's sounds.json entries and `assets/awaken/armour/sound_layers.json`;
  `check` fails on a recording this game does not have.
- **In the game.** An event's entry in sounds.json is the recipe's first recording, as a reference to Minecraft's event
  (`"type": "event"`, with the recipe's volume and pitch: vanilla multiplies them in, and its own variants come along).
  A recipe's other recordings cannot be said in sounds.json, so the client adds them (`ArmourSoundsClient`, on
  NeoForge's `PlaySoundEvent`): at the same place, scaled by the volume and pitch the caller asked for (a pitched note
  stays in tune), at once or a tick or more late. No `sound_layers.json`: the first recording plays alone.
- **The 25 sounds built on 29 October** (seven hammers, the bellows, pull, quench, count, note, cut, fit, wake, miss;
  charged, Bastion, Flow, Edge, rune, overchannel, Ring, Rooted, Gore) are remade this way. Their old files stay in the
  repo until Euan has marked the page ("As built" plays them; `specs/armour_sounds_before.json` is their entries), then
  go.
- **What a set is made of** (`ArmourSounds.Family`): hide (Wildhide, Rootwarden, Nightcourt), cloth (Cleftrunner,
  Veilwoven, Sovereign Weave, Signal's Echo), mail (Amberwing, Lanternlight, Tidebreaker, Riftwalker), plate
  (Bellguard, Bladeward, Gatewrought, Sunward), heavy plate (Hornlord, Vaultbreaker, Lordscale, Leviathan, Starfall),
  crystal (Frostwalker, Shardcrown, Halo Choir, Dreamsteel), bone and shell (Beastbound, Deepcarapace, Hollowheart),
  feathers (Cloudrunner, Galewing).
- **Putting a piece on** sounds like what it is made of (`armour.equip_<family>`, the piece's own equip sound), for the
  23 sets with items of their own. The six Hunter sets' items are the gear module's and keep their rank's vanilla
  sound until that module asks `ArmourSounds.equip(set)`.
- **Walking in a set** (`armour.move_<family>`, client only): one soft sound a stride (1.7 blocks on the ground) from
  every armoured player within 12 blocks, by their cuirass (else their greaves), a quarter louder at a sprint, silent
  at a sneak (subtitle "Armour shifts": every sound event of ours has one, `audio_events_resolve`). Setting **Armour
  movement sound** 0 to 100, default 60, where a stride plays as loud as its recipe
  says; 0 is off (`/awaken armour movesound <0-100>`).
- **A blow landing on your armour** (`armour.struck_soft|plate|crystal|bone`, server): under Minecraft's own hurt
  sound, on what the cuirass is made of, louder with the damage (0.35 + 0.05 a point, at most 0.9).
- **A set becoming whole** (§44.11): the first three notes of the Forge Song it is made with (`forge.note`, pitched,
  three ticks apart, the last a little louder) at its wearer, the stand's `forge.wake` quiet under them.
- **By ear.** Nobody has heard any of it. `python3 tools/art/armour_sounds.py listen` serves a page on 127.0.0.1 only
  (`run-autopilot/armour-listen/`, gitignored, never hosted) that plays every pick alone and in its moment from this
  machine's own copy of the game; Euan marks one a row, `apply` then `build` puts his choices in the game. His ear is
  the gate: the picks are guesses until then.
- Test `armour_sounds_named`: every armour and forge sound event has its entry, every entry and layer names one of
  Minecraft's events, every set has its family and its pieces go on with its sound.

**44.13 The bigger options (after the Finish; Euan chose Admire and the abilities that use the suit).**
- **The suit answers its ability.** When a set's ability or twist fires (the release's flare, `ArmourPayloads.Charge`
  with a flash), its living parts (§44.10) take a **kick** for 0.7 s: at once to full, easing out
  (`ArmourGlow.kick`). Each part's own `kick` in the kit's `LIVE` table says how hard: a sway swings that many times its
  amount further (the wind or the kick, whichever is larger, never both), a tilt or a drift grows by that share, a
  pulse swells by it, a turn whips half a turn times it and settles back. So on Gust Galewing's wings are thrown open
  (30 degrees) and fold; on Hymn the halo rings wider and its wings beat; on Riftstep the rift tears five times as
  wide; on Hollow Pulse the heart swells; the System's marker whips round on Echo; Leviathan's frills flare on Abyss
  Pull; plumes, lanterns, ribbons, the sun's rays and Dreamsteel's shards answer too. The 17 sets without living
  parts keep the flare alone. From the render state and the glow record: nothing new is sent. The kit's sweep check
  covers the kicked range (three kicks were lowered because a lantern, the halo and the shards reached their set).
  `/awaken armour kick` flares your own set on your client (tours and demos).
- **Admire.** Hold **O** (`key.awaken.admire`, "Admire your armour (hold)") with a piece of ours on and nothing open:
  the view leaves your eyes, starts in front of you and circles you once, close (4 blocks, field of view 42, six
  seconds: three blocks of height in frame, so the tallest crest and the boots both show), stopping short of any wall between it and you. You stand still (`InputLock`), the HUD steps aside, and
  the set is drawn in a **hero light**: never darker than block light 11, what glows as if half charged. Letting go,
  moving, a blow, death or anything opening ends it at once. It rides the Forge Song's camera (`ForgeCamera`), which
  now leaves your body drawn while Admire has it. `/awaken armour admire` runs one circle without the key.


**44.14 One suit to a stand (Euan, 11 Nov 2026).** A Fitting Stand builds one set at a time. The first piece that stands on
it locks it to that piece's set (`FittingStandBlockEntity.held()`: the set of what stands on it); while it is held,
nothing of another set starts there (`ArmourForge.start` refuses, and every other set's offers carry `HELD_OTHER` and
lose `CAN`); it is free again when the last piece is taken off. A piece of the held set can be made again over the one
standing (the old one goes to your pack, as before). Offers of the held set say which pieces stand (`ON_STAND`).
- **Taking:** `ArmourPayloads.TAKE` with `a` 1 to 4 takes the piece in that slot; 0 takes everything, as sneak-use on the
  stand still does. The server then sends the stand's offers again (`HallNet.Suits`), so the Hall shows the lock gone.
- **In the Hall:** a held stand opens on its suit (Esc steps back to the terraces). The suit carries "On this stand · n of
  4" at its feet, the other suits step back (drawn at a third), the head reads "This stand holds Wildhide · 1 of 4", and
  another suit's close-up says "This stand is holding Wildhide. Take it off the stand and you can build this one here."
  with its forge button off. Pieces are taken from the suit itself: "Take it" for the piece you're on, "Take all n" for
  the rest; a standing piece is labelled "On the stand". The line "Take the suit (n of 4)" in the terraces' corner is gone.
- A stand left holding pieces of two sets from before this rule is held by the first of them until it is cleared.
- Test: `armour_forge_fold_starfire` (the lock, the offers' flags, one piece taken, the stand free again).

## 45. Enchanting: the Inscribing Table (plan docs/enchanting/PLAN.md, page https://claude.ai/artifact/TsFe2Y1CfJrTxeyFZMKYiF; Euan approved the full plan 2026-11-02: "Go ahead with the full plan. AAA LEVEL BABY. Make it look AMAZING")

Module `enchant` (`dev.awaken.enchant`). The rule: **your forge decides how strong a thing is; enchantments add what the
forge can't** (wards, banes that spare Lords, work and spoils, carrying, keeping). Vanilla's enchantment engine stays
(effects, tooltips, the `minecraft:enchantments` component); how enchantments are found, learned and written is ours.

### 45.1 S0: the sculpted sets take enchantments
- The 23 sets with items of their own (`ArmourItems`, every set but the six Hunter sets) are in vanilla's
  `#minecraft:enchantable/head_armor`, `chest_armor`, `leg_armor`, `foot_armor` and `durability` tags, through
  `src/main/merge/enchant` (no armour file touched), so every armour enchantment and Unbreaking fit them. Test
  `enchant_forged_sets_take` (all 92 pieces; Respiration only on helmets, Feather Falling on boots).

### 45.2 Pages and knowledge (`Pages`, `PageItem`, `Known`)
- **`awaken:enchantment_page`** (rare, stacks to 16): one enchantment in `minecraft:stored_enchantments` (its own vanilla
  lines hidden) and where it came from in `custom_data.awaken_where`. Named "Page of Heat Ward"; it says its family, what
  it fits, its line, where it came from and "Use it to learn it for good". Never foil.
- **Use it** to learn it for good. Knowledge lives in the `awaken:enchant_known` attachment (copied on death, synced to its
  owner; `Known`, schemaVersion 1: learned `{id: where, day}`, in memory, gate kinds paid, the first-page toast told,
  inscriptions written, a table ever set down, a table ever used in a Study). A learned page is spent. A page you already
  know stays in your hand ("You already know this. You can give it away."). A page whose enchantment can't be written
  any more fades to paper.
- **Old enchanted books** (vanilla's, from old worlds and chests): using one teaches every enchantment on it that can
  still be written, and it becomes a plain Book. One with nothing writable says so and stays.
- **Where pages come from**:
  - **A gate's Lord.** A `MobRole` BOSS with a gate theme, killed with a player's hand in it: every player within 48 blocks
    gets that kind of gate's page in their pack ("The Ember Tyrant carried a page of Heat Ward. Use it to learn it.") the
    first time they clear that kind (`Known.gates`), and 1 time in 5 after that. The kind's page is
    `Inscriptions.ofGate(theme)`; the night market reads as the Lantern Market. The first page ever also toasts "Every
    kind of gate keeps its own enchantment, and its Lord carries the page."
  - **The village scribe** (`village.Trade` through `EnchantApi.marketPages`): six market pages are drawn per village per
    day (seeded by the village and the day) and the scribe shows three of them, pages you don't know yet first
    (`Trade.forBuyer`). Price `min(64, 6 + top × 4 + 0..4)` emeralds.
  - **Old books** in chests and fishing: `#minecraft:on_random_loot` is replaced by the writable books list.
- Fifteen gate kinds each keep one page (Inscriptions' `gate`); fourteen of those are found nowhere else (the five wards,
  Blast and Projectile Protection, Clear Blood, Bane of the Dead and of Crawlers, Looting, Respiration, Swift Sneak and
  Unbreaking), and Mending (the Abyssal Shrine's) also turns up in old books. The rest come from the market or old books.

### 45.3 The thirty (`Inscriptions`, `data/awaken/enchantment`)
The Journal numbers them 1-30 (`Inscriptions.ALL`): five wards, Blast and Projectile Protection, Feather Falling, Clear
Blood; four banes; Looting, Fortune, Silk Touch, Efficiency, Harvest, Insight, Luck of the Sea, Lure; Respiration, Aqua
Affinity, Depth Strider, Swift Sneak, Loyalty, Riptide; Unbreaking, Mending, Infinity. Nothing else can be written:
anything adding damage, armour or an element (Sharpness, Smite, Bane of Arthropods, Power, Protection, Fire Protection,
Fire Aspect, Flame, Knockback, Punch, Thorns, Impaling, Density, Breach, Wind Burst, Multishot, Piercing, Quick Charge,
Lunge, Frost Walker, Soul Speed, Sweeping Edge, Channeling) stays only where it already is.
- **Wards** (`awaken:heat_ward`, `frost_ward`, `charge_ward`, `gravity_ward`, `spirit_ward`; armour, I-III, one per piece:
  `#minecraft:exclusive_set/armor`): each level on each piece takes 2.5% off damage of its Force, capped at 30% for the
  suit, 20% from a Lord's or boss's blow (agreed with boss-fights 2026-11-02). The Force is `Forces.forceOf`, else fire
  is Heat, freezing Frost, lightning Charge, magic Spirit. Anything that bypasses invulnerability is never warded, and
  plain melee has no Force. Heat Ward also shortens burning (`burning_time`, as Fire Protection).
- **Clear Blood** (armour, I-II): poison, wither and spore effects lose 10 more ticks per level every 10 ticks.
- **Banes** (`bane_of_the_dead`, `bane_of_crawlers`, `bane_of_beasts`, `bane_of_the_deep`; main hand weapons, I-III, one per
  weapon: `#minecraft:exclusive_set/damage`): 8% more per level on a direct melee hit by a player, applied last
  (LOWEST, after the Arms damage stack). Never on a player, a boss, a Warden, anything with a creature title, the Ender
  Dragon, the Wither or an Elder Guardian. The Dead: undead, and a Bell Crypt's creatures. Crawlers: arthropods, and a
  Hive's. Beasts: unowned animals and our fauna, never kin. The Deep: the Hollows, the Descent, and hostile creatures
  below y 0 in the overworld.
- **Harvest** (weapons, I-III): a wild beast you kill has one chance in two per level to drop one more of its hide, bone,
  pelt, leather, fur, scale or rabbit's foot drops.
- **Insight** (weapons and mining tools, `#awaken:enchantable/insight`, I-III): +15% experience per level from kills and
  mined blocks.
- Sources are tags: `#minecraft:in_enchanting_table` is empty, `#minecraft:tradeable` holds the market list, mobs spawn
  and trade only with Unbreaking, Aqua Affinity and Depth Strider, and ours are `#minecraft:non_treasure`. Test
  `enchant_rule`.

### 45.4 Room, depth and price (`EnchantRules`)
- **Room** (how many enchantments a piece holds): a forged armour piece its Forge Song quality + 1 (Fine 1 to Masterwork
  3, read through `core.api.ForgeHooks`); a found weapon (Marked, or Lord-forged: `ArmsApi.found`) 3; a bow, crossbow,
  trident or fishing rod 2; our forged weapons 2 (until the War Anvil's quality lands, stage 3); the Delver's Pick by its
  verse (§45.14: 1, and one more at II, IV and VI); anything else 1. An old
  piece over its room shows **Full** and takes nothing new until one is scraped off.
- **Depth** (how deep each can go): the piece's rank (its set's, its weapon's tier, else its material: leather, wood,
  stone and gold E, iron and chain D, diamond C, netherite A, else its rarity): E I, D II, C III, B and up the
  enchantment's top. Outside a Study nothing goes past II (**the Study**: `HearthHooks.studyAt` the table). A set's
  archetype goes one deeper for its kind: Bulwark wards, Strider carrying, Channeler keeping; a Lord-forged weapon its
  own. Deepening keeps the slot.
- **Price**: 3 levels and 1 lapis per level written (deepening pays the difference); Mending and Silk Touch 10 levels and
  4 lapis per level. A clean trace gives back a third of the levels (rounded down). Creative pays nothing.
- **Fit**: vanilla's `supportsEnchantment`, and never Efficiency on the Delver's Pick (`awaken:waking_pick`: its verses
  are its speed). Exclusive sets as vanilla's.
- The reasons, in these words: "It doesn't fit this.", "It can't go with X.", "No room left: scrape one off first." /
  "Full: scrape one off first.", "It's as deep as it goes.", "Deeper than II needs your Study.", "It's as deep as this
  piece allows.", "This piece takes it to N at most.", "You need 6 levels and 2 lapis.". Test `enchant_room_depth`.

### 45.5 The Inscribing Table (`InscribingTableBlock`, `Inscribe`)
- **`awaken:inscribing_table`**: lapis, stick (a book until §45.15), lapis / planks, essence shard, planks / stone, lapis, stone (`#planks`,
  `#stone_crafting_materials`); axe-mineable; drops itself. (The plan's "unlocks when you first hold a page" is not
  built: the recipe is always known.)
- **Use it holding a piece** to lay it on the slate and open the book. The server opens a session (table, hand slot, a
  snapshot of the piece): the piece never leaves your hand, so nothing can be duplicated or dropped. One writer per table
  ("Someone is writing here."). Using it with nothing you could write or scrape says why.
- **Choosing** checks everything again, takes the price and starts the trace (or memory's one stroke). **Strokes** are
  counted in order, no faster than 6 ticks each, each one's share on the line clamped 0-1. **Finishing** writes the
  enchantment onto the same piece; every stroke done at 80% or more on the line is a **clean hand**: a third of the
  levels back, and the mark goes **into memory** (from then on "From memory" writes it in one stroke, at full price).
- **Scraping** takes one off, free, giving nothing back.
- Esc, walking 6 blocks away, logging out, changing slot or the piece, or the table broken end the session and refund a
  choice not yet written. Test `enchant_inscribe` (and two players at one table).
- Others see it: the table shows a copy of the piece on the slate, turns its book to the page being looked at, and fills
  its channel with the enchantment's colour while it's traced (synced, never saved).

### 45.6 The vanilla fold (`Fold`)
- Any vanilla enchanting table you use turns into an Inscribing Table in place (facing you, with a flare) and opens as
  one. The vanilla table can't be crafted: `data/minecraft/recipe/enchanting_table.json` and its recipe advancement
  carry `neoforge:never`. NeoForge ships its own `enchanting_table` recipe, so the mod loads **after NeoForge**
  (`ordering="AFTER"` in `neoforge.mods.toml`): our data and assets sit above NeoForge's.
- The anvil repairs and renames but never adds or merges enchantments: an enchanted book or page on the right gives
  nothing; two of a kind repair, the left keeping only its own enchantments. The grindstone strips them and gives a third
  of the experience it used to. Test `enchant_fold`.
- The Hunter perk Keen (crafted weapons) is Unbreaking I a fifth of the time, no longer Sharpness I.

### 45.7 Enchantments seen at work (`EnchantFx`, server side)
A ward that takes some of a blow, a bane that bites, a Harvest drop, a page learned and an old table turning each send one
small `enchant_fx` message (kind, entity, place, colour, strength) to players within 48 blocks, through `AwakenNet`
(never to a player without our channel), with a sound: the family's note for wards, banes and spoils.

### 45.8 Tasks (`EnchantGoals`, through `core.api.Goals`)
Only once you're awakened. Steps, each leaving the moment it's done:

| Key | Tab | Shows | Place |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enchant/page/armour` | Armour | wearing armour, knowing nothing that fits it | optional, 70 |
| `enchant/page/weapons` | Weapons | carrying a weapon, knowing no weapon enchantment | optional, 70 |
| `enchant/read` | the page's | carrying a page that would teach you something | `PATH_FIRST_GATE + 1` |
| `enchant/table` | the first known's | knowing one, never having set down a table (needs the recipe's items) | `PATH_FIRST_GATE + 2` |
| `enchant/first` | the piece's | a table set down, nothing written yet, a carried piece something you know fits (Levels, Lapis) | `PATH_FIRST_GATE + 3` |
| `enchant/room/armour`, `enchant/room/weapons` | Armour, Weapons | after the first, while a carried piece has room for or can deepen something you know | optional, 40 |
| `enchant/study` | the piece's | carrying a piece that could take something you know past II, never having used a table in a Study | optional, 30 |

A piece's tab is Armour for armour, Weapons for anything else; an enchantment's is Armour when it fits armour. Test
`enchant_tasks`.

### 45.9 Hooks with the neighbours
- `core.api.ForgeHooks` (agreed with the weapon forge 2026-11-02): `Reader` (quality 0-3, rank, archetype) installed by
  armour (the Forge Song's `Forged`) and arms (the weapon's tier); `Listener.forged(player, stack, quality, station)`;
  `CardLine` (enchant installs "Room for N enchantments" for result cards).
- `core.api.ArmsApi.found(stack)`, `core.api.HearthHooks.studyAt(level, pos)` (the Study's gift now reads "enchantments
  written here go deeper"), `core.api.EnchantApi` (the market's pages, what a buyer wants, a page by id) used by
  `village.Trade`.

### 45.10 The writing scene, the table drawn, the Journal (`enchant.client`)
(Since §45.15 the book's two pages and the result card are the `classicTable` setting only, the table is a desk with the
book on a rest, and the piece on the slate is the thing itself. The view, the hands, the trace and its numbers stand.)
- **You step to the desk and the view leans in** (a change from the plan's "cinematic by default"): as the scene opens
  you take a short walk (a few moves over 12 ticks, collisions and all) to the spot 0.36 out from the table's front,
  where both hands reach the slate, if you're within three blocks of it, on its floor (within 0.6) and there's room
  to stand; otherwise you stay put. The eye is then your own: the view turns (`ComputeCameraAngles`, LOW) and narrows
  (`ComputeFovModifierEvent`) toward each beat, framing it in the middle of the band the screen leaves clear: the piece
  with the floating book behind it above the book's pages, close on the piece while you trace (above the line and
  pips), held close through the wake's turn (the payoff fills the view; measured live, framing for the card from the
  first tick had the turn play out at a fifth of the screen), then a little back once the card comes (above it). Eased per tick (0.22), in over 12 ticks, out over 10, a slight
  breath. First person is forced for the scene and restored after: the world
  hands (`core.api.FirstPerson.world`, "enchant_table", priority 210) only draw from the player's own camera. The HUD
  steps aside (subtitles and chat stay), the block outline goes, the player model is hidden.
- **Hands**: the off hand brings your piece down onto the slate over 14 ticks (the table holds off drawing it for you
  meanwhile) and then draws back out of the view for the rest of the session (over the slate it would hide the piece in
  the book and the mark in the trace); the main hand holds the table's **burin** (`awaken:burin`, never held as an
  item: `Sources.neverHeld`) resting at the slate's near corner, and while you trace, follows the cursor where it meets
  the slate; from memory it runs the mark by itself.
- **The book's pages** (`InscribeScreen`): the left page is your piece (its name drawn large, rank, room line, what's
  on it with **scrape**: a second click within two seconds takes it off, sent as its registry number (its mark flares on
  the piece above the pages and crumbles from its first end into dust over 18 ticks; the book stays up), and how deep this
  table writes). The right page lists what you know that fits it: its mark, name and target level (the deepest this
  piece allows here by default; ‹ › step it between one above what's on it and that), "Up to II here (IV in your
  Study)", the price (red when you can't pay), or plainly why not; **from memory** when its mark is in memory (at the
  end of the second line, so the name keeps its line for the level and its arrows, and the price shortens round it); the foot
  of the page says what the one under the cursor does. Resting on a row for 4 ticks sends LOOK (watchers see the
  floating book turn) and lays that mark faintly on the piece.
- **The trace**: the mark (`Marks`, the same strokes the server counts) lies on the piece, 0.4 blocks across, scored
  into it (a dark rim either side of every line, so it reads on a bright piece) and faint at first; the view leans in
  until the mark fills most of it. The stroke to draw now is brighter and wider than the ones to come, and while it
  waits a light runs it from its glowing end to its far end (the way to draw it). Each stroke is picked up at its
  glowing end (within 0.3 mark units; a press anywhere else taps the slate dully and the end flares). The pen's run
  between frames is followed in steps of at most 0.03, each finding the nearest part of the stroke from two samples
  behind to six ahead of the cut: the cut follows the pen (to the nearest sample it has reached, within 0.34 of the
  line) and never runs ahead of it (on a slow frame it may look further on, as far as two and a half times the pen's run
  along the stroke, never so far it could skip a loop to where the stroke crosses itself). The game sees the pen once a
  frame, so a step between two frames is never judged further off the line than the two real points either side of it
  (a slow frame's straight chord across a corner costs nothing; measured live, a frame drop to 19 fps had cost a careful
  hand 0.54 on a chevron). The share on the line is by distance drawn, so it reads the same at any speed or
  frame rate: inside 0.06 of the line (the drawn line's own width) counts fully, fading to nothing at 0.16. Measured
  with a dev hand (eased, wobbling strokes of 0.1-0.8 s): a careful hand (wobble up to 0.1) scores about 0.9 and is
  clean, a loose one (0.13) about 0.8, a shaky one (0.18) about 0.73, a sloppy one (0.24) under 0.6. While it cuts on
  the line the burin throws lapis sparks (every 0.08 drawn) and ticks faintly (every 0.3, climbing in pitch toward the
  stroke's end), and its cut runs under the hand (`EngraveLoop`, `enchant.cut_metal` or `cut_leather`): a loop that
  swells with the pen's speed on the line (full at 0.15 a tick, volume 0.32, pitch 0.85-1.24) and falls quiet the
  moment the hand stops or strays. Leather, wood and string pieces (leather armour, wooden tools, bows, crossbows, rods,
  elytra, the turtle shell) take the burin's leather bite and drag; everything else metal. The burin's point, not the fist, is at the pen (the fist sits below and left of it on screen by the
  burin's reach). The piece on the slate is drawn without vanilla's violet shimmer (`ENCHANTMENT_GLINT_OVERRIDE` off on
  the table's copy), so the only light on it is the mark being written. A finished stroke
  burns lapis in its core and the family's colour round it, rings its family's note a step higher than the last (a
  dull scratch if under 60% on the line); one that rings is **sealed**: it blooms for 12 ticks while a white-hot light
  sweeps it from end to end in 5, ten sparks leap off its far end, and the view nods in 0.8° and settles over 6 ticks and is sent as STROKE no sooner than 7 ticks after the previous one; FINISH
  follows 6 ticks after the last. From memory the whole mark writes itself in 40 ticks. Pips under the name show each
  stroke (bright when clean, with a lapis centre once done, so a pale family's pips still read as done), with a bar for how much of the current one is on the line; a first-trace hint says what
  to do and that Esc gives the levels back. `LiveHand` (autopilot runs only) drives a live client's mouse for these
  checks from `<game>/enchant-live/in.txt`.
- **The wake**: the mark flares white-hot and settles into its colour over 50 ticks while a band of light runs the
  piece and the piece rises a hair (0.04), turns once on the slate (from 6 to 40 ticks, eased) and settles; at 42 ticks
  (it has turned) a card comes up and says what was written ("A clean hand" and the levels back,
  "Its mark is in your memory now"), with Write another and Done.
- **The table as everyone sees it** (`InscribingTableRenderer`): the leather book (`awaken:block/inscribing_book`, the
  vanilla book's layout) floats over a brass bracket at the back, opening toward whoever's near and toward the front
  while someone writes, turning its pages to the one being looked at; the writer's piece lies flat on the slate; the
  lapis channel one pixel in from the slate's edge glows faintly when someone's near, fills with the enchantment's
  colour from the front round both sides while it's traced, and flares on the wake; watchers see the mark itself
  pulsing faintly on the piece. The block faces its placer (the front, where you stand); its shape follows the facing.
- **Enchantments at work** (`EnchantFxClient`, at most 32 at once): a ward's ring closing in at the chest, a bane's
  three spears of light, a glint of gold rising over an extra drop, a column with rings climbing round you as a page is
  learned, rays and a spreading ring out of an old table as it turns.
- **Tooltips**: every enchantable piece says its room under its name ("Room for two enchantments", "No room left",
  "Full"); a page you already know says "You know this one".
- **The Journal's ENCHANTMENTS category** (`StatusSections.Shelf.ENCHANTMENTS`, a fixed set of 30): each one you know
  with what it does, its family, what it goes on and how deep, where you learned it and whether its mark is in memory;
  the rest stay blank.
- **Sounds** (`tools/art/specs/audio_enchant.py`, audiokit synthesis with Kenney CC0 transients): book open, page turn,
  burin on metal and on leather (a bite each, and a seamless two-second loop each for the running cut: synthesis only,
  mastered by gain alone so the seam keeps no dip), scratch, the five family notes (C5), wake, learn, flare, drift, scrape.
- **Art** (`tools/art/specs/enchant.py`): the table's slate top with its lapis channel, framed dark-wood panels (the
  front with a lapis ring and spear), the trim, brass, the book, the page item and the burin; blockstate by facing.
- **Commands**: `/awaken admin enchant learn <all|id> | remember all | forget` (server, for testing and tours); the
  client's `/awaken enchant pilot hover <no> | choose <no> | memory <no> | trace | again | close` is the autopilot's
  hand at a table (tours can't drag a mouse: the pilot traces each stroke from its end, on the line, a breath between).

### 45.11 The script line: an enchanted piece's own light (`EnchantGlow`, `core.api.EnchantApi.Glow`)
- Our sculpted weapons (`arms_weapon` shader) and armour (`armour` shader) drop the single violet shimmer for the piece's
  own enchantment light: a thin line of script along its edges (where the surface turns from the eye), its letters
  drifting hilt to tip on weapons and feet to crown on armour, a slow wave of brightness running the same way, what
  glows of itself (the material map's emissive) taking the colour, a few pixels catching it, and a faint rim. Foil with
  none of ours on it (a Marked weapon with nothing written) keeps the violet.
- **Colour, in turn**: each enchantment on the piece holds the line for 30 ticks, swelling and fading but never quite
  out (brightness 1-7 of 7), then hands it to the next. The palette, by index: 1 Heat Ward ember `FF8A4C`, 2 Frost Ward
  ice `8FD8FF`, 3 Charge Ward gold `FFD84A`, 4 Gravity Ward violet `B993FF`, 5 Spirit Ward teal `4FE0C2`, 6 the other
  wards steel `B9C3D2`, 7 Clear Blood green `9FE07A`, 8 banes red `FF5F63`, 9 spoils gold `F2C45A`, 10 carrying blue
  `4FB5EA`, 11 keeping bone `F3EAD6`, 12 anything not in the thirty lapis-violet `8C6BFF`.
- **The bits**: both shaders read UV1.x's low 8 bits as before (energy, or the Forge Song's heat) and bits 8-14 as the
  script: the palette index in 8-11 (0 none) and the brightness in 12-14. Arms (`WeaponRenderer`: its cached `State`
  carries `glow`) and armour (`ArmourLayer.draw`, `FittingStandRenderer`) pack `EnchantApi.glowBits(stack)`; enchant
  installs the reader (`EnchantApi.glow`) on the client, and with none installed it is 0 and the shaders draw as before.
  `tools/art/mesh_render.py` mirrors the line (without the pixels, which need texel coordinates).
- Vanilla's own items keep vanilla's glint.

### 45.12 Enchantments at work, stage 2 (`EnchantFx`, `EnchantFxClient`)
The `enchant_fx` message gains the mark to show (`no`, the enchantment's number; for a mend, the slot mended) and the
angle on the ground the blow came from (`dir`, NaN when there's no telling). The client keeps at most 48 at once.
- **Ward** (18 ticks): the ward's own mark stands where the blow landed, between you and where it came from (0.3 out
  from your side, at the chest), white-hot and settling into the Force's colour as it grows a little, a ripple
  spreading out of it, a faint ring round you. A blow from nowhere in particular keeps the closing rings.
- **Bane** (16 ticks): the bane's mark burns on the creature's side the blow came from, red going from near-white, with
  the three spears of light fainter behind it.
- **Gold on extra drops** (34 ticks): a glint rides the drop down with a short trail of sparks and two rising off it.
  Harvest's extra drop; with Looting (the killer's weapon) or Fortune (the tool), the first one or two drops that came
  as a stack of more than one, with the spoils note once.
- **Silk Touch** (20 ticks): when the block itself came away, its outline lifts 0.35 out of where it sat and fades,
  a soft gold ring spreading at its foot. No sound (mining is loud enough).
- **Mending** (14 ticks): each orb that will mend something (vanilla picks the piece; the thread aims at that slot's
  place on the body, hands at your side) draws a thread arching from it into the piece, a bead of warm light running
  it and the thread fading behind.
- **Feather Falling** (20 ticks): a fall of four blocks or more on boots that carry it puffs a soft ring over the
  ground and six motes lifting off it, brighter for a longer fall (full at twelve).
- **Depth Strider** (24 ticks, the client's own, nothing sent): a player within 32 blocks moving through water on boots
  that carry it leaves a faint blue V opening behind them on the water (at their feet when under it), one every three
  ticks.

### 45.13 The Study's drifting letters (`InscribingTableBlockEntity`, `LetterParticle`)
- Letters of our own script (`awaken:enchant_letter`, a coloured particle; twelve 8x8 runes, white with a faint halo,
  from `tools/art/specs/enchant.py`) drift off bookshelves standing where vanilla's table reads them (two out, with air
  between, `EnchantingTableBlock.isValidBookShelf`) into the floating book: they lift off the shelf, sway, arc over and
  speed into the book, brightening to white as they arrive, gone as they touch the page (36-55 ticks, full-bright).
- Only while a player is within four blocks or someone writes: now and then anywhere (one try a tick, one in seven),
  thicker in your Study (two tries, one in three), thickest while someone writes (three tries, one in three), and then
  in the colour of what's being written; otherwise lapis light (`8FB0FF`).
- The table knows it's in a Study from the server (`HearthHooks.studyAt`, looked at every five seconds per table and
  sent with the table's update); in a Study a quiet paper hum (`drift`, 0.18) goes with the letters every 4.5 seconds
  while they come.

### 45.14 Stage 3: more doors, Word Stones and the pick's room (`Doors`, `WordStones`, `delve.api.Pick`, `living.api.Hunts`)
- **The hunts.** A named beast (`CreatureTag` kind `BEAST`, "Terror of Ashfen") brought down by a player pays a page of
  Bane of Beasts, "From Terror of Ashfen, brought down"; a ledger population's alpha (a deep-wild herd's bull, a deep
  pack's leader: `living.api.Hunts.alpha`, elite with the `awaken_ledger` tag) pays Harvest, "From a herd's leader,
  brought down".
- **The Deep.** An elite creature that means harm (`Enemy`, never a Lord, Warden or named beast) killed below the rock's
  zero in the overworld (`delve.api.Bands` Deep band) or anywhere in a Descent pays Bane of the Deep. Breaking a lode's
  heart that's still whole (`delve.api.Lodes.heart`, not `heartBroken`, and the block is one of the delve's
  `awaken:*_lode_heart` blocks) pays Fortune; in the Deep band the first one pays Silk Touch, and after that a Deep heart
  rolls Silk Touch or Fortune evenly. Read at NORMAL, ahead of the delve's LOW listener that marks the heart broken, so a
  heart dug up and set down again pays nothing; creative breaks pay nothing.
- **Every door pays like a gate's Lord:** the page the first time (doors `hunt:beast`, `hunt:leader`, `deep:bane`,
  `deep:fortune`, `deep:silk`, kept with the gates in `Known`), then a spare one time in five. The page goes into the pack
  (else at your feet) with one plain line in the enchantment's colour: "A page of Harvest was caught in the leader's
  hide. Use it to learn it.", "A page of Fortune was pressed into the lode's heart. Use it to learn it."
- **The Delver's Pick's room** reads `delve.api.Pick.verse` (a facade over `PickVerses.verse`): 1, and one more at II,
  IV and VI. Still never Efficiency.
- **The Forge Song's finished card** shows the lines other modules add through `ForgeHooks.cardLine` under its words
  (`ForgeSongScreen.doneLines`, read once when the card comes, the piece made with its quality): enchanting's "Room for
  three enchantments" in lapis-violet (`A898FF`). The War Anvil's card does the same when it lands.
- Test `enchant_doors` (a named beast's page and its words, no page without a player, the heart blocks, the pick's room
  at verse 0 and IV).
- **Precursor Word Stones** (`awaken:word_stone`, `WordStoneBlock`, `WordStones`): a stele of the ruins' dark plating on a
  low plinth, a panel let into its face with three runes carved down it, glowing (emissive, cutout) in the enchantment's
  colour through a block tint. The carving is the state's `word` (the enchantment's number, 1-30) with `facing`, so it
  needs no saved data. Unbreakable, no loot, never held, light 6.
  - **Where**: every Precursor ruin's builder calls `RuinBuilder.Sink.stone(x, y, z, facing, set)`, placed by
    `EnchantApi.placeStone(level, pos, facing, set, seed)` with the block's position as the seed: the vaults' sealed
    chamber (14, 1, 15) across the terminal from the drafting stand, the monolith's chamber (12, 1, 8) facing the stand,
    the ocean lab's storage dome (17, 1, 6), the sky platform's cabin (C-3, deck+1, C), the spire's crown (C+1, top+1, C+1).
  - **Sets**: "" (vaults, monolith) Insight, Efficiency, Infinity, Feather Falling; "sky" Feather Falling, Infinity,
    Insight; "sea" Aqua Affinity, Depth Strider, Loyalty, Riptide, Luck of the Sea, Lure. None a gate keeps, none a hunt
    or the Deep pays.
  - **Touch**: hold your hand to it (use, any hand) and you learn it ("Copied from a Word Stone", the usual learn line,
    sound and mark); known, it says "The stone is carved with Insight, and you already know it." in the action bar.
  - **The look**: while the nearest player is you and you haven't learned it, its letters (`awaken:enchant_letter`, in
    its colour) lift off the face every three ticks and gather above it, with the paper hum (0.14) every 4.2 seconds;
    the moment you learn it 28 letters stream from the face into you; known, it goes quiet. Looking at it says, in its
    colour, "A Word Stone carved with Insight. Hold your hand to it to learn it." (or "You know this one."). Learned while
    you look, the line clears at once for the chat line that says what you learned, and stays away until you look elsewhere.
  - Test `enchant_word_stone` (every ruin kind places one, in open air on a floor; the sea set; the same seed the same
    carving; a touch teaches once).
- **The wake's chord**: with the wake sound, the new enchantment's family note (0.8), and each other enchantment on the
  piece adds its own family's note a major third, a fifth and an octave above (0.55; three at most), so a piece rings
  with everything written on it.
- **The Inscribing Table's book on a narrow page** (Euan's MacBook, GUI 4): each row's line drops detail until it fits,
  so the price always shows: "Up to II here (III in your Study) · 6 levels and 2 lapis", then without the Study, then
  without "here", then the price alone; the foot's hint wraps.

### 45.15 The polish pass: the door, the desk, one script (plan docs/enchanting/POLISH.md, page https://claude.ai/artifact/GGUiB3qof3qZMVuxQoMAsb; Euan approved the full plan 2026-11-11: "go ahead with the full plan", with three changes)
His changes, which override the page where they differ: **no menu** ("let's not make it a menu for enchanting. It should
stay 3D inside of the actual world, like similar to how it is now, maybe just better, like more cinematic"); an
inscription's look **must not distract from the armour set** but should give "a nice shine" or a small aura (§45.17);
and **a page must say how it is used** ("I thought the pages were like being automatically applied... say: you enchant
this onto a weapon by doing XYZ"). What the audit found is in POLISH.md §2: across two worlds he was given six pages, read
four, and never built the table. Built first as a pilot (the door, the desk, his three banes and Lantern); the other five
new words followed the same day (§45.16), at his word that every approved plan be finished.

- **A page says how it is used.** Its own lines end "Use this page to learn it. That puts it on nothing yet." and
  `Entry.howTo()`: "To put it on a weapon, hold the piece and use an Inscribing Table." (the noun by what it fits:
  `Entry.piece()`). The line when one is given: "The Hive Regent carried a page of Bane of Crawlers. Use the page to learn
  it, then write it onto a weapon at an Inscribing Table." (`Pages.then`). Reading one, chat says "You learned Bane of
  Crawlers. It isn't on anything yet." while the card below is sure to show (five lines of chat lay over it at his
  size), and once the card is paced, all of it: "... To put it on a weapon, hold the piece and use an Inscribing Table.
  It fits your Beastbound Maul. You can make a table: it's on your Tasks page." (the last two only where they hold).
  The first time ever the System's line about gates follows as a paced toast short enough to show whole: "Each kind of
  gate keeps its own enchantment." (it was a longer toast, cut after "and its L").
  **Two System panels** say the same in the room a panel has, which is a title and three lines of 188 pixels at the size
  he plays at (the first cut had a body and rows: the body was cut with "..." and the how-to folded behind "Press K to
  see 2 more"). Each line is a row with no value, which a panel draws at full width. Given (`Pages.givenCard`, 7 s):
  "Page of Bane of Crawlers" / "It isn't on your gear yet." / "Use the page to learn it. Then" / "write it on at an
  Inscribing Table." Read (`Pages.learnedCard`, 12 s): "Learned: Bane of Crawlers" / "It isn't on anything yet." / "To
  write it on, hold the piece" / "and use an Inscribing Table." Until you have written your first enchantment both
  panels are CRITICAL, so the System's pacing never holds them (`Pages.doorTier`: paced, the first filmed run showed
  neither, a new world being quiet for its first five minutes); after that they are paced like any notice. A page held
  to the table is read there.
- **A bane's line leads with what it does** ("Your hits land 8% harder for each level on spiders, bees and the creatures
  of a Hive."); what it won't touch is the Journal entry's small print.
- **The recipe** takes a stick where it took a book: lapis, stick, lapis / planks, essence shard, planks / stone, lapis,
  stone. Tasks' `enchant/table` asks for the stick.
- **A converted vanilla table** opens facing as the server says (`Open.facing`): the scene framed itself before the new
  block reached the client and fell back to north.
- **The door's log**: `[enchant] door: page given|read|table set|opened|written[ clean| from memory] <id> t=<game time>`.
- **One script** (`Marks`, written by `tools/art/specs/_enchant_glyphs.py java`): 36 designed glyphs in place of five
  generated templates. A glyph is its family's frame (wards a shield, banes a spear, spoils a cup, carrying a gable,
  keeping a knot) and the enchantment's own sign, straight cuts between points of a 7 by 7 grid, 2 to 5 strokes, sampled
  about every 0.11 of the mark with every corner a sample. `Marks.frame(no)` counts the frame's strokes; `Marks.grid(no)`
  gives the corners. Numbers 32 to 36 are drawn for the words not built yet. A Word Stone's `word` runs 1 to 36.
- **Every page has its own leaf**: 36 item textures (`enchantment_page_<path>`: the sign in dark ink on a parchment with a
  band in the family's colour) chosen by the item model select `awaken:page` (`PageSelect`: the enchantment's id path).
- **The scribe's desk** (the block's model, `tools/art/specs/enchant.py`): two trestle ends and a stretcher, an apron with
  a brass pull, the slate (its top at 12 of 16) with the lapis channel, a rail along the back, a brass rest at the
  writer's left where the book lies (shut when nobody is near, opening as they come), and an inkwell of lapis at their
  right with the burin standing in it while nobody writes and while its writer still chooses: the hand takes it up as
  the chosen page comes down (`InscribeScene.burinOut`; held through the choosing, the fist lay over the right-hand
  pages). While you choose the arm rig still holds that arm, low by your side and out of the view: left to the game, its
  own hand came back into the corner still holding the piece. The floating book is gone. Shape and outline follow.
- **The piece is the thing itself** (`InscribingTableRenderer.lay`): drawn with `ItemDisplayContext.NONE`, where our
  weapons and armour are their own meshes, and laid by the bounds of what is drawn: a flat icon or a weapon on its side
  across the slate (0.8 of a block along its diagonal), a breastplate or leggings on their back (half a block across), a
  helm or boots standing (0.42 across and never taller than 0.32). A sculpted armour piece's item says only that it
  fills a block, so its real width, height and depth are measured from its meshes as the armour's item renderer fits it
  (`InscribingTableRenderer.shape`; taken as the block, a breastplate floated a third of a block over the slate and the
  view to its mark went flat). The glyph rides on the piece's top (`InscribeScene.lift`).
- **Choosing in the world, no menu** (`Desk`; the screen only frees the pointer). The pages of what you know that fits
  rise out of the book over 10 ticks and hang in a row over the desk's near edge, each the real page, leaning back toward
  your eyes, at most sixteen. Pointing at one (its place on screen from the camera) lifts it, shows its glyph on the
  piece, and shows one label over the row on the page's own side of the piece, so it covers neither the row nor the
  piece: its name and level, its line, "Up to II here, III in your Study", the price as the
  things themselves (red when you can't pay) and "Click to write it." (the wheel changes the level; a page in memory:
  "Click: from memory. Shift and click: trace it."). A click takes the page down onto the piece over 8 ticks while the rest
  sink, and the trace begins. What can't go on lies flat on the slate, dim, and its label says why. What is written
  shows as glyphs in sockets let into the slate down its left side (behind the piece, a longsword's point lay over the
  one it had), a framed glyph for each thing written and an empty frame for each it still has room for; a press held
  on one for 16 ticks closes a ring round it and scrapes it off, its label to its left. A line of key caps at the foot
  says the rest.
  The view frames the whole desk while you choose. The room steps back (a soft dark frame at the screen's edges).
- **The wake** shows the enchantment's name in the Hall's blackletter over a soft light, how it came out ("A clean hand",
  "Written", "From memory") and, at the foot, the levels that came back and "Its mark is in your memory now." with Space
  to write another and Esc to step away. No card. It is drawn here, not through `HallMoment`, whose anvil doesn't belong
  at a desk.
- **`classicTable`** (`config/awaken-enchant-client.toml`, off): the old book of two pages and the result card, kept for
  one build.
- Dev: `/awaken admin enchant page <id>` gives a page as a door does. Tour `tools/autopilot/enchant-polish.txt`. Tests
  `enchant_glyphs`, `enchant_door`.

### 45.16 The six new words (`Lantern`, `LanternGlowBlock`, `Words`)
- **`awaken:lantern`** (helmets, I-III, carrying): your helmet lights the dark around you. The Lantern Night Market's
  Lord carries its page; Looting, which he carried, is sold at the market and found in old books.
- Where the wearer's head is darker than the word's own light (8, 10, 12), one `awaken:lantern_glow` stands there: a block
  with nothing to see, touch or hold that only gives light, so friends see by it too. It follows when the wearer has gone
  two blocks, sits in water as water, and goes out in daylight, by a brighter fire, when the helmet comes off, at death,
  on leaving, or when left four blocks behind. What the old glow still lends a place doesn't count as light of the
  world's own (`Lantern.dark`). A glow nobody wears clears itself on its own tick (a crash, a chunk that slept).
  Asked every fourth tick a wearer.
- One soft sound as it catches (`block.lantern.place`). **Its frame time on the Mac is not measured yet**: each move
  rebuilds a chunk section. Test `enchant_lantern`.

**The other five** (`Words`; numbers 32 to 36 in `Inscriptions.ALL`, each with its glyph and page; thirty-six in all).
Four Lords who carried a vanilla name carry these, and the vanilla four (Unbreaking, Respiration, Blast Protection,
Projectile Protection) are sold at the market, found in old books and carved on Word Stones (the vaults gain Unbreaking
and Blast Protection, the ocean lab Respiration, the sky platforms Projectile Protection).
- **Wayfarer** (`awaken:wayfarer`, boots, I-III, carrying; the Glass Desert's Lord): on a laid road
  (`RoadHooks.nearestRoad` within a block) or a path under the feet you move 8, 14 or 20% faster (a transient
  `awaken:enchantment.wayfarer` on movement speed, held through a jump, gone when you land off the road), and what a
  sprint there cost in hunger is given back (a tenth a block). Motes of its script at your heels while it works. Looked
  at every fifth tick.
- **Gather** (`awaken:gather`, weapons and tools, I-II, spoils; the Precursor Lab's Lord): what you break and what you
  kill with it goes into your pack from within 8 or 12 blocks (`BlockDropsEvent`, `LivingDropsEvent`, after Harvest's
  extra and the glints); what doesn't fit falls where it would have. Never another player's pack, and never what a Lord
  or a named beast leaves, which lies there for everyone who fought. A gold thread from where it fell to your hand for
  the first three, and one soft pickup.
- **Regrowth** (`awaken:regrowth`, anything that wears, I-III, keeping; the Overgrown Temple's Lord): under open sky by
  day, or with rain falling on you, each worn or held piece that carries it mends one use every 12, 8 or 5 seconds, a
  green thread coming down into it. Never on a piece with Mending (the data's `exclusive_set`, and the tick skips one).
  The boss branch's Lasting touches the same durability: whichever merges second fits to the first.
- **Remembrance** (`awaken:remembrance`, anything that wears, one level, keeping; the Drowned Archive's Lord): when a
  Lord, a Warden, a named beast or one of vanilla's great creatures (`EnchantEffects.spared`, never a player) falls to
  you, the weapon in your hand and each piece you wear that carries the word keep its name: item component
  `awaken:remembered` (schemaVersion 1, a list of names oldest first, twelve at most, saved and synced). A Lord is named
  as the game says it ("the Bell Warden"), a named beast with its title. Chat: "Your Beastbound Maul remembers the Bell
  Warden." (or "Your gear remembers ..." for more than one piece); the tooltip lists them under "It remembers:", three
  a line. The notch of light on the piece's script line for each name is not built: the light on a piece is packed by
  the arms and armour renderers, which have no room in it for a count.
- **Long Arm** (`awaken:long_arm`, chestplates, I-II, carrying): data alone, one or two blocks on
  `minecraft:block_interaction_range`; entity reach is untouched, so it never strikes further. Found only on the sky
  platforms' Word Stones (two of that set's six).
- **Clear Blood** pulses green where you stand once a second while it burns poison, wither or spores off, and while
  **Insight** is in your hand experience comes in with a gold glint (one in eight ticks, however many orbs).
- Test `enchant_new_words`. The tour films Gather and Wayfarer.

### 45.17 Seen at work, and on the piece
- **On our weapons and armour** (both shaders' enchantment block; `tools/art/mesh_render.py` in step): what glows of
  itself keeps its own colour (it took the enchantment's, which made the piece read as a different one). An inscribed
  piece shows a shine, a clean band of light crossing it on its metal in about a second every five, with its script
  showing for a moment in the band's wake and a few pixels catching it, and a small aura, the enchantment's colour held
  faintly (a tenth) on the faces turned furthest from you, breathing. Between crossings the piece is itself. Nothing
  here may be bright for long: in the hand nearly every face of a blade is turned away, and the first cut, with the
  letters and the aura always on, striped the whole blade in the enchantment's colour.
- **A ward's plate**: its glyph stands between you and the blow, 0.8 of a block across, a soft halo, a body in the
  Force's colour and a white-hot core, held bright for half of 24 ticks. What it took off flies from the plate as
  sparks of the Force's colour, four to nine by how much it took.
- **A bane's brand**: its glyph on the creature where the blow landed, white-hot for 8 ticks, then glowing on it as it
  moves for two seconds. A creature a bane kills goes out in the bane's red: a ring of it over the ground where it fell,
  motes lifting off (`EnchantFx.banedOut`).
- **A page given** flies from where it was (a fallen Lord, a lode's heart) to the one it goes to over 16 ticks, its sign
  showing, with a page's turn and a soft pickup.
- **Reading** (a page, an old book, a Word Stone): the glyph lifts in front of the reader, cut by cut in the order it
  will be traced, holds, then runs down into their hand; the column of light is softer.
- An extra drop's glint is larger, and the drop rides a gold thread from where it came out (Looting, Fortune,
  Harvest).
- **The drifting letters** (a table in a Study, a Word Stone, Wayfarer's motes): one in three is the sign of a word you
  know, the rest the script's twelve letters (`LetterParticle.pick`; 36 sign sprites after the letters in
  `particles/enchant_letter.json`, written by the art spec in that order).

### 45.18 Sound (first picks; Euan's ear decides on `tools/art/enchant_listen.py`)
Every beat is Minecraft's own recordings by name. A stroke seals with one recording (`enchant.seal`, an eye set into an
