  with the day in and the door shut, walking into the Loop lights your path and it stands where you were, at three
  quarters night sweeps round, standing on your own trail its replay reaches you, at half the outer ring falls and the
  causeway stays, from a quarter the Seed's door turns and opens, over the edge is a fall and you wake by the arch with
  the hall whole again, it comes again, the win opens the door with a path of light and is rank Sovereign, the hall is
  put back). `descent_rules` (the Seed waits for Sovereign), `hearth_pure_rules` (every rank's trial is a Proving).

**47.11 Sight (Euan's playtest 2026-11-03: "mobs in gates should attack based on line of sight").** A creature notices,
chases and fires at you only while it knows where you are: it sees you (eye to eye, blocks in the way), or it hears you
close by (4 blocks, a Hunter's ear 12; heard is moving, swinging, struck or off the ground, a sneak is silent; creative
and spectators make no sound). Its wake-up (`AwakenMob`'s player target) takes only someone it senses, never someone
through a wall (Hunters used to notice through walls: now they hear further instead). One set on you without sensing
you (a room its door woke) knows where you were from that. Fighting you, after 3 s (`LOSE_TICKS` 60) of neither seeing
nor hearing you it lets you go and walks to the last place it knew you were and looks about there for 10 s
(`SeekSound`, every creature now, was Listeners only); it notices you again the moment it sees or hears you. Listeners
keep their own rule (they lose you 3 s after you go quiet).
- **Shots need a clear line.** A ranged or poison ability (bolt, arrows, beam, cloud, rain, cone, roots, fangs, lift,
  pull) starts only with you in sight, as a charge, a leap or a blink does, and checks again when it lets go: ducked out
  of its line during the wind-up, it lets go with a puff of smoke and a hiss and nothing flies (`AbilityRunner.blind`;
  the cooldown is spent). Kit bosses fire through the same runner, so the same holds in their arenas.
- **Bosses** keep you while you hide (their room is the fight, `keepsTarget`), but their shots still need the line, so
  a pillar is cover from a boss too. Melee was already line-checked (§47.3's capsules).
- **The Wilds' forms** (`living.combat.MarkGoal`): a volley, snipe, spit or pull is held at release without a clear line
  (`Moves.held`, the same puff), and a spit's ray stops at the first block (`Moves.rayTarget`).
- Test: `mobs_sight` (an ink-spitter in a stone pen, you 8 off and walking: it doesn't notice you; set on you, it never
  fires and nothing strikes you, it lets you go within 3 s and goes to where you were; the wall comes down and it
  notices you).

**47.12 Every death ends (Euan's playtest 2026-11-03: "killed a beast but the body is still there").** Each of our
creatures (gate creatures, bosses, beasts, forms, kin) is gone within its own fall (vanilla's second; a beast's fall,
`NamedBeast.deathTicks`, 1.8 s; a kit boss's topple up to 4 s) and its death runs its drops. The body that stayed was the
hunt's carcass (§41.6), laid at a fixed second while a beast's longer fall still played beside it, and drawn standing:
our renderers never read the carcass mark. Now the carcass is laid only once the falling body has gone (checked every
tick, laid anyway after 5 s, `Carcass.FALL_MAX` 100), where and as its fall ended (a body can slide or drift as it
falls: the Lantern Maw's did), and every renderer of ours (hero, wild, kit, the creature renderer and the forms') draws a
carcass as at the end of its fall, its light out, without the red and without landing it again (`LivingHooks.carcass`,
both sides; `Life.lies`). A beast is the hunt's quarry only as the world brings it (`AwakenMob.configure`, through
`Mobs.spawn` or `/awaken fauna summon`); vanilla's `/summon` skips that, so such a beast leaves no carcass.
- Test: `mobs_every_death` (every awaken creature, over 150, on a stone floor inside the forced ground, spawned and
  killed by a player with no knockback, Rises spent first: each is gone within its fall plus 2 ticks, each ran its drops,
  no carcass is laid beside its own falling body, and each hunted beast's carcass lies where it fell within 3 ticks of
  its body going).
- A body is no longer a creature (Euan's playtest 2026-11-08, the Briar Sow's carcass: "still shows the vanilla heart plate
  and info, and I still get the lock-on HUD"). A carcass keeps its health, so it read as alive to everything that asks,
  and it wears no plate, so Jade read it out in full. `Aim.body` (a carcass, or anything dying, both sides) now takes it out
  of Jade's ray trace (`JadeClient.body`), the mark and the lock (`Lock.foe`, and the creature under the crosshair) and the
  server's check of a press (`Aim.meant`). You can still use it to carve it. A creature lying fallen that will get up is
  alive: it keeps its card and its lock. Test `aim_bodies`.
- A body rests on the ground, never in it (Euan's playtest 2026-11-11, a Plumed Coil's carcass on jungle grass: "the body
  of a beast fell through the floor here and is also glitchy visually, like the texture is shimmering"). Three causes.
  Vanilla's sideways flip (and the life layer's topple, which replaced it for our creature renderer) turns a body about
  the middle of its feet, so half its width went under the ground; several of our death clips ended low (the Coil's
  dropped its head 9.5 px and rolled it 80 degrees, so the coil stood on end into the ground, 27 of its cubes below it);
  and a flier killed on the wing kept its no-gravity while it died and its carcass was laid where it hung (a carcass has
  no mind, so nothing brings it down). The shimmer was the ground's own face cutting through the sunken body, and the
  body's flat plumes and faces lying in or across it.
  - `mobs.client.BodyRest`: every dying or lying body (`deathTime` above 0: a fall, a carcass, a fallen or toppled
    creature) within 64 blocks is measured each frame as it will be drawn: its renderer's own chain (`BodyRest.Posed` on
    the hero, wild, kit, creature, humanoid, skinned and forms' renderers; vanilla's flip for vanilla's, 180 degrees for
    spiders, silverfish and endermites; cube mobs, fish, squid, phantoms, shulkers, the wither and armour stands are left as
    they are), posed and drawn into a probe that keeps every vertex. It is leaned along the lie of the land under it (read
    at half its size each way from the feet, at most 20 degrees, eased in over half a second; read where it lies, not where
    its pose reaches, so the lean never jumps), then raised until its lowest point lies 1/64 block above the ground under
    that point, plus a sheep's wool (1.75 px) or worn armour (1 px). Its middle (the middle half of its spread each way)
    rests on the ground; a part outside it (a weapon, an antler, a wing, a pole, a feeler) holds the middle up at most
    3/16 block times its size, and past that goes into the ground, so a duelist's blade or a lamplighter's pole never
    stands the body on end. It may be let down at most half a block onto ground it floats above (never in water). The
    ground is the top of the first block down each column from 9/16 above the feet to
    2 below, where it stops a body or, if its outline spans the whole block, where it is seen (snow layers, soul sand,
    mud); grass and flowers are no ground; ground higher than a step is a wall and holds nothing; and within a quarter
    block of a higher column the ground rises to meet it, so a body sweeping onto a step rises, never jumps. Nothing under
    it in reach (in the air, mid-water): its lowest point stays at least at its feet. Eased in over its first three ticks.
    It pushes in `RenderLivingEvent.Pre` at the lowest priority and pops in `Post` at the highest; a renderer whose model
    can't be measured is left as drawn from then on.
  - A flier killed in the air (not in water, not a kit boss's scripted fight) falls through its death throes
    (`AwakenMob.die`: gravity back on; dead, its server step no longer turns it off). A carcass whose fall ended off the
    ground is laid on the ground under it, or on water it would fall into, at most 64 blocks down (`Carcass.restY`). A
    cave creature hanging from the roof already lets go when struck.
  - The death clips that ended in the ground were re-authored so the body itself lies on it, measured with the rule
    above (`tools/art/specs`): the Plumed Coil lies in a flat S on its side, head on its cheek, jaw slack, plumes and
    streamers lying back, its wings folding over it; the Old Antler goes down on its side with its neck stretched
    along the ground instead of its antlers dug in; the Mire Mother's reeds fold flat both ways; the Hollow Owl's
    under wing folds under its body and the other sprawls; the Empress Moth's wings close over its back; the
    Thousandfoot's legs give, it sinks onto its belly, tips onto its side with its body riding up over its edge, the
    legs it lies on held up until it lands and then flopping out flat past its belly, and it curls belly in, flat on the
    ground (its old sideways curl stood it on end); the Mycelord's cap hits first and tips back onto its rim, top up,
    instead of standing in the ground like a wheel (a body on a cap that size rests on rim and root, its stem a little
    above the ground); the Briar Sow's head lolls level instead of burying chin and tusks; the Brook Otter on its back
    rests its head on its cheek; the Hushling's arms fall forward; the Pollen Grazer's under wings lie back along the
    ground. The Weaver Queen still kneels, as authored; water creatures (Lantern Maw, Tidesteed, Breathbell,
    Glimmerfin) mostly die in water and keep their clips.

**47.13 Beasts at range (Euan's playtest 2026-11-03: the Briar Sow, "when I saw it at a distance, it was shaking a ton
for some reason and glitching").** Each guess was checked against film and a frame-by-frame trace: the client's smoothing
of a tracked body against our renderers, the life layer's far step at 32 blocks (springs and idles off), and a fight over
position between server and client. On open ground none of them shook a beast: tour `fights-beasts-far` films eight
beasts 36 to 58 blocks off at a narrow view (fov 30, so they fill the frame at their real distance), with their AI, while
the camera glides in across the far step, and with no AI; and `/awaken lifetrace <type> <frames>` (dev, client) logs the
nearest of a kind each frame it's drawn (where, its turn, every way the life layer moves its body, which feet are up, a
blow's flinch and its red), since a clip on CI runs at about 6 frames a second and can't resolve a shake. The shake was
the brambles. Vanilla's sweet berry bush holds anything living but a fox or a bee (0.8 of its speed, its momentum gone
each tick) and pricks it while it moves (1 damage, as often as its hurt allows: twice a second). The Briar Sow's wallow is
ringed with ripe bushes (`LairBuilder`), as are other lairs (their ring scatter) and the kin's nooks (`KinSpawner`). Each
prick flashed her red, flinched her life layer and cried her hurt, and the bush stopped her dead at every step, so she
went on in little jerks: from afar a shudder for as long as she moved among them, walking her wallow or charging through
it at you. A small wild thing (an ambient one) also bolts from a hit with no attacker (`FaunaMob.hurtServer`, 5 s), so
among bushes it fled a new way at each prick. Now our wild things (`FaunaMob` and all its kinds: beasts, named
beasts, cave, deep and water fauna, wild mounts) and the kin (`KinBeast`) live among brambles as a fox does: a berry bush
neither holds them (`makeStuckInBlock`) nor pricks them (its damage turned aside). Our own Bramble (§41.2) pricks only a
sprinter, which none of them is, and its hold stays: a thicket slows a beast as it slows you.
- Dev: the autopilot's `opt fov <30-110>` (films far things at their real distance); `/awaken lifetrace` (client only).
- Test: `mobs_brambles` (a Briar Sow driven straight across eight blocks of ripe berry bushes, walled in so there is no
  way round: never pricked, and across in under 7 s; before the fix she was pricked within 2 s).
- Nothing paths through a berry bush (26.3 marks it DAMAGING, blocked), and a beast as wide as the Sow (2.1 blocks) is
  steered round them, so only a straight drive puts her among them: her Bramble Charge, or your blows' knockback.
- Tour: `fights-beasts-far` (CI): the living row, the glide, the still row, the Sow charging through a belt of ripe
  bushes 34 to 39 blocks off at a still cow beyond it that struck her, and a Sow killed at 36 lying where she fell; each
  filmed and traced, run before and after the fix (2026-11-03, runs 41597858314 and 41597858169). Before: her charge
  stuck on the belt's far edge for 3 s, pricked five times (red, and the life layer's dip to 1.3), inching out between
  pricks. After: through the belt in 0.4 s at full speed, never pricked, and unpricked standing in it for 4 s after a
  second charge. On open ground, both runs: the drawn path smooth and still bodies still, near and far.

**47.14 Fair damage (Euan's playtest 2026-11-04: in a hive gate "every single mob would explode and take out like 75% of
my health", then "I entered the boss room, and I basically insta-died with no way to do anything").** Nobody who
belongs in a fight loses most of their health to one thing in it; a rank gap may still be deadly. The reference player
is the weakest who belongs: the rank's first level (E 1, D 10, C 25, B 45, A 70, S 100, Sovereign 135), a sixth of its
points in VIT, the rank's Hunter set with its set bonus, Normal difficulty (`core.api.FairShare`; its health at a
content level is 20 + 0.3 a level). Every number below is a share of that player's max health, after armour, VIT and
the blow's class, poison and burn left behind counted in full (poison stops at half a heart, which is still most of you).
- **Budgets, one blow.** A gate's normal 25% (a PERILOUS blow, drawn before it lands and answered by a dodge, 30%), an
  elite 35% (40%), a warden 40% (45%), a Lord, guardian, Sovereign, Proving Warden or the last 40% (PERILOUS or its
  signature 50%). Nothing takes more than half. A Lord's string (its moves one after another, §47.3) is one source:
  50% together. The move a Lord opens the fight with, 25%.
- **Where each is met.** A creature is fought from its theme's home rank up to S at the gate's level (a dream's at 0.8
  of it, a Trial's at the rank's first level: both softer); a stratum's at the stratum's level (`Strata.contentLevel`;
  the odd strata open a rank before their level, so an early diver meets the one-rank-under numbers); a Sovereign in the
  Hollow Court at S, and the Reflection again at the Sovereign Reassessment (135); a Proving's Warden at its
  Reassessment's first level; the last at the Seed's.
- **The fair guard** (`mobs.entity.FairGuard`, after armour, lowest priority), the backstop under the budgets: for a
  player at or above the rank of what hurts them (`MobLoot.rankFor` of its level, or the gate's rank for what has no
  creature behind it in a gate: its traps, water, falling floors, `GateHooks.rankOf`), one blow takes at most half their
  health and one source at most half in any 4 s (80 ticks: nine in ten Lord strings land inside it). A Lord and what it
  calls are one source. The land's creatures carry the land's level (`CreatureTag`: vanilla monsters, herds, a hunt's
  lead, a camp's) and are held by it: a vanilla creeper's blast, the same at every level, took 131% of the E reference
  player a block and a half off and 90% of the D player; both land half now. What it holds back is what would have come off; nothing else changes (the blow still lands,
  knocks and flashes). It doesn't hold a rank gap, the void or /kill, or anything outside a gate with no creature behind
  it. A Glass gate's doubled blows meet it too: Glass makes small hits hurt, never one blow a death.
- **A Lord's moment.** Walking into a boss room never kills: the moment a Lord first sees you (its intro, or its fight
  script's first move), for 3 s everything together, the Lord, its company, the room, takes at most a quarter of you
  (`FairGuard.arrive`, from `AwakenBoss.moment`). One moment at a time; not for a rank gap.
- **What the audit changed** (first measured 4 Nov: 69 creature blows and 428 Lord blows over at every rank, 20 and
  294 once each was measured only where it's met). Ability power, a creature's melee or a kit move's damage scaled to
  fit (bestiary and `kit/moves`), then raised again from the two measured points to land 90% of the budget at the
  worst rank, never above where they were (armour takes a bigger share of a small blow, so the first cut overshot: the
  Herald's Collapse fell to 19%): the Hollow Herald's Collapse 2.2 to 1.18 (141% of the A reference player to 42%), the
  Signal's Shadow's Seed Collapse 2.6 to 1.51 (128% at S to 46%), the Seed Warden's Door Light 2.2 to 1.61, the three
  Sovereign bursts (Shutdown, Deafening Silence, Never Wake) 2.2 to 1.62 (80% to 44%), the Abbot of Frost's Glacial Vow
  2.2 to 1.67, Moonbeam, Instruction, Inverted Scream, the Curator's Silence in the Stacks, and the E and D wardens'
  charges and slams (the Rot's Rot Charge 60% at E to 43%, the Overgrowth, the Overseer, the Sexton), 41 blows in all;
  the Rot's Choking Field and the Mother of Spores' Bloom keep their power but poison I, not II (poison II took 42% of
  the E player alone). Strings are left to the guard: 131 of them would take more than half (the Hollow Herald's
  stride, swipe, swipe 98% at A), and land 50%.
- **Volatile bursts once.** A Volatile body (the modifier's tag, a dream room's, or a FUSE creature) bursts once, and
  the creature owns it (`AwakenMob.burst`): its reach (blast power x 2; an elite's x 1.3 wider) is drawn on the ground in
  the dodge colour the moment it falls, its floor filling to the edge over 1.25 s (`FairShare.BURST_FUSE`), with one
  hiss, then one blast (carrier BURST, `Carriers.burst`, client `CarrierView.burst`). The blast is vanilla's for its push
  and smoke, but its damage peaks at 40% of the fair health at its content level (an elite's 15% harder) and falls along
  vanilla's curve to nothing at the reach (`Blasts`): 17% of the E reference player one block off, less at
  every rank above. It is the body's blast, so a dodge answers it (`Strikes.of`: a blast with a cause is PERILOUS).
  Bosses never burst. Before: the creature burst at 0.5 s with vanilla's power 2 and the gate's Modifiers burst again
  0.5 s later, ownerless (no dodge) at 2.2, the same at E as at S; one block off they took 175% of the E reference
  player's health, and two hisses and two blasts a death crowded the sound pool. A FUSE creature's fuse (1.5 s, held
  still) draws the same reach and its blast is the same one; put out (you got 7 blocks away), its drawing ends. Your own
  Gravity detonation of a Volatile pair is their burst: it untags them before the kill, so they don't burst again.
- **Tests.** `fights_volatile_once`: the E reference player beside a Volatile creature as it dies: its reach drawn at
  once, nothing for the fuse, one blast within 30% of their health (17%; the old two blasts replayed beside it: 175%),
  and one standing just past the drawn edge untouched. `fights_fair_creatures`: every creature that isn't a Lord, its
  melee, abilities and kit moves, wherever it's met, against its budget (with the one-rank-under reading logged).
  `fights_fair_lords`: every Lord's abilities, kit moves, strings (through the guard) and opening move. `fights_fair_guard`:
  a 90% blow takes half, the same creature again inside the window nothing more, another creature's lands, a rank under
  takes all, past the window it lands again. `fights_fair_arrival`: three blows of twice the E player's health in a
  Lord's moment take a quarter together. `fights_fair_gates`: each of a gate's traps (the gauntlet's pit and press, the
  collapse's pit, a cave-in's stone, a world's catch) on every rank's reference player, 30% at most alone, under half
  under Glass; the gauntlet's press was 55% of the E player under Glass (4 + 12% of health), now 3 + 11% (42%, 18% alone).
  `fights_fair_wilds`: a levelled creeper's blast and a formed creeper's seed (rung 3, `Combos`) beside each rank's
  reference player, never more than half landing (the seed takes 40% at E on its own). Not tested, by reading: a
  herd's trample (4) and a storm cell's lightning (3) are flat, at most a fifth of the E player; the Descent's zones and
  the holdfasts deal nothing of their own (their creatures are audited, the Descent's water is vanilla drowning); a
  dream's Chase and Duel can't kill (a killing blow wakes you, `DreamEvents`) and their creatures are audited at the
  dream's level.

**47.15 Aimed blows (Euan's playtest 2026-11-08, the Hive Regent on build f7530d2d5: "sometimes the boss was literally
swinging in midair", "it would dash and then it would be like in the middle of the air", "it was flying like super
high", "even when I parred ... it was missing me anyways").** All one fault at the bottom: a swing was begun because
its body was near you, not because its blade would meet you. Before: 201 own-swing moves from 1,506 start places, 46%
landed as drawn (`fights_reach_table`); in a live fight against someone standing still the Regent began 13 melee blows
and landed 6, the Sky Leviathan 26 and 10, the Glass Serpent 15 and 8. Range was measured flat, so height never counted;
many clips cross the aim line over a player's head; every kit charge ran its root motion and then 14 more ticks at a
block a tick, up to the chest and with no gravity for a flier, so it overshot by 8 blocks and hung there; a flier's hover
followed every jump. And a deflect only ever fires on a blow that really lands (`ArmsServer.onShieldBlock`), so a miss
is a parry that does nothing.

- **The blow is aimed (`BlowAim`).** At the blow's lock tick the body takes the cheapest correction that brings the
  sweep of its capsules onto you where you stand: a turn (to 50 degrees), a step (to 1.2 blocks, never onto you), a lean
  about the hips (to 24 degrees, synced and drawn), for a flier a dip (to 1.5 blocks, never through the floor), for a lunge
  a shorter or longer run (0.35 to 2 times, never past your centre). It takes that once. Move after the lock and the blow
  misses, as it should: the lock is the moment you are read, and the wind-up after it is your window.
- **A blow with no correction isn't begun.** `FightRunner.reaches` runs the same solve first; a move that can't land from
  here isn't tried again for 8 ticks, the body closes instead, and a string's next blow stops the string (a duel's phrase
  still ends in its opening). A height band (the sweep plus 1.2, plus 1.5 more for a flier) keeps a body from starting
  anything over or under you. A body inside its own swing (edge under 0.35) makes room at 0.16 a tick.
- **A charge stops at you.** A kit charge (ability CHARGE) has no root motion on top; it runs from where it is to 1.5
  blocks past you (`AbilityRunner.chargeRun`), level with your feet for a flier, in as many ticks as that takes (4 to 18),
  and its ground line draws that length.
- **Fliers hold your floor.** `FlyHunt.scripted` holds a kit flier 0.35 over the ground under you, not over your head;
  it follows you up only when you've been in the air 60 ticks (and then to a block under you). A wanted height at floor
  level makes the flight control detour upward, hence the 0.35 and the dip to reach you. One down on the floor (a dive
  or a charge ends level with your feet) flies off it level: its clearance under it stops at the ground it is on
  ("Fliers find their way").
- Two moves redrawn at the cause: the Regent's Royal Dive (its capsules were 2.6 to 4.7 over its feet) and the Sovereign
  of Sleep's Buffet (it beat its wing too high and wide to touch anyone; it now drops two blocks into the beat). A string
  played by hand (tests, the studio) skips the gate.

After: 94% of the table once aimed, and every move can reach someone. Live against someone standing still: Regent 25 begun, 24 landed, never over 1.7
blocks above them; Sky Leviathan 26 and 24; Glass Serpent 15 and 13; Ember Tyrant 24 and 23; Gearwright Colossus 17
and 16. Tests `fights_reach_live_<id>` (five bodies, a real fight of 1,400 ticks through every phase) and
`fights_reach_table`. `tools/sim/combat_sim.py` still reads a move's reach without the aim, so it undercounts these hits.

**Answering it.** With blows landing, a parry has something to answer. Test `fights_reach_parry` plays the Regent's cut
at a real guard: unanswered it lands, into a raised sword it does no damage, goes into the stance and the Regent reels.
The ring existed all along and only fires on a blow that lands, so nothing rang on the misses. Added: a guard's raise has
its own sound (`arms.guard_raise`, three takes built from Kenney's CC0 cloth recording already in tools/art/sources, -16 dB, so
you know it's up), the deflect is 1 dB louder, a deflected limb sounds at the body (its own `impact` set at 0.8), and a melee
deflect throws sparks off the blade and jolts the hands (own view and everyone else's), which only a shot did before.

**A shot's own look.** Euan: "just kind of green particles, like vanilla green particles". They were: the thorn's trail was
vanilla's `HAPPY_VILLAGER`, and every other `BoltKind` trailed a vanilla particle too, half a block above the shot
(vanilla's `AbstractHurtingProjectile` adds 0.5 for a 1-block fireball; ours is 0.4). Now seven shapes of our own
(`MobParticles.Shot`: spark, ember, flake, wisp, puff, drop, sliver; sprites `tools/art/specs/shot_particles.py`, movement
`mobs.client.ShotParticles`), tinted per kind, on the shot's centre, for the trail and the burst it breaks into. Each kind has
a body (`BoltKind.Form`): a needle along its flight for stingers, thorns and glass, a bead with a trailing point for honey
and water, a glow for the rest, all still in the colour of how you answer it (§47.2). `BoltKind.STINGER` (appended, kinds are saved
by ordinal) is the Regent's Stinger Volley: venom-amber. A heal and a frenzy lost their green and red villager sparkles the
same way. Test `fights_shots_own_look`.

**The fire-tick crash.** A guard that turned a kit ability's blow on the tick it fired (the Bell Warden's clapper) ended the move
inside `abilityRunner().fire`, and the next line read the ability that had just been cleared: a ticking-entity crash that took
the world down. `FightRunner.step` now returns if the move ended there. Test `fights_reach_parry_fires`.

**47.16 The dead get up once, and you can stop them** (Euan's playtest 2026-11-08, "they're fake dying": every creature in an
Echoing gate fell, stood up with health again, and couldn't be hit while it lay, with nothing to say why).

- **Say so.** Walking into an Echoing gate, the entry card reads "In this gate, the dead get up once. Hit them again while
  they're down and they stay down." (`Modifiers.entryLine`, after any twist's line; not in a friendly gate).
- **Finishing.** For its 2.5 seconds on the ground a fallen creature takes any blow someone struck: a player's weapon, shot or
  power, or a vanilla pet's (`AwakenMob.finishes`: the source has an attacker, and that isn't one of our creatures; our own tame beasts count as those). Fire, falls,
  a poison's tick and the creature's own kind pass over it. The next blow lands at once (the fall clears the hurt cooldown).
  It lies at 1 health, so a real blow ends it there, as a real death: loot, kill credit, its death effects.
- **The rise is spent when it falls** (`Forces.markRisen` moves from the rise to the fall), so a finished body doesn't get up,
  a gate doesn't replace it and a Descent zone doesn't raise it. Left alone it gets up at half health as before. Saved mid-fall,
  it gets up as soon as it's loaded.
- **Nothing turns the finishing blow:** falling ends a guard and a phase, and a fallen REFLECT creature doesn't bounce shots.
- **A boss holds a tenth of its health while it lies** (`AwakenBoss.fallenHealth`; the RISES Guardian and Nightmare, and gate
  Wardens under Echoing). Its getting up is part of the fight, so a stray tap can't skip it; a real flurry in the 2.5 seconds can.
- A fallen creature is alive, so it keeps its card and its lock (§47.12's `Aim.body` is for real bodies only). Same path for
  `Forces.Tag.ECHO` and `Trait.RISES`. Test `mobs_echo_finish`; the entry line in `gates_modifiers_live`.

## 48. Fights That Read You (plan docs/fights/read-you.html, page https://claude.ai/artifact/NkwLujmbiY1iF9hfnYqYn2; approved in full 2026-11-09)

A boss stops rolling dice at you: it watches what you've started, answers it where you can see it notice, changes its mind
partway through a string, and in time moves like a fighter between blows and takes turns in a pack. Built pilots first (the
Hive Regent and the Gearwright Colossus); the other 45 wait until Euan has played those. The rules that never bend: it never
reads input, only what has visibly started and only after its reaction time; every blow keeps its tell, colour and at least its
minimum warning; a blow begins only if it can land; every string ends in an opening; none of this adds damage, health or speed;
everything is decided on the server, per target.

**48.1 Watching (stage 1).** `core.api.Watch.facts(entity)` says what anyone could see a fighter doing: drinking or eating and
a raised guard (vanilla's own state), a heavy being held, a blow's recovery and a dodge (Arms' `ArmsServer.watched`), a cast
or a channel (Powers' `Casting.watched`, for 12 ticks after a cast). Never a key press. `FightMind` keeps, for its one target,
when each fact began, and a fact only counts once it has been true for its reaction time: 12 ticks at rank E, one less each rank,
7 at the top (`reaction(Rank)`, the boss's home rank; a script's `react` overrides it). A new target starts the read again. Two
facts are worked out rather than asked for: a dodge just made (16 ticks past the reaction time) and a stop after a run (three
half-second samples running away, then standing still within a second).

**48.2 Answers and the notice.** A fight script's `mind.answers` (schema 2; a script without a `mind` plays exactly as it did)
ties a fact to a list of moves. An answer is weighed once when it comes due and then rests (`cooldown`, default 200 ticks; 40
after a failed roll), and the newest thing you started wins. It uses the first move on its list that can land on you now, and
never the move it just made. It can only start between blows: with nothing playing, or at a string's link, where the
follow-through ends as it would for the string's next blow. A swing that has begun is never cancelled and an opening is never
cut short. At a phrase's *last* blow only an answer marked `press` may start (the pilots' drink): you began that while it was
still swinging, so it carries on, and the opening, longer for the longer phrase, comes after. An answer shows it noticed: 5
ticks with `KIT_POSE_NOTICE` (the head turns and the body drops and leans, procedural, so it works on every rig), the palette's
`notice` set, else `step`, else `impact` at half volume; then the answer's wind-up with its tell, colour and class as always.
If you've got out of reach during those 5 ticks the normal choice takes over.

**48.3 Cooldowns, held blows and the caught dodge.** With a mind, the dice may not pick the move just made nor one still resting
(`mind.cooldowns`, else by class: LIGHT 0, HEAVY 30, PERILOUS and GRAB 80, a move that hurts nobody 240). If nothing it may start
reaches you for 2 seconds its blows' rests are waived; a move that hurts nobody (a buff, a heal, a summon) always keeps its rest. It
never makes the same move twice running by choice. The one exception is a last resort: a blow may follow itself when nothing else it
could do has reached you for 10 seconds (3 seconds in a phase with only one close blow, which has nothing else to do there), so a
spot only one move reaches isn't safe. A string doesn't repeat either: a next blow that would be the move just made is dropped (a
fork can land on the blow that was coming anyway). And a body whose longest close blow is the one it just made steps in, after 0.75 s
with nothing to start, until a shorter one reaches, instead of standing there. Any blow may be
held a beat at its peak (`holdChance` 25%, `holdTicks` 6, or its own authored hold if longer), which only ever adds warning. Having
deflected it again and again it always holds. The third dodge in a row (each within 2 seconds of the last) is caught: once it has
seen that third dodge, the next blow holds for at least 10 ticks and keeps turning to you through the hold, so it lands where you
do. The streak is then spent. A held-blow fake is a separate promise, for top-rank duellists and Wardens only, and isn't built yet.

**48.4 Forks.** A string entry's `forks` give, for the blow after each one, what to play by what you're doing at the link: `guard`
if your guard has been up its reaction time, `dodged` if you've just dodged (the newest of the two wins), else `stayed`. Until the
fork the branches look identical. A branch that can't land on you now is skipped and the string goes on as written. A pool entry's
`band` keeps it to a range of edge distance. `FairAudit` reads every string a fight can play: the pools', with forks taken, and the
answers'. The runtime's fair guard still holds any one string to half your health.

**48.5 The pilots, and what a mind must hold.** The Hive Regent and the Gearwright Colossus carry schema 2 scripts
(`tools/art/specs/kit/bosses/<id>.py`, no new art). In their answers a drink brings the dive or the stride from afar and the Sting or
the Slam up close and presses on through a last blow; a guard kept up for 1.5 s brings the Sting, or the Grab or the Strikes; a
heavy being held is hit first with a quick one; a cast brings the gap-closer; a pause after a run brings the pounce; a recovery the
blow that punishes it. Tests (`FightMindTests`, one per mechanism): the read waits, new targets start again, each answer gives one of its
moves with its tell after the notice, each fork, the caught dodge, the facts themselves (`arms_watched`, `powers_watched_cast`). Gates,
in `fights_record_*` for any fight with a mind: every repeat is that last resort (exact, since a percentage of a dozen moves is noise;
the table holds the worst fight to 10%). In `fights_mind_drinks_<boss>`: at least 60%
of drinks in reach (one of the answer's moves, in its phase, could land while the drink is seen) get an answer that starts
before the drink ends, over 448 drinks (with 56, one run's own fight moved the share 6% either way, and the Regent's,
about 70% since the Stinger Volley waits for phase 2, passed or failed on the dice; fifteen fights of 224 still ran from
65% to 79%); every drink it was free to answer
(between blows, a move it may answer with able to land, 3 ticks before the drink ends) is answered; at least three in
four drinks are in reach; the player stands on the ground. By the table: guard-beating moves (PERILOUS and GRAB) when you turtle
at least double what they are against someone standing.

**48.6 Every boss has a mind (Euan 2026-11-09, after playing the pilots: "apply these changes ... to all bosses").** The 45 others
get what the two pilots have, from `tools/art/specs/kit/minds.py`, made from each body's own moves and nothing new: a drink
brings its gap-closer or shot from afar and its guard-beater, heavy or quick blow up close; a cast and a stop after a run its
gap-closer or shot; a heavy being held its quickest blows; a guard kept up its red moves and grabs, else its heavy; a recovery its
hardest close blow. A string's next blow forks to the guard-beater (or the heavy) on a raised guard and to the gap-closer after a
dodge. Its gap-closers rest 60 ticks. A move that fills the room or ends the fight (a signature with no blade of its own, or a
reach of 40) answers nothing, and neither does a move kept for behind. A script written with its own `mind` keeps it. **An answer or a fork never reaches for
a move its phase hasn't got yet** (`FightRunner.inPhase`), so a late phase's moves stay in the late phase; the Regent's Stinger Volley
now answers only from her second phase on. Tempers, footwork and each boss's own trick aren't in this. `fights_mind_every_boss`
checks they all have one; `fights_record_<boss>_guard` runs each of the others once, the Lantern Broker excepted (it trades with you and only duels if you ask).

**48.8 The body keeps the clip's clock (Euan's playtest 2026-11-09: the Ember Tyrant's run "is super glitchy ... not super smooth";
"double check all different bosses").** The clip runs on the server's clock (`ServerPace`), but the body's place reached the client
every third tick and took three more to arrive, so a body carried by a move began to travel after its legs began to run and went
on gliding after they stopped: on a real client (`fights-charge-trace`, CI 42601411803) the Tyrant's 12-tick run ended at 1.4 s on its
clip and at 1.6 s on the ground, a third of the run out of step. Any late packet also stopped it dead for a tick, since the place was
only ever three ticks ahead of what had been drawn. All 47 bodies now: are placed every tick (`updateInterval(1)`) and glide to it
in three steps (`LinearInterpolationHandler`), which a packet one or two ticks late doesn't stop; and while a move or a charge carries
one, it's sent ahead by two ticks of what's left of its run (`AwakenBoss.trackingPosition`, `FightRunner.lead`, `AbilityRunner.lead`),
never further than the move still goes (an ability charge brakes to a fifth on its last tick, so that tick counts for a fifth:
CI 42603379006 showed the Guardian of the Gardens running 0.42 past its stop and sliding back; `fights_charge_stops_where_sent`),
and not at all if a wall is there. Two ticks is exactly what the glide lags at a steady speed:
the client draws the body where the server has it on every tick, start and end included (`fights_body_keeps_up`, all 66 moves that
carry a body). The server's own place, and so every reach and every hit, is unchanged. A move cut short (a deflect) can pull the drawn
body back up to two ticks of its run. What a carried body's legs do isn't touched: the charge's stride swings about 34 degrees a tick
where the same body's run swings about 8, the next thing to look at if the run still reads wrong.

**48.7 The recorder (stage 0).** `FightRecorder`: `fights_record_<boss>_<kind>`, six bosses (more as the roll-out reaches them)
against six kinds of player (stands still, runs, circles, holds guard, keeps away, stays behind), 72 s each with fixed seeds;
`fights_record_pack` counts a pack of 12 winding up at once. It logs one `[record]` line a fight and asserts only that the fight
ran, including that the boss never left ticking ground (`AwakenTests.wideArea`). `tools/fights/record_table.py` makes the table;
the numbers before the mind are in docs/fights/read-you-baseline.md.


## 52. The Hall of Arms (choosing weapons and armour; page https://claude.ai/artifact/UZX5KofQPGeXHeiPxJ9sxK)
Euan 9 Nov: the Armoury, Fitting Stand and War Anvil windows were "just a block of text... ugly... too linear". They become one
place you stand in. Package `dev.awaken.hall`; the old screens stay behind `classicScreens` in `awaken-hall-client.toml` for one
build, then go.

**The sheet.** Every Hall screen is laid out on one 1708 x 960 sheet (`Stage`), fitted to the window and letterboxed; text sizes
snap to whole real pixels. Blackletter is Jacquard 24 baked to a bitmap (`tools/art/hall/title_font.py`; OFL text beside it; the TTF
is not in the repo). Weapon meshes are the real ones, drawn live by `PicRenderer` into their own textures with the Hall's shader
(`hall_weapon`), once when the wall changes and every frame only for the weapon brought close.

**The Wall.** 16 kinds across (five bays: Blades, Heavy, Reach, Close, Strange), 6 ranks up, receding. Dark except round your lantern
(the mouse) and below the tide (your level, the line and the words "You, level N"). `HallServer.wall` judges each niche and the client
only draws it: `SHAPE` not found (black, no name), `OFFER` on Hale's rack at your rank (iron), `OVER` known but above your level (its
true look), `KNOWN` known and short of parts (dimmed), `READY` (lit even in the dark), `MADE` held or remembered (lit even in the
dark). Filters: Everything, Ready now, Tracked. 15 seals for the Lord-forged: closed until you have taken one, and one you hold opens
close up. It never names a boss in advance.

**A weapon brought close.** Clicking a niche zooms the wall away and flies that weapon to the middle of the screen, turning; drag to
turn it. Left: the six ranks of the kind (a click changes rank). Right, in a dark panel: rank and name; blurb; damage (`damage + 1`),
swings a second (`speed + 4`), uses and reach (the chain's longest strike); against the weapon in your hand; **what makes it
different**, from the numbers the blows use (`HallSpecial`, never typed by hand per weapon); **what it takes**, each material as the
real item (a tag's members in turn) with have/need and where it comes from; and what you can do here at this door. The action
stands at the bottom and is the Armoury's own logic: at a War Anvil Hold to forge (0.6 s, Space or the mouse, or one click with
`clickToCommit`), From memory, Forge the blade, Rebuild it; at the Forge Raise it, Draw a copy; at Hale's rack Buy; Track anywhere.
A paragraph that won't fit is left out whole, never cut. Unfound: "Unknown", no numbers, nothing given away.

**Refreshing.** Twice a second the screen hashes your pack; a change asks `ArmsArmoury.REFRESH`, so what you pick up shows without
reopening. Test `hall_wall`: the wall says the same as the Armoury's list.

**The Armour wing.** 29 suits on six terraces climbing away, ranks E (nearest) to S, kinds across; each row stands in the gaps of the
one before it, the rows zigzagging, so a suit at the back is hidden as little as possible (`TerraceLayout`, offsets found by search).
Lit round your lantern and below your level; unfound suits are black shapes with no name. The same filters as the wall. Clicking one
brings it close: it stands turning, each piece named on the figure (`Helm`, `Cuirass`, `Greaves`, `Boots`, with what state it's in; a
click or Tab picks the piece); the same kind at every rank on the left; on the right what the suit does (its two-piece and four-piece
abilities come before the piece's own rows: that is why you'd want it; the four-piece line comes first and a full panel never drops it,
giving up in turn where a material comes from (it moves to a tip on the material), a reason the red counts already give, then the comparison; five or six materials share one row), the armour of the whole suit, what the piece you picked does
against what you wear, the real items it takes, an inlay of any catalyst you carry, and Hold to forge the piece. Unfound patterns
say where patterns come from, never which creature. `Your looks` (each piece's look, one dye) moved here. Track a suit and it goes on
K > Tasks as `armour/tracked` (one at a time). The Fitting Stand opens this wing; K's way in looks and tracks only. Test `hall_suits`.

**The War Anvil.** No window: your weapon hangs turning over your own forge, which is out of focus and dim behind it, and your hand is
empty while it does. Three rites wait underneath, each shown by a real thing from the game: the smith's hammer (Temper), the Forge
(Reforge), the stones in turn (Attune). Never a drawn sigil (Euan 9 Nov: "need actual icons that still feel like MC"). Point at a rite
and the steel shows it, the numbers drawn out of the weapon: heat runs down the blade for Temper, the next rank's weapon hangs over it
for Reforge, the Force's colour fills it for Attune. Choosing a rite arms it; every cost is its real item; Hold commits, and the weapon
lands. Attune takes any stone you carry, with the off hand's stone chosen first; a stone you don't have is still drawn in full, so you
know it when you find it. Tests `arms_anvil_*`.

**The line-up.** A step on K > Tasks that offers a choice of armour ("Choose your first armour", "Make your D-rank armour") opens the
suits themselves, tall and side by side, instead of a list (`LineUpScreen`; `SetPreviewScreen` stays behind `classicScreens`). Each has
its name, its kind and how close you are. A click brings it close in the same view as the Armour wing, with "Choose this one" where
Track would be and left and right moving between the offers only. The step's choice is the Tasks page's own (`TaskPage.choose`).

**The moment it's made.** When the Forge Song or the anvil's song finishes: a hit of light a quarter of a second long, then the piece's
name in blackletter and how it came out ("Flawless", "Temper II", "Attuned") for about three seconds (`HallMoment`), over whatever
screen finished it. The details stay on that screen's own card.

**Sounds.** Minecraft's own recordings by name, nothing built (`HallSounds`): you come in, `block.furnace.fire_crackle` low; something
brought close, `block.chain.place`; a different rank, rite, stone or wing, `item.armor.equip_iron`; back, `block.iron_trapdoor.open`;
a held press, the fire rising in three steps; the weapon coming down, `block.anvil.land` quietly; made, `block.anvil.land` and
`block.heavy_core.place`.

**For everyone.** High Contrast brightens the quiet text. Hide Lightning Flashes takes out the hit of light. Distortion Effects under
50% means things arrive rather than fly and nothing turns by itself (drag still does). The narrator reads what is brought close and
which rite is picked, on a change only. On the sheet, text sizes snap to whole real pixels, rounding down unless the size is within .35 of a pixel of the next step (at 1.93 real pixels to a sheet pixel, size 2 stays 4 real pixels rather than falling to 3). A line can come out a few percent wider than laid out, so widths, fits and wraps all measure text at its snapped size.

**Hover (Euan, 11 Nov 2026: "you don't actually see well which one you're about to click on").** On the wall and on the
terraces the thing under the pointer has a hover state of its own, beyond the lantern and the name at the head: the
band's corner brackets round its niche or its figure (`Stage.brackets`), warm light under it, and the thing itself drawn
again fully lit and a touch larger (7% a suit, 10% a weapon) in its own picture (`KEY_HOVER`), redrawn only when the pointer
moves to another. The light never gives anything away: what you haven't found stays a shape and a kind on offer stays
plain iron. The arrow keys' cursor shows the same state. A Fitting Stand that is holding a suit: §44.14.

## 50. Powers in Full Voice (plan docs/powers-aaa/PLAN.md, page https://claude.ai/artifact/G6vDNHxaMBnyHF84e51pFg, all 43 yes 9 Nov 2026)

Stage 0 is the proof: Haymaker, Shockwave, Gravity Well and Railgun rebuilt to the plan's bar, and nothing else. Later stages wait for Euan to play this one.

### 50.1 Standing rules

A plain press does at least what it did before. The server decides damage. The 20% boss hit cap (`PowerMath.capBossHit`) beats everything; under it, all bonuses together stop at 1.6x (`PowerMath.capBonus`). Terrain changes put themselves back (`TerrainLedger`). Bonuses never apply against players, and no slam or fold is ever done to a player or a boss. A timed moment has two ticks of grace and is judged when you pressed (`PowerMath.pressedAge`: the age less your latency, at most 6 ticks forgiven). Only six powers are timed at all (Haymaker, Charged Shot, Railgun, Brace, Dash, Barrier): Euan rejected timing on every power.

### 50.2 Stance

`PowerStance.add` goes through `Strikes.posture` and answers to the same rules as a blade: an opening takes 1.5x, a duel body standing braced 0.5x (`ArmsRules.OPENING_POSTURE`, `GUARDED_POSTURE`). Weights: Light 3, Medium 6, Heavy 12, Massive 20. Never a player. These numbers still need agreeing with the Fights That Read You work before Stage 1.

| Power | Stance |
|---|---|
| Haymaker | 6 at a tap, climbing to 12 at full charge; 16 when clean |
| Shockwave | Light for each body |
| Gravity Well | A boss standing in it is not pulled: 2 every second instead |
| Railgun | (6 + 6 x charge + 4 x overcharge), falling to half at 48 blocks |
| Wall slam | Medium from a Haymaker, Light from a wave |

### 50.3 Haymaker

Held up to 600 ticks and cast on the let-go; a long hold is just a full punch. Full charge is `chargeTicks(20)`. Reaching it sends `HOLD_READY` and the knuckle lock (`HAY_PEAK`). A let-go from two ticks before full to five (plus two grace) after it is clean: damage x1.25 through `capBonus`, stance 16, knock x1.25, a Piledriver stuns 15 ticks longer, 150 ms of hit-stop, `FxKind.PERFECT` and `FxFold`, which folds the target's model along the punch for 9 ticks. Never on a player. A clean plain punch also starts `WallSlam` for 26 ticks: a body still moving at 0.32 blocks a tick when it hits a wall takes half the punch again, 12 ticks of stun, comes off the wall and cracks it (`FxWallCrack`: real block crack stages, healing a stage every 7 ticks, and the wall's own chunks). Punching a bare wall at 40% charge or more cracks it the same way, and hurts nothing.

First person: the fist draws further back through the charge and shakes harder once it's there; the let-go is a real punch across the screen (`fp_p_haymaker_end`).

### 50.4 Shockwave: the ground wave

The wave is the real ground. `WaveSurface` is shared by server and client so that what you see is what hit: columns are stepped at 0.7 blocks along each ray, climbing at most 2, dropping at most 4, riding fluid; anything taller stops it. No ground under the caster (or Minimal effects) falls back to the old arc. The server takes the wave's arrival from one travel speed (range / 0.9 ticks, at least 10). A body is hit only if the wave reaches its near side and it stands within 4 above or 3 below the ground there. At the crest (the far 28% of the reach, 58% on a climb of 5 or more) damage is x1.35 and it throws them up; before it, it bowls them along. `WAVE_KNOCK` for each of the first five bodies. `WallSlam` for 16 ticks at 0.6 of its damage.

`FxGroundWave` lifts real baked block quads, tinted as they are in the world, with plants riding along, water and lava throwing spray, inside the debris budget (`FxBudget.debrisCap`: 160/64/0). The roll sound travels along the front.

### 50.5 Gravity Well

Every body in it past the first adds 8% (40% at most, through `capBonus`, not against players). Bosses aren't pulled. Items and orbs drift in (40 at most, every other tick) only if what's below the centre is solid within 48 blocks and isn't lava, and never for Repulsor. Non-ally shots within the radius bend towards the core at their own speed and are swallowed within max(1.2, radius x 0.22); a boss's shot is leaned on at 30% and never swallowed, since it may be part of the fight. A player's shots are left alone. The client spirals real surface blocks in, drawn only, and throbs the whole of its life.

### 50.6 Railgun

Held up to 600 ticks; nothing fires by itself. Full is `chargeTicks(24)` (12 for Coil). `RAIL_READY` one tick before it. Holding on past full for up to 60 ticks is overcharge: damage up to x1.3 through `capBonus`, a bigger line and more stance. Recoil is 0.3 + 0.35 x charge + 0.25 x overcharge, x1.4 on the ground, its vertical part kept between -0.3 and 0.45, and none on a mount. The view narrows while held (`FxScreen.zoomTo`, off with camera shake), and the let-go throws your arm back (`fp_p_railgun_end`).

At level 5 a full shot bores (`Bore.through`): up to 14 blocks along the line and the four round each one, through `TerrainLedger` with no drops and no particles (`quiet`, saved schema 2). A protected or unliftable whole block stops the shot; soft things that can't be lifted (sand, fences; hardness 0 to 5, no block entity) are passed through and left. It closes 4.5 seconds later from the far end back. It never closes on a player: a tunnel with one inside waits, checked every second, with no limit.

### 50.7 Sounds

`tools/art/specs/audio_power_voice.py`. Each power has a charge or wind, a release, an impact, a tail and a level 5 layer, two versions of each, from CC0 recordings and air (Kenney, `tools/art/sources/ritual`). Nothing pitched or struck above the sub. The family's level-up stinger is off for these four (`PowerSounds.ownPack`), since that's where the dings came from. Loops are mastered wrapped round themselves, so there is no dropout at the join. The sound build fails any new file with a held tone in its loud part (`ding_check.py`: a line above 800 Hz, 14 dB over the third-octave around it, held 45 ms, within 14 dB of the loudest frame). It can't see below 800 Hz. Old files stay until Euan has passed the new ones.

Light bending round the Well (decision 10) is not in Stage 0: nothing in the game can warp the screen around a point in the world yet, so it needs its own pass in the Lens chain.

### 50.8 Scores (docs/powers-next; Euan 9 and 10 Nov 2026: built sounds read fake, "the sounds are a big one")

A power's sound is a score: for each beat of its cast a few layers, and every layer is one of Minecraft's own recordings named the way
`sounds.json` names it (`awaken:voice.<name>` → `minecraft:<file>`), at a volume, a pitch and a start tick. The game plays them from
its own files; nothing of Mojang's is in the mod.
- **Beats** (`powers.fx.Voice.Beat`): GATHER, PEAK, RELEASE, TRAVEL, IMPACT, TAIL, ECHO, HOLD, END, LEVEL5, EXTRA_A, EXTRA_B. The
  server names a beat with `Cast.voice(...)` (an `FxKind.VOICE` event: the beat in `ticks`, intensity in `scale`, and the power's
  classic sound, volume and pitch riding along). GATHER, PEAK and HOLD are never held back to the release frame.
- **Client** (`powers.client.fx.PowerVoice`, `assets/awaken/power_voices.json`, schema 1): picks one of a beat's sets by the cast's
  seed, wanders each layer's pitch a little, plays at most 12 layers (2 beyond 24 blocks), cuts what was gathering on a let-go, adds the
  break sound of the block a hit lands on (`surface`), and ducks the world for a few ticks under a big release. At level 5 the LEVEL5
  set plays under the hit (or the release when the power has no hit).
- **Classic or New**: client setting `newPowerVoice` (and `/awaken fx voice new|classic`). Classic, or a power with no score for a
  beat, plays the classic sound the event carries, exactly as before. An empty set is a beat meant to be silent.
- **Subtitles**: one line a power (`subtitles.awaken.voice.<power>`, "Frost Nova freezes"), shown on GATHER, RELEASE, IMPACT and HOLD.
  It rides an event of its own (`voice.say.<power>`) played too quietly to hear, and only while subtitles are on.
- **Authoring**: `tools/art/specs/power_voices.py build`. It refuses a recording this Minecraft doesn't ship, any tonal source
  (amethyst, note blocks, bells, the level-up, the experience orb), more than 12 layers, a volume above 1 or a pitch outside 0.5 to 2.
  Today: 64 powers, 157 beats, 591 layers over 386 recordings. The ring check stays a tripwire; Euan's ear is the judge.
- Left as plain sounds for now: bolts in flight, Force reactions, zones, the ladder's step hooks, flying blocks, the movement twists.

### 50.9 Arms Duets (`powers.ArmsDuets`; Euan 10 Nov 2026: "it really feels like you're actually doing combos between the weapon and then the power")

One power and one weapon style make something neither does alone. Nothing is timed: a cast opens a few seconds in which the blade's own
moments answer it (`core.api.FightMoments`), or the power answers the weapon in your hand as it lands. The style is read from the held
item's own name, so nothing in Arms changes. Damage goes through `Combat` under the usual caps. They are found by trying; the System
names each the first time with how many you have found ("There are more"), and the Journal keeps it. Counters `awaken:arms_duets/<key>`.

| Duet | Power + weapon | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| Both Barrels | Haymaker + Gauntlets | A second blow from the other fist for 60% |
| Chain Step | Shadow Step + Daggers | A kill or finisher within 2 s brings Shadow Step straight back |
| Icebreaker | Frost Nova + Maul | For 6 s a finisher or perfect heavy on its ground throws a row of ice spikes 7 blocks ahead |
| Reap | Gravity Well + Scythe | A hit on anything inside your Well cuts everything else inside it (once a Well) |
| Still Cut | Flow + Katana | Each hit during Flow hangs a cut on its target, six at most; they all land when Flow ends |
| Mirror Guard | Barrier + Shieldblade | A deflect or guard while Barrier is up throws a blast at what struck you |
| Crossing | Lightning Step + Twin Blades | Everything on the line is cut a second time as you arrive |
| Long Reach | Spirit Palm + War-staff | The palm lands 3 blocks further away |
| Edge of Light | Beam + Greatblade or Longsword | Hold Beam a second; your next finisher or perfect heavy within 3 s throws it as a crescent 11 blocks long |
| Thunder Javelin | Charged Shot + Spear | At half charge or more the bolt goes through three more bodies |
| Batter Up | Terrain Rip + Maul or War-staff | The rock is struck, not thrown: half again as fast, 30% wider |

Not built: Recall (Telekinesis + any weapon), and the 36 Weaves performed by the weapon itself, which need Arms' swing code.

### 50.10 Break finishers

A cast at a body whose stance you broke within the last 2.5 seconds (`ArmsDuets.FINISH_WINDOW` 50 ticks, within 16 blocks) is a
finisher: the power lands half again on it (at least as a 4-damage power would), an `FxKind.FINISHER` event plays the family's own
ending on the body (nine looks in `Signatures.finisher`: Kinetic goes straight through and breaks the ground, Velocity cuts from every
side, Flight lets the ground go, Energy comes out of its back, Shadow's shape finishes it a beat late, Mind closes rings on its head,
Architect pins it from the floor, Tech fires from all round, Spirit's palm goes through), and the caster gets a held beat. Named by the
System the first time for each family; counters `awaken:break_finishers/<family>`. The break gives the seconds: nothing to time.

### 50.11 Earned powers (`powers.catalog.EarnedPowers`, `powers.Earned`; Euan 10 Nov 2026: "surprise me, as long as it still feels like MC"; 9 Nov: "easy unlocks")

Five powers no Power Core rolls (hidden). Each is given the moment you have done enough of something you were doing anyway and hold the
rank it asks, and each fills a hole: Heat and Frost had one power apiece while every weapon attunes to both, nothing answered the forge,
nothing tied Flight to climbing, and nothing used the land you stand on. They level through mastery like any hidden power.

| Power | Family, force | Cost, cooldown, damage | Given for | Rank |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Brand | Spirit, Heat | 18, 8 s, 9 | Forging a weapon on the War Anvil | E |
| Hoarfrost Lances | Spirit, Frost | 24, 18 s, 5 a lance | Ten kills where it is cold enough to snow | D |
| Updraft | Flight | 20, 12 s, 3 | Six seconds off the ground in one go, on your own (no wings, mount, water, ladder, levitation or slow falling) | E |
| Backdraft | Spirit, Heat | 30, 20 s, 6 and up | Setting off fifteen Brands | D |
| Thornwake | Spirit | 26, 16 s, 5 | Ten kills on green ground (grass, moss, podzol, leaves, flowers, crops) | D |

- **Brand**: press your palm to a body within 4.5 blocks (a quarter hit) and leave a mark for 8 s, or aim at a block within 5.5 and
  leave it on the ground as a trap (armed after 15 ticks, goes off under the first enemy within 1.5). Three marks at most. Your next
  melee blow of any kind on the marked body (or on anything within 2.5 of a ground mark) sets it off two ticks later: full damage to
  the body, 60% to everything within 3.5, all set burning. A finisher or perfect heavy sets it off for half again, 30% wider. If the
  body dies of something else first, the mark leaps to the nearest unmarked enemy within 6 with 5 s on it, once. Variants: Slow Burn
  (twice as long, 80%), Flash Brand (40% wider, 85%). Ladder: Deep Brand (+3 s), Wildfire (the burst's share 85%, and burning),
  Second Brand (leaps twice), Forge Mark (the burst sears the ground: 4 s of burning at a quarter a second).
- **Hoarfrost Lances**: three lances hang over your shoulders for 12 s. Each melee blow you land looses one at what you hit (70%
  of the power's damage, Frost, slowed and Frosted for 3 s; at most one every 6 ticks); a finisher or perfect heavy looses all that
  are left (60% each). Pressing the key again throws the rest at what you aim at within 22 blocks, or along your look. The cooldown
  starts when the last one flies or the time runs out. Variants: Long Winter (twice as long, 85%), Heavy Lances (two, 170%). Ladder:
  Long Winter (+3 s), Rime (a lance into something already Frosted bursts for half within 2.5), Fourth Lance, Glacier Crown (two
  more, and when the last flies a ring of frost bursts round you for 80% within 4).
- **Updraft**: a column of rising air where you stand, 2.2 blocks wide and 14 tall, for 6 s. You and your allies inside it are
  carried up by the game's own Levitation (about 9 blocks a second) with no fall damage after; enemies take the power's damage once,
  are thrown up for a second and a half and dropped (bosses and heavy bodies are only hit); projectiles that aren't yours are swept
  upward. Variants: Far Draft (placed where you aim, up to 14 blocks away), Tall Draft (half again as tall, 70% as long). Ladder:
  Thermal (20% taller), Gust (thrown higher, held half a second longer), Wide Draft (25% wider, 2 s longer), Skyward Gate (6 taller,
  and the top throws each rider forward along their look).
- **Backdraft**: after a 7-tick breath in, every fire within 8 blocks is taken: burning bodies stop burning (yours and your friends'
  too), fire blocks go out, your own Brands are swallowed, and up to two campfires or lava blocks feed it without going out. Eight
  fires at most. Three ticks later it all comes back as a cone: 7 blocks and 26 degrees, +0.5 block, +1.5 degrees and +25% damage a
  fire, setting alight. With no fire near it is a small puff. Variant: Deep Breath (draws from half again as far, 90%). Ladder: Deep
  Breath (+20% draw), Cinder (the ground it crossed burns 3 s), Kindle (twelve fires), Dragon's Breath (a jet 60% longer and
  narrower, and fire can't hurt you for 5 s).
- **Thornwake**: wakes the plants within 7 blocks. Each root seizes one enemy (nearest first): the power's damage, and held still for
  2.5 s (bosses only slowed). Two roots, plus one for every two living plants near (flowers, leaves, saplings, crops, tall grass,
  vines, bamboo, cane, cactus) and one for every 24 blocks of turf, six at most; a root comes from the plant nearest its enemy. On
  bare ground: one thin root for half, held 1 s. Variant: Briar Ring (60% of the reach, held 60% longer). Ladder: Deep Roots (+1 s),
  Briar (held enemies are cut every half second), Overgrowth (two more), Elder Grove (one great root under the strongest enemy: hit
  again for 120% and held in the air 2 s).

**Tasks** (`Earned.steps`, thread `powers.earned`): nothing is announced beforehand. Once you have made a start (one cold kill, a few
seconds of air, one Brand set off, one green kill) and hold the rank, a Lead says what kind of thing is waking and where ("Fight in
snow country"), with the count. Brand has no such line: forging your first weapon is already on the main path. Once you own one, a
single plain step says how it is used, until you have used it once (`awaken:brands_set_off`, `awaken:lances_loosed`,
`awaken:updraft_rides`, `awaken:fires_breathed`, `awaken:roots_woken`). Brand and the two it leads to sit on Weapons; Updraft and
Thornwake on Out there.

**Each has** an icon and a Core crystal (a commanded Core still shows right), a ladder (§36), a cast profile with its own
first-person clip (Brand and the Lances are left-handed so the blow can follow at once; Backdraft takes both hands), a score, a screen
moment and a signature: the brand is one rune that keeps its shape on the side of the body you are looking at, and its burst leaves
cooling cracks; the lances hang where the server throws them from (in your own eyes, ahead in the top corners) and one fewer hangs each
time one flies; the column's edge is drawn in thin rising lines with curls of wind, dust and the odd leaf; the breath is big soft flame
down the cone for as long as the lungs last; roots are still jagged lines of bark with a green heart, soil thrown up, leaves falling.
## 53. One short list (the Tasks page through the whole game; plan docs/tasks-progression/PLAN.md, page https://claude.ai/artifact/JqgFfTyCLV13rx6N1XupRd; Euan approved all sixteen recommendations 2026-11-09)

The Tasks page (§27.13) keeps its model: steps stay derived from the world, no quest flags. This section is what it now promises.

**Lessons.** A lesson (a `lesson:` Now id) is never urgent and never the step on top, however fresh it is: `NowMap` holds it under `TaskBook.URGENT` and `TaskBook.top` skips it. A hunter who skipped the Veil no longer has "Meditate 10 s" as Do this next from C-rank on.

**Your Village** (trail) is told through beasts and works, since people no longer move in: `beasts:N` (Kin, how many live at your home) replaces `settlers:N` on it. The tier steps say what `TierRules` asks. "Choose your first armour" is for an E-rank hunter with nothing worn; at any other rank the step is "Make your X-rank armour". The Training Grounds' last step counts a strike on a dummy (`awaken:training_dummy_hits`).

**The cap.** `TaskBook` shelves every book by goal: at most one row per thread and three rows a tab (`TAB_CAP`), one Out there row (`OUT_CAP`); the rest wait in Later, read-only with Pin. So Now is at most seven rows: the step on top, one per tab, one Out there. A source can't exceed it, because the cap is in the book. `tasks.cap=false` in the world config brings back the old list.

**Threads and voices.** A step says `.thread(id, order)` (no thread makes it its own), `.lead()` for what is told by kind and place, `.hidden()` for what's never listed, `.opens(line)` and `.teaches(ids)`. Which of a thread's steps comes up: whatever is on top or pinned, then the lowest order. Priority when places conflict: urgent, the pin, the main path, a place already held, ready, closest to done.

**Places hold.** `TaskState` schema 2 saves which threads hold which places per goal (`held`), what's set aside and when (`aside`) and which tabs have opened (`tabsSeen`); a schema 1 save loads with those empty. A finished row's next step comes up in the same place, marked NEW; a place whose thread has run out goes to the next waiting. Set aside takes a row off the list with Undo, which puts it back exactly where it was; pinning clears it. A row can't be set aside if it's urgent. A trail only fills a place nothing else wants and gives it up when something does, is marked WHEN YOU WANT, and is never on Now. A tab opens the first time it has something of its own to do, and stays.

**The quiet line.** Under a row: "Pick one: A, B or C" for three or fewer picks not made; on the step on top, "Then:" and the main path's next; else "Then:" and the next in its thread. A Lead says nothing of what comes after it, and no line names a Lead coming up. READY shows when every need is met. The foot of a tab says what the next rank or level opens (`Goals.registerFooter`, and the road's next stop on Gates in place of a row).

**Tests.** `tasks_caps` walks the seven stops of `docs/tasks-progression/proof/rows-at-each-stop.txt` (Now at most 7, a tab at most 3, one row per thread, nothing lost, a lesson never on top). `tasks_slots_stay` covers places holding, the next step taking the finished one's place, Set aside and Undo, a pin in Later, trails giving way, an old save.

**The Hearth tab.** Three lines of work. `hearth.home`: the guide, the Anchor, the Forge's tiers and the home's tiers (a tier only shows once your rank opens it; until then the foot of the tab says when, because nothing on the list is out of reach). `hearth.build`: the Armoury, the Forge room, and **Add to your home** (`hearth/add`), one row with up to three picks. `hearth.beasts`: the beasts, each a Lead, a kind your standing rooms are waiting on first (a Storehouse waits on a Totter, an Ore Shed on a Pebblepup, a Smeltery on an Emberkit, a Rookery on a Chimewren).

Picks are `HearthGoals.OPTIONS`, in the order they're offered: a room you've started comes first and the one you picked stays on offer. Each has the rank it's told at, which is not a lock: a room counts whenever it's built. Pick one and the row becomes it, with Change to go back. The Storehouse is told at C-rank, with the Granary Keystone as a Lead (every town's granary keeps one against a ground-floor wall). The Sanctuary is a pick once there's an Anchor. The Now tracker's room suggestion now covers the works too, once two of their pieces are down.

The plan put Forge tiers on `hearth.build`; they're on `hearth.home` so that raising the Forge never hides Add to your home. The foot of the Hearth tab names the first tier the next rank opens, for the Forge and the home; Armour and Weapons name the next rank's set and weapon.
## 56. A Place for Everything (storage)

Plan and reasons: `docs/storage/PLAN.md`, approved in full by Euan 9 Nov 2026 (automatic "keep my bag tidy" is a no). Module
`dev.awaken.storage`. Built in stages; this section says what exists.

**The sorts (Stage 0).** One list, in this order, used by the bays, the signs and the Ledger, and by Tidy: Stone and earth, Wood,
Building and light, Ore and metal, Gems, Food, Plants and seed, Beast and monster drops, Gate loot, Gear, Books and brews, Bells and
leads, Odd things. It replaces §43.12's eleven bays. `Sorts` resolves every item once, the first time it's asked after tags load
(components aren't bound when the tag event fires), so a lookup is one hash read and nothing is saved. A tag
`awaken:sort/<key>` beats every rule, then the rules run: gear, potions, food, ores and metal, gems, plants, wood, creature drops,
dressed blocks (glass, wool, concrete, terracotta) to Building, dug-up stone and earth, any other placeable block to Building, any
other item of ours to Gate loot, and what's left is Odd. Items of ours from a common creature's loot table are listed in
`sort/drops`, boss loot stays in Gate loot by that last rule. No name matching at run time.

Measured on this build: 2,673 items (without spawn eggs), 68 in Odd things (2.5%, was 63%): pottery sherds, smithing templates and
music discs. `storage_sort_golden` holds 300 hand-checked everyday items. `storage_sort_share` fails at 10% and writes every item's
sort to `run/storage-sorts.txt`.

**Bays (Stage 0).** A chest's sort is what most of its stacks are. `Storehouse.bayFor`: the chest already holding that exact item,
else one mostly of its sort with room, else an empty one, else null. `WorkRooms.containers` counts a double chest once (either half
opens the whole of it), counts copper chests, and follows the room's cells when it has them, so a pantry inside an L-shaped hall's
box isn't the hall's.

**Tidy, Undo and Pins (Stage 1).** Server-side, on an exact list of menus: `ChestMenu` over a real chest, barrel, minecart or ender
chest (not someone's button panel on a `SimpleContainer`), `ShulkerBoxMenu`, `DispenserMenu`, `HopperMenu`, and the bag. `Tidy.plan`
is pure: skip the hotbar and pinned slots, merge identical stacks, order by the sort list then family then name then biggest then
least worn, each sort on its own row when that fits, and check every item's total before anything is written. A menu whose state id
disagrees is refused and resynced; four requests a second a player; a slot that won't take its stack stops the whole Tidy. One step
of Undo per player, kept in memory, dropped on close or when anything in the section changes. `BagPins` (attachment `awaken:bag_pins`,
copied on death) is a bit per Inventory slot, and "Empty my bag" at the Drop leaves pinned slots too.

The bag's keys sit right of the recipe book's button, which is where the prototype had put Tidy: Tidy and Pin at y 58, eleven tall, and
Stow under them at y 71 when it comes. On a chest: Tidy in the title row and Tidy and Pin in the row beside "Inventory". `GlassChestScreen`
and `GlassShulkerScreen` subclass vanilla's screens and only change the drawing, so every click, Mouse Tweaks and JEI behave as before;
they replace only the exact vanilla classes, and only while the bag is glass. Keys T and Z work only in those screens, and after any
text box or other mod has had the key. Alt-click (Option on a Mac) pins; the Pin key is a mode where any click does. Flights are
220 ms ease-out, up to 40 ms staggered, over slots already holding their final contents; a click lands them at once. Sounds by name:
`item.bundle.insert` low, `item.bundle.remove_one` for Undo, `item.bundle.insert_fail` when refused, `block.chiseled_bookshelf.insert` for a pin.
Every line under the panel fits inside its width, beside Undo too, so nothing reaches JEI's columns. Client setting `tidy_keys` (`awaken-storage-client.toml`, default on) takes away the buttons, keys and Alt-click together; pins stay saved.


## 52. Made by Hand (the chill side; plan docs/made-by-hand/PLAN.md, page https://claude.ai/artifact/HYetCkcLzxjB21CnH3XT88)

Euan, 9 Nov 2026: "go ahead with all recommendations, but the keybinds need to not interfere with the current power keybinds etc".
Nothing here automates building, adds a chore or a task list. Stages, each with a switch: 0 Proof (built; stops for Euan to play),
1 Mallet, 2 Stock, 3 Hang, 4 Lift and Raise, 5 Boss pieces and Kin, 6 Garden, A Riding Along. Package `dev.awaken.shaping`.

**52.1 The Mallet and its controls.** Two sticks and a cobblestone, stack of 1. Every control is on the mouse and only with the Mallet
in the main hand; no key changes meaning, so powers stay on Z X C V and R with the Mallet out. Right click: what the Mallet is set
to (Knock, or Look: put the look it carries on the block; held, a look drags from block to block, one each; Hang, Lift and Raise
join in their stages). Sneak and scroll: change what right click does. Sneak and right click on a block: the Looks ring. Middle
click (pick block): copy that look onto the Mallet, learn it, and set the Mallet to Look. A press that starts or ends a lock-on is
still the lock's. Sneak and left click: undo. Right click on a block that has its own use still uses it, as with any item.
The Mallet carries `MalletData` (mode, look id).

**52.2 Knock.** One block `awaken:shaped` (no item) with state SHAPE, FACING, WATERLOGGED, GLOW (the base's light, so light never
reads a block entity off the main thread) and a block entity holding `base` and `look` as block states (schema 1). Nine shapes, one
outline each, pushed across the block and turned by the facing: FULL, HALF_BOTTOM, HALF_TOP, SLAB, NOTCH, BEVEL, ROUND, UNDER, COVE.
Mesh, collision (slopes in steps of an eighth), occlusion and preview come from the same outline. Where you hit picks the cut. On a
side: above 0.62 the top (NOTCH, BEVEL, ROUND, whole), below 0.38 under (UNDER, COVE, whole), else the middle (SLAB, whole). On the
top or underside: within 0.25 of an edge is the top or under of that side; the centre is HALF_BOTTOM or HALF_TOP, then whole. A hit
on a surface a cut made carries on with that cut, so knocking the same place steps through the shapes. It has its base's hardness,
tool and blast resistance, drops its base, and sounds like its look. Whole blocks can't be waterlogged; cut ones can.

**52.3 Real blocks wherever they exist.** A real slab or stair reads as its cut, and a cut writes back as the real block if one exists:
NOTCH or UNDER facing f is a stair facing the opposite way (bottom or top), a half is a slab. A whole block wearing its own look
is the real block again. No gain: a slab knocked whole stays a cut block of base slab and drops a slab. Refused, with one plain
line: block entities, unbreakable blocks, ores, anything not a whole solid block, a family slab or a family stair.

**52.4 Looks.** Ordinary building stone, brick, terracotta, concrete and wood (`Looks.families`) are always on offer, free and instant.
Anything else whole and solid is learned by middle-clicking it, or by right-clicking a kept block (kept in a `LookBook` attachment,
through death, schema 1). Never offered: block entities, ores, storage blocks, `#awaken:never_a_look`. Within a family on a whole
real block the look makes the real block; otherwise it's worn and the base stays. The ring opens while Sneak is held, world not paused
or dimmed: its own family first, then learned, then the rest, eight a page, scroll for more. Moving over a look shows it on every
block it would change, only on your screen. Left click: this block. Right click: every touching block of the same look, up to 64,
spreading out a ring a tick, each block rechecked as it's reached. Letting go of Sneak changes nothing.

**52.5 Where.** The Mallet needs `player.mayBuild`, `level.mayInteract` and `Constructs.mayChange`, and outside creative no gate, no civic
block, no `awaken:` dimension and no enforced ward. Refused there, but a right click still learns the look.
Undo: 32 per player, in memory; an undo leaves alone anything changed since, and stops a run in progress.

**52.6 Drawing.** `ShapedModel` wraps the shaped block's model and returns one part per look, shape and facing, built once from
`LookMaterials` (the look's own baked quads: sprite and how the texture lies on each side, so a log's grain survives). Runs on Sodium's
meshing threads. The look is read from the block entity first (never stale), then model data. Before a knock a chalk band shows the part
that will go; the ring's preview is the real mesh a hair proud of the block. `awaken-shaping.toml`: `mallet`, `draw_shapes`.

**52.7 Feel.** No particle sheet: real chips cut from the block's own texture that tumble and land, a little dust in its map colour, a 0.35°
kick of the view for whoever swung. Sound is the block's own hit under `awaken:shaping.knock` (Minecraft's own `mob/zombie/wood` recordings, named).

**52.8 Tests.** `ShapingTests`, prefix `shaping_`: every mesh is a closed solid facing outward, a knock steps through the cuts, a custom block
takes a cut, no gain and no ore, real or worn, a run's kind and cap, kept blocks, undo, every look on offer can be worn. Rendering under
Sodium and how a knock feels can't be tested: Stage 0 stops for Euan to play it.
## 55. Riding Along (Stage A of Made by Hand; page https://claude.ai/artifact/HYetCkcLzxjB21CnH3XT88; approved 2026-11-09)

A partner who isn't good at fighting comes along and is useful, without being able to go down, without making anything
harder and without being carried to rank. Module `dev.awaken.riding`; other modules ask `core.api.RidingHooks`.

**The bond.** One rider, one anchor. It's held in memory; only the run's `riding` mark is saved (`RunState` schema 3).
- Both have to agree. **No key of its own and none taken over:** the K menu's Status page has a RIDING ALONG section
  (`[ Ride ]`, `[ Bring ]` beside anyone within 48 blocks, `[ Let go ]` once tied), and a right click on a gate's door offers
  to go in with the nearest free player within 12 blocks (tied, the door lets go). `/awaken riding status|with|bring|off`.
- The answer is a 30-second Signal card. The server remembers who it asked, so a client can't answer a question it wasn't
