  asked. If both ask for the same thing it forms at once. A door card that runs out chooses nothing.
- Letting go takes both, but silence for 30 seconds counts as yes; an explicit "Not yet" keeps it.
- Refused, in plain words: already tied; not within 48 blocks in the same level; either in a fight (`Powers.inCombat`); in a
  trial; not awakened; in different gates (or one in, one out); the story's own gates; a second rider in one run.
- It ends when both let go, when either leaves the run, goes down or logs off. If it's the anchor and the rider is in a gate,
  the rider is brought out next tick with their Satchel, alive and with no Fracture. A rider who logs off comes back outside
  (`Runs.onLogin`): the thread doesn't survive it. If the rider leaves, the anchor carries on.

**The rider.** Keeps every power and weapon.
- Hits count for 40% (`LivingDamageEvent.Pre`, LOWEST, so after every other bonus; pets and summons with an owner too), and
  stance damage the same (`ArmsServer.addPosture`).
- Doesn't count towards party scaling (`Rooms.partyOnFloor`): no extra monsters, no elite, no Lord health.
- Isn't picked first: every target goes through `LivingChangeTargetEvent`. While anyone who isn't a rider is in the monster's
  sight (its follow range, clamped 16 to 48, and `canAttack`, `GateHooks.mayTarget`), the monster takes them instead. A
  once-a-second sweep turns round any monster already on a rider. Alone, a rider can still be hunted, so riding off by
  yourself is no way to walk through a gate unseen. Bosses take their target the same way and needed no change.

**The catch.** A killing blow on a rider within 48 blocks of a living anchor in the same level is cancelled (HIGHEST
`LivingDeathEvent`, before a gate counts the death or Cheat Death is spent; `/kill` stays real).
- Back to half health at once, so a crash during the fold can't lose anyone. Fire and harmful effects go, casts end.
- For 4 seconds they're folded: their body and name are gone for everyone, nothing can touch them, and they can't hit, use
  anything or cast. They see through the anchor's eyes under a dark veil with a countdown. Nothing is saved.
- They come back beside the anchor (behind first, on sturdy ground in a clear line, else on the anchor with Slow Falling) with
  2 seconds before anything can hurt them. If the bond ended during the fold, they get up where they are.
- They never go down and never lose the Satchel near their partner.

**Out of reach.** The penalties always apply; the protection only within 48 blocks, so stepping away is never an advantage.
A killing blow past the reach is a real death. In a gate, though, a rider still banks the whole Satchel as a claim, keeps
their gear and takes no Fracture (`Runs.onDeath`). A toast says so once on crossing.

**What it pays.** Their own loot rolls and boss pieces (`ArmsApi.lordSpoils`, `lordPattern`, the hoard) stay.
- Half the XP. A floor's pay is halved and capped at what a gate of their own rank would pay (`Runs.riderReward`), which
  covers the kill share, Satchel XP and bonus. HOME, WORLD, DESCENT and ANOMALY XP are halved in `Progression.grant`.
- No rank credit: `Progression.count` ignores the gate and boss counters for a rider, and `claimLord` sets no records, best
  moments or latent flags. Reassessments can't be ridden: a bonded player, either side, is refused at the Monolith and in
  `Trials.start`, and left out of a Proving's party (`Provings.begin`). A Penalty trial is still a Penalty trial.

**Out in the Wilds.** Everything above works anywhere, and a bond is a party of its own (`GateParty`), so kills are shared.

**The look.** One thin thread of ivory light with a rose-gold halo, sagging and swaying between the two, with three beads
travelling from rider to anchor. Past 36 blocks it pulls straight and turns amber; past 48 it frays into red dashes. A catch
streams into the partner's feet and a ring round them burns down the four seconds; coming back is a burst of the same light.
Drawn as world light (`RigPipelines.light()`), no particles. Sounds are Minecraft's own by name (`riding.bond`, `riding.let_go`,
`riding.fold`, `riding.spring`: beacon power and deactivate, respawn anchor deplete and set spawn), low and without a ding.

**Tasks.** `riding/together`, optional, on Gates and rank, shown only with someone within 48 blocks, until you've done it once.

**Tests.** `bond_` prefix, one per mechanism: `bond_needs_both`, `bond_door`, `bond_not_mid_fight`, `bond_one_rider_per_run`,
`bond_hits_forty`, `bond_fold_catches`, `bond_anchor_dies`, `bond_no_scaling`, `bond_no_aggro`, `bond_no_rank`, `bond_range`,
`bond_left_on_logout`, `bond_goals_step`.
## 49. The Forged Pick (plan docs/forged-pick/PLAN.md, page https://claude.ai/artifact/Smj9nEuNHbq6MZ4y2X1CaB; Euan approved all of it 2026-11-09)

Picks are forged at the War Anvil, as weapons are. Four forms, six ranks, 24 items named `<prefix>_pick_<form>`; package
`dev.awaken.delve.forged`, and `delve.api.Pick` answers for old and forged picks alike.

### 49.1 The first pick
The stone at the end of an adit gives the Delver's Old Head, once a player, ever (`WakingPick.PULLED`; anyone who already pulled the
finished pick has what it would make). Where no adit is near, the Hearth hands it over. The head, a log and string hang the E Delver at
the War Anvil. Nothing makes the old `waking_pick` now, but saves that hold one keep it: it mines as before and its verses wake as before
until its owner brings it to an anvil (§49.7). A lost head never strands anyone: the E Delver can also be forged from the rank's parts.

### 49.2 Forms
| Form | Rock speed | Earth, wood | Uses | Damage | Way | Opens |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Delver | 100% | none | 100% | +0 | hums toward a lode within 16 | at the start |
| Breaker | 85% | none | 130% | +0 | heavy strike glints at 14 ticks, one less extra wear | break a lode's heart (`deed_heart`) |
| Mattock | 90% | 120% | 110% | +0 | pick, axe and shovel rules; strips and flattens, sneak to till; turns in the hand (§49.8) | at the start |
| Sounder | 90% | none | 80% | -1 | seam 0.40 wide, bonus ore 40%, hums within 24, taps 50% further | light a Delver's lamp (`deed_lamp`) |

Form and rank are the item; `PickForged` (component `awaken:pick_forged`, schema 1) holds what the smith did and what the pick has been
through: quality, temper, colour, smith, maker, day, tally (blocks, ores, hearts, keen), gifts, the rank it was first forged at, story bits, and
enchantment room.

### 49.3 Numbers (`PickStats`)
Rank speed 5, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12.5. Uses 300, 650, 1800, 2200, 2700, 3400. Damage 2, 3, 4, 4.5, 5, 6. Each item's Tool rules are fixed by rank and
form, so `/give` and creative stacks are whole; quality, colour, keen and blunt go through a `BreakSpeed` factor that runs on both sides, and only
MAX_DAMAGE is per stack (a Tool rule per stack was the first plan, and a data change every Dressing would have restarted block breaking on the
client). Temper, the steps of quality the Forge could hold, adds 0/4/8/12% to speed and uses. Colour c runs 0 (straw, +8% speed, -20% uses) to
0.75 (blue, -6%, +30%), peacock 0.5 even. A pick never breaks: at its last use it goes blunt (30% speed, and no heavy strike, whose wear it could no longer pay) until dressed. Forged picks are kept through
death, and A and S are fire resistant. Efficiency is out, since rank and forging are its speed. A forged pick has no repair material: Dressing is the
way (one metal, mends a quarter, keen for 200 blocks at +10%). Its enchantment room is quality + 1, or the old pick's room if larger.

### 49.4 At the anvil (`arms.anvil.PickAnvil`)
A pick is an `AnvilWork` with `pick` set (schema 6) and style `pick_<form>`; the server judges it as it judges a sword, and it uses no pattern, no grindstone and no quench.
Stages by rank, first time at that rank: **E** knap, bind, hang. **D** heat, cut the eye, draw the points, run the colours, hang. **C** adds steel the tips. **B** adds thread the spine.
**A** adds pour the seam, on a Lord's anvil. **S** adds the starlight, after the colours. A raise above D does the heat, the drawing, and only the new rank's own act, then colours and hang. From memory (after a Masterwork at that rank and form) it's the heat, the drawing and the colours, Fine at best. Knap and bind are the hand ranks' work, the Forge is never asked at E, and metal always is.
Songs: Delver `x.x.x...` a miner's steady three, Breaker `x.....x.x.......` a long lift and a double, Mattock `x..x..x.....` a triple swung, Sounder `x.x.x...x.x.x...` light and even. Marks are on the arms, never on the eye. Run the Colours is a hold: oxide creeps from the eye toward the points at 0.05 a tick and the lift sets the colour; held past blue it goes grey and is still sound, so the colour can't fail. Quality, the 0.6 timing + 0.4 aim of §39, adds the acts as the weapon's score does; burnt caps at Masterwork.
**Options on a pick you hold:** Raise (next rank's parts less one metal); Re-draw to another form (half cost, full scene at its rank); Work in (a deed done since: free, three taps); Dress (one metal, a quarter of its wear off, keen for 200 blocks). Raise and Re-draw keep the tally, gifts, enchantments, curses, name, lore and repair cost, take the better quality and temper, and the new colour unless none was run. Wear clears on a raise or re-draw. Dressing and working in stay in the hand: back in the hand, else the pack, else at your feet, no draw from the stone.
**Backing out:** the Heat, or a first Knap or Tend blow not yet struck: everything comes back, the pick first so the parts can't take its hand. After the first blow the work waits like any other.
**Make it again:** your best rank (`ForgedPicks.BEST_TIER`) at half cost, offered only when you carry no forged pick.
With the Hall of Arms the default, a pick's offers still open the cards window (`AnvilPayloads.Held.rites()` is false for them, and the Hall's anvil stage is only a weapon's three rites), and a pickaxe in hand at the anvil's door opens the Armoury with its Picks side, which the Hall doesn't have yet.
The rebuild gates stay: C on an Ironbound anvil, A on a Lord's anvil. Picks never touch the Weapons tab's best or forged lists: `SmithMemory` only remembers them for the from-memory road.

### 49.5 Gifts and Sounding
`Pick.Gift` in the order the old pick woke them: Hum, Kindle, Sounding, Wide Seam, Long Sounding, Hush, Call. Forged picks hold them as bits, and the
player's deed opens the gift: heart Kindle (D+), lamp Sounding (C+), Deepglass Long Sounding (B+), seep Hush (A+). Wide Seam comes with C and Call with
S. Forged picks take deeds done before they existed; a gift earned later is worked in free at any anvil in 5 s.
Sounding replaces Echo and Glass for old picks too (nothing is drawn through the rock any more): stand still, sneak and tap. 26 rays walk out to 12 (24
with Long Sounding, x1.5 on a Sounder) and report the first roomy hollow; the client plays the answers from those sides, nearest first, shakes dust off
that part of the wall, and a lode within reach answers last at its ore's note. 20 s rest.

### 49.6 The tally and the name
A pick counts blocks and ores, and hearts of a lode, flushed every 20 breaks, on logging out, on dying and on changing slot, so a crash loses at most 19. Lines read on the item: who made it, on what day, in what colour, how much it has dug, and which rank it began at. Three bits are story: `TWIN` struck with a friend, `MEMORY` made from memory, `ARMOURY` the Master of the Armoury's bonus; `OLD` was remade from the old pick.

### 49.7 Old picks and old mattocks
An update never changes a pick by itself. Holding the old `waking_pick` at any anvil, built or not, with no Forge, offers one free row: five taps and it's a Delver at the verse's rank (verse 0 E, 1-2 D, 3-4 C, 5 B, 6 A), holding every gift it had, its enchantments and its room, at the same share of its wear, marked `OLD`, with no maker claimed. It comes straight back to the hand. Old `<prefix>_mattock` items convert the same way, free, to the Mattock of their rank. Both old items stay registered for good; nothing makes new ones (recipes retired, §49.9).

### 49.8 In the hand
The picks draw as meshes (`arms.client.PickRenderer`, `awaken:pick` special model, `AWMS` with a group byte per triangle): the handle takes the rank's rings only for ranks the pick has passed; the head shows its Temper colour at its working end (the oxide it was stopped at), its wear, and a notch per ten lode hearts, up to six. Any pick is one haft and one head, so it reads from across a cave by its shape.

**The dig** (`delve.client.DigMotion`, `PickHands`): a two-handed overhead blow timed to the bite clock. The off hand grips the haft while it's empty and stays where it is when not. It pulls back further for a big bite and less for a quick one, and it stops at the wall rather than passing through it. Third person uses an arm-pose transformer (`AWAKEN_PICK_DIG`), so other players see it too.

**The Mattock turns in the hand** (`arms.client.PickTurn`), Euan 2026-11-09: look from rock to earth or wood and the holder tosses it a little way up the haft, spins it a half turn about the haft and catches it with the adze leading; look back at rock and it goes round again. 7 ticks a turn (3 with reduced motion), after a steady look of 2 ticks, at most one turn every 2 ticks. Purely what's seen and heard: the server isn't told, the dig is never slowed, and the block breaks at the same pace whichever end leads. It's worked out for anyone holding one within 32 blocks, from where they're looking, one ray a tick. A freshly drawn Mattock takes its side at once with no flourish. Which end leads is the item's own (`plus_leads` in the JSON per display context), since the two hands and third person mirror differently.

### 49.9 Round the game
- **Retired**: the six `<prefix>_mattock` recipes and the level road's grants of them; the Now suggestion for a mattock; the through-the-rock pipeline. The items stay, named "Old Wildhide Mattock" and so on, with a tooltip line that any War Anvil remakes them free. The ledger declares them, and the old `waking_pick`, as no longer made.
- **Tasks** (`arms.anvil.PickGoals`, on the Weapons tab): find the old head; forge your first pick; and, off the main path and only while it applies, bring an old pick, raise yours to your rank, work in a deed, dress a blunt edge.
- **Trail** `the_delvers_pick`: pull the head, forge it, then the four deeds, a Sounding and a raise. Steps read counters (`awaken:delve/deed_*`, `awaken:pick_forged`, `awaken:pick_remade`, `awaken:delve/soundings`), so a deed done before the trail opened is ticked at once.
- **Armoury**: at an anvil's door there's a Weapons and a Picks side. Holding a forged pick opens on Picks, on the next rank up from the best you carry (within your level). A pick has no pattern to buy or Track, and no blade to make alone. The anvil's window for a pick in hand scrolls when its offers don't fit.
- **Kept through death**: on the player (`awaken:kept_picks`, schema 1, copied on death) so a restart while they're on the death screen loses nothing. Only ever the old pick, a forged pick, or the head.

### 49.10 What you hear
Every forged-pick sound is one of Minecraft's own recordings, named in `merge/delve_picks` (`"minecraft:item/hoe/till1"`), so the game plays them from its own files and none of Mojang's audio is in the mod. The first set, built from CC0 impacts and matched to vanilla's loudness and brightness, sounded synthetic to Euan (9 Nov): numbers can't tell you a sound belongs. Each entry's `volume` levels it against the block's own hit, and its `pitch` sets it apart; a form never gets a sound vanilla doesn't have.

- Each form bites with its own recording under the block's sound (`pick.strike_<form>`, played at 0.6, 0.9 on the last blow, varied 10% so thousands of blows don't tire the ear). An ore already has its own strike (`DelveContent.STRIKE`) and a true strike its note, so the bite isn't pitched to the ore.
- A Mattock in soil is a hoe going into dirt (`pick.strike_earth`), in timber an axe on a log (`pick.strike_wood`); a blunt pick knocks dully (`pick.strike_blunt`).
- The turn: `pick.mattock_toss`, `pick.mattock_catch`. Sounding: `pick.sounding_tap` (server, heard by anyone near) and `pick.sounding_hollow` (client, from the hollow's side).
- At the anvil: `anvil.eye`, `anvil.tip`, `anvil.hang`, `anvil.tend`, `anvil.thread`, `anvil.pour`, `anvil.colours`. A held press's sound (`pour`, `colours`) loops and stops when you let go or leave.
## 50. Gates as Worlds (plan docs/gates-as-worlds/PLAN.md, page https://claude.ai/artifact/3hQVhu5jQKPEWDMbMenkaB)

Approved by Euan on 9 Nov 2026, all 18 decisions, with two additions: a loading screen between the overworld and a gate
that looks really cool (§50.5), and nothing may ever float (§50.6). The plan is the design; this section records what's built.

Order of work, each stop waiting for him beside the gate's painting: 0 repeats and pay on today's gates. 1 foundation behind
the `gateRealms` switch and the Build Kit. 2 Amber Reach, **stop**. 3 boss spaces, the first six also into today's gates, **stop**.
4 a jungle Stronghold and the Hour Crypt, **stop**. 5 a Deep and a Sky, **stop**. 6 E pool to 14, switch on for new worlds.
7 D to S waves to 88, every Lord placed. 8 old worlds into Dungeons and acts, Far Sight, 128 over time.

### 50.2 The bag (no repeats)

The old rule wrote a theme into memory on every roll, so gates you never walked into pushed real ones out and his first two
gates were both Hives. Now `GateMemory.seenThemes` holds the themes you've **gone into** (`Runs.enter`), newest first.
`Director.bag`: a new gate's theme fits its rank, isn't in the bag's seen list, and isn't standing for you (derived from the
registry each roll, so a closed gate goes back by itself). When only friendly themes are left the bag refills with everything
that fits the rank, except the last two places you went. If every theme left is standing somewhere, a twin beats no gate.
Worlds get the same treatment: in `GateWorlds.pickWorld` an everyday world (common or uncommon) only comes up while none has
been met less, and a world standing in another of your gates counts as met; rare and mythic ones keep their odds. Test
`gates_bag_no_repeat`: 10,500 rolls.

### 50.3 Gate pay

`Curve.gatePay`: E 2, D 3, C 4, B 2, A, S and Sovereign 1.25, on top of the old reward (`Curve.worldReward`, which the open world's
camps, stars and rifts still use, so the open world didn't change). `KILL_SHARE` 0.6: 60% lands as you fight, 40% rides in the
Satchel. A gate above your rank pays half as much again per rank above. A Lord's first clear, once per theme and rank, adds half
of the whole gate's floors (`GateMemory.firstClears`; not story gates or Ascension trials). Mastery need falls to
4,500 / 8,500 / 15,500 / 24,000 to keep a main power's level 3 near player level 20 and level 5 near 45.

Simulated, the balanced player (`tools/sim/pacing_sim.py`, 300 runs): level 5 at 0.85 h, 10 at 2.25, 25 at 8.75, 50 at 25.8, 135 at
60.9 (was 0.89, 3.75, 16.8, 57.1, 104.6). Ranks: D 3.3 h, C 10.1, B 23.6, A 35.8, S 47.6, Sovereign 61.8. Main power level 3 at player
21.5, level 5 at 48. Deaths per 10 gates D 1.42, C 1.87, B 2.16, all in target. The deep's metal for C now arrives a little after its
level: median wait 0.7 h, p90 4.2 h (was 0 and 2.0).

### 50.4 The Lord's payout

When a Lord falls, the Satchel's XP and any first clear land there and then, not on the way out (the loot still goes home with
you as a claim). `run/LordPay`: 30 ticks after the kill, then a level every 14 ticks (8 when many are still to come); each beat
grants exactly enough XP for the next level (`Progression.grantXpQuietly`, so each level's own toast and sound stay out of the
way) and strikes a bell, vanilla's `block.bell.use` walked over a low pentatonic scale (0.63 to 1.26, never higher). The last
beat adds `block.bell.resonate`, then the usual level moment and pane once the fight is over. On screen (`client/LordLevels`): one
number in the middle of your view, climbing with every bell, the old number rising away and the new one landing a little too
big, a rule flaring from it, points so far beneath, a mark per level. `GateMemory.lordXp` holds what hasn't landed, saved with the
player; logging out pays the rest at once, and after a crash it plays on the next login. Test `gates_lord_pay_beats`.

### 50.5 The crossing (the loading screen between the overworld and a gate)

Euan asked for it to look really cool. NeoForge's `RegisterDimensionTransitionScreenEvent` gives the gate dimensions their own
`LevelLoadingScreen` (`gates/client/Crossing`). Just before the move the server sends `GatePayloads.Crossing`: which painting (today
the theme, later each gate's own), the small line (`E-rank Hive`), the name (the first floor's world, else the theme) and the world's
one plain line. The screen is full-screen on a shader (`core/gate_crossing.fsh`, optional pipeline; if it won't compile the painting
just fades): a ragged tear opens down the dark, its edge bending the painting and parting its colours, light rushing out of it; the
painting drifts in very slowly with dust hanging in front and black bars top and bottom; the name surfaces letter by letter from its
middle, a rule draws out under it, then the plain line; the land's progress is one hair of light in the bottom bar. Held at least
2.8 s going in and 1.5 s coming out so it can be read, and it closes when the land has loaded. The painting stays up as a layer a
moment longer and burns away from the centre, 1.15 s, into the real place, the bars sliding off with it.

Paintings: `textures/gui/crossing/<key>.png`, 1536×864, made by `tools/art/crossing_paintings.py`; `default` for anything without its
own. A death, a command or a teleport with no word from the server gets a plain dark screen. Moving between a gate's own floors
across its two dimensions shows nothing over the Journey (§38.7). Tour: `tools/autopilot/gate-crossing.txt`; `/awaken gate crossing
<theme> <ms>` freezes one instant.

### 50.6 Nothing may ever float

Euan caught fence posts standing in the air beside a road in the proof, and asked that it never happen. Three rules, all checked:

1. **Everything is anchored to the ground that is really there.** `Land.ground(x,z)` returns the exact top block, every per-column
   rule included, and it is the one source of the height (`AmberReach.column`). Pieces read it, and `V.foot(x,y,z,state)` fills from
   the piece straight down to whatever holds it up. No piece may use a guessed height.
2. **`check/FloatCheck` walks the real result.** It draws a Realm exactly as the game does and walks out from the ground through
   everything solid (faces and edges count as touching, a lone corner doesn't). Whatever the walk can't reach is in the air, from one
   post to a whole roof. A plant must stand on something, a hanging thing must hang from something, a vine must be on something, and
   a plant can't hold up a post. Only a piece that says `airborne` is let off. `realm_float_check_catches` proves the check fails on a
   planted post, plant and lantern. `realm_amber_never_floats` runs it from the Mouth to the citadel's stair.
3. **Pieces are placed through one door** (`check/LookChecks.clash`): none through another piece, none on a road, a stair or a door's
   way, except a piece marked `mayOverlap` (a spire on its plinth) or `startsWay` (the ring a road starts from). The first full run
   found what no eye had: the pavilion's roof sat four blocks above its columns, every hut's finial stood over a hole in its dome, and
   a lamp cut the pavilion's middle post in two.
4. **Half a block of air is air** (11 Nov; Euan, in the Cinder Workings: "There are some floating things here... we need to make
   sure that never happens in any gates"). A slab laid low carries people and other bodies, but its top is lower than its cell's,
   so a plant, a crystal, a candle or a drift set in the cell above stands half a block up (`Kinds.low`). A stair is not counted:
   half its top is whole, and Amber Reach's candles down a flight of steps stand on it. The float check reports it as a floater, `Settle` takes it out and counts it, and the rolled dungeons' small
   things (`GeneratedCrawl.detail`) are set only where the floor is a whole block: until now they were set over the half steps the
   depth pass had laid, which is what he saw. A cache a pack leaves makes the slab under it whole (`RealmRun.spoils`). The first
   run of the stricter check over every land found 96 more in three hand-built lands that are never settled (Kingsroot Keep 79,
   the Vine Seat 13, Saltcomb Flats 4: grass, ferns, drifts and a dead bush on pale slabs); each now takes them out as it draws
   (`Settle.overSlabs`).

### 50.7 Realms (the foundation)

A Realm is a whole land generated in dimension `awaken:realms` (384 tall, sky). `data/awaken/realms/<id>.json` is the blueprint
(`Blueprint`: form, theme, ranks, the program that draws the land, sky, life, folk, law, sites, heart, moods, one plain line for the
crossing); `LandPrograms` maps a program to its `Land` class, so each great land is its own code with its own painting. Behind
`AwakenConfig.gateRealms` (off) until the E wave is ready; `/awaken gate realm <rank> <id>` forms one anyway, `/awaken gate realm_at
<kind> <index> <dx> <dy> <dz>` moves you to one of its sites.

**Which Realms a gate in the world can be** (Euan, 11 Nov: he walked into a hive gate in the world, expected a new dungeon and
got the old kind, because the switch was off; asked whether gates in the world should lead to the finished new ones, "Yes,
set it up"). A blueprint says `"ready": true` when it is finished. With `gateRealms` on, a new gate whose theme and rank
have a ready Realm is that Realm (`Blueprints.open` and `pick`: one its finder has not seen first); every other gate is
floors as before. A blueprint that does not say it is ready is never rolled, only entered by command, so a land still being
built cannot turn up in play. Ready on 11 Nov: Amber Reach, The Hour Crypt, The Broodwarren and the seventeen rolled kinds
(§50.9). Not yet: Kingsroot Keep, The Vine Seat, The Quiet Barrow, Saltcomb Flats, The Wax Galleries (their owners set the
line when they are done) and the blockouts. (Later the same day those five were marked ready at Euan's word, and after
them the five rolled lands of §50.9 "Rolled lands": the Cinder Crown, Fallwater Vale and the High Caps from E, the Glass Sea
from D, the Hush Tarn from C. Each had walked clean in the real game, their tests were green under the stricter float rule,
and the Cinder Crown had been seen under its own red sky, run 43013074163. He had seen the first of them and said "this
looks really good. Let's keep going in this direction", then "Yes, merge them".) The switch's default stays off in code until a full suite has run with it on
(the old gates' tests make gates and expect floors); a world turns it on in `config/awaken-synced.toml`. Gates already
standing keep what they are.

**Open lands switched off** (Euan, 12 Nov, after Saltcomb Flats at E, the hive gate 4 of his world: "I was just very
confused about what I was supposed to do. Like nothing guided me, nothing showed me... I went to that big building, but the
big building was closed. So how do I open the doors? ... it just like dumps you in a place with barely any mobs", and "The
dungeon type gates are actually like much better, I think, with like the movement, the jumping, and everything... So maybe
for now we deactivate all of the massive open world ones, for the time being ... and we only have the [rolled] dungeon
ones"). `AwakenConfig.gateOpenLands` (synced, default off; an existing `awaken-synced.toml` gains the key as false): with it
off a new gate never rolls a Realm whose land is under the open sky (`Blueprints.open(theme, rank, false)` and `pick`).
`Blueprints.openLand` asks `LandPrograms.open(program)` and draws nothing: every program but those in `LandPrograms.ROOFED`
(the crawls, the Hour Crypt, the Wax Galleries) is open, so a new program counts as open until it is listed there, and
`realm_open_lands_off` draws each roofed one that rolls to check its land really is under a roof (`RealmCountry.has`).
Off with it today: Amber Reach, Saltcomb Flats, Kingsroot Keep, The Vine Seat, The Quiet Barrow and the five rolled lands
(the Cinder Crown, Fallwater Vale, the High Caps, the Glass Sea, the Hush Tarn), and Gate Worlds' open worlds (§38.11).
Every theme that had an open Realm keeps two or more under a roof at each of its ranks: Bell Crypt four, Hive four, Frost
three, Fungal, Ember, Overgrown Temple and Glass Desert two each. At the next start a gate standing on an open land that
nobody has entered (`GateService.unentered`: READY or BUILDING, no party, no entries, not the story's) is made again
(`remakeOffOpenLand`, a line in its trace): a Realm's land goes to the eraser and the gate rolls again in a fresh Realm
cell; a gate of floors with an open world is dressed again in a fresh cell, as a content rebuild is (no free cell: it stays
as it is). A gate someone has been in keeps what it is. `/awaken gate realm` still forms any Realm, and switching it on
brings them back for new gates. The fix is planned on its own before anything is built.
The theme bag follows the switch (`Director.inBag`): with it off, a theme stays out of the bag at a rank where it has
nothing under a roof, neither a Realm (`Blueprints.open(theme, rank, false)`, while `gateRealms` is on) nor an ordinary
floor world (`GateWorlds.roofedWorld`: enabled, not open, everyday, deep or wonder, its rank reached, not in
`gateWorldsOff`; mastery is left out because it depends on the player), since its gates would otherwise be the oldest plain
rooms and Euan asked for the dungeon runs only. It follows the data, so today that leaves out the Lantern Night Market (D
to Sovereign: every world of it is open but its secret vault, which is never picked) and the Sky Archipelago (B to
Sovereign: all open); every other theme keeps its ranks. The second gate's theme (a twist's annex) is chosen from the same
bag. A rank where this would leave no theme at all keeps every theme that fits, with one warning in the log. The roll's
trace says what was left out ("open lands off so not ..."). `realm_open_lands_off` checks the bag on the real data with the
switch on and off, that 120 rolls a rank never give either theme, and that an empty bag falls back.

Cells sit `RealmCells.PITCH` (8,192) apart from 135,168, past the old gate grid, so `Cells.cellAt` and `Where.at` find nothing in a Realm.
A Realm gate keeps its normal cell, `GatePlan` and `GateLayout` (only the abstract numbers are used: rewards, the Lord's id) and adds
`GateRecord.realm` (`RealmRef`: blueprint, seed, version, cell). `RealmPlan.of` is a pure function of those, so a restart rebuilds the
plan and nothing about the land is saved except what happened in it (`RealmData`, `RealmState`, schema 1). All drawing is in local
coordinates, 0,0 the Realm's middle; `V` is a scratch volume per chunk with a one-block margin.

Runs hands a Realm gate to `RealmLive` before the floors' code sees it: no pressure clock, no rooms, no twists yet (a gate with a twist
stays floors until its Realm form is built). Your way home is the arch by the Mouth, any time, Satchel banked; bag per owner
(`GateMemory.seenRealms`). Monsters wake within 56 blocks of their den or Warden. Wardens fall in any order and the last opens the way
to the Lord, never announced (decision 12).

Pay (§50.3): a Realm's pool is what the same gate's floors would pay. 60% is split kill by kill (a den about five shares, a Warden
four); of the other 40% each Warden banks a sixth and the Lord pays what's left, plus first clear and the Lord's payout as usual.

**Waystones** replace Rest Shrines in a Realm (decision 13). Laying a hand on one marks it found, banks your Satchel and XP there and then, and
offers the next one you've reached, so you can walk the valley and come back. `RealmLive.useWaystone`, `RealmLive.travel`, `Interactions.WAYSTONE`.

**The valley's edge** is a wind, not a wall: `Land.edge(x,z)` past 0 pushes you back toward the middle, harder the further you go.

**Amber Reach's life and air.** `RealmLife` runs for each player every two seconds: a herd of three to five Pollen Grazers turns up 36 to 58 blocks off whenever fewer
than five are within 64, Amberflies over the open ground, and up to nine Wax-folk near their village within 130 blocks, each kept to its own door. Laying a hand on a
Wax-folk lets them speak and sell honey (`RealmLife.talk`), and from then on the plate over their heads says what they are. Their spawn eggs exist only for testing.
Outdoors the land plays `realm.amber.air`, indoors `realm.amber.hall`, both built from vanilla recordings; Lens uses its own amber look for the valley and the hall.

**Finds** are single caches set where you have to look: 24 around the valley and one on top of each great rock, each rock with a column of rising air
beside it (`UpdraftBlock`, `SiteKind.UPDRAFT`; crouch to sink). The Law of Amber Reach is `updrafts`: one physical rule, per decision 14.

**The honey river** is its own block, `realm_honey`: light 9, 7/16 high to walk in, slows you to 62% (`HoneyFlowBlock`), animated. It replaces water
in this land, so no block of it can ever flow.

**The heart of a Realm** (`Land.inHeart`, `Land.change(moment)`, `RealmState.doorShut, heartStage`): the Lord sleeps until someone comes in. The door
is wax as thick as a wall until the last Warden falls (`heart_open`); it shuts behind whoever's fighting once nobody's lingering at it (`heart_shut`);
the room answers the fight at two thirds and one third of the Lord's life (`heart_weeps`, `heart_winds`), and stills when it dies (`heart_still`).
Nobody left in the fight (`RealmState.fighters`, §68.6 "The fight holds"): the Lord goes, the hall resets, the door opens again, and
everyone in the gate is told so. Moments are block edits sent with `Block.UPDATE_CLIENTS`, computed by the land so a restart redraws the same thing.

**Life** (`RealmLife`, spawned from a blueprint's `life` and `folk`): kept up by density around each player, once every two seconds, always at least
28 blocks from anyone. A herd of 3-5 where fewer than 5 are within 64; 6 flies within 40; up to 9 folk round a village once a player is within 130. All
ambient and `placed`, so no biome ever rolls them. The folk (`wax_folk`) say one plain line about their lives when you put a hand on them, offer honey
while they have some to spare (three bottles for two emeralds, six sales per Realm), and can be overheard (a toast, at most one every 40 s). They never
fight beside you, set tasks or give directions. Grazers use the rig's `graze` clip through `WildPose.S_GRAZE`.

**Growing things stand clear** of Waystones, Finds, vents and the arch (`clearings`), and tall wheat grows only in the heart of a patch: you can always
see over the crop.

### 50.8 The Build Kit

Seven passes on every land, in order: bones (ground and big masses), courses (no face one flat plane), pieces (each anchored, placed
through the door), shade (painted darkness only under a real two-deep ledge), weathering (drips, crumbs), growth (only on ground that's
really there), light. `N` holds the noise and hex helpers; `Piece` knows its footprint and draws into whichever chunk it touches. Tests:
`realm_cells`, `realm_blueprints_parse`, `realm_bag_empty`, `realm_float_check_catches`, `realm_amber_never_floats`,
`realm_amber_plan_checks`, `realm_amber_all_reachable`, `realm_amber_sites_open`, `realm_amber_heart`, `realm_seeds_differ`, `realm_mouth_safe`,
`realm_no_holes`, `realm_amber_sight` (median view 30+, 90th percentile 150+, 30% of views past 64), `realm_flag_off_rolls_floors`, `realm_party_split`,
`realm_life_creatures`.

The preview: `tools/preview/preview.sh <tour> [seeds]` draws a land's real blocks from its tour's own cameras (the same `realm_at` and
`look` lines) with no game client, in about a minute, against 15-20 for a walk. `Preview` runs as the GameTest `realm_preview`, which does
nothing unless the script set its environment. Pictures, `sheet.png` and `report.txt` (cameras blocked, all sky, one block over 60% of a
view, vanilla over 30%) land in `run-preview/<tour>/`. It paints the ground truth (every block the land draws) but shades it plainly:
sun, soft corners and haze, no creatures, no Lens. It judges shapes, framing, tone and broken builds; the real look still needs a walk.
`volume.sha` holds a hash of every block for each seed asked for: a change to the kit that shouldn't change a land must not move it.

The kit is working parts, not a look. In `realms/kit`: `KitLand<M>` (the piece list, `place` with the clash rule, `waystone`, `clearSites`/`tended`,
`jit`), `Mats` (materials by job, named `<land>_stone`, `<land>_stone_worn`... with a land's own growth and glow passed in as `Accents`; a land extends
it for what only it has), `River`, `Road`, `Build` (`stair`, `under`, `top`, `lit`), and in `kit/piece`: `Waystone`, `Find`, `Updraft`, `Lamp`, `Boulder`,
`Tree`, `Stall`, `Pylon`, `Hut`, `Pavilion`, `MouthRing`. `Waystone`, `Find`, `Updraft`, `Lamp` and `Boulder` can be used as they are. A land's houses, arrival
and great build are its own shape: the rest take shape parameters as soon as a land needs them, added then and not before, and proved with `volume.sha`
that the lands already built didn't move. Amber's own (`Flower`, `Plinth`, `Spire`, `Heart`, the hex-column cliffs) stay in `AmberReach`: used twice they
would make two gates the same place.

A new land, in order: the painting approved; materials (a copy of `tools/art/specs/realm_amber.py` with its own palette and textures, `Def` lines in
`ThemeBlocks` with the same suffixes, the tag `blocks_motion_no_leaves`); `data/awaken/realms/<id>.json` and its biomes (their `sky_color`, `fog_color`
and `grass_color` are also what the preview shades with); a `KitLand` subclass (land shape, one great build, `build()` placing the rest) entered in
`LandPrograms`; a tour copied from `realm-amber.txt`; then preview, fix, preview, and only then a walk.


**The Hour Crypt (gate 2 of 88, E and D, Dungeon, Bell Crypt).** One great drum with a bell the size of a house hung over a sunk floor; the
stair head and nave run north, an Ossuary east, a flooded Sunk Aisle west, a bell tower south, the Candle Keepers' cloister off the nave.
Every wall is one function (`niche`) for straight and round faces. The law is `tolls` (`RealmToll`): every 1,200 ticks the great bell rings
and all six iron doors drop for 180 ticks; a door cell with something alive in it stays open. Land hooks added for it: `indoors()`,
`portalAxis()`, `heartClosedLine()`. The Lord's floor is lit by low hidden light (a 7-block grid of level 13 at floor+4) because candles round
the rim alone leave the middle black, and a fight has to be read.

**One family per theme, not per gate.** Bell Crypt's lands all build in Knell (`tools/art/specs/realm_knell.py`, 22 blocks and 16 cuts), Hive's
in Amber, so 88 lands don't mean 2,700 blocks. Under a blue moon a green patina has to be painted yellow-green or it reads as cyan.

**More checks.** `WalkCheck.unreachable(land)`: breadth-first from the Mouth with `heart_open` applied (step up 1, drop up to 4, 2 cells of
headroom), every site within 4 blocks of a walked cell. `FloatCheck` now knows things meant to float on water (`crypt_lily_candle`,
`market_boat_lamp`: fail with no water under them), and a small stray's failure names the block and what it stands on. Tests:
`realm_hour_walks_to_everything`, `realm_hour_nothing_floats`, `realm_hour_doors_toll`. The preview lights an `indoors()` land by flood fill on
the volume (warm candle, cool moon) and draws candles as their real sticks. Where two halls cross, neither draws its wall across the other.

**The bar (10 Nov 2026).** `docs/gates-as-worlds/BAR.md` is the standard every gate is held to: what Amber Reach and The Hour Crypt have, and the preview's `relief`, `wall`, `shaped`, `contrast` measures and FLAT, PLAIN, WASHED flags.

**Air.** Realms now take part in Gate Air (SPEC 38.9). `RealmAir` tells a client on arrival and every half minute, no card: blueprint `sky.air` lists the client's air and small life, and `Land.air()` (built with `kit/AirPlan`) gives mist layers, shafts, lights and still water, which Lens reads. Amber Reach and The Hour Crypt have both.

**Walking.** `WalkCheck` now swims: you can cross water and climb out where the bank is a step high.

**Kingsroot Keep (gate 10, Overgrown Temple).** Keep family: cold wet ashlar, verdigris tile, black oak, pale roots, rust cloth (`tools/art/specs/realm_keep.py`). Two rings of curtain wall and a stepped keep on a hill inside a river gorge; every gate is shut. The rule: `keep_climb_root` (a root net, tagged `minecraft:climbable`) hangs on the walls where the great roots have broken them, and `WalkCheck` now climbs. The Lord waits in the great hall, nave and galleries with no roof. A shared wall profile (`wall`) makes every face step in four planes: batter, pilasters, blind arches with lit slits, corbelled parapet. Folk: wall-hobs in the outer ward.

**Saltcomb Flats (gate 7, Hive, Desert and Ruin).** Salt family: bone wax, ochre stone, blue-black shade, white crust, dune sand, charcoal paving (`tools/art/specs/realm_salt.py`). A white salt pan of hexagon plates with brine pans, crossed by a road of black hexagon stones from the Mouth (0, 66, 244) to the door of the Sinking Court. A dry hive-city climbs the dunes behind it: spires of stepped comb tiers (`Spire`), comb domes, stepped blocks of cells, dark ribs. Realms can't change their sky per gate, so the rule isn't tied to a clock in the sky: law `salt` (`RealmSalt`) sets the crust over the three fords (z 188, 128, 72) hard for 60 s and soft for 40 s, a run or a slow swim, via `change("salt_soft"/"salt_hard")`; a cell with something in it stays brine until the next turn. Lord: `hive_regent` in the Sinking Court (drum at (0, -60), arena radius 42, wall inner radius 60): hex floor over brine, tiers of steps, a gallery at +30 with two stairs, lit niches, sand running down every third pilaster, a corbelled roof with a hole 22 across, a cracked comb dome in the middle. `heart_weeps` and `heart_winds` sink whole floor tiles into the brine in two sectors; the door is sealed with fresh comb. Folk: salt-rakers.

**The Vine Seat (gate 3, Overgrown Temple).** Fane family: pale cut stone, green tile, teak, gilt, three leaf shades (`fane_leaf`, `_lit`, `_deep`), pale water (`fane_fall`). A stepped temple of six courses on a lagoon, split by one tree, with two great faces either side of the stair and a screen wall rising behind the trunk. Every wall comes from one rule, `facade`: plinth, pilasters every fourteen, bays with a lit niche or a carved panel, frieze, overhanging cornice. Rule `roots` (`RealmRoots`): curtains of roots shut across doors you've used and part for anyone moving at them; stand still and they climb your legs. The Lord's place is the Root Bowl at the foot of the trunk, opened by three Wardens.


### 50.9 The Run (plan page https://claude.ai/artifact/S2hFD95MozxhM8twqcfXQ9, approved in full 10 Nov 2026; build log docs/gates-as-worlds/the-run/BUILD.md)

A gate is a run, not a place to look at: you go from point to point, up and down, fight several different packs, get past
traps and movement, beat the Wardens and the Lord. A Realm's land carries its run as data (`Land.route()`), a list of **legs**:

| Leg | What happens | Runs on |
|---|---|---|
| ARRIVE | The Mouth. | |
| FIGHT | A pack stands in view at a DEN site and waits; it wakes when it sees you inside 13 blocks, when you come inside 5, or when one is hurt. | `RealmPacks.den`, `Encounters.holdFree` |
| AMBUSH | Nothing stands there. Walk inside the leg's radius and its pack comes up awake round you; the land's `ambush_<leg>` blocks change as it springs. | `RealmRun` |
| MOVEMENT | A stretch you can fall from. Inside its box (`Land.Course`) a fall of more than 6 puts you back on the last of its ledges you stood on, for 3 + 8% of your health. | `RealmRun.course` |
| TRAP | Presses, spitters, floor that gives way (below). | `RealmTraps` |
| WARDEN | A Warden and its company at a WARDEN site. | `RealmPacks.warden` |
| BREATHER | A place to stop. Pressure sends nothing after a player standing in one. | `RealmLive.pressure` |
| SHORTCUT | A way that opens when its `when` is met ("warden2": that Warden is down; "den1": that pack is dead): the land's `shortcut_<leg>` blocks, once, with the land's line if it has one. | `RealmRun` |
| HIDDEN | A place off the route. The first player inside it banks its share for everyone in the gate; the land's `found_<leg>` blocks change. | `RealmRun` |
| LORD | The Lord's hall (§50.8). | `RealmLive.heart` |

A leg is `id, kind, name, x y z, radius, site, pack, when, exits`. `pack` names the monsters ("hive_larva*4", "hive_guard"), from
the mobs each theme already has, with one more of the first for every two ranks; empty rolls from the theme as before. `exits`
are the legs you can go on to. A land nobody has designed a run for still has one, read off its sites (arrive, every den a
fight, every Warden a Warden, the Lord), and plays exactly as it did.

**Doors.** A leg whose land answers `change("seal_<leg>")` has doors. They shut while its pack is awake and a player of the gate
stands inside it (radius + 2), and open the moment either stops being true, so nobody is ever locked in or out; a cell with
anyone in it stays open. A Warden without doors keeps the soft ring of stage 0 (the ground past ring + 6 turns you back).
Which legs are shut is saved with the Realm (`RealmState.sealed`).

**Traps** (`Land.Trap`, in the land's own blocks, on the Realm's clock; hurt as the old Gauntlet does):
- PRESS: a box of cells fills for 30 ticks of every `period`, after 30 ticks of dust and cracking. Whoever is in it takes
  3 + 11% of their health and is put outside on the nearer side. It never closes on a monster.
- SPIT: a cell lights for 20 ticks, then everything on its line takes 2 + 8% and Slowness II for 2 s, once per beat.
- CRUMBLE: floor that goes 15 ticks after it is stood on and grows back 100 ticks later, never into anyone.

**Pressure** as §7: 4 minutes with no pack woken and nothing killed and waves come (2, then up to 6, every 45 s); at 8 minutes
the hunter (the theme's Warden kind). Not in the Lord's hall, not in a breather, not on peaceful.

**Pay.** Kill pay is unchanged (60% of the land's pay, split over the run's monsters: a rolled den counts 5, a named pack what it
names, a Warden 4 plus its company). Of the other 40%: the Wardens bank half between them (a sixth each where there are three);
where the land has a hidden leg the Wardens bank four tenths and the hidden legs hold 15% between them, paid only to those who
find them; the Lord pays what is left.

**The check** (`RouteCheck`, in the bench and the tests) proves a designed run: every leg has its job (a den, a Warden, a trap,
a course, blocks that open) and can be walked to, the first fight is within 150 blocks of the Mouth, no two joined legs are more
than 260 apart, there is a loop or a shortcut, a place under a roof rises or falls 20 or more, and each fight has 12 walkable
columns a monster. The walk (`WalkCheck`) now makes the one jump anyone can (a sprint over one to three missing cells, level or
down) and goes through everything a land lists as `walk_open`.

**The crawl kit** (`kit/crawl/CrawlLand`). A dungeon crawl is rock with a run hollowed out of it, part by part: `Cave` (an oval
room with a wandering rim), `Arena` (a round room with a ring of pillars for cover), `Tunnel` (a way between two points that
climbs in half steps, never steeper than one in two), `Shaft` (a ledge winding down a round shaft, breakable at its quarter
points, over a pool it runs down into). Parts meet at the same height. The land that extends it says what the rock, floors and
doors are made of and what grows on the walls (`adorn`), which is where a crawl gets a look of its own.

**The Hour Crypt as a run** (15 legs). The nave (ghouls and archers), the walk round the pit (a breather), then three wings in
any order. East: three rows of stone teeth come up across the Ossuary's gallery one after another (PRESS, period 100), the
Ossuary's pack, an ambush of wisps in the north chapel, and the Warden of bones, whose door shuts on the fight. Off the cross
aisle's south end is the reliquary (HIDDEN): its door stands open only while the bell rings, and for good once someone has been
in. West: the Sunk Aisle's pack in the water, an ambush in the drowned bays, the Warden of water behind its door. South: the
ringers' tower, its stair broken in three places (three cells each, a sprint clears them; a fall is caught), to the Warden
among the ropes. Its fall lets a bell rope down from the bridge to the walk round the pit (SHORTCUT; `crypt_bell_rope` is
climbable). Then the Lord.

**The Broodwarren (gate 14, Hive, a short crawl; `land/Broodwarren`, blueprint `awaken:broodwarren`).** Brood family
(`tools/art/specs/realm_brood.py`): nest paper in three tones laid in layers, rooted earth, resin and its slab, brood comb and
comb with something lit in it, sacs, royal jelly, spitter cells, and the red skin that is its door. Fifty blocks down in nine
legs: the split root (a crack of daylight behind you), the antechamber (larvae and honey slimes), the spitting gallery (five
cells, a second apart), the nursery (a shaft of hanging comb; the ledge is broken at three quarter points and has two stretches
of thin comb that give way), the larder (the sacs burst round you: larvae and drones), the jelly cell behind the larder's
curtain of sacs (HIDDEN), the workers' crawl back up to the antechamber once the larder is cleared (SHORTCUT), the comb ring
(the Swarm Mind with a guard and drones) and the brood chamber (the Hive Regent; its pillars wake as she is worn down).

**Creatures with bodies of their own in the packs.** A pack can name any creature the mobs module has, not only its theme's:
the cave hunters (§23) are gate monsters now, with the bodies and motion they already have. A name marked "~" keeps its own
habits instead of standing and waiting (a Drip Lurker leaps up and hangs from a roof three to nine blocks over it and drops on
whoever walks under it in the dark; a Hushling hunts by sound and leaves the light alone); such a monster counts as fighting
only once it has a target, so a room of them does not shut its doors on someone who is sneaking through. A Warden's pack that
starts "!name" names the Warden itself. The Broodwarren: three Drip Lurkers hang among the larder's sacs before its ambush
springs, and the comb ring's Warden is the Thousandfoot (the ring has no pillars). The Hour Crypt: three Hushlings keep the dark
south aisle in front of the reliquary's door, which is why you wait for the toll there quietly (16 legs).

**A cache per herd.** When a fight's or an ambush's pack is all down, a gate cache appears where it stood (as a room's does in
the old gates), with the cache sound and a burst of light.

**Rolled crawls** (`kit/crawl/GeneratedCrawl`). A crawl whose run is rolled from the gate's seed, so one blueprint is a
different dungeon every time it forms. Always: the way in, a fight in sight of it, two to five legs out of a bag (more fights,
a gallery of spitters, a hall of three teeth, a shaft with a broken ledge and thin floor, and always one ambush), the Warden
behind its door, the Lord behind the heart's door. Ways turn (they try up to seven headings and take the first that runs into
nothing; galleries, halls and shafts keep to the four straight ways) and drop four to seven blocks each; a run with a shaft in
it may climb three now and then. Every fight, ambush and Warden room has a door on each way out of it. A side cell off the first
fight joins the way beyond it, so there is always a way round (and a find in it); a hidden cell goes off the ambush where there
is room (two finds, and the hidden share of the pay). The same checks as a designed run prove every seed (test
`realm_generated_crawls_play`, six seeds a skin).

A **skin** is the land that extends it: rock, floors, the half step, the door, what grows on the walls (`adorn`), who lives
there (a few herds it goes round, the ambush, the Warden's company), what its spitters, teeth and thin floor are made of, and
how much it wanders (1 dug, 0 built). A new skin is a new kind of dungeon; its layouts come free. Skins so far:
- **The Lower Combs** (`awaken:brood_burrow`, Hive): the Brood family, as The Broodwarren. Larvae and slimes, drones and a
  guard, lurkers in the roof with larvae under them, slimes and drones; the Thousandfoot as Warden; the Hive Regent.
- **The Bone Roads** (`awaken:catacombs`, Bell Crypt): the Knell family, built (clean round vaults, straight ways, coursed
  stone with a band every six). Skulls in niches at head height, bone packed into the walls in patches, candles gathered along
  the foot of every wall with a light over each cluster, a small bell on its rope here and there, bell ropes down every shaft.
  Ghouls and archers, archers and wisps, Hushlings with a ghoul, wisps and a Crypt Keeper; the Sexton; the Bell Warden. Teeth of
  pale stone, a bronze mouth that turns gilt before it spits, boards that give way.

**Naming a monster** (`core.api.MobHooks.spawnNamed(level, id, pos, contentLevel, tags, gateId)`, added to the §12 API). A pack's
names are spawned through it: any creature by its id, in the role its own tier gives it (normal, elite or Warden; never a
Lord), scaled to the gate's content level and counted and paid as a monster of the gate. `spawnCreature` stays what it was (a
Realm's peaceful life, no gate role), which is why a pack could not use it. A name nothing answers to gets one of the theme's
own instead, so a typo never empties a room. Test `realm_packs_spawn_by_name`.

**Herds for a den nobody designed** (`gates/run/Herds`). A land whose run is only read off its sites (Amber Reach, The Vine
Seat, Kingsroot Keep, Saltcomb Flats, The Quiet Barrow, The Wax Galleries, until each gets its own) takes its dens' packs from
its theme's herds, four each for the Hive, the Bell Crypt and the Overgrown Temple, gone round den by den from a start the
seed picks, so two camps in one land are not the same fight. Under a roof a fifth herd joins the round: Drip Lurkers or
Hushlings with one of the theme's own. A theme with no herds rolls from its roster as before.

**The run on the HUD.** In a Realm the run HUD's hint line reads "Herds 2 / 5 · Wardens 1 / 3" (packs that stand and wait and
are all down, of those the run has; a herd that keeps its own habits isn't counted), then "Every Warden is down. The way on is
open." until the Lord falls (`RealmLive.hint`).

Three more skins, each one file a builder wrote from a thirty-line brief in ten to twenty minutes (bench on three seeds, then
the six-seed test here):
- **The Hollow Hills** (`awaken:hollow_hills`, Bell Crypt, the Barrow family): passages under a mound, packed earth shored
  with kerb stones, urns and shields, grave-glow low on the walls; darker than the catacombs, with pools, because Hushlings
  live in it.
- **The Root Cellars** (`awaken:root_cellars`, Overgrown Temple, the Fane family): a temple's undercroft half swallowed by
  roots, moss and vines, lit leaves and braziers; the temple's hounds, archers and creakers, with Lurkers in one herd.
- **The Tallow Runs** (`awaken:tallow_runs`, Hive, the Wax family): soot rock that pale wax has run down and set over, candle
  banks at the foot of the walls, lit comb in the ambush and the Lord's hall; the one that glows.

**Light in a rolled crawl, after the first real-game walks.** The Bone Roads and The Hollow Hills could barely be read in the
real game. The Bone Roads: candles along half of every wall's foot (was three tenths), a light over four in ten clusters, at
15. The Hollow Hills: grave-lights in three quarters of a room's wall cells of four and along the ways too, each with a light
of 15 over it and, in a room, a second two higher. A skin is judged in the real game, not on the checker: the checker draws
these two brighter than the game does.

**Nothing in a Realm can be dug or built on.** The gates' protection (§17: no breaking but a power's own constructs, no placing,
no buckets, no blast damage, creative excepted) covers a Realm as it covers a floor, so a fight's door, a trap's teeth and a
gap in a stair can't be got round with a pickaxe or a stack of blocks. Test `realm_blocks_cannot_be_dug`.

**Sizes and shapes of a rolled crawl.** A seed also rolls how long the run is and which way it goes.
- Size: short (one or two legs between the first fight and the Warden, besides the ambush), standard (three or four), great
  (three, then the Warden, then three more with a second ambush and a second Warden before the Lord). Three in ten, about
  half, one in six. A great run is about fifteen legs.
- Shape: delve (steadily down, four to seven a way), plunge (six to eight a way, two shafts first out of its bag), climb (the
  Mouth is at the bottom and every way rises to a Lord at the top; a shaft is walked upward and has no breaks, since nobody
  jumps a gap upward), sprawl (wide rooms, no shaft, nearly level). Forty, twenty-five, seventeen and eighteen in a hundred.
- Legs of the same kind after the first take a number (`shaft2`, `ambush2`, `warden2`).

**The chasm** (`CrawlLand.Chasm`, a MOVEMENT leg). A straight room with no floor but a pool ten blocks down, a shelf at each
end, and a row of flat-topped pillars between them: three cells long (four before a gap of three), two or three cells apart,
each beside the last by at most one cell and never higher than it. A fall is caught as on any course. A ramp down one wall goes
from the first shelf into the pool, so whoever lands in it walks back up; the far end can only be reached across. The
generator clears anything with a body out of the air over the pool and off the pillars after a skin has dressed the place.

**What a skin's growths may hold on to.** `adorn` is told about a wall, floor or roof only when it is the dungeon's own rock
(solid by the parts' shapes, and still there), never something another `adorn` call put into the air. Found the hard way: a
shelf fungus had attached itself to a hanging glowcap that one chunk had drawn in its margin and the next chunk, which owned
the cell, had not; the shelf was left floating. Nothing can hold on to a thing that isn't rock, so nothing can be left behind.

Three more skins from builders, one per gate theme with that theme's own blocks, monsters and Lord: **The Cinder Workings**
(`awaken:cinder_workings`, Ember Mines), **The Sunken Stacks** (`awaken:sunken_stacks`, Drowned Archive, ranks D and C),
**The Sporewells** (`awaken:sporewells`, Fungal Hollow). The Realms dimension lists every gate theme's biome, so a skin
takes its theme's air and sky.

Three more, the same way: **The Frozen Cells** (`awaken:frozen_cells`, Frost Monastery, ranks C and B: a monastery's cells
under ice, pale stone and ring-lamps), **The Glass Warrens** (`awaken:glass_warrens`, Glass Desert, ranks D and C: burrows in
sandstone shot through with lit amber glass), **The Stopped Works** (`awaken:stopped_works`, Clockwork Foundry, ranks D and C:
riveted plate, brass and furnace light, machines stopped mid-stroke).

**A wall is one thing with things in it.** Seen in the real game on The Sporewells: a skin that picks each wall cell's block at
random from four or five (rock, lit rock, moss, stalk, cap, gills) reads as a chequer and nothing else, however good each block
is. A wall is its rock (courses or veins from noise); growths and fittings come in whole patches a few cells across (a bracket
of fungus is a dark cap with its gills lit along the underside), and a floor is one stuff with beds of another. Light comes from
the fittings, never from salting lit blocks through the rock. A great run's crossing over a pool is lit from its walls alone, so
a skin lights them more than a room's (The Lower Combs' first one was near black in the game).

**A climb is never dark.** Skins light rooms, and two of them lit no shaft at all. So the generator itself sets an unseen light
(level 14) three cells over the ledge every eighth of a turn down a shaft, and over each shelf and pillar of a chasm, after the
skin has dressed the place. A skin still dresses a climb's walls; it no longer has to make the jumps visible.

Three more kinds: **The Silvered Halls** (`awaken:silvered_halls`, Mirror Palace, ranks C and B: bays of tall mirror between dark
piers, a gilt cornice, chequered floors), **The Sealed Wing** (`awaken:sealed_wing`, Precursor Lab, ranks C and B: pale panels,
lit strips at knee height and under the roof, tanks for pillars), **The Sleepless Ward** (`awaken:sleepless_ward`, Nightmare,
ranks C and B: papered corridors as a dream remembers them, a rail that slips out of line, doors and windows that lead nowhere).
The false doors are real doors set in solid wall: a player may open one and finds wall.

Three more, which bring the kinds to seventeen: **The Unlit Stair** (`awaken:unlit_stair`, Abyssal Shrine, ranks A and S: black
dressed stone with one pale band every sixth course, niches with votives, a pale line down every way, nothing on the floors),
and two second kinds for themes that had a built one, each wild where the first is built: **The Rime Hollows**
(`awaken:rime_hollows`, Frost Monastery: natural ice caves, stone at a wall's foot, then snow, then blue ice, sheets of it lit
from inside, icicles in clusters) and **The Green Dark** (`awaken:green_dark`, Overgrown Temple: wet jungle caves, moss taking
whole walls, curtains of vine and glow berries along lines in the roof). With these every theme that suits a crawl has a kind.
Sky Archipelago (fliers, open sky) and the Lantern Night Market (neutral monsters, a Lord who trades) have none: neither suits
a crawl as the generator stands. A layout comes from the seed alone, whatever the kind, and the test tries 104 of them.

**No two alike.** Euan, 10 Nov, on the first seventeen: "they look very repetitive, just with different themes... add more
variation in terms of the different parkour things and everything, so that they never look exactly the same." He was right:
the generator knew one room, one Lord's hall, one shaft and one chasm, and a kind changed only the blocks. Now every leg rolls
what it is cut like, and a kind says which cuts are its own (`GeneratedCrawl.Style`, one `style()` per kind):

- **Rooms** (`Cave.Form`, eight): the oval; a long hall; a cross; a ring round a core of rock; a hall with two rows of piers; a
  room with a terrace three up along one side and two ramps onto it; a pit with a walk two up all round it and four ramps down;
  a rift, long and tall, whose floor steps up a block and then two more. The first fight and the ambush take only level
  forms, because other ways lead off them.
- **Wardens' rooms and Lords' halls** (`Arena.Plan`, six): a ring of pillars; a nave with two rows; a cross with four at the
  crossing; a rotunda with two rings and a higher dome; a round floor with two tiers of steps round it; a square hall on four
  great piers. The middle is always open and level, because the Lords were built for a level floor. A Warden that needs the
  floor (no pillars) gets a plan with nothing raised.
- **Gulfs** (`Chasm.Kind`, eight ways across): pillars; a bridge with two spans gone, on piers, what fell lying in the pool;
  rafters one cell wide, each ending on a cross beam a block lower, the next beside it or over a gap of two; a ledge along the
  left wall, a pillar in the middle, a ledge along the right; platforms hung from the roof by a chain; great steps down, two
  or three lower each time (never on a climb); a ford, wall to wall in shallow water, with stones at the water's top and more
  that lead nowhere; a deck that gives way under whoever stands on it (the crumbling floor's rule: a block goes fifteen ticks
  after you step on it and comes back after a hundred), where a fall puts you back on a shelf, never on the deck.
- **Shafts**: round, or square with flights along four walls for what was built.
- **Ways**: as wide and as high as the kind says (2 to 3 each side, 4 to 6 high).
- **How often.** From a standard run up there is always a gulf to cross (it takes the place of a second fight if the bag
  drew none), and a great run's second stretch has a climb or a crossing of its own.
- **A branch.** From a standard run up, where there is room: off a den after the first or a Warden's room, to one side, a way to a gulf with no
  fall in it and a vault beyond with two caches. Nobody has to cross it; whoever does is paid for it. It is only ever a
  crossing that is as easy to come back over as to go out on (never the great steps, never the pillars with their run-ups),
  and the den's doors shut it with the rest.

Rules these keep, so that a skin written for the oval and the pillars dresses all of them without knowing:
`feet` is a room's lowest floor and every other level is raised from it (what a skin draws at `feet` is on the floor or
under it, never in the air); a new room is still a `Cave`, a new hall an `Arena` with `pillar()`, a new crossing a `Chasm`;
every jump is a sprint over one to three cells straight along or straight across, level or down, and the only way up is a
step of one; what was built (`wild()` under a half) stands square to the compass however the way came to it; whatever a skin
grows is cleared from over every stand; every stand has a light over it. A tour can't name a place in a rolled run, so it
names a leg: `/awaken gate realm_leg <kind> <n> <dx> <dy> <dz>` stands at the n-th leg of a kind, turned toward where it
leads. The wide sweep (eight seeds a kind) fails unless every room form, every Lord's plan and every crossing turned up.

**A stand** (Euan, 11 Nov: "maybe some gates that are like almost kind of like a wave system... survive 10 waves"). A blueprint whose
`land.params` has `"stand": 1` is cut by a rolled kind's skin but is no run: the way in, one great room (an ambush leg eighteen or
so across, nine high, its `when` reading `waves:N`), its Warden, the Lord. N is six at E rank and one more for every rank above. A
wave comes when the last is down and someone still holds the room (`RealmRun`, markers `wave<site>_<k>` in the saved `woken` set);
every other wave is the theme's own roll in place of the kind's herd, so no two waves are the same company; the room's doors stay
shut until the last wave falls. A stand pays what any gate of its rank pays: its waves count as shares (`RealmLive.units`). Eight
on 11 Nov: The Ossuary Floor, The Slag Pit, The Spore Ring, The Drowned Hall, The Glass Bowl, The Chapter House, The Night Ward,
The Black Landing.

**The right amount** (the same day: "the big worlds we've built so far... look pretty good, like with the right amount of mobs in
them"). An open land (anything that is not a crawl) is never empty between its dens. The first cut of this put one more pack
thirty to forty-four blocks from a player every twenty seconds (`RealmPacks.wander`); it is gone, replaced the same day by:

**Who lives there** (`RealmCountry`; Euan, 11 Nov, on the first rolled land: "Also think about mob and herd spawns etc to make
these really fun and immersive"). A land under a sky (not a crawl, not under a roof) is read in cells 56 across, and each cell's
haunt comes from the seed and the shape of the ground alone (`Land.ground`), so the same land has the same life for everyone, a
herd is where a herd would stand, and it is all there before anyone arrives. Nine places in a cell are looked at: the most
level, the highest, and a second level one. A cell holds one of:

- **nothing**: 50 cells in a hundred, so the country has quiet stretches and nothing comes at even steps (Euan, 10 Nov: world
  content "must feel natural, with quiet stretches");
- **a herd** (44 in a hundred of the rest): four to seven of the land's herd animal on ground that falls no more than two blocks
  in three, each kept within eighteen blocks of it;
- **small creatures** (28): two to four of the land's little ones, on rougher ground;
- **a pack on the prowl** (14): a den's worth of the theme's monsters, by herd where the theme has herds, walking a beat between
  the cell's two level places: the spot they keep moves from one to the other every forty seconds by the world's clock
  (`Dormant.stop`), so the whole pack turns together and each keeps its place in it. They notice and fight as a den's do. You
  can watch them go, wait them out, or meet them;
- **a lookout** (9): one of the theme's (its marksman where it has one) on the cell's highest place, which must stand four
  blocks or more over the level one, and three or four more (one more for every two ranks) waiting on that level ground behind
  it. A lookout sees twenty-four blocks with a clear line, up or down a slope, where the rest see thirteen. Seen by it, you hear
  a raid horn and everyone of its own within thirty-eight blocks wakes and comes for you. Put it down unseen and the reserve
  never knows;
- **the big one at home** (5): the theme's Warden kind with two of its own (three from B rank), on level ground at least 64
  blocks from every leg and site. Nobody has to go near it. Put down, it leaves a cache where it lived.

Mostly animals, on purpose: a hostile haunt is an event, not the texture of the land, which the run's own dens already are (the
first weights, 22, 16 and 8, put 75 hostile haunts in Amber Reach's 336 cells, about eight along one walk; these put about
four; and the first walk of the Cinder Crown met nine herds of rams for one pack, so half of all cells are empty now and
herds are a little rarer, the hostile kinds as common as before). Ground under the water is never a haunt: it is the most
level ground a land has, and Amber Reach's first herd ground was a pool's bed. A cell that asks for something its ground cannot give takes the next gentler thing (a lookout with no perch is a pack on the
prowl; a herd on a slope is small creatures) or nothing. Every haunt keeps 24 blocks clear of every site and 26 of every leg,
and 56 of the way in. A land has its share of each hostile kind (packs 4 and one and a half more a rank, lookouts 2 and one more
every two ranks, one lair, two from B); a cell past the share holds nothing. A haunt fills when someone is within 92 blocks and
nobody within 50, as a den's pack does at 80, and a hostile one fills once (`RealmState.woken`: `haunt_<n>` when settled,
`hauntp`, `hauntw`, `hauntl` by kind, `hauntd` once a lair's cache is out). The run comes first: nothing of the country's stands
while the gate already holds more than twenty-eight monsters (its cap is forty), or where a pack already stands within
twenty-four blocks. The country's monsters pay as any kill does, on top of the gate's own
shares: whether that stays is Euan's call.

Herds and small creatures are not monsters of the gate: they are the wide world's own wild animals (`MobHooks.spawnNamed` with
no gate, at the gate's level), not counted, paying nothing from the pool, gone when nobody is near and back on their ground six
minutes later if most of a herd is missing and nobody is there to see. Each theme has a kit (`RealmCountry.KITS`): the Ember
Mines have crag rams, scree marmots and peak kites overhead; the Overgrown Temple crested basilisks, dart frogs and lumen moths;
the Frost Monastery frost stags and frostfinches; the Glass Desert dune rays and glass scarabs; the Fungal Hollow mossbacks and
mudskippers; the Hive pollen grazers (and its elite, the Door, as its lookout: a bee on a rock cannot be seen); the Bell Crypt hollow owls; the Drowned Archive bog toads, mudskippers and bogwicks. No
animal in a kit changes the land (none that plants, grows things or leaves a trail). A blueprint's `life.herds` names its own
herd animals instead of the kit's, and `life.ambient` what is in its air; both may now name a wild animal as well as a Realm's
own. Only a peaceful animal comes (`MobHooks.peaceful`: one that is never hostile, or only fights back): a night hunter or a
named beast named in a sheet gives nothing. The Quiet Barrow's sheet had named the Old Antler as its herd, which gave nothing
for as long as only a Realm's own creatures could be named and then, on the country's first walk, five of him on the moor; its
herd is frost stags now. Amber Reach's pollen grazers stand on grounds like every other herd. Under a roof a Realm's herds are still kept round the
player as before (`RealmLife.herd`). The wide world's named beasts (the Stonehorn and the rest) are not used: each is one of a
kind out there.

**Every rank.** Each finished blueprint lists every rank from the one its theme opens at up to S, not the two it first had. Packs
already grow with rank (`RealmPacks.roll`, `den`, `warden`). A run's shape does not change with rank yet.

**Depth.** Euan, 10 Nov, on the pictures of the new shapes: "the rooms and the setups and stuff is decent now, but the
atmosphere itself is completely missing... a completely flat floor, completely flat walls... it's still all one block
distances. There's no half blocks, there's no grass, there's no mushrooms... no variation in the depth of the floor or the
walls." The old gates had been given exactly this (§38.14: gentle on the way, bold at the edges, with a theme's slabs,
stairs, drifts and bits); the rolled dungeons had none of it. They take that section's blocks and its rule:

- **Ground** (`Cave.depth`, `relief2`). Over every level room the ground rises and falls in half blocks. Nothing rises on
  the way through (the lines from each doorway to the middle; round a ring's core, the middle of the walk), so the way reads
  as a path worn into the floor. Off it the ground stands a slab or two higher and rolls, and banks up two or three blocks
  against the walls. A step is half a block nearly everywhere and never more than one. A half step is the kind's own slab.
  Rooms whose form already has levels (terrace, pit, rift) keep them and take no ground; a Warden's room and a Lord's hall
  stay level to five sixths of the way out and only bank at the wall; the small cells (way in, side cell, hidden cell, vault)
  stay level. A room is told of every way into it (`door`) before anything asks how high its floor is there.
- **Ways** are worn down their middle with half a step up along their sides: ragged where the place was dug, a kerb where it
  was built.
- **Walls and roofs.** What was built: a pilaster stands a block out of every straight wall every six cells, and a beam
  crosses a hall's roof every five. What was dug: the roof swells and dips, comes down in knots, and comes down in lumps at
  the walls so a wall leans in over you. (Lumps cut into the wall itself were tried first and could hang a cell clear of it;
  what comes down from the roof is always joined to it.)
- **Small pieces** (`Trim`, one per kind, set last by `detail`): a stair at about half the wall feet off the way, its back
  to the wall; a stair hung upside down where the roof steps; a drift one layer deep along the rest of the wall feet; plants
  in clumps that thicken away from the way; bits underfoot; things hanging where the roof is high. All from the kind's own
  theme (its §38.14 depth blocks and its plants), a few of Minecraft's where a theme has none (cobwebs, hanging roots, moss
  carpet, fern). Nothing with a body but the stairs. Nothing where a door shuts, in the narrow ways or in a hall of traps.
  The Lower Combs and The Tallow Runs have no stairs yet: their rock has no cut shapes.
- **The long walls** (`Chasm.walls`, `Shaft.walls`). The first walk in the real game with depth in it showed where none
  had reached: the two long walls of every gulf and the four of every stairwell, dead flat for thirty blocks. They are cut
  back one cell, never built out, so nothing can stand in the way of a jump. What was built: bays four wide between piers
  two wide. What was dug: scoops in patches. A gulf's are under the level of its shelves, from two over the water, and
  never beside anything there is to stand on (the ramp back up included). A stairwell's are between the passes of its
  ledge: the wall is whole from five under the ledge to five over the feet of whoever is on it, so there is never a hole
  beside the climb, and the bays step down the wall with the stair.

**Air.** The same message: "Same with like the atmosphere in the air... Same when it comes to sounds and everything, and
music." The kinds had been sharing borrowed biomes and one copied list of small life (a foundry with bats). Now each kind
has its own, written from one table (`tools/realms/kinds_air.py`):

- **Its own biome** (`awaken:realm/<kind>`, a copy of its theme's gate biome so nothing spawns): its fog colour and how
  near the fog stands (from 3 to 12 blocks out, gone by 42 to 110: the first numbers, 56 to 140, stood too far out to be
  seen inside a room), what drifts in the air (ash, spores, snow, motes,
  fireflies, sparks), the colour of its block light and of its dark, an ambient loop, a mood sound, an occasional sound and
  its music. Every sound is one of Minecraft's own recordings by name. The Silvered Halls has no loop; The Unlit Stair has
  no sound at all, which is its theme's one line.
- **Its own Lens look** (`biome:awaken:realm/<kind>` in `looks_gates.json`): its theme's look with more haze, a mist, a
  little more glow, and the haze tinted from its fog.
- **Its own small life** (blueprint `sky.air`): only what belongs there (embers and steam in a foundry, snow and wind in ice,
  fish and paper in a drowned library).
- **Gate Air from the kit** (`GeneratedCrawl.airOf`, on top of what the skin asks for, inside §38.9's limits): a soft light
  in the kind's colour over the middle of every room something is fought in, so its mist is lit; still water and a low
  mist in every gulf and at the foot of every shaft; a shaft of light down every shaft.
- **Light comes down** (`GeneratedCrawl.wells`). Every room with the roof for it has a well of light, the Lord's hall two:
  a slot in the roof three cells by one, off the middle, over open floor, going six cells up into the rock to a light
  nobody sees the source of. It is real light: unseen lights down the middle of it every three cells, so the pool reaches
  the floor however high the roof is and what grows and lies there can be seen. (A light at the roof alone never reached
  the floor of a tall room: the first walk showed a lit slot and nothing under it.) A well is only cut where nothing else
  of the run comes within three cells of it. The side cell and the way in have none (the way in has its own crack to the
  sky). Gate Air has a shaft down each well, in the colour of the day at the way in, and every kind asks for `shaft_dust`
  first in its list, so motes turn in it. First, because the client takes a list in order and stops at 260 sprites: in a
  kind full of fireflies nothing late in the list was ever reached.
- **Mist layers** are written down for the biggest rooms (the Lord's, which a skin lays itself, then the Wardens', then
  the dens, widest first, inside the six §38.9 allows; gulfs and shafts take three at most). Nothing draws them yet.
- **What reads Gate Air here, and the beams that are not there.** In this build only the client's small life reads Gate
  Air (§38.9's sprites): nothing in Lens reads a land's shafts, mist layers or lights, whatever §38.3 says of marching
